# TortalPortal Lite — option catalog, POST adversarial verification

Exported 2026-09-12 from workflow run `wf_426424f2-e93` (complete — all phases finished, 0 agent errors). 286 options: 197 first-round (all verified under two independent lenses — decompile accuracy, vanilla-client reality) + 89 gap-fill (all verified under a single combined adversarial pass). Numbering 1–177 is the original 8 first-round domains (topologies, routing, access, ops, economy, lockdown, wildcard, ux); 178–197 is the targeted-portals domain (completed in a later resume); 198–286 is gap-fill, in designer start order (ops, targeted, access, routing, wildcard, lockdown, ux, economy).

Legend: feasibility `OK` feasible · `CAV` caveats · `CHK` needs in-game check · `OUT` ruled out — enforcement `SRV` server-enforced · `CLI` client-honoured · `REACT` reactive-only · `ADMIN` admin-facing · `NONE` not enforceable. Arrows show designer claim → verifier-adjusted value.

**Merge rule (identical to the workflow script):** majority-refuted → ruled-out; otherwise feasibility = worst of designer and both lenses (first-round) or the single gap-fill verifier; enforcement = first verifier that disagreed with the designer; status = refuted / confirmed-with-correction (any verifier supplied corrections) / confirmed / unverified (no matching verdict).

## Options in full


### 1. Simple Pair (vanilla baseline)

`topologies:Simple Pair (vanilla baseline)` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Two portals sharing one byte-identical tag, each holding the other's ZDOID — the only shape vanilla itself builds.


**How it works:** Encoding: two portal ZDOs P and Q. `P.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, T)` and `Q.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, T)` where T is the same ordinal string (ZDOVars.s_tag = "tag".GetStableHashCode(), assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78617). Then `P.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, Q.m_uid)` and the mirror on Q (ZDO.SetConnection :73656-73666). Server-side write recipe, copied from Game.SetConnection :100637-100651: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(Portal, target); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` — do this for both ends. ZDO.SetConnection already calls IncreaseDataRevision() and ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() (:73661-73664), so the portal chunk file is flagged for save. A bare tag write does NOT set that flag, so a tag-only change needs an explicit `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702).

Vanilla reconciliation (Game.ConnectPortals :100589-100626, verified body): pass 1 iterates ZDOMan.GetPortalList() and clears any connection whose target ZDO is null, whose target's s_tag string differs, or whose target's own Portal connection is ZDOID.None. A mutual pair passes all three. Pass 2 only touches portals whose connection IsNone(). So a correct pair is a fixed point — the 5 s coroutine (:100580-100587, started only under `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` at :100074) confirms and re-confirms it forever at zero cost, because ZDOExtraData.SetConnection early-returns false when type+target are unchanged so no DataRevision bump and no network traffic.

You do not need to own the ZDO to write it (no ZDO setter checks ownership) but you should claim it to win the revision race against the owning client, and expect ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926, every 2 s) to hand ownership back to any peer within ~96 m.


**Player experience:** Player walks up to a portal; hover reads `Teleport tag:"forest" [$piece_portal_connected]` (TeleportWorld.GetHoverText :143453-143464) and the mesh glows because UpdatePortal's 0.5 s InvokeRepeating lights m_connected/m_target_found (:143491-143509). Walking into the collider fires TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143672-143681), Teleport() re-reads the connection ZDOID live (:143539), computes `targetPos + targetRot*forward*1.0 + up*1.0` (:143542-143545) and calls TeleportTo(distantTeleport:true). Black screen with the swirl for a minimum of 8 s (Player.UpdateTeleport :15349), then they stand 1 m in front of the far portal facing the same way the far portal faces. Walking straight back in returns them — but only after ~2 s of m_teleportCooldown, and only if they step OUT of the destination trigger first, because OnTriggerEnter is enter-only.


**Failure modes:**
- If one member is destroyed, the survivor holds a dangling ZDOID until the next 5 s pass; ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO (:76963-77000) does not touch the partner. During that window TargetFound() returns false and the player gets a silent no-op (Teleport returns at :143519 with no message).
- Three or more portals sharing one tag: floor(N/2) pairs form and exactly one member is permanently orphaned. It never rotates in, because the surviving pairs keep re-confirming themselves in pass 1 and pass 2 only touches IsNone() portals. Which one is stranded depends on Dictionary bucket order in m_portalObjects and is not stable across restarts.
- Every untagged portal in the world shares the default tag "" (ZDO.GetString defaultValue is "", never null), so a freshly placed unnamed portal auto-pairs with a random unnamed portal anywhere on the map.
- Tag equality is bare C# `string !=` (:100601, :100611) — ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant. "Base", "base" and "Base " are three separate networks with no diagnostic anywhere.

**Designer citations:** Game.ConnectPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100626 ; Game.SetConnection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100637-100651 ; Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100580-100587 (started at Game.Start :100074) ; ZDO.SetConnection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73656-73666 ; ZDOVars.s_tag — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78617 ; TeleportWorld.Teleport — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143517-143549 ; TeleportWorld.GetHoverText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143464 ; ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702

- Game.ConnectPortals is a staged two-tick commit: pass-2 pairs are recorded in m_currentlyConnectingPortals (100681-100687) and force-written both ways at the start of the next tick (ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals 100690-100698, ForceSetConnection 100629-100635).

TargetFound() issues RequestZDO when the target ZDO is not yet on the client (CLIENT:144390-144404; server RPC_RequestZDO -> peer.ForceSendZDO, SERVER GetPeer/RPC_RequestZDO) — that request is only fired by the 0.5 s poll while a teleportable player is within 5 m, so a sprinting player can hit the trigger before the far ZDO arrives and Teleport() silently returns (CLIENT:144265).

(3) Game.SetConnection (100637-100650) is private and routes via RPC_SetConnection to an online owner unless owner==0/offline/force — the option's 'recipe' is the local branch only, which is fine for a mod but should say so. (4) 'must step OUT of the destination trigger first' assumes the arrival point (target + forward*1 + up, 143545) lies inside the trigger box — prefab collider data, not in the decompile; needs in-game check.

### 2. Fan-In Star (many spokes → one hub)

`topologies:Fan-In Star (many spokes → one hub)` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


N spoke portals all point at a single hub; the hub points back at exactly one designated return. Fully stable under pure vanilla with no Harmony patch and no re-write tick.


**How it works:** This is the headline result of the whole catalogue: vanilla's reconciler never checks reciprocity, so a non-reciprocal star is a fixed point.

Encoding. Choose one tag string T. Write `s_tag = T` on the hub H and on every spoke S1..SN. Then, for each spoke: claim + `Si.SetConnection(Portal, H.m_uid)` + ForceSendZDO. For the hub: `H.SetConnection(Portal, Sr.m_uid)` for one chosen return spoke Sr (or an anchor, see the Anchor-Terminated option). Ordering matters only in that every member must end the write batch with a non-None connection before the next 5 s tick.

Why pass 1 leaves it alone (verified at :100594-100606): for spoke Si the test is `zDO == null || zDO.tag != T || zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None` evaluated against H. H exists, H.tag == T, H.connection == Sr ≠ None. All three fail → no teardown. For H the same test against Sr: Sr exists, tag matches, Sr.connection == H ≠ None. No teardown. There is deliberately NO check that the target points back (compare ZDOMan.ConvertPortals :77832, the legacy migration, which DID require `A.target == B && B.target == A`). Pass 2 (:100607-100622) skips every portal whose connection is not IsNone(), so nothing is re-paired. The star survives indefinitely with vanilla's own coroutine actively re-validating it.

Cost per tick: zero. The mod does not need a faster timer, does not need to patch anything, and does not race the server's own 5 s pass. It only needs to re-assert after a member is destroyed or after a world reload (see failure modes).

Scale limit: none from the connection layer. The practical limit is that every spoke must carry the identical tag string, so all N+1 portals show the same name on hover.


**Player experience:** Twelve outpost portals scattered across the Black Forest and Swamp all read `tag:"hub"`. A player at the Swamp outpost walks in, sits through the 8 s loading swirl, and steps out 1 m in front of the great hall portal at the base — the same destination every time, from every outpost. There is no ambiguity and no random shuffling: the twelfth outpost built yesterday goes to the same hall as the first. Walking into the hall portal sends them to whichever spoke the admin designated as the return (say, the Swamp outpost), which is why in practice the hub is paired with a Switchboard so the return is the spoke you last came from. All twelve outpost portals and the hall portal glow and read `[$piece_portal_connected]`, so nothing looks unusual.


**Failure modes:**
- Destroying the hub H strands every spoke: on the next ≤5 s pass every spoke's target resolves to null and pass 1 nulls all N connections, then pass 2 randomly pairs the spokes with each other inside tag T. A 12-spoke network instantly becomes 6 random pairs. The mod must subscribe to ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed (public Action<ZDO>, :76033, invoked :76975) and re-provision or re-scramble the tag immediately.
- Destroying the designated return spoke Sr nulls only H's outbound; pass 2 then pairs H with any other unconnected same-tag portal, silently hijacking the star's exit. Mitigate by pointing H at an Anchor instead of a real portal.
- A player retagging any spoke removes it from group T; its own connection is cleared by TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag (:143595) and it is re-paired inside its new tag group. Detect by polling s_tag on ZDOMan.GetPortalList(), or by prefixing ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC/RouteRPC on the "RPC_SetTag" method hash — but note a client that OWNS the portal ZDO executes RPC_SetTag purely locally and no packet reaches the server (ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC :83588 skips RouteRPC when targetPeerID == m_id), so polling is mandatory and interception is only a bonus.
- World reload collapses the star. See the reload note in prerequisites/openQuestions and the Directed Ring entry for the mechanism.

**Designer citations:** Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 predicate — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100600-100604 (no reciprocity check) ; Game.ConnectPortals pass 2 guard — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100609 ; ZDOMan.ConvertPortals (legacy reciprocal check, for contrast) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77832 ; ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76033, invoked :76975 ; ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC local-dispatch shortcut — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83588-83594 ; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag clears own connection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143595


**Open questions:**
- Does a client standing at a spoke pick up a server-side connection rewrite without a zone reload? Teleport() re-reads the ZDO at transit (:143539) so logically yes, but TargetFound() (:143640) also needs that client to actually hold the hub ZDO. In-game: rewrite a spoke's target to a portal in an unvisited region and see whether the first walk-through silently fails (gate 1 returns with no message) and the second succeeds.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Add: after every reload AND whenever pass 2 has paired any star member, the mod must clear Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals (private List<ConnectingPortals>, SERVER:99903) or the next tick's ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (100690-100698) force-rewrites the vanilla pair over the star, causing a 5 s oscillation.
- Add: a vanilla client owning a spoke can retag it with no packets (TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag 143587-143601, requires IsOwner; ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC 83577-83594 dispatches locally when target==self), leaving the spoke None until the mod re-asserts.
- Newly built spokes start with tag "" and are randomly paired with other untagged portals by vanilla; the mod must adopt them when their tag becomes T (there is no server hook on the retag — poll GetPortalList).
- Prereq must read: Harmony postfix on Game.ConnectPortals (public, :100589) that (a) rewrites the star and (b) clears the private Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals list (:99903) via reflection — otherwise ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-reverts staged members on the next tick, every tick.
- Load-time order is LoadChunks -> ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:76515) -> Game.instance.ConnectPortals (:76523) with DirtyPortalObjects=false at :76527; 'right after OnWorldReady' is too late to prevent random pairing, and the postfix fires on that load-time call too, which is the correct place.
- RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) overwrites hashData[target] per source; for a star only the pair formed by the last-iterated spoke (or hub↔return, depending on Dictionary order) survives — state which pair is unpredictable.
- Hub retag or return-spoke retag collapses the whole star within one tick (pass 1 reads live state mid-iteration); RPC_SetTag's partner-clear is a vanilla no-op because it reads the connection after clearing it (CLIENT:144341-144343), so the hub is only ever torn down by pass 1.
- New/re-tagged spokes on tag T are never auto-attached by vanilla (pass 2 needs two None members); the mod needs an onboarding write on ZDO creation/retag.
- m_onZDODestroyed (:76033) is invoked at :76975-76977 before the portal is removed from m_portalObjects (:76980-76985); exclude the dying ZDO when re-asserting inside that callback.
- 'Switchboard return = spoke you last came from' is reactive-detection-only (PositionWatch-style transit inference), not a server decision.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Core claim holds: pass 1 (SERVER:100595-100606) tests only null/tag/target-non-None against the target and never that the target points back; pass 2 (100607-100622) skips non-None portals. A star where every member is non-None is untouched by the reconciler, and ConvertPortals (77815-77848, reciprocity test at 77832) is the only place a reciprocal check exists. Save collapse is real: RegenerateConnectionHashData (75461-75478) writes one ZDOConnectionHashData per ZDOID, last-writer-wins, so at most one spoke/hub pair survives a reload; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (77850-77893) relinks hash pairs both ways and Game.instance.ConnectPortals (76523) random-pairs the rest. Two missing hazards: (1) staging oscillation — after any tick (including the load-time call at 76523) in which pass 2 paired star members, m_currentlyConnectingPortals holds them and the NEXT tick's ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (100690-100698) force-writes that vanilla pair back over the mod's edges; a postfix that only rewrites the star will oscillate every 5 s with DataRevision bumps and ForceSendZDO traffic each time. The re-assert must also clear the private m_currentlyConnectingPortals list (99903) or prefix-skip ConnectPortals. (2) Any vanilla client that owns a spoke can retag it locally with zero packets (RPC_SetTag 143587-143601 gated on m_nview.IsOwner(); InvokeRoutedRPC local dispatch 83577-83594), which sets that spoke's connection to None; pass 2 then finds no None partner in the star so the spoke stays dead until re-asserted. Any client can also RPC_DestroyZDO the hub (76953-76961, no checks). Enforcement is server-enforced at the route level but not tamper-proof against vanilla clients.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Runtime fixed-point claim holds: pass 1 (SERVER:100594-100606) never tests reciprocity, and ZDOMan.ConvertPortals (:77812-77848) is indeed the only place `A.target==B && B.target==A` is required. The client honours it: TeleportWorld.Teleport reads only its own ZDO's connection and the target's position/rotation (CLIENT:144282-144293); RequestZDO pulls the hub ZDO to any client near a spoke. But the option's stability framing hides three real failure paths. (1) Save boundary is worse than 'needs a re-assert': RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) writes hashData[target] for every source, so the hub's slot is overwritten by whichever spoke iterates last and the return spoke's own source slot is overwritten by the hub's target write (:75474); ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load (:77850-77893) reconstructs at most one reciprocal pair, then Game.instance.ConnectPortals is called synchronously inside LoadChunks (:76523) and randomly pairs the orphaned spokes among themselves in tag T BEFORE any OnWorldReady hook runs. (2) Staged-commit revert: the load-time and every later pass 2 stage pairs in the private Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals (:99903); the NEXT tick's ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) ForceSetConnection()s them regardless of what the mod wrote in between. A postfix that re-asserts the star without also emptying that list flip-flops those members every 5 s with revision bumps and ForceSendZDO traffic forever. (3) Cascade on hub/return retag: RPC_SetTag on the owning client (CLIENT:144333-144348) clears only its own connection; if the hub or the designated return spoke is retagged, pass 1 nulls the hub (tag mismatch or target None) and — because the predicate reads live state during the same foreach — every spoke iterated after the hub in that same pass, after which pass 2 stages random spoke↔spoke pairs. The star must be re-asserted inside the same ConnectPortals call (postfix), not on a slower timer. Also 'no re-write tick' is false for onboarding: a freshly built or re-tagged spoke on T sits at None forever (pass 2 finds no other None member) until the mod writes it. The player-experience line 'paired with a Switchboard so the return is the spoke you last came from' silently depends on reactive transit detection (there is no server hook on the act of teleporting) and should be labelled as such. Effort is small-medium only if the m_onZDODestroyed hook accounts for the fact that it fires BEFORE the dying portal is removed from m_portalObjects (:76975-76985).

### 3. Fan-Out Star (one hub → many simultaneously) — RULED OUT

`topologies:Fan-Out Star (one hub → many simultaneously) — RULED OUT` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **not-enforceable** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A single portal cannot hold more than one destination; the connection slot is one readonly ZDOID.


**How it works:** Structural impossibility, not an unimplemented feature. `ZDOExtraData.s_connections` is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` — one value per ZDO — and `class ZDOConnection` declares exactly `public readonly ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType m_type;` and `public readonly ZDOID m_target = ZDOID.None;` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75524-75534). There is no list, no array, no per-type slot. `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection(zid, type, target)` (:74951-74961) overwrites that single entry.

Consequences that are easy to get wrong:
- A ZDO holding a Portal connection can never simultaneously hold a SyncTransform connection, so a portal cannot be parented to a moving object while also being routed.
- `ConnectionType` is `[Flags] { None=0, Portal=1, SyncTransform=2, Spawned=3, Target=0x10 }` (:74747-74755) — Portal/SyncTransform/Spawned are overlapping small integers, not independent bits. Only `Target` is a real flag. So you cannot OR two route types into one slot to fake two destinations.
- Writing `Portal|Target` (0x11) onto a live portal does NOT create a second slot; `ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID` requires exact type equality (:75094-75102), so `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` returns None and vanilla will treat that portal as unconnected and re-pair it in pass 2.
- TeleportWorld.Teleport reads exactly one ZDOID (:143539) with no fallback, no list, and no selection UI.

Everything the assignment calls "fan-out" must therefore be realised as one of: a **Portal Bank** (N physical portals at the hub, one destination each), a **Switchboard** (one portal, repointed between transits), or a **Carousel** (one portal, repointed on a timer). A true simultaneous one-to-many is unreachable by any ZDO write, and would require a client mod to present a destination picker — which is exactly what full TortalPortal's PortalUIManager does client-side.


**Player experience:** Nothing to experience — this shape cannot be built. The nearest server-only substitutes are: a room of six portals each labelled for a different biome (Portal Bank), or one portal in the middle of the room whose destination the player changes with an emote before stepping in (Switchboard).


**Failure modes:**
- A mod that writes a second connection onto the hub silently overwrites the first with no error, because SetConnection returns true and bumps the revision — the previous destination is simply gone.
- A mod that writes Portal|Target to try to stash a second route makes the portal read as unconnected to every client (HaveTarget :143631 and TargetFound :143640 both query bare Portal), and vanilla's pass 2 will then randomly re-pair it inside its tag group.

### 4. Directed Ring / Cycle

`topologies:Directed Ring / Cycle` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A→B→C→…→A, every member on one tag; one-way circular travel that vanilla's reconciler accepts indefinitely.


**How it works:** Encoding. N portals P0..P(N-1), all with `s_tag = T`. For each i: claim ownership, `Pi.SetConnection(Portal, P((i+1) % N).m_uid)`, ForceSendZDO. N single writes, no reciprocals.

Stability. Pass 1's predicate for Pi is evaluated against P(i+1): non-null ✓, tag == T ✓, `P(i+1).GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != ZDOID.None` ✓ (it points at P(i+2)). Every edge survives. Pass 2 finds nothing IsNone(). The ring is a fixed point of vanilla's own 5 s reconciler (:100594-100622). This is the direct consequence of the missing reciprocity check and it holds for any N ≥ 2 — note N = 2 collapses to the ordinary pair, and N = 1 becomes the Self-Loop.

Ordering under a live server. Write the whole ring in one batch inside one frame. If you write only some edges and a 5 s tick lands mid-batch, the not-yet-written members read IsNone() and pass 2 will randomly pair them inside T, after which your remaining writes are fighting an already-formed pair (which you can simply overwrite — SetConnection is unconditional). Safest is a prefix on `Game.ConnectPortals` that returns false while a managed rewrite is in flight, or just doing the batch synchronously.

Ownership. Each write must be preceded by `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` for a durable result; ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) runs every 2 s and gives ownership of any portal within a peer's active area back to that peer, so the mod either re-claims on each write or installs the Wonderland `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix guard (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313) keyed on portal prefab hash.

Do NOT reposition ring members: `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73756) so a moved portal stays filed under its creation-time sector in m_portalObjects and HandleDestroyedZDO (:76980) will fail to remove it, leaking a dead ZDO into GetPortalList() forever.


**Player experience:** Five portals named `tag:"caravan"` at Meadows/Black Forest/Swamp/Mountain/Plains outposts. A player at the Meadows portal walks in and arrives at the Black Forest one. To get back to Meadows they must go all the way round: Black Forest → Swamp → Mountain → Plains → Meadows, four more 8 s loading screens and four deliberate walk-ins (after arrival the destination portal's trigger has already been entered, so they must step out and back in, and the 2 s m_teleportCooldown must elapse — Player.TeleportTo :15315). Every portal hovers as connected and glows normally; nothing in the vanilla UI hints that the link is one-way. Players discover the direction by experiment, which is either the whole point (a pilgrimage route, a raid ingress) or a support ticket.


**Failure modes:**
- Destroying any one member breaks the ring into a chain, and a chain is unstable: the node whose target vanished has its connection nulled by pass 1, and the node pointing AT that node then sees `target.connection == None` and is also nulled by pass 1 on the following tick. The damage propagates backwards one hop per 5 s until pass 2 randomly re-pairs whatever is left. A 7-node ring degrades to random pairs within ~30 s of one portal being demolished.
- World reload destroys rings >2. ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478, read directly) writes `s_connectionsHashData[source] = {Portal, h}` then `s_connectionsHashData[target] = {Portal|Target, h}`, one slot per ZDO, iterating s_connections in dictionary order — each later edge overwrites the previous entry for a shared node. For A→B→C→A you end with A={Portal|Target,h3}, B={Portal,h2}, C={Portal,h3}. On load ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) matches C↔A by h3 and writes both directions reciprocally, and B has no matching Target so it is left unconnected and Game.instance.ConnectPortals (:76523) pairs it at random. Net: one bidirectional pair plus one wanderer.
- Mod uninstalled: whatever configuration survived the last save is re-linked reciprocally at load and then the vanilla 5 s pass leaves it alone. The ring does not come back; the world settles into ordinary pairs plus one orphan if N is odd.

**Designer citations:** Game.ConnectPortals pass 1/pass 2 (verified body) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100626 ; ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75461-75478 ; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (load-time hash relink, writes BOTH directions) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77879-77885 ; ZDOMan.LoadChunks ordering — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76515 and :76523, DirtyPortalObjects=false at :76527 ; ZDO.SetSector portal exemption — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73752-73756 ; ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76901-76926


**Open questions:**
- Exact enumeration order of s_connections during RegenerateConnectionHashData determines WHICH pair survives a reload. It is a BinarySearchDictionary/Dictionary order, effectively arbitrary. In-game: build a 3-ring, save, restart, and log which two nodes came back paired — then just re-assert unconditionally rather than trying to predict it.

- SetSector leak applies only when the reposition crosses a zone boundary (GetSectorIndex 73776 derives from m_position; HandleDestroyedZDO 76980-76984 looks up by live sector).
- 'Destination trigger already entered on arrival' is an assumption about the trigger volume extent (prefab data); needs in-game check.

- Mandatory: the re-assert postfix on Game.ConnectPortals must also clear Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals (private List<ConnectingPortals>, :99903); otherwise ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) reverts staged members at the next tick and the ring flip-flops or unravels.

Ordering advice is incomplete: the real hazard is not a tick landing mid-batch (a synchronous batch cannot be interleaved by the coroutine) but stale entries in Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals (:99903) from the previous pass 2 — ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-writes them at the start of the next tick, breaking the ring, after which pass 1 unravels the rest one hop per tick. ### 5. Bidirectional Ring — RULED OUT (twin counter-rotating rings are the substitute)

`topologies:Bidirectional Ring — RULED OUT (twin counter-rotating rings are the substitute)` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A node cannot hold both a clockwise and an anticlockwise neighbour; two portals per station is the only way to get a two-way loop.


**How it works:** A truly bidirectional ring needs each node to store two targets. It cannot: one ZDOConnection per ZDO (:75524-75534). Any second write overwrites the first.

Substitute — twin counter-rotating rings. Place TWO portals at each station, on two different tags. Station i gets portal Ci on tag `T_cw` and portal Ai on tag `T_ccw`. Write `Ci.SetConnection(Portal, C((i+1)%N).m_uid)` for the clockwise ring and `Ai.SetConnection(Portal, A((i-1+N)%N).m_uid)` for the anticlockwise ring. Both rings are independently stable for the same reason a single Directed Ring is: within each tag group every target is non-null, tag-matched and itself non-None.

Cost: 2N portals for N stations, and 2N ZDO writes per re-assert. Both rings must be re-asserted after a world reload for the same RegenerateConnectionHashData reason.

Degenerate case worth knowing: with N = 2 the twin rings collapse to two ordinary pairs between the same two stations, which is exactly what two vanilla portal pairs on two tags already give you — no mod needed.

A cheaper approximation with N+1 portals: build one Directed Ring plus a single Switchboard portal at each station that the player repoints to "previous station" on demand. That gets two-way travel with 2N portals anyway, so the twin ring is usually simpler.

Note that the two tags must be genuinely distinct strings or vanilla will merge the two rings into one 2N-member tag group and the reconciler will happily keep whatever edges you wrote (it does not care about cycles) — but any member that ever loses its connection will be re-paired across the ring boundary by pass 2's random pick (Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100679).


**Player experience:** At each of five outposts there is a pair of portals a few metres apart, one signed `caravan-e` and one signed `caravan-w`. Stepping into the east one takes you one stop clockwise; the west one takes you one stop anticlockwise. Both glow, both hover as connected. Players learn the convention from the tags, and a wrong choice costs one extra 8 s hop rather than a four-hop detour.


**Failure modes:**
- Demolishing one portal of a twin breaks only that ring's direction at that station, and the break propagates backwards one hop per 5 s exactly as in the single ring.
- A player retagging `caravan-w` to `caravan-e` merges the two groups; the retagged portal's connection is cleared by RPC_SetTag (:143595) and pass 2 can pair it with any unconnected clockwise member, producing a bridge between the two rings that will look like a routing bug.

**Designer citations:** class ZDOConnection single readonly target — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75524-75534 ; Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100664-100679 ; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag clears own connection on retag — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143595-143597


**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Inherits the Directed Ring correction: re-assert must clear Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals (SERVER:99903) after any vanilla pairing tick, including the one inside ZDOMan.LoadChunks (76523).
- TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag (143587-143601) clears only its own connection; SetConnectedPortal is invoked with ZDOID.None because GetConnectionZDOID is read after UpdateConnection(None), so the old partner is left dangling until pass 1 clears it on the next tick.
- Inherit all Directed Ring corrections: postfix on Game.ConnectPortals that rewrites BOTH rings and clears Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals (:99903); world-load re-assert happens via that postfix on the LoadChunks-time call (:76523), not at OnWorldReady.
- Enforcement for the ruled-out primary claim is not-applicable; the twin-ring substitute is server-enforced at the route level only.
- Player experience: hover shows `[$piece_portal_connected]` on both portals but nothing indicates direction (HaveTarget is connection != None, CLIENT:144381-144388); the tag string is the only in-game convention carrier.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Single-slot impossibility verified (ZDOConnection SERVER:75524-75534; SetConnection overwrite 74951-74960). Twin-ring substitute is just two Directed Rings on distinct tags; pass 1 (100601) compares tag strings so the two groups never interact unless a member goes None, in which case FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (100664-100679) only picks candidates with equal tag and None connection — so cross-ring re-pairing can only happen if the tags are identical, as stated. Cited RPC_SetTag 143595-143597 is the UpdateConnection(None) line; note the subsequent SetConnectedPortal call receives the already-cleared (None) ID, so vanilla retag never clears the partner — the partner is cleared by pass 1 next tick. Inherits every caveat of Directed Ring: save collapse, staging-list oscillation, owner-local retag, RPC_DestroyZDO.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Impossibility is structural and verified (single ZDOConnection per ZDO, :74794 and :75524-75534). The substitute is literally two Directed Rings on distinct tags and inherits every caveat of that option: save-boundary collapse to at most one reciprocal pair per ring (:75461-75478, :77850-77893), synchronous random re-pairing at LoadChunks :76523, staged-commit revert via ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) unless the private staging list is cleared, and destroy/retag cascades. The tag-merging warning is right: FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100664-100679) filters on exact tag string, so distinct tags fully isolate the two rings' pass-2 behaviour. N=2 degenerate case is correct. Enforcement label 'server-enforced' for a ruled-out shape is meaningless; the substitute's route topology is server-owned, the transit itself is client-executed. Effort 'medium' is fair. Nothing here is independently refutable beyond the inherited corrections.

### 6. Open Chain / Relay with a Terminator

`topologies:Open Chain / Relay with a Terminator` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A→B→C→…→Z as a one-way relay; the last hop MUST terminate in a self-loop, an anchor, or a wrap to the head, or vanilla unravels the whole chain backwards.


**How it works:** Encoding. Chain members P0..Pn all on tag T. `Pi.SetConnection(Portal, P(i+1).m_uid)` for i < n. The tail Pn is the whole problem.

Why a naive chain unravels. If Pn's connection is ZDOID.None, pass 1 evaluating P(n-1) hits the third clause `zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None` and nulls P(n-1) (:100601-100604). On the next tick P(n-2) sees P(n-1) as None and is nulled. The chain dissolves from the tail backwards at one hop per 5 s, and pass 2 randomly re-pairs the freed members inside T. This is the single most common way a hand-built topology quietly turns into vanilla soup.

Three legal terminators:
1. **Self-loop**: `Pn.SetConnection(Portal, Pn.m_uid)`. Pass 1 on Pn resolves the target to itself — non-null, tag equals its own tag, connection non-None — so it survives. Runtime-stable, but erased by every save (RegenerateConnectionHashData writes `hashData[Pn]={Portal,h}` and then immediately overwrites it with `{Portal|Target,h}` because m_target != None, :75472-75475, leaving a Target with no source), so re-assert at load.
2. **Wrap to head**: `Pn.SetConnection(Portal, P0.m_uid)` — this is exactly the Directed Ring and is the most robust choice.
3. **Anchor**: point Pn at a non-portal ZDO carrying the same tag and a non-None connection (see the Anchor-Terminated One-Way option). Best of the three: the anchor is never iterated by ConnectPortals because it is not in m_portalObjects, so it can never be torn down or re-paired.

All writes take the standard claim/write/force-send triad. Batch the whole chain in one frame.


**Player experience:** A five-stage descent into the Mistlands: portals tagged `descent` at (1420,-3310), (1980,-3720), (2510,-4060), (2990,-4380) and a final one at the Queen's approach (3310,-4610). The player steps into stage 1, black screen, arrives 1 m in front of stage 2, steps out of the volume, turns around, steps back in, black screen, stage 3. Each hop costs about 10 s of real time (8 s minimum distant-teleport hold plus the 2 s cooldown before the next TeleportTo is accepted, Player.UpdateTeleport :15349 and Player.TeleportTo :15315). There is no way back up the chain — walking into stage 3 sends them to stage 4, not stage 2. The final portal loops onto itself, so stepping into it after arriving gives an 8 s black screen and deposits them back where they were standing: a deliberate dead end.


**Failure modes:**
- Forgetting the terminator: silent, delayed, total. The chain looks correct for 5 s and then dissolves backwards over the following 5n seconds.
- A destroyed mid-chain member splits the chain and the upstream half unravels; the downstream half survives if its own terminator is intact.
- Arrival lands the player 1 m in front of the next portal, potentially INSIDE that portal's trigger volume. Because OnTriggerEnter is enter-only (:143672-143681) and m_teleportCooldown gates re-entry for 2 s, they do not bounce — but any design that widens the trigger or shortens the cooldown would produce an infinite relay. Do not attempt to shorten either; m_exitDistance is a compiled Inspector field with no ZDO backing (:143413).
- World reload: hash-pair matching recovers at most one bidirectional pair out of the chain and randomly re-pairs the rest.

- Does the arrival position (target + targetRot*forward*1.0 + up*1.0) actually land inside the destination portal's TeleportWorldTrigger volume? Collider geometry is Unity asset data. In-game: teleport in, do not move, wait 5 s, and see whether anything fires.

The result is a chain with a vanilla-chosen reciprocal bounce at the tail, not full dissolution.
- Re-assert must also clear Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals (SERVER:99903) after any tick in which vanilla paired chain members (including the load-time call at ZDOMan.LoadChunks 76523), else ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (100690-100698) re-imposes the vanilla pair every 5 s.
- Self-loop save erasure line range is 75470-75475 (source slot written at 75471, overwritten by the Target slot at 75474 because m_target == key).
- Anchor terminator is not exempt from the save boundary: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) emits hashData for the anchor as a source and overwrites it as Pn's target; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) then either pairs anchor↔Pn reciprocally or leaves Pn None (Dictionary order). All chain edges and all terminators need the ConnectPortals-postfix re-assert.
- Unravel cadence: within a single pass 1 the collapse advances as many hops as GetPortalList order allows (live-state predicate, :100594-100606); do not model it as strictly one hop per 5 s.
- Same staged-commit hazard as the ring: re-assert postfix must clear Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals (:99903) or ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) reverts staged members on the next tick.
- Anchor needs a Portal-type connection (any target, e.g. itself) written via ZDO.SetConnection, and its s_tag string must be byte-identical (ordinal !=, :100603); write the anchor before the chain edges so no tick sees Pn's target with None.

### 7. Self-Loop Dead End & Paired Decoy

`topologies:Self-Loop Dead End & Paired Decoy` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A portal pointing at its own ZDOID: reads as connected, glows, and teleports the player back to where they already stood.


**How it works:** Encoding. One write: `P.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); P.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, P.m_uid); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(P.m_uid);`

Why vanilla keeps it. Pass 1 resolves the target ZDOID to P itself: `zDO == null` false, `zDO.GetString(s_tag) != @string` false (a string is equal to itself), `zDO.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == ZDOID.None` false. All three clauses fail, so no teardown (:100600-100604). Pass 2 skips it because its connection is not IsNone() (:100609). A self-loop is a stable runtime fixed point.

What the client does with it. HaveTarget() is `connection != ZDOID.None` → true, so the hover reads `[$piece_portal_connected]` and Update() lerps the emission colour to m_colorTargetfound (:143511-143515). TargetFound() resolves GetZDO(P) → non-null → true, so m_target_found lights whenever a teleportable player is within m_activationRange. On transit, Teleport() reads P's own position and rotation and moves the player to `P.pos + P.rot*forward*1.0 + up*1.0` (:143542-143545) — roughly where they were already standing — via a full distantTeleport, so they eat the 8 s black screen for nothing.

Paired decoy layout. Build a room of, say, six identical portals all carrying the same visible tag. Five of them are self-loops; one is the real edge into the network. Since s_tag, the glow, and the hover string are identical across all six, a vanilla client has no way to tell them apart short of walking in. Note the six must NOT share a tag with anything else you care about, or a destroyed decoy would free a slot that pass 2 fills from the real network.

Alternative decoy that is less punishing: point the decoys at a nearby Anchor two metres behind the portal, so the player is "teleported" to the far side of the room rather than into their own footprint.


**Player experience:** Six identical black-marble portals in a vaulted hall, every one hovering `tag:"vault" [$piece_portal_connected]` and pulsing with the connected emission. The player picks one, walks in, gets the full swirl and black screen for eight seconds, and fades back in standing one metre in front of the same portal in the same hall. No message, no error, nothing in the log they can see. They try another. On the fourth try the screen fades in over the Mountains. This is a genuine puzzle/toll mechanic that a 100% vanilla client renders correctly and cannot short-circuit — the destination is only read at the instant of transit.


**Failure modes:**
- Erased by every world save. RegenerateConnectionHashData writes the source slot for P then immediately overwrites it with the Target slot because m_target != None (:75472-75475), leaving a Target hash with no matching source. On load, ZDOMan.ConnectPortals finds no pair and Game.instance.ConnectPortals then re-pairs P at random inside its tag group. MUST be re-asserted at world load.
- If the self-looped portal is the only member of its tag group it is left permanently unconnected after a reload (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal returns null for an empty candidate list, :100674-100678) — which is actually a safe failure, just not a self-loop.
- Players may report it as a bug ('the portal ate my eight seconds'). If the decoy room is not signposted in-fiction it reads as a broken server.
- Using self-loops as hub terminators leaves the hub's exit pointing at the hub — walk into the hub and you stay at the hub. Usually you want an Anchor instead.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Add: self-loops do not survive a world save. RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) collapses the single hash slot to (Portal|Target); ZDOMan.ConnectPortals on load (:77850-77891) needs an exact-Portal slot, so P reloads unconnected and Game.ConnectPortals (called from ZDOMan.Load :76658 / LoadChunks :76523) immediately pairs the freed decoys with each other. The mod must re-assert every self-loop after that call (Harmony postfix on ZDOMan.Load/LoadChunks or on the first Game.ConnectPortals), keyed on something other than ZDOID because ZDOIDs are regenerated on load (:74552).
- Add: re-assert must be idempotent against the staged two-tick commit. If vanilla staged a pair in tick t, ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-writes it at the start of tick t+1 over the mod's write; a Harmony PREFIX on Game.ConnectPortals that restores all mod edges first keeps pass 2 from ever firing.
- Citation fix: RegenerateConnectionHashData begins at :75461, not :75472-75475 (those lines are inside its body).
- Clarify enforcement scope: the route is server-owned against a vanilla client, but Game.RPC_SetConnection (:100653-100662) has no sender check and is registered on every peer (:100066), and ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO likewise; a modded client can rewrite or delete any decoy. 'Cannot short-circuit' holds for vanilla clients only.
- Player-experience nit: the first walk-in on the REAL edge can be a silent no-op if the client does not yet hold the remote target ZDO (TargetFound -> RequestZDO -> return false, :143650-143654); the decoys never have this delay because their target is P itself. An attentive player can therefore tell the real portal apart by the one that 'fails' once.
- Persistence: a self-loop is saved as (Portal|Target) and is never restored; Game.ConnectPortals runs synchronously during world load (:76523/:76658) and randomly re-pairs same-tag orphans before the mod can act. Mod must re-assert all self-loops immediately after load and periodically thereafter.
- Registry must be keyed on a mod-written persistent string key on the ZDO, not ZDOID (ZDOIDs regenerate at ZDO.Load :74552).
- Ownership claim is transient: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) reassigns P to any nearby player every 2 s; the connection value survives because nothing rewrites it, but any client can clear it via RPC_SetTag (:143587-143602) with no server veto — 'cannot short-circuit' is vanilla-client-honoured plus reactive re-assert, not a hard guarantee.
- Remove the 'destroyed decoy frees a slot' paragraph; no portal points at a decoy. Replace with: after a restart, un-reasserted decoys pair with each other and with the real edge if it is also orphaned.
- Effort is 'small' only for the write itself; the mandatory load-time re-assert + string-key registry is shared infrastructure of medium effort.
- Player.TeleportTo cooldown (client :15316) means a player can re-enter the same decoy 2 s after fading in; the 8 s wait per attempt is real (client :15352).

TeleportWorld.HaveTarget (:143631-143638) is a bare `!= ZDOID.None`, so hover shows `$piece_portal_connected` (:143461) and Update lerps to m_colorTargetfound (:143511-143515). Client side: HaveTarget (client TeleportWorld :144xxx, identical to SERVER:143631-143638) is `connection != None` -> hover reads $piece_portal_connected (SERVER:143461) and Update() lerps emission (:143511-143515); TargetFound (:143640-143656) needs only GetZDO(P) != null, which the client holds because it is standing next to P; Teleport (client :144280-144288) reads only GetPosition/GetRotation of the target and calls TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport:true); Player.UpdateTeleport (client :15352) holds the black screen until m_teleportTimer > 8f for distant teleports, so the '8 s for nothing' is real. Player.TeleportTo requires m_teleportCooldown >= 2 s (client :15316) so immediate re-entry is throttled but possible. REFUTED sub-claims: (1) 'One write' / persistence. RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) writes hashData[P]=(Portal,h) then, because target==key, overwrites hashData[P]=(Portal|Target,h). ZDO.Save stores that single slot (:74243-74249). On load, ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) only takes sources from GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(Portal) which is an exact-type match (:75414-75425), so P is never a source and its s_connections entry is never recreated -> P is an orphan. Game.instance.ConnectPortals is then called synchronously inside LoadChunks/Load (:76523, :76658) before any mod update tick, so the five 'vault' decoys are randomly paired among themselves (two real pairs + one stranded) via UnityEngine.Random.Range (:100678). The mod MUST re-assert every self-loop after every load, and ZDOIDs are regenerated on load (ZDO.Load :74552 `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`), so the registry must be keyed on a mod-written persistent ZDO string key (strings are saved), not on ZDOID. ### 8. Anchor-Terminated One-Way / Dead Drop

`topologies:Anchor-Terminated One-Way / Dead Drop` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Point a portal at a fabricated non-portal ZDO: an arrival point with no portal at it, permanently invisible to vanilla's reconciler.


**How it works:** This is the strongest primitive in the whole catalogue, because the anchor is never iterated by Game.ConnectPortals.

Create the anchor. `ZDO a = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, hash);` where `hash` is a NON-portal prefab hash (something harmless and persistent). CreateNewZDO (:76674-76692) allocates the ZDOID, sets owner to the server session and calls AddIfPortal(zdo, hash) — which returns immediately because the hash is not in Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash (:77734), so the anchor goes into the ordinary sector array, not m_portalObjects. Then replicate ZNetView.Awake's fabrication block yourself (:82613-82620), all five lines: `a.Persistent = true; a.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; a.Distant = false; a.SetPrefab(hash); a.SetRotation(facing);` — omit SetPrefab and m_prefab stays 0, the client's CreateObject returns null and the server destroys it as invalid; omit Persistent and AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) skips it and it is gone on restart.

Make it a legal target. Pass 1 evaluates the PORTAL, not the anchor, so you need the anchor to satisfy the portal's three clauses: `a.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, T)` matching the portal's tag, and `a.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, a.m_uid)` (a self-loop on the anchor) so that `a.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != ZDOID.None`. The anchor's own self-loop is never evaluated by anything, because the anchor is not in GetPortalList(). Then `P.SetConnection(Portal, a.m_uid)` and ForceSendZDO both.

Why the client accepts it. TeleportWorld.Teleport does `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connection)` and reads only GetPosition() and GetRotation() (:143539-143545). There is no prefab validation anywhere on that path. TargetFound() only needs GetZDO != null, and if the client lacks the anchor it calls RequestZDO and the server force-sends it (:143646-143654, ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO :77689-77692).

The anchor's rotation is the arrival facing and its +forward is the 1 m push direction.


**Player experience:** A portal in the Mistlands outpost tagged `drop` glows and reads connected. A player steps in, black screen, and fades in on a stone shelf at (4180, 62, -5220) in the Ashlands — an open ledge with no portal on it, no way back, and nothing to interact with. The only way home is to walk, sail, or die. A second player at the same outpost portal gets the identical one-way delivery. Because there is no portal at the destination, there is no glow, no hover text, and no ambiguity — the endpoint simply is not a portal.


**Failure modes:**
- The anchor must stay alive in ZDOMan or the link dies at the next SAVE, not just at runtime: RegenerateConnectionHashData only persists a connection when BOTH endpoint ZDOs resolve in m_objectsByID (:75468). Give the anchor Persistent = true and never destroy it.
- At world load ZDOMan.ConnectPortals re-links the hash pair RECIPROCALLY (:77879-77885), so the anchor comes back pointing at the portal instead of at itself. That is harmless in play (nobody can walk into an anchor) but it means the anchor's self-loop must be re-asserted if you rely on it as a terminator for other members.
- Never use a portal prefab hash for the anchor. AddIfPortal would register it in m_portalObjects (:77732-77750) and vanilla would iterate it, tear down its self-loop when the hash data goes stale, and re-pair it.
- The client will try to instantiate the anchor prefab when the player's active area covers it. Choose a prefab that is cheap, silent and harmless.
- ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex clamps any zone beyond roughly ±16320 m to Sector 0 (:115755-115774), the same bucket the server's pinned reference position maps to. Do not place anchors out there.

- Does a vanilla client cleanly handle a portal whose destination ZDO has a prefab it must instantiate (an anchor)? Teleport only reads pos/rot, but ZNetScene will still CreateObject for that ZDO when in range. In-game: try an anchor with a harmless real prefab (a marker piece) versus an unregistered hash and watch the client log for CreateObject failures.
- Is there a prefab in ZNetScene whose instantiation is a genuine no-op on the client? In-game: dump ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefabNames() on the server and pick one.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Replace 'the server destroys it as invalid' with: on a dedicated server ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted never runs for player-area objects because Game.FixedUpdate pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) (:100458-100466); a prefab-0 or unknown-hash anchor survives on the server (FilterZDO loads unknown prefabs with a warning, :76346-76361) but makes every nearby vanilla client spam 'Missing prefab hash' each frame (CLIENT:82225-82237). Use a real, non-interactive, persistent prefab.
- Add: cross-chunk hash desync. Each save regenerates every connection hash (GetUniqueHash :75445-75459) but only rewrites dirty files — the portal chunk when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77631), the anchor's sector chunk when its chunk is dirty (:76707-76721). A save where only one side is dirty leaves mismatched hashes on disk and the link is lost at next load. Mitigate with a Harmony prefix on ZDOMan.PrepareSave (public, :76197) calling SetDirtyPortals() and SetDirtySector(anchor), and/or re-assert topology after ZDOMan.Load's Game.ConnectPortals call (:76658).
- Prefer anchor.SetConnection(Portal, P.m_uid) (mutual) over an anchor self-loop: the self-loop's hash slot is overwritten in iteration order (:75469-75476) and may not match the portal's on reload; a mutual pair is restored identically to a vanilla pair (:77850-77891). Fan-in of several portals onto ONE anchor still collapses to a single restored pair on reload and must be re-asserted.
- ZDOIDs are regenerated on load (:74552): the mod cannot store anchor ZDOIDs across restarts; re-find anchors by a mod-written string key or by position+prefab.
- Ownership: ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) will hand the anchor to any nearby client every 2 s. Harmless for a passive prefab, but a prefab with a WearNTear/Piece component can be deconstructed by that client, and ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO has no sender check — pick a prefab with no destructible component.
- First walk-in may be a silent no-op if the anchor ZDO has not yet arrived (Teleport :143519-143522 -> TargetFound -> RequestZDO :143650-143654). Pre-push with ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(peer, anchor) (:77714-77725) when a player approaches the portal.
- Do not self-loop the anchor. Write A.SetConnection(Portal, P.m_uid) (mutual pair) so the link survives world save/load regardless of dictionary enumeration order in RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) — the self-loop variant is lost on load whenever A is enumerated after P.
- Set a.Persistent = true BEFORE any revision-incrementing write (SetPrefab, SetRotation, Set). ZDO.Initialize's AddToSector (:73496-73504 -> :76722-76729) and SetDirtySector (:76696-76702) both skip the dirty-chunk mark while Persistent is false, and only dirty chunks are saved (:77556-77559).
- Anchor prefab hash must exist in the vanilla client's ZNetScene; otherwise the client logs 'Missing prefab hash' every frame while nearby (client ZNetScene.CreateObject :82233). The ZDO is NOT destroyed by the client (destroy branch is IsServer-only, client :82364-82370).
- A real-prefab anchor is destroyable by any client (RPC_DestroyZDO :76953-76961, no ownership/ward check); hook ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed (:76976) and recreate, and expect pass 1 to orphan P within 5 s in between.
- 'Never reconciled' applies only to Game.ConnectPortals; load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) does process the anchor's saved hash slot.
- Add a targeted ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(peerID, anchorID) (:77714-77725) when a player nears the portal; TargetFound returns false silently until the client holds the anchor (:143640-143656).
- Effort medium is right; add registry-by-string-key + load-time re-verify, as ZDOIDs regenerate (:74552).

Player.UpdateTeleport then loads the destination zone itself (IsAreaReady/FindFloor, CLIENT:15351-15375), so no GameObject is needed at the anchor. The ZNetView.Awake fabrication lines (:82613-82620) are correctly quoted. Three claims are wrong or incomplete. (1) 'the server destroys it as invalid' if SetPrefab is omitted: that branch (ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted, CLIENT:82357-82363) only runs for objects within the server's own active area, and Game.FixedUpdate pins the dedicated server's reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) (:100458-100466), so it never fires; the real failure is the client logging 'Missing prefab hash' every frame the anchor is in range (CLIENT:82225-82237) — still a reason to use a real prefab. Unknown-prefab ZDOs are loaded with a warning, not dropped (ZDOMan.FilterZDO :76346-76361). (2) Save/reload: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) gives the anchor a (Portal|Target,h) slot and the portal a (Portal,h) slot; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals on load (:77850-77891) matches them and then writes BOTH directions, so after a reload the anchor's connection becomes `portal`, not its self-loop — harmless, but note the anchor's own self-loop is itself subject to the single-slot overwrite: if s_connections iterates the anchor after the portal, the anchor's slot ends up (Portal|Target,h_anchor) != h_portal and the link is lost. Writing the anchor as a mutual partner (anchor.SetConnection(Portal, P.m_uid)) instead of a self-loop makes the pair order-independent, exactly like a vanilla pair. (3) Incremental chunked saves: portals are written only when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77631) and ordinary sectors only when their chunk is dirty (SetDirtyChunks :76707-76721), while GetUniqueHash generates fresh hashes on every save (:75445-75459). If one file is rewritten and the other is not, the on-disk hashes desync and the link is silently dropped at next load, followed by Game.ConnectPortals pairing the orphaned portal with any same-tag orphan. Vanilla never hits this because both ends of a real pair live in the same portal chunk file.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism holds. CreateNewZDO (:76674-76692) -> ZDOPool.Create -> ZDO.Initialize (:73496-73504) adds the ZDO to m_objectsBySector, so it is sector-synced and saved; AddIfPortal (:77732-77736) returns early for a non-portal hash, so it never enters m_portalObjects and GetPortalList (:77648-77656) never enumerates it; Game.ConnectPortals therefore never evaluates it. Pass 1 on P needs the anchor to carry s_tag == P's tag and a non-None Portal-type connection (:75094-75102 GetConnectionZDOID requires matching type) — correctly described. Client TeleportWorld.Teleport (client :144280-144288) reads only GetPosition/GetRotation, no prefab check; TargetFound -> RequestZDO -> server RPC_RequestZDO -> peer ForceSendZDO (:77684-77692) is real. FilterZDO on load keeps unknown prefabs ('Will load anyway', :76346-76370). Client never destroys an unknown-prefab ZDO (CreateObjectsSorted destroy branch is IsServer-only, client :82364-82370) but logs 'Missing prefab hash' every frame while the ZDO is in the near area (client :82233). CORRECTIONS: (1) Save-order hazard with the anchor self-loop. RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) iterates s_connections: entry P->A writes hashData[P]=(Portal,h1), hashData[A]=(Portal|Target,h1); entry A->A writes hashData[A]=(Portal,h2) then overwrites to (Portal|Target,h2). If A is enumerated after P, hashData[A] carries h2 != h1 and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) finds no partner for P -> P loads as an orphan and Game.ConnectPortals (:76523) pairs it at random with any same-tag orphan. Dictionary enumeration order is not guaranteed after removals. Fix: make the anchor point BACK at P (A->P) instead of at itself; then both entries share the pair and whichever is enumerated last becomes the source with the other as Target under the same hash, so the P<->A link is restored deterministically on every load. Pass 1 on P is still satisfied (A.connection = P != None). (2) Fabrication ordering: ZDO.Initialize calls AddToSector while Persistent is still false, so SetDirtyChunks is skipped (:76722-76729); the chunk only becomes dirty via IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector (:73832-73840, :76696-76702) which also checks Persistent. `a.Persistent = true` must precede SetPrefab/SetRotation/Set(s_tag) or the anchor is not written to disk (AddObjectsPerChunk only saves dirty chunks :77556-77559). (3) 'Harmless prefab' must be a hash the vanilla client has in ZNetScene, otherwise per-frame warning spam; a real prefab is a real object at the arrival point that any client can destroy (ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO :76953-76961 has no checks), after which pass 1 tears P down within 5 s and pass 2 re-pairs it with any same-tag orphan. Subscribe to m_onZDODestroyed (:76976) and recreate. (4) 'Permanently invisible to vanilla's reconciler' is true for Game.ConnectPortals but NOT for load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals, which reads hash data for every ZDO regardless of prefab (that is exactly what makes the mutual variant survive saves). (5) First walk-in may silently fail if the client does not yet hold the anchor (TargetFound returns false after RequestZDO); in practice UpdatePortal polls TargetFound every 0.5 s while a teleportable player is within 5 m (:143490-143509) so it is usually resolved before entry, but a targeted ForceSendZDO(peer, anchor) when the player approaches is the robust fix. (6) Mod uninstall leaves anchor ZDOs in the world forever (persistent, never cleaned).

### 9. Directed In-Tree (local → regional → world hub)

`topologies:Directed In-Tree (local → regional → world hub)` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A tiered fan-in: every leaf points at its local hub, every local hub at its regional hub, the regional hubs at the world hub. Travel is inward only; outward needs banks.


**How it works:** Encoding. One tag T for the entire tree — every node from leaf to root must carry the identical s_tag string, because pass 1 tears down any edge whose two ends disagree (:100601). Write one edge per node: `leaf.SetConnection(Portal, localHub.m_uid)`, `localHub.SetConnection(Portal, regionalHub.m_uid)`, `regionalHub.SetConnection(Portal, worldHub.m_uid)`, and finally `worldHub.SetConnection(Portal, <anchor or designated return>)`.

Stability. Identical argument to the Fan-In Star, applied recursively: each node's target is non-null, tag-matched and itself non-None. Every internal edge survives pass 1 and pass 2 never fires. The only node that needs care is the ROOT, whose own connection must be non-None or the entire tree unravels level by level at one level per 5 s.

The crucial asymmetry. A tree edge in a graph is undirected; a portal edge is not. Because a ZDO holds one ZDOID, a hub CANNOT simultaneously point at its children. So the "tree" you can build is strictly an in-tree — all arrows toward the root. Travel is one hop per walk-in: leaf → local hub (8 s), then walk into a DIFFERENT portal at the local hub to continue. If the local hub portal itself points at the regional hub, walking into the same portal you arrived at continues inward. That produces a genuinely nice "express line" feel: keep stepping into the portal in front of you and you ratchet inward to the world hub.

Outward travel requires a Portal Bank at each hub: at the world hub, one portal per regional hub; at each regional hub, one portal per local hub; at each local hub, one portal per leaf. Those bank portals need their own tags (one tag per bank slot, paired with an anchor or with a dedicated arrival portal at the child site). Total portal count for a 3-tier tree with branching factor b: inward edges N, outward bank portals N, so 2N.

Tick rate: none. Write once, re-assert on member destruction and on world load.


**Player experience:** A player at a Plains farmstead walks into the farmstead portal (`tag:"realm"`). Eight seconds later they are at the Plains regional waystation, standing in front of the portal they arrived from. They step out, step back in, and eight seconds later they are in the world hub's arrival hall. Total: two walk-ins, ~20 s, and they have crossed the map. To go home they cross the hall to the departures colonnade — twelve portals, one per waystation, each signed with its region — step into `realm-plains`, arrive at the Plains waystation departures rack, step into `realm-plains-farm`, and they are home. Inbound is one express line with no choices; outbound is a wayfinding exercise through two labelled racks.


**Failure modes:**
- The root's connection is the single point of failure for the whole tree. Point it at an Anchor, never at a player-destructible portal.
- All nodes share one tag string, so a player retagging any single portal removes it from the tree; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag also clears that portal's own connection (:143595), and the node that pointed AT it is then torn down by pass 1 on the next tick. A tiered network needs a tag-normalisation tick (re-assert s_tag on every managed portal) or the Displaced Routing option.
- Because every tier shares one tag, hover text is identical everywhere. Players cannot tell a leaf from the world hub without external signage. Signs (ZDOVars.s_text, server-writable) are the practical mitigation.
- World reload flattens the whole tree into pairs. Mandatory re-assert.

**Designer citations:** Game.ConnectPortals tag-equality teardown — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100601 ; Game.ConnectPortals pass 2 IsNone guard — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100609 ; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag clears connection then writes tag — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143587-143602 ; ZDOVars.s_text (server-writable sign text) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78629


**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Reword 'Tick rate: none': the tree must be re-asserted (a) after ZDOMan.Load/LoadChunks calls Game.instance.ConnectPortals() (:76658/:76523), because the single-slot hash format (:75461-75478) reduces the tree to a random pairwise matching on reload and pass 2 then re-pairs orphans at random within the shared tag; and (b) every tick, ideally as a Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals (:100589), so a player retag (RPC_SetTag -> SetConnectedPortal nulls the parent hub, :143587-143618) never reaches pass 1 as a None connection.
- Registry cannot be ZDOID-keyed across restarts (ZDO.Load :74552 regenerates every m_uid); identify nodes by a mod-written string key on the ZDO or by position+prefab.
- 'One level per 5 s' is an upper bound: pass 1 mutates in place while iterating one flat list (:100594-100606), so descendants evaluated after their parent collapse in the same tick.
- The root terminator, if an Anchor, inherits the Anchor option's cross-chunk hash-desync caveat (portal chunk vs ordinary chunk, :77621-77631 / :76707-76721).
- Enforcement scope: server-owned route against vanilla clients; Game.RPC_SetConnection (:100653-100662, registered on every peer :100066) and RPC_DestroyZDO have no sender checks, so a modded client can rewrite any edge.
- Replace 'Write once' with: rebuild the entire tree on every world load (Game.ConnectPortals runs synchronously inside ZDOMan.Load/LoadChunks at :76523/:76658 and randomly pairs the collapsed nodes) and re-assert on a periodic tick.
- State the save-boundary behaviour explicitly: each ZDO saves one connection slot (:75461-75478, :74243-74249); a fan-in of b children onto a hub survives as at most one child<->hub pair, order-dependent.
- Registry must be keyed on a mod-written string key per portal, not ZDOID (ZDO.Load :74552 regenerates IDs).
- Use a mutual root<->anchor link rather than an anchor self-loop so the root terminator survives saves (see Anchor verdict).
- Note that a single realm-wide tag T makes any player-built portal tagged T a pass-2 candidate during transient orphan windows; the mod should either use a hard-to-guess tag or police foreign T-tagged portals.
- Enforcement is server-owned for the route field but any client can clear a node via RPC_SetTag with zero packets (:143587-143602); protection is reactive re-assert only.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Runtime stability verified against the pass-1 predicate (:100600-100604): for every node, its target is non-null, carries the same tag, and has a non-None connection, so no edge is torn down; pass 2 (:100609) never fires because no node is None. The reciprocity gap (no check that target points back) is real. The 'walk back into the arrival portal to continue inward' mechanic is consistent with Teleport placing the player 1 m in front of the destination portal (:143543-143545) and Player.TeleportTo's 2 s cooldown (CLIENT:15315). The option's own text says 'Tick rate: none. Write once, re-assert on member destruction and on world load' — but understates what 'on world load' means. RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) stores ONE hash slot per ZDO: a hub with k children and its own outbound edge has its slot written k+1 times and only the last write survives, so on reload ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77891) restores at most a pairwise matching, and because Game.instance.ConnectPortals() runs inside ZDOMan.Load/LoadChunks (:76658, :76523) before the mod's coroutines, pass 2 immediately pairs the orphaned nodes RANDOMLY among themselves (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100679, Random.Range) — and every node shares one tag, so the whole tree is scrambled, not merely dropped. Re-assertion must run after that call and cannot use stored ZDOIDs (regenerated at :74552). Second gap: the 'unravels one level per 5 s' claim is only an upper bound — pass 1 iterates a single flat list and writes SetConnection(None) in place, so a child evaluated after its parent in the same foreach is torn down in the same tick. Third gap: any player retagging ANY node runs TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag on the owning client (:143587-143602), which nulls that node's connection and calls SetConnectedPortal on its target (:143604-143618) — claiming ownership and nulling the PARENT hub's connection (or RPC_SetConnected to its owner, :143620-143628). Next pass 1 then tears down every sibling pointing at that hub. Without a per-tick re-assert running BEFORE pass 1 (Harmony prefix on the public Game.ConnectPortals :100589) a single retag transiently collapses a whole branch. PrivateArea.CheckAccess in Interact (:143473) is client-side and a vanilla client honours wards, which limits but does not prevent this.
- [vanilla-reality:downgraded] Runtime topology claim is correct: pass 1 (:100595-100605) only tests that each node's target is non-null, same-tag and non-None, never reciprocity, so leaf->localHub->regionalHub->worldHub->anchor is a runtime fixed point, and the root must be non-None (:100605 tears down any node whose target has None, cascading one level per 5 s tick). ### 10. Nested / Layered Airlock (vestibule pattern)

`topologies:Nested / Layered Airlock (vestibule pattern)` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


An outer portal drops you into a sealed vestibule containing the real network's portals; the vestibule is the only ingress and the mod controls what is inside it.


**How it works:** Encoding is a composition of two independent tag groups that never touch.

Outer layer: portals O1..On out in the world, all on tag `T_out`, each written `Oi.SetConnection(Portal, V_in.m_uid)` where V_in is a single arrival portal inside the vestibule room. V_in carries `s_tag = T_out` and points at an Anchor placed at the vestibule floor (so V_in satisfies pass 1 and stepping into V_in is a no-op that dumps you back in the vestibule). This is a Fan-In Star with an anchor terminator, and it is vanilla-stable.

Inner layer: inside the vestibule, a Portal Bank B1..Bm on tags `T_in_1`..`T_in_m`, each paired with a remote portal at the corresponding destination. These are ordinary pairs — vanilla maintains them for free.

The nesting property is that the two layers share no tag, so vanilla's reconciler can never bridge them: FindRandomUnconnectedPortal only considers candidates whose s_tag is string-equal to the orphan's (:100669). An outer portal that loses its connection can only be re-paired with another outer portal, never with an inner one. That containment is the whole point — it is the closest thing the ZDO layer offers to an access-control boundary.

Deeper nesting is just recursion: the vestibule's bank leads to sub-vestibules, each with its own tag namespace. Depth is unbounded; cost is one physical portal per edge.

The mod's leverage inside the vestibule: it can null a bank portal's connection to close a wing (`Bk.SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)`), but must also break Bk's tag or pass 2 re-pairs it within 5 s — see Tag-Scramble Lockdown. Alternatively repoint Bk at a jail Anchor (Black-Hole Sink) which is stable and needs no tag surgery.


**Player experience:** Every outpost portal in the realm is signed `gate`. They all lead to one round stone chamber lit by four braziers, with no exit door and a single portal on the far wall (also `gate`) that does nothing useful if you step into it. Ringing the chamber are eight portals: `gate-mead`, `gate-forest`, `gate-swamp`, `gate-mtn`, `gate-plains`, `gate-mist`, `gate-ash`, `gate-deep`. A player from the Swamp outpost arrives in the chamber, reads the ring, steps into `gate-mtn`, and eight seconds later is at the Mountain waystation. When the admin closes the Ashlands during an event, `gate-ash` stops glowing and hovers `[$piece_portal_unconnected]` — visibly shut, not mysteriously broken.


**Failure modes:**
- A player building their OWN portal and naming it `gate` joins the outer star's tag group; if its connection is None, pass 2 will pair it with… nothing, because every legitimate outer member already has a non-None connection. It sits unconnected. But if the mod's re-assert tick blindly enumerates tag `gate` it may adopt the intruder. Filter managed membership by a mod-private ZDO key or by position, not by tag alone.
- Destroying V_in strands the whole outer star (all N outer portals get nulled, then randomly re-paired with each other, producing an outpost-to-outpost mesh nobody designed). Protect V_in: it should be out of reach, and the mod should re-provision it from ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed.
- The vestibule is not a security boundary against a modified client — a hacked client can invoke Game's routed `RPC_SetConnection` (registered on every peer at Game.Start :100066-100070, handler :100653-100662, zero sender validation) and rewire any portal to any ZDO. Server-side detection is a per-tick connection audit.
