### 11. Portal Bank / Departures Hall (the mesh approximation)

`topologies:Portal Bank / Departures Hall (the mesh approximation)` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


N physical portals side by side, each a plain vanilla pair to a different fixed destination — the only way to give one place many exits.


**How it works:** Encoding is deliberately boring: N ordinary pairs. Bank slot k gets `s_tag = T_k` (a distinct string per slot) and its remote twin gets the same T_k; write the mutual connection on each pair or simply let vanilla's pass 2 form it (two same-tag unconnected portals pair on the next 5 s tick with no mod involvement at all).

What the mod adds over doing nothing: (a) provisioning — CreateNewZDO a portal-prefab ZDO at a surveyed coordinate with the five ZNetView.Awake lines (:82613-82620) so admins do not have to hand-place; (b) tag ownership — re-asserting T_k every tick so a player cannot retag a bank slot and hijack it; (c) labelling — writing adjacent Sign ZDOs' s_tag/s_text; (d) detecting a slot's twin being destroyed and repointing that slot at a "temporarily closed" Anchor instead of letting vanilla pair it with something random.

Bank as a mesh approximation. A full mesh over S sites needs every site to reach every other. With banks that is S×(S−1) portals total (each site holds S−1 outbound slots) — quadratic but perfectly stable and entirely vanilla. A hub-and-bank hybrid is linear: each site gets ONE outbound portal into a Fan-In Star at the hub, and the hub holds one bank slot per site for the return. Total 2S portals for full any-to-any reachability in two hops. That hybrid is the recommended real-world shape.

Do NOT try to save portals by giving two bank slots the same tag: three same-tag portals strand one permanently, and four form two pairs by dictionary-bucket order that is not stable across restarts.


**Player experience:** A long timber colonnade behind the great hall with fourteen portals in a row, each with a rune sign above it: Haldor, Bonemass, the Elder, Moder's altar, the north dock, the iron mine, the copper camp, and so on. Every portal glows and hovers with its own distinct tag. The player walks the line, reads the signs, picks `hall-haldor`, steps in, and eight seconds later is standing at the trader's fire next to the return portal which is also tagged `hall-haldor`. Stepping back into it brings them home. This is the shape players already expect from vanilla — the mod's contribution is that nobody can accidentally retag `hall-haldor` into `hall` and swap two destinations, and a demolished twin shows as `[$piece_portal_unconnected]` instead of silently re-pairing with the copper camp.


**Failure modes:**
- Full mesh is quadratic. 20 sites = 380 portals = 380 ZDOs in m_portalObjects, all resident in server RAM permanently (portals are never released — ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS only reassigns ownership, :76872-76883) and all flattened into a fresh List<ZDO> on every GetPortalList() call, i.e. every 5 s. Measurable but not alarming; cache the list if you poll faster.
- A destroyed twin leaves the local slot unconnected and, because its tag is unique, FindRandomUnconnectedPortal returns null and it stays unconnected forever — a safe, honest failure that the hover text reports.
- If an admin reuses a tag string across two banks, the four portals form two pairs by dictionary order and the mapping silently reshuffles on the next server restart.
- Any mass re-tag or mass re-link across a large bank must be throttled: every ZDO.SetConnection bumps DataRevision and ForceSendZDO pushes to every peer. Wonderland's StructureUpkeep caps routed broadcasts at 256 per sweep for exactly this reason.

**Designer citations:** Game.ConnectPortals pass 2 auto-pairing of two same-tag unconnected portals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100607-100622 ; Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (null for empty candidate list) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100664-100679 ; ZDOMan.GetPortalList (fresh List every call) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648-77656 ; ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS (never removes ZDOs) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76872-76883 ; ZNetView.Awake fabrication block for provisioning — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82613-82620


**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Replace 'dictionary-bucket order' with: FindRandomUnconnectedPortal selects via UnityEngine.Random.Range (:100678); with 3+ same-tag portals the pairing is random on every reconciliation, and the leftover orphan changes whenever any pair is disturbed.
- Retag protection is reactive, not preventive: TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag runs on the owner client with no server hook (:143587-143602) and also nulls the twin via SetConnectedPortal/RPC_SetConnected (:143604-143628). The mod detects the s_tag change and rewrites tag and BOTH connections; run the rewrite as a Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals (:100589) so pass 2 cannot re-pair the retagged slot first.
- Drop or re-purpose the ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS citation (:76872-76883): it only reassigns ownership every 2 s.
- Provisioning order: set Persistent = true before SetPrefab/SetRotation (IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector checks Persistent, :73838-73841 / :76694-76699); prefab hash must be one of Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash (:100021, :100029) or the ZDO is not a portal to vanilla at all.
- Slot registry must survive ZDOID regeneration on load (:74552): key on tag string (unique per slot) or position, not m_uid.
- Enforcement scope: routes are server-owned against vanilla clients; Game.RPC_SetConnection (:100066, :100653-100662) and RPC_DestroyZDO have no sender checks.

- Anti-retag is reactive-detection-only: RPC_SetTag runs on the owning client with no server hook (:143587-143602); the mod reverts after the fact. A tag-only restore must call ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702) or it is lost at the next save.
- Provisioned portals are real client-side pieces; the server cannot do collider ground checks. Placement must use WorldGenerator height math and support/decay behaviour needs an in-game check.
- 'temporarily closed' anchor must carry the slot's tag and a non-None connection or pass 1 tears the slot down (:100603-100605); prefer a mutual slot<->anchor link for save stability.

In the window, pass 1 orphans the twin (:100605) and pass 2 can pair the twin with any same-tag orphan. Tag-only restores must call ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702) because ZDO.Set(string) does not mark the portal chunk dirty (only SetConnection does, :73656-73666). (3) Provisioned portal ZDOs are instantiated by vanilla clients as real pieces; ground/support is client-side physics that the server cannot evaluate (server ref pos pinned), so placement height must come from WorldGenerator math and whether an unsupported portal_wood decays under WearNTear needs an in-game check. (4) Sign labelling via s_text (:78629) is read by the client Sign component (client :142584-142590) — fine, but Sign also writes s_author back from the client (client :142590) so the mod should expect churn on that key. (5) Detecting a destroyed twin: m_onZDODestroyed (:76976) fires for local and remote destroys; repointing the slot at a 'closed' anchor requires the anchor to carry the slot's tag and a non-None connection (pass 1 :100603-100605).

### 12. Switchboard (one physical portal repointed on demand)

`topologies:Switchboard (one physical portal repointed on demand)` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A single hub portal whose destination the player selects via emote or map ping; the server rewrites one ZDOID and the very next transit uses it.


**How it works:** Encoding. Hub H and destinations D1..Dn all on one tag T. Every Di points at H (a Fan-In Star, so all inbound legs are permanently stable). H points at whichever Dk is currently selected.

The repoint is three lines: `H.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); H.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, Dk.m_uid); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(H.m_uid);` — plus `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, Dk.m_uid)` targeted at the requesting player, because TargetFound() (:143640-143654) requires that client to actually HOLD the destination ZDO; if it does not, the first walk-through calls RequestZDO and returns false with no message at all.

Why the repoint survives reconciliation. After the switch, pass 1 on H tests Dk: non-null ✓, tag == T ✓, Dk.connection == H ≠ None ✓ → survives. Pass 1 on the PREVIOUS destination Dj tests H: H.connection == Dk ≠ None ✓ → Dj's inbound leg is untouched. So flipping the hub's outbound never disturbs any inbound leg. Verified directly against the pass-1 body at :100594-100606. No Harmony patch, no faster tick.

Latency. TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` at the instant of transit (:143539) — nothing is cached — so a repoint applies to the very next walk-in. The 0.5 s UpdatePortal InvokeRepeating only drives the glow (:143491-143509), not routing.

Input channel. A vanilla client has exactly two reliable ways to tell the server anything: an emote (poll ZDOVars.s_emoteID / s_emote on the character ZDO, Wonderland's EmoteSignals pattern) or a map ping, which is `Chat.SendPing` → routed `"ChatMessage"` at targetPeerID 0 carrying the clicked world Vector3 (:42058-42068) and therefore always reaches the server even with one player online. Ping is the better fit: middle-click the map at a destination, server picks the nearest managed portal to that coordinate and repoints the hub. Confirm with PlayerNotify.Toast.

Single-writer caveat: the hub has ONE connection globally. Two players selecting different destinations within a few seconds of each other will fight. Serialise with a short per-hub lock (≈15 s) and toast the loser.


**Player experience:** One portal in the great hall, signed `gate`. The player opens the map, middle-clicks the Mountain waystation, and a moment later gets a top-left toast: `Gate set: Mountain Waystation`. They walk into the portal, eight seconds of swirl, and step out at the waystation. Another player who middle-clicks the Swamp while the first is mid-transit gets `Gate busy — try again in 12s`. Every waystation portal in the realm is also signed `gate` and always leads back to the hall, so the return trip never needs a selection. The hub portal's glow and hover text never change; only where it goes changes.


**Failure modes:**
- First transit after a repoint to a never-visited region silently fails: TargetFound returns false at gate 1 and Teleport returns WITHOUT calling player.Message (:143519-143522). No error, no message, nothing. Always pre-push the destination ZDO with the targeted ForceSendZDO(peerID, id) overload before toasting success.
- Map pings are public — Chat.SendPing broadcasts to every peer, so everyone sees the requesting player's ping marker and a 5 s map pin. It is also trivially spammable; debounce per player.
- Ownership churn: ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926, every 2 s) hands the hub's ZDO to whichever player is standing next to it, so the server's SetOwner claim is transient. The connection VALUE survives (it was already ForceSendZDO'd) but the next repoint must re-claim. For heavy use, install the Wonderland ZDO.SetOwner prefix guard (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313) filtered on portal prefab hash, and allow uid==0 and uid==GetSessionID() through.
- A player already standing inside the hub's trigger when the repoint lands will NOT re-trigger — OnTriggerEnter is enter-only (:143672-143681). They must step out and back in. This is the real constraint on switchboard responsiveness, not the 0.5 s glow poll.
- A hacked client can repoint the hub itself via the unauthenticated routed RPC_SetConnection (:100653-100662). Audit the hub's connection every tick and revert.

### 13. Carousel (auto-rotating hub destination)

`topologies:Carousel (auto-rotating hub destination)` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


One portal whose destination the server cycles on a timer — a lottery, not a route.


**How it works:** Mechanically identical to the Switchboard minus the player input: a timer in the subsystem's OnUpdate writes `H.SetConnection(Portal, D[(k++) % n].m_uid)` + ForceSendZDO every P seconds. All Di point at H so the inbound legs are stable, and pass 1 never objects for the same reason as the Switchboard.

The reason this is caveated rather than recommended: the destination is resolved at the instant of transit (:143539), not at the instant the player decides to walk in. If the carousel period is short relative to the player's approach, the destination they saw advertised (on a sign, in a toast) is not the one they get. There is no way to latch the destination to the player, because there is one connection slot and it is global. The honest framings are:
- Long period (≥5 minutes) with a server-written Sign next to the portal naming the current destination (write ZDOVars.s_text; Sign.UpdateText repaints on a 2 s InvokeRepeating when the ZDO DataRevision changes). Then the advertised destination is accurate for practically the whole period.
- Short period as a deliberate randomiser — a "wild gate" that drops you somewhere unpredictable.

One useful hardening: pause the rotation whenever any connected character's ZDO position is within ~8 m of the hub (poll ConnectedCharacters + ZDO.GetPosition, or ZdoSpatialQuery), so the destination cannot flip under someone's feet. That converts the worst race into a bounded one.

Per-tick cost is one ZDO write plus one ForceSendZDO broadcast. Because ZDOExtraData.SetConnection returns false for an unchanged value (:74954-74957), re-asserting the same destination is free; only real changes generate traffic.


**Player experience:** A weathered portal at the crossroads signed `wildgate`, with a rune stone beside it that reads `Currently: the Sunken Crypt at Swamp North`. Every ten minutes the stone's text changes and the gate leads somewhere else. A player who reads the stone and steps in within the next nine minutes gets what it promised. A player who reads it, wanders off to fight a troll, and comes back eleven minutes later gets the Mountain cave instead, with no warning — the gate looked identical the whole time. If the admin sets the period to 30 seconds instead, the gate becomes a genuine lottery and players treat it as one.


**Failure modes:**
- Destination-at-transit race: unavoidable and structural. The player cannot reserve a destination and the server cannot hold one per player.
- If the rotation lands on a destination the player's client does not hold, their first walk-in silently no-ops (gate 1 at :143519 returns without a message). Broadcast ForceSendZDO(newTarget) to all peers on each rotation, or accept occasional silent failures.
- A rotation that fires while a player is mid-teleport is harmless — Teleport() already captured the position and Player.UpdateTeleport pins m_teleportTargetPos (:15343).
- Very short periods generate a ZDO write plus a full-broadcast ForceSendZDO every period; at 1 s with many carousels this becomes real traffic since ZDOMan.SendZDOs re-serialises the entire ZDO with no delta encoding (:77053-77062).

**Designer citations:** TeleportWorld.Teleport resolves destination at transit — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143539 ; ZDOExtraData.SetConnection no-op on unchanged value — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74954-74957 ; Player.UpdateTeleport pins m_teleportTargetPos — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15343 ; ZDOVars.s_text — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78629 ; ZDOMan.SendZDOs (no delta encoding) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77053-77062


**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Add: the star does not survive a world save — at most one Di<->H link is restored (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461-75478 single hash slot per ZDO; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals :77850-77890), and Game.instance.ConnectPortals() inside ZDOMan.LoadChunks (:76523) re-rolls the remaining same-tag Di into random pairs before the mod runs; the mod must re-assert the star on its first tick, keyed by position (ZDOIDs renumber, ZDO.Load :74552).
- Add: after each rotation, a client at H that has not yet received D[k]'s ZDO sees TargetFound()==false -> RequestZDO (:143649-143655); glow off and walking in is a silent no-op until the ZDO arrives; pre-send D[k] to nearby peers before flipping.
- Sign write: leave s_author empty (or the sign is only viewable if the author id resolves); Sign.UpdateViewPermission grants on PlatformUserID.None (CLIENT:142612-142620).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Runtime mechanism holds. Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 (SERVER:100600-100604) tests only target!=null, tag equality and target.connection!=None — never reciprocity — so H->D[k] plus every Di->H is stable and pass 2 (:100607-100622) finds nothing None. Destination is resolved on the client at the instant of transit (TeleportWorld.Teleport :143537-143545 reads GetConnectionZDOID then Player.TeleportTo pins m_teleportTargetPos; UpdateTeleport :15330-15380 then only uses the pinned target), so the race described is real. ZDOExtraData.SetConnection returns false on unchanged value (:74954-74961), so re-asserting is free. Sign repaint is real: client Sign.Awake InvokeRepeating("UpdateText",2f,2f) (CLIENT:142519), UpdateText re-reads s_text when DataRevision changes, and an empty s_author yields PlatformUserID.None -> Granted -> text shown (CLIENT:142619). ### 14. Invisible Tag Sharding via rich-text-stripped suffix

`topologies:Invisible Tag Sharding via rich-text-stripped suffix` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Append `<x>` to a portal's tag: vanilla's hover strips it from display but the reconciler still compares the full string, so two portals that look identically named refuse to pair.


**How it works:** The mechanism is a genuine asymmetry between what routes and what displays, and both halves are verified in code.

Routes on the RAW string. Game.ConnectPortals compares `item.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` with bare `string !=` (:100601) and FindRandomUnconnectedPortal filters on `portal.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) != tag` (:100669). No trimming, no normalisation, no stripping.

Displays a STRIPPED string. TeleportWorld.GetHoverText does `text = tagInfo.text.RemoveRichTextTags()` (:143459), and RemoveRichTextTags is `Regex.Replace(text, "<[\\/a-zA-Z0-9= \"\\\"''#;:()$_-]*?>", string.Empty)` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703 — read directly). The character class covers letters, digits, `/`, `=`, space, quotes, `#`, `;`, `:`, `(`, `)`, `$`, `_`, `-`. So `<a>`, `<p17>`, `<f:red>`, `<s_2>` are all stripped.

Therefore: `s_tag = "base<f:red>"` hovers as `base` on every vanilla client but is a different routing namespace from `"base"` and from `"base<f:blue>"`.

Uses. (a) Per-faction or per-player namespaces that players never see. (b) Shard isolation across a large server. (c) Per-portal uniquification for a server-enforced lockdown (see Tag-Scramble Lockdown) where every portal gets `<p{n}>` and nothing can pair, while the hover text is unchanged. (d) Preventing a visitor's identically-named portal from joining a managed network.

Budget. TeleportWorld.Interact calls `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (:143482) and TextInput.Show assigns `m_inputField.characterLimit = charLimit` then `m_inputField.text = text` (:61515-61521). Ten characters total including the suffix if a player is ever to retype it. Keep display names ≤ 5 chars, or accept that the mod must re-apply the suffix after every player retag. RPC_SetTag itself applies no cap (:143587-143602) so the SERVER can write any length.

Alternative carrier: a zero-width space (U+200B). Invisible in both the hover and the edit field, one char of budget, and not touched by the regex. Less provable from code than the `<>` form, so verify in-game.


**Player experience:** Two guilds each build a portal they both call `home`. Guild A's portals carry `home<a>` and Guild B's carry `home<b>`, written by the server on placement based on the piece's ZDOVars.s_creator. Both guilds hover their portals and read exactly `Teleport tag:"home" [$piece_portal_connected]`. A guild-A member who walks into their `home` portal always arrives at guild A's hall, never guild B's, and no amount of retyping the tag will cross the boundary because the server re-applies the suffix within a second. From the players' side it simply looks as though portals only connect to their own guild's — which is exactly the feature.


**Failure modes:**
- A player who opens the tag dialog sees the RAW tag in the edit field, including the suffix, because TextInput.RequestText pre-fills with sign.GetText() = GetTagInfo().text = the raw s_tag (:143551-143554, :143556-143570). It is hidden in hover, not in the editor.
- 10-character budget in the client editor. Whether GuiInputField clamps a programmatically assigned .text longer than characterLimit is a Unity behaviour question — if it does, a player opening and confirming the dialog on a server-written long tag saves back a TRUNCATED tag, silently destroying the shard suffix.
- A retag by the player wipes the suffix AND clears that portal's connection (:143595), so the portal drops out of its shard and pass 2 may pair it with whatever else shares its now-bare tag. A normalisation tick (re-write s_tag and call ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()) is mandatory.
- Angle brackets are not the only hazard: Chat.OnNewChatMessage replaces '<' and '>' with spaces, so never round-trip a sharded tag through a chat-based tool.
- Support burden: when two portals that visibly share a name refuse to connect, nothing anywhere explains why. Log the raw tags in the mod's audit trail.

### 15. Per-Player Private Networks

`topologies:Per-Player Private Networks` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Every player's portals silently share a namespace of their own, keyed on the builder recorded in the piece ZDO.


**How it works:** Identity source. Every player-placed piece records its builder: `Piece.SetCreator` writes ZDOVars.s_creator (a long equal to that player's PlayerProfile UID, identical to ZDOVars.s_playerID on their character ZDO) and s_creatorIndex (an index into ZNet.World.m_playerHistory, which the server persists in the .fwl and fills from socket-verified PlatformUserIDs). A portal's builder is therefore readable server-side, offline, forever.

Namespacing. On a tick (2-5 s is ample), enumerate ZDOMan.GetPortalList(); for each portal read `creator = zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator, 0L)` and the current s_tag. Strip any existing managed suffix, then write `s_tag = <displayTag> + "<p" + shortCode(creator) + ">"` using the Invisible Tag Sharding mechanism, followed by `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (a tag write alone does NOT set DirtyPortalObjects, so the rename is lost at the next save otherwise — :73832/:76702/:77621). Portals whose creator is 0 (world-gen, admin-spawned, or placed before the field existed — SetCreator only writes when `GetCreator() == 0 && m_nview.IsOwner()`, :136415-136424) go into a shared "public" namespace.

Result. Vanilla's own reconciler now enforces the partition for free: FindRandomUnconnectedPortal only considers exact-tag matches (:100669), so player A's `forest<pA1>` can never be paired with player B's `forest<pB7>`. Two players can both name a portal `forest` and never interfere.

Sharing. To let A grant B access to one portal, rewrite just that portal's suffix to a shared group code (`<gAB>`). Because the routing suffix is data the server owns, sharing is a one-line rewrite plus a ConnectPortals call for instant re-pairing (`Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` is public, :100589).

Grant/revoke must also handle the in-flight connection: changing a portal's suffix out from under an existing pair leaves the PARTNER holding a now tag-mismatched target, which pass 1 tears down within 5 s — correct behaviour, just not instantaneous. Call ConnectPortals() yourself to make it immediate.


**Player experience:** Astrid and Bjorn both build a portal at their own farm and both call it `farm`. In vanilla they would have paired with each other and spent an evening confused; here each pairs only with their own second `farm` portal at their own mine. Both hover as `tag:"farm"`. When Astrid wants Bjorn to be able to reach her mine, she emotes /point at the portal and a top-left toast reads `Portal shared with the nearest player: Bjorn`. Within a second Bjorn's `farm` portals and Astrid's shared one are in the same group, and the next time Bjorn steps into his farm portal he may come out at Astrid's mine.


**Failure modes:**
- s_creator is 0 for admin-spawned and world-gen portals, and for anything placed under conditions where SetCreator's `GetCreator() == 0 && IsOwner()` guard did not fire. Treat 0 as public, never as 'owned by nobody in particular'.
- s_creator is written by the PLACING CLIENT, so it is a client self-report. It is cross-checkable only via s_creatorIndex into ZNet.World.m_playerHistory (socket-verified PlatformUserIDs, :81271-81280, :81436-81461) — and that index is -1 when the placer was not yet in the history.
- A player retagging their portal wipes the suffix and clears the connection. The normalisation tick restores it within one tick, but pass 2 may have paired the portal into the bare-tag public group in the interim. Reduce the window by calling Game.instance.ConnectPortals() immediately after normalising.
- The whole partition is one ZDO string write per portal — a hacked client can simply write s_tag itself via ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77139), which validates nothing beyond the DataRevision. Server-side this is detect-and-revert, not prevention.
- 10-char editor budget: a player's display tag effectively shrinks to ~5 characters once a suffix is applied.

**Designer citations:** Piece.SetCreator writes s_creator / s_creatorIndex — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:136415-136424 (read back Piece.Awake :136248-136249) ; ZDOVars.s_creator / s_creatorIndex / s_playerID — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78393, :78395, :78539 ; ZNet.World.m_playerHistory (persisted, socket-verified) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:112396; UpdatePlayerHistory :81436-81461 ; Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal exact-tag filter — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100669 ; ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals (required after a tag-only write) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702; portal chunk gate :77621-77635 ; Game.ConnectPortals is public — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589 ; ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData validates nothing — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77076-77139

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Key on s_creatorIndex -> ZNet.World.m_playerHistory[i].m_id (per account, socket-verified server side) rather than s_creator, which is PlayerProfile.m_playerID = Utils.GenerateUID() (:105662), a random per-character id; otherwise one player's characters cannot share portals.
- State that s_creator/s_creatorIndex are written by the placing CLIENT (Piece.SetCreator IsOwner gate :136417); the partition is server-enforced but the identity input is client-supplied.
- Suffix code must be 1-2 chars (mod index), not derived from the 64-bit UID, to fit the 10-char rename field; it is visible in that field (GetText :143551-143553, TextInput.Show :61517-61521).

- Tag write needs SetDirtyPortals because portals are excluded from sector chunks (:77572) and saved only in the portal chunk (:77621-77635); confirmed.
- Handle the staged-commit forced revert (:100690-100698) in the normalisation tick — run it idempotently at ≥1 Hz.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism verified: Piece.SetCreator writes s_creator and s_creatorIndex only when IsOwner && GetCreator()==0 (:136415-136424), called from Player.PlacePiece with GetPlayerID() (:12516); Piece.Awake reads them back (:136247-136249). Tag-only writes do not mark the portal chunk dirty (ZDO.Set(int,string) :73719-73725 -> IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector :76694-76699 dirties the regular chunk only; portals are saved from m_portalObjects into ChunkPortal only when DirtyPortalObjects :77621-77631), so SetDirtyPortals() (:76702) is genuinely required. Game.ConnectPortals is public (:100589). Historical player list is server-persisted and pushed to clients (SendHistoricalPlayerList :81317-81341; RPC_HistoricalPlayerList :81419-81433), so s_creatorIndex is a valid index into ZNet.World.m_playerHistory. Enforcement is route-form via vanilla's own exact-tag filter. Corrections: (1) s_creator is PlayerProfile.m_playerID = Utils.GenerateUID() (:105662), a random per-CHARACTER id — the same account with two characters gets two disjoint networks; the per-ACCOUNT key is s_creatorIndex -> m_playerHistory[i].m_id (PlatformUserID), which the option mentions but does not use in the tick. (2) Both fields are written by the placing client (IsOwner gate), so identity is client-supplied — honest from vanilla, forgeable from a modified client; the routing partition itself is server-enforced. ### 16. Team / Faction Networks

`topologies:Team / Faction Networks` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Guild-scoped namespaces derived from a mod-side roster rather than from the builder, so membership can change without rebuilding.


**How it works:** Same sharding mechanism as Per-Player Private Networks, but the suffix is derived from a roster the mod maintains rather than directly from s_creator. Roster key must be durable: ZDOVars.s_playerID (the profile UID, written once into the character ZDO by Player.SetPlayerID, :10129-10136) or the socket-verified PlatformUserID from `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()` — never ZNetPeer.m_uid (a per-connection id) and never ZNetPeer.m_playerID (permanently 0, because no vanilla client ever invokes the "PlayerID" RPC).

Portal→faction resolution, in priority order: (1) a mod-private ZDO key written by the mod when the portal was claimed (e.g. `zdo.Set("tpl_faction".GetStableHashCode(), factionId)` — arbitrary int-keyed ZDO data round-trips through save and network for free); (2) s_creator looked up in the roster; (3) the ward the portal stands inside — PrivateArea's roster is fully server-readable from the ward ZDO as `zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_permitted)` plus the raw string keys `"pu_id"+i` (long) and `"pu_name"+i` (string), written by PrivateArea.SetPermittedPlayers (:137338-137347). Option (3) is attractive because it reuses a UI players already understand, but the ward radius is a compiled Inspector field (PrivateArea.m_radius, class default 10f, :137132) and must be measured or configured; PrivateArea.CheckAccess itself is useless server-side because m_allAreas is always empty and it therefore returns true vacuously (:137547-137593).

The rest is identical: normalisation tick writes `s_tag = display + "<f" + factionCode + ">"`, SetDirtyPortals(), and vanilla's tag-equality filter partitions the world.

Cross-faction gateways: give one designated portal per faction a SHARED suffix (`<fx>`) and wire them as a Fan-In Star into a neutral hub. Faction members reach the neutral hub from their own network, and from the hub a Portal Bank reaches the other factions' public halls.


**Player experience:** The Wolves and the Ravens each have a hall. Wolf portals all hover as `hall`; Raven portals also all hover as `hall`. A Wolf stepping into any `hall` portal always arrives at the Wolf hall. In the neutral market square stand two portals, `market` and `market`, one per faction, both leading to the same neutral rotunda; from the rotunda a colonnade of eight labelled portals reaches every faction's public hall. When a player is promoted from Raven to Wolf, the admin runs one command; within about two seconds every portal they built repoints, and their old `hall` portals now take them to the Wolf hall instead. Nothing they can see on the portal changed.


**Failure modes:**
- Faction membership changes must re-normalise every affected portal in one batch; doing it piecemeal leaves half-migrated networks where pass 1 tears down cross-suffix edges (correctly) and pass 2 re-pairs the freed ends randomly inside their new group.
- A mass migration is a mass broadcast: every changed ZDO bumps DataRevision and ForceSendZDO pushes to all peers. Budget it (Wonderland's StructureUpkeep caps at 256 routed broadcasts per sweep for exactly this reason).
- Ward-derived membership is only as good as PrivateArea.m_radius, which the decompile cannot supply, and PrivateArea's permitted list is itself plain ZDO data any client can rewrite via RPC_ZDOData.
- PrivateArea.RPC_ToggleEnabled and RPC_TogglePermitted ignore the routed-RPC sender entirely and act on a payload playerID (:137399-137421), so ward membership is spoofable by any client. Treat it as a convenience, not authorisation.
- Vanilla's own portal system has no concept of a faction; if the mod is uninstalled, every portal is left carrying a visible-but-stripped suffix and the world settles into whatever pairs those raw strings produce — the faction partition actually SURVIVES uninstall until someone retags, which may be surprising.

**Open questions:**

### 17. Tag-Scramble Lockdown (server-ENFORCED portal shutdown)

`topologies:Tag-Scramble Lockdown (server-ENFORCED portal shutdown)` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Give every portal a unique invisible tag suffix so no two can ever pair — a shutdown a modified client cannot lift, unlike the NoPortals global key.


**How it works:** Why the obvious approach fails. Writing `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` on every portal does NOT lock anything: pass 2 of Game.ConnectPortals re-pairs every same-tag unconnected portal within 5 s (:100607-100622). And `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` is CLIENT-HONOURED only — TeleportWorld.Teleport reads the key on the traveller's machine (:143523) — and worse, ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey / RPC_RemoveGlobalKey perform ZERO sender validation (:116022-116037), so any connected client can clear the lockdown with one packet.

The enforced version. For every portal P in ZDOMan.GetPortalList(): stash the original tag in a mod-private ZDO key (`P.Set("tpl_tag_saved".GetStableHashCode(), original)`), then write `P.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, original + "<L" + P.m_uid.ID + ">")` and `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`. Every portal is now the sole member of its own tag group. FindRandomUnconnectedPortal's candidate list is empty for every portal and it returns null (:100674-100678), so pass 2 can never pair anything. Then null every connection: `P.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); P.SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(P.m_uid);`

The result is enforced at the ZDO layer — TeleportWorld.Teleport's gate 1 (`if (!TargetFound()) return;`, :143519) is the ONLY one of its four gates that is server-controllable, and a None connection fails it unconditionally on any client, modified or not.

And because the suffix is stripped from the hover by RemoveRichTextTags (:143459), every portal still displays its original name; only `[$piece_portal_unconnected]` and the dead glow reveal the shutdown. Lifting it is the reverse pass: restore s_tag from the stash, SetDirtyPortals(), and call `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` to re-pair instantly.

Throttle: this is a world-wide write. On a 400-portal world that is 800 ZDO writes and 400 full-ZDO broadcasts to every peer. Budget it across ticks (≤256 broadcasts per sweep) unless the server is empty.


**Player experience:** Ten seconds before a server-wide raid event, every portal in the world goes dark. Hover text still reads `Teleport tag:"base"` — the name the player chose — but the bracket now says `[$piece_portal_unconnected]` and the stone no longer glows. Walking in does nothing at all: no black screen, no `$msg_blocked`, no message of any kind, because gate 1 returns silently (:143519-143522). Players with cheat clients get exactly the same result. When the event ends the portals light up again within a second and every original pairing is restored, including custom hub topologies, because the mod re-asserts them explicitly rather than letting vanilla re-roll.


**Failure modes:**
- Absolutely silent to the player. Pair it with a PlayerNotify.Toast broadcast ("The ways are shut") or the shutdown reads as a server bug.
- Losing the stash loses the tags. Write the stash to the ZDO (round-trips through save automatically) rather than to a mod-side file keyed by ZDOID — ZDOIDs are renumbered on every world load (ZDO.Load does m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID), :74552), so a ZDOID-keyed file is worthless after a restart.
- A restore that runs while vanilla's 5 s pass is mid-flight can produce transient random pairings. Prefix Game.ConnectPortals to return false for the duration of the restore batch, then call it once explicitly.
- Do not use the connection-nulling half alone. Without the tag scramble it is undone in ≤5 s by vanilla itself.
- Mod uninstalled mid-lockdown: the scrambled tags persist in the save, every portal stays a singleton group, and every portal in the world is permanently dead until someone retags them by hand. This is the most dangerous option in the catalogue for that reason — always restore before shutdown (Plugin.OnDestroy).

**Designer citations:** Game.ConnectPortals pass 2 re-pairs None connections within 5s — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100607-100622 ; Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal returns null for an empty candidate list — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100674-100678 ; TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 (silent, server-controllable) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143519-143522 ; TeleportWorld.Teleport NoPortals gate (client-executed) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143523-143527 ; ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey / RPC_RemoveGlobalKey (no sender validation) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:116022-116037 ; TeleportWorld.GetHoverText RemoveRichTextTags — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143459 ; ZDO.Load renumbers ZDOIDs — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74552 ; ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702


**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Remove 'cheat clients get exactly the same result': the transit decision is client-side (TeleportWorld.Teleport :143517-143546, TeleportWorldTrigger :143675-143682); a modified client can bypass. The honest claim: cannot be lifted by any vanilla client and cannot be cleared by the unauthenticated global-key RPCs.
- Suffix must be a random/GUID code, not m_uid.ID — ZDOIDs renumber on load (:74552) so id-derived suffixes can collide across restarts.
- Lifting: stash the pre-lockdown partner (by position) and re-assert connections directly; calling ConnectPortals() re-rolls random same-tag pairs (:100678) and does NOT restore custom topologies.
- Document that the lockdown persists through restart and mod uninstall (tags saved via SetDirtyPortals :73656-73665); ship an explicit unlock path/uninstall hook.
- Minor: a pair staged in the previous ConnectPortals tick is force-committed once more by ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) at lockdown start; expect one 5-s blip.
- Remove 'cheat clients get exactly the same result': TeleportWorld.Teleport reads the local ZDO copy (:143539) and Player.TeleportTo (:15318-15326) / Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer (:41962-41968) are client-executed with no server gate; a modified client moves itself freely.
- Modified clients can re-open routes for vanilla clients by writing tag/connection via ZDOData (RPC_ZDOData :77076-77139) and by dropping vanilla's routed RPC_SetConnection teardown (Game.SetConnection :100636-100650 writes nothing locally when the owner is online). The lockdown holds only as long as the mod re-asserts unique tags + None connections every tick with forced local writes.
- Retag race bounded to one mod tick; the staged-commit forced relink (:100690-100698) is undone by pass 1 (:100601) within the same ConnectPortals call.
- Ownership claims do not stick near players (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76925); harmless for this option but the doc should not imply persistent server ownership.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core claims hold. NoPortals is read on the traveller's client in TeleportWorld.Teleport (:143523-143527) and ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey have no sender check (:116022-116037). Pass 2 re-pairs None connections (:100607-100622) so nulling alone fails. With unique tags FindRandomUnconnectedPortal's list is empty and returns null (:100674-100678). Gate 1 (:143519-143522) returns silently; HaveTarget()==false drives hover to $piece_portal_unconnected (:143460) and the emission lerp to m_colorUnconnected (:143510-143513); m_target_found is deactivated (:143506). Tag+None writes persist because ZDO.SetConnection calls SetDirtyPortals on change (:73656-73665). Route-form enforcement is honest for VANILLA clients. Refuted sub-claims: (1) 'Players with cheat clients get exactly the same result' is false — Teleport() runs entirely on the client against the client's own ZDO copy; a modified client can overwrite its local connection with any loaded ZDOID (or call Player.TeleportTo directly) and the server never sees a transit decision. What the scramble resists is any vanilla client plus one-packet global-key removal; say that. (2) `<L{m_uid.ID}>` is not unique across restarts: ZDO.Load renumbers IDs from ZDOID.m_loadID (:74552), so a portal placed after a restart can receive a suffix equal to a stale suffix still stored on another portal; use a random/GUID code. (3) 'every original pairing is restored' contradicts 'call ConnectPortals() to re-pair': pass 2 picks a RANDOM same-tag partner (Random.Range :100678), so groups of >2 same-tag portals re-roll; restoring originals requires stashing the partner (by position) and writing connections explicitly. (4) Persistence hazard: the scrambled state is saved and survives restart AND mod removal; an uninstall mid-lockdown leaves every portal permanently unpaired until players hand-edit the (visible in the rename dialog, GetText :143551-143553) suffix. (5) ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals force-commits pairs staged on the previous tick regardless of tags (:100690-100698 -> ForceSetConnection :100625-100631), so a pair staged just before lockdown reappears for one 5-s cycle until pass 1 tears it down; the mod's own re-null tick covers it. Effort estimate plausible.
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism verified. Pass 2 re-pairs any None-connection portal that has a same-tag None candidate (:100607-100622); FindRandomUnconnectedPortal returns null on an empty candidate list (:100673-100676), so unique per-portal tags make pass 2 inert. Gate 1 of TeleportWorld.Teleport is `if (!TargetFound()) return;` (:143519-143522) with no message; TargetFound() (:143644-143660) is pure ZDO-connection data. The NoPortals gate (:143523-143527) reads the global key on the traveller's client, and ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey / RPC_RemoveGlobalKey ignore `sender` entirely (:116022-116037). Hover stays on the original name via RemoveRichTextTags (:143459) and `<L123>` matches the regex class (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703); HaveTarget() drives `$piece_portal_unconnected` and the emission fade (:143498-143508). ZDO.SetConnection auto-dirties portals (:73656-73665); the tag write needs SetDirtyPortals (:76702) because portals are saved only in the portal chunk (:77572, :77621-77635). ZDO.Load renumbers ZDOIDs (:74552) so `<L{ID}>` suffixes change across restarts — harmless. Corrections: (1) 'Players with cheat clients get exactly the same result' is FALSE. Teleport() reads the cheater's LOCAL ZDO copy (:143539) and Player.TeleportTo is a client-local call (:15318-15326; also reachable via Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer :41962-41968 which any peer can route to any peer), so a modified client can move itself regardless of any portal state. (2) A modified client can also re-open routes for VANILLA clients: it can rewrite s_tag/connection through ZDOData (RPC_ZDOData validates nothing and accepts higher revisions, :77076-77139) and vanilla's pass-1 teardown on a peer-owned portal is a routed 'RPC_SetConnection' the cheater can drop (Game.SetConnection :100636-100650 does NOT write locally in that branch). Only the mod's own forced local writes (SetOwner(session) + SetConnection + ForceSendZDO) defeat this, so it is a write war the mod wins by re-asserting each tick — not an unliftable lock. (3) Vanilla-client retag race: two players retagging locked portals to the same bare string between mod ticks lets pass 2 stage a pair; the mod's re-suffix + null is then force-reverted once by ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) but pass 1 tears it down again in the same call (tags differ), so exposure is ≤ one mod tick. (4) ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands ownership to any nearby peer every 2 s (:76872-76925, portals included via FindObjects :77367-77381), so SetOwner(session) is transient; it only matters for making vanilla's SetConnection take the local path. Enforcement stays server-enforced in the route sense for vanilla clients; claim about modified clients must be rewritten.

### 18. Black-Hole Sink (all portals → one destination)

`topologies:Black-Hole Sink (all portals → one destination)` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Repoint every portal at a single jail/lobby anchor: portals keep working, but everything arrives in the same room.


**How it works:** A softer, stabler alternative to the Tag-Scramble Lockdown that needs no tag surgery at all.

Create one anchor Z at the lobby coordinate (see Anchor-Terminated One-Way for the full CreateNewZDO recipe). Then for every portal P you want swallowed: `P.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, T_sink)`, `P.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, `P.SetConnection(Portal, Z.m_uid)`, `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(P.m_uid)`; and on the anchor `Z.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, T_sink)` plus `Z.SetConnection(Portal, Z.m_uid)`.

Stability. Every portal's pass-1 test is evaluated against Z: non-null ✓, tag == T_sink ✓, Z.connection == Z ≠ None ✓. No teardown. Pass 2 finds nothing IsNone(). One anchor swallows an unbounded number of portals with no per-tick cost — this is Fan-In taken to its extreme, and it is the cheapest world-wide topology write in the catalogue because it needs one target ZDOID for every source.

If you want the sink to be reversible without stashing tags, do NOT rewrite s_tag: instead give the anchor the tag of whichever group you are swallowing and run one anchor per tag group. More anchors, zero tag churn, trivially reversible by restoring each portal's connection from a mod-private ZDO key holding the pre-sink target's position (not its ZDOID — ZDOIDs renumber on load).

Uses: a jail (portal offenders into a warded pen), a maintenance mode, a raid-night funnel where everyone who portals ends up at the muster point, or a PvP mechanic where a captured region's portals all dump into the capturing faction's holding cell.


**Player experience:** A player steps into their base portal expecting the mine. Black screen, eight seconds, and they fade in inside a stone rotunda with no exit portal, a sign reading `THE WAYS ARE WARDED — SPEAK TO A JARL`, and half a dozen other confused players. Every portal in the world behaves the same way. The portals still glow, still hover as connected, and still give the full teleport experience — they simply all arrive at one place. Unlike the tag scramble, players immediately understand something deliberate has happened.


**Failure modes:**
- If the anchor is destroyed or fails to persist, every swallowed portal is nulled by pass 1 and then randomly re-paired inside T_sink — producing an instantaneous world-wide random portal shuffle, the worst possible failure. The anchor MUST have Persistent = true and a real SetPrefab (ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO sets neither, :76684-76692).
- Players can be sunk mid-journey and have no way back; provide an egress (a portal in the rotunda on its own tag paired to a release point, or a server-driven RPC_TeleportPlayer).
- At world load ZDOMan.ConnectPortals matches hash pairs reciprocally (:77879-77885) and only ONE portal can win the anchor's single Target slot; the rest are unconnected and then randomly re-paired by Game.instance.ConnectPortals (:76523). Re-assert the sink at OnWorldReady, unconditionally.
- Mod uninstalled: the sink survives only until the next world reload, at which point the world settles into random pairs within T_sink. If every portal shares T_sink, that is a complete randomisation of the server's entire portal graph. Restore before shutdown.

### 19. Roulette / Periodic Shuffle

`topologies:Roulette / Periodic Shuffle` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Leave a large group on one tag and let vanilla's own UnityEngine.Random pairing do the work — optionally forcing a re-roll on a timer.


**How it works:** Zero-mod version: place N portals all carrying the same tag string. Vanilla's pass 2 (:100607-100622) pairs them using `list[UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, list.Count)]` from the shared global Unity RNG (:100678), producing floor(N/2) arbitrary pairs plus one permanent orphan if N is odd. Because pass 1 never tears down a healthy pair, the arrangement then freezes until something breaks.

Forced re-roll: on a timer, for every member `P.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); P.SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(P.m_uid);` then call `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` (public, :100589) once to re-pair immediately rather than waiting up to 5 s. Every member is IsNone() so pass 2 re-pairs all of them with fresh random picks.

Subtlety that bites: Game.SetConnection defers to the owning client over RPC_SetConnection when the portal is owned by a CONNECTED peer (:100641-100650), leaving the server's own copy reading the OLD connection. Pass 2 in the same tick then sees `!IsNone()` and skips that portal, so a portal a player is standing next to takes two or more ticks to re-roll. Avoid by doing the null writes yourself with explicit SetOwner (which makes GetPeer(serverSessionID) null and forces the immediate local path) rather than going through Game.SetConnection.

Also reproduce vanilla's `IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal` guard if you re-implement pass 2 yourself (:100609, :100671) — it exists precisely because a deferred write leaves the server's copy reading None and would otherwise let the same portal be paired twice in one pass.

The orphan is a feature: designate a known-odd count so exactly one portal in the roulette is always dead, and let players hunt for it.


**Player experience:** Seven identical standing stones scattered across the Black Forest, all tagged `wyrd`. Three pairs are live and one stone is dark. Every hour at the top of the hour every stone briefly goes dark and then relights in a new configuration — the stone that took you to the river camp now takes you to the mountain pass, and a different one is the dead stone. Players build their evening's route around whatever the current roll is, and there is no way to predict it from inside the game because it is drawn from the shared UnityEngine.Random stream.


**Failure modes:**
- Not deterministic and not seedable from the mod's side. If you need deterministic pairing, postfix the private Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (AccessTools.Method(typeof(Game), "FindRandomUnconnectedPortal")) and overwrite __result with your own pick — the minimal, lowest-risk intervention that leaves the two-phase commit, ownership handling and logging intact.
- The orphan's identity is not stable across a restart, because iteration order is m_portalObjects dictionary-bucket order (:77648-77656).
- A re-roll that lands a player's destination in an unvisited region makes their first walk-in silently fail (TargetFound → RequestZDO, :143646-143654).
- Every re-roll is 2N ZDO writes plus 2N full-ZDO broadcasts. At N=40 hourly that is fine; at N=400 every minute it is not.

**Designer citations:** Game.ConnectPortals pass 2 / FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (UnityEngine.Random.Range) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100607-100622, :100664-100679 ; Game.SetConnection deferred branch for connected-peer owners — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100641-100650 ; Game.IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal guard — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100609, :100671, :100700-100710 ; Game.ConnectPortals is public and callable on demand — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589 ; ZDOMan.GetPortalList (dictionary-bucket order) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648-77656


**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Game.SetConnection / ForceSetConnection / RPC_SetConnection / m_currentlyConnectingPortals are private on Game (SERVER :100629-100662, :100681-100710); only ConnectPortals() (:100589) is callable. Do the triad (SetOwner :74627, SetConnection :73656, ForceSendZDO :77706) yourself.
- ConnectPortals() first flushes previously staged pairs via ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals → ForceSetConnection (:100591, :100629-100635, :100692-100699). A re-roll that runs within 5 s of a pass that created new pairs will see them re-forced. Steady-state (frozen) roulette has an empty staged list, so this only matters on the tick after a roll.
- Idempotent re-asserts do not bump DataRevision (ZDOExtraData.SetConnection returns false on unchanged value :74951-74959); a dropped update on an owner-client whose copy has an equal revision stays diverged until some other write. Bump a mod nonce key when forcing a re-roll to guarantee a resend.
- Reciprocal pairs survive save/load (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461-75478; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals :77850-77893) so the roll and the orphan persist across restarts — this can be stated affirmatively.
- To make the dark→relight moment visible, hold connections at None for ≥1-2 s (one or more SendZDOs cycles) before re-pairing; a same-tick null+repair is invisible to clients and never fires m_connected.Create (:143495-143497).
- Any player can add a same-tag portal via RPC_SetTag (no cap, no ward check when the client owns the ZDO, :143587-143602); the odd-count orphan guarantee needs the mod to retag or exclude foreign portals, or to run its own pairer over a mod-marked set.
- Game.instance.ConnectPortals() begins with ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100591); pairs staged by vanilla in the previous cycle are force-restored before pass 1, so the mod should either wait for m_currentlyConnectingPortals to be empty or re-implement pass 2 itself (reproducing the IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal guard :100700-100710).
- ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924, every 2 s :76874-76884) hands the portal back to any peer whose active area covers it; the SetOwner(session) claim is only a write-time trick, not a standing ownership.
- Tag-only writes do not mark the portal chunk dirty (ZDO.Set(string) → SetDirtySector marks the normal sector chunk, :73832-73839; the portal file is written only when DirtyPortalObjects, :77621-77635) — irrelevant here because SetConnection calls SetDirtyPortals (:73656-73666), but relevant if the mod also retags.

Symmetric pairs survive save (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461-75478 assigns both endpoints one hash; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals load path :77850-77893 re-links them) so the frozen roll and the odd-count orphan persist across restarts. - [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Zero-mod behaviour holds: Game.ConnectPortals pass 2 (:100607-100622) pairs any two None-connection portals sharing a tag via FindRandomUnconnectedPortal's UnityEngine.Random.Range (:100664-100679); pass 1 (:100598-100604) only tears down links whose target is null/tag-mismatched/None, so healthy pairs freeze; odd N leaves one orphan. Forced re-roll also holds: ZDO.SetOwner(session) (:74627) makes Game.SetConnection's `ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner) != null` test false (ZNet.GetPeer iterates m_peers only, :80492-80501; the server is not a peer) so pass 2's SetConnection takes the immediate local path (:100641-100646). Game.ConnectPortals is public (:100589) and callable on demand. Pairwise matchings survive save/reload (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461-75478 + load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals :77850-77893 reconstruct symmetric pairs exactly). Three claims do not survive: (1) the 'every stone briefly goes dark then relights' experience is not real if null+repair happen in the same server tick — the client's UpdatePortal (0.5 s, :143488-143504) and the m_connected effect (:143495-143497) only react to a state the client actually received, and SendZDOs (:77008-77071) serialises current state, so a same-tick None→new-pair write coalesces into a single update; (2) the 'known-odd orphan' is not under mod control — any vanilla client can build a portal and tag it `wyrd` (RPC_SetTag has no cap or permission, :143587-143602), changing parity and joining the pool; (3) calling Game.instance.ConnectPortals() first runs ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100591, :100690-100698) which ForceSetConnection-restores any pair vanilla staged in the previous ≤5 s window, overwriting the mod's None write for those two portals that roll. Effort small is fair. Enforcement 'server-enforced' is honest: the rule is 'which ROUTE is open', not 'which player may pass'.

### 20. Displaced Routing — own the pairing, free s_tag for display

`topologies:Displaced Routing — own the pairing, free s_tag for display` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium-large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Harmony-prefix Game.ConnectPortals to return false and run your own pairer keyed on a mod-private ZDO string; s_tag becomes a pure label with no routing meaning.


**How it works:** The master enabler. Every constraint elsewhere in this catalogue — one tag per network, identical hover names across a tier, invisible suffixes, 10-character budgets, players accidentally retagging a hub out of existence — exists only because vanilla routes on s_tag. Take that over and all of them dissolve.

Implementation. `[HarmonyPatch(typeof(Game), nameof(Game.ConnectPortals))] static bool Prefix() => false;` (the method is public and instance-level, :100589). Wrap it with SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch. The coroutine keeps running and keeps calling a now-empty method every 5 s — harmless. Alternatively `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")`, which is valid because Start used the string overload (:100074), but the prefix is safer and reversible.

Then run your own pass on a timer you choose (1-5 s). Read routing from a mod-private key: `int ROUTE = "tpl_route".GetStableHashCode(); string route = zdo.GetString(ROUTE, "");` — arbitrary int-keyed ZDO strings persist through save and network automatically (ZDO.Set/GetString :73721/:73967) and are invisible to the player and to any other mod. Encode whatever you want: `"hub:realm/spoke"`, `"ring:caravan/3"`, `"bank:hall-haldor"`.

Write edges with the same triad (SetOwner / SetConnection / ForceSendZDO). Reproduce vanilla's useful bits: pass 1 self-heal against destroyed targets, and the IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal double-pair guard if you ever defer a write.

What this buys: arbitrary directed graphs with per-portal display names of arbitrary length (RPC_SetTag applies no cap, :143587-143602 — only the client's TextInput widget does, :143482); true trees where every tier can be labelled differently; per-portal metadata; one-way links that cannot be torn down; and immunity to player retagging (a retag changes only the label).

A related, riskier trick worth knowing: `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` returns the LIVE m_portalObjects dictionary (:77643-77646), so a portal removed from it becomes invisible to vanilla's pairer without a patch. Do not do this — the portal chunk file is written wholesale from m_portalObjects (:77621-77635), so a hidden portal is also an unsaved portal.


**Player experience:** Players see richer portals than vanilla allows. The hall portal hovers `Teleport tag:"Grand Hall of Hrafnsborg"` — a 25-character name no vanilla client could have typed. The four waystations read `North Waystation`, `East Waystation` and so on, all distinct, and all four still lead to the Grand Hall because routing has nothing to do with what is written on them. A player who retypes their portal's name to something rude changes only the sign; the route is untouched and the portal keeps working. Caveat: the moment a player opens the tag dialog on a long name, the edit box's 10-character limit may clamp it, so the mod re-writes the label from its own record on the next tick.


**Failure modes:**
- Mod uninstalled = total collapse, and this is the single biggest trade in the catalogue. Vanilla's ConnectPortals resumes on the next 5 s tick, sees a world of arbitrary directed edges, tears down every edge whose two ends have different s_tag strings (which, with per-portal display names, is nearly all of them), and randomly re-pairs everything inside whatever tag groups remain. A 200-portal curated network becomes 100 random pairs in one tick. Mitigate by writing a sane s_tag alongside the route key so the fallback is at least sensible, and by restoring a vanilla-legal configuration in Plugin.OnDestroy.
- A hacked client can still rewire any portal via the unauthenticated routed Game RPC_SetConnection (:100653-100662) or by writing the ZDO directly through RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77139). Your own pass re-asserts within one tick, which is the practical answer.
- Your pairer now owns the two-phase-commit problem vanilla solved. If you ever defer a write to an owning client, reproduce IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal or you will double-pair.
- Never cache ZDO object references across ticks. ZDOPool.Release/Get recycles ZDO objects on destruction and ZDO.Reset sets m_uid = ZDOID.None (:78286-78311, :73536-73545) — vanilla itself violates this in m_currentlyConnectingPortals. Cache ZDOIDs and re-resolve with ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id) every tick.
- Other mods that patch Game.ConnectPortals will conflict.

- Does Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine") actually stop it? Start used the string overload so per Unity's API it should, but that is a runtime claim. In-game: call it, place two same-tag portals, and watch for the absence of `[ Connected N portals ]` in the server log.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Retag is NOT label-only: TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag on the owning client calls UpdateConnection(Portal, None) before Set(s_tag) (SERVER :143587-143602); the route is torn down until the mod's next pairer tick. The pairer must re-assert every tick, and the 'route is untouched' sentence must go.
- Directed/non-reciprocal edges do not survive a world save: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) keeps one hash slot per ZDO (last writer wins), and the load path ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) only re-links hash-matched pairs. The pairer MUST rebuild all edges from the persisted tpl_route keys on the first tick after load. Registry must be keyed on the route string, not ZDOID (ZDO.Load renumbers uids :74552).
- Game.instance.ConnectPortals() is also invoked from ZDOMan.Load (:76523, :76658); the Harmony prefix must be installed before the world loads.
- Idempotent re-asserts produce no DataRevision bump (ZDOExtraData.SetConnection :74951-74959 returns false on unchanged value), so a dropped update on a client holding an equal revision stays diverged; include a nonce write when re-asserting.
- Postfix on FindRandomUnconnectedPortal is unnecessary once ConnectPortals is prefixed out; drop it or keep as fallback only.
- Retag is NOT label-only on a vanilla client: TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag on the ZDO owner executes zDO.UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None) then writes s_tag/s_tagauthor (:143587-143602). The mod's pairer must re-assert the route on its next tick; replace 'immunity' with 'self-healing within one pairer tick'. (SetConnectedPortal is then called with the already-nulled ID, :143593-143594, so the partner is not touched.)
- The Game.ConnectPortals prefix does not disable ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (private load-time relink, :77850-77893). Every world load rebuilds symmetric pairs from ZDOConnectionHashData, so the mod must run its pass immediately after ZDOMan.Load (Harmony postfix on ZDOMan.Load or first Update) using the persisted `tpl_route` string as source of truth; ZDOIDs are renumbered at load (ZDO.Load :74552 `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`), so the key must encode names/positions, never ZDOIDs.
- Label writes (s_tag) must be followed by ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702-76705); Set(string) only dirties the normal sector chunk (:73832-73839) and portals are saved from the portal file gated on DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77635).
- Hover text is `$piece_portal $piece_portal_tag:"..." [connected]` (:143453-143463), i.e. 'Portal Tag:', not 'Teleport tag:' (GetHoverName 'Teleport' :143466 is a separate string).
- Server ownership of a portal silently drops vanilla RPC_SetTag (no ZNetView on the server, ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC :83646-83662) but is lost to any nearby peer within 2 s (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76924); do not design around holding ownership.

- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Core is sound. Game.ConnectPortals is public instance (:100589) and a Harmony bool-prefix skips it; the string-overload StartCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine") (:100074) makes StopCoroutine(string) valid. Note ConnectPortals() is ALSO called directly from ZDOMan.Load (:76523, :76658) right after the load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals — the prefix covers those if applied before world load (BepInEx Awake precedes it). ZDO.Set(int,string) :73721 / GetString(int) :73967 exist; strings are saved via ZDOExtraData.GetSaveData (:75500-75520, only s_sessionOnly hashes filtered) and shipped in Serialize (:74112+), so mod-private route keys persist and replicate. RPC_SetTag (:143587-143602) has no length check; the 10 cap is only TextInput.RequestText(..., 10) at :143482. GetPortals() returns the live m_portalObjects (:77643-77646) and GetSaveClonePerChunk writes ChunkPortal from that dictionary (:77621-77632) — the 'do not hide' warning is right. Two claims are wrong: (1) 'immunity to player retagging — the route is untouched': the owning client's RPC_SetTag executes zDO.UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None) BEFORE writing the tag (:143591-143597), and a player standing at the portal owns it (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76924), so every retag tears the route down for up to one mod tick; the mod's pairer must re-assert continuously, not once. (2) 'one-way links that cannot be torn down' and 'arbitrary directed graphs' hold only at runtime. On save, RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) collapses each ZDO to one ZDOConnectionHashData slot with last-writer-wins, and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load (:77850-77893) only re-creates hash-matched reciprocal pairs; non-reciprocal edges vanish and are then handed to the load-time Game.instance.ConnectPortals() call (prefixed out). The design survives only because tpl_route strings persist per ZDO and the pairer can re-derive every edge after load — this must be stated as a hard requirement, and the registry must key on the route string, since ZDO.Load renumbers every ZDOID (m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID) :74552). Also: a same-revision collision between the server's re-assert and a concurrent owner-client write is dropped on both sides and an idempotent re-assert will not resend (ZDOExtraData.SetConnection returns false when unchanged :74951-74959) — bump a nonce or SetOwner+nonce when re-asserting.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism verified: Game.ConnectPortals is public instance (:100589), started via StartCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine") string overload under IsServer (:100069-100073); a Harmony prefix returning false disables both passes. Pairing exists nowhere on the client (TeleportWorld never compares tags; it only reads its own ZDO connection at trigger time, :143521-143548), so a server-side pairer keyed on a mod-private ZDO string is the sole routing authority and s_tag becomes label-only. RPC_SetTag applies no cap (:143587-143602); only the client TextInput widget does (:143482). GetPortals returns the live dictionary (:77643-77646) and the portal file is written from it (:77621-77635), so the 'do not hide portals from it' warning is right. Two claims are wrong and one omission is load-bearing. (1) 'A retag changes only the label / immunity to player retagging' is false: the owning vanilla client's RPC_SetTag calls zDO.UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None) BEFORE writing the tag (:143591-143596), so a retag nulls that portal's own route on the client's authority; the mod's pairer must detect and re-write it (an outage of one mod tick). If the server currently owns the portal the RPC is dropped entirely (server HandleRoutedRPC needs a ZNetView instance, :83646-83662; none exists on a dedicated server) — but ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924) gives ownership to any nearby peer within 2 s, so this cannot be relied on. (2) The save boundary: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) collapses each ZDO to one hash slot and load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893, private, NOT touched by the Game.ConnectPortals prefix) rebuilds a symmetric pairwise matching from those slots, then ZDOMan.Load calls Game.instance.ConnectPortals() (:76524, :76650) which the prefix skips. Any non-pairwise graph is therefore wrong on disk and wrong for the window between load and the mod's first pass; the design is sound only because `tpl_route` is a persisted per-ZDO string (ZDO.Set(int,string) :73721; strings saved unless in s_sessionOnly :74776) from which the pairer rebuilds — this must be stated as THE persistence mechanism, not a position-keyed registry. (3) Tag writes alone never mark the portal chunk dirty (ZDO.Set(string) → IncreaseDataRevision → SetDirtySector marks the normal sector chunk :73832-73839; the portal file is only written when DirtyPortalObjects :77621-77635), so display-label rewrites must be followed by ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702-76705) or they are lost at the next save. Enforcement 'server-enforced' is honest for the route; effort medium-large is fair.

### 21. Asymmetric Round-Trip ("one-way door, long way home")

`topologies:Asymmetric Round-Trip ("one-way door, long way home")` · domain **topologies** · source `topologies`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A→B and B→C where C sits next to A: a portal you can only travel one direction through, and a separate return leg you must find.


**How it works:** A three-portal directed chain closed by geography rather than by graph structure, and the cheapest genuinely one-way experience that still lets players get home.

Encoding. Three portals A, B, C all on one tag T. `A.SetConnection(Portal, B.m_uid)`, `B.SetConnection(Portal, C.m_uid)`, `C.SetConnection(Portal, A.m_uid)` — formally this is a 3-ring, so it is a vanilla fixed point for exactly the reasons given in the Directed Ring entry (every target non-null, tag-matched, non-None). The design content is in the PLACEMENT: A and C are put twenty metres apart at the home site, B is at the far site. So the travel graph reads home→far (via A), far→home-ish (via B), and home→home (via C, the twenty-metre hop that closes the ring and which nobody uses on purpose).

Better variant with two portals and an anchor: A (home) → B (far), B → anchor placed two metres behind B. Then B is a dead end and the far site genuinely has no return. Use when you want a true expedition.

Best variant, three portals, no useless hop: A (home) → B (far); B → C where C is at the home site; C → anchor at the home site. Now A is the outbound door, B is the return door, C is an arrival pad that goes nowhere useful, and no edge is wasted. All on tag T. Pass 1 accepts it: A→B ok (B.connection = C ≠ None), B→C ok (C.connection = anchor ≠ None), C→anchor ok (anchor.tag = T, anchor.connection = anchor ≠ None). Stable.

Why bother instead of a plain pair: it makes the two directions independently controllable. The mod can null or repoint the return leg (B→C) for an event without touching the outbound leg, which a symmetric pair cannot express at all.


**Player experience:** At the base, two portals stand side by side under one roof: the left one signed with a runic arrow pointing out, the right one with an arrow pointing in. Stepping into the left portal takes the player to the Mistlands camp. There is exactly one portal at the camp; stepping into it brings them back — to the RIGHT portal at the base, not the left one. Stepping into the right portal again does nothing useful (an eight-second black screen and they are back on the same flagstones). During a server event the jarl closes the return leg: the camp portal goes dark and hovers `[$piece_portal_unconnected]`, so everyone at the camp has to walk out, while the outbound door stays lit and people can still be sent in.


**Failure modes:**
- Same unravelling risk as any chain if the terminator is lost: if the anchor dies, C is nulled, then B is nulled on the next tick, then A. Anchor persistence is load-bearing.
- All three portals share one tag so they all hover with the same name — signage or the Displaced Routing option is needed to make the in/out distinction legible.
- World reload recovers at most one pair out of the three-edge structure; mandatory re-assert.

- [vanilla-reality:downgraded] Runtime claim holds: a directed 3-ring A→B→C→A on one tag satisfies pass 1 for every member (target non-null, same tag, connection non-None, :100598-100604) and pass 2 skips non-None portals (:100609), so it is a fixed point of the 5 s loop while nothing else touches it; the client only reads its own portal's connection ZDOID at trigger time (:143539-143548), so arrival at C for a B-departure is real. Everything else needs correction. (1) Not save-stable, and the option asserts 'Stable' without qualification: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) writes hd[src]=(Portal,h) and hd[target]=(Portal|Target,h) per edge, overwriting per ZDO, so a 3-ring leaves exactly one matched hash; load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893) relinks that one pair symmetrically and the third portal has no connection; ZDOMan.Load then immediately calls Game.instance.ConnectPortals() (:76524/:76650) which commits the collapsed state. Concretely, in insertion order A,B,C the world reloads as C↔A (the useless 20 m home hop, now bidirectional) with the far portal B dead — the worst possible outcome. ZDOIDs are renumbered on load (:74552) so recovery requires a position/name-keyed registry and a re-assert pass right after load. (2) The 'close the return leg' player experience is impossible under vanilla reconciliation: setting B→None makes A→B fail pass 1 (`target.connection == None`, :100601) so A is nulled in the same pass, then pass 2 sees two None portals on tag T and pairs A↔B as an ordinary vanilla pair (:100607-100622). The outbound door cannot 'stay lit' while B is dark. Closure must be B→B (self-loop) or B→anchor beside B: pass 1 accepts it, the hover reads [connected], and the player gets an 8 s swirl back to the same spot (Player.UpdateTeleport distantTeleport minimum 8 s, :15334-15350). A visibly dark portal with a live inbound route requires disabling pass 1 (Displaced Routing prefix). (3) Any vanilla retag on any member nulls that member (:143591-143596), which cascades through pass 1/pass 2 into random vanilla pairs within 5 s; the mod must re-assert. (4) The m_exitDistance citation is wrong: Teleport uses `this.m_exitDistance` of the SOURCE portal along the TARGET's forward (:143542-143545), not the target's field. Enforcement remains route-level server-enforced, but 'small' effort undercounts the persistence + repair loop.
