### 57. Ungated RPC Hardening

`access-control:Ungated RPC Hardening` · domain **access** · source `access-control`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Sender checks on the four unauthenticated global routed RPCs a client can use to defeat any portal policy — `SetGlobalKey`, `RemoveGlobalKey`, `RPC_SetConnection` and `RequestZDO`.


**How it works:** Four handlers that run on the dedicated server (all ZDO-less routed RPCs, so `HandleRoutedRPC` takes the `m_functions` branch at :83648-83654) and validate nothing.

**(1) `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey(long sender, string name)` (:116022-116029) and `RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` (:116031-116037).** Registered only on the server (:113444-113455) and neither inspects `sender`: `if (!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)) { GlobalKeyAdd(name); SendGlobalKeys(0L); }`. Any connected client can set or clear `noportals`, `nobossportals`, `teleportall` and `dungeonbuild` at will. Any policy built on those keys (see Progression Gate) is one packet from being lifted. Harmony **prefix** both: allow through only when the Authentic Sender Context resolves to the server's own id or to an account in `m_adminList` (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName())`, :81811); otherwise return false, audit, and toast. Note `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors every key with ordinal < `GlobalKeys.NonServerOption` (41) into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113483-113513, list write :113511) which is written to the .fwl on every autosave — so an unhardened server that gets griefed once has `noportals` baked into the world file permanently.

**(2) `Game.RPC_SetConnection(long sender, ZDOID portalID, ZDOID connectionID)` (:100653-100662).** Registered on **every** peer, outside the `IsServer()` block (:100066-100070). No sender check, no ownership check, no prefab check: it takes ownership of the named ZDO, writes an arbitrary Portal connection, and ForceSendZDOs it. This is a complete portal-hijack primitive — and it also means a "lockdown" implemented by forcing every connection to `ZDOID.None` can be undone instantly by one malicious client. Prefix it with the same admin/server check. Keep in mind you must still let the *legitimate* vanilla path through: `Game.SetConnection` (:100637-100651) routes this RPC to an owning client, and the sender in that case is the server itself.

**(3) `ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO(long sender, ZDOID id)` (:77689-77692).** `GetPeer(sender)?.ForceSendZDO(id)` — using the *spoofable payload* `sender`. A client can force the server to push any ZDO it names to any other peer: a reconnaissance and amplification primitive (enumerate the whole world's portal set, or flood another player's connection). Prefix it to replace the payload `sender` with the authenticated peer's uid, which both closes the amplification and makes the legitimate `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` → `RequestZDO` path (:143650) work exactly as before.

**(4) `ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject(long spawner, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, int prefabHash)` (:82355-82366, registered :81954).** The one exception to "a dedicated server instantiates nothing" — it does a bare `Instantiate` of any prefab in `m_namedPrefabs`. Not portal-specific, but it is free unauthenticated server-side instantiation and belongs on the same hardening list.

All four prefixes are one shape: resolve the authentic peer from the ambient context, check admin, return false with an audit line if not. Each is a handful of lines and each closes a hole that would otherwise make several other options in this document decorative.


**Player experience:** Nothing changes for honest players. A player with a cheat client who tries `SetGlobalKey teleportall` to carry iron through portals finds the key never applies, gets a console-visible refusal (`ZNet.RemotePrint(peer.m_rpc, …)`, :81635), and appears in the admin audit. The server operator's `noportals` maintenance lockdown can no longer be cancelled by a player.


**Failure modes:**
- `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` stringifies PascalCase (`"NoPortals"`, :115938-115941) while the store holds only lowercase, so `RPC_SetGlobalKey`'s `!m_globalKeys.Contains(name)` dedupe (:116024) never trips and every call re-adds and re-broadcasts the entire key list. Your own server-side calls must use lowercase literals or pre-check with `GetGlobalKey`, or you create a broadcast storm.
- Hardening `RPC_SetGlobalKey` also blocks any *other* mod or vanilla client path that legitimately sets a key (e.g. the `setkey` console command issued by an admin client, which arrives via `ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand`, :81879-81889 — that one is already admin-gated, so allow it).
- `RPC_RequestZDO`'s spoofable sender is also how a *legitimate* client asks for a portal's destination ZDO. Replacing rather than rejecting is essential or you break `TargetFound` for everyone.
- `RPC_SetConnection` is vanilla's own cross-machine write protocol; a prefix that is too strict breaks `Game.SetConnection`'s deferred path and portals stop pairing near online players.
- `ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd` dereferences `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()` (:113506-113508) and its `UpdateWorldRates` tail dereferences `Minimap.instance` (:101203) with no null guards; these survive headless only because the dedicated build instantiates the GUI scene. Do not call them before Game/Minimap exist.

**Designer citations:** ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey / RPC_RemoveGlobalKey (no sender check) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:116022-116029, :116031-116037 ; ZoneSystem.Start server-only registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113444-113455 ; ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd mirrors into World.m_startingGlobalKeys — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113483-113513 (:113511) ; ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey PascalCase stringification — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115933-115946 ; Game.RPC_SetConnection (registered on every peer, no checks) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100066-100070, :100653-100662 ; Game.SetConnection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100637-100651 ; ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO uses payload sender — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77689-77692; registration :76156 ; ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82355-82366; registration :81954 ; ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand admin gate — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81879-81889 ; ZNet.RemotePrint — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81635-81648 ; ZNet.IsAdmin — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81811


**Open questions:**
- Does any vanilla client path legitimately invoke `SetGlobalKey` from a non-admin client in normal play (e.g. a boss defeat writing `defeated_*`, or `BaseAI.SetAlerted` writing `activeBosses` at :27258)? Those are written by whichever client owns the boss — blocking them would break progression. IN-GAME CHECK: log every `RPC_SetGlobalKey` with its authenticated sender over a boss fight and a full progression run before enabling the block; almost certainly you must allow the ordinal ≥ NonServerOption keys through and restrict only 0..40.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Do NOT gate RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey to admin/server only: boss-defeat keys, activeBosses and other progression keys are sent by non-admin clients through this RPC (Character.OnDeath :3153-3164, BaseAI.SetAlerted :27256-27260, BossStone :120184-120188, OfferingBowl :135738, ItemDrop :145637, :148013). Gate by key class: refuse gk < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption (ordinals 0-40, via GetKeyValue :113560-113581) from non-admins; allow NonServerOption keys from any authenticated peer.
- RPC_SetConnection on a dedicated server only ever runs for client-originated packets (Game.SetConnection targets the owning client peer, :100648, never self); refuse every non-admin invocation — there is no legitimate server-to-self path to preserve.
- The payload sender is never rewritten server-side (RPC_RoutedRPC :83634-83637 deserialises m_senderPeerID from the packet); the Authentic Sender Context must be a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC mapping the ZRpc to ZNet peer uid and stashing it for the handler prefixes.
- ZNet.RemotePrint delivers to the client's console window (:81644 rpc.Invoke("RemotePrint")), not the HUD; use the Player 'Message' RPC for a visible toast.
- 'SpawnObject' is dead vanilla API (no callers of ZNetScene.SpawnObject); it is also broadcast to 0L so each receiving client instantiates its own copy — refuse it entirely.
- Admin-only gating of RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey breaks vanilla. Ordinary non-admin clients legitimately send these: Character.OnDeath sets m_defeatSetGlobalKey (client decompile :3155-3158, i.e. defeated_*); BaseAI.SetAlerted sets activeBosses (:27256-27262 server copy, executed on the boss-owning client); pieces/items set and remove world keys (client :120924-120928, :136478, :146377, :148753); Ship sets AshlandsOcean (client :141499). The gate must be key-scoped: refuse from non-admins only keys with gk < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption (world modifiers) plus the mod's own private key names; pass everything GetKeyValue (:113560-113581) classifies as NonServerOption. Consequence: vanilla progression keys stay spoofable by any client.
- GlobalKeys.NonServerOption is ordinal 43 in this build (enum :101270-101326: NoMap=33, NoPortals=34, NoBossPortals=35, DungeonBuild=36, TeleportAll=37, NoHeavySnow=40, AllHeavySnow=41, Preset=42, NonServerOption=43), not 41.
- The four routed RPCs are not the only — or largest — unauthenticated write path. ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77137) accepts, from any peer, data for any ZDOID with a higher DataRevision, including the owner field and the Portal connection (ZDO.Deserialize :74228-74233), with no owner/prefab/sender check; it is the same channel vanilla owners use, so it cannot be blanket-refused. Hardening RPC_SetConnection therefore does not close the hijack primitive; connection re-assertion (Managed Network Governor) remains necessary.
- RPC_SetConnection needs no 'let the legitimate path through' carve-out. The server's own SetConnection delegation (:100649) targets the owner peer ≠ m_id, which InvokeRoutedRPC never self-dispatches (:83576-83583); no vanilla client code invokes RPC_SetConnection. Every inbound RPC_SetConnection at a dedicated server is illegitimate and can be rejected unconditionally. Registration line is :100067.
- RPC_RequestZDO amplification is bounded: the forced send still passes ZDOPeer.ShouldSend in AddForceSendZdos (:77270-77275), so a victim only receives ZDOs it does not already hold at the current revision. The reconnaissance use (enumerate by ZDOID against the attacker's own peer id) stands.
- RPC name is "SpawnObject" (registration :81954), handler RPC_SpawnObject; RemotePrint is console-only on the client (client RPC_RemotePrint :81879-81884 → Console.instance.Print), not HUD.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] All four holes verified. RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey (:116022-116037) registered server-only (:113445-113449) and ignore sender; GlobalKeyAdd mirrors gk < NonServerOption into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (:113487, :113511) which SaveWorldFWLData writes (:112581-112584, called from the save thread :80632). Game.RPC_SetConnection registered on every peer (:100066) with no checks (:100653-100662). RPC_RequestZDO uses payload sender (:77689-77692); RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID comes straight off the wire in RPC_RoutedRPC (:83634-83637) — nothing on the server rewrites it, so 'Authentic Sender Context' (prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC capturing the ZRpc) is a genuine prerequisite. ZNetScene 'SpawnObject' registered in Awake with no IsServer gate (:81954), handler does bare Instantiate (:82355-82366); vanilla never calls ZNetScene.SpawnObject (only definition at :82339-82343, zero callers), so blocking it breaks nothing. The critical error: a blanket admin/server-only prefix on RPC_SetGlobalKey breaks vanilla progression. Boss defeat keys are set by the boss's OWNING CLIENT — Character.OnDeath → SetGlobalKey(m_defeatSetGlobalKey) (:3153-3155) and the activeBosses decrement (:3162-3164); BaseAI.SetAlerted writes activeBosses (:27256-27260); OfferingBowl (:135738), ItemDrop use (:145637), BossStone set AND remove (:120184-120188), plus :148013 — all client-side, all non-admin, all via this same RPC. The prefix must be key-class-aware: refuse ordinals < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption (world modifiers, classified by GetKeyValue :113560-113581) from non-admins and pass NonServerOption keys (defeated_*, activeBosses, custom) from any authenticated peer; same for RemoveGlobalKey. RPC_SetConnection is simpler than stated: Game.SetConnection routes it to a client owner (:100648), so on a dedicated server the local handler runs only for client-originated packets — refuse all non-admin invocations outright, no 'let the legitimate path through' carve-out needed. RemotePrint (:81635-81644) prints to the F5 console, not the HUD.
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] All four handlers exist as described and validate nothing: ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey (:116022-116037) registered server-only in ZoneSystem.Start (:113446-113450); Game.RPC_SetConnection (:100653-100662) registered on every peer at :100067; ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692) uses the payload sender; ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject (:82355-82366) does a bare Instantiate, registered as "SpawnObject" at :81954. GlobalKeyAdd mirrors keys with gk < NonServerOption into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (:113483-113513). HandleRoutedRPC passes the spoofable payload m_senderPeerID (:83651) — confirmed. Prefixes on these do execute on the dedicated server, so the enforcement label is right for these four RPCs. Two corrections are load-bearing: the proposed admin-only gate on the global-key RPCs breaks vanilla progression, and the four RPCs are not the biggest hole — RPC_ZDOData is.

### 58. Progression Gate

`access-control:Progression Gate` · domain **access** · source `access-control`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Require a world global key before a network is wired at all — server-ENFORCED at the connection layer, which is strictly stronger than the client-honoured `NoPortals` key everyone reaches for first.


**How it works:** There are two completely different ways to gate portals on progression and they sit on opposite sides of the enforcement line.

**Client-honoured (weak).** Set `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` (ordinal 32) or `NoBossPortals` (33). `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey` is `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name)` (:115943-115946), which on the server self-dispatches synchronously to `RPC_SetGlobalKey` (:116022) and then `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` (:113466-113471) broadcasts the full key list; each client's `RPC_GlobalKeys` clears and rebuilds its set (:113473-113481). `TeleportWorld.Teleport` reads both keys **live at the moment of transit** (:143523, :143528) and refuses with `$msg_blocked` / `$msg_blockedbyboss`. This is genuinely vanilla-respecting — an unmodified client honours it exactly as it honours vanilla's own boss gating — and it reaches already-connected players within one network frame with no relog. But it is client-executed, so a modified client ignores it entirely, and it is world-wide, not per-network. It also gives **no visual warning**: `GetHoverText` still reports `$piece_portal_connected` and `UpdatePortal` still lights the target-found effect (:143453-143508), so a blocked portal looks completely normal until you walk in.

**Server-enforced (strong).** Gate the *connection* instead of the transit. The Managed Network Governor simply refuses to write a Portal connection for any portal whose network's required key is not present: `ZoneSystem.instance.GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.defeated_bonemass)` (:115948) is a plain dictionary lookup on the server. An unconnected portal cannot teleport anyone — `TeleportWorld.Teleport`'s gate 1 is `!TargetFound()` → silent return (:143519), and `TargetFound` requires a non-None connection (:143640-143655). A modified client cannot fake a connection into existence, because the destination comes from the ZDO the server owns and re-asserts. When the key appears, the governor wires the network on its next tick and the gates come alive.

Useful keys and their persistence, which differ sharply by ordinal (`GlobalKeys` enum :101270-101325): ordinals **0-40** are world-modifier keys — `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors them into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113511) which is persisted to the **.fwl** and stripped from the .db by `ZoneSystem.Save` (:113742-113760), and `SetStartingGlobalKeys` (:115904-115931) wipes ordinals 0..40 on every world load and re-adds only what the .fwl held — so a mod-owned world-modifier key must be reapplied in a **postfix** on `SetStartingGlobalKeys` (the Wonderland WorldRatesPatches pattern, WorldRatesPatches.cs:9-15), never a prefix, because a `preset` key (ordinal 40) causes `ServerOptionsGUI.SetPreset` to reapply a whole key set at :115920-115926. Ordinals **≥41** (`defeated_eikthyr` 42 … `defeated_bonemass` 46, plus any arbitrary custom string, which `GetKeyValue` classifies as `NonServerOption` at :113560-113581) go the other way: .db only, never .fwl. Progression keys are therefore in the .db and survive normally.

Custom keys work fine as gate conditions: any unrecognised string becomes a NonServerOption key persisted in the .db, which is how a mod records "this clan has unlocked the swamp network" (the FirstSpawnGrant `wonderland_starter_<id>` pattern). Set them with the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` + `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` if you want session-only semantics.


**Player experience:** Your server's `⌁HUB-SWAMP` gate stands finished in the hub from day one, glowing dead and reading `unconnected`. The hover text never changes and walking into it does nothing at all. The night the server kills Bonemass, the key lands, and within five seconds every swamp gate on the network snaps live simultaneously — the connected effect fires at each one and the hover reads `$piece_portal_connected`. No client mod, no relog, and no amount of client-side cheating opens it early, because there was never a destination to teleport to.


**Failure modes:**
- Unhardened, any client can set or clear the key (`RPC_SetGlobalKey` has no sender check, :116022). Requires Ungated RPC Hardening or the gate is decorative.
- `NoBossPortals` is a **world-wide blackout**, not a per-fight lock: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` checks `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() != null || activeBosses > 0` (:143528). One player aggroing Eikthyr blocks every portal for every player. Worse, `activeBosses` is maintained by whichever client has the boss loaded (`BaseAI.SetAlerted` :27258-27259), so a mid-fight client crash can leave it stuck above zero and portals permanently blocked — a server mod should watch for and zero it.
- `NoPortals` does **not** close dungeon/crypt doors: `Teleport.Interact` (:143345-143370) never reads it and never calls `IsTeleportable`. Advertise it as "disables all constructed portals", never "disables all teleporting".
- Setting a world-modifier key at runtime permanently edits the world's .fwl modifier list (:113511) — remove the mod later and `noportals` stays baked in. Use `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` for session-only.
- `GlobalKeys.TeleportAll` does not allow everything: `Inventory.IsTeleportable` rejects any item with `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` **before** consulting the key (:68860-68880).
- The Steam/PlayFab browser modifiers badge is snapshotted in `ZNet.OpenServer` (:79454-79480) and refreshed only on the registration-retry path, so a live toggle leaves the public listing stale. Cosmetic.

**Designer citations:** GlobalKeys enum with ordinals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:101270-101325 ; ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey / GetGlobalKey / RemoveGlobalKey — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115933-115946, :115948-115982, :115984-115992 ; ZoneSystem.SendGlobalKeys / RPC_GlobalKeys — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113466-113471, :113473-113481 ; ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd (mirror into m_startingGlobalKeys) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113483-113513 ; ZoneSystem.Save strips ordinals <41 from the .db — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113742-113760 ; ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys (wipes 0..40, preset reapply) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115904-115931 ; ZoneSystem.GetKeyValue classification — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113560-113581 ; TeleportWorld.Teleport gate order — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143517-143537 (:143519, :143523, :143528, :143533) ; TeleportWorld.TargetFound — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143640-143655 ; TeleportWorld.GetHoverText / UpdatePortal give no blocked affordance — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143508 ; Teleport.Interact never reads NoPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143345-143370 ; Inventory.IsTeleportable toolTier>=1000 pre-gate — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:68860-68880 ; BaseAI.SetAlerted writes activeBosses — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:27256-27262 ; Wonderland WorldRatesPatches re-assert postfix — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/WorldRatesPatches.cs:9-15


**Open questions:**
- Is `Minimap.instance` genuinely non-null on a headless 1.0.7 server? `GlobalKeyAdd` → `UpdateWorldRates` → `UpdateNoMap` dereferences it unguarded (:101199-101204). Wonderland calls GlobalKeyAdd live on a dedicated server, which is strong indirect evidence. IN-GAME CHECK: run `setkey noportals` on the dedicated console and confirm no NullReferenceException.
- Does `activeBosses` reliably return to 0 after a boss dies and after a client force-quits mid-fight? IN-GAME CHECK: `setkey nobossportals`, aggro a boss, alt-F4 the fighting client, then `listkeys` on the server console.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Enforcement scope: the connection gate is server-enforced against vanilla clients; against a modified client the Portal connection is plain ZDO data writable by the ZDO owner over RPC_ZDOData (ZDO.Deserialize :74219-74224; :77076-77140 has no owner check) and the local TeleportWorld honours the local copy — reactive-revert only there. Replace 'no amount of client-side cheating opens it early'.
- 'Session-only semantics' claim is wrong for custom/NonServerOption keys: ZoneSystem.Save strips only gk < NonServerOption (:113749-113753), so a custom key always persists in the .db regardless of canSaveToServerOptionKeys. Session-only behaviour is only available for ordinals 0-40 (wiped by SetStartingGlobalKeys :115906-115910).
- Teleport.Interact (dungeon doors) ignores NoPortals but does honour NoBossPortals inside an active boss dungeon (:143354-143358).
- Removing a required key later does not un-wire an existing network: vanilla phase 1 keeps connected same-tag pairs; the governor must actively write None when the key disappears.
- The prereq chain is heavier than 'small-medium': it inherits the Managed Network Governor (medium-large) and Ungated RPC Hardening; the standalone effort figure only covers the client-honoured key path.
- Ordinals are off by two throughout: GlobalKeys enum (:101270-101326) has NoMap=33, NoPortals=34, NoBossPortals=35, DungeonBuild=36, TeleportAll=37, NoPseudoDrops=38, NoBuildingFall=39, NoHeavySnow=40, AllHeavySnow=41, Preset=42, NonServerOption=43, defeated_eikthyr=44, defeated_dragon=45, defeated_goblinking=46, defeated_gdking=47, defeated_bonemass=48. The .fwl mirror (GlobalKeyAdd :113487) and the .db strip (ZoneSystem.Save :113749-113753) use gk < NonServerOption, i.e. ordinals 0..42; the SetStartingGlobalKeys wipe loop is the literal `for (int i = 0; i < 41; i++)` (:115906), i.e. 0..40 — AllHeavySnow and Preset are mirrored to the .fwl but not wiped. Preset detection (:115915-115918, SetPreset :115923) is by enum value, not ordinal 40.
- 'No amount of client-side cheating opens it early' is false. ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey (:116022-116029) accepts any string from any peer, and progression keys (defeated_*) cannot be admin-locked without breaking vanilla (Character.OnDeath sets them from the boss-owning client, client decompile :3155-3158). A protocol-level client sends SetGlobalKey defeated_bonemass and the governor wires the network on its next tick. Mitigation: gate on a mod-private key name that the hardening refuses from non-admins and that the server writes itself; note the server still has no first-hand boss-kill signal (it observes the client-reported key or the boss ZDO's client-reported death), so the gate is strong against vanilla and local-toggle cheats only.
- 'Session-only semantics' via GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false) is wrong: that flag only skips the .fwl mirror (:113487, :113509-113511). A NonServerOption key still enters m_globalKeys and is written to the .db by ZoneSystem.Save, whose RemoveWhere strips only gk < NonServerOption (:113749-113753). There is no session-only global key.
- The strong tier's prereq chain is self-inconsistent as written: if Ungated RPC Hardening is applied admin-only, defeated_bonemass never lands and the gate never opens. The hardening must be key-scoped (see that verdict).
- SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys) stringifies PascalCase (:115938-115941) while GlobalKeyAdd lowercases (:113487 keyStr.ToLower()); RPC_SetGlobalKey's m_globalKeys.Contains(name) pre-check (:116024) therefore misses for PascalCase input and re-runs GlobalKeyAdd (idempotent) — harmless, but do not rely on the Contains short-circuit.
- Line cites: Teleport gate order is :143517-143543 (TargetFound :143519, NoPortals :143521, NoBossPortals :143526, IsTeleportable :143531).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Client-honoured half verified: TeleportWorld.Teleport gate order is TargetFound → NoPortals → NoBossPortals(with boss event / activeBosses>0) → IsTeleportable (:143517-143537); GetHoverText only reports connected/unconnected (:143453-143463) and UpdatePortal's target_found effect ignores the keys (:143489-143506), so a blocked portal looks live. ### 59. Key-Item Requirement

`access-control:Key-Item Requirement` · domain **access** · source `access-control`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium-large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A network that only wires while a specified item sits in a designated container beside the gate — server-enforced, because the server can read container inventories even though it can never read a player's.


**How it works:** The server cannot see a traveller's inventory. `Player.Save` serialises inventory, skills, recipes and uniques into a `ZPackage` that `PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData` stores in `m_playerData` and writes only to that client's own `.fch` (:14091-14170, :105706-105711); `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles` (:79653-79670) merely tells each client to save its own disk file and returns nothing. An exhaustive scan of the Character/Humanoid/Player ZDO writes yields only vitals, identity, pose and equipment — never `s_items`. `ZDOVars.s_items` is written by exactly one live path, `Container.Save()` (:122294-122300). So "must be carrying X" is impossible; "must have deposited X" is easy.

Design: each managed portal may declare a *key container* — the nearest container ZDO within a configured radius, found with `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(portalPos, radius, buffer)` (Wonderland ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25) filtered by `ContainerRegistry.IsContainer` (ContainerRegistry.cs:58), and recorded by rounded position in the Portal Record Store. On each governor tick, for each such portal: read the container's inventory with `ZdoInventoryIO.Load` over the `s_items` byte blob, skipping any container with `ZDOVars.s_inUse` set (a player has the UI open — `Container.UpdateUseVisual` :121990-122000, `ZdoInventoryIO.IsBusy`); count the required item; if the requirement is met, write the Portal connection, otherwise write `ZDOID.None`. A consumed-toll variant additionally removes the item (`ZdoInventoryIO.MoveMatchingItem` with add-then-remove ordering) and journals it through the ItemLedger (ItemLedger.cs:43/:51) — never remove items without an audit trail.

This is genuinely server-enforced: an unconnected portal cannot teleport anyone, because `TeleportWorld.Teleport` returns silently at gate 1 when `!TargetFound()` (:143519, :143640-143655) and the destination is re-read from the live ZDO at the instant of transit (:143539-143543). A modified client cannot conjure a connection the server did not write, and the Managed Network Governor re-asserts the correct state every tick.

Equipment is a partial exception worth naming: `VisEquipment` mirrors the *visible equipped* items into the character's own ZDO as prefab stable hashes — `s_rightItem`, `s_leftItem`, `s_helmetItem`, `s_chestItem`, `s_legItem`, `s_shoulderItem`, `s_utilityItem`, `s_trinketItem`, the back slots (:20569-20708). So "must be **wielding** the Swamp Key" is server-readable in real time, unlike "must be carrying it". But it cannot gate a transit per-player (see Per-Player Transit Gate) — only whether the network is wired at all, which makes it a poor fit for a key-item mechanic with multiple users.


**Player experience:** The `⌁DEEPMINE` gate has a stone chest beside it with a plaque-sign reading `FEED ME IRON`. While the chest is empty the gate reads `unconnected` and walking into it does nothing. Drop a single iron bar in and within a couple of seconds the gate hums to life and connects to the mine. Take the bar back out and it goes dark again. In toll mode the bar disappears when the first traveller comes through, and the clan's Discord logs `⌁DEEPMINE toll: 1x Iron consumed (Bjorn).`


**Failure modes:**
- **All-or-nothing per network, never per player.** The connection is global; once the toll is paid the gate is open to everyone until it lapses. There is no way to charge each traveller.
- Container ownership races: the container's owning client rewrites `s_items` on every inventory change (`Container.Save` :122294-122300 runs from `OnContainerChanged` when IsOwner). A server write must claim ownership at the moment of commit and respect `s_inUse`, or it will silently lose the race or duplicate items. Use Wonderland's ZdoInventoryIO which already implements this discipline.
- The container can be moved, destroyed or replaced; the position-keyed binding must be re-validated each tick and the portal fails closed when the container is missing.
- `TargetFound` requires the client to actually hold the destination ZDO (:143646-143654); the first walk-through after a newly-written connection to a distant partner fails **silently** with no message at all. Pre-push with `ForceSendZDO(peerUid, targetId)` (:77714) when the connection is made.
- A toll that consumes items is a duplication/loss risk under any ZDO race. Journal every transfer and every rejection (ItemLedger pattern) and prefer a non-consuming "presence" requirement for anything valuable.
- Container ZDOs are ordinary sector ZDOs, not world-resident like portals — a container in an unloaded region may be absent from `FindNear`. Cache the last known contents and fail closed, not open.

**Designer citations:** Player.Save / PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData (inventory is local-file only) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:14091-14170, :105706-105711 ; ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles returns nothing — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79653-79670, :79672-79675 ; Container.Save / Load write ZDOVars.s_items — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:122294-122300, :122302-122324 ; Container.UpdateUseVisual writes s_inUse — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:121990-122000; ZDOVars.s_inUse :78673 ; VisEquipment mirrors equipped items into the character ZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:20569-20708 ; TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 / TargetFound — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143519, :143640-143655; destination re-read :143539-143543 ; ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(long, ZDOID) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77714 ; Wonderland ZdoInventoryIO — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs:68 and header :11-16 ; Wonderland ContainerRegistry — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ContainerRegistry.cs:58 ; Wonderland ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25 ; Wonderland ItemLedger — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ItemLedger.cs:43, :51


**Open questions:**
- How quickly does a container's `s_items` blob reach the server after a player drops an item in? `Container.Save` runs on the owner's OnContainerChanged and the ZDO syncs on the ~0.05s `ZDOMan` cadence, but the perceived latency matters for the UX. IN-GAME CHECK: drop an item and time the gate coming alive.

- Do not SetOwner the portal to the server session as part of the write; ZDO.Set/SetConnection need no ownership, and a server-held portal is handed back to any nearby peer within 2 s by ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76927) anyway.
- Replace 'A modified client cannot conjure a connection the server did not write' with: enforcement holds against vanilla clients only; a modified client can set its local connection field (Teleport reads the local ZDO, :143539) or push ZDO data with a bumped DataRevision (RPC_ZDOData has no owner/sender check, :77106-77132).

Document or write s_items without SetOwner (server ZDO.Set has no ownership check, :73648-73654).
- Toll consumption is reactive (position-jump heuristic); state explicitly that the traveller has already crossed when the item is removed.
- Fix citation: ContainerRegistry.IsContainer is ContainerRegistry.cs:45, not :58.

### 60. Team / Guild Networks

`access-control:Team / Guild Networks` · domain **access** · source `access-control`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium-large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A server-side roster keyed on platform-verified accounts, mapping players to named networks, with membership changes driven by emotes and enforced by the governor's refusal to wire non-members.


**How it works:** Valheim has no faction, guild or team concept for players. `PrivateArea.m_ownerFaction` exists but any non-zero value makes `PrivateArea.Interact` early-return (:137376) and routes damage handling down an entirely different path — it is for creature-faction structures, not player groups. There is no PvP team field on the character ZDO beyond `s_pvp` (a plain bool). So the roster has to be the mod's own.

Roster storage, two options with different properties:
- **World global keys.** `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey("tplite_net_<network>_<platformUserId>")` — an arbitrary string is classified as `NonServerOption` by `GetKeyValue` (:113560-113581) and therefore persisted in the **.db** and never in the .fwl. On the server `SetGlobalKey` self-dispatches synchronously (:115943-115946 → :116022), so the key is readable the instant it is set, and it travels with the world and its backups. This is the FirstSpawnGrant pattern (FirstSpawnGrant.cs:91, :185). Downside: the key set is broadcast in full to every client on every change (`SendGlobalKeys(0L)` :113466), so a large roster is real per-change bandwidth and every player can read every membership.
- **A mod file** alongside the Portal Record Store. Private, arbitrary structure, no broadcast cost. Preferred for anything beyond a handful of members; use global keys only for the small once-only facts.

Key on `PlatformUserID` (from `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`, the only platform-verified identity), not on `s_playerID` — `s_playerID` is a per-character-file value the client writes into its own ZDO (`Player.SetPlayerID` :10129-10136) and a player with several characters has several of them. Keep a secondary `playerID → PlatformUserID` map, learned each session while both halves are in hand (the Authentic Sender Context), so that ward permitted lists and `s_creator` values — which are playerID-shaped — can be resolved to accounts. `ZNetPeer.m_playerID` is useless: the server registers the `"PlayerID"` RPC (:79916, handler :80919-80927) but no vanilla client ever invokes it, so the field is permanently 0.

Enforcement is the Managed Network Governor plus the Portal ACL. A network name maps to a roster; a portal in that network is wired only to other portals in the same network; a portal carrying the network's tag whose owner is not on the roster is refused a partner and optionally re-tagged. Membership changes through emote commands with proximity (the CacheClaimControl shape): leader stands next to a candidate, `/challenge` to invite, candidate `/point` to accept, both get `PlayerNotify` toasts. Leadership and invite rights live in the roster record.

Cross-session identity resolution for *offline* members is why the roster must be account-keyed: `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` (:112396, persisted :112587-112591) gives you display names for every account that has ever played, and `s_creatorIndex` on any piece resolves into it — so an admin report can say "this portal was built by an account that last played in March and belongs to network VALHALLA" without that player ever logging in again.


**Player experience:** Your clan leader stands beside you and does the `/challenge` emote; you get a toast `Bjorn invites you to network VALHALLA — /point to accept.` You `/point` and get `You joined VALHALLA.` Every portal your clan tags `⌁VALHALLA` wires into the clan ring. A stranger who builds a portal and somehow sets the same tag gets nothing — his gate reads `unconnected` forever and he never learns why, because nothing in vanilla tells him. Months later, after you have all stopped playing, an admin's report still reads `⌁VALHALLA: 6 gates, network owner Bjorn (Steam:7656…), last active 2026-03-14`.


**Failure modes:**
- The whole roster is mod-side state with no vanilla backing. A corrupted or deleted file orphans every network; back it up alongside the world save and reconcile on boot.
- Emote-driven invites are ambiguous when several players stand close together. Require the nearest candidate within a tight radius and confirm by name in the toast.
- `s_playerID` is per-character, so a player switching characters appears as a new identity to anything keyed on it. Always resolve through the account map.
- `ZNetPeer.m_playerID` is always 0 (the `"PlayerID"` RPC is registered at :79916 but never invoked by any vanilla client). Reading it looks correct and yields nothing.
- Global-key rosters are world-readable by every client and re-broadcast on every change (`SendGlobalKeys(0L)` clears and rebuilds the client's set, :113473-113481). Not suitable for anything private or large.
- Players cannot see their own network membership except through toasts you send them. There is no vanilla UI to hook.

### 61. Retag Rate Limit

`access-control:Retag Rate Limit` · domain **access** · source `access-control`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** reactive-detection-only → **reactive-detection-only** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A per-account token bucket on tag and connection changes, enforced by reverting everything over budget and escalating to an ownership pin or a kick — the defence against flap attacks and scripted tag churn.


**How it works:** The Tag Watchdog is a revert loop, and a revert loop can be attacked by out-writing it. A scripted client pushing `RPC_ZDOData` with a bumped DataRevision every frame will make a contested portal flap between the attacker's tag and yours at whatever rate your tick runs, generating a `ForceSendZDO` broadcast to every peer on each revert (`ZDOMan.SendZDOs` re-serialises the **entire** ZDO with no delta encoding, :77053-77062) — so the attacker turns your defence into an amplifier against your own bandwidth.

The rate limit sits in the watchdog's policy chain, before the ALLOW/DENY decision:
- Per account (keyed on the notarised `PlatformUserID`), a token bucket: N tag changes per window, refilling at R per minute, configurable, with a separate and smaller budget for connection changes.
- Per portal, a cooldown: after a successful retag, further retags of the same portal are refused for T seconds regardless of who asks. This is also the anti-squatting cooldown — it stops a griefer cycling a contested tag faster than the legitimate owner can respond.
- Exhausting the bucket escalates in stages: (1) revert and toast; (2) apply a temporary Ownership Pin to the contested portal, which makes further retags physically impossible because `RPC_SetTag` now routes to a server with no instance (:82855-82858, :83656-83664) — this is the stage that actually stops the attack rather than absorbing it; (3) `ZNet.instance.Kick(hostName)` (:81658) or `Ban` (:81744), both public and server-side, resolving by PlatformUserID exactly as vanilla's adminlist does.
- Suppress the broadcast half of the revert while flapping: `ZDO.Set` is a no-op when the value is unchanged (`BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false, assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345, so `IncreaseDataRevision` is skipped), so re-asserting an already-correct tag is genuinely free — but the first revert after each attacker write is not. Cap reverts-with-broadcast per sweep the way Wonderland's StructureUpkeep caps health broadcasts at 256 (StructureUpkeep.cs:29-40), and prefer stage (2) over grinding.

All counters live in the Portal Record Store (`lastRetagAt`, `retagCount`) and a per-account in-memory bucket rebuilt on boot; nothing needs to persist beyond a rolling window except the abuse tally you want in the audit trail.

Be honest about the classification: this is reactive-detection-only in stages 1, and becomes server-enforced only at stage 2. A rate limit alone never prevents the first offence.


**Player experience:** An honest player renaming their portal a few times while deciding on a name notices nothing. A player who renames the same portal fifteen times in a minute gets `Slow down — that gate was just renamed.` and the change is refused for thirty seconds. A scripted attacker hammering a contested portal sees the tag lock solid after a few seconds — the gate becomes server-held and stops responding to them entirely — and an admin gets a Discord alert naming their Steam ID and the portal's coordinates.


**Failure modes:**
- Stage 1 absorbs the attack rather than stopping it, and each revert costs a full-ZDO broadcast to every peer (no delta encoding, :77053-77062). Escalate to the pin quickly.
- Attribution depends on the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix catching the packet; a change whose sender cannot be resolved must be charged to nobody, which means an unattributable attacker is only rate-limited per-portal, not per-account. Rely on the per-portal cooldown for that case.
- A per-portal cooldown can be weaponised: a griefer retags your portal once, and your own corrective retag is refused for T seconds. Exempt the record's owner and admins from the per-portal cooldown.
- Kicking on a false positive (a laggy client re-pushing a stale ZDO repeatedly) is a bad outcome. Require sustained abuse over a long window and log heavily before ever enabling stage 3.
- `ZNet.Kick`/`Ban` resolve by PlatformUserID or player name via `InternalKick` (:81689); player names are not unique, so always pass the host name.

**Designer citations:** ZNetView.InvokeRPC targets the owner; server has no instance — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82855-82858, :83656-83664 ; ZDOMan.SendZDOs full re-serialisation, no delta — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77053-77062; ZDOPeer.ShouldSend :76003-76015 ; ZDO.Set no-ops on unchanged value (skips IncreaseDataRevision) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73601-73607; BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue — assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345 ; ZNet.Kick / Ban / InternalKick — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81658, :81744, :81689 ; ZNet.RemotePrint — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81635-81648 ; Wonderland StructureUpkeep broadcast cap — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/StructureUpkeep.cs:29-40

IN-GAME CHECK: instrument the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix and count portal-ZDO arrivals per second per peer under normal play to set a sane threshold.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Stage 2 (Ownership Pin) does not stop a scripted RPC_ZDOData attacker: RPC_ZDOData applies owner, revisions and all data from any peer's packet with no sender/owner check (:77108-77127). Reclassify stage 2 as vanilla-client-only; the attack in the threat model is stopped only by stage 3 kick/ban.
- Stage 2 against vanilla clients additionally requires a Harmony patch on ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76927): IsInPeerActiveArea(point, m_sessionID) is always false server-side (:76887-76891, ref pos 1e6), so a server-held portal is re-assigned to any nearby peer every 2 s.
- Add revision-jump defence: DataRevision is uint (:73494) and the server adopts the client's value (:77120); reject or clamp implausible jumps before Deserialize, or a wrapped revision makes every server revert invisible to peers.
- Key the bucket on the RPC_ZDOData sender (ZDOPeer via FindPeer(rpc), :77078) and note it identifies the portal's current owner, not necessarily the player who typed the tag; s_tagauthor (:143597) is client-supplied and spoofable.
- The claim 'becomes server-enforced only at stage 2' should read: stage 2 is client-honoured (vanilla only, with ReleaseNearbyZDOS patched); stage 3 is server-enforced.
- Delete 'becomes server-enforced only at stage 2' and 'makes further retags physically impossible'. RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77139) has no sender/owner check; a scripted client pushes ZDO data directly and also rewrites the owner field from the packet (:77126-77128). The Ownership Pin only blocks vanilla RPC_SetTag.
- The pin decays within 2 s: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76874-76880 cadence, :76901-76927 body) reassigns a server-owned portal to any peer in whose active area it sits because IsInPeerActiveArea(pos, m_sessionID) (:76885-76889) tests the pinned server reference position (:100463). Requires sub-2 s re-assertion or a ZDO.SetOwner Harmony guard (Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301).
- Per-account attribution: the ZDOData sender is the portal's owner peer, not necessarily the typist; s_tagauthor (:143588) is client-asserted. State that the bucket keys on the owning peer / s_tagauthor and can misattribute at shared hubs.
- Stage 3 (ZNet.Kick :81658 / Ban :81744) is the only mechanism that actually stops a scripted attacker; say so.
- Classification stays reactive-detection-only end-to-end; feasibility becomes feasible-with-caveats.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:downgraded] Detection and bucket side holds: ZDOMan.SendZDOs serialises the whole ZDO per send (:77053-77062), ZDOPeer.ShouldSend is revision-based (:76003-76013), ZDO.Set no-ops when BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue returns false on an equal value (assembly_valheim_SERVER :73601-73607; assembly_utils_SERVER :321-329) so IncreaseDataRevision is skipped, ZNet.Kick/Ban are public server-side (:81658, :81744) resolving via PlatformUserID.TryParse in InternalKick (:81689-81700). The load-bearing claim — stage 2 Ownership Pin 'makes further retags physically impossible' and is 'the stage that actually stops the attack' — fails against the attacker the option itself defines (a scripted client pushing RPC_ZDOData). RPC_ZDOData has no sender or owner check: when the packet's DataRevision exceeds the server's, it unconditionally sets OwnerRevision, DataRevision, owner and all data including tag and connection (:77108-77127; connection at :74227-74233). Ownership is just another field in that packet; the pin is overwritten by the next push. The pin only blocks VANILLA clients, because SetText → ZNetView.InvokeRPC routes to m_zdo.GetOwner() (:82855-82858) and the server's HandleRoutedRPC drops it when FindInstance returns null (:83656-83664), and the client-side RPC_SetTag is also gated on IsOwner (:143587). Even that requires the mod to Harmony-patch ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS: IsInPeerActiveArea(point, m_sessionID) tests against the server's (1e6,0,1e6) reference position (:76887-76891) so it is always false, and the pinned portal is handed to any nearby peer within 2 s (:76901-76927, timer :76873-76884). Against the scripted attacker only stage 3 (kick/ban) terminates the flood. Additional hardening gap: an attacker can push DataRevision near uint.MaxValue (DataRevision is uint, :73494); the server adopts it (:77120) and the next revert increments/wraps, after which the server's writes are ≤ every peer's recorded revision. The RPC_ZDOData sender is the portal's owner, not necessarily the typist when two players are near the portal.
- [vanilla-reality:downgraded] The amplification premise is real: ZDOMan.SendZDOs serialises the whole ZDO (:77053-77062) and AddForceSendZdos delivers to every peer whose ShouldSend passes, including peers that never had the ZDO (:77262-77282, :76003-76015). ZDO.Set no-op on unchanged value is real (Set -> ZDOExtraData.Set -> InitAndSet -> BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue returns false, assembly_utils_SERVER :321-330, so IncreaseDataRevision :73832 is skipped). Kick/Ban are public and server-side (:81658-81666, :81744-81752). But the stage that the option says 'actually stops the attack' does not, against the attacker it describes: (1) ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData has no sender or owner check — any peer's packet with num4 > DataRevision is applied wholesale, including SetOwnerInternal from the packet (:77106-77132). A scripted client pushing RPC_ZDOData bypasses the Ownership Pin entirely; the pin only blocks the vanilla RPC_SetTag path (InvokeRPC to owner :82855-82858; HandleRoutedRPC finds no server instance :83656-83664). (2) Even against a vanilla client the pin decays: ReleaseNearbyZDOS runs every 2 s (:76874-76880) and IsInPeerActiveArea(pos, m_sessionID) tests the server's reference position (:76885-76889), pinned to (1e6,0,1e6) by Game.FixedUpdate (:100463), so any peer within the active area gets ownership back within 2 s (:76920-76923) and can retag again. Holding a pin requires a <2 s re-assert or a Harmony guard on ZDO.SetOwner (Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-302). (3) Attribution is weaker than claimed: a retag arrives as ZDO data from whichever peer OWNS the portal, which is the typist only if ReleaseNearbyZDOS assigned it to them; with two players at a hub the other player's peer is the sender. s_tagauthor (:143588 written from the client's own PlatformUserID) is the only per-retag identity and it is client-asserted. So the 'notarised PlatformUserID' bucket keys on the owner peer, not necessarily the typist. Net: stage 1 is reactive detection, stage 2 is a vanilla-client-only speed bump with a 2 s hole, stage 3 (kick/ban) is the only real stop and it is out-of-band. The line 'becomes server-enforced only at stage 2' must be deleted.

### 62. Password Tags

`access-control:Password Tags` · domain **access** · source `access-control`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** reactive-detection-only → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Using the tag string itself as a shared secret — RULED OUT as secrecy (the tag is visible to anyone who hovers the portal) but viable as a shared token that only members are told.


**How it works:** The naive design: a network's tag is a secret string; you can only join by knowing it. It does not survive contact with the hover label.

`TeleportWorld.GetHoverText` (:143453-143463) builds its text from `GetTagInfo()` (:143561-143573), which reads `ZDOVars.s_tag` straight off the ZDO, and the hover appears for **any** player who looks at the portal — there is no ownership or ward check on hovering. `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` gates `Interact` (the rename dialog) but not `GetHoverText`. So every member of your network is walking advertising: anyone who finds one of your gates reads the password off it. The secret has zero entropy against an attacker who has seen one portal, and vanilla's 10-character client-side input cap (`TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)`, :143482) means the secret can be at most 10 typeable characters anyway. It is also strictly weaker than the Managed Network Governor, which does not care what the attacker knows.

What *does* work is the degenerate but useful version: the tag is not a secret, it is a **token you must be told**, and the actual authorisation is the roster. The password-shaped part is a convenience — a player who knows the network name types it and, if their account is on the roster, the governor wires them in; if not, the tag sticks (or reverts, by policy) but no connection is ever made. This gives the *feel* of a password with none of the false security, and it fails safe.

A second, genuinely secret variant is possible but needs a different channel: keep the network identity in a mod-private ZDO key (`tp_net`) rather than in `s_tag`, set it via an emote command or a map ping rather than the rename box, and leave `s_tag` as a cosmetic display name. The mod-private key is not shown by any vanilla UI — nothing in the client reads it — so it genuinely is not visible to a hovering stranger. It survives a client's ZDO push because `ZDODataHelper.ReadData` only adds the keys present in a packet and never clears (:74718-74730). But then the tag no longer drives pairing at all, which means vanilla's `Game.ConnectPortals` will happily tear your topology down on its 5s tick (:100601) — so this variant *requires* the Managed Network Governor to replace pairing entirely.

Either way, be blunt in the mod's documentation: a tag is public. There is no secret-bearing field a vanilla client displays only to authorised players.


**Player experience:** Honest version: your clan's gates all read `⌁VALHALLA`. Anyone can read that. A stranger types `⌁VALHALLA` on his own portal and it stays named that — and never connects to anything, because his account is not on the roster. He has the password and it buys him nothing. Secret version: your gates read whatever cosmetic names you like (`Front Gate`, `The Mine`), the network binding is invisible, and a stranger has no way to even discover what network he would need to join.


**Failure modes:**
- **The hover label is public.** `GetHoverText` has no access check (:143453-143463). Any design that treats `s_tag` as confidential is broken on contact.
- 10-character typeable limit on the client side (:143482) caps the entropy of anything a player enters.
- The secret-in-a-mod-key variant divorces pairing from `s_tag`, so vanilla's 5s reconcile (:100601) will destroy your topology unless the governor fully replaces `Game.ConnectPortals`.
- A mod-private key can be read (and forged) by a modified client that inspects its own ZDO copies — it is obscure, not secret.
- If the policy is "reject the tag" rather than "reject the connection", an honest player who mistypes a network name gets a confusing revert; prefer refusing the connection and explaining in a toast.

### 63. Per-Player Transit Gate

`access-control:Per-Player Transit Gate` · domain **access** · source `access-control`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **not-enforceable** · **Effort:** large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Making a portal work for one player and not another — RULED OUT. The connection is a single global ZDO field read by the traveller's own client; there is no per-player dimension anywhere in the mechanism.


**How it works:** This is the feature most people want first ("portals that only work for the player who built them", "PIN-protected portals", "only clan members may travel"), and it cannot be built server-side. The reasons compound:

**1. The transit decision is 100% client-executed with no server hook.** `TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` has exactly one call site in the entire assembly: `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter(Collider)` (:143664-143682, call at :143679), gated on `colliderIn.GetComponent<Player>() != null && Player.m_localPlayer == component`. A dedicated server has no trigger collider, no Player GameObject and a null `m_localPlayer` — and the deeper cause is that `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition((1e6,0,1e6))` every physics tick in the server build (:100458-100466, a line absent from the client's `Game.FixedUpdate` at :100886), so `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` (:82268-82276) never instantiates any world ZDO. No packet is sent at the moment of transit; the server learns about it only from the character ZDO's position changing afterwards.

**2. The destination is one field with no player dimension.** `ZDOExtraData.s_connections` is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` and `ZDOConnection` is `{readonly ConnectionType m_type; readonly ZDOID m_target;}` (:74797, :75524-75534) — one connection per ZDO, no list, no per-player slot. `Teleport()` resolves it with a bare `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(GetConnectionZDOID(Portal))` (:143539) and reads that ZDO's position and rotation. Whatever the server writes is what *everyone* gets.

**3. Every per-portal behavioural knob is a compiled field.** `m_allowAllItems`, `m_exitDistance`, `m_activationRange`, `m_proximityRoot` and all the colour/effect references (:143411-143437) are plain Inspector values with zero ZDO or RPC involvement. Harmony-writing them server-side mutates a copy no client will ever read.

**4. There is no server-side prompt.** A PIN needs a text-entry dialog at the moment of use; `TextInput` is a client UI singleton driven by `TeleportWorld.Interact` (:143471-143484), which the server never runs. TortalPortal's own PIN feature is client-side by construction (`SecurityPatch.CanConfigure` reads `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().GetPlayerID()`, SecurityPatch.cs:51 — and on a dedicated server `GetPlayerProfile()` returns a junk profile named "Stranger" with a random UID created in `Game.Awake` at :100047, so every vanilla `IsCreator`/`IsMine`/`IsOwner` helper silently returns garbage rather than throwing).

**5. You cannot even check what the traveller is carrying.** The player's inventory is never networked (see Key-Item Requirement); the ore check `player.IsTeleportable(m_allowAllItems)` (:143533 → `Inventory.IsTeleportable` :68860-68880) is unreproducible server-side.

**The three closest approximations, and their honest limits:**
- **Time-sliced connection rotation.** Poll the owner's character ZDO position and write the connection only while they are within N metres of the portal; write `ZDOID.None` otherwise. The destination is re-read at the instant of transit and is *not* cached (:143539-143543), so this takes effect immediately. But `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` fires on **enter only** — a player already standing in the volume when you change it will not re-trigger; they must step out and back in. And it is a race: any other player inside the volume at the moment the connection is live travels too.
- **Server-driven forced teleport.** `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, true)` (handler `Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` :41962-41968, registered in `Chat.Awake` :41627) or the ZDO-scoped `"RPC_TeleportTo"` (`Character.RPC_TeleportTo` :4126-4132, registered :886) moves any vanilla client with no client install and is genuinely per-player — the server chooses who moves and where. Trigger it from an emote or a map ping rather than from portal geometry. This is a *different feature* (a warp command), not a portal, and it bypasses every vanilla rule including the ore check and `NoPortals`. It also silently no-ops if the target teleported within the last 2s (`Player.TeleportTo` :15302-15326), is dead (`UpdateTeleport` runs only in the `!IsDead()` branch of `Player.FixedUpdate`, :10213/:10226 — a teleport sent to a dead player latches `m_teleporting = true` and never executes), or is attached/sleeping (`UpdateAttach` re-snaps the transform every tick before `UpdateTeleport`, :10217/:10226; `AttachStop` early-returns while `m_sleeping`, :15890-15918 — pre-check `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed)`).
- **`ZNetView.LoadFields` per-portal overrides.** `LoadFields` (:82669, client copy assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82898-82970) runs in `ZNetView.Awake` and reflects over every public instance field of every component on the prefab, overriding from the ZDO under `"<TypeName>.<FieldName>"` keys gated by the ZDO bools `HasFields` / `HasFields<TypeName>`. So a server can make `TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems` genuinely per-portal on a 100% vanilla client by writing three ZDO values — a real and under-appreciated capability. But it is still **per-portal, not per-player**, it is client-honoured rather than enforced, and it only applies at instantiation, so a flip does not reach players already standing there; they must leave the area and return.

Ship the feature as "private networks" (the governor refuses to wire outsiders in) rather than "private portals" (the gate refuses outsiders at the threshold). The first is enforceable; the second is not.


**Player experience:** What players will ask for: "my portal should only work for me." What you can honestly deliver: their portal connects only to *their* network's other portals and no stranger's gate can ever be wired into it — but if a stranger walks into their portal, they will travel, because the client made that decision locally and the server was never consulted. Say this in the mod description. The approximation people find acceptable in practice is the proximity-gated hub: a gate that is simply dark (`unconnected`, no glow, walking through does nothing) unless its owner is nearby.


**Failure modes:**
- Time-sliced rotation leaks to anyone in the trigger volume during the live window, and does not re-trigger for someone already standing in it (`OnTriggerEnter` is enter-only, :143672-143681).
- Forced teleport is not a portal: it bypasses `NoPortals`, `NoBossPortals`, `PrivateArea` and the ore check entirely, and gives the server no success/failure signal at all — `Player.TeleportTo`'s bool return is discarded by both RPC handlers (:41966, :4130). The only confirmation is watching the character ZDO's position change ~2s later.
- `distantTeleport: false` rubber-bands the player back to origin with a misleading `$msg_portal_blocked` when `ZoneSystem.FindFloor` misses (:15369-15374). Always send `true` for a forced teleport; it force-lands on solid ground at t=15s and can never fail.
- `LoadFields` overrides apply only at `ZNetView.Awake` (:82631) — a per-portal `m_allowAllItems` flip does not reach anyone already at the portal.
- `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` returns true for everything server-side (m_allAreas empty) and `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile()` returns a junk "Stranger" profile (:100047) — every vanilla ownership helper silently lies rather than throwing. Never call them.

**Open questions:**

This is the single highest-value unverified capability in the whole research set — it would make per-portal (not per-player) item policy real with zero client install. IN-GAME CHECK: write the three ZDO values from the server onto one portal, have a player leave and re-enter the area carrying ore, and see whether the transit is allowed.
- Does `TeleportWorld` sit on the prefab root or a child? `LoadFields` uses `GetComponentsInChildren<MonoBehaviour>` (:82676) so it should reach either, but the `HasFields<TypeName>` gate key is `TeleportWorld` regardless of depth. IN-GAME CHECK: log the component hierarchy of the portal prefab.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Time-sliced rotation: 'any other player inside the volume at the moment the connection is live travels too' overstates it — OnTriggerEnter fires only on entry (:143673), so a bystander already inside does not travel either; only a player who ENTERS during the live window does.
- TortalPortal SecurityPatch.CanConfigure begins at SecurityPatch.cs:50; the GetPlayerProfile().GetPlayerID() read is at :59, not :51.
- Client LoadFields also has callers at assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:44450 and :103150 besides Awake (:82860); none re-runs for an already-instantiated portal, so the 'must leave and return' caveat stands.
- Time-sliced connection writes succeed only if the server's DataRevision exceeds the owning client's; the server adopts the client's revision on every push (:77120) before incrementing, so this holds barring a same-tick client write.
- LoadFields keys written to a portal ZDO are only persisted when DirtyPortalObjects is set for that save cycle (:77621-77631); call ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702) after writing HasFields/HasFieldsTeleportWorld/TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems.
- Dead-player latch (m_teleporting=true with UpdateTeleport skipped, :10213/:10226) is cleared on respawn because a new Player object is instantiated; it is a lost command, not a permanent stuck state.
- Forced teleport into an unloaded area holds the player at the target until IsAreaReady/FindFloor succeed, up to 8 s (distant) or 15 s fallback (:15350-15376).

### 64. PortalCensus — the single-source-of-truth index engine

`ops-admin:PortalCensus — the single-source-of-truth index engine` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A 1 Hz main-thread snapshot of every portal ZDO in the world, built from ZDOMan's own always-resident portal registry, that every other ops engine reads and none of them writes.


**How it works:** Tick from the subsystem's OnUpdate at a configurable interval (default 1.0 s; floor 0.25 s). Each tick call `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648), which flattens the private `m_portalObjects` dictionary (:76039) into a fresh `List<ZDO>` — one allocation of P refs, P = world portal count. For a zero-alloc read-only hot path use `GetPortals()` (:77643), which returns the live dictionary; never mutate it.

For each ZDO build an immutable record: `m_uid` (ZDOID), `GetPrefab()` (:73876), `GetPosition()` (:73822), `GetRotation()` (:73827), `GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` (s_tag :78617), `GetString(ZDOVars.s_tagauthor)` (:78619), `GetConnectionZDOID(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal)` (:74002), `GetOwner()` (:74608), `GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator)` (:78393), `GetInt(ZDOVars.s_creatorIndex, -1)` (:78395), and DataRevision. Biome comes from `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(Vector3)` (:151692) — pure procedural noise, no colliders, safe headless. Do NOT use `ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight`/`IsBlocked`/`FindFloor`: they are `Physics.Raycast` (ZoneSystem.Awake mask build :113419-113425) and always return the no-hit fallback because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f,0f,1000000f))` every tick (:100465).

Key the index by a **rounded world position** (0.5 m grid), not ZDOID: `ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)` (:74552) so every ZDOID is renumbered on world load. Hold ZDOIDs only for the current session and re-resolve each tick with `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id)` (:76754) — `ZDOPool.Release` calls `ZDO.Reset()` which zeroes `m_uid` (:73536-73545), so a cached ZDO object reference can silently become a different object.

Diff this tick's tuple against last tick's to produce a change event stream (tag/author/connection/position/owner). Publish the snapshot as an immutable DTO list so background threads (HTTP, Discord) never touch ZDOMan.


**Player experience:** Nothing. This engine performs zero writes. An operator sees one log line at OnWorldReady — `[Census] 214 portals across 61 tags, 3 unpaired` — and after that only the derived reports produced by other engines. A player standing at a gate notices no hitch, no glow change, no hover-text change.


**Failure modes:**
- Caching ZDO object references across ticks: ZDOPool recycles the object and Reset() sets m_uid = ZDOID.None (:73536-73545), so the record silently points at an unrelated ZDO.
- Assuming the ZDOID is a stable identity — it is renumbered on every world load (:74552), so any on-disk index keyed by ZDOID resolves to nothing after a restart (the exact bug TortalPortal/Favorites.cs:109-124 hit and fixed by switching to a rounded-position key).
- Trusting the m_portalObjects dictionary key as a location: AddIfPortal files a portal under the sector it had when it was registered and ZDO.SetSector early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73756), so the key goes stale if anything ever moves a portal. Always read zdo.GetPosition().
- Calling ZoneSystem ground/solid/lava helpers for the biome or height column and getting a plausible-looking but meaningless fallback with no error and no log.

**Designer citations:** ZDOMan.GetPortalList — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648 ; ZDOMan.GetPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77643 ; ZDOMan.m_portalObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76039 ; ZDO.GetConnectionZDOID — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74002 ; ZDOVars.s_tag / s_tagauthor — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78617, :78619 ; ZDOVars.s_creator / s_creatorIndex — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78393, :78395 ; WorldGenerator.GetBiome(Vector3) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:151692 ; ZoneSystem.Awake raycast mask setup — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113419-113425 ; Game.FixedUpdate reference-position pin — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100465 ; ZDO.Load ZDOID renumber — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74552 ; ZDO.Reset — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73536-73545 ; ZDO.SetSector portal early-return — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73752-73756


**Open questions:**
- What is P in practice on a long-running world? Log `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList().Count` alongside `ZDOMan.instance.NrOfObjects()` (:77658) at boot and hourly for a week; this sets whether 1 Hz is wasteful or fine.
- Which prefabs are in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021, filled Game.Awake :100029-100031)? Log each hash resolved through `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)?.name` at OnWorldReady — this is the only authoritative list and it picks up modded portal pieces for free.

- Portal ZDOs are still keyed in m_portalObjects by the SectorIndex captured at insertion; a portal moved by a mod (not possible in vanilla) would not be re-bucketed — irrelevant for vanilla clients, but do not rely on the dictionary key for position.
- Citation nits only: :73876 is a blank line (GetPrefab is immediately adjacent); :76754 is GetZDO as claimed; everything else lands on the named member.

### 65. Full-realm portal enumeration report (the canonical data model)

`ops-admin:Full-realm portal enumeration report (the canonical data model)` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


One report record per portal — tag, position, biome, zone, connection, partner tag, owner peer, builder, tag author, first-seen and last-changed — rendered into every output surface from a single DTO.


**How it works:** Define one DTO and render it N ways. Fields and their exact sources:

- `id` — rounded-position key `x:y:z` at 0.5 m (durable across restarts).
- `sessionZdoId` — `zdo.m_uid.ToString()` (`ZDOID.ToString` yields `userID:ID`, :75884). Marked explicitly as session-scoped.
- `prefab` — `zdo.GetPrefab()` resolved via `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)?.name` (:82045). Needs an in-game check that the prefab table is populated headless.
- `tag` / `tagAuthor` — `GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` / `s_tagauthor`. Emit `tagAuthorTrusted: false` always: `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` writes the client-supplied authorId verbatim with no cross-check (:143587-143602).
- `pos` / `rot` — `GetPosition()` / `GetRotation()`.
- `biome` — `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(pos)` (:151692). `zone` — `ZoneSystem.GetZone(pos)` (:115741).
- `interior` — `Character.InInterior(pos)` i.e. `pos.y > 3000f` (:4538-4541); flags a portal built inside a dungeon, whose XZ zone is identical to the surface above it.
- `connection` — `GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal)`; resolve to the partner record and emit `partnerTag`, `partnerPos`, `reciprocal` (does the partner point back), `distance`.
- `ownerPeer` — `GetOwner()` (:74608) joined against `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` `m_uid` (:81630, ZNetPeer.m_uid :78786). 0 = unowned; `ZDOMan.GetSessionID()` (:77362) = server-owned.
- `builder` — `GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator)` joined against `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` via `s_creatorIndex` (World.m_playerHistory :112396, persisted SaveWorldFWLData :112587) to get an authenticated PlatformUserID.
- `firstSeen` / `lastChanged` — **mod-maintained**. Vanilla stores no wall-clock on a ZDO: the whole field set is `m_uid, m_rotation, m_position, m_tempSortValue, m_prefab, m_dataFlags, m_tempRemoveEarmark` (:73309-73321) plus DataRevision/OwnerRevision. Stamp `DateTime.UtcNow` the first tick a change is observed and persist the map alongside the network file.


**Player experience:** No player-visible effect. An operator running `tplite.list HUB` in their in-game F5 console sees, printed back into that console: `HUB  (3 portals)` then `#1 (0.0, 32.0, 4.0) Meadows z(0,0) -> #2 'HUB' 2140m  owner:server  built-by:Rohan  tagged-by:76561198… (untrusted)  changed 4h ago`. The same rows land in `portals.json`, in a Discord embed, and in the SVG map.


**Failure modes:**
- Reporting `tagauthor` as ownership. It is a forgeable client self-report (:143587-143602) and can disagree with `s_creator`, which is the placer's profile UID written by their own client in Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424).
- `s_creator == 0` on world-generated or very old portals — Piece.SetCreator only writes when `GetCreator() == 0 && m_nview.IsOwner()` (:136417). Render as 'unknown builder', never as 'nobody'.
- `s_creatorIndex == -1` when the placer was not yet in m_playerHistory at placement time — the PlatformUserID join silently yields nothing.
- Emitting ZDOID as the stable id in an exported file that an operator then scripts against; it changes on every restart.

**Designer citations:** ZDOID.ToString — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75884 ; ZDO field set (no timestamp) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73309-73321 ; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag unverified authorId — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143587-143602 ; Piece.SetCreator — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:136415-136424 ; ZNet.World.m_playerHistory — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:112396; persisted World.SaveWorldFWLData :112587 ; ZoneSystem.GetZone — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115741 ; Character.InInterior(Vector3) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:4538-4541 ; ZNetScene.GetPrefab(int) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82045 ; ZNet.GetPeers / ZNetPeer.m_uid — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81630, :78786 ; ZDOMan.GetSessionID — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77362


**Open questions:**
- Does `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)` return non-null on the dedicated server build? The prefab table is built in ZNetScene.Awake (:81941-81952) but nothing is instantiated. Log `GetPrefab(Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash[0])?.name` at OnWorldReady; if null, the report must carry raw hashes.
- Is `ZDOVars.s_creator` reliably non-zero on a player-placed portal in 1.0.7? Place one on a vanilla client, dump `s_creator` server-side, and confirm it equals that character ZDO's `s_playerID` (:78539).

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- 'builder ... authenticated PlatformUserID' is overstated: Piece.SetCreator runs on the OWNING CLIENT (m_nview.IsOwner(), :136417) and writes s_creator (the client's own player ID, a client-chosen long) and s_creatorIndex from the client's copy of m_playerHistory (received via the historical player list RPC, :81421-81433). Both are client-written ZDO fields; a modded client can forge them. Emit builderTrusted:false alongside tagAuthorTrusted:false. Only ownerPeer (socket-verified peer uid) is server-authenticated.
- Line cites: ZNetPeer.m_uid is :78784 (:78786 is m_server).
- prefab name resolution via ZNetScene.GetPrefab(hash) is safe to assume: ZNetScene.instance is required by ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC on the server (:83658) and m_namedPrefabs is filled in its Awake; the 'needs in-game check' hedge can be dropped.
- `builder` must carry the same `trusted: false` marker as `tagAuthor`: s_creator and s_creatorIndex are written by the owning client in Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424); the index is into the client's received copy of m_playerHistory and can be anything.
- Drop the 'needs an in-game check that the prefab table is populated headless' hedge: ZNetScene.Awake populates m_namedPrefabs unconditionally (:81940-81950).
- Citation nit: ZNetPeer.m_uid is :78784, not :78786 (:78786 is m_server).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Field sources check out: ZDOID.ToString is GetUserID(UserKey)+":"+ID (:75883-75886); ZNetScene.GetPrefab(int) looks up m_namedPrefabs (:82045-82052) and ZNetScene exists on the server (HandleRoutedRPC calls ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance, :83658); TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag stores the client-supplied authorId verbatim with no check (:143587-143602); ZoneSystem.GetZone :115741-115746; Character.InInterior is pos.y>3000 (:4538-4541); ZNet.GetPeers :81630-81633 and ZNetPeer.m_uid (:78784); ZDOMan.GetSessionID :77362; ZDO field set has no wall-clock (:73309-73321 plus revisions at :73492-73494); World.m_playerHistory :112396 and Piece.SetCreator writes s_creator + s_creatorIndex = playerHistory.FindIndex (:136415-136424). The report is pure reads on the census DTO. Two claims overstate trust and one is unverified headless.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Field sources verified: ZDOID.ToString is GetUserID(UserKey)+":"+ID (:75882-75885); ZNetScene.Awake fills m_namedPrefabs unconditionally from m_prefabs/m_nonNetViewPrefabs (:81940-81950) so GetPrefab(int) (:82045) works headless -- the 'needs in-game check' hedge can be dropped; ZoneSystem.GetZone (:115741-115746); Character.InInterior is pos.y > 3000f (:4538-4541); ZDO field set is as listed (:73309-73321) with no timestamp; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag stores the client-supplied authorId verbatim (:143587-143602). ZNet.GetPeers (:81630), ZDOMan.GetSessionID (:77362) exist. One substantive overstatement: `builder` is described as an 'authenticated PlatformUserID', but Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424) runs on the OWNING CLIENT and writes both s_creator and s_creatorIndex (an index into the client's copy of ZNet.World.m_playerHistory, which the server sends at :81324-81341) -- both values are client-supplied and unverified, exactly like tagauthor. The server only maintains m_playerHistory (:81446-81457); it never cross-checks the index a client writes.
