### 66. Admin command channel: server-registered ConsoleCommand + RPC_RemoteCommand

`ops-admin:Admin command channel: server-registered ConsoleCommand + RPC_RemoteCommand` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** refuted


Register onlyServer/remoteCommand console commands from a Terminal.InitTerminal postfix; an admin types them in their own vanilla F5 console and the server executes them, replying into that admin's console.


**How it works:** Harmony-postfix `Terminal.InitTerminal` and construct commands:

`new Terminal.ConsoleCommand("tplite.list", "[tag] — list portals", handler, isCheat:false, isNetwork:false, onlyServer:true, isSecret:false, allowInDevBuild:false, hideBehindDevCommands:false, optionsFetcher:null, alwaysRefreshTabOptions:false, remoteCommand:true)` — exact 13-parameter ctor at :43094/:43112.

The delivery path, all verified: the admin's client runs `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:45734); `ConsoleCommand.IsValid` (:43203) fails because `OnlyServer` requires `ZNet.instance.IsServer()`; control falls to the `value.RemoteCommand && !ZNet.instance.IsServer()` branch (:45743) → `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text)` (:81869) → server `RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879), which is admin-gated by `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())` — the same authenticated PlatformUserID vanilla uses for kick/ban (:81670) → `InternalCommand(rpc, command)` (:81891) → `Console.instance.TryRunCommand(command)`.

`Console.instance` **is** non-null on a dedicated server: `Game.Awake` instantiates `m_consolePrefab` when absent (:100038-100041).

Reply to the requesting admin with `ZNet.instance.RemotePrint(peer.m_rpc, line)` (:81635) → client `RPC_RemotePrint` → `Console.instance.Print`. Resolve the peer from the ZRpc by reproducing the private `ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` (:80504) as `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)`. Also call `args.Context.AddString(line)`, which additionally writes `ZLog.Log("Console: " + line)` (:45983-45985) so every admin action is in the server log.

Command set: `tplite.list [tag]`, `tplite.show <x,z>`, `tplite.dump <x,z>` (full ZDO key dump via `ZDOExtraData.GetData` :75108), `tplite.health`, `tplite.repair [--dry-run]`, `tplite.reload`, `tplite.export`, `tplite.snapshot <name>`, `tplite.restore <name>`, `tplite.tag <x,z> <tag>`, `tplite.link <a> <b>`, `tplite.unlink <a>`, `tplite.lockdown on|off`, `tplite.uninstall --clean-keys`.

Namespace every command `tplite.` — `ConsoleCommand`'s ctor does `commands[command.ToLower()] = this` (an indexer assignment, :43096/:43114), so a name collision with another mod **silently overwrites** rather than throwing.


**Player experience:** An operator joins the server with a vanilla client, is on adminlist.txt, presses F5, types `tplite.health` and presses Enter. Two seconds later their console fills with `[tplite] 214 portals / 61 tags / 2 stranded / 1 dangling / 0 cross-tag`. A non-admin typing the same command gets `You are not admin` printed back by ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand (:81883). Ordinary players never see anything.


**Failure modes:**
- Calling `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(cmd)` from server-side mod code: the IsServer() branch passes a null rpc (:81873) into `InternalCommand`, which dereferences `rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName()` unconditionally at :81893 → NullReferenceException. Call `Console.instance.TryRunCommand(cmd)` directly instead.
- Registering a command name another mod already took: the indexer assignment (:43096) clobbers silently, with no log, and the loser's command simply stops working.
- Setting `isCheat:true` — `Terminal.IsCheatsEnabled()` requires the static `m_cheat` flag (:45721-45732), so a cheat command may refuse on the server; keep ops commands non-cheat and rely on the adminlist gate.
- Assuming `onlyAdmin:true` adds a check — `ConsoleCommand.IsValid` (:43203-43217) never reads `OnlyAdmin`; the ConsoleEvent overload does not even fold it into OnlyServer (:43120), unlike the ConsoleEventFailable overload (:43100). The real gate is RPC_RemoteCommand's adminlist test.
- Long reports: one RemotePrint per line is one ZRpc.Invoke each. Chunk to ~40 lines per response and paginate.

On the server, Harmony-prefix the private ZNet.InternalCommand(ZRpc rpc, string command) (:81891-81895) — reached only after the adminlist check in RPC_RemoteCommand (:81881) — and when `command` starts with `setkey tplite.` parse and handle it, returning false so the real setkey never runs (otherwise a global key literally named 'tplite.list HUB' is created). Reply with ZNet.instance.RemotePrint(rpc, line) (:81635-81648); the ZRpc is the prefix's own parameter, so reproducing GetPeer(ZRpc) (:80504-80513) is unnecessary.
- The ConsoleCommand constructor has 14 parameters, not 13: a trailing `bool onlyAdmin = false` was added and `OnlyServer = onlyServer || onlyAdmin` in the failable overload (:43094-43111, :43112-43127). Server-side registration is still possible and still useful for the file-queue channel, but it is not what makes the in-game path work.
- Terminal.InitTerminal is private static and called from Terminal.Awake (:45762-45765), which Console (a Terminal, :42856) runs on the dedicated server because Game.Awake instantiates m_consolePrefab when Console.instance is null (:100035-100041), gated only on FejdStartup.AwakePlatforms() succeeding (:97083-97096) — that part of the claim holds.

- Vanilla clients cannot execute mod-registered command names: Terminal.TryRunCommand checks the client's own `commands` dictionary before the RemoteCommand fallthrough (:45736-45742, unknown-command path :45755). The described 'admin types tplite.health in F5' flow prints 'not a recognized command' locally and sends nothing.
- Working replacement: tunnel through the vanilla `setkey` remote command (remoteCommand:true, onlyServer:true, isCheat:false, free-form FullLine :43510-43534). Harmony-prefix ZNet.InternalCommand(ZRpc rpc, string command) (:81891-81895) -- private instance, patchable -- to intercept commands beginning with `setkey tplite`, execute, RemotePrint(rpc, ...) the reply, and return false so vanilla never calls ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey with the payload. The admin gate in RPC_RemoteCommand (:81881) still runs first, for free.
- Non-admin feedback 'You are not admin' (:81883) still holds for the tunnelled form.
- Reply path RemotePrint -> client RPC_RemotePrint -> Console.instance.Print requires the admin's console to be enabled client-side (F5 implies that).

A server-only mod registers `tplite.*` only in the SERVER process's dictionary; the vanilla client has never heard of it and prints "'tplite.list' is not a recognized command" (:45757-45759) without sending anything. Everything downstream (ZNet.RemoteCommand :81869-81877, RPC_RemoteCommand adminlist gate :81879-81889, InternalCommand :81891-81895, RemotePrint :81635-81648, Console.instance existence via Game.Awake :100035-100041, Terminal.InitTerminal from Terminal.Awake :45762-45765) is verified correct, but is never reached for a mod-named command. The channel can be salvaged only by piggy-backing on a vanilla command name that the client already knows and marks remoteCommand:true.

The CLIENT half is refuted as written: the admin's vanilla client runs Terminal.TryRunCommand (:45734-45757), whose FIRST step is `commands.TryGetValue(array[0].ToLower(), out value)` against the CLIENT's own static dictionary. A server-only mod cannot add `tplite.*` to a vanilla client's dictionary, so the text falls straight to `'tplite.list' is not a recognized command` (:45755) and never reaches the `value.RemoteCommand && !ZNet.instance.IsServer()` branch (:45742). Mod-defined command names therefore can NOT be typed in a vanilla F5 console. What DOES work: piggyback on a vanilla command that is remoteCommand:true, onlyServer:true, isCheat:false and forwards free-form text -- `setkey` (:43510-43534) passes `args.FullLine.Substring(...)` and is not blocked by Console.isAllowedCommand (only IsCheat commands are, :43xxx override). An admin types `setkey tplite list HUB`; the client forwards it via ZNet.RemoteCommand (:81869-81877); on the server a Harmony prefix on ZNet.InternalCommand(ZRpc, string) (:81891) intercepts the `setkey tplite` prefix, handles it, replies via RemotePrint(rpc, ...), and returns false -- which is mandatory, because otherwise the vanilla handler calls ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey("tplite list HUB") and pollutes global keys (:43520). HideBehindDevCommands only affects ShowCommand listing (:43190-43196), not execution. Server-side registration of `tplite.*` in Terminal is still useful for the file-queue channel and for InternalCommand(null, ...) but is not a client entry point.

### 67. File-queue command channel (scriptable, no in-game presence)

`ops-admin:File-queue command channel (scriptable, no in-game presence)` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A watched text file the operator appends command lines to from ssh/cron; the mod polls its mtime, executes each line on the main thread, and writes the result to a sibling response file.


**How it works:** Extend Wonderland's existing config-poll pattern (WonderlandPlugin.PollConfigFile, Plugin.cs:97) to a second file. Every 1 s (configurable) compare `File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc(<config>/TortalPortalLite.cmd)` against a cached stamp. On change, read all lines, execute each through the same handler table the console commands use, append `<timestamp> <command> -> <result>` to `TortalPortalLite.cmd.out`, then truncate the input file (write-temp-then-File.Replace, the atomic pattern SupplySwitch.Save and TortalPortal/PortalExport.Write:75 both use).

Everything runs on the main thread inside `Update()`, so ZDOMan access is safe — ZDOMan has no locking anywhere and vanilla's only background thread (`ZNet.SaveWorldThread`, :80583) deliberately operates on a clone built on the main thread by `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` (:76197-76205).

This is the only command channel that works with zero players connected, zero admin clients, and (if the stdin question resolves negative) zero interactive console. It makes every ops action cron-able: a nightly `echo tplite.export >> …/TortalPortalLite.cmd` produces a fresh JSON dump; a monitoring script tails `.cmd.out`.

Security model: the file lives inside `BepInEx/config`, so filesystem permission on the server box *is* the authorization. Explicitly refuse to accept a command file outside `BepInEx.Paths.ConfigPath`, and never make the handler table reachable from any network path without the adminlist check.

If a background thread ever needs to emit text (an HTTP handler, a webhook callback), do not touch Terminal directly — enqueue into the public `Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog` `ConcurrentQueue<string>` (:43245), which `Console.Update` drains one line per frame into `AddString` → `ZLog.Log` (:42923-42925). Vanilla's own save thread uses exactly this to report save errors (:80675, :80710).


**Player experience:** Invisible to players. An operator on a phone over ssh runs `echo 'tplite.repair --dry-run' >> ~/valheim/BepInEx/config/TortalPortalLite.cmd; sleep 2; tail -20 ~/valheim/BepInEx/config/TortalPortalLite.cmd.out` and reads `would relink 'merchant-ring' member #3 (4420,95,2180): connection None -> #1; would retag 2 portals 'trade' -> 'TRADE'`.


**Failure modes:**
- Executing the file's contents off the main thread — ZDOMan is not thread-safe and a concurrent GetPortalList during a SendZDOs sweep will throw or corrupt.
- Not truncating after execution: the same commands re-run on the next unrelated mtime bump.
- Leaving the file world-writable on a shared host — this channel has no authentication beyond filesystem permissions.
- Editor tools that write via rename rather than in-place can make mtime jump backwards; compare for inequality, not greater-than (the same reason Wonderland's PollConfigFile compares `stamp == _configStamp`, Plugin.cs:109).

**Designer citations:** WonderlandPlugin.PollConfigFile — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Plugin.cs:97-131 ; SupplySwitch.Save atomic write — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/SupplySwitch.cs:100-165 ; PortalExport.Write atomic write — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PortalExport.cs:75 ; ZDOMan.PrepareSave main-thread clone — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76197-76205 ; ZNet.SaveWorldThread — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:80583 ; Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:43245; drained Console.Update :42923-42925; vanilla producer :80675


**Open questions:**
- How fast does the operator expect a response? A 1 s poll costs one File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc per second; measure that on the target filesystem (network/overlayfs mounts can make stat expensive).

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**

- This channel does not depend on the refuted in-game console path — its handler table should be the canonical one and the setkey-carrier hack (see admin channel verdict) and any RemoteCommand path should call into it, not the other way round.
- Console.Update only drains Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog when IsConsoleEnabled() (:42892-42895, :42953-42958); on a dedicated server started without `-console` (:97288-97291) the queue is never consumed. Either pass -console, drain it in the mod's own Update, or log from background threads via ZLog.Log directly.
- Prereq wording: the file channel does not depend on the RPC_RemoteCommand channel being reachable from vanilla clients (which it is not for mod-named commands); it only needs the shared server-side handler table.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed] All engine claims verified. WonderlandPlugin.PollConfigFile is a real mtime-poll pattern (Plugin.cs:97-131). ZDOMan has no locking; ZNet.SaveWorldThread (:80583) runs on a background thread but only against clones prepared on the main thread by ZDOMan.PrepareSave -> GetSaveClonePerChunk -> item.Clone() (:76197-76205, :77560-77636) and ZDOExtraData.PrepareSave dictionary clones (:75480-75491), so main-thread Update() access to ZDOMan is the only safe model and this option respects it. With the in-game RPC channel refuted as designed, this becomes the PRIMARY command channel, not a fallback. Note that AddString's ZLog side effect happens regardless of whether a Console UI exists, so results land in the server log.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Threading claims verified: ZNet.SaveWorld calls m_zdoMan.PrepareSave() on the main thread (:80532) which builds clones via GetSaveClonePerChunk and ZDOExtraData.PrepareSave (:76197-76205, :75480-75490) before the save thread (:80537, :80583) runs, so main-thread Update access to ZDOMan is the only safe pattern and is what the option prescribes. Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog is public static (:43245) and the save thread enqueues into it (:80675, :80710). ### 68. Network definition as a hot-reloaded JSON file (with worked example)

`ops-admin:Network definition as a hot-reloaded JSON file (with worked example)` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A separate, position-keyed JSON document next to the .cfg that declares admin-defined portal networks (ring / hub / pairs / one-way chain) and is re-parsed and re-applied on save without a restart.


**How it works:** BepInEx's flat `key=value` `.cfg` cannot express a list of networks each with a list of members, so put the topology in its own file and keep the `.cfg` for scalars. Poll `File.GetLastWriteTimeUtc` on a 5 s timer exactly as `WonderlandPlugin.PollConfigFile` does (Plugin.cs:97), parse into an immutable model, validate, and only then swap the live model (never mutate in place mid-tick).

**Members are resolved by position, never by ZDOID** — ZDOIDs are renumbered every world load (`ZDO.Load` :74552). Resolution: for each declared `at`, scan the census for the nearest portal ZDO within `radius` (default 6 m); ambiguity (two portals inside the radius) is a validation error, not a coin flip.

```jsonc
// BepInEx/config/TortalPortalLite.networks.json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "world": "Wubarrk",          // advisory; warn if != ZNet.instance.GetWorldName() (:80876)
  "defaults": { "reassertSeconds": 2.0, "onMissingMember": "warn", "tagCase": "exact" },
  "networks": [
    { "id": "merchant-ring", "enabled": true, "topology": "ring", "tag": "TRADE",
      "members": [
        { "name": "Haldor",   "at": [1240.5, 31.2, -3310.0], "radius": 6.0 },
        { "name": "Docks",    "at": [-210.0, 33.9, 180.0],   "radius": 6.0 },
        { "name": "Mistvale", "at": [4420.0, 95.4, 2180.0],  "radius": 6.0 }
      ] },
    { "id": "spawn-hub", "enabled": true, "topology": "hub", "tag": "HUB",
      "hub":   { "name": "Spawn Gate", "at": [0.0, 32.0, 4.0], "radius": 8.0 },
      "rotation": { "mode": "cycle", "dwellSeconds": 120 },
      "spokes": [
        { "name": "Swamp",  "at": [-980.0, 30.5, 1420.0] },
        { "name": "Plains", "at": [2600.0, 41.0, -700.0] }
      ] },
    { "id": "lore-gate", "enabled": false, "topology": "oneway-chain", "tag": "DEEP",
      "members": [ {"name":"A","at":[10,30,10]}, {"name":"B","at":[20,30,20]} ] }
  ]
}
```

**`tag` is load-bearing, not cosmetic.** `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 clears any connection whose partner's `s_tag` string differs (:100601) using bare ordinal `string !=`. Every member of a network must carry one byte-identical tag or vanilla tears the network down within 5 s. The validator must therefore reject two networks sharing a tag, and reject a tag that collides with an unmanaged portal's tag.

Validation before swap: unique `id`; unique `tag`; ≥2 members for ring/pairs; hub has ≥1 spoke; no member appears twice; no `at` beyond ±16320 m (`ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex` clamps out-of-range zones to sector 0, :115755-115774); no `at` with y>3000 unless explicitly allowed (`Character.InInterior` :4538). On any error, keep the previous model, log every error, and write them to the `.cmd.out` file.


**Player experience:** An operator edits `TortalPortalLite.networks.json` in nano, saves, and within 5 s the server log prints `[Networks] reloaded: 3 networks, 8 members, 0 errors`. Within a further 2 s a player standing at the Docks portal sees its hover text change from `Teleport — 'docks'` to `Teleport — 'TRADE'` and the gate's blue connected-glow snap on (TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal re-evaluates every 0.5 s, :143491-143509). Walking through now lands them at Haldor rather than at whatever random same-tag gate vanilla had picked.


**Failure modes:**
- Two networks declaring the same `tag`: vanilla's random same-tag pairing (Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100679) will cross-link them the instant the reassert loop is late, and phase 1 will not tear it down because the tags match.
- Declaring a per-member display tag: impossible without patching. Phase 1's `zDO.GetString(s_tag) != @string` test (:100601) transitively forces every linked portal in a network onto one literal string.
- A member coordinate that no longer has a portal (player demolished it): with `onMissingMember: "warn"` the ring silently degrades to a chain; the health scanner must surface it loudly.
- Whitespace or case drift in `tag` ('Base ' vs 'Base') producing two invisible networks — the comparison is ordinal and whitespace-significant.
- Hot-swapping the model mid-tick while the reassert engine is iterating it.

**Designer citations:** Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 tag-equality teardown — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100594-100606 (tag test :100601) ; Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100664-100679 ; ZDO.Load ZDOID renumber — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74552 ; ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex out-of-range clamp — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115755-115774 ; Character.InInterior — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:4538-4541 ; ZNet.GetWorldName — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:80876 ; WonderlandPlugin.PollConfigFile — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Plugin.cs:97


**Open questions:**
- Which JSON parser? BepInEx 5.4.23.5 ships no JSON library and TortalPortal vendors none; Wonderland's DiscordWebhook hand-rolls only an escaper (DiscordWebhook.cs). Either vendor a ~400-line reader or use `UnityEngine.JsonUtility` — but JsonUtility cannot deserialize top-level arrays or Dictionary and needs [Serializable] mirror classes. Decide before writing the schema.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Save boundary must be stated: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData writes ONE ZDOConnectionHashData per ZDO, the Target entry overwriting any outbound entry the same ZDO had (:75462-75477), and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load pairs a Portal entry with a Portal|Target entry of equal hash bidirectionally (:77850-77893, from LoadChunks :76515). Rings, hubs and one-way chains come back from a restart as an arbitrary pairwise matching; the 2 s reassert repairs them only because the JSON is the source of truth — say so, and make reassert run before the first Game.ConnectPortals staged commit after load (ZDOMan.Load calls Game.instance.ConnectPortals() immediately, :76658).
- Live tag collisions are not just a validation problem: any player can retag any portal at any time (RPC_SetTag runs on the owning client, :143587-143602). An unmanaged portal retagged to 'TRADE' with connection None will be paired by phase 2 (:100608-100621) with any member whose connection was momentarily None (e.g. right after a member was retagged by a player, which clears both ends, :143591-143594 and :143604-143620), and once it points at a member it passes phase 1 forever (member tag equal, member connection not None). The reconcile loop must also detect unmanaged portals whose connection targets a member and clear them (or retag them) — or take over Game.ConnectPortals entirely as the Dial option does, which removes the tag constraint.
- Server writes into client-owned member ZDOs: a nearby player owns the member ZDO (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76927). Vanilla's own Game.SetConnection either routes to the owner via RPC_SetConnection or force-claims with SetOwner(sessionID) then SetConnection (:100636-100646). The reassert should mirror the force path (SetOwner first) so the OwnerRevision bump makes the client accept the write; a bare SetConnection on a client-owned ZDO races the client's DataRevision (:77118-77130) and can diverge.
- Retagging members to the network tag rewrites the player-visible tag; the hover text change described is real (GetHoverText reads s_tag each frame, :143453-143464) but it also means a player at a member who presses E sees and can edit the network tag — every such edit clears both ends and must be reverted by the next reassert.
- `oneway-chain` is not feasible with vanilla Game.ConnectPortals running: phase 1 clears any portal whose partner has connection None (:100601), phase 2 re-pairs the two (:100609-100620). Either add the ConnectPortals prefix takeover as a prereq for one-way topologies or drop the topology.
- Save/restart: ring and hub links collapse to pairwise matching on disk (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75459-75477); at load ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77863) then Game.ConnectPortals (:76522) run before any mod tick and randomly pair leftover members. The engine must reassert from the JSON at OnWorldReady and accept a transient wrong-pairing window of up to reassertSeconds; state this.
- Sector clamp bound: SectorToIndex accepts zones -256..255, i.e. x/z in [-16416, +16352) -- the ±16320 figure is slightly conservative, fine as a validator but cite the actual math (:115762-115773).
- Do not copy Game.SetConnection's owner-routing (private, :100629-100641): direct ZDO.SetConnection + ForceSendZDO from the server propagates without ownership; routing through an online owner hands the write to an untrusted client's Game.RPC_SetConnection (:100643-100652).
- Enforcement is server-enforced at the route level only; a player's right to pass (ore check, NoPortals) stays client-side.

The tag-is-load-bearing analysis is exactly right for ring/hub/pairs: ConnectPortals phase 1 (:100594-100606) only tears a link down when the partner's tag differs or the partner has NO connection; it never tests reciprocity, so same-tag rings and fan-in hubs are runtime-stable under vanilla's 5 s pass without any Harmony patch. SectorToIndex clamps |zone| >= 256 to sector 0 (:115755-115774); InInterior :4538; GetWorldName :80876. Hover/glow experience is real: GetHoverText reads the ZDO each call (:143453), UpdatePortal polls at 0.5 s (:143446, :143491). Direct ZDO.SetConnection from the server needs no ownership (ZDOPeer.ShouldSend is revision-only) and itself calls SetDirtyPortals (:73656-73665). Two things are wrong or missing. (1) The `oneway-chain` topology is NOT stable under vanilla: for A->B with B.connection == None, phase 1 tears A down every 5 s (:100601 third clause), phase 2 then pairs A<->B (or B with any other unconnected same-tag member), and the mod's 2 s reassert fights it -- the link flaps between one-way and bidirectional and players intermittently walk into an unlinked frame. One-way topologies require the Game.ConnectPortals prefix takeover, which this option does not list as a prereq. (2) Save boundary: RegenerateConnectionHashData gives each ZDO one hash slot (:75459-75477), so rings/hubs collapse to a partial perfect matching on disk; on load ZDOMan.LoadChunks runs ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (hash pairs :77863) and then Game.ConnectPortals (:76522), which randomly pairs the leftover same-tag members BEFORE the mod's first reassert. Topology is restored by the mod within one reassert interval, but the option is silent about it and must run its reassert on world-ready, not just on file change.

### 69. NetworkReassertEngine — the only writer, and the race with vanilla's 5 s pass

`ops-admin:NetworkReassertEngine — the only writer, and the race with vanilla's 5 s pass` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A 2 Hz loop that force-writes each managed portal's intended tag and connection using ownership-claim + ForceSendZDO, designed so vanilla's own reconciler never tears the topology down.


**How it works:** Exactly one engine in the mod writes `s_tag` or `ConnectionType.Portal`. Every tick (default 2.0 s; must be < 5 s) it walks the resolved network model and, per member, compares the census's current tag/connection against the intended values. If they differ it performs vanilla's own immediate-write recipe verbatim (`Game.SetConnection` :100637-100646):

```
zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID());                       // :74627 / :77362
zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, intendedTag);                       // :73721
zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, intendedTarget);  // :73656
ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);                   // :77706
ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals();                         // :76702 (SetConnection already does this, :73661; a tag-only write does NOT)
```

Use `SetConnection`, never `UpdateConnection` — `ZDOExtraData.UpdateConnection` returns false and writes nothing when no connection entry exists (:74962-74976).

**Why this survives vanilla.** `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 (:100596-100605) only clears a connection when the partner ZDO is missing, the partner's tag differs, or the partner's own connection is `None`. It never checks reciprocity. So a ring A→B→C→A, a fan-in hub, and even a self-loop are all indefinitely stable *at runtime* as long as every member shares one literal tag and no member's connection is `None`. Phase 2 (:100607-100622) only touches portals already reading `None`. Therefore a correctly-asserted network is invisible to vanilla and the 2 s loop is a repair mechanism, not a race.

**Idempotence is free.** `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` early-returns when type and target are unchanged (:74951-74961) and `BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false on an equal value (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345), so `ZDO.Set` skips `IncreaseDataRevision`. An unchanged re-assert generates zero DataRevision bumps, zero network traffic and zero disk dirtying. Budget `ForceSendZDO` calls per tick (cap 256, mirroring StructureUpkeep.MaxHealthBroadcastsPerSweep) so a first-boot mass repair does not spike every peer in one frame.

**Ownership contention.** `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` runs every 2 s and hands any persistent ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer (:76872-76885, :76901-76927). Our claim will be stolen back — that is fine, the *value* already went out via ForceSendZDO. Only add the `ZDO.SetOwner` Harmony prefix guard (the WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313 pattern) if measurement shows write-back contention; keep the predicate a single `PortalPrefabHash.Contains` test and never block `uid == 0` or `uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()`.


**Player experience:** A player demolishes one gate of a three-gate ring. Within ≤5 s vanilla's reconciler notices the dangling partner and nulls the neighbours' links; within ≤2 s of that the reassert engine re-closes the ring between the two survivors and their hover text goes from `unconnected` back to `connected`. A player retagging a managed gate through the vanilla 10-character box sees their new tag persist for at most 2 s and then snap back to `TRADE`, with a toast: `This gate belongs to the TRADE network.`


**Failure modes:**
- Setting reassertSeconds ≥ 5 s: vanilla's phase 2 wins a window and randomly re-pairs a briefly-orphaned member (`UnityEngine.Random.Range` :100678).
- Writing a tag without calling `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702): `ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision` (:73832) only routes to `SetDirtySector`, and portals are explicitly excluded from the ordinary chunk save (`AddObjectsPerChunk` filter :77572). The rename is live but silently absent from the next world save.
- Racing vanilla's deferred branch: `Game.SetConnection` only defers to an online owner (:100647-100650). Our direct claim-and-write bypasses that, which is correct — but it means a client that currently owns the portal may push a conflicting higher-DataRevision blob back via `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77103-77133), which replaces the whole ZDO with no field-level merge. The 2 s loop re-corrects it; instantaneous consistency is not achievable.
- Caching ZDO object references between ticks — vanilla itself does this in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` and can force-write through a pooled, recycled reference (Game.ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698 vs ZDOPool.Release in HandleDestroyedZDO :76990). Do not copy that.

**Open questions:**
- Does a client already standing at a gate pick up a server-side `s_tag` rewrite without a zone reload? `UpdatePortal` runs on a 0.5 s InvokeRepeating (:143450) and drives the glow, but hover text comes from a separate `GetTagInfo` read (:143563-143569) evaluated per hover frame. Stand at a gate, rewrite the tag, and watch.
- Measure the real ownership tug-of-war: log `zdo.GetOwner()` on one managed portal every second for 60 s with a player standing next to it, to decide whether the SetOwner prefix guard is needed at all.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Game.SetConnection immediate write is the fallback path (owner==0 / dead peer / forceImmediateConnection); for an online owner vanilla delegates via ZRoutedRpc RPC_SetConnection (:100637-100648). Direct server writes under a live owner risk DataRevision collision (RPC_ZDOData rejects revision <= local, :77103-77112); bump zdo.DataRevision (public setter :73494) by a margin after every corrective write.
- ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-overwrites both sides of any pair staged on the previous pass, including managed portals that transiently read None; expect a one-bounce overwrite per disturbance (≤7 s), not 'never'. Consider a Harmony prefix on Game.ForceSetConnection/SetConnection (both private) for managed ZDOIDs.
- While the server owns a managed portal, a vanilla retag RPC targets the server (ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) → m_zdo.GetOwner(), :82855-82858) and is dropped in HandleRoutedRPC because ZNetScene.FindInstance is null on a dedicated server (:83650-83664); the 'snap back after ≤2 s' experience only holds while a client owns the ZDO.
- ZDO.SetOwner is at :74624-74631 (cited :74627 is inside it, fine); ForceSendZDO still requires peer.ShouldSend (AddForceSendZdos) so it prioritises, never bypasses revision gating.
- Tag-only writes: IncreaseDataRevision → SetDirtySector → SetDirtyChunks on the sector chunk (:73832-73840, :76694-76700) which excludes portal prefabs (:77572); explicit SetDirtyPortals() (:76702) is required — confirmed.
- Add an explicit 'tag reservation' step: any UNMANAGED portal whose s_tag equals a managed network tag must be retagged (or its connection cleared and tag suffixed) by the same engine, otherwise a member's transient None window lets vanilla phase 2 stage U↔A and ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-writes it 5 s later; the leftover U→A one-way link is never cleared by phase 1 (:100600-100603 requires tag mismatch or partner None).
- Replace 'zero network traffic' with: zero traffic only when the engine skips ForceSendZDO on an unchanged member; ZDOPeer.ShouldSend (:76003-76013) returns true for any peer lacking the ZDO, so a ForceSendZDO on an unchanged ZDO still ships it to every peer that never had it.
- State the save-boundary behaviour: the intended topology is re-derived from the network file each boot, but ZDOIDs are regenerated on load (ZDO.Load :74552 `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`), so the network model must key members by a stable identity (position+prefab, or a mod-written ZDO string key), never by ZDOID. Rings/self-loops collapse in RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) and are only restored by the engine's first tick after LoadChunks → Game.ConnectPortals (:76524).
- Note that during the ≤2 s server-ownership window a vanilla retag is silently dropped (ZNetView.InvokeRPC targets owner :82855-82858; server HandleRoutedRPC FindInstance==null :83651-83664) — the player sees no change and no toast unless the engine emits one from the census diff.
- The 'toast' in playerExperience is not free: it needs a PlayerNotify-style RPC to the retagger, whose identity is only probable (census diff) unless the retag crossed the wire (see AuditEngine).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited member exists with the claimed shape and the core mechanism holds on a dedicated server: Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine is started only under ZNet.IsServer() (Game.Start :100070-100075) with no local-player dependency; phase 1 (:100596-100605) clears a link only when the partner is null, has a different tag, or reads None — no reciprocity test, so rings/fan-in are runtime-stable; phase 2 (:100607-100622) only touches portals reading None. ZDO.SetConnection → ZDOExtraData.SetConnection is a genuine early-return no-op on equal (type,target) (:74951-74961) and ZDO.Set(string) → s_strings.InitAndSet → BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue returns false on Equals (utils_SERVER :321-345), so unchanged re-asserts do not bump DataRevision; AddForceSendZdos additionally requires peer.ShouldSend (revision-gated), so a no-op write produces zero packets. UpdateConnection refuses to create (:74962-74976) — correct to use SetConnection. ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands a server-owned portal to any nearby peer because IsInPeerActiveArea(pos, m_sessionID) tests against the pinned (1e6,0,1e6) ref position (:76888-76899, :76901-76927). Three real defects in the write-up: (1) The 'verbatim vanilla recipe' is vanilla's FALLBACK path — Game.SetConnection takes it only for owner==0, a dead peer, or forceImmediateConnection; for an online owner vanilla deliberately delegates via RPC_SetConnection (:100637-100648). Writing directly under a live client owner creates a DataRevision collision hazard: RPC_ZDOData rejects any incoming revision <= local (:77103-77112) and the client's RPC_ZDOData does the same, so if client and server both write from the same base revision (e.g. player retags twice within a reassert interval), server and client end up with equal DataRevision and different content and stay desynced until the next write. DataRevision has a public setter (:73494); the engine must bump it by a margin (e.g. +1000) after each corrective write so the server copy always wins. (2) 'Never tears the topology down' is overstated: ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-writes BOTH directions of every pair staged on the previous pass via ForceSetConnection (forceImmediateConnection:true), regardless of what the reassert loop wrote in between. Any disturbance that makes a managed portal read None (partner demolished, partner retagged) lets phase 2 stage it against ANY unconnected same-tag portal — including a player's unmanaged one — and the next 5 s pass overwrites the reassert value once; the 2 s loop then re-fixes. Bounded (~7 s) but it is a race, and the staged victim (a player's portal pointing at a managed gate) is torn down by phase 1 on the following pass. Mitigation: Harmony-prefix Game.ForceSetConnection/SetConnection (private, need AccessTools) for managed ZDOIDs, or clear m_currentlyConnectingPortals entries touching managed portals. (3) The player-experience snap-back is wrong for the ownership window: client TeleportWorld.SetText → ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) targets m_zdo.GetOwner() (:82855-82858 both builds). While the server holds ownership (after the engine's SetOwner, until ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands it back ≤2 s later) the retag RPC routes to the server, whose HandleRoutedRPC does ZNetScene.FindInstance(zdo) → null on a dedicated server (:83650-83664) and drops it silently; the player's box closes with no tag change at all and the mod's toast never fires. Also client RPC_SetTag applies only when m_nview.IsOwner() (client :144327-144341), so an owner==0 portal accepts no retag from anyone.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism holds against the decompile. Game.SetConnection immediate branch (SERVER :100637-100651) is exactly SetOwner(session) → SetConnection → ForceSendZDO; ZDO.SetConnection (:73656-73666) bumps DataRevision and calls SetDirtyPortals only for Portal type; ZDO.Set(int,string) (:73721-73727) → ZDOExtraData.Set → s_strings.InitAndSet (:74918, :75681-75685) → BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue returns false on Equals (utils_SERVER :321-330), so an equal tag write does not bump revision; ZDOExtraData.SetConnection early-returns on equal type+target (:74951-74961); UpdateConnection returns false with no entry (:74962-74976). ConnectPortals phase 1 predicate (:100596-100605) is exactly `null || tag differs || partner None` — no reciprocity, so rings/fan-in/self-loops are runtime-stable. Phase 2 (:100607-100622) only touches None portals. Client-side acceptance verified: ZDOPeer.ShouldSend (:76003-76013) sends when server DataRevision > peer's last-seen, and the client's RPC_ZDOData whole-ZDO replace mirrors :77103-77133, so the server's write (rev = last-accepted client rev + 2) always wins the round; convergence within ~2 ticks even if the client writes concurrently. Vanilla client retag path (CLIENT TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag :144327-144342) does UpdateConnection(None)+Set(tag)+Set(tagauthor) on the owner, reaching the server through ClientChanged (:73832-73836) → CreateSyncList client branch (:77241-77258). Ownership steal by ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76927) confirmed: a server-owned portal in a peer's active area is reassigned to the peer within 2 s because IsInPeerActiveArea(session) tests against the pinned ref pos (:76887-76899). Refutations of specific sub-claims: (a) 'invisible to vanilla' is false during any window where a member reads None (destroyed partner, player retag): phase 2 will pair that member with an UNMANAGED portal carrying the same literal tag, stage it, and ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-writes that pairing 5 s later via ForceSetConnection (:100629-100635), fighting the engine for one round; the residue is a one-way U→A link that phase 1 never clears (tags equal, A non-None) — an unmanaged portal permanently fans into the managed network. (b) 'zero network traffic' on unchanged re-assert holds only because the engine skips ForceSendZDO when nothing differs; a ForceSendZDO on an unchanged ZDO still transmits to every peer that has never received it (ShouldSend returns true for an absent m_zdos entry, :76003-76012). (c) During the ≤2 s the server owns a member, a vanilla retag is silently dropped: ZNetView.InvokeRPC targets the owner (:82855-82858) = server, whose HandleRoutedRPC hits ZNetScene.FindInstance == null (:83651-83664). Harmless but real. (d) The 'RPC_ZDOData whole-ZDO replace' citation points at the server's receive path; the symmetric client path was verified in the client decompile. Enforcement: honest as server-enforced under the reviewer's ROUTE test — the connection field and tag are server-owned and re-asserted; a vanilla client cannot durably change them. It does not stop RPC_DestroyZDO (:76953-76961, no sender/ward check).

### 70. HealthScanEngine — orphan, strand and corruption detection

`ops-admin:HealthScanEngine — orphan, strand and corruption detection` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A 30 s pure-read pass over the census that classifies every pathology vanilla's pairing algorithm can produce, including the permanent one-member strand that 3+ same-tag portals always create.


**How it works:** Runs on the census snapshot, writes nothing. Each finding carries severity, portal id(s) and a suggested repair.

1. **Odd-count strand (the big one).** Group portals by exact `s_tag`. For any group of size N ≥ 3, vanilla's strictly-pairwise phase 2 leaves exactly ⌊N/2⌋ pairs and `N mod 2` permanently orphaned members: the surviving pair re-confirms itself every tick, so the orphan never rotates in. Report every unmanaged tag group with N ≥ 3, naming the currently-orphaned member and warning that *which* member is orphaned is dictionary-bucket order and changes across restarts (iteration order comes from `m_portalObjects` enumeration in `GetPortalList` :77648-77656).
2. **Dangling connection.** `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` non-None but `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id)` returns null. Vanilla clears this within 5 s (:100600-100603); report only if it persists across two scans, which indicates something is re-writing it.
3. **Non-reciprocal link.** A→B while B→C or B→None. Legal and stable in vanilla (phase 1 has no reciprocity check) — informational for unmanaged portals, an error for a network declared `pairs`.
4. **Self-loop.** A→A. Stable at runtime, but **erased at save**: `RegenerateConnectionHashData` writes the source slot then immediately overwrites it with the Target slot because target != None (:75461-75478). Flag as 'will not survive restart'.
5. **Cross-tag link.** Partner tag != own tag; vanilla will tear it down within 5 s.
6. **Duplicate / near-duplicate tags.** Ordinal comparison means `Base`, `base` and `Base ` are three networks. Report groups that differ only by case or trailing whitespace.
7. **Out-of-world.** |pos.xz| beyond ~16320 m falls into `ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex`'s clamp-to-sector-0 bucket (:115755-115774) — the same bucket the server's own pinned reference position maps to.
8. **Interior portal.** `pos.y > 3000f` (:4538) — built inside a dungeon; shares the surface XZ zone, worth flagging for operators who forbid it.
9. **Unknown prefab.** `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(zdo.GetPrefab())` null — a portal from an uninstalled mod.
10. **Sector duplication.** The same ZDOID appearing twice in `GetPortalList()` — `AddIfPortal` adds under the current sector without removing the old entry (:77732-77752), so any repositioned portal duplicates and `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76980-76986) can only clean one bucket, leaking the other permanently.

Note there is **no** 'portal in an unloaded zone' pathology: portals live in `m_portalObjects`, are loaded wholesale from the dedicated `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal` file at world load (:76474-76482), are never released (`ReleaseZDOS` only reassigns ownership, :76872-76885), and `FlushClientObjects` is client-only (:76180-76183). The census is always complete.


**Player experience:** No player-visible effect. The operator's 30 s log line reads `[Health] OK` most of the time, and on a problem: `[Health] tag 'home' has 5 portals — 2 pairs + 1 permanently stranded at (410,33,-88); tag 'Base ' (trailing space) is a separate 1-portal network, probably a typo for 'Base'`. A player who tagged three gates `home` and wondered why one never connects finally gets an answer an admin can give them.


**Failure modes:**
- Reporting a dangling connection during the normal 5 s window after someone demolishes a gate — require two consecutive scans before flagging.
- Reporting every untagged portal as one giant broken group: `ZDO.GetString` defaults to `""` (ZDOExtraData.GetString :75079-75082), so every untagged portal in the world is a single tag group and freshly placed untagged gates genuinely do auto-pair at random. Treat tag `""` as a special case with its own message.
- Treating the orphan as a stable identity — it is bucket-order-dependent and can differ after a restart.
- Missing a duplicated portal because the diff is keyed by rounded position, which collapses the two entries; key the duplicate check on ZDOID reference count within the raw list.

### 71. Automatic repair pass (with dry-run and blast-radius cap)

`ops-admin:Automatic repair pass (with dry-run and blast-radius cap)` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Turn each health finding into a bounded, logged, reversible corrective ZDO write — normalising tags, splitting odd groups, clearing dangling links — gated behind an explicit config opt-in and a --dry-run default.


**How it works:** A repair is a (finding → action) table executed on demand (`tplite.repair`) or on a slow timer if `AutoRepair` is enabled. Default is **dry-run**: compute and print every action, write nothing.

Actions, each using the reassert engine's write primitive (claim owner → write → ForceSendZDO → SetDirtyPortals):
- **Tag normalisation.** Trim trailing/leading whitespace and optionally case-fold, when and only when it merges a 1-member group into an existing group. Writing `s_tag` alone requires `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` explicitly (:76702) — `ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision` (:73832) routes to `SetDirtySector`, which the portal chunk ignores (`AddObjectsPerChunk` filter :77572).
- **Odd-group resolution.** For an N≥3 unmanaged group, either (a) suffix the orphan's tag (`home` → `home-2`) so it stops competing, or (b) promote the whole group into a managed ring in the network file. Never silently retag a player's gate without `AllowTagRewrite=true` and an audit entry naming the original tag.
- **Dangling clear.** `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` — identical to what vanilla does 5 s later, useful only when combined with an immediate `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` call (public, :100589) to re-pair in the same frame instead of waiting.
- **Self-loop removal.** Break it before the next save silently does.
- **Duplicate-bucket cleanup.** Not repairable through any public API: the duplicate lives inside the private `m_portalObjects` dictionary. `GetPortals()` (:77643) returns the live dictionary and *can* be mutated to remove the stale entry — powerful and dangerous; gate behind a separate `AllowRegistrySurgery` flag and log loudly.

Every repair emits an audit line and is preceded by an automatic state snapshot (see the snapshot/rollback option), so `tplite.restore pre-repair` undoes the whole batch.

Cap actions per invocation (default 64) and per tick (default 16). Vanilla's own cost model makes this cheap — idempotent re-writes are free — but a first repair on a neglected 400-portal world can otherwise issue hundreds of `ForceSendZDO` calls in one frame, each of which re-serialises the entire ZDO to every peer with no delta encoding (`ZDOMan.SendZDOs` :77053-77062).


**Player experience:** An operator types `tplite.repair` and gets a printed plan: `DRY RUN — 4 actions: retag (410,33,-88) 'home' -> 'home-2' [orphan of 5]; trim 'Base ' -> 'Base' at (12,30,80); clear dangling link at (2600,41,-700); break self-loop at (0,32,4). Re-run with --apply.` They run `tplite.repair --apply`; the log shows `[Repair] applied 4/4, snapshot 'pre-repair-2026-09-12T14:02Z' saved`. A player who had two gates tagged `Base ` and `Base` walks into one and now arrives at the other for the first time.


**Failure modes:**
- Auto-repair on by default: silently retagging player-built gates is the single fastest way to make an operator uninstall the mod. Default off, default dry-run.
- Repairing during the 5 s window in which vanilla is itself mid-repair — the two writes fight and produce audit noise. Skip any portal whose connection changed within the last 6 s.
- Mutating the live `m_portalObjects` dictionary returned by `GetPortals()` (:77643) while `Game.ConnectPortals` is iterating a `GetPortalList()` snapshot of it — the snapshot is a copy so it will not throw, but `AddIfPortal`/`HandleDestroyedZDO` bookkeeping desynchronises.
- Assuming a repair persists: without `SetDirtyPortals()` a tag-only repair is live in memory and absent from the world file.

- Does removing an entry from the live `m_portalObjects` dictionary cause any vanilla path to throw? `GetSaveClonePerChunk` (:77621-77632), `FindObjects` (:77367-77381) and `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` (:77457-77469) all enumerate it. Test on a scratch world before enabling registry surgery.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- `tplite.repair` cannot be typed from a vanilla client console: client Terminal.TryRunCommand forwards only commands present in the client's own table with RemoteCommand=true (client assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:45734-45760); the server's RPC_RemoteCommand (:79921, body via Console.instance.TryRunCommand) never sees mod-only names. Vanilla dedicated server has no stdin command reader (no ReadLine/OpenStandardInput in assembly_valheim_SERVER). Provide a mod-owned trigger.
- Apply the DataRevision-margin rule from the reassert engine on every repair write under a live client owner (RPC_ZDOData revision gate :77103-77112).
- Registry surgery on the live m_portalObjects dictionary must call SetDirtyPortals() (:76702) afterwards and must delete the entry under the stale sector, not the current one.
- Vanilla's 'dangling clear' may route through the owner via RPC_SetConnection (:100637-100648); the mod's write is the forceImmediateConnection path.
- Tag normalisation must check the target group's parity: merging a 1-member group into an existing EVEN group (a paired pair) produces N=3 and strands the merged portal permanently (phase 2 :100607-100622 never repairs a live pair). Merge only into a size-1 group or an odd group with a stranded member.
- Enforcement is admin-facing-only, not server-enforced: for unmanaged portals each action is a single write with no re-assertion; a vanilla owner client can retag it back at any time (TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag client :144327-144342) and vanilla's 5 s pass keeps operating on the result. Continuing enforcement exists only for portals then adopted by the reassert engine.
- Registry surgery on GetPortals(): the leaked entry is a ZDOPool-released object (HandleDestroyedZDO :76988), so identify it by m_uid == ZDOID.None / !IsValid(), never by position; and set DirtyPortalObjects (SetDirtyPortals :76702) afterwards so the corrected list is what gets saved.
- Soften the ForceSendZDO spike claim: SendZDOs is budgeted per peer per frame (10240 bytes, :77007-77046) with overflow left in m_forceSend (:77260-77280); the mod cap avoids queue growth, not a single-frame burst.
- Snapshot/rollback prereq must not key on ZDOID (ZDO.Load :74552 regenerates IDs); restoring a 'pre-repair' snapshot after a restart requires stable keys.

**Verifier reasoning:**

Corrections: (1) The `tplite.repair` console trigger is not reachable from a vanilla client: client Terminal.TryRunCommand only forwards to ZNet.RemoteCommand when the command exists in the CLIENT's own dictionary with RemoteCommand=true (client :45734-45760); an unknown `tplite.*` command prints 'not a recognized command' and never leaves the client. RPC_RemoteCommand on the server (:79921 register; body admin-gated by adminlist hostname → Console.instance.TryRunCommand) therefore only ever carries vanilla remote commands. Terminal.UpdateInput is GUI/input-focus driven (:45775-), and the dedicated server has no stdin reader in vanilla (no Console.ReadLine/OpenStandardInput anywhere in the server assembly). Invocation must come from the mod's own channel (config flag/timer, a watched file, a stdin thread the mod owns, or a piggy-backed vanilla remote command). (2) Inherits the reassert engine's DataRevision-collision caveat: repairs under a live client owner must bump DataRevision by a margin. (3) 'Dangling clear identical to vanilla' — vanilla's path delegates to an online owner via RPC (:100637-100648); the mod's direct write is vanilla's force path. (4) A tag suffix like `home-2` is fine, but any mod-written tag longer than the client's 10-char input limit cannot be re-entered by a player. (5) Registry surgery on m_portalObjects must also set DirtyPortalObjects (SetDirtyPortals) or the corrected bucket state is not written at the next save; and removing the stale duplicate must remove the entry whose sector != zdo.GetSectorIndex(), otherwise HandleDestroyedZDO later fails to find the live one.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Write primitives are real: Game.ConnectPortals is public (:100589) and callable on demand (it first runs ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698, committing any staged pair early — harmless); ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals (:76702-76705) is required for a tag-only write because IncreaseDataRevision → SetDirtySector (:73832-73839, :76695-76700) only marks a normal chunk and AddObjectsPerChunk excludes portal prefabs (:77572) while the ChunkPortal file is written only when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77631); GetPortals returns the live m_portalObjects (:77643-77646). Two design errors: (1) 'Tag normalisation ... when and only when it merges a 1-member group into an existing group' recreates the odd-count strand whenever the target group is already an even pair — merging 'Base ' into a 2-member 'Base' yields N=3 and the merged portal becomes the permanent orphan (phase 2 :100607-100622 only pairs None portals). The merge must be gated on target-group parity (size 1, or odd with a stranded member). (2) The enforcement label is wrong: for unmanaged portals every repair is a one-shot write; nothing stops a vanilla client from retagging 'home-2' back to 'home' the next second (client RPC_SetTag :144327-144342 needs only ownership, which ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76927 grants within 2 s), and vanilla's reconciler keeps acting on the result. Only portals subsequently handed to the reassert engine are enforced. Registry surgery caveat verified: the stale duplicate entry references a ZDOPool-released object (:76988), so mutation must compare by m_uid/IsValid, not object identity alone. The ForceSendZDO fan-out concern is overstated: SendZDOs (:77007-77062) already caps each peer's packet at the 10240-byte send budget and breaks (:77043-77046), leaving the rest queued in m_forceSend (:77260-77280) — the per-tick cap is still good practice, but vanilla does not spike 'every peer in one frame'.

### 72. AuditEngine — attributed change log for every tag and link write

`ops-admin:AuditEngine — attributed change log for every tag and link write` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** reactive-detection-only → **reactive-detection-only** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Census-diff as the complete channel, an RPC_RoutedRPC prefix for authenticated attribution, and m_onZDODestroyed for deletions — with 'probable' vs 'confirmed' actor never conflated.


**How it works:** Three complementary sources, only one of which is complete:

**(1) Census diff — the only complete source.** Every tick, diff (tag, tagauthor, connection, position, owner) per portal. This catches changes that never touch the wire: `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally and skips `RouteRPC` entirely when `targetPeerID == m_id` (:83577-83595), and `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string,…)` targets `m_zdo.GetOwner()` (:82855-82858), so a client that already owns a portal retags it in-process with zero packets. The resulting ZDO change still reaches the server, because `ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision` queues `ZDOMan.ClientChanged` on a client (:73832-73849, :77727-77730) and `CreateSyncList`'s non-server branch drains that queue to the server peer regardless of distance (:77241-77258). Detection latency = the census tick.

**(2) `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` Harmony prefix — authenticated attribution when available.** `RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (:83632) is the one and only place where the authentic socket and the payload coexist; `m_senderPeerID` is deserialised straight off the wire (`RoutedRPCData.Deserialize` :83487-83495) and is a client self-report everywhere downstream. In the prefix: save `pkg.GetPos()`, deserialise a **copy** (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())`), match `m_methodHash` against `"RPC_SetTag".GetStableHashCode()`, resolve the true sender as `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)`, and take `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()` — the PlatformUserID the Steam session ticket / PlayFab auth actually verified at connect (ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo :79843-79870; the same identity vanilla's own admin check uses, ZNet.RPC_Kick :81670). Restore `pkg.SetPos()` and return true.

**(3) `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed`** (:76033, invoked :76975) — a public `Action<ZDO>` field fired before removal, so the portal is still readable. Filter with `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())`. **Combine, never assign**: `ZNetScene.Awake` already attaches its own handler (:81953).

Record shape: `{utc, portalId, field, from, to, actor, actorConfidence}`. `actorConfidence` is `confirmed` only for source (2); for a census-detected change with no matching RPC it is `probable`, resolved to the nearest connected character within 40 m at detection time (`ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS` :81024-81044), or `unknown`. Follow `AuditLog.Flag`'s discipline of writing `Unknown` rather than guessing (AuditLog.cs:15). Suppress the mod's own writes by having the reassert engine register each intended change in an 'expected' set the audit subtracts.

Store as a bounded ring buffer (2000 entries, the `ItemLedger` pattern) plus an append-only `portal-audit.log`.


**Player experience:** No player-visible effect unless the operator enables the optional toast. The log reads `[AUDIT] tag (1240,31,-3310) 'trade' -> 'TRADE' by 76561198…/Rohan (confirmed) at 14:02:11Z` for a retag that crossed the wire, and `[AUDIT] link (0,32,4) #A -> #B by (probable) Rohan @ 6m` for one that did not. A player who demolishes someone else's gate shows up as `[AUDIT] destroyed (410,33,-88) tag 'home' builder Sigrid`.


**Failure modes:**
- Reading the live `ZPackage` in the RPC prefix without saving/restoring `GetPos()` — the real handler then reads garbage and every routed RPC on the server breaks.
- Assigning to `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` instead of `Delegate.Combine` — this wipes ZNetScene's own handler (:81953) and breaks client-side object destruction for the whole server.
- Trusting `m_senderPeerID` or `s_tagauthor`: both are unverified client input (:83489, :143587-143602).
- Presenting a 'probable' actor as fact in a Discord channel where players read it — this is how a mod gets someone falsely accused of griefing.
- Missing changes made while the mod was down: the audit is a live diff, not a reconstruction. Snapshot at shutdown and diff at boot to catch the gap.

- Deletions are authenticatable: prefix-match "DestroyZDO" (registered :76155, routed with targetPeerID 0 at :76950) in the same RPC_RoutedRPC prefix; payload is a ZPackage of ZDOIDs. Upgrade destroyed-portal actor to 'confirmed' when matched.
- s_tagauthor is client self-reported (client TeleportWorld.SetText :144323) — never a confirmed actor.
- RPC_PeerInfo spans :79774-; Steam ticket check :79842-79852; PlayFab check is async and non-blocking (:79854-79868).
- Source (2) attribution is an attempt record, not proof of effect: the RPC only takes effect if the owner client has the portal instantiated and passes IsOwner (client RPC_SetTag :144329); when owner is 0 or the server, HandleRoutedRPC drops it server-side (:83651-83664) and no client applies it. Mark actorConfidence 'confirmed' only when the census diff shows the corresponding tag change within one tick of the RPC; otherwise log 'attempted'.
- Owner-local retags (zero packets) are the COMMON case, not the exception: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76927) hands any nearby portal to the nearby peer within 2 s, so the player standing at a portal is almost always its owner. Expect most entries to be 'probable', and set expectations in the playerExperience text accordingly.
- s_creator is a long player ID; 'builder Sigrid' requires a persisted ID→name map (ZNetPeer.m_playerName is client-supplied and only available while online).
- Census-diff latency and the 'expected' suppression set both depend on the census tick; document that a client change that is overwritten by the reassert engine within the same tick is invisible to the diff (only the RPC prefix, if the retag crossed the wire, sees it).

### 73. MetricsEngine — portal counts, transit counts and most-used routes

`ops-admin:MetricsEngine — portal counts, transit counts and most-used routes` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** reactive-detection-only → **reactive-detection-only** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Inventory metrics for free from the census; transit metrics only from Wonderland's position-straddle heuristic, because vanilla's own PortalsUsed stat never leaves the client.


**How it works:** **Free, exact metrics** (census-derived, zero extra cost): total portals; portals per tag; per biome (`WorldGenerator.GetBiome` :151692); per builder (`s_creator`); connected vs unconnected; managed vs unmanaged; new/destroyed per hour (from the audit stream). Plus server-wide context vanilla already exposes: `ZDOMan.instance.NrOfObjects()` (:77658), `GetSentZDOs()`/`GetRecvZDOs()` (:77663-:77671), `ZDOPool.GetPoolActive/Size/Total` (used by vanilla at :42773) — all public and all useful for the 'is my ZDO count exploding' question that portal mods get blamed for.

**Transit counts are heuristic only.** Vanilla increments `PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed` (ordinal 15, :106516) via `Game.IncrementPlayerStat` → `PlayerProfile.IncrementStat` (:100569-100572, :106287-106300), which writes an in-memory dictionary saved only into that client's own `.fch`. `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles` (:79653-79670) merely tells each client to save its own file and returns nothing. So the server can never read it.

The usable signal is the straddle test Wonderland already ships and has already tuned against a live false-positive: `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit(fromPos, toPos, radius=40f)` (PositionWatch.cs:148) walks `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()` (zero-alloc, :77643) and fires when both ends of a position sample sit within 40 m of some portal, with a secondary check that one end's `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` target is within 60 m of the other end. Sample every 3 s from `ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` (:81024). Invert its sense (count the transit instead of suppressing the speed alarm) and additionally record the two nearest portal ids → a (from,to) route counter, which yields 'most-used routes'.

Exclusions, all cheap and exact: skip when `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)` (respawn); skip when `Character.InInterior(pos)` (:4538) changes across the sample or |Δy| > 1000 (a dungeon door — `class Teleport` has no ZDO at all, :143316-143390, so it must never be counted as a portal transit); skip admins (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName())` :81811) whose `tplite` teleports would otherwise inflate the numbers.

Aggregate on a 60 s timer into a rolling window; emit into the heartbeat line, the JSON export and Discord.


**Player experience:** Players see nothing. The operator's heartbeat line becomes `[Heartbeat] 'Wubarrk' up 3h12m | 4 online: Rohan, Sigrid, … | 214 portals / 61 tags | 37 transits/hr | top route Spawn->Swamp (11)`. A community Discord gets a weekly `#portal-report` embed showing the busiest gates.


**Failure modes:**
- Presenting heuristic transits as exact. A 3 s sample can miss a player who walks through and back, and two portals within 40 m of each other produce false positives.
- Counting dungeon-door transits as portal transits — `Teleport.Interact` (:143345-143370) never touches `NoPortals` and has no ZDO, but produces a huge position jump.
- Counting server-issued teleports (RPC_TeleportPlayer, :41957-41968) as portal use.
- Trying to read `PortalsUsed` from anywhere server-side — it is not networked at all.
- Sampling faster than 3 s on a large server: the cost is O(players) ZDO reads plus a `GetPortals()` walk per player per sample.

**Open questions:**
- What is the real false-positive/false-negative rate of the 40 m straddle on a dense base with many gates close together? Instrument both the heuristic and a manual tally over a play session.
- Does a portal transit reliably produce two samples on opposite sides at a 3 s interval, or does the ≥8 s distantTeleport black screen (Player.UpdateTeleport :15349) mean the arrival sample lands mid-teleport at the frozen origin? Log raw samples around a known transit.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit is private static (PositionWatch.cs:148) — copy it; and its nearFrom/nearTo are first-match, not nearest.
- For route counting make the partner test mandatory: fromPortal.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) resolved via ZDOMan.GetZDO must lie within radius of toPos; the primary 'both ends near some portal' test alone counts hub walk-throughs as transits.
- Admin teleports via Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer execute on the client (gated on Player.m_localPlayer, :41962-41968); the admin-skip is correct but should key on the mod's own teleport log rather than admin status, or admins' real portal use is also dropped.
- IsPortalTransit as shipped is a suppression filter reached only after speed > ceiling (PositionWatch.cs:66-76, :140); used standalone it fires when both ends are within 40 m of any portal, including the same one. The counter must require displacement (e.g. distance > 2×radius or speed > ceiling) and nearFrom != nearTo.
- The helper returns the first matching portal in m_portalObjects iteration order (PositionWatch.cs:160-176), not the nearest; for route attribution rewrite it to select the nearest portal at each end and to prefer the pair where nearFrom's ConnectionZDOID == nearTo (the extended check at :183-207 already encodes this).
- Respawn skip via s_dead is redundant: the respawned player is a new ZDO (new ZDOID, new peer.m_characterID), so a ZDOID-keyed sampler never compares across death. Keep it only as belt-and-braces.
- Route keys must be stable across restarts (position or mod key), since ZDOIDs are regenerated on load (ZDO.Load :74552); a rolling window that spans a restart otherwise fragments.
- State explicitly that transit counts are a lower-bound heuristic: a transit and return within one 3 s sample window, or a transit between two portals < 80 m apart, is missed or double-counted.

Critical flaw in the 'invert its sense' plan: in Wonderland IsPortalTransit is only reached AFTER the speed gate (speed > 40 m/s, PositionWatch.cs:66-76 → IsLegitimateTransit :119 → :140). Called standalone it returns true whenever BOTH sample ends are within 40 m of ANY portal — including the same portal — so a player idling beside a gate would register a 'transit' every 3 s. The counter needs the displacement/speed gate and nearFrom != nearTo. Route attribution: the helper returns the FIRST portal within radius in dictionary iteration order (:160-176), not the nearest; in a hub with several gates within 40 m the (from,to) route is misattributed unless the helper is rewritten to pick the nearest and prefer the connection-target match. Respawn exclusion via s_dead is unnecessary but harmless (respawn creates a new character ZDO, so the per-ZDOID sample map never straddles it). Admin exclusion undercounts admins' legitimate portal use.

### 74. Output surface: atomic JSON/CSV file export

`ops-admin:Output surface: atomic JSON/CSV file export` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A periodic and on-demand write of the full census, health findings and metrics to a JSON (and CSV) file under BepInEx/config, written temp-then-replace so a reader never sees a torn file.


**How it works:** Serialise the immutable census DTO plus the current health findings and the metrics window. Write to `<name>.tmp`, then `File.Replace`/`File.Move` — the exact atomic pattern `TortalPortal/PortalExport.Write` (PortalExport.cs:75) and Wonderland's `SupplySwitch.Save` (SupplySwitch.cs:100-165) already use, so an external tool tailing the file never reads a half-written document.

Cadence: on a timer (default 300 s), on every network-file reload, on `tplite.export`, and once from the `ZNet.WorldSaveStarted` hook (`public static Action`, :78989, invoked at :80524 on the main thread before `PrepareSave`) so the export is always consistent with the world file on disk.

Two files: `portals.json` (full, nested, machine-readable) and `portals.csv` (flat, one row per portal, for spreadsheets and `awk`). CSV columns: `id,tag,x,y,z,biome,zone,prefab,connected,partnerId,partnerTag,distance,reciprocal,network,ownerPeer,builder,tagAuthor,firstSeen,lastChanged`.

Prior art is already server-side and directly liftable: `PortalExport` is an `IsServer()`-gated coroutine that waits for ZDOMan/Game, counts portals per `s_creator` from `PlacementPatch.GetAllPortals()` (which wraps `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` with a prefab-iterative fallback, PlacementPatch.cs:195) and joins names from `PlayerNames` — the only two files of full TortalPortal that already run exclusively on the server.

Build the DTO on the main thread; serialisation itself can be done on a thread-pool task from the already-copied DTO, never from live ZDOs.


**Player experience:** Invisible to players. A community website cron-rsyncs `portals.json` every 5 minutes and renders a public gate directory. An operator runs `jq '.portals[] | select(.connected==false) | .tag' portals.json | sort | uniq -c` to find every broken network in one line.


**Failure modes:**
- Writing directly over the live file — a reader mid-read gets a truncated document. Always temp-then-replace.
- Serialising live ZDO objects from a background thread; they are pooled and can be recycled mid-serialise (ZDOPool.Release → ZDO.Reset :73536-73545).
- Exporting `sessionZdoId` as the primary key and letting an external tool build state on it — it changes every restart.
- Exporting on a very short timer with a large world: JSON for 1000 portals is ~400 KB and rewriting it every 10 s is pointless disk churn.

**Designer citations:** PortalExport.OnZNetStart / Write — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PortalExport.cs:32, :75 ; PlacementPatch.GetAllPortals — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PlacementPatch.cs:195 ; SupplySwitch.Save atomic write — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/SupplySwitch.cs:100-165 ; ZNet.WorldSaveStarted — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78989, invoked :80524 ; ZDOMan.GetPortalList — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648

### 75. Output surface: Discord webhook reporting

`ops-admin:Output surface: Discord webhook reporting` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Fire-and-forget posts of health findings, audit events and a periodic portal summary through Wonderland's already-shipped DiscordWebhook helper.


**How it works:** Lift `DiscordWebhook` verbatim (DiscordWebhook.cs): one shared static `HttpClient` with a 10 s timeout, `Send()` fire-and-forget, `SendBlocking(msg, timeoutMs)` for the shutdown message only — the process can exit before a fire-and-forget task runs — and a hand-rolled JSON escaper so no JSON library is needed. It requires a `System.Net.Http` reference resolved from the net472 reference assemblies (Wonderland.csproj:72).

Event classes, each independently toggleable in config:
- **Health digest** (default: only when findings change) — 'tag `home` now has 5 portals; one is permanently stranded'.
- **Audit stream** (default off, high volume) — retags and relinks with attribution and a confidence marker.
- **Destruction notices** — from `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` (:76033), filtered to `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021).
- **Network reload** — 'networks.json reloaded: 3 networks, 0 errors' / the full error list on a failed parse.
- **Periodic summary** — shares the Heartbeat timer rather than running a second one, exactly as Wonderland's `Heartbeat.OnUpdate` shares between the log and Discord heartbeats (Heartbeat.cs:21-56).
- **Server lifecycle** — 'portal engine online / offline', the offline one via `SendBlocking` from `OnDestroy`.

Rate-limit and coalesce in the mod, not in Discord: batch findings into one message per interval, and hard-cap messages per minute. Delivery is best-effort by design — a failed post is logged and dropped, never retried, because nothing else depends on it landing.

Everything posted is derived from the main-thread DTO; the HTTP call itself happens on a thread-pool task and must never touch ZDOMan.


**Player experience:** Players see nothing in-game. The server's Discord gets, in `#server-ops`: `🌀 **Portal health** — 214 portals / 61 tags. ⚠️ tag `home` (5 portals) permanently strands one gate at (410, 33, -88). ⚠️ tag `Base ` looks like a typo for `Base`.` Community members who built the gates learn why one never connects, without an admin having to log in.


**Failure modes:**
- Posting the audit stream by default: a busy server generates dozens of retag events an hour and the channel becomes unreadable.
- Posting 'probable' attribution to a channel players read — a false griefing accusation.
- Using `Send()` from `OnDestroy` — the process exits first and the offline message never arrives; that is exactly why `SendBlocking` exists.
- Creating a new HttpClient per post: socket exhaustion under Mono.
- Leaking the webhook URL into the exported JSON or a log line.

**Designer citations:** DiscordWebhook.Send / SendBlocking / IsConfigured — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/DiscordNotify/DiscordWebhook.cs:27, :42, :20 ; System.Net.Http reference — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Wonderland.csproj:72 ; Heartbeat shared timer — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Heartbeat.cs:21-56 ; ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76033 ; Game.PortalPrefabHash — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100021


**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Subscribe with `+=` / `Delegate.Combine`, never assignment: vanilla `ZNetScene.Awake` already chains its own `OnZDODestroyed` onto the same field (:81953) and the server does run ZNetScene. Subscribe only after `ZDOMan.instance` exists (e.g. Harmony postfix on `ZNetScene.Awake` or `ZNet.Awake`), not from the plugin's own Awake.
- The destruction callback carries no sender identity. If the audit stream wants 'destroyed by <player>', take it from a Harmony prefix on `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO(long sender, ZPackage pkg)` (:76950) where the routed sender is available; the callback alone can only say 'destroyed'.
- Audit 'attribution' for retags is inherently partial: an owning client retags with no routed RPC on the wire (prior review), so the only evidence is the ZDO data change plus owner id; the 'confidence marker' must reflect that, and it depends on the audit/health engines that are prerequisites, not on anything in this option.
- Note for the Health digest example: an odd-sized tag group strands one gate because `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (:100664-100679) pairs randomly with no tie-break, so the stranded gate changes identity across reconnects; the digest should say 'one of N is stranded' rather than naming a permanent loser unless the health engine has pinned it.
- `m_onZDODestroyed` is a public multicast field that `ZNetScene.Awake` populates with `Delegate.Combine` (:81953). The mod must `+=` (Combine), never assign `=`; assigning after ZNetScene.Awake silently removes ZNetScene's own `OnZDODestroyed` handler.
- The destroy callback carries no sender. Destruction attribution (who deleted the gate) needs a Harmony prefix on `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO(long sender, ZPackage)` — the callback alone cannot say who.
- `Heartbeat.OnUpdate` (Heartbeat.cs:21-56) is Wonderland-specific code driven from WonderlandPlugin.Update and reads WonderlandConfig; 'sharing the timer' means copying the pattern into TortalPortal Lite, not calling Wonderland.
- `SendBlocking` from `OnDestroy` only fires if the plugin MonoBehaviour is destroyed during an orderly `Application.Quit`; a SIGKILL/container stop skips it. Fine as best-effort, but do not promise the offline post.

**Verifier reasoning:**
