Wonderland's `DiscordWebhook` is exactly as described: static `HttpClient` with 10 s timeout, `Send` fire-and-forget (DiscordWebhook.cs:27), `SendBlocking` (:42), `IsConfigured` (:20), hand-rolled `JsonEscape`; `System.Net.Http` reference at Wonderland.csproj:72 and `System.Net.Http.dll` is physically present in the dedicated server's Managed folder (verified by listing /home/rohan/valheim-server/server/valheim_server_Data/Managed). `Heartbeat.OnUpdate` shares one timer between log and Discord (Heartbeat.cs:21-56). Nothing here depends on a local player or a GameObject. Corrections are about subscription hygiene and attribution honesty.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism holds. Vanilla ZNet itself already constructs a System.Net.Http.HttpClient on the dedicated server (`ZNet.m_httpClient` :79067, `new HttpClient()` :79394, HTTPS GETs to icanhazip etc. :79398-79426), so the assembly is loaded and TLS works headless; System.Net.Http.dll is in the Managed provenance table (REFERENCE-DLL-PROVENANCE.md:314). ### 76. Output surface: in-process HTTP endpoint

`ops-admin:Output surface: in-process HTTP endpoint` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


An HttpListener on a configurable loopback port serving the census/health/metrics snapshot as JSON and Prometheus text, answered entirely from a main-thread-built immutable DTO.


**How it works:** `System.Net.HttpListener` lives in `System.dll` and the dedicated server ships a full Mono runtime, so no new dependency beyond what the csproj already resolves for `System.Net.Http`.

Architecture is forced by thread-safety: ZDOMan has no locking anywhere, and vanilla's only background thread (`ZNet.SaveWorldThread` :80583) deliberately operates on a clone built on the main thread by `ZDOMan.PrepareSave` (:76197-76205). So the listener thread must **never** touch ZDOMan, ZNet, ZoneSystem or WorldGenerator. Instead: the census engine publishes `volatile Snapshot _latest` (fully immutable, pre-serialised to a `byte[]` on a thread-pool task) each tick; the listener thread only hands out `_latest`.

Routes: `GET /portals.json`, `GET /portals.csv`, `GET /health` (200 with `{ok:true}` or 503 with findings — directly usable as a container health probe), `GET /metrics` (Prometheus text: `tplite_portals_total`, `tplite_portals_unconnected`, `tplite_tag_groups`, `tplite_transits_total`, `tplite_repairs_total`, plus `valheim_zdos_total` from `ZDOMan.NrOfObjects()` :77658 sampled on the main thread).

Security: bind `127.0.0.1` by default and require an explicit `Bind` config change plus a bearer token to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Refuse to start without a token when bound non-loopback. No write routes at all in v1 — writes go through the file-queue or the admin console, both of which already have an authorization story.

Any text the listener thread wants in the server log must go through `Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog.Enqueue(...)` (`public static ConcurrentQueue<string>`, :43245), drained one line per frame by `Console.Update` into `AddString` → `ZLog.Log` (:42923-42925) — vanilla's own save thread reports errors exactly this way (:80675, :80710).


**Player experience:** Invisible in-game. An operator points Grafana at `http://server:9101/metrics` and gets a graph of portal count and transits per hour; their Docker healthcheck hits `/health` and restarts the container if the portal engine stops ticking.


**Failure modes:**
- Touching any Valheim singleton from the listener thread — ZDOMan, ZNetScene and ZDOExtraData are all unsynchronised static state; this will produce intermittent, unreproducible crashes.
- HttpListener requiring elevated privileges or an http.sys URL ACL on Windows hosts — Linux/Mono is fine, Windows dedicated servers may need `netsh http add urlacl`.
- Binding 0.0.0.0 with no token and exposing the full builder/PlatformUserID list to the internet.
- Not disposing the listener in `Shutdown()`/`OnDestroy` — the port stays bound across a BepInEx hot reload.
- Serialising on the listener thread from live objects instead of from the pre-built byte[].

**Designer citations:** ZNet.SaveWorldThread (vanilla's only background thread) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:80583 ; ZDOMan.PrepareSave main-thread clone — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76197-76205 ; ZDOMan.NrOfObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77658 ; Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:43245; drained Console.Update :42923-42925; vanilla producer :80675 ; System.Net.Http csproj reference precedent — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Wonderland.csproj:72


**Open questions:**
- Does `System.Net.HttpListener` actually start under the dedicated server's bundled Mono? Test with a trivial listener on 127.0.0.1 in a throwaway plugin before designing around it.
- Does BepInEx's Mono resolve `System.dll` for the plugin without an explicit reference? Confirm at build and at load.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- WRONG: 'Any text the listener thread wants in the server log must go through Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog'. That queue (`public static ConcurrentQueue<string>`, :43245) is drained only inside `Console.Update` (:42922-42925), which early-returns at :42892-42895 unless `IsConsoleEnabled()`; on a dedicated server that is true only with `-console` on the command line (`FejdStartup.ParseArguments` :97288-97290) or the `EnableConsole` PlatformPref (:42880). Without it the queue is never dequeued and grows without bound. Vanilla's own save thread logs directly with `ZLog.Log(" ### Save World Thread Started! ### ")` (:80597) — `ZLog.Log` is a bare `UnityEngine.Debug.Log` wrapper (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:13049-13054) and Unity's Debug.Log is thread-safe. Use `ZLog`/`Debug.Log` or BepInEx's ManualLogSource from the listener thread; do not use the Terminal queue.
- WRONG: 'vanilla's only background thread (ZNet.SaveWorldThread)'. The server assembly also spawns `ZNtp.NtpThread` (:82916), `PlayFabZLibWorkQueue.WorkerMain` (:89324), `ZPlayFabMatchmaking.BackgroundLookupPublicIP` (:90716), `HeightmapBuilder.BuildThread` (:129677) and `LiquidVolume.UpdateThread` (:132692). The conclusion (never touch ZDOMan off-thread) is unchanged.
- `tplite_transits_total` cannot be a server-observed count: there is no server-side hook on teleport (see central constraint); it must be labelled as the PositionWatch `IsPortalTransit` heuristic (Wonderland/Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs), i.e. reactive-detection-only.
- `Console.Update`'s `AddString` path is `ZLog.Log("Console: " + text)` plus a chat-buffer write (:45983-46002), so even when drained it adds nothing a direct `ZLog.Log` would not.
- Mono `HttpListener` caveats to state explicitly: prefixes must end in '/', `GetContext`/`BeginGetContext` callbacks run on thread-pool threads (never call Unity APIs there), and the listener must be stopped in `OnDestroy` or the port stays bound until process exit.
- Do NOT route listener-thread log lines through `Terminal.m_threadSafeConsoleLog`: `Console.Update` drains it only when `IsConsoleEnabled()` (:42890-42893, :42923), which on a dedicated server requires `-console` (:97288-97291) or the EnableConsole pref (:42880). Log directly with `ZLog.Log`/`UnityEngine.Debug.Log` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:13051) or the BepInEx logger — both thread-safe; vanilla's save thread does exactly that at :80673.
- 'vanilla's only background thread' is false: `ZNtp.NtpThread` (:82916), `PlayFabZLibWorkQueue.WorkerMain` (:89324), `ZPlayFabMatchmaking.BackgroundLookupPublicIP` (:90716), `HeightmapBuilder.BuildThread` (:129677), `LiquidVolume.UpdateThread` (:132692), plus `Task.Run` in ZNet's public-IP lookup (:79415). The conclusion (ZDOMan has no locking; touch it only on the main thread) still stands.
- `tplite_transits_total` cannot be a real counter: no server-side hook observes a teleport. It is a heuristic from player position jumps near two portals (Wonderland PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit, PositionWatch.cs:148) and must be labelled as such in /metrics.
- Loopback-by-default contradicts the stated Grafana experience: `http://server:9101/metrics` from another host needs the non-loopback bind + bearer token path. Inside Docker, a 127.0.0.1 bind serves the container's own healthcheck but nothing outside.
- 'pre-serialised each tick' is wasteful and unnecessary; serialise on change (the census ticks on a multi-second cadence anyway).

### 77. Output surface: generated realm map (SVG first, PNG as a stretch)

`ops-admin:Output surface: generated realm map (SVG first, PNG as a stretch)` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A server-rendered top-down map of every portal, coloured by biome and linked by its connection, emitted as plain-text SVG — with a hand-rolled PNG encoder only if a raster is truly required.


**How it works:** **SVG (recommended, feasible today).** Pure string building, zero image libraries, zero graphics device. World XZ maps to SVG coordinates with `sx = (x + 10500) * scale`, `sy = (10500 - z) * scale` (world radius constants: `WorldGenerator.worldSize = 10000f`, `waterEdge = 10500f`, :151118-151122). Draw, in order: a background disc for the ocean; optional biome tinting by sampling `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(x, z)` (:151725) on a coarse grid (a 256×256 sample grid = 65 536 closed-form noise evaluations — run it once at OnWorldReady on a time-sliced coroutine, never per export, and cache); a `<line>` per portal connection; a `<circle>` per portal coloured by network; a `<text>` label per tag. Output ~50–200 KB, opens in any browser, zooms losslessly, and is trivially diffable in git.

For an even cheaper variant, use `ZNet.World.m_biomeData` (`AltBiomeWorldData`, assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:92332) — a precomputed 2048×2048 grid at 12 m/cell with `PointBiomes[x,y]` and `PointHeights[x,y]`, populated by `ZNet.ServerLoadWorld` before any peer connects (:79273-79285), indexed via `AltBiomeWorldData.WorldSpaceToMapSpace(float)` (:92424). That is an O(1) lookup per cell with no noise evaluation at all.

**PNG (stretch, needs an in-game check).** `Texture2D` + `EncodeToPNG` requires the ImageConversion module and a graphics device; a dedicated server reports `SystemInfo.graphicsDeviceType == GraphicsDeviceType.Null` (vanilla itself branches on exactly that in `ZNet.UpdatePlayerList` :81245-81299). `System.Drawing` is unreliable under Mono without libgdiplus. The safe route is a ~120-line hand-rolled PNG writer (IHDR + zlib *stored* blocks + Adler-32 + CRC-32 + IEND) over a raw RGB byte buffer — no compression, larger files, but no dependency and no GPU.

Either renderer runs off the main thread from the census DTO, writing temp-then-replace.


**Player experience:** No in-game effect. The operator opens `portals.svg` in a browser and sees the whole realm: 214 dots on a biome-tinted disc, coloured lines showing every link, the `TRADE` ring drawn as a closed triangle, and three grey dots with no line at all — the stranded gates. They post it in Discord and players immediately understand the network layout without any client mod.


**Failure modes:**
- Calling `Texture2D`/`EncodeToPNG` headless and getting a null graphics device exception at runtime, or worse a silently black image.
- Sampling `WorldGenerator.GetBiome` per export instead of once — 65 536 noise evaluations on every 5-minute export is pure waste.
- Using any `ZoneSystem` raycast helper for terrain shading; they all return the no-hit fallback server-side (Game.FixedUpdate reference pin :100465).
- Labelling every portal at full zoom — 200 overlapping `<text>` nodes is unreadable; label per tag group, not per portal.
- Drawing interior portals (y > 3000, :4538) at their XZ position on top of the surface gate above them without a distinct marker.

- PNG stretch: `UnityEngine.ImageConversionModule.dll` IS shipped in the dedicated server's Managed folder (verified listing), so the module-availability concern is moot; the remaining unknown is only whether `Texture2D.EncodeToPNG` works under `GraphicsDeviceType.Null` (Unity's CPU-side texture path normally does in -batchmode -nographics) — keep as needs-ingame-check for that single call.
- `System.IO.Compression.dll` is also present in Managed, so a hand-rolled PNG writer can emit a real zlib stream via `DeflateStream` (2-byte zlib header + deflate + Adler-32) instead of stored blocks; stored blocks remain the zero-risk fallback.
- `GetBiome(float,float)` early-returns based on `m_world.m_menu` (:151727) — irrelevant on a server but the cheaper route is the precomputed grid; note `VerifyBiomeData` loads `cache/biomedatacache.bin` and regenerates only when missing or `m_worldVersion != DeepNorth` (:92398-92407), so the first boot on a world may spend seconds generating 4.2 M samples before the mod's OnWorldReady runs — not the mod's cost, but it explains a slow first start.

- `PointBiomes` is `Heightmap.BiomeIndex[,]`, not `Heightmap.Biome`; convert with the `ToBiome()` extension (:129582). Index order is `[x, y]` (`GenerateBiomePoints` writes `PointBiomes[j, i]` with j from world x, :92439-92449). Outside `waterEdgeSqr` it is pre-filled Ocean with height -1000 (:92442-92446).
- The 'needs a graphics device' claim for PNG is unsupported: `Texture2D.SetPixels`+`EncodeToPNG` do not use the GPU (the documented headless trap is `Graphics.Blit`/`ReadPixels`, HEADLESS-AND-EMPTY-SERVER-FACTS.md:12-24), ImageConversionModule.dll is in the server Managed folder, and `Heightmap` already does `new Texture2D` headless (:128580). Treat EncodeToPNG as needs-ingame-check (one call), with the hand-rolled writer as fallback. Texture2D is main-thread-only, so the PNG variant cannot 'run off the main thread'.
- Prefer the `m_biomeData` grid to re-sampling `GetBiome` on a coroutine: the grid is already computed at load (:79281) and read-only afterwards, safe to read from the render thread; a 256×256 downsample of it is 65k array reads, not 65k noise evaluations.

### 78. Network state snapshot, rollback and migration

`ops-admin:Network state snapshot, rollback and migration` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Capture the live portal topology (positions, tags, links) to a versioned file that can be diffed, restored onto a running server, or replayed onto a different world.


**How it works:** A snapshot is the census DTO plus a schema version and a world fingerprint (`ZNet.instance.GetWorldName()` :80876, `GetWorldUID()` :80871, `ZNet.World.m_seedName` :112376). Written temp-then-replace to `<config>/snapshots/<name>.json`. Taken automatically before every `--apply` repair, on every network-file reload, and on `ZNet.WorldSaveStarted` (:78989/:80524) so the newest snapshot always matches the world file on disk.

**Restore** re-resolves every snapshot entry by rounded position (never ZDOID — `ZDO.Load` renumbers, :74552), then issues the reassert engine's write primitive for each tag and connection that differs. Portals present in the snapshot but absent from the world are reported, not recreated, unless `--recreate` is passed; recreation uses `ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, portalPrefabHash)` (:76674-76692) followed by the mandatory five lines `ZNetView.Awake` normally performs (:82613-82620): `Persistent = true; Type = ObjectType.Default; Distant = false; SetPrefab(hash); SetRotation(rot);` — `CreateNewZDO` sets none of them, and a prefab-less ZDO will not survive a save. Pass the real portal hash to `CreateNewZDO` so `AddIfPortal` (:77732-77752) files it in `m_portalObjects` and sets `DirtyPortalObjects`; setting the prefab afterwards on a hash-0 ZDO leaves it in the sector array, where `AddObjectsPerChunk` (:77572) then skips it as a portal and it is written to no chunk file at all.

**Migration to another world** rewrites the network file's `at` coordinates but cannot move the portals themselves — never call `zdo.SetPosition()` on a portal: `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73756) so the `m_portalObjects` key goes stale, clients in the new zone never receive it through sector sync, and `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76980-76986) later fails to remove it, leaking the entry permanently. Destroy and recreate instead: claim ownership (`DestroyZDO` is a silent no-op unless `IsOwner()`, :76929-76935) then `ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)`. Note the recreated portal must use a **fresh** ZDOID — `m_deadZDOs` (:76043) causes the server to immediately re-destroy any ZDO recreated under a previously-destroyed id (`RPC_ZDOData` :77133-77137).

Complement this with vanilla's own safety net: `ConsiderAutoBackup` runs inside `SaveWorldThread` (:80601-80604), so a bad mass repair is also recoverable from the world backup.


**Player experience:** No player-visible effect during a snapshot. During a restore, players near affected gates see hover text change and the connected-glow flicker once as links are rewritten. The operator types `tplite.restore pre-repair-2026-09-12T14:02Z` and gets `restored 4 portals, 0 missing, 0 recreated`.


**Failure modes:**
- Restoring a snapshot taken on a different world — the position keys resolve to unrelated portals. Refuse on a world-UID mismatch unless `--force`.
- Recreating a portal without the five ZNetView.Awake lines: the ZDO is non-persistent and prefab-less, vanishes at the next save, and clients log a CreateObject failure.
- Recreating under an old ZDOID: `m_deadZDOs` makes the server destroy it again immediately.
- Repositioning a portal instead of destroy-and-recreate: permanent `m_portalObjects` corruption.
- Snapshotting during a save: take it from `WorldSaveStarted` (before `PrepareSave`), never from `WorldSaveFinished`, which is reached through `PrintWorldSaveMessage` (:80566-80581) — a method that dereferences `MessageHud.instance` unguarded at :80574/:80578.

**Designer citations:** ZNet.GetWorldUID / GetWorldName — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:80871, :80876 ; World.m_seedName — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:112376 ; ZNet.WorldSaveStarted / WorldSaveFinished — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78989, :78991; invoked :80524, :80580 ; ZNet.PrintWorldSaveMessage unguarded MessageHud — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:80566-80581 ; ZNet.SaveWorldThread ConsiderAutoBackup — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:80601-80604 ; ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76674-76692 ; ZNetView.Awake fabrication lines — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82613-82620 ; ZDOMan.AddIfPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77732-77752 ; ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk portal exclusion — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77572 ; ZDO.SetSector portal early-return — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73752-73756 ; ZDOMan.DestroyZDO owner gate — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76929-76935 ; ZDOMan.m_deadZDOs / RPC_ZDOData re-destroy — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76043, :77133-77137 ; ZDO.Load ZDOID renumber — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74552


**Open questions:**
- Does `WorldSaveFinished` actually fire on a dedicated server, or does `PrintWorldSaveMessage` NRE on `MessageHud.instance` first (:80574)? Probe by subscribing and logging; if it never fires, the post-save hook is unavailable and only `WorldSaveStarted` can be used.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- The `m_deadZDOs` warning is misplaced: `CreateNewZDO(Vector3,int)` cannot reuse a dead id (fresh `m_sessionID` per process, monotonically increasing `m_nextUid`, :76674-76682). The re-destroy at `RPC_ZDOData` :77133-77137 applies only to ZDOs newly created from a PEER packet (`flag == true`); it protects against a client re-sending a destroyed ZDO, not against server-side recreation. Keep the note but reattribute it.
- Restore's write primitive must claim ownership first: `ZDO.SetConnection` from the server on a client-owned portal bumps DataRevision and pushes to peers, but the owning client's own subsequent writes (and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` handing ownership to a nearby peer) can overwrite it; vanilla's own `Game.SetConnection` delegates via `RPC_SetConnection` to an online owner (prior review). The 'restored 4 portals' report must be verified on the next reconcile tick, not assumed at write time.
- Durability caveat must be explicit: the on-disk format holds one `ZDOConnectionHashData` slot per ZDO (`RegenerateConnectionHashData` :75461-75478), so a restored ring/fan-in/one-way/self-loop topology lives only until the next world load; the snapshot file plus a boot-time reapply is the ONLY durable record. Restore-then-restart without the mod re-applying at boot silently degrades to pairs.
- Recreation: also set `zdo.SetRotation`/`Persistent = true` BEFORE the next save and call `SetDirtyPortals()` is already implied by AddIfPortal; but the tag write (`Set(ZDOVars.s_tag)`) does NOT dirty the portal chunk (see footprint verdict) — since AddIfPortal already dirtied it in the same tick this is fine only if tag and creation happen before the next save; otherwise call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` after tag writes.
- Minor: `ZNet.PrintWorldSaveMessage` (:80566-80581) is cited but unused; `WorldSaveFinished` fires from it on the main thread after the save thread completes, which is the correct hook for a post-save snapshot verification if wanted.
- `ConsiderAutoBackup` is not a per-save safety net: it backs up only when `m_backupCount != 1` and only at `m_backupShort` (7200 s) / `m_backupLong` (43200 s) intervals (:80718-80732, :79053-79057, `-backupshort/-backuplong/-backups` :97463-97473). A bad `--apply` followed by the next autosave is recoverable from vanilla only if a backup happened to be due at that save; the mod's own pre-apply snapshot is the real rollback path.
- Restore writes go through `Game.SetConnection`, which is private and routes to the owning online client via `RPC_SetConnection` unless owner==0/dead peer/force; and `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901-76926) runs every 2 s and reassigns ownership of Persistent ZDOs in a peer's active area to that peer. Restore of gates with a player nearby must claim ownership per write and accept a round-trip; the 'flicker once' experience is real only when the write lands directly.
- `WorldSaveStarted` fires on the main thread inside `SaveWorld` (:80524) before `PrepareSave` — snapshot there is consistent with the clone — but for non-pairwise topologies the on-disk file does NOT match the snapshot (the file collapses rings/one-way links); say 'the snapshot matches the live state at save time', not 'the world file'.
- Snapshot position keys must be rounded coarsely enough to survive a client repositioning nothing (portals do not move) but not so coarse that two adjacent gates collide; also `m_seedName` is the user-typed seed string while `m_seed` is the int — fingerprint on `m_uid` + `m_seed`.

### 79. World-save footprint of mod-created ZDOs, and how to clean them up

`ops-admin:World-save footprint of mod-created ZDOs, and how to clean them up` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Quantify exactly what the mod adds to the world file — one portal chunk rewrite plus per-portal key bytes — and ship an explicit garbage-collection command for mod-created anchors and keys.


**How it works:** **Where portals live on disk.** Every portal in the world is written to one dedicated chunk, `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal = new ChunkIndex(1, 0)` (:113180). `GetSaveClonePerChunk` clones *every* entry of `m_portalObjects` into it (:77621-77632, via `ZDO.Clone` :73552) — but only when `DirtyPortalObjects` is set (:77621). There is no `Persistent` filter on that path, unlike ordinary chunks (:77572). Consequences:
- Adding a mod key to every portal grows exactly one file. At ~16 bytes per int key, 500 portals × 3 keys ≈ 24 KB. Negligible.
- Any single portal change dirties the flag and rewrites the **whole** portal file at the next autosave (default `Game.m_saveInterval = 1800f`, :99914; overridable by `-savinterval`, :97477).
- Idempotent re-assertion costs nothing: `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` early-returns on an unchanged value (:74951-74961) and `BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false on equality (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345), so no DataRevision bump, no dirty flag, no rewrite.
- After a world load `LoadChunks` ends with `DirtyPortalObjects = false` (:76474-76531), so a freshly loaded world will not rewrite the portal file until something actually changes.

**Non-portal anchor ZDOs** (used for computed-coordinate destinations) go into ordinary chunks and are only written when `Persistent == true` (:77572). `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` does **not** set Persistent (:76674-76692).

**Cleanup.** Tag every mod-created ZDO with a mod-private int key (e.g. `"tplite_owned"` = a schema version). GC pass: enumerate `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Int, hash)` (:75390-75407 — Float/Long/Int/String only; an unindexed nested scan, so one-shot at boot, never per tick), and for each result not referenced by the current network model, claim ownership and `ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)` (:76929). For keys written onto *player-built* portals (which must survive), remove the key instead with the public statics `ZDOExtraData.RemoveInt/RemoveString/RemoveFloat` (:75122+) and then `SetDirtyPortals()`.

Expose the footprint in the report: mod-created portal count, mod-created anchor count, total mod keys, and the estimated added bytes.


**Player experience:** No player-visible effect. The operator runs `tplite.footprint` and sees `mod-created portals: 4 (hub anchors); mod-created anchors: 2; mod keys on 214 portals: 642; est. added save bytes: ~11 KB; portal chunk rewritten on 3 of the last 10 autosaves`. On uninstall they run `tplite.uninstall --clean-keys --destroy-anchors` and the footprint drops to zero.


**Failure modes:**
- Creating an anchor without `Persistent = true` — it vanishes on the next restart with no error and the portal it served becomes permanently dangling.
- Creating an anchor with a fabricated prefab hash: `FilterZDO` only drops prefabs in `s_brokenPrefabsToFilterOut` (two entries, :76109/:76350); an unknown hash merely logs a warning and the ZDO is **kept forever** (:76346-76361), so every boot prints 'ZDOs with prefabs not supported' and clients attempt to create an object for it. Always use a real, harmless prefab hash.
- Running `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` or `GetAllZDOsWithHash` on a tick — the former walks a 512×512 = 262 144-slot array ~400 non-empty sectors per call (:77442-77494), the latter is an unindexed nested walk over every ZDO's field dictionary (:75390-75407).
- Calling `DestroyZDO` without claiming ownership: it is a silent no-op (:76929-76935).
- Assuming a tag write persists without `SetDirtyPortals()`.

**Designer citations:** ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113180 ; ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk portal branch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77621-77636 ; ZDO.Clone — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73552 ; ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk persistence filter — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77572 ; ZDOMan.LoadChunks clears DirtyPortalObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76474-76531 ; ZDOMan.DirtyPortalObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76139-76149 ; Game.m_saveInterval / -savinterval — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:99914, :97477 ; ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76674-76692 ; ZDOMan.FilterZDO / s_brokenPrefabsToFilterOut — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76346-76361, :76109 ; ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75390-75407 ; ZDOExtraData.RemoveInt/RemoveFloat — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75120-75130 ; ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77442-77494 ; ZDOMan.DestroyZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76929-76935 ; BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue — assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345


**Open questions:**
- Measure the real portal chunk file size on a mature world before and after enabling the mod, to replace the byte estimate with a number.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- WRONG: 'Any single portal change dirties the flag and rewrites the whole portal file'. `DirtyPortalObjects` is set ONLY by `ZDO.SetConnection`/`UpdateConnection` with `ConnectionType.Portal` (:73657-73677), `ZDOMan.AddIfPortal` (:77751), `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76986), legacy `ZDOMan.Load` (:76539) and explicit `SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702-76705). A tag or mod-key write goes `ZDO.Set` -> `IncreaseDataRevision` (:73832-73840) -> `SetDirtySector` -> `SetDirtyChunks` (:76696-76722), which dirties the ORDINARY chunk hierarchy for that sector — a file the portal is not in (AddIfPortal removed it from `m_objectsBySector`) — and leaves the portal chunk clean. Net effect: every mod key write on a portal triggers a wasted rewrite of up to four ordinary chunk files and is silently dropped at the next save unless the mod also calls `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`. Even a client's own retag arriving through `ZDO.Deserialize` (:74206-74241) dirties nothing; vanilla only persists it because the resulting `Game.ConnectPortals` disconnect calls SetConnection.
- Consequence for the GC/`--clean-keys` command: `ZDOExtraData.RemoveInt` etc. are raw table edits with no DataRevision bump and no dirty flag; the option's 'then SetDirtyPortals()' is mandatory, and the removal is also never pushed to connected clients (use the instance methods `zdo.RemoveInt/RemoveString` :74060-74075 style if propagation matters; they still do not dirty the portal chunk).
- Byte estimate: an int key on disk is 4-byte hash + 4-byte value (~8 bytes) plus a per-type count byte, not ~16; the conclusion (negligible) stands.
- Flag spelling: the server argument is `-saveinterval` (`FejdStartup.ParseServerArguments` :97475-97478, `Mathf.Max(5, result4)`), not `-savinterval`.
- `GetAllZDOIDsWithHash` with an unsupported type calls `UnityEngine.Debug.Break()` after LogError (:75403-75405) — harmless in a player build but never pass Vec3/Quat/ByteArray.
- Enforcement label: this is an operator report plus a mod-scoped GC; nothing player-facing is enforced. The destroy/remove writes are server-authoritative only after an ownership claim (`DestroyZDO` :76929-76935).
- 'Any single portal change dirties the flag' is false for key/tag writes. Only `ZDO.SetConnection`/`UpdateConnection` (Portal type) call `ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals()` (:73656-73676; sole callers :73663, :73675). `ZDO.Set(int,int)`/`Set(int,string)` → `IncreaseDataRevision` → `SetDirtySector` → `SetDirtyChunks(sector)` (:76694-76700) marks the ORDINARY chunk of the portal's sector — which does not contain the portal — so the mod key is not saved and an unrelated chunk file is rewritten. Every mod key write onto a portal ZDO must be followed by `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`; this is also why tag writes are silently lost.
- Side effect to add to the footprint report: each mod key write on a portal dirties that sector's ordinary chunk hierarchy (3 sizes, `SetDirtyChunks` :76706+), so 'grows exactly one file' is wrong on the first write pass — it also rewrites up to one ordinary chunk per portal sector touched. Subsequent idempotent writes cost nothing.
- `ZDOExtraData.RemoveInt`/`ZDO.RemoveInt` (:75126-75129, :74027-74030) do not bump DataRevision: the removal never replicates to connected clients and does not persist unless `SetDirtyPortals()` (portals) / `SetDirtySector` (anchors) is called. Worse, `ZDO.Deserialize` merges with `ZDOExtraData.Add` (:73xxx Deserialize, ReadData → Add), so a client that still holds the key and later becomes owner (`ReleaseNearbyZDOS` :76901-76926) re-adds it on its next push. Run `--clean-keys` on an empty server (or at boot before peers connect), then save.
- Anchor GC by `GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Int, hash)` is fine, but note `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO` is a no-op unless `IsOwner()` (:76929-76935) — claim ownership with `SetOwner(sessionID)` first; and a destroyed ZDOID lands in `m_deadZDOs` (:76993-76995) so never reuse ids.
- `FilterZDO`'s unknown-prefab warning (:76346-76361) only runs when `newVersion` (chunk saved under a different world version) — it is not a per-boot log spam source; the real cost of an unknown-prefab anchor is a ZDO that no client can instantiate.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The on-disk facts are right: `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal = new ChunkIndex(1, 0)` (:113180); `GetSaveClonePerChunk` clones every `m_portalObjects` entry into that chunk with no `Persistent` filter, but only `if (DirtyPortalObjects)` (:77621-77632); ordinary chunks require `item3.Persistent && !PortalPrefabHash.Contains(prefab)` (:77572); `LoadChunks` ends with `DirtyPortalObjects = false` (:76527); `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` returns false on an unchanged value (:74951-74961) and `BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false on `Equals` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345) via `InitAndSet` (:75681-75685), so idempotent writes bump nothing. `GetAllZDOIDsWithHash` supports Float/Long/Int/String only (:75390-75407). `ZDOExtraData.RemoveFloat/RemoveInt/RemoveLong/RemoveVec3/RemoveQuaternion/RemoveString/RemoveByteArray` all exist as public statics (:75121-75155). `Game.m_saveInterval = 1800f` (:99914). BUT the option's central dirty-tracking claim is wrong and, if believed, loses data: mod key writes on portals do NOT dirty the portal chunk.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Disk model is right: `ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal = new ChunkIndex(1, 0)` (:113180); `GetSaveClonePerChunk` clones every `m_portalObjects` entry into that chunk with no Persistent filter, gated on `DirtyPortalObjects` (:77621-77632), while ordinary chunks filter `Persistent && !portal` (:77572); `LoadChunks` ends with `DirtyPortalObjects = false` (:76527); `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` early-returns on equality (:74951-74961) and `BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue` returns false on `Equals` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321-345) so idempotent re-assertion bumps nothing. `GetAllZDOIDsWithHash` supports Float/Long/Int/String only (:75390-75407); `ZDOExtraData.RemoveInt/RemoveFloat` are public statics (:75121-75129) and `ZDO.RemoveInt` wraps them (:74027-74030); `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` covers `m_portalObjects` (:77457-77459). The important thing the option gets WRONG is the dirtying model: only `ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection` call `SetDirtyPortals()` (:73656-73676; the only callers of `SetDirtyPortals` are :73663 and :73675). A plain `Set(int/string)` goes `IncreaseDataRevision` → `ZDOMan.SetDirtySector` → `SetDirtyChunks(zdo.GetSectorIndex())` (:73605, IncreaseDataRevision body, :76694-76700), which dirties the ORDINARY chunk for that sector — one the portal is not in — and never the portal file. So writing `tplite_owned` onto 500 portals rewrites up to N unrelated ordinary chunk files at the next save and does not persist the keys at all unless the mod calls `SetDirtyPortals()`. `RemoveInt` bumps nothing (:74027-74030) so removals neither replicate nor persist without the same call. Net: feasible, but the footprint arithmetic and the 'any single portal change dirties the flag' sentence need rewriting. ### 80. What happens when the mod is removed (graceful-uninstall design)

`ops-admin:What happens when the mod is removed (graceful-uninstall design)` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Nothing corrupts and no phantom portals appear — but managed topologies degrade to random same-tag pairs after one restart, so ship an explicit uninstall command that lands the world in a clean, vanilla-stable state.


**How it works:** Traced end to end through the decompile:

**Mod-created portal-prefab ZDOs survive and behave like normal portals.** They are written into the portal chunk unconditionally when dirty (:77621-77632) and `LoadChunks`'s portal branch loads them straight into `m_portalObjects` and `m_objectsByID` with **no** `FilterZDO` call at all (:76474-76482). Vanilla then pairs them by tag like any other gate. No phantoms, no orphan files.

**Mod keys on portal ZDOs become dead bytes.** Nothing reads them; they cost a few bytes each in the portal chunk forever. Harmless, but removable — hence `tplite.uninstall --clean-keys`.

**Non-portal anchor ZDOs** persist if `Persistent` was set and the prefab is real. With an unknown prefab hash they are *kept* and merely warned about (:76346-76361) — a permanent log-spam legacy. Destroy them on uninstall.

**Topologies unravel, in two stages.** At runtime, a ring A→B→C→A survives indefinitely because `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 never checks reciprocity (:100600-100604). At the **next world load**, it does not: the on-disk format gives each ZDO exactly one `ZDOConnectionHashData` slot (`RegenerateConnectionHashData` :75461-75478 writes the source slot then overwrites it with the Target slot), which can only express a pairwise perfect matching. So `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (:77850-77893) restores at most one pair per ring and vanilla randomly re-pairs the leftovers. One-way links come back **bidirectional** (ConnectPortals writes both sides, :77879-77885). Self-loops are erased entirely.

**Therefore the honest answer is: no corruption, but any non-pairwise topology is lost at the first restart after removal, silently and without warning.**

`tplite.uninstall` should: (1) snapshot; (2) collapse every managed network into plain vanilla pairs, or split tags so that each group has an even count (eliminating the permanent strand); (3) remove mod keys; (4) destroy mod anchors; (5) write a final report naming every gate whose tag was changed so the operator can tell players. Also expose `tplite.export --for-uninstall` producing a human-readable 'here is what your networks were' document.


**Player experience:** If the operator just deletes the DLL: for the rest of that session every gate keeps working exactly as it did. After the next server restart, players find the three-gate `TRADE` ring has become one working pair plus one gate that says `unconnected` forever, and nobody can tell them why. If the operator runs `tplite.uninstall` first, every network has already been split into clean pairs with distinct tags (`TRADE-1`, `TRADE-2`) and a Discord post lists the new tag for each gate, so nothing changes at the restart.


**Failure modes:**
- Removing the mod without running uninstall and only discovering the topology loss days later, after a restart.
- Leaving anchors with unknown prefab hashes behind — every boot logs 'ZDOs with prefabs not supported' and clients fail to create the object.
- Leaving an odd-sized managed tag group behind: vanilla permanently strands one member (Game.ConnectPortals phase 2, :100607-100622).
- Assuming `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (load-time, hash-based, :77850) is the same thing as `Game.ConnectPortals` (runtime, tag-based, :100589) — patching or reasoning about the wrong one gives the wrong uninstall model.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- 'At most one pair per ring' is only guaranteed for a 3-ring. For rings of n>=4 the surviving pairs depend on `s_connections` Dictionary iteration order: pair X->Y survives iff X's Portal slot and Y's Target slot are both the last writes to those keys, so a 4-ring can come back as two pairs (order B,D,A,C) or one. State it as 'a subset of a pairwise matching, order-dependent, at most floor(n/2)'; the 3-gate TRADE example is correct as written.
- 'A permanent log-spam legacy' for unknown-prefab anchors is wrong server-side: `FilterZDO` only classifies when `newVersion` (`bool newVersion = world != version`, :76476; guard at :76348), i.e. only on the first load after a game-version change; on same-version loads unknown prefabs load silently. The real spam is client-side: `ZNetScene.CreateObject` logs `"Missing prefab hash: ..."` (client assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82225-82236) on every create pass while a player is in that sector. Still destroy them on uninstall — the reason is client log noise and a phantom ZDO in sector sync, not server logs.
- Uninstall step (2) must claim ownership before every tag/connection write and call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` after tag writes: `ZDO.Set(s_tag)` does not dirty the portal chunk (see footprint verdict), so a split-tag uninstall followed by a save without any connection change would lose the new tags. In practice the split changes connections too (phase-1 tag mismatch -> SetConnection(None) dirties), but do not rely on it.
- 'Mod keys become dead bytes ... forever' is true only for keys that reached disk, which requires a portal-chunk-dirtying event between the write and a save; keys written without `SetDirtyPortals()` may never have been saved at all.
- Also note the degradation is not specific to uninstall: any non-pairwise topology is lost on EVERY restart; the mod itself must re-apply from its network file at boot. Uninstall merely removes the re-applier. The design should say so, since it defines what the 'reassert at boot' engine must do.
- 'With an unknown prefab hash they are kept and merely warned about — a permanent log-spam legacy' is wrong: `FilterZDO` (:76346-76361) only evaluates `s_brokenPrefabsToFilterOut`/`HasPrefab` when `newVersion` is true (chunk saved under a different world version than current, :76472). Unknown-prefab anchors are kept silently on normal boots; the warning appears once per version transition. They should still be destroyed on uninstall — clients can never instantiate them.
- 'split tags so that each group has an even count (eliminating the permanent strand)' is arithmetically impossible for an odd group: pairing leaves one gate over regardless of tags. The uninstall command can only make the strand explicit (name the gate, or retag it to a solo tag) — it cannot eliminate it. State this instead of promising even counts.
- Mod-created portal ZDOs survive only if the mod set `Persistent = true` and the real portal prefab hash at creation (`CreateNewZDO` sets neither, :76674-76692; `ZNetView.Awake` :82613-82620). They are then written unconditionally because the portal chunk path has no Persistent filter (:77621-77632) — but a portal created with hash 0 then `SetPrefab` stays in the sector array and is dropped by `AddObjectsPerChunk` (:77572), i.e. it vanishes at the first save, not 'survives'.
- The uninstall command's own tag/connection rewrites must call `SetDirtyPortals()` after tag writes (only `SetConnection` does it automatically, :73656-73676) and route through ownership (`Game.SetConnection` delegates to an online owner) — otherwise the 'clean pairs' state is not what the world file contains at the next save.

### 81. Version migration — mod schema, world version and Valheim build fingerprinting

`ops-admin:Version migration — mod schema, world version and Valheim build fingerprinting` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Version every persisted artifact, fingerprint the game build at boot, and refuse to run destructive passes when the fingerprint is unrecognised.


**How it works:** Three independent versions, all recorded in every persisted file and in the boot log:

1. **Mod schema version** — an int in `networks.json`, every snapshot and the audit file. Migrations are forward-only, run on load, write the upgraded file back after taking a `.bak`, and log every field they changed. Refuse to load a schema newer than the running mod.
2. **Valheim build** — `Version.GetVersionString()` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:112112) plus the network version literal (40u as seen at :42875/:97033) logged at Awake. Keep a config'd allowlist of verified builds; outside it, run in read-only mode (census/health/export still work, reassert and repair refuse) until the operator sets `AcceptUnverifiedBuild=true`. Precedent: TortalPortal's MIGRATE-1.0.md re-verified the mod unmodified against 1.0.12 (build 25253764, network version 40) with 37 types / 55 method bodies changed and all 48 Harmony targets still resolving — so the 1.0.7 decompile is a valid authority through at least 1.0.12 for everything this mod touches.
3. **World version** — `ZNet.World.m_worldVersion`/the `Version.World` enum used by `ZDOMan.LoadChunks(…, Version.World version)` (:76486). Record it so a snapshot taken on an older save format is flagged on restore.

Structural self-checks at Awake, all cheap and all failing *soft*: confirm `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` is non-empty (:100021); confirm `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` returns without throwing; confirm the Harmony targets resolve via `AccessTools.Method` before patching and wrap each patch set in `SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch` (SubsystemRegistry.cs:99), which degrades a signature change to a logged warning rather than killing Awake.

Honour the Mono JIT rule GameShape.cs encodes: a compile-time binding to a member the loaded assembly lacks throws at JIT of the *calling* method, so an internal try/catch does not save it. Any version-sensitive call must live in its own method reached only after a reflection-based probe confirms the shape (GameShape.Detect, Core/Compat/GameShape.cs:72). Never use the single-result `Type.GetMethod` overload — a compatibility patcher can inject a same-name/same-parameter overload and make it throw `AmbiguousMatchException` (GameShape.cs:155 comment, learned live).


**Player experience:** Nothing player-facing. On a game update the operator sees `[tplite] Valheim 1.0.14 is not in the verified list (last verified 1.0.12). Running READ-ONLY: census/health/export active, reassert and repair disabled. Set AcceptUnverifiedBuild=true to override.` Their gates keep working exactly as vanilla does; the mod simply stops writing until a human says it is safe.


**Failure modes:**
- Silently continuing to write ZDOs after a game update that changed a signature — the worst possible failure for a mod that rewrites persistent world data.
- Binding at compile time to a member that may not exist and taking down the whole Awake at JIT time.
- Migrating a file in place without a `.bak` — a bad migration is unrecoverable.
- Using the game version string as a Harmony-target guarantee; verify the targets directly with AccessTools.

### 82. Compatibility with other server mods that touch ZDOs

`ops-admin:Compatibility with other server mods that touch ZDOs` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Enumerate the exact shared mutable surfaces — m_onZDODestroyed, ZDO.SetOwner prefixes, Game.ConnectPortals patches, Terminal.commands, ZRoutedRpc.Register — and adopt a defensive convention for each.


**How it works:** Each contention point, with the safe convention:

1. **`ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed`** (:76033) is a single public `Action<ZDO>` field, and `ZNetScene.Awake` already attaches its own handler (:81953). Always `Delegate.Combine`; never assign. An assignment silently disables ZNetScene's destruction handling for the entire server.
2. **`ZDO.SetOwner` prefixes.** Wonderland's `WaterBuoyancyEngine.ZdoSetOwnerPatch` (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313) already prefixes this global hot path (`ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` calls it for every peer every 2 s, :76901-76927). Two mods both vetoing is a real hazard. Convention: only add the guard if measured contention demands it; fail fast on `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(prefab)` as the very first test; never block `uid == 0` or `uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID()`; log once per minute when a veto fires so contention is visible.
3. **`Game.ConnectPortals` patches.** A prefix returning false disables *all* vanilla pairing, including for portals we do not manage. Do not do it. If our cooperative model is being defeated because another mod prefixed it, detect that (managed links stop being torn down when we deliberately mistag a probe portal) and log a compatibility warning rather than fighting.
4. **`Terminal.commands`.** The ConsoleCommand ctor does `commands[command.ToLower()] = this` (:43096/:43114) — an indexer assignment, so a duplicate name silently clobbers with no exception and no log. Namespace every command `tplite.` and, at registration, check whether the key already exists and log if so.
5. **`ZRoutedRpc.Register`.** Per the digest it uses `Dictionary.Add`, so re-registering an existing name throws `ArgumentException`. Never register a vanilla name (`ChatMessage`, `ShowMessage`, `RPC_SetConnection`); for a mod-private RPC use a GUID-prefixed name and probe the private `m_functions` dictionary via `AccessTools` before registering.
6. **Sender identity.** `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653-100662) is registered on every peer with **no** sender check and will rewire any ZDO's Portal connection to any target. Any mod (or malicious client) can undo our topology instantly. Our reassert loop restores it within 2 s; do not claim 'unbypassable'. The same applies to `ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey`/`RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` (:116022-116037), which also have no sender validation.
7. **Other mods writing `s_tag`.** Detect: if the census sees a managed portal's tag change to a value we did not write, and no `RPC_SetTag` crossed the wire, log a 'foreign writer' warning naming the portal rather than silently fighting forever.

Ship a `tplite.compat` command that lists every Harmony patch currently applied to the methods we care about, via `Harmony.GetPatchInfo(MethodBase)` — this turns a support ticket into one line of output.


**Player experience:** No player-visible effect. ### 83. Performance budget and cache-invalidation policy

`ops-admin:Performance budget and cache-invalidation policy` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portal ops cost is independent of world ZDO count because portals live in their own always-resident dictionary — everything expensive is a non-portal query, and this option defines the budgets for each.


**How it works:** **The headline fact:** portals are not in `m_objectsBySector` at all. `AddIfPortal` files them in `m_portalObjects` and explicitly calls `RemoveFromSector` (:77732-77752); they are loaded wholesale from the dedicated portal chunk at world load (:76474-76482) and never released (`ReleaseZDOS` only reassigns ownership :76872-76885; `FlushClientObjects` is client-only :76180-76183). So `GetPortalList()`/`GetPortals()` is O(P) in portal count and completely independent of whether the world holds 10 000 or 300 000 ZDOs.

**Budgets:**
- `GetPortalList()` — one `List<ZDO>` alloc of P refs (:77648-77656). At P = 500 and 1 Hz that is ~4 KB/s of gen-0 garbage. Acceptable. `GetPortals()` (:77643) is zero-alloc for read-only walks; `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit` already uses it.
- Census tick 1.0 s; health 30 s; reassert 2.0 s; metrics sample 3.0 s; metrics aggregate 60 s; export 300 s; file-queue poll 1.0 s; config poll 5.0 s; heartbeat 15 min.
- **Non-portal queries are the expensive ones.** `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative` (:77442-77494) walks a 512×512 = 262 144-slot array (`new ZDOMan(512)` :79163, `ResetSectorArray` :76163) at ~400 *non-empty* sectors per call, re-hashing the prefab name each call — one full pass is ⌈nonEmpty/400⌉+1 calls. `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash` (:75390-75407) is an unindexed nested walk over every ZDO's field dictionary. Both are one-shot/boot-only. Use Wonderland's `PrefabSetSweeper` with an explicit `sectorBudget` (ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:135, :153) when several prefab families are needed in one walk; its header records the name-based scanner taking *hours* for ~800 prefabs.
- Spatial 'nearest altar/bed/ship' lookups use `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear` (ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25) over `ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects` (:77142) — note that method reuses a shared `m_visitedSectorIndices` HashSet and is **not reentrant**.
- Broadcast budget: cap `ForceSendZDO` at 256 per sweep (StructureUpkeep.cs:29-40 precedent); `ZDOMan.SendZDOs` re-serialises the entire ZDO with no delta encoding (:77053-77062) and a 10 240-byte per-peer send-queue cap (:77010-77016).

**Cache policy:** cache the biome grid (immutable for the life of the world), the prefab-hash→name map (immutable after OnWorldReady), and the `s_creator`→name map (append-only). Invalidate the census every tick — there is no dirty flag to key off, and `GetPortalList` has no cache of its own. Never cache ZDO object references across ticks (ZDOPool recycling, :73536-73545). Cache ZDOIDs and re-resolve.


**Player experience:** No player-visible effect, which is the point: the operator's `ServerLog` line (vanilla's own 10-minute `InvokeRepeating("ServerLog", 600f, 600f)`, :100048/:100089-100096) showing `Connections N ZDOS:M sent:X recv:Y` should be indistinguishable with and without the mod. `tplite.perf` prints each engine's last and 95th-percentile tick cost in microseconds so a regression is visible immediately.


**Failure modes:**
- Running any prefab-iterative or hash scan on a tick instead of at boot.
- Calling `FindSectorObjects` from inside a loop already iterating its results — the shared visited-set makes it non-reentrant.
- Mass `ForceSendZDO` in one frame on first boot after enabling networks.
- Assuming `GetPortalList()` is cached and calling it several times per tick from different engines instead of once into a shared snapshot.
- Scaling worry to world ZDO count — the relevant number is portal count, and it is the one to alarm on.

So ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear / FindSectorObjects results will contain portal ZDOs; dedupe against the census by ZDOID if both sources feed one index. (Only FindDistantObjects, :77384+, skips portals.)

ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(ZDOID) (:75998-76000) just adds to each peer's m_forceSend HashSet; the actual per-tick send is already bounded by the 10240-byte queue cap in SendZDOs (:77010-77016), so the 256 cap is a mod-side smoothing choice, not a vanilla-derived budget.
- GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative's terminal pass (index >= array length) scans sector 0 AND all of m_portalObjects (:77445-77468) — one full pass is ⌈nonEmpty/400⌉ + 1 calls as stated, but the +1 call is not free at large portal counts.
- IncreaseDataRevision fires only on the owner for position changes (InternalSetPosition checks IsOwner() before bumping); DataRevision is still a valid 'something changed' signal per ZDO for the census diff but not a per-field dirty flag — consistent with 'invalidate the census every tick'.
- A portal dirty flag does exist: ZDOMan.DirtyPortalObjects (private, :76139-76149; set :77751, :76986, :73663, :73675; cleared :76527; consumed by save :77621-77635). It is since-last-save and is NOT set by s_tag writes (ZDO.Set → IncreaseDataRevision → SetDirtySector :73832-73840), so per-tick invalidation remains correct.
- Portals are excluded from m_objectsBySector but FindObjects merges m_portalObjects into every FindSectorObjects result (:77367-77380) — ReleaseNearbyZDOS, CreateSyncList and ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear all see portals; only GetPortalList is O(P).

### 84. Subsystem architecture — registry, engines, tick rates, data ownership, config surface

`ops-admin:Subsystem architecture — registry, engines, tick rates, data ownership, config surface` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


One BepInEx plugin, one ops subsystem, nine engines with disjoint write ownership and a fixed intra-tick ordering, mirroring Wonderland's registry/heartbeat shape so the two mods are maintainable side by side.


**How it works:** **Plugin shell** (copy `WonderlandPlugin`, Plugin.cs:35-143 and `SubsystemRegistry`, SubsystemRegistry.cs, renamed). `Awake()`: init logger → `GameShape.Detect()` (only if `FindNear` is used) → build `ConfigSync` → `TpLiteConfig.Bind` → `RegisterSubsystems()` → `Subsystems.InitializeAll(Config, ConfigSync, harmony)` → `SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch(harmony, typeof(WorldReadyHook))`. `WorldReadyHook` is a postfix on `ZNetScene.Awake` — the first point prefab lists are populated. `Update()`: `PollConfigFile()` (5 s) → `PollNetworkFile()` (5 s) → `PollCommandFile()` (1 s) → `Heartbeat.OnUpdate(dt)` → `Subsystems.OnUpdate()`. `OnDestroy()`: `Subsystems.ShutdownAll()` → `_harmony.UnpatchSelf()` → `DiscordWebhook.SendBlocking("portal engine offline")`.

**One subsystem, `PortalOpsSubsystem`**, owning nine engines. Fixed intra-tick order, because ordering is semantics not taste:

1. `PortalCensus` — 1.0 s. **Owns** the snapshot + the change stream. Writes nothing.
2. `NetworkModel` — event-driven on file change. **Owns** the parsed networks and their position→ZDOID resolution.
3. `AuditEngine` — consumes the change stream *before* any write this tick, subtracting the reassert engine's declared 'expected changes' set. **Owns** the ring buffer and `portal-audit.log`.
4. `NetworkReassertEngine` — 2.0 s. **The only writer of `s_tag` and `ConnectionType.Portal`.** Declares its intended writes to the audit engine before issuing them.
5. `HealthScanEngine` — 30 s. **Owns** findings. Pure read.
6. `RepairEngine` — on demand / slow timer, opt-in, dry-run by default. Writes only through the reassert engine's primitive; never writes directly.
7. `MetricsEngine` — 3 s sample, 60 s aggregate. **Owns** counters + route table.
8. `ExportEngine` — 300 s + on-change + on `ZNet.WorldSaveStarted`. Pure read; serialises off-thread from the DTO. **Owns** `portals.json`, `portals.csv`, `portals.svg`.
9. `CommandEngine` — registers ConsoleCommands from a `Terminal.InitTerminal` postfix; drives the file queue; dispatches to the others. **Owns** nothing.

Plus a mod-wide `Heartbeat` ticked directly from `Update()` (not through the registry), exactly as Wonderland does (Heartbeat.cs:21) — it is a mod-wide concern, not any one engine's.

**Ownership rule, enforced by convention and by code review:** exactly one engine may write any given ZDO field, and the census may never write at all. Everything else reads the census snapshot, never live ZDOs.

**Config surface** (BepInEx `.cfg`, scalars only; topology lives in `networks.json`): `[General]` Enabled, VerboseLogging, AcceptUnverifiedBuild. `[Census]` IntervalSeconds. `[Networks]` File, ReassertSeconds, AllowTagRewrite, MaxWritesPerTick. `[Health]` IntervalSeconds, ReportUnmanagedOddGroups, ReportInteriorPortals. `[Repair]` AutoRepair (default false), DryRunDefault (true), MaxActionsPerRun. `[Audit]` Enabled, LogFile, RingSize, ToastOnBlockedRetag. `[Metrics]` TransitDetection, SampleSeconds, StraddleRadius. `[Export]` Json, Csv, Svg, IntervalSeconds, Directory. `[Discord]` WebhookUrl, Health, Audit, Destructions, Heartbeat. `[Http]` Enabled, Bind, Port, Token. `[Commands]` FileQueueEnabled, ConsolePrefix.

Every scalar is bound through the `BindSynced*` helpers (WonderlandConfig.cs:406-442) and registered with `ConfigSync` — pointless for a zero-client mod but free, and it gains the locking/version behaviour if a companion client ever appears.


**Player experience:** Ordinary players experience the mod only as: gates that stay correctly connected, occasionally a tag that snaps back to the network's tag with a toast (`This gate belongs to the TRADE network.`), and nothing else. The operator experiences it as one `.cfg` of scalars, one `networks.json` of topology, a set of `tplite.*` console commands, a JSON/CSV/SVG export directory, a Discord channel and a heartbeat line every 15 minutes.


**Failure modes:**
- Two engines writing the same ZDO field — the classic way a self-healing mod oscillates forever.
- Running the audit after the reassert without an 'expected changes' set, so the mod attributes its own writes to players.
- Putting topology in the BepInEx `.cfg` — flat key=value cannot express nested lists, and the resulting stringly-typed format is unvalidatable.
- Doing ObjectDB/ZNetScene prefab reads in `Initialize()` instead of `OnWorldReady()`; worse, assuming `ObjectDB.instance` is non-null even at `OnWorldReady` — it frequently is not (BuffRosterEngine.cs:83-96 retries once per tick until it resolves).
- Letting an engine throw and take down the whole plugin — every call must go through the registry's try/catch (SubsystemRegistry.cs:29-79) and every patch through `SafePatch` (:99).

**Designer citations:** WonderlandPlugin.Awake / Update / OnDestroy — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Plugin.cs:35, :71, :78 ; WorldReadyHook on ZNetScene.Awake — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Plugin.cs:151-159 ; SubsystemRegistry.InitializeAll / OnUpdate / SafePatch — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/SubsystemRegistry.cs:24, :63, :99 ; IWonderlandSubsystem contract — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/IWonderlandSubsystem.cs:7 ; Heartbeat ticked from Update — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Heartbeat.cs:21 ; WonderlandConfig Bind helpers — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/WonderlandConfig.cs:150, :406-442 ; BuffRosterEngine ObjectDB retry — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/StatusEffects/BuffRosterEngine.cs:83-96 ; ZNet.WorldSaveStarted — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78989, invoked :80524 ; Wonderland.csproj (net472, server assemblies, publicizer) — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Wonderland.csproj:1-31, :19-27


**Open questions:**
- Should this be a separate plugin or a Wonderland subsystem? A separate plugin duplicates ~600 lines of shell (Plugin/Registry/Heartbeat/Config/AuditLog/DiscordWebhook/ZdoSpatialQuery/ConnectedCharacters/PlayerNotify) but keeps the portal problem out of a general-purpose mod, which is the reason TORTALPORTAL-LITE.md was split out in the first place. Decide before writing the shell.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- CommandEngine: a `tplite.*` ConsoleCommand registered on the server is unreachable from any vanilla client — Terminal.TryRunCommand (:45734-45747) forwards via ZNet.RemoteCommand only for names present in the CLIENT's dictionary with RemoteCommand=true, and the headless server reads no stdin. State explicitly that console registration serves (a) the file queue, (b) HTTP, (c) other server mods, and optionally (d) a Harmony prefix on ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand (:81879-81889) intercepting `setkey tplite.<verb> …` — `setkey` is vanilla remoteCommand:true (:43510-43534), the client forwards its raw text, and the adminlist check (:81881) has already run. Update the operator playerExperience line accordingly: admins do not get `tplite.*` in their in-game console.
- [Http] HttpListener: not verifiable from the decompile (the game assemblies never reference it). Precedent in this workspace: Wonderland ships System.Net.Http.HttpClient on the server (DiscordWebhook.cs:18) and TheRavensCall/Companion.cs:27-80 constructs an HttpListener in a Valheim mod — same Unity Mono System.dll — but neither is a verified Linux-headless run of HttpListener. Mark the HTTP engine needs-ingame-check (bind ACL, System.dll presence in the server's Managed/ folder) and keep it optional/off by default.
- 'Registered with ConfigSync — free': ServerSync sends its config package to every peer via a routed RPC on connect; vanilla clients drop it silently (ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC :82778-82786, unknown m_methodHash → no-op) but it is not zero bytes. Acceptable, just not 'free'.
- Plugin.OnDestroy is at Plugin.cs:76-80 (cited :78) and does not call DiscordWebhook.SendBlocking — that is an addition, and SendBlocking (DiscordWebhook.cs:42, 3000 ms default timeout) exists to support it.
- Structural probes (PortalPrefabHash, GetPortalList) referenced by the sibling version option belong in OnWorldReady, not Awake — Game.instance/ZDOMan.instance are null at plugin Awake (:100026, :79163).
- CommandEngine: server-only ConsoleCommands are unreachable from vanilla clients (Terminal.TryRunCommand :45733-45757 checks the client's own dictionary; RPC_RemoteCommand :81879-81888 relays only client-known RemoteCommand names) and the dedicated server reads no stdin. Treat the file queue / HTTP as the only real command surfaces; console registration is only for other mods or the mod's own dispatcher via Console.instance.TryRunCommand.
- Do not route server-side dispatch through ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand — its IsServer branch calls InternalCommand(null, cmd) which dereferences rpc.GetSocket() (:81869-81901) and throws NRE. Call Console.instance.TryRunCommand directly.
- Terminal.InitTerminal is private static (:43297) called from Terminal.Awake (:45762-45765); a postfix fires at first Terminal Awake, before ZNet exists — acceptable because ConsoleCommand.IsValid (:43203-43217) checks OnlyServer/ZNet at run time.
- The 'single writer of s_tag / Portal connection' rule is an intra-mod convention only; vanilla Game.ConnectPortals (:100589), Game.RPC_SetConnection (:100653) and client RPC_SetTag/ZDO sync also write those fields.
- [Http] HttpListener availability under the game's Mono runtime remains unverified.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The Wonderland shape it copies exists exactly as cited: Plugin.Awake/Update/OnDestroy (Plugin.cs:35, :69-80), WorldReadyHook postfix on ZNetScene.Awake (:151-159), SubsystemRegistry.InitializeAll/OnUpdate/SafePatch (:24, :63, :99), IWonderlandSubsystem (:7), Heartbeat.OnUpdate ticked from Update (Heartbeat.cs:21), WonderlandConfig.Bind/BindSynced (:150, :406+), BuffRosterEngine's ObjectDB retry (:83-96), DiscordWebhook.SendBlocking (DiscordWebhook.cs:42). ZNet.WorldSaveStarted is a public static Action (:78989) invoked at the top of SaveWorld on the main thread (:80524) — a valid export trigger. Terminal.InitTerminal is `private static void` (:43297), patchable by name, and Console exists on the dedicated server (ZNet.InternalCommand calls Console.instance.TryRunCommand, :81894). The design is internally sound. Two surfaces are over-promised for a zero-client deployment: the console command engine and the [Http] block.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The Wonderland shape it copies is real and the citations resolve (Plugin.cs Awake :35, Update :71-76, OnDestroy :78-82, WorldReadyHook postfix on ZNetScene.Awake :151-159; SubsystemRegistry.InitializeAll :24, OnUpdate :63, SafePatch :99; Heartbeat.OnUpdate :21; WonderlandConfig.Bind :150, BindSynced :406; BuffRosterEngine ObjectDB retry :83-96; csproj net472 + publicizer). `ZNet.WorldSaveStarted` is a public static Action (:78989) invoked synchronously at the top of SaveWorld (:80524) before the portal clone (:77621-77630) — a valid export hook. The architecture is sound as an intra-mod convention. The material error is the CommandEngine: on a zero-client dedicated server `tplite.*` ConsoleCommands have no caller. A vanilla client's `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:45733-45757) resolves against the CLIENT's own `commands` dictionary and prints 'not a recognized command' for unknown names, and only forwards names it already holds with RemoteCommand=true via `ZNet.RemoteCommand` → `RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81869-81888, admin-gated). The server assembly has no stdin reader (no System.Console/ReadLine/StandardInput references), and BepInEx provides none. So the console registration is dead surface unless another mod or the mod's own file-queue/HTTP dispatcher calls `Console.instance.TryRunCommand` — which exists on the dedicated server because vanilla's own RPC_RemoteCommand depends on it (:81896-81900). Never call `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand` from the server: its IsServer branch calls `InternalCommand(null, …)`, which dereferences `rpc.GetSocket()` (:81869-81901) → NullReferenceException. `Terminal.InitTerminal` is `private static` (:43297) invoked from `Terminal.Awake` (:45762-45765) — a postfix works but runs at the first Terminal Awake, before ZNet; `ConsoleCommand.IsValid` (:43203-43217) evaluates OnlyServer/ZNet at run time, so early registration is fine. The 'only writer' ownership rule is intra-mod only: vanilla `Game.ConnectPortals` (:100589) and `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653) also write the Portal connection and any client's RPC_SetTag/ZDO sync writes s_tag. `[Http]` under Mono was not verified here (no game-side evidence either way). The player-facing toast is a ShowMessage routed RPC — client-honoured display, not enforcement. ConfigSync registration is, as the option says, inert for zero-client.

### 85. RULED OUT — vanilla PortalsUsed / PortalDungeonIn / PortalDungeonOut as server metrics

`ops-admin:RULED OUT — vanilla PortalsUsed / PortalDungeonIn / PortalDungeonOut as server metrics` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **not-enforceable** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portal usage counters exist in vanilla but are written to each player's local character file and never networked to the server in any form.


**How it works:** `TeleportWorld.Teleport` ends with `Game.instance.IncrementPlayerStat(PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed)` (:143548), and `Teleport.Interact` (dungeon doors) increments `PortalDungeonIn`/`PortalDungeonOut` (:143362). `Game.IncrementPlayerStat` delegates to `PlayerProfile.IncrementStat` (:100569-100572), which writes an in-memory `Dictionary<PlayerStatType,float>` inside `PlayerProfile.m_playerStats` (:106287-106300) and feeds `Achievements`. That dictionary is serialised only into that client's own `.fch` via `PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData`/`SavePlayerToDisk` (:105706-105711, :105760+).

There is no path off the client. `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles` (:79653-79670) sounds like a collector and does the opposite: it invokes the `SavePlayerProfile` RPC on each peer, whose handler calls `Game.instance.SavePlayerProfile` on that client (:79672-79675, :100204-100240) — writing that client's own local file and returning nothing.

The only client→server per-player dictionary is `ZNet.m_serverSyncedPlayerData` (:79051), serialised in `SendServerSyncPlayerData` (:80365-80377) and received in `RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData` (:80395-80410) — and vanilla populates it with exactly three unrelated keys (`platformDisplayName`, `baseValue`, `possibleEvents`, written at :79212, :11400, :11095). A server-only mod cannot add a key to it because that would require client code.

Also note the counters would be wrong even if readable: the stat is incremented on `TeleportTo`'s *acceptance*, before `UpdateTeleport` moves anything, so a teleport that later fails and restores position (`Player.UpdateTeleport` :15359-15376) still counted.


**Player experience:** A player's own in-game stats screen shows their true portal count. The server, and therefore any leaderboard, Discord report or admin query, can never see that number. An operator asking 'who uses portals most' gets the heuristic answer or none.


**Failure modes:**
- Building a leaderboard on a number that is silently always zero server-side.
- Assuming `SaveOtherPlayerProfiles` gathers data.

**Designer citations:** TeleportWorld.Teleport IncrementPlayerStat — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143548 ; Teleport.Interact dungeon stats — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143362 ; PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed / PortalDungeonIn / PortalDungeonOut — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:106516, :106584, :106585 ; Game.IncrementPlayerStat — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100569-100572 ; PlayerProfile.IncrementStat — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:106287-106300 ; PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:105706-105711 ; ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles / RPC_SavePlayerProfile — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79653-79670, :79672-79675 ; ZNet.m_serverSyncedPlayerData / RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79051, :80395-80410 ; Player.UpdateTeleport failure restore — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15359-15376

TeleportWorld.Teleport (:143546-143548) calls player.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport: true) and IGNORES its bool return, so PortalsUsed increments even when Player.TeleportTo (:15302-15326) returned false — already teleporting, or m_teleportCooldown < 2f. The restore-to-origin branch with $msg_portal_blocked in Player.UpdateTeleport (:15369-15374) is the `!m_distantTeleport` path, i.e. dungeon Teleport doors (distantTeleport:false, :143360); a portal transit (distant) never restores — after 15 s it drops the player at GetSolidHeight of the target (:15361-15366). Dungeon counters, by contrast, are only incremented when TeleportTo returned true (:143360-143362).
- Minor: cite Player.UpdateTeleport as :15328-15380 (whole method) rather than :15359-15376 if the point is 'a rejected/failed teleport still counts'.

Only the dungeon Teleport.Interact gates on the return value (:143360-143362).

Only the dungeon `Teleport.Interact` gates on the return (:143360). So the client-local number over-counts more than stated.
