### 86. RULED OUT — a vanilla per-portal 'last changed' timestamp, and offline link reconstruction by ZDOID

`ops-admin:RULED OUT — a vanilla per-portal 'last changed' timestamp, and offline link reconstruction by ZDOID` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **not-enforceable** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed


No ZDO carries a wall clock, and the on-disk connection is a random int hash pair rather than a ZDOID — so both 'when did this change' and 'read the links out of the world file' must be mod-maintained.


**How it works:** **No timestamp.** `ZDO`'s complete field set is `m_uid`, `m_rotation`, `m_position`, `m_tempSortValue`, `m_prefab`, `m_dataFlags`, `m_tempRemoveEarmark` (:73309-73321), plus the revision counters. `DataRevision`/`OwnerRevision` are monotonic `uint`s with no time base, and `IncreaseDataRevision` (:73832-73840) bumps them for *any* field change, so they cannot even distinguish a tag edit from a position sync. The only clock anywhere near a ZDO is `ZDOMan.m_deadZDOs[uid] = ZNet.instance.GetTime().Ticks` in `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76993-76998) — a destruction time, for destroyed ZDOs only, in a private dictionary. Conclusion: `lastChanged` must be stamped by the mod's own census diff and persisted alongside the network file, and is therefore blind to anything that happened while the mod was not running.

**No ZDOID on disk.** `ZDO.Save` writes `(byte)connectionData.m_type` plus `connectionData.m_hash` (:74315-74317) — an int generated by `ZDOExtraData.GetUniqueHash` seeded from the session id (:75440-75459) — not the target ZDOID. `RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461-75478) gives the source side `ConnectionType.Portal` (1) and the target side `Portal|Target` (0x11) with the same hash, and `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (:77850-77893) re-pairs by matching those hashes at load. So offline tooling reading a `.chunk` file cannot resolve a portal's destination by id; it must replicate the hash-matching pass. Worse, `ZDO.Load` renumbers every `m_uid` (:74552), so the ids in the file bear no relation to the ids in the previous session.

**Implication for ops:** the durable identity for any portal record is its rounded world position, and the durable representation of a link for export/backup purposes is a *pair of positions*, never a pair of ZDOIDs.


**Player experience:** Nothing player-facing. The operator sees `changed ~4h ago (observed)` rather than an authoritative timestamp, and `tplite.export` emits position pairs rather than id pairs, with a note that ids are session-scoped.


**Failure modes:**
- Exporting ZDOID-keyed links and building external tooling on them.
- Using `DataRevision` as a change clock — it advances for position syncs too, so on a portal a player is standing next to it can advance constantly.
- Writing an offline world-file reader that expects ZDOIDs in the connection field.

**Designer citations:** ZDO field set — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73309-73321 ; ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73832-73840 ; ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO m_deadZDOs timestamp — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76993-76998 ; ZDO.Save connection hash — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74315-74317 ; ZDOExtraData.GetUniqueHash — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75440-75459 ; ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75461-75478 ; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (hash matching) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77850-77893 ; ZDO.Load ZDOID renumber — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74552


**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed] Read every cited site. ZDO's instance fields are exactly m_uid, m_rotation, m_position, m_tempSortValue, m_prefab, m_dataFlags, m_tempRemoveEarmark (:73309-73321) plus the OwnerRevision/DataRevision properties — no clock. IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) is a bare DataRevision++ plus ClientChanged/SetDirtySector, invoked from 15 setters including InternalSetPosition (owner only), so it is a 'something changed' counter, not a field-level or time-based one. The only timestamp is the private m_deadZDOs[uid] = ZNet.instance.GetTime().Ticks in HandleDestroyedZDO, server-only branch (:76993-76998). ZDO.Save writes (byte)m_type + m_hash for the single connection slot (:74315-74317); GetUniqueHash is seeded from ZDOMan.GetSessionID().GetHashCode() + a counter (:75440-75454); RegenerateConnectionHashData assigns the source ConnectionType.Portal and the target Portal|Target with the same hash (:75461-75478); ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (private, :77850-77893) re-pairs by hash equality and force-owns both sides; ZDO.Load renumbers m_uid via ++ZDOID.m_loadID (:74552). All claims hold; the implication that durable identity must be position-based is correct.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed] Every claim verified against the source. ZDO instance fields are exactly `m_uid, m_rotation, m_position, m_tempSortValue, m_prefab, m_dataFlags, m_tempRemoveEarmark` (:73309-73321) plus revision counters; `IncreaseDataRevision` just does `DataRevision++`, notifies ClientChanged on clients, and `SetDirtySector` (:73832-73840) — no time and no field discrimination. The only clock near a ZDO is `m_deadZDOs[uid] = ZNet.instance.GetTime().Ticks` in `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76995-76999), server-only, for destroyed ZDOs; and `ZNet.GetTime()` (:81535-81539) is derived from `m_netTime` (game net time), not wall clock — so even that is not a real-world timestamp. On disk `ZDO.Save` writes `(byte)connectionData.m_type` + `connectionData.m_hash` (:74313-74317); `GetUniqueHash` seeds from `ZDOMan.GetSessionID().GetHashCode()` (:75445-75459); `RegenerateConnectionHashData` assigns the same hash to source (type) and target (type|Target) (:75461-75478); `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` re-pairs by hash equality at load (:77850-77893), taking the first match and breaking; `ZDO.Load` renumbers with `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)` (:74552-74555; SetID :75877-75881 also resets UserKey). Attack from the save boundary strengthens rather than weakens it: because the file holds one hash slot per ZDO and pairing is first-match, any non-pairwise topology collapses on reload, so a position-pair export is the only durable representation. Minor nuance, not a correction: ZDO extra-data string/long keys could in principle hold a mod-written net-time stamp, but vanilla writes none on TeleportWorld (its RPC_SetTag writes only s_tag/s_tagauthor :143594-143598), and any such key is invisible to offline tooling anyway. Position-as-identity is sound for portals (static pieces, position written once at placement).

### 87. RULED OUT — the vanilla noportals command, and any in-game admin GUI

`ops-admin:RULED OUT — the vanilla noportals command, and any in-game admin GUI` · domain **ops** · source `ops-admin`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **not-enforceable** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The stock noportals command is inert on a dedicated server and cannot even be fired remotely; and any panel, list or picker rendered in-game is inherently client work.


**How it works:** **`noportals`.** Its entire body is wrapped in `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null)` (:45284-45298), which is never true on a dedicated server — `Player.m_localPlayer` is populated only by `Player.SetLocalPlayer` (:10110) and no Player GameObject is ever instantiated, because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f,0f,1000000f))` every physics tick (:100465) and `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` only builds objects around that reference position (:82268-82276). It is also registered `remoteCommand:false` (:45298), so an admin cannot fire it from a client console either. Note the correction to the existing spec: the neighbouring `nomap` command is **equally** dead — its `IsServer()` branch is nested *inside* the same `Player.m_localPlayer != null` guard (:45261-45283), not an alternative to it. Use `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey("noportals")` (:115943) or the `setkey` console command (`onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true`, :43510-43534).

**In-game GUI.** Every rendering surface is client-side: `Minimap`, `InventoryGui`, `MessageHud`, `TextInput` and IMGUI all require a local player and a graphics device. The server's only channels to a vanilla client are (a) `PlayerNotify.Toast` via the per-character `"Message"` routed RPC (Player.Start registration :10072, RPC_Message :14820-14825), (b) the global `"ShowMessage"` RPC (MessageHud.Start :55808, RPC_ShowMessage :55848-55851), (c) a saved map pin via `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"` (registered for every peer, Game.Start :100068; handler :100823-100829), (d) floating world text via `"RPC_DamageText"` (DamageText.Awake :46352-46356), (e) a one-shot VFX/SFX via `"SpawnObject"` (ZNetScene.Awake :81954; RPC_SpawnObject :82355-82366), and (f) the portal's own hover text through `s_tag`. None of those is a panel, a list, or a picker.

The admin's interface is therefore the F5 console, the config files, the export files, the HTTP endpoint and Discord — not anything drawn in the game world.


**Player experience:** An operator who expects to open an admin panel in-game does not get one. What they get instead: press F5, type `tplite.list TRADE`, read the reply in the console. A player who expects a gate directory in-game gets, at most, a server-pushed map pin per gate and the tag on the gate's hover text — never a browsable list. This is precisely the gap full client-side TortalPortal exists to fill.


**Failure modes:**
- Planning an admin UX around an in-game panel and discovering at implementation time that no rendering surface exists.
- Using the vanilla `noportals` command in operator documentation and having it silently do nothing.
- Citing `nomap` as the correct counter-example — it is equally dead.

Log all five at OnWorldReady.

The 'RemotePrint' ZRpc is registered on every peer at :79912. This makes a server-pushed TEXT list feasible; only panels/pickers are ruled out.

The 'cannot be fired remotely' statement is true only of the `noportals` command itself, not of the NoPortals key.

A mod-defined command is only reachable from the dedicated server's own stdin console, or by smuggling it behind a vanilla `remoteCommand:true, onlyServer:true` token (e.g. `setkey tplite.list TRADE`) and intercepting it in a Harmony prefix on `ZNet.InternalCommand` (:81891) BEFORE `TryRunCommand` — otherwise unpatched `setkey` would write the junk string as a global key (:43520).

The vanilla command is the reason 'Global-Key RPC Hardening' is needed.

- Add the one viable in-console admin path: carrier commands. A prefix on Terminal.TryRunCommand (server) can intercept e.g. 'setkey tplite list TRADE' and answer with ZNet.RemotePrint(rpc, …) (:81635) which lands in the admin's console (:81650). This is admin-authenticated, unlike the key RPCs.

### 88. The Routing Kernel

`economy-progression:The Routing Kernel` · domain **economy** · source `economy-progression`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Take ownership of portal pairing from vanilla so that "which routes exist right now" becomes a pure server decision, and the tag string is freed up as a display channel.


**How it works:** Everything else in this domain is a child of this option. Vanilla's authority lives in `Game.ConnectPortals()` (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589), driven by `Game.ConnectPortalsCoroutine` (:100580) which `Game.Start` launches only under `if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` (:100074) and which fires immediately then every 5.0s forever. Its two passes are: (1) teardown — for each portal in `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (:77648), clear the connection if the partner ZDO is missing, the partner's `ZDOVars.s_tag` string differs, or the partner's own connection is `ZDOID.None` (:100600-100604); (2) pairing — for each still-unconnected portal, pick a uniformly random same-tag unconnected partner via `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (:100664, `UnityEngine.Random.Range` at :100678) and write both directions through `Game.SetConnection` (:100637).

Three escalating levels of takeover:

**L1 — selection override.** Harmony postfix on the private `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(List<ZDO>, ZDO skip, string tag)`, overwriting `__result` with your own choice (nearest, oldest, admin-designated, or `null` to refuse). Lowest risk: vanilla keeps teardown, ownership handling, the two-phase commit through `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` / `Game.ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals` (:100690), and its own `ZLog` audit lines (:100619).

**L2 — full replacement.** Harmony prefix on `Game.ConnectPortals` returning `false`, then run your own topology pass in the same frame. You must reproduce the `IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal` guard (:100609/:100671) or you will double-pair portals owned by online players, whose connection writes are deferred over `RPC_SetConnection` (:100649) and therefore still read `None` in the server's own copy that tick.

**L3 — coroutine stop.** `Game.instance.StopCoroutine("ConnectPortalsCoroutine")` (started by the string overload at :100074, so the string form is valid) and drive your own timer.

Write primitive, copied verbatim from `Game.SetConnection` (:100643-100645): `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.Portal, targetId); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);`. `ZDO.SetConnection` (:73656) is idempotent — `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` (:74954-74957) returns false on an unchanged type+target, so no DataRevision bump and no packet. Re-asserting the whole topology every tick is therefore free. It also calls `ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals()` for you, which is what actually gets the portal chunk written at save (`ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk` :77621).

The decisive consequence: once you own pairing, `ZDOVars.s_tag` (:78617) stops being the routing key and becomes a free 80-column display string on every vanilla client's hover text (`TeleportWorld.GetHoverText` :143453). That is what makes "MINE 43/50c" or "LEASED til d.412" possible at all.


**Player experience:** Invisible when idle: gates pair the way they always did, except deterministically (the nearest same-tag partner rather than a coin flip), so the third portal on a shared tag stops being randomly orphaned. What players notice is that the tag text starts carrying information the game never put there — walking up to a gate reads `Teleport tag:"MINE 43/50c" [Connected]` instead of `tag:"mine"`. Renaming still works: the player presses E, the 10-character vanilla text box opens pre-filled, and whatever they type becomes their *label*; the server re-decorates it on the next tick and the route they belong to is unchanged, because routing is now a server-side table keyed on position, not on the string.


**Failure modes:**
- L2/L3 inherit a latent vanilla bug: `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` caches raw `ZDO` object references for a full 5s, and `ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76990) releases destroyed ZDOs back to `ZDOPool`, whose `ZDO.Reset()` (:73536) sets `m_uid = ZDOID.None`. Never cache `ZDO` objects across ticks — cache `ZDOID` and re-resolve with `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(id)`.
- `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) runs every 2s per peer and reassigns portal ownership to any player within ~96-112m (`ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea` :82297). Your `SetOwner` claim evaporates; the connection VALUE survives because it was already `ForceSendZDO`'d, but the next write must re-claim. Guard with the `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix pattern from Wonderland `Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301` if you need a persistent claim.
- Non-pairwise topologies (rings, one-way, self-loops) survive at runtime but are mangled at save: `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461-75478) gives each ZDO exactly one hash slot, so a 3-ring loses a link and a self-loop is erased. The kernel must re-assert its whole topology in an `OnWorldReady` pass after every load.
- If another mod also patches `Game.ConnectPortals`, an L2 prefix returning false silently disables theirs. Use `SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch` (Wonderland `Core/SubsystemRegistry.cs:99`) and log loudly.
- Two classes are named `ConnectPortals`. `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (:77850) is private, runs only at world load, and matches save-file hashes with no tag involvement. Patching it achieves nothing at runtime.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- 'Tag becomes a free display string' holds only at L2/L3. At L1 vanilla pass 1 still runs and nulls any link whose two ends carry different s_tag strings (`zDO.GetString(s_tag) != @string`, :100601). Decorated text must be byte-identical on both ends of every route, or the mod must replace ConnectPortals entirely.
- 'Re-asserting the whole topology every tick is free' is false for the primitive as quoted. ZDO.SetOwner bumps OwnerRevision whenever the current owner differs (SetOwner body, ZDOExtraData.GetOwner != uid), and ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands every portal in a player's active area back to that player every 2 s (:76870-76884, :76901-76926), so an unconditional SetOwner each tick flaps ownership, emits a packet per portal per tick, and — because the server owning a portal makes HandleRoutedRPC drop RPC_SetTag (:83656) — silently breaks vanilla renaming for everyone near a portal. Guard like vanilla's ForceSetConnection (:100630-100636): compare GetConnectionZDOID first and only claim ownership when a write is actually needed.
- Renaming tears the route: the owning vanilla client's RPC_SetTag calls UpdateConnection(Portal, None) on itself and SetConnectedPortal on the old partner (:143594-143597, :143604-143618) before writing the new tag, so every rename produces an [Unconnected] flicker until the kernel re-asserts on its next tick. The RPC_SetConnected path to the partner's owner (:143615) also fires on the wire.
- TextInput prefill is capped: RequestText sets characterLimit = 10 before assigning the current tag (:61509-61522), so a decorated tag longer than 10 characters pre-fills truncated and pressing Enter submits the truncated string. Label parsing must treat 'first 10 chars of the decorated tag' as no-change.
- Restart: ZDOMan.ConnectPortals relinks purely from saved hash data (:77850-77890) and Game.ConnectPortals is invoked inside LoadChunks (:76524) — both before any per-tick kernel pass. Because RegenerateConnectionHashData persists only one slot per ZDO (:75461-75477), any non-pairwise topology (fan-in, ring, one-way) comes back as a pairwise matching or not at all; the kernel must persist its own table (keyed on position, not ZDOID — ZDOIDs are regenerated at load) and re-assert after ZNet finishes loading.
- Modded clients: a client that owns a portal can write any connection via its ZDOData (Deserialize -> ZDOExtraData.SetConnection, :74224-74232; accepted at :77107-77118 when DataRevision is higher); the kernel re-asserts within one tick. Enforcement is over the route field, not over the traveller — movement remains client-authoritative.
- L1 does NOT free the tag: Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 (:100601) clears any link whose partner tag differs, so the tag is still the routing key at L1. Tag-as-display requires L2 or L3 (or identical decoration on both ends of every pair).
- Write primitive must be gated on GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != target (vanilla ForceSetConnection :100628-100634). Unconditional per-tick SetOwner (ZDO.SetOwner bumps OwnerRevision on any owner change) fights ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) every 2s and emits a packet per portal per tick; only ZDO.SetConnection is idempotent.
- After any client-side drift, force a DataRevision bump: server and client writes at the same revision are mutually rejected (ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77108-77118 and client twin), and ShouldSend does not re-send an unchanged revision.
- Renaming: the owning vanilla client's RPC_SetTag nulls both ends (:143587-143629); the kernel must capture the player's raw text from the incoming ZDO update before re-decorating, and the route is down for up to one kernel tick.
- L2 prefix also blocks the load-time Game.instance.ConnectPortals() call in ZDOMan.LoadChunks (:76523); run the kernel pass there too. ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77891) restores only a pairwise matching from saved hash data and ZDOIDs regenerate per load, so the position-keyed table must be re-applied after LoadChunks.
- TextInput charLimit is 10 (:61515-61522; RequestText :143486) - decorated tags longer than 10 chars are truncated in the rename prefill.

### 89. Park and Release

`economy-progression:Park and Release` · domain **economy** · source `economy-progression`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The atomic enforcement primitive: hold a named route closed until a condition is met, and open it the instant it is — three techniques with different visibility, cost and failure characteristics.


**How it works:** A parked portal has `GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) == ZDOID.None`. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` then returns at its very first gate — `if (!TargetFound()) return;` (:143519) — with no message, no effect and no way for a modified client to route around it, because the destination simply is not in the ZDO the client holds. This is the only one of `Teleport`'s four gates that is genuinely server-ENFORCED rather than client-honoured (the other three read global keys or the local inventory, :143523/:143528/:143533).

Naively writing `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` loses: vanilla's pass 1 and pass 2 run in the *same* `Game.ConnectPortals()` call (:100594 then :100607), so a nulled portal is re-paired ≤5s later, often within the same frame. Three ways to actually hold it:

**A — Tag mutation (no Harmony).** Rewrite `ZDOVars.s_tag` (:78617) to a value no other portal shares, e.g. `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, label + " #" + token)`. Pass 1 clears the existing link on tag mismatch (:100601); `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (:100669) finds no same-tag candidate and returns null forever. Follow with `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702) — a tag-only write does NOT set `DirtyPortalObjects` (only `ZDO.SetConnection` :73661, `AddIfPortal` :77750 and `HandleDestroyedZDO` :76986 do) so it is silently lost at the next world save. Cheapest, zero patches, but the tag is the routing key AND the display, so parking mangles the label.

**B — Pairing veto (recommended).** Postfix `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` and return `null` when `skip` is in your parked set; separately force `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` on parked portals each tick (idempotent, so free after the first write). Tag stays pristine and available for status text. Requires the Routing Kernel at L1.

**C — Decoy sink.** See the Customs House option.

Release is the inverse: drop the park flag, restore the tag (A) or clear the veto (B), and call `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` directly for instant re-pairing rather than waiting up to 5s.

Timing caveat for both: pass 1's clear is NOT forced (`SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None)` at :100603 with `forceImmediateConnection` defaulting false), so when an online player owns the portal ZDO the clear is deferred over `RPC_SetConnection` to that client and the server's own copy still reads the old value that tick. Re-pairing after a release near a standing player takes 2+ ticks. Write with force semantics yourself (`SetOwner` then `SetConnection` then `ForceSendZDO`) to make park and release single-tick.


**Player experience:** A player walks up to a gate they have used for weeks and the frame reads `[Unconnected]` instead of `[Connected]`, and the runic ring has gone dark (`TeleportWorld.Update` lerps `m_colorAlpha` toward 0 when `m_hadTarget` is false, :143511). Walking into it does absolutely nothing — no message, no shove, no error — which is exactly how vanilla behaves for a portal with no partner, so it reads as a game state rather than a mod refusal. Because that silence is confusing, pair every park with a reason in the tag (`"BRIDGE closed"`, `"MINE 43/50c"`) and a one-line toast to anyone standing within 20m at the moment of parking, via `PlayerNotify.Toast` (Wonderland `Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs:15`). The release is dramatic in a good way: the ring lights, `m_connected` EffectList fires on the 0.5s `UpdatePortal` poll (:143496), and the player can step through on the next stride.


**Failure modes:**
- First transit after a release to a distant partner silently fails: `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` (:143640) requires the client to actually HOLD the destination ZDO, and calls `ZDOMan.instance.RequestZDO` and returns false when it does not. The player walks through, nothing happens, they walk through again and it works. Mitigate by `ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerUid, destinationId)` (:77714) to every peer within 40m of the released gate at the moment of release.
- Technique A mangles the label, and `TeleportWorld.Interact` opens the vanilla text box capped at 10 characters (`TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` :143482, cap applied at `TextInput.Show` :61519) pre-filled with the current tag — a player who opens and confirms the dialog on a long server-written tag may save back a truncated version, permanently corrupting your routing key.
- A parked portal whose tag still matches another parked portal will pair them to each other under technique A if your token is not unique. Derive the token from the ZDO position, not a counter.
- `Game.RPC_SetConnection` (:100653) is a global routed RPC registered on every peer with NO sender check and NO ownership check. A malicious client can rewire any portal to any ZDOID at will, undoing a park in one packet. Harden with a prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632) dropping that method hash from non-server senders — that hook has the authentic `ZRpc` socket in scope and nothing downstream does.
- Parking a gate a player is currently standing inside does not eject them, and `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` fires on ENTER only (:143672) — they must step out and back in after a release.

- Confirm a parked portal's dark/unconnected state actually propagates to a client standing next to it without a zone reload, and stays dark for 60s (i.e. the owning client does not clobber the write). Check with a player parked at the gate while the server nulls the connection every 2s.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Technique B's postfix must veto `__result` as well as `skip`. FindRandomUnconnectedPortal's candidate filter (:100667-100673) excludes only skip, tag-mismatch, already-connected and staged portals, so when another same-tag unconnected portal is the `skip`, the parked portal is a legal candidate and pass 2 writes SetConnection on BOTH (:100614-100615). The mod's per-tick null on the parked side then leaves the partner holding a live one-way door into the parked location (partner's TargetFound is true, :143640-143655) until pass 1 clears it up to 5 s later (:100601-100604). Return null when either `skip` or `__result` is parked, or prefix-filter the candidate list.
- 'No way for a modified client to route around it' is false: Player.TeleportTo is entirely client-local (:15302-15327) and a modded client can teleport to any coordinate without a connection, or write a connection into its own ZDO copy if it owns the portal (ReleaseNearbyZDOS grants ownership to nearby peers every 2 s, :76901-76926). Parking is server-enforced against VANILLA clients only.
- Technique A side effect: pass 1 also nulls the former partner (its target's tag now differs), and the partner is immediately re-paired with any other same-tag unconnected portal in the same call (:100607-100621) — parking one gate of a three-gate tag reshuffles the other two.
- SetDirtyPortals: when the parked portal was connected, pass 1's SetConnection(None) already dirties the portal chunk (:73661-73664); the silent loss occurs only for tag writes on an already-unconnected portal. Still call it unconditionally.
- The recommended force primitive (SetOwner -> SetConnection -> ForceSendZDO) claims server ownership; until ReleaseNearbyZDOS returns it (≤2 s), vanilla RPC_SetTag on that portal is dropped at HandleRoutedRPC (:83645-83663). Guard with a compare-before-write so ownership is claimed only when the value actually changes.
- Release via Game.instance.ConnectPortals() (public, :100589) is valid; note it also runs ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) early, which is harmless, but with an online owner the fresh pairing writes are still deferred over RPC_SetConnection and finalized by ForceSetConnection on the next call — so 'instant' re-pairing near a standing player needs the force primitive, as the option already says.
- Player-experience timing: m_hadTarget is refreshed by UpdatePortal every 0.5 s (:143496-143507) and m_colorAlpha lerps at 1/s (:143511-143513), so the ring takes ~0.5-1.5 s to go dark after the park lands on the client.
- Technique A is trivially undone by a vanilla rename (RPC_SetTag :143587-143602 -> RPC_ZDOData -> pass 2 re-pair within 5s); it only holds when re-asserted every tick, and even then the mangled tag is visible for a tick.
- State the modified-client boundary: a client can write any Portal connection into its own ZDO copy (ZDO.Deserialize :74219-74233 accepts any target) and TargetFound (:143640-143654) checks only the local copy. The park is fully enforced for vanilla clients and enforced with a one-tick window for modified clients, provided the server forces a DataRevision bump on drift (revision tie is mutually rejected, ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77108-77118).
- Gate the forced null on GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != None before SetOwner (vanilla ForceSetConnection :100628-100634); unconditional per-tick SetOwner bumps OwnerRevision and ping-pongs with ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926).
- Key the parked set by portal position, not ZDOID (ZDOIDs are regenerated at world load; ZDOMan.Load :76532-76537 sets a new session ID).
- Line ref: m_connected.Create is :143499 inside UpdatePortal (:143491-143507); Teleport gate 1 is :143519-143521.

Corrections: (1) Technique A is defeated by a vanilla E-press: the owning client's RPC_SetTag rewrites s_tag to the player's text, the update lands on the server via RPC_ZDOData, and pass 2 re-pairs on the next 5s tick - A holds only if re-asserted every tick and is visibly mangled. (2) Modified clients: the park is enforced against vanilla clients, but a modified client can write a Portal connection into its own copy (Deserialize path :74219-74233 accepts any target) and pass TargetFound immediately; the server's re-null lands only on its next write AND only if its DataRevision exceeds the client's (tie is mutually rejected, :77108-77118) - so parking is server-enforced with a one-tick window against modified clients and needs a forced revision bump on observed drift. (3) The forced write primitive (SetOwner each tick) fights ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926); gate it on GetConnectionZDOID != None as vanilla's ForceSetConnection does (:100628-100634). (4) Parked-set keying: ZDOIDs regenerate per world load, key the parked set by position. (5) 'Toast to anyone within 20m' via PlayerNotify.Toast (Wonderland PlayerNotify.cs:15-30) is a routed 'Message' RPC to the player's own ZDO - exists as cited.

### 90. The Customs House

`economy-progression:The Customs House` · domain **economy** · source `economy-progression`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Instead of disconnecting a gate, route it to a server-fabricated dead-end anchor — the portal reads Connected and glows, but walking through drops you in a holding area two metres away or at a toll booth.


**How it works:** `TeleportWorld.Teleport` performs NO prefab validation on its destination — it resolves `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(GetConnectionZDOID(Portal))` and reads only `GetPosition()` and `GetRotation()` off it (:143539-143543), then computes `pos + (rot * Vector3.forward) * m_exitDistance + Vector3.up` and calls `player.TeleportTo(..., distantTeleport: true)`. Any ZDO with a position is therefore a legal destination.

Fabricate the anchor: `var z = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(anchorPos, anchorPrefabHash); z.Persistent = true; z.SetPrefab(anchorPrefabHash); z.Distant = false; z.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; z.SetRotation(rot);` — `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` (:76674) sets neither prefab nor persistence; those five lines mirror `ZNetView.Awake` (:82613-82620) and omitting them yields a ZDO that vanishes at world save.

Two anchor flavours:

**Portal-prefab anchor.** Pass a hash from `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021). `ZDOMan.AddIfPortal` (:77732) files it in `m_portalObjects`, so it is always resident, saved wholesale in the `ChunkPortal` file (:77621), and `ForceSendZDO`-able. But it now participates in vanilla pairing, so give it the sink's tag and manage it through the Routing Kernel.

**Non-portal anchor.** Any other persistent prefab hash. Vanilla's pairer never iterates it (it only walks `GetPortalList()`), so it is invisible to teardown — but `Game.ConnectPortals` pass 1 inspects the *partner*, so the anchor MUST carry the same `s_tag` string as the gate and a non-`None` Portal connection back, or the gate's link is torn down within 5s (:100601).

Sink geometry decides the experience. Set the anchor 2m in front of the gate facing back at it and a transit is a ~10s black screen that returns you where you started — an honest "you may not pass" with vanilla's own visual grammar. Set it inside a built customs hall with a payment chest and an exit gate and the closed route becomes a place. Note `Player.UpdateTeleport` (:15337-15352) pins the player at the frozen target for ≥8s under `distantTeleport: true` regardless of distance, so even a 2m hop costs the full loading screen.

Persistence: `ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData` (:75461) persists a connection only when BOTH endpoints resolve in `m_objectsByID`, and `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` (:77850) relinks by hash at load and writes BOTH directions — so a gate↔anchor pair survives a restart, but a deliberately one-way gate→anchor link comes back two-way.


**Player experience:** The gate looks perfectly healthy — ring lit, hover text `[Connected]`, tag reads `"CUSTOMS"`. You walk in, the screen goes black with the familiar teleport swirl, eight seconds pass, and you are standing in a small stone room with a chest labelled by a sign, a second portal on the far wall, and no way back except the gate you came from. Drop 50 coins in the chest, walk to the far gate, and it is lit; walk to it without paying and it is dark. The mod never told you "no" — it moved the refusal into level design. The cheap variant is more brutal and also fine: you walk in, black screen, and you are standing two metres from where you started facing the gate. Repeat it and you learn.


**Failure modes:**
- A vanilla client near an anchor with a prefab hash it cannot instantiate logs `Missing prefab hash:` from `ZNetScene.CreateObject` (:82003) and does nothing further — harmless, but the SERVER's own `CreateObjectsSorted` would destroy such a ZDO (:82137). In practice the server never sees it because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins the reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) (:100465), but a mod that ever moves that reference position would silently delete every anchor.
- `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal-prefab ZDOs (:73752), so a portal-flavoured anchor stays filed under its creation sector in `m_portalObjects` forever. Never reposition an anchor — destroy it (claim ownership first: `ZDOMan.DestroyZDO` is gated on `zdo.IsOwner()` at :76929) and create a new one.
- The 8s `distantTeleport` floor makes a 2m bounce feel like a bug to a first-time player. Pair it with a `PlayerNotify.Toast` fired on arrival so the black screen resolves into an explanation.
- `ZDOMan.m_deadZDOs` (:76043) makes the server destroy any ZDO re-created under a previously-destroyed ZDOID (`RPC_ZDOData` :77133). Always mint a fresh id via `CreateNewZDO`.
- Anchors accumulate. Every parked gate that uses a sink adds a persistent ZDO; without a reaper keyed on "no portal points at me" they leak into the save forever.

**Designer citations:** TeleportWorld.Teleport (destination read, no prefab check) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143539 ; ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76674 ; ZNetView.Awake (the five mandatory follow-up lines) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82613 ; ZDOMan.AddIfPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77732 ; Game.ConnectPortals (partner tag/connection test) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100601 ; Player.UpdateTeleport (2s/8s/15s gates) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15329 ; ZNetScene.CreateObject (missing prefab) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81995 ; ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted (server destroys invalid-prefab ZDOs) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82137 ; ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75461 ; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (load-time relink, writes both directions) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77850 ; ZDO.SetSector (portal exemption) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73752 ; ZDOMan.DestroyZDO (owner-gated) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76929


**Open questions:**
- Does a vanilla client cleanly handle a portal connected to a ZDO carrying a harmless real prefab (a marker piece) versus an unregistered hash? Check: build both, stand near each with a vanilla client, and watch the client log for CreateObject failures and whether `TargetFound` returns true.
- What is the portal prefab's ZNetView `m_persistent` / `m_type` / `m_distant`? A portal-flavoured anchor should match exactly or the first owning client rewrites Type/Distant in `ZNetView.Awake` (:82632-82640). Check on a client: `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab("portal_wood").GetComponent<ZNetView>()`.
- Does a two-metre `distantTeleport` actually complete at the 8s mark, or does `ZNetScene.IsAreaReady` (:82064) pass instantly and the 8s timer dominate? Measure the black screen length in game.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- The cited server-side 'destroys invalid-prefab ZDOs' path (CreateObjectsSorted :82137-82148, CreateDistantObjects) only runs for ZDOs the server's CreateDestroyObjects visits — the Sector-0 bucket around the pinned reference position (:82268-82276, SectorToIndex clamp :115763-115768). An anchor at a real coordinate is never visited, so a bogus prefab hash is NOT cleaned up server-side; instead every vanilla client whose active area contains it calls CreateObject at 30 Hz and logs 'Missing prefab hash' each time (:81996-82006; the client branch has no destroy). The anchor MUST be a real prefab hash.
- A real-prefab anchor is instantiated as a GameObject on nearby vanilla clients (it sits in m_objectsBySector, not the portal list) and, being Persistent, is handed to the nearest player by ReleaseNearbyZDOS every 2 s (:76901-76926). That client's components then run against it — WearNTear can be damaged/deconstructed, ItemDrop despawns, Piece can be hammer-removed — and the client's own ZNetScene.Destroy -> DestroyZDO (:82023-82036) or RPC_DestroyZDO (no sender check) erases it, tearing down the route within 5 s. Choose an inert, invisible, non-interactable prefab, and have the vault re-create it on I1 failure. IsAreaReady (:82062-82078) additionally requires the anchor instantiated on the arriving client before the black screen ends.
- Per-player gating is not available: the exit gate's park/release state is a single server-owned field, so once any player pays, the exit gate is open for everyone in the hall until re-parked. The 'walk to it without paying and it is dark' line is only true while nobody else has paid recently.
- Portal-prefab anchor variant: with a real portal prefab it is rendered as a visible portal on clients and its ownership migrates to nearby players like any portal; with SetPrefab omitted it is unsaveable (m_prefab unset) — the option's warning is correct, and additionally GetPrefab() of an unset ZDO is not the passed hash, so HandleDestroyedZDO's PortalPrefabHash check (:76980) would then fail to remove it from m_portalObjects (leak, see harness V5).
- Dead-end geometry: the traveller lands at anchor + forward*1 + up (:143541-143543) and SetLookDir points them along the anchor's forward (:15340); with the anchor 2 m in front of the gate facing it, the player materialises 1 m from the gate facing it, and stepping forward re-triggers after the 2 s cooldown (:15313). Fine as designed, but describe it as 1 m, not 2 m.
- One-way gate->anchor links do not survive even at runtime (pass 1 nulls a link whose partner's connection is None, :100601-100604) — the restart behaviour is moot; the anchor must always carry the reciprocal Portal connection and identical s_tag.
- ZDO.SetSector portal exemption (:73752-73756) is cited but irrelevant to a non-portal anchor; it matters only for the portal-prefab flavour, where it is the V5 hazard if the anchor is ever moved.
- ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted/CreateDistantObjects (:82137, :82166-82172) only destroy invalid-prefab ZDOs the SERVER tries to instantiate, which is the Sector 0 clamp bucket around the (1e6,0,1e6) pin; an anchor at a normal position is never touched by the server. The vanilla client near the sink DOES instantiate the anchor prefab (CreateObject :81995-82012): it is a visible, interactable object, and an unknown hash logs 'Missing prefab hash' every CreateDestroyObjects pass on the client.
- Portal-prefab anchor participates in pass 2 (AddIfPortal :77732-77752 -> GetPortalList): it must carry a tag no gate uses and be vetoed in FindRandomUnconnectedPortal, or vanilla will pair it with a same-tag gate.
- Customs-hall geometry: the traveller arrives at the anchor, not at the origin gate, so the hall must contain its own exit portal; 'no way back except the gate you came from' is only true for the 2m-sink variant.
- Save persistence requires Persistent=true BEFORE the first Set/SetRotation/SetConnection (IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector :73832-73840 is gated on Persistent); the order given in the option is correct, keep it.
- ZDOIDs regenerate at load; any gate->anchor registry must be re-derived from the saved mutual pair (ZDOMan.ConnectPortals :77850-77891) or from positions, not from stored ZDOIDs.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Verified: TeleportWorld.Teleport reads only GetPosition/GetRotation off whatever ZDO the connection names (:143537-143546) and TargetFound only needs the client to hold that ZDO, requesting it otherwise (:143648-143652); RPC_RequestZDO force-sends any ZDO by id with no filter (:77684-77692, AddForceSendZdos :77263-77285), so a non-portal anchor is reachable. CreateNewZDO(pos, hash) files the ZDO by the passed hash in m_portalObjects but never calls SetPrefab or sets Persistent (:76674-76690); the five follow-up lines mirror ZNetView.Awake (:82613-82620). Pass 1 requires the partner's tag to match and its connection to be non-None (:100601), so the anchor must link back. RegenerateConnectionHashData needs both endpoints (:75468) and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals relinks both directions from hash data (:77850-77890), so a mutual gate<->anchor pair survives restart and a one-way link returns two-way. Player.UpdateTeleport holds the traveller ≥8 s under distantTeleport (:15329-15346) with a 2 s cooldown (:15313). The design works for vanilla clients; the caveats are about what the anchor prefab does on clients and a mis-cited server destroy path.
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Destination read verified: TeleportWorld.Teleport :143540-143548 does ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connection) and reads only GetPosition()/GetRotation(), computes pos + rot*forward*m_exitDistance + up, calls player.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport:true). No prefab check anywhere; TargetFound (:143640-143654) only needs the ZDO to resolve on the client, requesting it via RequestZDO -> RPC_RequestZDO -> peer.ForceSendZDO (:77684-77693) which works for any ZDO regardless of prefab. ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(pos, hash) (:76674-76691) creates via ZDOPool.Create (AddToSector :73496-73504), sets owner, calls AddIfPortal, and sets neither Persistent nor prefab - the five follow-up lines mirror ZNetView.Awake :82611-82618 exactly. Persistence chain: IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector (:73832-73840) only if Persistent, so setting Persistent before SetPrefab/SetRotation/SetConnection is what dirties the chunk; regular chunks save non-portal persistent ZDOs (:77572), portal-prefab anchors go to the portal chunk via AddIfPortal (:77732-77752, :77621-77636). Pass-1 partner test confirmed (:100601): a non-portal anchor must carry the same s_tag and a non-None Portal connection back. Player.UpdateTeleport (:15329-15350) holds distantTeleport for >8s regardless of distance and Player.TeleportTo rejects when m_teleportCooldown < 2f (:15302-15320). Save/load: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75477) writes hash data for both endpoints when both resolve (last-processed entry wins, hashes stay consistent for a mutual pair); ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load (:77850-77891) matches Portal-typed against Portal|Target-typed hash data with no prefab check and writes both directions - a mutual gate<->anchor pair survives, a one-way link comes back two-way, exactly as claimed. Owner-gated DestroyZDO (:76929-76935) as cited. Corrections: (1) ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted/CreateDistantObjects 'server destroys invalid-prefab ZDOs' (:82137, :82166-82172) applies only to ZDOs the server tries to instantiate, i.e. those in the Sector 0 clamp bucket around the (1e6,0,1e6) pin; an anchor at a normal position is never touched by that path, but a vanilla CLIENT near the anchor will instantiate the prefab (CreateObject :81995-82012), so the anchor prefab is a real, visible, interactable object at the sink - pick it deliberately, and an unknown hash spams 'Missing prefab hash' on the client at 30Hz because Created never becomes true. (2) Portal-prefab anchor: AddIfPortal puts it in GetPortalList, so pass 2 will pair it with any other portal sharing its tag unless the kernel vetoes; give it a tag no gate shares and veto it explicitly. (3) 'no way back except the gate you came from' is wrong for the customs-hall geometry - the arrival point is the anchor, not the origin gate; a hall needs its own exit portal or the player is trapped. (4) The 2m-sink 'returns you where you started' places the player 1m in front of the origin gate (anchor pos + 1m forward + up), i.e. the same spot a normal arrival puts them; verify in-game that this does not sit inside the TeleportWorldTrigger collider (vanilla's own 1m exit implies it does not).

### 91. Prepaid Toll Escrow

`economy-progression:Prepaid Toll Escrow` · domain **economy** · source `economy-progression`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium-large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A gate that is connected only while a bound chest holds at least N of an item — the flagship genuinely-enforced economy mechanic, because the check happens before anyone travels, not to anyone travelling.


**How it works:** Bind one Container ZDO to each tolled portal: the nearest ZDO within `BindRadius` (4m default) found with `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(portalPos, 4f, buf)` (Wonderland `Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25`) whose prefab classifies as a container via `ContainerRegistry.IsContainer` (Wonderland `Core/Data/ContainerRegistry.cs:58`). Persist the binding keyed on the rounded portal POSITION, never on a ZDOID — `ZDO.Load` does `m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)` (:74552) so every id is renumbered at world load.

Read the balance: skip if `zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_inUse) == 1` (a player has the UI open — `Container.UpdateUseVisual` :121996), then `ZdoInventoryIO.Load(zdo, w, h)` deserialises `ZDOVars.s_items` into a scratch `Inventory` and you count matching stacks. Cost warning: `Inventory.Load` (:68543) routes through `AddItem(int prefabHash, ...)` (:68726) which does `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(itemPrefab)` + `Destroy` for every stack, resolving through `ObjectDB.instance.GetItemPrefab`. That is real GC churn. Gate every read on a cheap `zdo.DataRevision` change filter — exactly the trick `Container.Load` itself uses (:122305) — and poll at 1 Hz, only for portals in a state where the answer matters.

**The enforcement design is a standing-balance requirement, not a debit.** Each tick: `open = (balance >= price)`. Park on false, release on true. No item is moved, so there is no race with the owning client, no clawback problem, and no way to travel-then-refuse. A player who empties the chest closes their own gate within one tick.

Layer a meter on top if you want consumption: debit `perTransit` on each detected transit (see Reactive Transit Toll) or `perHour` on a timer, via `ZdoInventoryIO.Save` → `zdo.SetOwner(ZNet.GetUID()); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_items, pkg.GetArray())`. The owning client's `Container.CheckForChanges` (`InvokeRepeating("CheckForChanges", 0f, 1f)`, :121920) picks the change up within 1s. Critically, the debit does not need to be reliable: if it races and loses, the standing-balance check on the next tick still closes the gate once the balance actually drops. The system is self-correcting because enforcement and accounting are decoupled.

Status in the tag, refreshed on change only: `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, label + "  " + balance + "/" + price + "c")` plus `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`. Requires the Routing Kernel so the tag is not the routing key.


**Player experience:** Your long-haul mine gate reads `Teleport tag:"MINE 0/50c" [Unconnected]` and its ring is dark. You open the small chest bolted to the frame, drop 50 coins in, close it, and within about a second the hover text flips to `"MINE 50/50c" [Connected]` and the ring lights. You step through. Every trip the counter ticks down — `48/50`, `46/50` — and at `48/50` the gate is still lit because the threshold is 50 for *opening* and the meter only bills for use; when it falls below the reopen threshold the ring goes dark mid-session and you have to walk home the old-fashioned way or top it up from the other end. Two players who share a base share one meter, which makes the chest a social object: somebody has to keep it fed, and whoever raids it for coins turns the lights off for everyone.


**Failure modes:**
- A player holding the chest's UI open sets `s_inUse = 1` and you must skip it entirely; a player who parks the UI open indefinitely freezes the meter. Treat `s_inUse` held for > 5 minutes as stale and read anyway (accepting a clobber risk), or just let the gate hold its last state.
- Conflict resolution is whole-ZDO, not per-field: `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77107-77132) discards an incoming packet only when its DataRevision is not higher, otherwise it replaces the entire blob. A server debit can be reverted wholesale by the owning client's next `Container.Save`. Standing-balance enforcement survives this; a debit-only design does not.
- Reading a 4x4 chest full of distinct stacks instantiates and destroys ~16 GameObjects per read. Ten tolled gates polled at 1 Hz with no revision filter is 160 Instantiate/Destroy pairs a second on the server.
- `ObjectDB.instance` is frequently still null at the `ZNetScene.Awake` postfix commonly treated as world-ready (Wonderland `Subsystems/StatusEffects/BuffRosterEngine.cs:83`). Retry the item-prefab resolution each tick until it succeeds or the first balance read silently returns zero and parks every gate on the server.
- Griefing: an unwarded toll chest is a free coin dispenser AND an off switch. The chest must be inside a ward or the toll is theatre. See Ward Tariff Classes.
- A chest destroyed (`WearNTear`) orphans the binding. Detect with `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(boundId) == null` and fall back to re-discovery by position, then park with a `"NO METER"` tag.

Counting needs no Inventory: Inventory.Save (:68510) writes int version (109), ushort count, then per-item `ItemData.Save`; `ItemDrop.ItemData.Load(ZPackage, Version.Item)` is public static (:69398) and returns (prefabHash, itemData) with m_stack, with zero ObjectDB/Instantiate. Writing back via ItemData.Save needs m_dropPrefab set (:69345/69382), so a hand-rolled writer must set it from ObjectDB.GetItemPrefab(hash) — a lookup, not an Instantiate.
- Gate only the DEBIT write on s_inUse, not the read. s_items is updated live during use because the owner's OnContainerChanged -> Save() fires on every change (:122284-122301); and s_inUse can stick at 1 if the owning client disconnects with the chest open (nothing writes 0), which would stall a read-gated gate indefinitely.
- Server ownership claim is transient: ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS runs every 2 s (:76872-76885); IsInPeerActiveArea for the server session tests InActiveArea(point, refPos=(1e6,0,1e6)) (:76890-76894) which is false for any real coordinate, so any server-owned ZDO near a player is handed to that peer within <=2 s. During that window Container.Interact's `InvokeRPC("RPC_RequestOpen")` is routed to the owner (ZNetView.InvokeRPC -> owner) and ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC drops it because ZNetScene.FindInstance is null on the server — the player's E press does nothing until ownership reverts.
- Revision race is symmetric: both server and client drop incoming data with DataRevision <= local (:77099-77108 server; same code client-side), so a server debit and a concurrent client write from the same base revision diverge until the next client write. Consistent with the option's 'debit need not be reliable' stance, but say it.
- Enforcement latency: park is visible to the client only after poll period (1 Hz) + ZDOMan.SendZDOToPeers2 0.05 s timer (:76837-76850) + RTT; a transit initiated in that ~1-1.5 s after the chest is emptied still succeeds.
- ContainerRegistry.IsContainer is at Wonderland Core/Data/ContainerRegistry.cs:45 (takes a GameObject prefab); :58 is ResolveTemplate.
- Park must defeat Game.ConnectPortals (:100592) — with vanilla tag routing an unconnected portal whose tag matches its partner is re-paired within two 5 s passes. The Routing Kernel prerequisite is load-bearing, not optional; and every s_tag rewrite for the balance display changes the vanilla pairing key.
- Replace the Instantiate/Destroy cost warning: count stacks with `ItemDrop.ItemData.Load(pkg, version)` (public static, :69398) after reading the version int and ushort count exactly as Inventory.Load does (:68543-68556); no ObjectDB, no Instantiate. Handle the pre-`Version.Item.Smaller` LoadOld layout (:68565) for chests untouched since the format change. Use Inventory.Load only for write-back.
- Add explicit hysteresis: openThreshold (e.g. 50) and closeThreshold (e.g. 0) — the current text has open = balance >= price and a gate that stays lit at 48/50, which is contradictory.
- Parked connections do not survive a world save (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461 emits no hash for a None target); at startup vanilla re-pairs at ZDOMan.LoadChunks :76523 and every 5 s. The state must be re-derived from the chest each tick and the Routing Kernel must replace Game.ConnectPortals entirely (its tag-mismatch loop :100595-100599 would disconnect status-suffixed pairs).
- Ownership claim is optional and hazardous: ZDO.Set(int,byte[]) has no owner check; while the server session owns the chest every client RPC to it (RPC_RequestOpen) is silently dropped (ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC :83650-83660, no server ZNetView). If you claim, immediately SetOwner back to the nearest peer's uid.
- s_inUse skip is only needed before a WRITE (Container.Load returns false while m_inUse :122307, so the client would later overwrite the server's blob); balance READS while the UI is open are fine because Container.Save fires on every item move (:122282-122298).
- Citation fix: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData revision compare is at :77109 (`num4 <= zDO.DataRevision`); the client accepts any higher DataRevision regardless of ownership.

Chest reads are legitimate: Container.Save writes s_items on every owner-side change (:122294), Load() gates on DataRevision (:122303), s_inUse is written by the owner in UpdateUseVisual (:121990). ZDO.Set has no owner check, so the claim is optional; if used, hand ownership back to the nearest peer immediately. ### 92. The Token Turnstile

`economy-progression:The Token Turnstile` · domain **economy** · source `economy-progression`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


An item stand beside the gate is the payment slot — a single readable int on its ZDO decides whether the route is open, with no inventory deserialisation anywhere.


**How it works:** `ItemStand` stores what is mounted on it as `ZDOVars.s_item` (:78465), an int holding `m_queuedItem.m_dropPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode()`, written by `ItemStand.UpdateAttach` (:131845) on the owning client, with the full `ItemData` additionally serialised through `ItemDrop.SaveToZDO` (:70653) and orientation/variant/quality in sibling fields. Removing the item writes `Set(ZDOVars.s_item, 0)` (:131795/:131824).

Server side this is a one-line read: `int mounted = standZdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_item);`. No `ObjectDB`, no `Inventory`, no `Instantiate`, no `s_inUse` race, no byte blob. Compare against a per-route allowed set of prefab hashes and park/release accordingly. Poll cost is negligible — you can run this at 4 Hz across hundreds of gates.

Binding: find the nearest item-stand-prefab ZDO within 4m of the portal via `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear`, classified by `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(zdo.GetPrefab())?.GetComponent<ItemStand>() != null` (the prefab table IS populated server-side, `ZNetScene.Awake` :81941). Persist by rounded position.

Consuming the token is also a single write: `standZdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); standZdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_item, 0);`. Every client with the stand loaded re-reads the ZDO on `InvokeRepeating("UpdateVisual", 1f, 4f)` (:131573), so the item visibly disappears within 4 seconds. That gives you a true turnstile: mount a token, the gate lights, walk through, the server detects the transit and eats the token, the gate goes dark behind you.

This composes into the whole progression economy: the token IS the key. A `TrophyEikthyr` on the stand opens the Black Forest route; a `DragonEgg` opens the mountain trunk; a crafted `PortalShard` item opens anything. Because the check is "what object is physically sitting here", it is legible without any UI, it is transferable, it is stealable if unwarded, and it is exactly as forgeable as the item itself.

Multi-slot variant: bind N stands to one gate and require a specific combination (three trophies) — still N integer reads.


**Player experience:** Beside the mountain gate stands a stone item stand, empty, and the gate is dark. You place a Wolf Trophy on it. Within a second the gate lights and the tag flips from `"SUMMIT locked"` to `"SUMMIT open"`. You step through; four seconds later the trophy is gone from the stand and the gate behind you is dark again — one trophy, one trip. The stand is a physical, readable, stealable object: it says what the toll is without a single line of UI, and a rival who breaks your ward can lift your trophy off it. For a permanent key instead of a fare, the server simply never consumes it: the trophy sits there forever and the route stays lit, which turns a gate into a trophy room that happens to be load-bearing.


**Failure modes:**
- Anyone who can reach the stand can take the token off it — `ItemStand.Interact` gates only on `PrivateArea.CheckAccess`, which is meaningful only client-side. An unwarded turnstile is a theft target and an off switch.
- A stand holding a stack-of-one only: `UpdateAttach` forces `itemData.m_stack = 1` (:131843), so there is no "50 coins" on a stand. Fares are one-token-per-trip or nothing.
- The prefab hash on `s_item` is the DROP prefab name hash, not the item's display name — you must build your allowed set from `ObjectDB`/`ZNetScene` prefab names at runtime, not hard-code strings.
- Server-clearing `s_item` leaves the `s_itemData` blob written by `ItemDrop.SaveToZDO` behind on the ZDO. `ItemStand.DropItem` reads `GetInt(ZDOVars.s_item)` first (:131807) so a zeroed item is treated as absent, but the stale blob wastes save space; clear it too.
- Visual lag: the item vanishes from the stand up to 4 seconds after the server consumes it (`UpdateVisual` interval, :131573). A fast player sees a ghost trophy they can no longer interact with.

- Which item-stand prefabs exist (wall, floor, armour stand, guardian stone) and do they all carry an `ItemStand` on the ZNetView root rather than a child? `m_netViewOverride` at `ItemStand.Awake` (:131559) suggests some use an override root, which would put `s_item` on a different ZDO than the one you find by position.
- Does clearing `s_item` server-side while a client has the stand loaded reliably remove the visual, or does the client's `m_visualItemDrop` persist until a scene reload? Check by mounting a trophy, clearing it from the server, and watching for 10s.
- Is the guardian-stone `ItemStand` variant (`m_guardianPower` at :131597) safe to use as a turnstile, or does mounting a trophy there trigger the power grant path?

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Token set is bounded by ItemStand.CanAttach (:131963-131981): the item prefab must have an `attach` or `attach_skin` child (GetAttachPrefab) AND be in m_supportedItems/m_supportedTypes and not in m_unsupportedItems. Trophies, weapons, shields, tools, armor pieces qualify; Coins, DragonEgg and generic materials are not stand-mountable — drop the DragonEgg example, or mark needs-ingame-check per item. A 'crafted PortalShard item' requires a client-side prefab and is impossible in a server-only mod — strike it.
- The consume step is reactive-detection-only: it depends on the position-jump detector. A missed detection leaves the trophy in place and the route open indefinitely; the option should not present 'one trophy, one trip' as enforced.
- SetOwner(server) before the clear opens a <=2 s window (ReleaseZDOS :76872-76885, IsInPeerActiveArea :76890) in which the client's `InvokeRPC("RPC_RequestOwn")` from UseItem (:~131875) is dropped by ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC; UseItem's `InvokeRepeating("UpdateAttach", 0f, 0.1f)` keeps polling IsOwner so it self-heals once ownership reverts — mention the delay.
- The clear leaves ItemDrop.SaveToZDO's sibling keys (durability, quality, variant, crafter) stale on the stand ZDO; harmless because HaveAttachment only tests s_item, but DropItem's LoadFromExternalZDO would read them if s_item were ever repopulated externally.
- Line cites: ItemStand.Awake begins :131558 (cited :131557 is blank); RPC_DestroyAttachment :131789; DropItem :131800.
- Remove `PortalShard`: no custom item can exist on a vanilla client. Tokens must be vanilla prefabs present in the client ObjectDB.
- Token eligibility is constrained client-side by ItemStand.CanAttach (:131963-131980): the item prefab needs an `attach` child (GetAttachPrefab) and must pass m_supportedTypes/m_supportedItems/m_unsupportedItems. Trophies qualify; DragonEgg and other Misc items need an in-game check per stand prefab (itemstand vs itemstandh).
- 'One trophy, one trip' has a ~2 s multi-rider window: the token is consumed only after transit detection; anyone entering the still-open portal before that rides free.
- After `standZdo.SetOwner(session); standZdo.Set(s_item, 0)`, hand ownership straight back (SetOwner(nearestPeerUid)) — otherwise the next player's RPC_RequestOwn is silently dropped for up to 2 s (HandleRoutedRPC :83650-83660, ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901).
- Optional instant visual: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(ZRoutedRpc.Everybody, standZdo.m_uid, "SetVisualItem", 0, 0, 0, 0)` mirrors vanilla :131797 so the trophy vanishes immediately instead of on the 4 s poll.
- Citation precision: UpdateAttach s_item write is at :131842-131846; UpdateVisual body :131857-131867.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Verified: ItemStand.UpdateAttach (:131834-131853) writes `s_item = m_queuedItem.m_dropPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode()` on the owner plus ItemDrop.SaveToZDO; RPC_DestroyAttachment (:131789-131797) and DropItem (:131800-131825) clear it to 0; HaveAttachment is `GetInt(s_item) != 0`; Awake registers RPC_RequestOwn and `InvokeRepeating("UpdateVisual", 1f, 4f)` (:131558-131575); UpdateVisual re-reads s_item/s_variant/s_quality and calls SetVisualItem, so a server clear is visually applied within 4 s. - [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The single-int read is real: ItemStand.UpdateAttach writes s_item = prefab name hash (:131842-131846), RPC_DestroyAttachment/DropItem clear it to 0 (:131795, :131824), UpdateVisual re-reads s_item on InvokeRepeating(1f,4f) (:131573, :131857-131867). (3) One token can admit several people: detection lands ~2 s after transit while the gate stays open, so a second player entering inside that window rides free; the option's 'one trophy, one trip' is approximate. (5) Clearing only s_item leaves the ItemDrop.SaveToZDO sibling fields — same as vanilla RPC_DestroyAttachment, harmless. ### 93. Reactive Transit Toll

`economy-progression:Reactive Transit Toll` · domain **economy** · source `economy-progression`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** reactive-detection-only → **reactive-detection-only** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Detect that a transit happened and bill afterwards — genuinely useful for metering and auditing, but structurally incapable of preventing anything, and the detector has a real false-positive tail.


**How it works:** There is no server hook on the moment of transit. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` has exactly one call site — `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` (:143672) — gated on `Player.m_localPlayer == component`, and a dedicated server instantiates no portal GameObject because `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f,0f,1000000f))` every physics tick (:100465), so `ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted` (:82105) only ever builds objects in a sector 1e6 m from the world. The server can only infer transits from the character ZDO's position.

Detector, sharpened from Wonderland's `PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit` (`Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:148`): every 0.25s, for each `ConnectedCharacters.All()` entry, sample `zdo.GetPosition()`. Keep the previous sample. On a jump exceeding `MaxLegitimateSpeed * dt`, test whether the FROM sample lies within `R` (use 8m, not Wonderland's 40m) of some portal P and the TO sample within `R` of a portal Q, AND `P.GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) == Q.m_uid`. That link check is what collapses the false-positive rate: a coincidental near-two-portals jump that is not along a live edge is rejected. Portals come free from `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()` (:77643, the live dictionary, zero-alloc).

Latency: `Player.UpdateTeleport` does nothing until `m_teleportTimer > 2f`, then force-assigns `transform.position = m_teleportTargetPos` every FixedUpdate (:15337-15343). `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` pushes that into the ZDO (:87527) and the client's ZDO change queue drains to the server on a 0.05s timer (`ZDOMan.Update` :76843). So the server learns ~2.0-2.3s after the player stepped in — which is inside the ≥8s black screen, but long after the decision was irrevocable.

Billing: on a confirmed transit, resolve the payer as `ConnectedCharacter.PlayerId` (`ZDOVars.s_playerID`, :78539) and debit the route's escrow chest, or increment a debt counter stored as a world global key `mod_debt_<playerID>` via `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey(key, value)` (:115933) — keys at or above `GlobalKeys.NonServerOption` (ordinal 41, :101313) persist in the world .db (`ZoneSystem.Save` strips only ordinals < 41, :113749).

What to do about non-payment is the whole point: you cannot stop the trip that already happened. You CAN park the route, park every gate the debtor built, or escalate — see Debtor's Lien.


**Player experience:** The player notices nothing at the moment of travel. Two seconds after they arrive, a toast appears in the top-left: `Bridge toll: 5 coins (chest 45/50)`. If the chest cannot cover it, the toast instead reads `Bridge toll unpaid — 5 owed` and the gate they just came through goes dark behind them, stranding them on the far side until somebody funds it. That is the honest shape of the mechanic: it never stops the first free ride, it makes the second one impossible. Over a week of play the ledger is visible in the tag (`"BRIDGE 45/50c"`) and in a Discord feed, so the social pressure does the enforcement the code cannot.


**Failure modes:**
- Fundamentally unenforceable as prevention. By the time the server sees the position change the player has already moved, has already been invulnerable for 2s (`Character.RPC_Damage` is suppressed while `IsTeleporting()`, :2425/:2429/:2582), and cannot be refused.
- False positives: an admin using `goto`/`recall` (`Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` :41962 — registered on every client with no sender check), a dungeon entry (interiors sit at y+5000, `Location.Awake` :133512), a `Ladder.Interact` instant snap (:132064, no cooldown and no checks at all), a respawn, and `Player.EdgeOfWorldKill`'s inward shove (:11132). Suppress on `ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName())` (:81811), on `Character.InInterior` boundary crossings (:4538), and on `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)`.
- False negatives: two portals of the same pair within 16m of each other make FROM and TO indistinguishable; a player who logs out mid-teleport never produces a TO sample; a 0.25s poll can miss a transit followed immediately by another move.
- A player can farm free trips by disconnecting before the debit lands — the character ZDO is non-persistent and destroyed by `ZDOMan.RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS` (:77406) on disconnect. Debt must be keyed on `s_playerID` and persisted outside the character ZDO.
- `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` returns the LIVE dictionary; iterating it while your own code mutates portal ZDOs in the same pass will throw. Snapshot with `GetPortalList()` (:77648) if you write during the sweep.

### 94. Debtor's Lien and Personal Gates

`economy-progression:Debtor's Lien and Personal Gates` · domain **economy** · source `economy-progression`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The move that converts an unenforceable per-player rule into an enforceable per-route one: you cannot refuse a player at a gate, but you can close every gate that player built.


**How it works:** This is the central design trick of the whole domain. Every player-placed piece records its builder: `Piece.SetCreator` writes `ZDOVars.s_creator` (a long equal to that player's `PlayerProfile.m_playerID`) and `ZDOVars.s_creatorIndex` (an index into `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory`, which the server maintains from socket-verified PlatformUserIDs), called from `Player.PlacePiece` for every placement (:136415, :12514). The same long appears on that player's live character ZDO as `ZDOVars.s_playerID` (:78539, written by `Player.SetPlayerID` :10129), so `ConnectedCharacter.PlayerId` (Wonderland `Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs:30`) joins the two.

So: iterate `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` (:77648), read `zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator, 0L)`, and you have a complete, offline-readable, whole-world map of who built which gate. Now a rule of the form "player X owes 340 coins" becomes the rule "every route whose gates were built by X is parked until the debt clears" — which lives entirely in the enforceable bucket.

**Personal gates.** Push it further: give each player a private tag namespace so their home gate pairs only with their own remote gates. Their route is then a 1:1 function of their identity, and every per-route lever (park, cooldown, fuel, lease, tier) becomes de facto per-player without ever needing a per-player check at the moment of transit. This is how you build "Bjorn's portal network is suspended" out of parts that only know about routes.

**Escalation ladder, weakest to strongest, all server-side:**
1. Tag notice — `s_tag` rewritten to `"MINE -340c"`, visible to everyone who walks past.
2. Toast on login and on approach — `PlayerNotify.Toast` (Wonderland `Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs:15`).
3. Map pin at the debt gate — `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse", name, (int)Minimap.PinType.Icon3, pos, false)` (`Game.Start` registration :100068, `Game.RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` :100823).
4. Lien — park every gate with that `s_creator`.
5. Repossession — `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo);` (:76929, owner-gated on send).
6. Kick / ban — `ZNet.instance.Kick(hostName)` / `Ban(hostName)` (:81658, :81744), resolved from `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`, the only platform-verified identity on the server (`ZNet.RPC_PeerInfo` Steam ticket verification :79843).

Persist debt as a world global key `mod_debt_<playerID> <amount>` — any string not parsing as a `GlobalKeys` member becomes a `NonServerOption` key (`ZoneSystem.GetKeyValue` :113560) and is saved in the .db rather than the .fwl.


**Player experience:** You skip out on four bridge tolls. Nothing happens for a day. Then you log in and a top-left toast reads `Toll debt: 340 coins. Your gates are suspended.` You run to your base and your own home portal — the one you built, with your own tag — reads `Teleport tag:"HOME -340c" [Unconnected]`, dark. So does the one at the mine, and the one at the swamp. Public gates still work fine, so you are not cut off from the world, you are cut off from *your* world, and everyone who walks past your base can read why. You put 340 coins in the toll chest and every one of your gates lights back up within five seconds. Nobody had to be online to enforce it and no admin had to be woken up.


**Failure modes:**
- `Piece.SetCreator` only writes when `m_nview.IsOwner() && GetCreator() == 0L` (:136417). World-generated structures and anything placed before the field existed have `s_creator == 0`. Never treat creator 0 as "owned by nobody in particular" without checking — and never lien on it, or you park every ancient or admin-spawned gate on the server.
- `s_creator` is a client-authored value: the placing client writes its own local `PlayerProfile` id. Two profiles can collide or be hand-edited. `s_creatorIndex` at least indexes the server-maintained `ZNet.World.m_playerHistory` (:112396, persisted in the .fwl at :112587), which IS built from verified PlatformUserIDs (`ZNet.UpdatePlayerList` :81271) — cross-check the two and refuse to act when they disagree.
- Collective punishment: a shared clan base has gates built by one member. Liening them punishes everyone. Offer an opt-in "clan account" keyed on the ward's permitted list instead (see Ward Tariff Classes).
- A debtor can dodge by demolishing and rebuilding gates under a fresh character (`s_playerID` is per character file, not per account). Key liens on the PlatformUserID resolved through `s_creatorIndex` → `m_playerHistory`, not on `s_creator`.
- Repossession is irreversible and will be read as the mod eating someone's base. Reserve step 5 for admin action, never automate it.

- Is `ZDOVars.s_creator` reliably non-zero on a player-placed portal in 1.0.7? TortalPortal's own `PortalExport` treats creator==0 as "admin-spawned or older than the field". Check: place a portal on a vanilla client, dump `s_creator` server-side, confirm it equals that character's `s_playerID`.
