### 117. Raid-Time Geofenced Restriction

`lockdown-safety:Raid-Time Geofenced Restriction` · domain **lockdown** · source `lockdown-safety`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Use the server-authoritative RandEventSystem raid state to lock only the portals inside the active event radius, so a base under attack cannot be escaped or reinforced through its own gate.


**How it works:** Raid state is genuinely server-side, unlike the boss gate. `RandEventSystem.UpdateRandomEvent` runs under `if (!ZNet.instance.IsServer()) return;` (:106838-106843) and `FixedUpdate` evaluates `IsAnyPlayerInEventArea(m_randomEvent)` (:106797) which itself iterates `ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` (:107111-107121) — so the server already reasons about raid geometry using character ZDOs, exactly the data a server-only mod has. `RandEventSystem.instance.GetCurrentRandomEvent()` is public (:107373-107376) and returns the live `RandomEvent` carrying `m_name`, `m_pos`, `m_time`, `m_duration` (default 60f) and `m_eventRange` (default 96f, :107451). `IsInsideRandomEventArea` is `position.y <= 3000f && Utils.DistanceXZ(position, re.m_pos) < re.m_eventRange` (:106829-106836) — trivially reimplementable. The engine ticks at 1Hz: read the current event; if non-null and its name matches a configured raid allowlist (or any event with a non-empty `m_spawn` list), compute the set of portal ZDOs from `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` whose `GetPosition()` falls inside `m_eventRange` of `m_pos`; force-disconnect exactly those, vaulting their wiring; when the event ends (`GetCurrentRandomEvent()` returns null, or `SetRandomEvent(null,...)` at :106800) restore them. Because the lock is a strict subset of portals it is far cheaper than a global lockdown and produces no world-wide save churn — though note `DirtyPortalObjects` has no per-portal granularity, so ANY portal write still rewrites the whole portal chunk at the next save. Optionally pair with a `RPC_DamageText` at each affected portal reading 'SEALED — RAID' so the reason is legible. A stricter variant locks the whole tag GROUP any affected portal belongs to, so the defenders cannot simply walk 100m to a second gate on the same network.


**Player experience:** A 'The ground is shaking' troll raid starts on a player's base. Every portal within 96m of the raid centre visibly goes dark — hover flips to `$piece_portal_unconnected`, the ring stops glowing, orange text floats above it reading 'SEALED — RAID'. The player cannot bail out through the portal and cannot summon a friend in through it; they fight or they run on foot. Portals elsewhere in the world are entirely unaffected. Sixty seconds later the raid ends and the same portals light back up with their original partners, which is the vault doing its job. A player mid-transit when the raid started still arrives — nothing can interrupt `UpdateTeleport`.


**Failure modes:**
- `m_eventRange` and `m_duration` are Inspector values per event; the 96f/60f in the class are defaults and the shipped raids may differ. Read them off the live `RandomEvent` rather than hard-coding.
- Locking on raid start and unlocking on raid end means a raid that is cancelled by `SetRandomEvent(null, ...)` for any reason (a `SetEvent` RPC from a client, an admin command, `m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea` logic) fires the unlock path — which is correct, but the reconciler must be level-triggered off `GetCurrentRandomEvent()` rather than edge-triggered off an event-start hook.
- `RPC_SetEvent` is a routed RPC (:106781) and on a non-server it sets the local event; the server's own `RandEventSystem` is authoritative and `SendCurrentRandomEvent` broadcasts it (:106952-106962). A client cannot forge a raid on the server, but do not read raid state from anything a client could influence.
- Portals just outside the radius become the obvious escape hatch, which may be the intended tactical texture or may be seen as a loophole. The tag-group variant closes it at the cost of surprising players whose unaffected remote portal also goes dark.
- Frequent short raids mean frequent portal-chunk dirtying and therefore a full portal-chunk rewrite on every save. On a large world that is the dominant cost of this feature.
- Does not and cannot stop a raided player from logging out, which is the actual escape most players use.

**Designer citations:** RandEventSystem.UpdateRandomEvent server-only — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:106838-106843 ; RandEventSystem.FixedUpdate IsAnyPlayerInEventArea — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:106793-106802 ; RandEventSystem.IsAnyPlayerInEventArea over GetAllCharacterZDOS — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:107111-107121 ; RandEventSystem.IsInsideRandomEventArea — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:106829-106836 ; RandEventSystem.GetCurrentRandomEvent — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:107373-107376 ; RandomEvent.m_eventRange / m_duration / m_spawn — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:107445-107498 ; RandEventSystem.SetRandomEvent / SendCurrentRandomEvent — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:107083-107109, :106952-106962 ; ZDOMan.GetPortalList — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77648-77656 ; ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk (no per-portal granularity) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77621-77632


**Open questions:**
- Do the shipped raid events actually use the class-default `m_eventRange = 96f`? Inspector data. IN-GAME CHECK: log `RandEventSystem.instance.GetCurrentRandomEvent()`'s `m_name`, `m_pos`, `m_eventRange` and `m_duration` during a live raid on the dedicated server.
- Is `RandEventSystem.instance` reliably non-null on a headless server at the time the subsystem's first tick runs? `Start` registers the `SetEvent` RPC at :106781. IN-GAME CHECK: null-guard and log on the first 60 ticks.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**

### 118. Biome and Region Restricted Networks

`lockdown-safety:Biome and Region Restricted Networks` · domain **lockdown** · source `lockdown-safety`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium-large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Enforce that a portal may only pair with a partner in an allowed biome or region, implemented as a server-side tag-namespace rewrite so vanilla's own pairing does the enforcing.


**How it works:** Do not fight `Game.ConnectPortals` — recruit it. Its phase 1 tears down any link whose partner's `s_tag` string differs (:100601) and phase 2 only pairs portals whose tags are byte-identical (`FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` :100669, ordinal `string !=`, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant). So enforcing a region rule reduces to: rewrite `s_tag` so that portals in different allowed-regions can never share a tag string. On a slow tick (30s) walk `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()`, and for each portal derive its region key purely from procedural world data — `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(pos.x, pos.z)` (:151725) for biome, or a configured named rectangle/circle list for hand-drawn regions. Collider-based classification is impossible server-side (the reference position is pinned at 1e6, so `ZoneSystem.GetGroundData`/`IsBlocked` always return their no-hit fallbacks), and `WorldGenerator` is the only viable terrain oracle. Then compute the desired tag as `userTag` (unchanged) if the portal's region is in the same allowed-group as its current partner, or `userTag + regionSuffix` when the rule requires namespacing. Write with `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, newTag)` (:73721 / :78617 — no length cap, no validation at this layer), then `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` EXPLICITLY, because a tag-only write does NOT set that flag (only `SetConnection`, `AddIfPortal` and `HandleDestroyedZDO` do) and the rename is otherwise silently lost at the next world save. Finally call `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` once to re-pair immediately rather than waiting up to 5s. Record the original user tag in the vault so the rule can be lifted. THE SUFFIX MUST KEEP THE TOTAL AT OR BELOW 10 CHARACTERS or a player who opens the rename dialog will truncate it — `TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (:143482) sets `m_inputField.characterLimit` and the field is pre-filled with the existing tag. A single-character suffix (`Base~M` for Meadows) is the safe shape. An alternative that avoids tag mutation entirely is to leave tags alone and instead patch `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` with a postfix that overwrites `__result` with null when the proposed partner's region is disallowed — a much smaller, lower-risk change that leaves all user-visible state untouched, at the cost of leaving one portal permanently unpaired with no explanation visible to the player.


**Player experience:** A player builds a portal in the Mistlands tagged 'ore' and another in the Meadows also tagged 'ore'. Under a 'no cross-biome-tier travel' rule the two never connect: both hover as `$piece_portal_unconnected` and stay dark. If the tag-suffix variant is used, the player sees their tags have become 'ore~M' and 'ore~m' and can work out why; if the FindRandomUnconnectedPortal variant is used they see nothing at all and will file a bug. A second Mistlands portal tagged 'ore' pairs with the first immediately. An admin-run `listregions` style report shows which portals are in which region group and which are orphaned by the rule.


**Failure modes:**
- `WorldGenerator.GetBiome` is blind to player terraforming and to a location's own flattening, and biome boundaries are fractal — a portal built exactly on a Meadows/BlackForest seam can flip region between ticks and thrash its tag. Hysteresis (require N consecutive samples of the new region) and a snap-to-first-observed-region cache are mandatory.
- Tag rewriting is visible, surprising, and collides with the 10-char client cap. A player re-saving a truncated tag corrupts the namespacing and silently re-enables a forbidden pairing.
- `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 will tear down an existing cross-region link the moment the tags diverge, stranding a player who was relying on it, with no warning. Announce before applying a new region rule.
- The `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` postfix variant is a private-method patch (`AccessTools.Method(typeof(Game), "FindRandomUnconnectedPortal")`) and will silently stop applying if the signature changes; wrap in SafePatch.
- Rich-text or unusual characters in the suffix are stripped from the hover label by `RemoveRichTextTags` (:143459), so the suffix must be plain.
- A tag-only write that forgets `SetDirtyPortals()` looks correct in memory and in the live game and vanishes at the next world save — a classic silent data-loss bug.

**Designer citations:** Game.ConnectPortals tag-equality teardown — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100594-100606 (:100601) ; Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal ordinal tag match — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100664-100679 (:100669) ; ZDO.Set(int,string) / ZDOVars.s_tag — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73721, :78617 ; ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals (public) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702-76705 ; ZDO.SetConnection is the only auto-dirty path — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73656-73666 ; TeleportWorld.Interact 10-char cap — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143482 ; TeleportWorld.GetHoverText RemoveRichTextTags — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143463 ; WorldGenerator.GetBiome — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:151725 ; ZoneSystem collider helpers dead server-side (FindFloor) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115604-115613 ; Game.FixedUpdate reference-position pin — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100465 ; Game.ConnectPortals public for on-demand re-pair — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589


**Open questions:**
- Does `GuiInputField` clamp a programmatically assigned `.text` to `characterLimit`? `TextInput.Show` assigns `m_inputField.text = existingTag` AFTER setting `characterLimit = 10` (:61515-61522). If it clamps, any server-written tag longer than 10 chars is truncated the instant a player opens the dialog. IN-GAME CHECK: server-write a 20-char tag, open and confirm the dialog on a vanilla client, re-read `s_tag`.
- How stable is `WorldGenerator.GetBiome` at a fixed coordinate across server restarts? It is pure and seed-driven so it should be bit-identical, but confirm before keying persistent state on it. IN-GAME CHECK: log the biome for 100 portal positions before and after a restart and diff.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Normalise tags in a Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals (:100589) rather than a 30s tick; otherwise a fresh rename can be cross-region paired for 5-10s and used.
- The FindRandomUnconnectedPortal postfix-null variant is nondeterministic and over-blocks (random single pick at :100677); replace with a prefix that filters the candidate list by region and keeps the IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal exclusion.
- Suffixing must strip its own prior suffix before re-deriving (rename dialog is pre-filled with the suffixed tag, client :144223); user tags of 9-10 characters cannot be suffixed without truncation.
- Rewritten tags are saved to disk and persist after mod removal; the vault must replay at least once to lift the rule.
- Portals in interiors (y>3000) are not classifiable by WorldGenerator.GetBiome; assign an explicit region.
- Server tag writes can revision-collide with a concurrent client RPC_SetTag (client RPC_ZDOData :77217); rare.
- Enforcement gap: a 30s rewrite tick vs the 5s ConnectPortalsCoroutine :100580-100587 means an owner-side rename (TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag :143583-143600 — no server hook, arrives only as ZDO sync) can get a cross-region pair connected for up to ~35s. To be server-enforced the backstop must live at pairing time: a Harmony PREFIX on private Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664 that removes disallowed candidates (or a prefix on ConnectPortals that runs the rewrite first). The described POSTFIX that nulls __result is wrong: the method picks `list[Random.Range(0,list.Count)]` :100679, so a postfix would non-deterministically block or allow depending on which candidate the RNG chose that tick.
- `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` is neither needed nor durable: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77076-77140 applies incoming ZDO data purely on DataRevision with no owner check (on both client and server), so the server's Set propagates regardless; and ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76925 hands server-owned portals inside a peer's active area to that peer within 2s. While the server transiently owns a portal, a player's rename (ZNetView.InvokeRPC routed to the owner) lands on a server with no ZNetView instance and is silently dropped.
- Revision race: if the client renames in the same window as the server rewrite, both bump from the same DataRevision and each side ignores the other's update (`num4 <= zDO.DataRevision` :77110); the next server rewrite (higher revision) wins. The 30s tick must be treated as the convergence bound, not 'immediate'.
- Blank tags: two empty-tag portals pair in vanilla (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal matches "" == ""); a suffix turns "" into "~M", which is visible and may surprise players.
- `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal`, `SetConnection`, `RPC_SetConnection` are all private on Game (:100636-100660, :100664) — Harmony can patch them, but there is no public API; say so.
- Nothing here survives a world save unless SetDirtyPortals is called, as the option says — confirmed by reading the dirty-flag setters; note vanilla itself has the same gap for client-originated renames (RPC_ZDOData -> AddIfPortal :77732-77752 does not dirty an already-registered portal), which is why ConnectPortals' forced second-tick commit (ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals -> ForceSetConnection -> local SetConnection) is what normally saves pairings.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core claim holds: Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 tears down any pair whose tag strings differ (:100601, ordinal !=) and FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100663-100677) only pairs byte-identical tags; ConnectPortalsCoroutine runs only under IsServer (:100070-100074), and a vanilla client never writes a Portal connection except to None (client RPC_SetTag/SetConnectedPortal :144327-144369), so pairing is a server-owned decision — server-enforced is honest. ZDO.Set(int,string) (:73721-73727) has no validation and does NOT touch DirtyPortalObjects (only ZDO.SetConnection :73656-73666, AddIfPortal, HandleDestroyedZDO :76986 and Load do), and portal ZDOs are excluded from the ordinary sector chunks (AddObjectsPerChunk filters PortalPrefabHash), so the explicit SetDirtyPortals() (:76702-76705) is mandatory as stated. WorldGenerator.Initialize runs on the server at world load (:79200/:79899) and GetBiome (:151725) is pure math. Client rename cap is 10 (client :144223). Corrections: (1) A 30s rewrite tick leaves a real hole: a player renames to 'ore', vanilla pairs it cross-region within 5-10s, and the player can transit before the mod re-suffixes. Do the region normalisation inside a Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals (public, :100589) so tags are canonical before every pairing pass — zero window and no separate tick. (2) The FindRandomUnconnectedPortal-postfix variant is worse than described: the method picks ONE random candidate (:100677) and a postfix that nulls a disallowed pick leaves the portal unpaired even when an allowed candidate exists in the same list, and the outcome changes from tick to tick. Use a prefix that re-implements the candidate filter (region-allowed AND same tag AND unconnected AND !IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal), which also preserves the two-tick staged commit. (3) Suffix bookkeeping must be idempotent: the rename dialog is pre-filled with GetText() == the suffixed tag, so users will re-submit 'ore~M' or 'ore'; the mod must strip its own suffix before re-deriving, and user tags of 9-10 chars cannot take a suffix without truncating user data. (4) Rewritten tags are persisted (tag is a ZDO string saved in the portal chunk) and survive mod removal; lifting the rule requires the vault replay to run at least once. (5) Server-side tag writes race the owning client's RPC_SetTag by revision number (client RPC_ZDOData :77217 discards num4 <= DataRevision) — rare but the same caveat as every server write to a client-owned ZDO. (6) Portals in interiors (y>3000) cannot be biome-classified by GetBiome; treat as a distinct region or skip. Case-distinct suffixes ('M' vs 'm') are technically valid under ordinal compare but user-hostile; use unambiguous single characters.

### 119. Per-Network Quarantine-Tag Lockdown

`lockdown-safety:Per-Network Quarantine-Tag Lockdown` · domain **lockdown** · source `lockdown-safety`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Lock a single named portal network by rewriting its members' tags to per-portal-unique quarantine strings, so vanilla's own reconciler tears the links down and can never rebuild them.


**How it works:** This is the self-reinforcing alternative to nulling connections, and it needs no `Game.ConnectPortals` suppression at all. To lock the network named `mine`: for every portal in `GetPortalList()` whose `s_tag` equals `mine`, vault `(position, "mine")`, then `SetOwner(sessionID)` and `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, uniquePerPortalString)` where the string is distinct for every member (e.g. `"!lk" + shortHash(position)` kept at or under 10 characters), then `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` and `ForceSendZDO`. Vanilla then does the enforcement for free: `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 sees each portal's partner carrying a different `s_tag` and calls `SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None)` at :100603 within 5s, and phase 2 can never re-pair them because `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (:100669) requires exact tag equality and no two quarantine strings match. The lock is therefore stable under vanilla's own 5s reconciler with zero Harmony patches on `Game.ConnectPortals`, which is a major robustness and compatibility win over the force-disconnect approach. Unlocking is the reverse tag write plus one `Game.instance.ConnectPortals()` call; because every member returns to the shared tag simultaneously, phase 2 re-pairs them — RANDOMLY, so the original partner assignment is not preserved unless the vault also re-asserts connections explicitly after the tag restore. Note phase 1's `SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None)` is NOT forced (:100603, no `forceImmediateConnection`), so for a portal owned by an online peer the clear is routed as `RPC_SetConnection` to that client and the server's own copy still reads the old value for at least one more tick — meaning the teardown takes 2+ ticks (up to ~10s) near a player rather than 5s. If the lock must be instant, do the tag write AND an explicit forced `SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None)` with `SetOwner` in the same pass.


**Player experience:** An admin runs the network-lock command for `mine`. Within about five seconds (or ten if a player is standing next to one) every portal on that network goes dark and its hover text changes from `$piece_portal_tag:"mine" [$piece_portal_connected]` to `$piece_portal_tag:"!lk3f2a" [$piece_portal_unconnected]` — visibly and legibly quarantined, unlike a silent connection null. Other networks are completely untouched and keep working. On unlock the tags revert to `mine` and the portals re-pair, though a player may find their mine portal now leads to a different one of the three mine portals than before unless the vault re-asserted the exact pairing.


**Failure modes:**
- MUTATES USER-VISIBLE STATE. If the server crashes while quarantined and the vault is lost or not replayed, players are left with portals permanently named `!lk3f2a`. Strictly worse failure surface than connection-nulling, which at least leaves tags intact.
- The 10-char truncation hazard is acute here: a confused player will absolutely open the rename dialog on a `!lk3f2a` portal. Keep quarantine tags ≤10 chars and expect some to be manually renamed by players mid-lock, which silently removes that portal from the vault's ability to restore it.
- Unlock re-pairs randomly via `UnityEngine.Random.Range` (:100678) unless connections are explicitly re-asserted from the vault after the tag restore. A 2-member network is unaffected; a 4-member one can come back completely rewired.
- A 3+ member network unlocked back to a shared tag strands exactly one member (vanilla behaviour, :100607-100622), and which one is arbitrary and unstable across restarts.
- Tag writes do not set `DirtyPortalObjects` automatically — forgetting the explicit `SetDirtyPortals()` loses both the lock AND the restore across a save.
- A player can defeat the lock on a portal they own by simply renaming it back to `mine` through the vanilla dialog; the mod must re-assert on a tick, and that re-assert is a tag write that dirties the portal chunk every time.

- Not self-reinforcing against players: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925, every 2 s) transfers server-owned portals to any nearby peer, after which vanilla RPC_SetTag (:143571-143585) can restore 'mine' or set any tag with no server hook; add a re-assert loop keyed on the vault and expect up to ~5-10 s transient reconnection windows.
- 'zero Harmony patches on Game.ConnectPortals' is true only for the reconciler interaction; enforcement still requires the mod's own periodic tag/ownership re-assert (not free of a runtime loop).
- ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals is mandatory for tag persistence: IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) -> SetDirtySector (:76694-76699) only dirties the spatial chunk, and GetSaveClonePerChunk rewrites the ChunkPortal file only when DirtyPortalObjects is set (:77621-77632).
- The 10-char TextInput cap (:143482) is client-UI only and does not constrain mod-written tags; keep quarantine strings short purely for hover-text legibility.
- Unlock re-pairing is random (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100677) — the vault must explicitly ForceSetConnection both directions to restore original partners.
- Quarantine strings must be >10 characters (e.g. 12-16), not <=10: vanilla clients cannot type tags longer than the TextInput charLimit of 10 (:143482; client :61572-61583), which is what stops a player retagging a spare portal to the displayed quarantine string and pairing into the locked network.
- The lock is not self-sustaining against vanilla clients: nearby peers receive ownership every 2 s (ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76926, portals included via FindObjects :77376-77381) and RPC_SetTag runs locally on the owner (:143587-143602) with no packets; a periodic tag reassert (level-triggered) is required, plus tolerance for RPC_ZDOData revision races (:77112-77135) that can briefly overwrite the server's tag.
- Because the mod SetOwner(sessionID)s before the tag write, phase-1 SetConnection takes the local branch (ZNet.GetPeer(sessionID) == null at :100639-100641), so teardown is normally immediate at the next 5 s pass; the routed 2-tick path only occurs when ReleaseNearbyZDOS handed ownership to a nearby player within the prior 2 s.
- Hover text format is '$piece_portal $piece_portal_tag:"<tag>" [<state>]' and the tag passes through CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC before display (:143453-143463, :143563-143576); pick quarantine strings that cannot trip the word filter.
- Unlock must re-assert the vaulted pairs via zdo.SetOwner(sessionID)+zdo.SetConnection (public ZDO API) or the original partner assignment is lost to Random.Range in FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100678).

### 120. TeleportAll and DungeonBuild Policy Levers

`lockdown-safety:TeleportAll and DungeonBuild Policy Levers` · domain **lockdown** · source `lockdown-safety`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The two remaining portal-adjacent world-modifier keys — cargo policy and dungeon building — with their exact, commonly-misstated semantics.


**How it works:** Both are plain global-key writes with the same propagation path as NoPortals (`SetGlobalKey` → `RPC_SetGlobalKey` → `GlobalKeyAdd` + `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` → every client's `RPC_GlobalKeys` clear-and-rebuild). TELEPORTALL (ordinal 35, :101307): read by `Inventory.IsTeleportable(bool allowAllItems)` (:68860-68880) which is reached from `Humanoid.IsTeleportable` (:8791-8794) and thence `TeleportWorld.Teleport` gate 4 (:143533). THE CRITICAL SEMANTIC: the method first rejects outright if ANY item has `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` (:68862-68868) and only THEN honours `allowAllItems || GetGlobalKey(TeleportAll)` at :68869. So `teleportall` is emphatically NOT 'allow all cargo' — a hard-coded tier-1000 item class remains non-teleportable regardless of the key and regardless of any per-portal flag. Any feature description must carry that caveat. The key also drives visible client UI with no extra work: `InventoryGui` sets `element.m_noteleport.enabled = !item.m_shared.m_teleportable && !GetGlobalKey(TeleportAll)` (:49462) and the item tooltip appends `$item_noteleport` under the same condition (:69755), both per-refresh reads — so toggling the key live updates every vanilla client's inventory icons and tooltips instantly, which is a free and honest UX signal. DUNGEONBUILD (ordinal 34, :101306): read in the client's piece-placement validation as `!component.m_allowedInDungeons && InInterior() && !EnvMan.instance.CheckInteriorBuildingOverride() && !GetGlobalKey(DungeonBuild)` (:13353) — setting it lets vanilla clients place any piece, portals included, inside dungeons. Purely client-honoured; the server never validates placement and there is no server-side placement veto short of the SpawnGovernor-style destroy-on-arrival hook (`ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO` postfix + `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix). Both keys are below `NonServerOption` so both persist into the .fwl unless written with `canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false`, and both appear in the server-browser modifier badge on the next registration.


**Player experience:** With `teleportall` set, a player opens their inventory and the little 'no teleport' badge disappears from their iron bars and tin ore in real time, with no relog — and they can carry them through a portal. With it cleared the badges reappear instantly and the next transit gives `$msg_noteleport`. Flametal-class tier-1000 items keep the badge and keep being refused either way, which will generate bug reports unless documented. With `dungeonbuild` set, a player standing in a burial chamber can place a portal inside it and it pairs normally with a surface portal on the same tag — dungeon interiors sit at the same XZ sector as the surface above (`ZoneSystem.GetZone` ignores y) so nothing about sync or pairing is special-cased.


**Failure modes:**
- `TeleportAll` does not override the `m_toolTier >= 1000` rejection (:68862-68868). Advertising 'carry anything' is wrong.
- Both keys are client-honoured. A modified client ignores the cargo restriction whether the key is set or not, and the server cannot detect it — player inventories are never mirrored into any ZDO, so there is no server-side audit of what was carried.
- Both keys are world-modifier ordinals and therefore permanently edit `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys` and the public modifier badge unless the session-only write is used.
- `dungeonbuild` is global — it enables dungeon building for every piece and every player, not just portals. There is no portal-specific variant.
- A portal built inside a dungeon is an ordinary portal in every respect, including being randomly paired by `Game.ConnectPortals` with any same-tag surface portal — which is usually the point, but it also means a dungeon portal participates in every lockdown and every network rule identically.

**Designer citations:** Inventory.IsTeleportable toolTier>=1000 gate before TeleportAll — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:68860-68880 (:68862-68869) ; Humanoid.IsTeleportable forwarder — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:8791-8794 ; TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 4 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143533-143537 ; InventoryGui m_noteleport badge — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:49462 ; Item tooltip $item_noteleport — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:69755 ; Player piece-placement DungeonBuild check — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:13353 ; GlobalKeys DungeonBuild=34 / TeleportAll=35 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:101306-101307 ; ZoneSystem.GetZone ignores y — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115741-115746 ; Location.Awake interior at +5000y — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133505-133515


**Open questions:**
- Which shipped items actually carry `m_toolTier >= 1000`? Inspector/ObjectDB data. IN-GAME CHECK: enumerate `ObjectDB.instance.m_items` and log every `m_itemData.m_shared.m_name` with `m_toolTier >= 1000`, so the caveat can name them.
- Does the portal piece itself have `m_allowedInDungeons` set on any prefab variant? Inspector data — if true for some variant, `dungeonbuild` is unnecessary for that piece. IN-GAME CHECK: read `GetComponent<Piece>().m_allowedInDungeons` on each portal prefab.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- `canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false` is a parameter of the PRIVATE ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd (:113480); no public SetGlobalKey overload (:115933-115946) exposes it — the RPC path always passes the default true. Session-only writes need reflection/Harmony on GlobalKeyAdd + private SendGlobalKeys(0L).
- Which items carry m_toolTier >= 1000 is prefab data and cannot be confirmed from the decompile; state the code rule (:68862-68868) and verify the item list in-game.
- Player placement check (:13353) sits in Player code that only runs on a client; the server assembly merely contains it.
- Location.Awake places the interior at base.transform.position.y + 5000f (:133510), not zoneCenter.y + 5000.
- The public ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string) routes through RPC_SetGlobalKey which calls GlobalKeyAdd(name) with canSaveToServerOptionKeys defaulted to true (:116022-116029); a session-only write requires reflection into the private GlobalKeyAdd(string,bool) followed by the private SendGlobalKeys(0L) - there is no public parameter to pass.
- Which items carry m_toolTier>=1000 is prefab data not present in the decompile; state the rule ('any item with toolTier>=1000 is never teleportable') rather than naming Flametal unless verified in-game.
- RPC_SetGlobalKey has no sender/admin check (:116022-116029), so the same key is also writable by any client; the server-side reconciler should re-assert the intended value rather than assume it is stable.

**Verifier reasoning:**

### 121. Ironman and Hardcore Rulesets

`lockdown-safety:Ironman and Hardcore Rulesets` · domain **lockdown** · source `lockdown-safety`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Named composite presets that combine the key levers, the disconnect lockdown and the region rules into one-line server personalities, with a single authoritative reconciler.


**How it works:** A ruleset is a named record that expands to a desired-state description, and one level-triggered reconciler drives the world toward it. Useful shapes, each expressible purely in the primitives already established: (1) NO PORTALS AT ALL — `noportals` session-only key plus a permanent force-disconnect of every portal plus a `Game.ConnectPortals` prefix returning false, so even a hacked client has no destination; optionally combined with a destroy-on-arrival cap of zero via the SpawnGovernor hook pair (`ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID,Vector3,int)` postfix to remember the id, `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` postfix to read the now-known prefab and, if it is in `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash`, `zdo.SetOwner(sessionID)` + `ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)` plus a toast) so portals cannot even be built. (2) ONE-WAY OUTBOUND ONLY — every portal keeps a connection but the return leg is nulled; note this is runtime-only because `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` at load writes BOTH directions from the matched hash pair (:77879-77885), so the one-way state must be re-asserted after every world load. (3) TIERED TRAVEL — the biome-region rule with allowed-group sets keyed to boss progression, read from the `defeated_*` global keys which are genuine .db-persisted world state (`Character.OnDeath` writes `m_defeatSetGlobalKey` at :3153-3156). (4) NIGHT CURFEW — the scheduled-window engine on in-game time. (5) RAID SEAL + BOSS BLACKOUT — the raid geofence plus `nobossportals` with the watchdog. (6) CARGO IRONMAN — `teleportall` cleared and documented with the tier-1000 caveat. The reconciler must be single: every rule contributes a desired per-portal state (`Locked | Free | RegionTag(x)`), the reconciler resolves conflicts by a declared precedence (locked beats tagged beats free), and applies the minimum diff. Never let two subsystems write the same portal independently — that is how a portal ends up flapping between states at 1Hz, dirtying the portal chunk on every save.


**Player experience:** An operator sets `Ruleset = Ironman` in the config and the file hot-reloads within five seconds. Every online player gets one centre-screen message: 'Server ruleset changed: Ironman — portals are disabled.' Every portal in the world goes dark and stays dark; attempting to place a new portal consumes nothing and produces a toast 'Portals are disabled on this server.' The `noportals` key also means an unmodified client that somehow reaches a connected portal still gets `$msg_blocked`. Crypt doors keep working, which the ruleset description states explicitly. Under `Tiered`, a player who has not killed Bonemass finds their Swamp portal refuses to pair with their Meadows one and the tags show a tier suffix; after the server-wide Bonemass kill the suffixes merge and the link forms on the next 5s pass.


**Failure modes:**
- Composite rules multiply the conflict surface. Without a single reconciler and a declared precedence, two rules will fight over one portal every tick, producing endless `DirtyPortalObjects` churn and a full portal-chunk rewrite on every save.
- The destroy-on-arrival portal cap destroys a ZDO the placing client already has a live GameObject for; whether that desyncs cleanly, leaves a ghost until the zone reloads, or refunds materials is untested for a Piece/WearNTear-bearing object.
- One-way topologies are silently converted back to two-way by `ZDOMan.ConnectPortals` on every world load (:77879-77885) and rings lose a link entirely because `RegenerateConnectionHashData` gives each ZDO one slot and overwrites source with target at :75474. Any non-pairwise ruleset is runtime-only and MUST be re-asserted post-load.
- Tiered rules keyed on `defeated_*` keys inherit `ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys`' boot-time replay: those keys are ≥ NonServerOption so they live in the .db and are restored by `ZoneSystem.Load` → `GlobalKeyAdd` (:113804-113805), which means any naive 'on key added' hook re-fires for every historical boss kill at every boot. Pre-seed an already-seen set from `OnWorldReady`, exactly as Wonderland's BossDefeatWatch does.
- A ruleset change is a large, sudden, world-wide state change. Applying one without the graceful announcement sequence will strand players far from home with no warning.
- Uninstalling the mod while a restrictive ruleset is engaged leaves the world in whatever state it was in — nulled connections, quarantine tags, and possibly a `noportals` key baked into the .fwl. The uninstall path must be a documented 'set Ruleset = None, wait for the reconciler, then remove'.

### 122. Modifier Badge Honesty

`lockdown-safety:Modifier Badge Honesty` · domain **lockdown** · source `lockdown-safety`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Reconcile the fact that the public server-browser 'modifiers' badge is a boot-time snapshot that a runtime lockdown never updates, so the listing lies about the rules.


**How it works:** The badge payload is `string[] modifiers = m_world.m_startingGlobalKeys.ToArray()` passed to `ZSteamMatchmaking.instance.RegisterServer(...)`, snapshotted at registration time and re-snapshotted only on the registration-retry coroutine (visible at :79457 inside `DelayThenRegisterCoroutine`). Clients render it via `ServerOptionsGUI.GetWorldModifierSummary(m_serverListEntry.m_modifiers, ...)` (:64826-64827). Three distinct dishonesty modes follow. (A) A runtime `SetGlobalKey("noportals")` with the default `canSaveToServerOptionKeys:true` DOES add to `m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113511) but the badge is not re-registered, so the listing keeps saying portals are on for the rest of the session and then permanently says they are off after the next restart — including for scheduled windows that are currently open. (B) A session-only write (`canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false`) never touches `m_startingGlobalKeys`, so the badge never reflects the lockdown at all, ever. (C) A force-disconnect lockdown is not a global key in any form, so the badge can never represent it regardless. There is no supported API to re-register with fresh modifiers at runtime. The honest options are therefore all out-of-band: (1) rewrite `ZNet.instance.m_ServerName` to carry the state — but that is also snapshotted at RegisterServer, so it has the same staleness; (2) push the truth through channels that ARE live — a `ShowMessage` on `OnNewPeer`, a Discord webhook status message (Wonderland's `DiscordWebhook.Send`, fire-and-forget with a shared static HttpClient), a status file/endpoint, and the `Heartbeat` log line; (3) document in the server description that portal rules are dynamic and where to check; (4) if the operator insists the badge be truthful for a long-lived ruleset, set the key persistently and restart once so the boot-time snapshot is correct, and accept that transient windows are never represented. Additionally: `ServerOptionsGUI.GetWorldModifierSummary` returns the literal string `"Error!"` when its `m_presets` is null, so any server-side use of it for a status report must be guarded.


**Player experience:** A player browsing the server list sees 'Portals: on' and joins expecting to portal home, then discovers the nightly maintenance window has every portal dark. With the mitigation, the moment they connect they get a top-left message: 'Portal network is currently CLOSED (nightly window, reopens 06:00).' The Discord channel carries the same state, and `/status` on the operator's side prints the authoritative rule set. The badge itself still says what it said at boot and is documented as doing so.


**Failure modes:**
- There is genuinely no runtime re-registration API. Anything short of a restart leaves the badge stale; this is a limitation to be communicated, not engineered around.
- Setting the key persistently to make the badge honest means permanently editing the world's `m_startingGlobalKeys`, which survives uninstalling the mod — trading one honesty problem for a world-integrity problem.
- `GetWorldModifierSummary` returns `"Error!"` if `m_presets` is null (prefab not initialised), so a naive status report can publish that string.
- The `OnNewPeer` announcement is the only channel guaranteed to reach a joining player, and it competes with every other join-time message; a player who dismisses it has no way to re-query state from a vanilla client except by walking to a portal.
- A force-disconnect lockdown is invisible to every metadata channel by construction. Operators will forget it is on.

Whether Steam's master server propagates a live SetGameTags change without a re-heartbeat is an in-game check. But the central premise 'there is no supported API to re-register with fresh modifiers at runtime' is refuted for the Steam backend: ZSteamMatchmaking.RegisterServer is public (:85571), re-callable, calls UnregisterServer (SetAdvertiseServerActive(false) :85684-85687) then SteamGameServer.SetGameTags with the compact 'm' modifier dictionary (:85579-85586) and re-enables advertising; the vanilla client's dedicated-server list decodes exactly that 'm' tag (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:86288-86315). A server mod can call it with any string[] - including the live global keys, or a synthetic 'noportals' entry to represent a force-disconnect lockdown - and the Steam master server reflects it on its next heartbeat. ### 123. Destination Safety Validator

`lockdown-safety:Destination Safety Validator` · domain **lockdown** · source `lockdown-safety`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A purely procedural server-side check that refuses to wire a portal to an unsafe coordinate — underwater, in lava, underground, inside a dungeon interior, or off the map edge.


**How it works:** Every collider-based helper is dead server-side (the reference position is pinned to (1e6,0,1e6) at :100465 so no Heightmap collider exists near real coordinates; `ZoneSystem.FindFloor` :115604 raycasts against `m_solidRayMask` and silently returns `height = 0f, false`; `GetSolidHeight`, `GetGroundHeight`, `IsBlocked`, `GetGroundData` and the instance `IsLava(Vector3)` :115647 all return their no-hit fallbacks WITHOUT throwing or logging). The validator must therefore be pure `WorldGenerator` math plus the one static lava test. The checks, in order of cheapness: (1) OFF-MAP — reject when `x*x + z*z > 110250000f` (`WorldGenerator.waterEdgeSqr`); `GetBiomeHeight` returns `-2f * GetHeightMultiplier()` = -400 beyond 10500m. (2) INTERIOR — reject when `pos.y > 3000f`, which is vanilla's own test (`Character.InInterior(Vector3)` :4538-4541); dungeon interiors are instantiated at `zoneCenter + 5000y` by `Location.Awake` (:133505-133515). (3) UNDERWATER — reject when `WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(pos.x, pos.z) < 30f` (sea level is `ZoneSystem.m_waterLevel = 30f`). (4) LAVA — reject when `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap(pos, 0.6f)` (:115637-115645), which is static, biome-gates to Ashlands first and then tests `mask.a > lavaValue` from `GetBiomeHeight`; NEVER use `ZoneSystem.instance.IsLava` because it goes through the dead raycast path and returns `defaultTrue` on a miss. (5) UNDERGROUND — reject when `pos.y < WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(pos.x, pos.z) - tolerance`; note this is blind to player terraforming and to a location's own flattening so a ±2m tolerance is mandatory. (6) SLOPE — reject when `WorldGenerator.instance.GetNormal(new Vector2(x,z), r).y` is below a threshold, or use `GetTerrainDelta(center, radius, out delta, out slopeDir)` (:152364-152390), which is the exact roughness test vanilla uses for location siting. A fast pre-filter for (3) is the `AltBiomeWorldData` grid: `ZNet.World.m_biomeData.PointHeights[WorldSpaceToMapSpace(x), WorldSpaceToMapSpace(z)]` is an O(1) 12m-resolution cached height. Crucially, the validator governs what the mod WIRES, not what the client does on arrival. What the client does is fixed: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` computes `pos = targetPos + (targetRot * Vector3.forward) * m_exitDistance + Vector3.up` (:143542-143545) and passes `distantTeleport: true` (:143546). With `distantTeleport:true` the teleport can never strand — `Player.UpdateTeleport` force-lands at `ZoneSystem.GetSolidHeight(target) + 0.5f` at t=15s (:15360-15366). With `distantTeleport:false` (which vanilla portals never use, but a mod-issued forced teleport might) a floor-find failure instead rubber-bands the player to `m_teleportFromPos` with a misleading `$msg_portal_blocked` (:15368-15374). So: always use `distantTeleport:true` for any mod-issued teleport, and use the validator to avoid wiring somewhere the player would merely be *unhappy* to arrive, since arrival itself is guaranteed.


**Player experience:** Invisible in the normal case. Where it bites: an admin tries to wire a hub to a coordinate the validator rejects and gets a console line 'Refused: destination at (1234, 18.2, -5610) is below sea level (terrain height 18.2, water 30)'. A server-fabricated anchor portal is never placed in an Ashlands lava field or 40m inside a mountain. A player pointed at a far unvisited region still experiences the standard vanilla behaviour: black screen, at least 8 seconds, then arrival — and if the zone is slow to generate, a hard landing on solid ground at 15 seconds rather than a fall or a stranding.


**Failure modes:**
- `ZoneSystem.instance.GetGroundHeight/GetSolidHeight/FindFloor/IsBlocked/IsLava(Vector3)` all COMPILE and RUN on a dedicated server and silently return their no-hit fallback. A `GetGroundHeight` that hands back `p.y` unchanged looks like a valid answer and is the single easiest way to ship a broken validator.
- `WorldGenerator` is blind to player terraforming and to location flattening, so a portal on a levelled building platform can be misjudged as underground and a portal in a dug-out pit as above ground. Tolerances must be generous and the validator must be advisory for existing portals, blocking only for mod-fabricated destinations.
- `mask.a` from `GetHeight(x, z, out Color mask)` means lava ONLY in the Ashlands; in Mistlands and Deep North that channel carries an unrelated value. Always go through `IsLavaPreHeightmap`, which biome-gates first.
- `GetTerrainDelta` uses `UnityEngine.Random` for its 10 samples (:152364-152390) and is therefore non-deterministic between calls — do not use it for a stable accept/reject boundary without averaging.
- The exit offset uses the DESTINATION portal's own `m_exitDistance` (a compiled Inspector field, :143413) and `+Vector3.up` — the mod cannot tune it, so a destination validated as safe at the ZDO position can still put the player 1m forward into a wall. Validate the exit point, not just the anchor.
- `ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask` (:113424) omits the 'vehicle' layer that `BaseAI` explicitly adds (:25909), so even client-side `FindFloor` cannot see a ship hull — landing a traveller on a deck is not something vanilla's teleport can do at all.

### 124. Mass-Rewrite Spike Control and Save-Bloat Budget

`lockdown-safety:Mass-Rewrite Spike Control and Save-Bloat Budget` · domain **lockdown** · source `lockdown-safety`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Bound the per-tick portal writes and the resulting network and save cost, because a naive world-wide lockdown floods every peer's sync queue and forces a full portal-chunk rewrite.


**How it works:** THE NETWORK COST. `ZDO.SetConnection` bumps DataRevision (:73660), which makes `ZDOPeer.ShouldSend` (:76003-76015) true for that ZDO for every peer. `ZDOMan.SendZDOs` performs NO delta encoding — it writes uid + OwnerRevision + DataRevision + owner + position (38 bytes) followed by a full `ZDO.Serialize` of every field, per peer, per send (:77053-77062) — and `SendZDOToPeers2` services ONE peer per `ZDOMan.Update` behind a 0.05s timer (:76837-76861) against a 10240-byte send-queue cap (:77010-77016). A portal ZDO carries prefab, position, rotation, connection, `s_tag` and `s_tagauthor`, so roughly 80-120 bytes. Nulling 500 portals is ~50KB per peer, i.e. ~5 full sweeps, i.e. ~0.25s per peer serialised round-robin — and `ForceSendZDO` pushes all of them to the HEAD of every peer's queue, displacing legitimate traffic for that whole period. MITIGATION: process at most N portals per tick (Wonderland's `StructureUpkeep` caps routed broadcasts at 256 per sweep after a first pass over a long-running world turned up thousands of dirty ZDOs at once); use `ForceSendZDO` only for portals within a peer's likely interest radius and let the rest ride the normal sweep; and exploit idempotence — `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection` returns false and writes nothing when type AND target are both unchanged (:74951-74960), so `ZDO.SetConnection` neither bumps the revision nor generates traffic, making a high-frequency re-assert loop genuinely free as long as nothing has drifted. THE SAVE COST. `DirtyPortalObjects` has NO per-portal granularity: one `SetConnection(Portal, ...)` anywhere sets the flag (:73661-73664) and `GetSaveClonePerChunk` then deep-clones EVERY portal in the world into the ChunkPortal bucket (:77621-77632), with no `Persistent` filter, on the main thread inside the save freeze. So the marginal save cost of locking one portal equals the cost of locking all of them; there is no incentive to batch for save reasons, only for network reasons. Budget accordingly: measure `m_portalObjects` total count at `OnWorldReady` and surface it in the Heartbeat line, because clone cost scales with it. THE CPU COST per write is negligible — `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73756) so no re-bucketing happens, and `IncreaseDataRevision` → `SetDirtySector` is skipped for the portal path. The real per-write tail is that `SetDirtyChunks` inserts up to 4 ChunkIndex entries per dirty persistent ZDO, which portals avoid.


**Player experience:** Operator-facing. Without the budget, engaging a world-wide lockdown on a 500-portal server produces a visible multi-second hitch for every connected player — position updates stall, creatures freeze, and the server log shows the send queue saturated. With the budget, the lockdown rolls out over ~10 seconds portal by portal (which is fine, because the announcement already gave a grace period) and nobody notices anything except the portals going dark in waves.


**Failure modes:**
- A rolling lockdown means a window during which some portals are locked and some are not — a player can beat the rollout by sprinting to a not-yet-locked gate. If atomicity matters, set the `noportals` key FIRST (one small broadcast, instant, covers all vanilla clients) and then roll out the disconnect behind it.
- `ForceSendZDO(ZDOID)` pushes to every peer; the single-peer overload `ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID id)` (:77714) is the targeted form and is internally server-guarded. Using the broadcast form for hundreds of portals is the main amplifier.
- Idempotent re-asserts are free ONLY when nothing changed. A tamper loop where a client keeps writing the connection back turns the re-assert into a real write every tick, with full serialisation cost per peer. Rate-limit the response and escalate to a kick rather than a write war.
- There is no way to save a subset of portals. Any portal mutation costs a full portal-chunk clone at the next save. On a very large world that clone happens inside the synchronous `PrepareSave` and is directly additive to the save freeze.
- Measuring the wrong thing: `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` allocates a fresh `List<ZDO>` on every call (:77648-77656). Calling it per tick to check the budget is itself a cost; use the live `GetPortals()` dictionary (:77643-77646) for hot paths as `PositionWatch` does.

- What is the real serialized size of one portal ZDO on the wire? IN-GAME CHECK: instrument `ZDO.Serialize` for a portal and log the package size, to replace the 80-120 byte estimate with a measurement.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Portal writes do NOT avoid SetDirtyChunks: IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) -> ZDOMan.SetDirtySector (:76694-76699) -> SetDirtyChunks(GetSectorIndex()) for every Persistent ZDO; only ZDO.SetSector (:73752-73756) has the portal early-return. Each portal write dirties its spatial chunk, and AddObjectsPerChunk re-clones every persistent ZDO in every dirty chunk (:77556-77578). Save cost scales with distinct chunks touched per save interval — batching DOES matter for save reasons.
- 'Marginal save cost of locking one portal equals locking all' holds only for the ChunkPortal file; the spatial-chunk clone cost is per touched chunk.
- The idempotent re-assert loop is free only if SetOwner is not re-issued each tick; ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925, 2 s) flips ownership near players and OwnerRevision bumps (:73842-) re-trigger ShouldSend.
- ForceSendZDO reaches peers that have never received the portal (ShouldSend true on miss, :76003-76015) — the flood is world-wide per peer, confirming the need for interest-radius filtering.
- ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) always calls ZDOMan.SetDirtySector -> SetDirtyChunks for Persistent ZDOs (:76694-76722); portals are NOT exempt. Each portal write dirties the portal's regular chunk (4 ChunkIndex sizes), and AddObjectsPerChunk re-clones and re-saves any chunk in m_dirtyChunks[0] (:77553-77556). Save cost of a world-wide lockdown = ChunkPortal clone + one full chunk rewrite per distinct portal sector touched.
- Consequently there IS a save-cost reason to minimise writes: rely on ZDOExtraData.SetConnection's no-op return (:74951-74960) so only portals whose connection actually changes get a revision bump, and never 'refresh' tags/connections that already match. Pacing alone does not reduce the dirty-chunk union.
- SendZDOToPeers2 cadence: one peer per ZDOMan.Update call, 0.05 s wait between rounds (:76837-76861); per-peer throughput is bounded by the 10240-byte send-queue cap per SendZDOs call, not by a per-peer timer.
- ForceSendZDO(ZDOID) (:77706-77712) queues to every peer irrespective of distance and AddForceSendZdos prepends them (:77263-77285); the per-peer overload ForceSendZDO(long,ZDOID) (:77714-77724) is the tool for the 'interest radius only' mitigation.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Network-cost claims verified: ZDO.SetConnection bumps DataRevision and sets DirtyPortalObjects (:73656-73666); ZDOPeer.ShouldSend is a pure revision gate and returns true for a ZDO the peer has never received (:76003-76015); SendZDOs writes uid/OwnerRevision/DataRevision/owner/position then a full ZDO.Serialize per ZDO with no delta (:77053-77062) under the 10240-byte / 2048-byte-minimum queue cap (:77010-77016); SendZDOToPeers2 services one peer per Update after a 0.05 s inter-round wait (:76837-76861); AddForceSendZdos inserts force-sent ZDOs at index 0 for every peer regardless of distance (:77263-77285), and portals are only otherwise synced through FindObjects for a peer's near sectors (:77367-77382). ZDOExtraData.SetConnection returns false on unchanged type+target (:74951-74960). Save-cost claims: GetSaveClonePerChunk clones every portal into ChunkPortal when DirtyPortalObjects is set, no Persistent filter (:77621-77632); AddObjectsPerChunk excludes portals from spatial chunks (:77572) and only clones chunks in m_dirtyChunks (:77556-77559). REFUTED SUB-CLAIM: 'IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector is skipped for the portal path... SetDirtyChunks ... which portals avoid' is wrong. ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) unconditionally calls ZDOMan.SetDirtySector(this), which for any Persistent ZDO calls SetDirtyChunks(zdo.GetSectorIndex()) (:76694-76699, :76709-76722) — GetSectorIndex is computed from position (:73776-73779) and the portal-prefab early return is in SetSector (:73752-73756), a different method. So every portal connection/tag write also marks the portal's SPATIAL chunk (up to 4 ChunkIndex sizes) dirty, and the next save re-clones and rewrites every persistent non-portal ZDO in each such chunk. A world-wide lockdown over 500 portals in ~500 distinct zones therefore dirties a large fraction of the world's chunk files, not just ChunkPortal — the save cost DOES scale with the number of distinct chunks touched, which reverses the option's 'no incentive to batch for save reasons' conclusion (spreading writes across save intervals bounds the per-save clone set). Additionally, the 'free re-assert loop' is only free if it does not also call SetOwner each tick: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925) reassigns ownership every 2 s near players, and SetOwner bumps OwnerRevision -> ShouldSend true, so an ownership-flapping loop generates traffic.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Network analysis verified: ZDOPeer.ShouldSend is a pure revision compare (:76003-76015); SendZDOs writes uid+OwnerRevision+DataRevision+owner+position then a full ZDO.Serialize per ZDO, no delta (:77043-77062), behind a 10240-byte queue cap with a 2048 minimum (:77018-77026); AddForceSendZdos inserts forced ZDOs at index 0 for every peer that has them queued (:77263-77285) and ForceSendZDO(id) adds to every peer regardless of distance (:77706-77712); ZDOExtraData.SetConnection is a no-op on unchanged type+target (:74951-74960) so ZDO.SetConnection neither bumps revision nor sets DirtyPortalObjects (:73656-73666); GetSaveClonePerChunk clones every portal when DirtyPortalObjects is set, no Persistent filter (:77621-77632); ZDO.SetSector early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73756). One claim is false and it flips the save-cost conclusion: ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision (:73832-73840) unconditionally calls ZDOMan.SetDirtySector, which for any Persistent ZDO - portals included - calls SetDirtyChunks and inserts up to 4 ChunkIndex entries (:76694-76722). AddObjectsPerChunk only clones chunks present in m_dirtyChunks[0] (:77553-77556), so every portal touched additionally forces a full re-clone and rewrite of that portal's regular terrain chunk (all non-portal persistent ZDOs in it) at the next save. A world-wide lockdown across N distinct sectors therefore dirties up to N regular chunks - potentially most of the world's chunk files - not just the ChunkPortal bucket. The 'no incentive to batch for save reasons' conclusion is wrong in direction: pacing does not shrink the dirty-chunk union, but minimising the number of portals actually written (idempotent no-op writes, touching only portals whose state differs) matters for save cost as much as for network cost. Cadence nit: SendZDOToPeers2 services one peer per Update call with a 0.05 s pause between full rounds (:76837-76861), not 0.05 s per peer.

### 125. Invariant Assertion Harness and Panic Restore

`lockdown-safety:Invariant Assertion Harness and Panic Restore` · domain **lockdown** · source `lockdown-safety`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A runtime self-check that verifies a fixed list of never-violate invariants every tick and, on a violation it cannot repair, restores the vault and disables itself loudly rather than continuing to corrupt the world.


**How it works:** The harness runs from the subsystem `OnUpdate` at 1Hz using the live `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals()` dictionary (zero-alloc) and a full `GetPortalList()` pass at a slower 30s cadence. THE INVARIANTS, each with its assertion and its repair. (I1) NO ORPHANED VAULT — every vault record's two endpoints resolve to a live portal within tolerance; on failure, drop the record and log (a portal was demolished). (I2) LOCK COMPLETENESS — while a lockdown is engaged, every portal in its scope has `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal).IsNone()`; repair by re-nulling with SetOwner + SetConnection + DataRevision bump, and count the repair as a tamper event. (I3) NO SELF-LOOP — no portal's connection equals its own `m_uid`; vanilla's reconciler tolerates self-loops indefinitely (phase 1 never checks reciprocity, :100601) but `RegenerateConnectionHashData` erases them at save (:75472-75475), so a self-loop is a silent data-loss bug. Repair by nulling. (I4) NO DANGLING TARGET — every non-None connection resolves via `ZDOMan.GetZDO` to a live ZDO; `RegenerateConnectionHashData` drops unresolvable connections at save (:75468), so a dangling link is lost at restart anyway. Repair by nulling and letting the vault or vanilla re-pair. (V5) NO DUPLICATE PORTAL ENTRY — `GetPortalList().Count` equals the count of distinct `m_uid` values; a mismatch means a portal was repositioned across a 64m sector boundary, because `AddIfPortal` (:77732-77752) adds to the bucket for the CURRENT sector without removing the old one while `ZDO.SetSector` is a no-op for portals (:73752-73756), and `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76976-76986) then looks it up by the recomputed sector and permanently leaks the other entry. THERE IS NO REPAIR — this is unrecoverable corruption of the portal registry. The only correct response is to assert loudly and to enforce the hard rule: NEVER call `SetPosition` on a portal ZDO; destroy and recreate instead. (I6) NO STALE ZDO REFERENCES — the mod caches ZDOID values only, never `ZDO` object references, across ticks, because `ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO` calls `ZDOPool.Release(zdo)` → `Reset()` which sets `m_uid = ZDOID.None` and the pooled object can be handed out for an unrelated new ZDO; vanilla itself violates this in `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` (:100681-100698). Assert by re-resolving every cached id through `GetZDO` before use. (I7) DIRTY-FLAG DISCIPLINE — every tag write is followed by `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()`; assert by checking a write-counter against a dirty-call counter in debug builds. (I8) NO TARGET BIT ON LIVE PORTALS — no live portal carries `ConnectionType.Portal | Target` (0x11), because `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)` requires exact type equality (:75094-75102) and would report such a portal as unconnected, causing vanilla to re-pair it. (I9) SINGLE WRITER — exactly one subsystem writes any given portal per tick; assert with a per-tick written-set and log a hard error on a second write. (I10) NO PORTAL AT AN OUT-OF-RANGE COORDINATE — `ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex` clamps any zone beyond ~±16320m to Sector 0, the same bucket the server's own pinned reference position maps to; assert no portal position exceeds that. PANIC RESTORE: on any repeated unrepairable violation, or on an unhandled exception inside the lockdown engine, the harness restores every vault record, clears the lockdown state, sets a `Disabled` flag that all subsystems check, logs `[TortalPortal] PANIC: <invariant> violated N times, lockdown disabled and wiring restored`, and posts to Discord. Failing open (portals work) is always the right failure direction for a portal mod; failing closed strands players.


**Player experience:** Operator-facing and, when it works, invisible. A cheating client that keeps writing a connection back to a locked portal produces `[SECURITY:LockTamper] <SteamID64> - portal (1204,-88) relinked 12 times in 60s`, and after a threshold either the player is kicked via `ZNet.instance.Kick(hostName)` or the mod stops fighting and logs that the lock is contested. If the mod itself malfunctions, players find their portals working normally and the operator finds one loud PANIC line explaining exactly which invariant broke — rather than a silently half-locked world that scrambles itself at the next save.


**Failure modes:**
- I5 has no repair. Once a portal is duplicated in `m_portalObjects` the registry is permanently corrupt for that ZDO and `Game.ConnectPortals` will keep processing a dead entry after it is destroyed. The harness can only detect and refuse to make it worse.
- A 1Hz full-list assertion on a very large world is itself a cost; tier the checks (cheap invariants at 1Hz over the live dictionary, expensive ones at 30s over an allocated list).
- Panic-restoring the vault while a legitimate scheduled lockdown is mid-rollout will unlock everything and the scheduler's reconciler will immediately re-lock it, producing a flap. The panic flag must be sticky until an operator clears it.
- Kicking on tamper escalates a cheating problem into a moderation problem and can false-positive on a legitimate `Game.RPC_SetConnection` from a client racing vanilla's own pairing. Require a sustained pattern, and prefer logging over kicking by default.
- Asserting I6 by re-resolving every cached id every tick costs a dictionary lookup per portal per tick — acceptable, but it must not be done inside the `ZDO.SetOwner` prefix, which is a global hot path.
- The harness cannot assert anything about client state. A client that has stale ZDO data believes a portal is still connected and the server has no way to know or to force a refresh short of `ForceSendZDO`.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- V5 assertion form is wrong: after HandleDestroyedZDO leaks a bucket entry, the leaked object has m_uid = ZDOID.None (ZDO.Reset :73540) and, once the pool re-issues it (ZDOPool.Get :78297-78310), carries the uid of an unrelated new ZDO — the distinct-uid count then still matches. Assert instead `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(entry.m_uid) == entry && Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(entry.GetPrefab())` for every entry of GetPortalList().
- V5 root cause: the duplicate is created by ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData, which calls InternalSetPosition then AddIfPortal (:77128-77132) on every client update; a server-side SetPosition (:73729-73735) never calls AddIfPortal, so it does not duplicate immediately — it misfiles the entry, HandleDestroyedZDO then fails to remove it, and the next client ZDOData for that portal creates the duplicate. The 'never SetPosition a portal' rule stands, with that mechanism.
- I2 tamper attribution cannot come from a 1 Hz poll: only ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg) (:77076) knows which peer wrote the connection (ZDO.Deserialize writes connections straight into ZDOExtraData.SetConnection, bypassing ZDO.SetConnection and SetDirtyPortals, :74206-74232). A Harmony prefix/postfix on RPC_ZDOData is required before any SteamID can be logged or kicked. Without the pairing veto from Park-and-Release technique B, vanilla's own pass 2 (:100607-100621) re-pairs a nulled portal every 5 s and would be counted as a 'tamper event' and, past the threshold, kick an innocent owner.
- I4 duplicates vanilla: pass 1 already nulls any connection whose target ZDO is missing within 5 s (:100598-100604). Keep it as a consistency check but it is not a mod-only concern.
- I8 is purely defensive: vanilla never writes a Target-flagged type into runtime s_connections (Target appears only in s_connectionsHashData, :75472-75475, and RPC_SetTag/ConnectPortals write plain Portal). It can only catch the mod's own bugs.
- I7: in the common case a tag mutation on a connected portal is followed within 5 s by pass 1's SetConnection(None) (:100603) which already calls SetDirtyPortals (:73656-73665); the loss only occurs for an already-unconnected portal. Still call SetDirtyPortals — the point stands.
- I10's consequence is not registry corruption: an out-of-range portal lands in the Sector-0 bucket that the server's own ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects visits (:82268-82276 -> FindObjects :77367-77382 includes m_portalObjects[Sector 0]) and, once IsActiveAreaLoaded is true at the pinned ref pos (:114054-114069), it is instantiated headless (TeleportWorld.Awake registers RPCs and InvokeRepeating UpdatePortal). Assert it, but describe the effect correctly.
- Kick path: ZNet.Kick(string) -> InternalKick parses a PlatformUserID and looks up the peer by host name (:81658-81667 and InternalKick body); pass the peer's host name, not the player name. The kick/threshold half of this option is reactive detection, not enforcement.
- Enforcement honesty: the repairs (re-nulling) are server writes to a server-owned field and are enforced against vanilla clients; a modded client that owns the ZDO can re-write the connection in its ZDOData (accepted when its DataRevision is higher, :77107-77118) and can teleport itself regardless, so the harness only narrows the window.
- V5: a server-side ZDO.SetPosition on a portal does not duplicate the entry by itself (SetSector :73752-73756 is a no-op so AddIfPortal is never re-run); it mis-files the entry, and the duplicate appears when AddIfPortal runs again on the next RPC_ZDOData for that ZDO (:77132). The leaked entry after HandleDestroyedZDO is a pooled ZDO with m_uid==None (Reset :73536-73549 clears m_uid/Valid but not m_prefab) that GetPortalList keeps returning - add asserts 'entry.Valid', 'entry.m_uid != None', 'ZDOMan.GetZDO(entry.m_uid) == entry' and 'PortalPrefabHash.Contains(entry.GetPrefab())' to the distinct-uid count.
- V5: repair IS possible - remove the stale entry from the private readonly Dictionary m_portalObjects (:76039) by reflection (the dictionary object is mutable). The 'never SetPosition a portal' rule remains good policy; if a move is unavoidable, reflection-move the bucket entry in the same call.
- I2: do not count every relink as a client tamper. Vanilla's own pass 2 (:100607-100621) and the staged force-write in ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) relink nulled portals every 5s, and for client-owned portals that write arrives through Game.RPC_SetConnection (:100649-100659) executed by the vanilla client. Tamper attribution is only valid once pairing is vetoed (Routing Kernel L1/L2) and should attribute via the RPC_ZDOData sender socket (:77080-77140 region), not the ZDO owner field.
- I2/I4 repairs: a no-bump idempotent re-null does not converge a client whose DataRevision tied with the server's (server :77108-77118 rejects num4<=DataRevision; client symmetric; ZDOPeer.ShouldSend only re-sends when the server's revision exceeds the peer record). Force a real DataRevision bump (e.g. Set a scratch int) whenever a client-side drift is observed.
- I4 is redundant with vanilla: pass 1 already nulls a connection whose target is null (:100598-100604) every 5s; keep the assert, drop the repair or make it force-immediate.
- Line refs: AddToCurrentlyConnectingPortals is :100681-100688 and ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698; SectorToIndex(int,int) body is :115762-115775.

Several assertions, however, are mis-specified or attribute vanilla behaviour to attackers, and the tamper/kick path is reactive detection that requires a hook the option does not name.
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited anchor exists at (or within 2 lines of) the cited line and the invariants are grounded in real code paths I read. Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 (SERVER :100594-100606) tests only target==null || target.tag!=my.tag || target.connection==None, never reciprocity, so a self-loop survives runtime (I3 correct). ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75477) skips connections whose target does not resolve (:75468) and, for a self-loop, overwrites the ZDO's own slot with Portal|Target at :75474 so at load ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77891) never lists it among Portal-typed entries; the self-loop is gone after a restart (I3/I4 correct). ZDOPool.Release -> ZDO.Reset (:78289-78294, :73536-73549) sets m_uid=None and Valid=false and pushes the object on a free stack, and ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO (:76963-77000) never clears Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals, so the raw ZDO refs cached at :100681-100698 are a genuine vanilla use-after-release (I6 correct). ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID (:75094-75102) requires exact type equality, and ZDO.Deserialize (:74219-74233) writes whatever ConnectionType byte a peer sends via ZDOExtraData.SetConnection, so a live Portal|Target entry is injectable by a modified client and vanilla would treat that portal as unconnected (I8 correct). ZDO.SetConnection (:73656-73666) sets DirtyPortalObjects only on change; a tag-only Set never does, and GetSaveClonePerChunk saves the portal chunk only if DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77636) (I7 correct). ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex (:115762-115775) clamps sectorX/Y outside [-256,255] to Sector 0, the same bucket the (1e6,0,1e6) pin of Game.FixedUpdate (:100465) resolves to (I10 correct). ZDOMan.GetPortals (:77643-77646) returns the live dictionary (zero-alloc claim correct). V5 is real but its mechanism is misdescribed: ZDO.SetPosition -> InternalSetPosition -> SetSector (:73729-73762) is a no-op for portal prefabs, so a server-side SetPosition alone produces a MIS-FILED entry (still in the old bucket), not a duplicate; the duplicate appears only when AddIfPortal is invoked again for that ZDO, which happens on every RPC_ZDOData receipt (:77132) and in CreateNewZDO (:76689) - AddIfPortal only checks the CURRENT-sector bucket for Contains (:77738-77744). Then HandleDestroyedZDO removes from the recomputed sector only (:76982), and the stale entry is a pooled/reset ZDO that GetPortalList keeps returning (m_uid None, m_prefab NOT reset by Reset) and that ConnectPortals will feed into FindRandomUnconnectedPortal with tag "". Also 'THERE IS NO REPAIR' is wrong: m_portalObjects is a private readonly Dictionary (:76039) whose contents are mutable via reflection. I2's tamper attribution is wrong as stated: a relink of a nulled portal is produced by vanilla itself (pass 2 at :100607-100621 and the staged force-write in ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698, delivered to client-owned portals through Game.RPC_SetConnection which vanilla clients execute) unless the lockdown also vetoes pairing; counting those as SteamID tamper events would kick innocent players. Revision tie split-brain: server write N+1 and client-owner write N+1 are mutually rejected (server ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77108-77118 num4<=DataRevision; client copy identical), and ZDOPeer.ShouldSend (:75990-76000 region) re-sends only when the server's revision exceeds the peer record, so an idempotent no-bump re-assertion leaves the client holding its own value; a repair must force a DataRevision bump past the client's. Enforcement is honest: every invariant is of the form 'is this ROUTE field in the state the server wants', which the server owns.
