### 126. RULED OUT — Moment-of-Transit Veto and Per-Portal Item Policy

`lockdown-safety:RULED OUT — Moment-of-Transit Veto and Per-Portal Item Policy` · domain **lockdown** · source `lockdown-safety`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **not-enforceable** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


There is no server-side hook on the act of teleporting and no networked per-portal setting of any kind, so per-transit approval, per-portal ore rules and PIN gates are all impossible without a client mod.


**How it works:** THE TRANSIT VETO. `TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player)` has exactly ONE call site in the entire assembly: `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter(Collider)` at :143679, which requires `colliderIn.GetComponent<Player>() != null` AND `Player.m_localPlayer == component` (:143673-143681). Three independent conditions make it unreachable server-side: no portal GameObject is ever instantiated (the SERVER build's `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `ZNet.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick at :100465, a line absent from the client's `Game.FixedUpdate`, so `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` :82268 only ever builds objects in an empty sector 1e6m out), no Player GameObject is ever instantiated (`Player.Awake` is what fills `s_players`, :10032-10035), and `Player.m_localPlayer` is null. `TeleportWorld.Teleport` is `public` and appears in any reflection dump, which makes it look callable — it is not usefully callable: `m_nview` would be null, `player.Message` needs `MessageHud.instance`, and `Game.instance.IncrementPlayerStat` writes the server's own throwaway profile. The server sees no packet either: the whole decision and the whole move happen inside the traveller's own process. PER-PORTAL ITEM POLICY. Every public field of `TeleportWorld` is a plain Inspector-compiled value with zero ZDO backing and zero RPC: `m_activationRange` (:143411), `m_exitDistance` (:143413), `m_proximityRoot` (:143415), the two colours (:143418, :143421), `m_target_found` (:143423), `m_model` (:143425), `m_connected` (:143427), `m_allowAllItems` (:143429), `m_hoverOffset` (:143431). A Harmony write to `m_allowAllItems` on the server mutates a copy no client will ever read. The only ZDO-backed fields the class touches are `ZDOVars.s_tag` (:78617) and `s_tagauthor` (:78619), plus the `ConnectionType.Portal` connection. PIN GATES. A PIN requires prompting the player at the moment of transit and refusing the move — both halves are inside the client-only path above. TortalPortal's own PIN implementation is entirely client-side: `SecurityPatch.CanConfigure` reads `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().GetPlayerID()` (a local profile that on a dedicated server is a throwaway `new PlayerProfile()` named 'Stranger' created in `Game.Awake` :100047), and `TeleportWorld_SetText_Prefix` writes the PIN key from the client. THE CARGO AUDIT. Even observing what a traveller carried is impossible: no character ZDO carries item data. `ZDOVars.s_items` is written by exactly one live code path, `Container.Save()` (:122294-122300); `Player.Save(ZPackage)` serialises inventory, skills and recipes into `PlayerProfile.m_playerData` which goes only to that client's own .fch (:14091-14170, :105706-105711); and `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles()` (:79653-79670) merely tells each client to save its own disk file and returns nothing. THE ONLY THING THAT IS SERVER-ENFORCEABLE at transit granularity is the destination's existence — nulling the connection, covered by the Force-Disconnect option. THE ONLY PARTIAL WORKAROUND for per-portal settings is `ZNetView.LoadFields()` (:82669, client copy assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82898), which is vanilla on both builds and reflects over every public instance field of every component on the instantiated prefab, overriding from the ZDO under keys `"HasFields"`, `"HasFields<TypeName>"` and `"<TypeName>.<FieldName>"`. Writing three ints to a portal ZDO would in principle give per-portal `TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems` on a 100% vanilla client — but it is client-honoured, it only applies at instantiation (`ZNetView.Awake` :82631, so a player standing at the portal is unaffected until they leave and return), and it is UNVERIFIED in-game. It is listed here as a lead, not as a shipped capability.


**Player experience:** Nothing. These features cannot be built, and the honest documentation line is: 'TortalPortal Lite cannot approve or refuse an individual teleport, cannot set per-portal item rules, and cannot ask for a PIN. It can make a portal have nowhere to go, which stops the teleport entirely — including for modified clients.'


**Failure modes:**
- Attempting a Harmony patch on `TeleportWorld.Teleport` or `TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter` on a dedicated server compiles cleanly, applies cleanly, and never fires once. This is the single most common wasted effort in this problem space.
- Attempting to patch `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` is equally dead: it is registered on the portal's ZNetView in `Awake` (:143448), the server never instantiates one, and `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` drops ZDO-targeted RPCs because `ZNetScene.FindInstance(zdo)` is always null (:83646-83663, :82229).
- Setting `m_allowAllItems` server-side via reflection appears to succeed and changes nothing observable, which reads as a subtle bug rather than an impossibility.
- Any 'portal toll' or 'cargo check' feature must be redesigned around an adjacent Container ZDO (`s_items`, readable and writable) rather than the traveller's inventory.
- The PIN concept can only degrade to an all-or-nothing per-portal lock (connection nulled / restored), which is a different product and must be named differently.

This is the single highest-value experiment available and would partially un-rule-out per-portal item policy (as a client-honoured setting). IN-GAME CHECK: write the three ZDO ints from the server onto one portal, have a player leave and re-enter the area carrying ore, and see whether the transit is allowed.
- Does `TeleportWorld` sit on the portal prefab root or a child, and does `LoadFields`' `GetComponentsInChildren<MonoBehaviour>` reach it? IN-GAME CHECK: enumerate `GetComponents<MonoBehaviour>()` on the portal prefab client-side and log the type names, which also confirms the exact `HasFields<TypeName>` key.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- 'It can make a portal have nowhere to go, which stops the teleport entirely — including for modified clients' is false. Movement is client-authoritative: Player.TeleportTo runs entirely in the owning client (:15302-15327) and a modded client can call it, or write any position into its own character ZDO, without any portal connection at all. Nulling the connection stops VANILLA clients only.
- The server is not entirely without a lever after the fact: the vanilla client registers Chat 'RPC_TeleportPlayer' on ZRoutedRpc (:41627) and the handler (:41962-41968) is gated only on `Player.m_localPlayer != null` with no sender check, so a server-only mod can relocate a vanilla player after detecting a transit (Wonderland PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit heuristic). That is a reactive bounce, not a veto, and belongs in a separate option — it does not change this ruling.
- LoadFields detail: `m_allowAllItems` is a bool and LoadFields has a `typeof(bool) && zDO.GetBool(text, out …)` branch (:82701); the three keys ('HasFields', 'HasFieldsTeleportWorld', 'TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems') are bools at the API level (stored as ints by ZDO.Set(string,bool)). The lead is correctly labelled unverified and client-honoured; it also only takes effect on ZNetView.Awake (:82631), i.e. after the portal is re-instantiated on that client.
- Minor: the RPC 'RPC_TeleportTo' is also registered per-character on ZNetView (:886) and its handler (:4126-4132) requires m_nview.IsOwner(), so it cannot be used from the server; only the Chat-level RPC_TeleportPlayer can.
- Replace 'only ever builds objects in an empty sector 1e6m out' with: the pinned reference position clamps to Sector 0 (ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex :115762-115775), the shared bucket for every out-of-range position and real sector (-256,-256); ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects (:82268-82276) therefore instantiates whatever ZDOs sit in that bucket. No Player exists in it, so Teleport is still unreachable.
- Qualify 'no character ZDO carries item data': equipped-item prefab hashes are in the player ZDO via VisEquipment (s_rightItem :20590, s_chestItem :20632); inventory contents, including ore, are not.
- LoadFields lead: note that vanilla's Console spawn command (client :44430-44450) already uses the same 'HasFields' key convention on arbitrary prefabs, and that the keys are read only in ZNetView.Awake (:82631) and LocationProxy.SpawnLocation (:103150), never on later ZDO updates.
- 'The server sees no packet' is true for the decision, but the resulting position jump is visible in the player's ZDO sync (basis of Wonderland PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit) - reactive detection of transits is possible, vetoing is not.

### 127. RULED OUT — Blocking Dungeon Doors and Vetoing Retags at the RPC Layer

`lockdown-safety:RULED OUT — Blocking Dungeon Doors and Vetoing Retags at the RPC Layer` · domain **lockdown** · source `lockdown-safety`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **reactive-detection-only** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Crypt and dungeon teleports have no networked state at all, and portal retags issued by the ZDO's owner never reach the wire — so neither can be blocked, observed, or audited server-side.


**How it works:** DUNGEON DOORS. `class Teleport` (:143316-143390) is a 75-line MonoBehaviour with exactly four fields — `m_hoverText`, `m_enterText`, `public Teleport m_targetPoint`, `m_hoverOffset` — and NO ZNetView field, NO Awake, NO m_nview, NO ZDO access and NO RPC registration anywhere in the class body. Its destination is a plain Inspector object reference resolved by Transform math (`GetTeleportPoint()` returns `transform.position + transform.forward - transform.up`, :143372-143375, and is private and called on the *other* instance so it is not even overridable through a public surface). It is therefore invisible to `ZDOMan`, absent from `m_portalObjects`, untouched by `Game.ConnectPortals`, and has no save-file representation. There is nothing for a server-only mod to read, write, redirect, log, or veto. Its only shared lever is `GlobalKeys.NoBossPortals`, and even that is a narrower and stranger check than the world-portal one: `Teleport.Interact` blocks only when `GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && character.InInterior() && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon(pos)` (:143355), where `InInterior()` is `y > 3000f` so it gates the OUTBOUND leg only, and `IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` (:133631-133645) returns false whenever `EnemyHud.instance` is null and otherwise depends on which boss health bar that specific client currently has on screen. Note also what `Teleport.Interact` does NOT do: it never reads `GlobalKeys.NoPortals` and never calls `Player.IsTeleportable`. So a full `noportals` lockdown leaves every crypt door working, ore and all — and vanilla never restricted ore through them in the first place. Worth cataloguing alongside it: `Ladder.Interact` (:132064-132079) performs an instant `character.transform.position = m_targetPos.position` with no `TeleportTo`, no 2s cooldown, no fade, no key check and no item check, gated only on interaction range — a third Transform-based relocation component, equally invisible to the server, which any 'all teleport paths' audit must list and which any server-side transit detector will misattribute. RETAG VETO. `TeleportWorld.SetText` invokes `m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", tag, authorId)` (:143579-143585), and `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string, ...)` routes to `m_zdo.GetOwner()` (:82855-82858). `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC` then handles the call LOCALLY and skips `RouteRPC` entirely whenever `targetPeerID == m_id` (:83577-83595, branch at :83588-83594). A client that owns the portal ZDO — which, because `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` hands ownership to any peer in whose active area the portal sits every 2s (:76901-76926), is the normal case for any portal near a player — therefore retags it entirely in-process with ZERO packets on the wire. The server cannot see it, cannot log it, and cannot drop it. And in the opposite case, if the SERVER owns the portal ZDO, the RPC is routed to the server and then dropped on the floor, because `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` needs `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zDO)` (:83656) which is always null headless — so server ownership of a portal silently BREAKS vanilla retagging for players. Separately, `authorId` is a raw client self-report never cross-checked against the sending peer (:143587-143602), so `s_tagauthor` is not an audit trail. THE ONLY WORKING APPROACH is detect-and-revert on the ZDO: poll `s_tag` on `GetPortalList()` against a desired-state map and rewrite on drift, accepting a poll-interval-sized window during which the player's tag stood.


**Player experience:** For dungeons: a player with `noportals` set server-wide walks into a burial chamber and out again completely normally, carrying iron. Operators who announced 'all teleportation disabled' will be contradicted. For retags: a player renames their own portal and it just works, with no server record of who renamed what or when — and if a mod has claimed server ownership of that portal, the rename appears to succeed client-side (the text dialog closes) and then silently does nothing, which is a far worse experience than a refusal.


**Failure modes:**
- A Harmony patch on `Teleport.Interact` compiles and applies on a dedicated server and never fires, because `ZoneSystem.CreateLocationProxy` passes `spawnNow = (mode == SpawnMode.Full)` so the visual location prefab never expands server-side and no `Teleport` component is ever instantiated.
- A Harmony patch on `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag` likewise never fires. A prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.RouteRPC` or `HandleRoutedRPC` keyed on `"RPC_SetTag".GetStableHashCode()` catches only the minority of retags that actually cross the wire.
- Claiming server ownership of portal ZDOs to 'control' them silently disables player retagging with no error on either side — a severe, hard-to-diagnose regression.
- Detect-and-revert on `s_tag` fights `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData`'s whole-ZDO clobber (:77107-77132): the owning client's next higher-DataRevision push restores its value. Winning requires bumping DataRevision aggressively and re-asserting on a tick.
- Any per-player audit keyed on `s_tagauthor` is spoofable (:143587-143602, `sender` never validated against `authorId`). Use `Piece` `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) for ownership instead, and cross-check identity against `peer.m_socket.GetHostName()`.
- `Ladder.Interact` bypasses even the 2s `TeleportTo` cooldown, so it is the cheapest vanilla-legitimate teleport in the game and will confuse any position-delta-based detector.

**Designer citations:** class Teleport full body — no ZNetView/ZDO/RPC — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143316-143390 ; Teleport.m_targetPoint Inspector reference — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143322 ; Teleport.GetTeleportPoint — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143372-143375 ; Teleport.Interact narrower NoBossPortals gate, no NoPortals, no IsTeleportable — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143345-143370 (:143355) ; Character.InInterior(Vector3) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:4538-4541 ; Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon EnemyHud dependency — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133631-133645 ; Ladder.Interact instant relocation — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:132064-132079 ; TeleportWorld.SetText → ZNetView.InvokeRPC → owner — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143579-143585; ZNetView.InvokeRPC :82855-82858 ; ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC skips RouteRPC when target is self — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83577-83595 ; ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC requires FindInstance — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83645-83663 ; ZNetScene.FindInstance — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82229 ; ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS 2s ownership transfer — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76901-76926 ; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag unvalidated authorId — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143587-143602 ; ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData whole-ZDO clobber — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77103-77132 ; ZDOVars.s_tag / s_tagauthor / s_creator — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78617, :78619, :78393


**Open questions:**
- Which ZDO owns a typical portal in steady state — the nearest client or the server? This determines what fraction of retags are invisible (owner-local) versus observable (routed). IN-GAME CHECK: log `zdo.GetOwner()` for every portal on a 10s timer with players nearby and away, and correlate against retag events.
- Does the `Teleport` component share a GameObject with a ZNetView on the shipped dungeon-entrance prefabs? It would not change the conclusion (the location prefab never expands server-side) but would settle whether a `Teleport` ever exists for a single frame during ghost world-gen. IN-GAME CHECK: patch `Teleport.OnTriggerEnter` on the dedicated server, log, and confirm zero hits across a full world-gen pass.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- 'Never reach the wire … cannot see it, cannot log it' applies to the RPC only. The owning client's RPC_SetTag writes s_tag, s_tagauthor and UpdateConnection(None) into its ZDO copy (:143594-143600), IncreaseDataRevision on a client queues the ZDO via ClientChanged (:73832-73839, :77728-77731), and the server receives it in ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage) (:77076) with the sending peer's identity available from `rpc`. Detection, attribution and revert are therefore possible after the fact (reactive-detection-only), which is what the option's own last paragraph describes. The claim line should say 'cannot be vetoed', not 'cannot be observed or audited'.
- Add the systemic consequence for the sibling options: any mod write that uses `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` (the Game.SetConnection primitive, :100643) makes the server the owner until ReleaseNearbyZDOS returns it (≤2 s, :76870-76884), and during that window every vanilla rename of that portal is silently dropped at HandleRoutedRPC (:83656). Mods that re-claim ownership every tick will break vanilla retagging continuously.
- Dungeon-door detection is likewise reactive: a client's character ZDO position crossing y = 3000 (InInterior threshold :4538-4541) is visible to the server, so entries/exits can be logged and bounced (Chat RPC_TeleportPlayer, :41627/:41962), but not prevented.
- TeleportHome (:143392-143400) is a fourth Transform-based relocation component (calls Game.RequestRespawn on trigger) worth adding to the 'all teleport paths' list alongside Teleport and Ladder.
- Retag CAN be observed and attributed server-side: the client-owner's tag write arrives via ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage) (:77080-77140); the ZRpc parameter identifies the sending peer. Replace 'cannot see it, cannot log it' with 'cannot veto it before it lands; can detect it event-driven with sender attribution and revert'.
- 'THE ONLY WORKING APPROACH is poll' is wrong - a Harmony hook on RPC_ZDOData (or a prefix that declines to Deserialize the package) is event-driven and poll-free. Reverting still requires bumping the server's DataRevision above the client's (revision tie is mutually rejected, :77108-77118).
- The server-owned case is not merely 'broken': a mod that pins portal ownership to the server (patch ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76926 / IsInPeerActiveArea :76887-76898 for PortalPrefabHash) and intercepts 'RPC_SetTag' in ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (:83632-83643) gets a real pre-write veto on retags from vanilla clients, with the caveat that all other owner-routed RPCs on the portal (WearNTear damage/repair/remove) must then also be serviced by the mod. Modified clients can still write the tag directly via ZDO sync.
- RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID is read from the client's packet (:83634-83636) and never overwritten from the socket - do not use it as an audit identity.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Dungeon half verifies exactly: class Teleport (:143316-143390) has four fields, no ZNetView, no ZDO access, no RPC registration; Interact checks only NoBossPortals && InInterior (y > 3000, :4538-4541) && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon (EnemyHud-dependent, :133631-133645) and never NoPortals or IsTeleportable (:143345-143370); GetTeleportPoint is private Transform math (:143372-143375). Ladder.Interact is an instant transform write with no key or item check (:132064-132079). Retag-veto half verifies: SetText -> ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) routes to m_zdo.GetOwner() (:143579-143585, :82855-82858); ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC handles locally and skips RouteRPC when targetPeerID == m_id (:83577-83595); HandleRoutedRPC on the server drops any ZDO-targeted RPC because ZNetScene.FindInstance is null headless (:83645-83663, :82229-82236); ReleaseNearbyZDOS runs every 2 s (:76870-76884) and hands Persistent ZDOs — including portals, which FindObjects pulls from m_portalObjects (:77376-77379) — to any peer whose active area contains them (:76901-76926); authorId is a raw self-report (:143587-143602). The one overreach is the claim that an owner retag 'cannot be observed or audited': the resulting s_tag/connection change does hit the wire in the client's next ZDOData packet.
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Dungeon half fully confirmed: class Teleport (:143316-143390) has four fields, no ZNetView, no Awake, no RPC; GetTeleportPoint is private Transform math (:143372-143375); Interact (:143344-143370) checks only NoBossPortals && character.InInterior() && Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon, never NoPortals, never IsTeleportable; InInterior is y>3000 (:4538-4541); IsInsideActiveBossDungeon depends on EnemyHud.instance (:133631-133646). Ladder.Interact (:132064-132079) is an instant transform set gated only on InUseDistance. Retag half: the wire claim is correct - TeleportWorld.SetText (:143579-143585) -> ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) routes to m_zdo.GetOwner() (:82855-82858); ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC (:83577-83595) handles locally and skips RouteRPC when targetPeerID==m_id; ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) transfers a server-owned ZDO to any peer whose active area contains it because IsInPeerActiveArea for the server session tests against the (1e6,0,1e6) pin (:76887-76898); and HandleRoutedRPC (:83645-83663) drops ZDO-targeted RPCs without a ZNetScene instance (:82229-82236). RPC_SetTag uses authorId verbatim (:143587-143602). BUT the headline 'cannot be observed or audited server-side' is refuted: the resulting tag write reaches the server as an ordinary ZDO update through ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage) (:77080-77140), whose ZRpc argument identifies the sending socket - a Harmony hook there gives event-driven, sender-attributed detection of every tag change (and every connection change) with no polling, and a prefix can even refuse to apply the package (the client's copy keeps its value until the server bumps DataRevision past it). Also, the 'server ownership silently breaks retagging' observation cuts the other way for a mod: a server that keeps portal ownership (patching ReleaseNearbyZDOS/IsInPeerActiveArea for portal prefabs) receives every vanilla retag as a routed RPC with a socket-identifiable sender and can accept, log or refuse it by handling 'RPC_SetTag' in a ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC/HandleRoutedRPC patch - at the cost of also having to service every other owner-routed RPC on that object (WearNTear damage/repair/remove). Note m_senderPeerID in RoutedRPCData is deserialised from the client packet (:83632-83636) and is spoofable; attribute via the ZRpc socket, not the field. So: veto-at-RPC-layer for client-owned portals is impossible (confirmed); observe/audit is reactive-detection-only, not 'impossible'.

### 128. The Void Anchor

`wildcard:The Void Anchor` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A destination ZDO whose prefab hash is literally 0 — invisible, never instantiated, never logged, ignored by IsAreaReady — turning any world coordinate into a valid portal exit.


**How it works:** TeleportWorld.Teleport (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143539-143546) resolves its destination with a bare ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connectionZDOID) and then reads only GetPosition() and GetRotation(). It never checks the target's prefab, tag, type, persistence or ownership. TargetFound (:143640-143656) requires only that the client holds the ZDO. So the destination does not have to be a portal — it does not have to be anything.

The cleanest anchor is a ZDO with prefab hash exactly 0. ZNetScene.CreateObject (:81996-82002) opens with `if (prefab == 0) return null;` BEFORE the GetPrefab lookup, so no GameObject is made and, uniquely, NO 'Missing prefab hash' warning is logged (contrast :82004-82008 for an unknown non-zero hash). ZNetScene.IsPrefabZDOValid (:81986-81993) also returns false for hash 0, so IsAreaReady (:82064-82082) skips it entirely and the arriving player's teleport is never blocked waiting for it.

Recipe, server-side: `var z = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, 0); z.Persistent = true; z.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; z.Distant = false; z.SetPrefab(0); z.SetRotation(rot);` Note CreateNewZDO (:76674-76692) leaves m_prefab at its pooled default of -1 (ZDO field decl :73317, `c_PrefabInvalid = -1`), and -1 DOES log a warning, so SetPrefab(0) is mandatory, not optional. Then on the player-facing portal: `portal.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); portal.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, z.m_uid); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(portal.m_uid);` (mirrors Game.SetConnection :100643-100645).

Delivery: the anchor is not in the traveller's sector, so it arrives only via TeleportWorld.TargetFound calling ZDOMan.RequestZDO (:143653), which routes to the server's RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692) and force-sends it. First walk-through therefore fails silently; the second succeeds. Pre-warm with ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerUid, anchorId) on peer join to remove the warm-up.

Persistence: prefab 0 is not in Game.PortalPrefabHash, so ZDO.SetSector (:73752) does NOT early-return and the anchor files normally in m_objectsBySector; AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) saves it because Persistent is true and the prefab is not a portal hash. FilterZDO (:76346-76361) only warns on unknown prefabs when the world version changed, and never removes them.


**Player experience:** A player walks into a portal tagged 'Sanctum'. The far end is not a portal — it is nothing at all. They arrive standing on a mountain ledge, or in the middle of a stone circle, or on a specific dock plank, facing a direction the server chose, with no return gate visible. The only way back is the way the server decided. Because the anchor is invisible, an admin destination cannot be griefed, deconstructed, or found by exploring — there is no object there to hit with a hammer. On the very first use after the link is created the player walks through and nothing happens, no message, no effect; they step out and back in and it works.


**Failure modes:**
- First transit after linking silently no-ops while RequestZDO fetches the anchor — TeleportWorld.Teleport returns at gate 1 (:143519) without any player.Message, so it reads as a bug
- Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 (:100601) nulls the portal's connection within 5s unless the anchor ZDO also carries the identical ZDOVars.s_tag string AND a non-None Portal connection of its own (a self-loop anchor.SetConnection(Portal, anchor.m_uid) satisfies the second clause)
- A self-loop on the anchor is erased at world save by ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75472-75475), which overwrites the source slot with the Target slot — so the link must be re-asserted after every world load
- An anchor placed beyond roughly +/-16384 m lands in ZoneSystem SectorToIndex bucket 0 (:115760-115773), the same bucket the server's own pinned reference position maps to, and the server will then reap it via ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted's IsServer() destroy branch (:82137-82143)
- Anchor ZDOIDs are renumbered on every world load (ZDO.Load sets m_uid via ZDOID.SetID), so mod state must key anchors by rounded position or a custom ZDO field, never by ZDOID

**Designer citations:** TeleportWorld.Teleport — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143517-143549 (destination read at :143539-143545, no prefab check) ; TeleportWorld.TargetFound — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143640-143656 (RequestZDO at :143653) ; ZNetScene.CreateObject — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81996-82022 (silent null return on prefab 0 at :81999-82002) ; ZNetScene.IsPrefabZDOValid — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81986-81993 ; ZNetScene.IsAreaReady — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82064-82082 ; ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76674-76692 ; ZDO m_prefab default -1 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73305-73317 ; ZDO.SetSector portal exemption — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73752-73757 ; ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk persistence filter — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77572 ; ZDOMan.FilterZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76346-76361 ; ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77689-77692 ; Game.SetConnection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100637-100651


**Open questions:**
- Does a vanilla 1.0.7 client tolerate a prefab-0 ZDO sitting in its own loaded sector indefinitely with zero log output? IN-GAME: create a prefab-0 anchor 10 m from a player, stand there 5 minutes, grep the client log for any ZDO-related line.
- Does ZDO.Save/Load round-trip prefab hash 0 without tripping any load-time guard? IN-GAME: create the anchor, force a world save, restart the server, and confirm ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO resolves it and the teleport still lands.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- 'First walk-through fails silently; the second succeeds' is overstated. UpdatePortal (:143489-143505) evaluates `flag2 && TargetFound()` every 0.5 s as soon as a teleportable player is within m_activationRange=5 m, so RequestZDO fires ~1 s before a walking player reaches the trigger and the force-send normally lands first; only a sprint straight into the arch races it. Pre-warm on peer join is still the robust fix.
- 'never logged' is false at boot: the chunked loader calls FilterZDO(newVersion: true) (:76583, :76602) and !ZNetScene.HasPrefab(0) (:82040) puts the anchor in warningZDOs → every server start logs 'Found N ZDOs with unknown prefabs. Will load anyway.' and 'Hash 0 appeared N times.' (:76371-76386). It IS loaded; only the log claim is wrong.
- m_prefab default: ZDO.Reset (:73536-73549) does NOT clear m_prefab, so a recycled pooled ZDO carries its previous occupant's hash — possibly a real prefab, which every client would then instantiate at the anchor. SetPrefab(0) is mandatory for that reason, not merely to avoid the -1 warning; do it before anything else.
- Save boundary — the suggested 'self-loop on the anchor' is order-dependently lossy: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75477) writes the anchor's single slot twice for Z→Z ((Portal,h) then (Portal|Target,h)) and again for P→Z; depending on s_connections iteration order the final pair of hashes may not match and load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77854-77891) drops the portal's link, after which vanilla Game.ConnectPortals re-pairs the portal by tag elsewhere. Use a mutual back-link (anchor→portal) instead: it is a proper pairwise matching and is restored on load regardless of order (ConnectPortals pairs any ZDO with a matching hash, not only portal prefabs).
- Dedicated-only: on a player-hosted world (IsServer() with a local player) CreateObjectsSorted destroys the anchor the moment the host comes within the active area (:82140-82146). Also do not place anchors outside ±16.4 km — those land in Sector 0, which IS the dedicated server's own near set (SectorToIndex :115760-115774, Game.FixedUpdate :100465) and would be destroyed the same way.
- Dirty-chunk ordering: Initialize→AddToSector runs with Persistent=false so no chunk is dirtied (:76723-76729); set Persistent=true BEFORE the first Set/SetPrefab so IncreaseDataRevision→SetDirtySector (:73833-73840, :76694-76700) marks the chunk; the back-link SetConnection does this anyway.
- Ownership: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76900-76927) will hand the anchor to whichever client stands near it; harmless (no instance, no writes) but expect GetOwner() != 0.
- Line nit: ZDO.Deserialize sets m_prefab from the wire (:74212) — a prefab-0 ZDO round-trips to clients unchanged; CreateNewZDO(pos, prefabHash) public overload is at :76674 and requires the int argument (not optional).
- Creation recipe: use ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, <non-zero non-portal hash>) then z.SetPrefab(0). With prefabHash 0, CreateNewZDO uses the pooled ZDO's stale m_prefab for AddIfPortal (:76684-76688); ZDO.Reset/Init never clear m_prefab (:73496-73550) and ZDOPool is LIFO (:78269-78300), so an anchor allocated right after a portal destroy is misregistered as a portal (in m_portalObjects, removed from m_objectsBySector, enumerated by GetPortalList and reconciled by Game.ConnectPortals).
- Replace the 'self-loop' prerequisite with a reciprocal link anchor->portal (ConnectionType.Portal). RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) keeps one hash slot per ZDO overwritten in dictionary order, so a self-loop can clobber the slot the portal link needs and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77852-77890) drops the pair at reload; a reciprocal pair survives for either ordering and still passes Game.ConnectPortals (:100600-100604) because the anchor's connection is non-None.
- 'First walk-through fails silently' is a race, not a rule: TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal calls TargetFound() (which issues RequestZDO) every 0.5 s while a teleportable player is within 5 m (client :144231-144247), so the anchor usually arrives during the approach. Pre-warming with ForceSendZDO(peer, id) on spawn removes the residual race.
- 'Never logged': ZDOMan.FilterZDO is always called with newVersion:true (:76573, :76591) so each world load logs a warning line for hash 0 ZDOs (WarnAndRemoveBrokenZDOs :76368-76385). Harmless, but not silent.
- Bounds: anchor position must stay within ±16,384 m; ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex sends out-of-range sectors to index 0 (:115758-115772), the bucket the dedicated server's pinned reference position also resolves to, where server-side CreateObjectsSorted/CreateDistantObjects destroy invalid-prefab ZDOs (:82105+, client mirror :82361-82372).

Three corrections. (1) Pool hazard: ZDO.Reset()/Init() never clear m_prefab (:73496-73550) and ZDOPool is a LIFO stack of released ZDOs (:78269-78300); CreateNewZDO(pos, 0) computes prefabHash = zDO.GetPrefab() when prefabHashIn==0 (:76684-76688) — a ZDO recycled from a just-destroyed portal carries the portal hash, so AddIfPortal files the anchor in m_portalObjects and removes it from the sector list (:77732-77752). Fix: call CreateNewZDO(pos, <any non-zero non-portal int>) so AddIfPortal returns early, then SetPrefab(0). The '-1 pooled default' claim is only true for never-used ZDOs. (2) Save boundary: the prereq 'self-loop on the anchor' is order-fragile — RegenerateConnectionHashData writes one hash slot per ZDO and a self-loop's own entry can overwrite the (Portal|Target) slot the player-portal's link wrote, after which ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load (:77852-77890, item2==item skipped) finds no partner and the link is gone; a reciprocal anchor->portal link instead survives deterministically as an ordinary pair (both orderings yield a matching P/P|T hash) and also satisfies Game.ConnectPortals' 'target connection != None' test (:100603). (3) 'First walk-through fails silently' is overstated: UpdatePortal polls TargetFound() every 0.5 s whenever a teleportable player is within m_activationRange=5 m (client :144231-144247), so the RequestZDO round-trip (server SendZDOs cycles per peer every 50 ms) normally completes during the approach; failure only on a sprint straight in. Pre-warm still recommended. Minor: FilterZDO passes newVersion:true unconditionally, so every load logs 'Found N ZDOs with unknown prefabs. Will load anyway. / Hash 0 appeared N times' — 'never logged' is false at load. Keep anchors within ±16,384 m: SectorToIndex maps anything outside to bucket 0 (:115758-115772), which is the server's own near set at the (1e6,0,1e6) pin and CreateObjectsSorted destroys invalid-prefab ZDOs there when IsServer().

### 129. Skyfall, Seabed and Underworld Exits

`wildcard:Skyfall, Seabed and Underworld Exits` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Exact arrival behaviour for destinations at impossible altitudes, derived from the 8s/15s/FindFloor/GetSolidHeight ladder in Player.UpdateTeleport.


**How it works:** Player.UpdateTeleport (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15329-15379) is a four-stage ladder and each stage has a hard number.

Stage 1, t <= 2s: nothing happens; the player is frozen at origin with a black screen.

Stage 2, t > 2s: transform.position is force-assigned to m_teleportTargetPos EVERY FixedUpdate (:15343), linearVelocity is zeroed (:15345), and m_maxAirAltitude is reset to the target's y (:15346). This means no fall accumulates DURING the hold.

Stage 3, the exit gate (:15349): for distantTeleport (which TeleportWorld always passes, :143546) completion requires t > 8s AND ZNetScene.IsAreaReady(target).

Stage 4, the floor test (:15354): ZoneSystem.FindFloor raycasts DOWN from target + Vector3.up * 1f for exactly 1000 m against m_solidRayMask (:115604-115613). If it hits, the teleport ends cleanly at t >= 8s. If it misses, at t > 15s the player is force-placed at ZoneSystem.GetSolidHeight(target) + 0.5f, where GetSolidHeight raycasts from target.y + 1000f down 2000 m and returns target.y unchanged on a miss (:115525-115534).

Concrete consequences for an anchor at height H above terrain:
- H <= 1000: FindFloor hits, teleport completes at t = 8s, m_maxAirAltitude is released at the target y, and the player falls H metres taking full fall damage on landing.
- H > 1000 but H <= 2000: FindFloor misses, 15s hold, GetSolidHeight hits (its ray spans target.y+1000 down to target.y-1000), player is placed 0.5 m above the ground directly below — a soft landing after a 15-second black screen.
- H > 2000: both miss, player is left at H + 0.5 and falls the full distance.

Below ground: Character.UnderWorldCheck (:1055-1075) runs EVERY frame for players (`m_underWorldCheckTimer > 5f || IsPlayer()`), raycasts ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight, and if position.y < groundHeight - 1 snaps the player to groundHeight + 0.5 with zeroed velocity. A buried destination therefore always pops the player to the surface directly above.

Underwater: sea level is 30 (ZoneSystem.m_waterLevel). The seabed is terrain and inside FindFloor's 1000 m reach, so an ocean-floor anchor completes at t = 8s and the player surfaces swimming with no damage.

World edge: Player.EdgeOfWorldKill (:11132-11152) pushes the player inward past 10420 m XZ while swimming or below y=30, and applies 99999 HitType.EdgeOfWorld damage past 10420 m when y < -10.


**Player experience:** Three distinct arrivals, each a deliberate design choice. 'The Drop': the screen clears at 8 seconds and the player is suddenly 300 m above the Black Forest canopy in freefall, with a few seconds to deploy nothing at all before they die — a one-way punishment gate, or a feather-fall gimmick if the server also grants a status effect on arrival. 'The Long Fall': a 1500 m anchor gives a 15-second black screen (noticeably longer than any normal portal, which is itself a tell) and then the player simply appears standing on the ground, no fall, no damage — a stealth long-hop. 'The Well': a destination buried 40 m underground means the player materialises, the screen clears, and in the same frame they are snapped up to the surface — visually indistinguishable from a normal arrival, which makes it a free 'land exactly on top of whatever terrain is here' primitive with no height calculation needed at all.


**Failure modes:**
- A destination above roughly 1000 m of clear air imposes a 15-second black screen, which players will report as a freeze or a crash
- Fall damage after a Stage-3 completion is entirely real and can kill; there is no server-side way to see it happened except the character ZDO s_dead flag
- A destination in a never-visited region may fail IsAreaReady past 8s; the 15s fallback then fires regardless, so worst case is always 15 seconds not infinity
- EdgeOfWorldKill kills outright at >10420 m XZ and y < -10 with a HitType the player sees as an unexplained death
- UnderWorldCheck uses ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight, a raycast — inside a dungeon interior (y > 3000) the dungeon floor mesh is what it hits, which is correct, but over a hollow cave with no collider below it can pop a player through geometry

**Designer citations:** Player.UpdateTeleport — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15329-15379 (2s gate :15338, position pin :15343, maxAirAltitude reset :15346, 8s+IsAreaReady gate :15349, FindFloor :15354, 15s fallback :15360-15367) ; ZoneSystem.FindFloor — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115604-115613 ; ZoneSystem.GetSolidHeight(Vector3) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115525-115534 ; Character.UnderWorldCheck — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:1055-1075 ; Player.EdgeOfWorldKill — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:11132-11152 ; TeleportWorld.Teleport passes distantTeleport true — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143546 ; ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask setup — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113424


**Open questions:**
- Exact fall-damage curve versus drop height for a 1.0.7 player with mid-game armour — Character fall damage is computed from m_maxAirAltitude minus landing y. IN-GAME: drop a test character from 50/100/200/400 m via a Void Anchor and record HP loss.
- Does IsAreaReady ever succeed for a point 1500 m above terrain? It queries the XZ zone only (:82066), so it should, but the sector's ZDOs must all be instanced. IN-GAME: time the black screen for a high anchor over a dense base versus open wilderness.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Delete the 'H > 1000 but H <= 2000' tier. GetSolidHeight(Vector3) :115525-115534 spans target.y+1000 → target.y-1000, the same ~1000 m downward reach as FindFloor (:115604-115613). For H > ~1000 both rays miss; the player is placed at target.y+0.5 after 15 s and falls the whole H. 'The Long Fall' stealth soft-landing does not exist. GetSolidHeight can only change the outcome by hitting something in the +1000 m ABOVE the target (e.g. a dungeon interior floor), which places the player higher, not lower.
- Fall damage is capped at 100 (Character.UpdateGroundContact :2949-2958: `Clamp01((num-4)/16)*100`, then m_seman.ModifyFallDamage). 'The Drop' from any height ≥20 m deals 100 damage; a player above 100 HP survives.
- 'The Well': FindFloor from a buried point never hits the terrain above its origin, so the arrival is the 15 s branch (GetSolidHeight from y+1000 finds the surface). Buried anchors give a 15-second hold, not an 8-second one, and the surface placement comes from GetSolidHeight/UpdateTeleport, with UnderWorldCheck (:1064-1073) only as a same-frame backstop afterwards.
- All of this runs only on the local owning client (Player.FixedUpdate :10204-10212 gates on m_nview.IsOwner() && m_localPlayer==this); the SERVER decompile citations are correct as code but the execution context is the client.
- REFUTE 'H > 1000 but H <= 2000 soft landing': GetSolidHeight(Vector3) at :115525-115534 starts at p.y+1000 and casts 2000 m, reaching p.y-1000 — the same reach as FindFloor (:115604-115613, p.y+1 minus 1000). For H > 1000 both miss, GetSolidHeight returns p.y, player is placed at target.y+0.5 after 15 s and falls the full height. Only three bands exist: H <= ~1000 (8 s, full fall) and H > ~1000 (15 s, full fall).
- 'The Well' takes the 15 s path, not 8 s: FindFloor is cast from m_teleportTargetPos (inside the terrain mesh, no backface hit) so it fails; the surface placement comes from the t>15 GetSolidHeight branch (:15360-15367), not from UnderWorldCheck. UnderWorldCheck (:1055-1075) runs before UpdateTeleport each FixedUpdate and is overwritten by the position pin.
- Fall damage is capped at 100 (Clamp01((num-4)/16)*100 at :2966-2968) and passes through m_seman.ModifyFallDamage; 'The Drop' is lethal only for players at <=100 HP. Water landings deal zero fall damage (:1644-1651).
- Anchors at y > 3000 make Character.InInterior true (:4538-4541); note this for very high anchors.
- Citation: the linearVelocity zero is at :15344 and m_maxAirAltitude reset at :15345 (option is off by one line); the 8 s gate is :15348.

**Verifier reasoning:**

Net: a buried anchor is a 15-second black screen ending on the surface, not 'visually indistinguishable from a normal arrival'. EdgeOfWorldKill (:11132-11152) and m_waterLevel=30 (:113218) are as claimed.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The four-stage ladder in Player.UpdateTeleport is exactly as cited (2 s gate, per-FixedUpdate pin of transform.position/linearVelocity/m_maxAirAltitude, 8 s + IsAreaReady gate for distantTeleport, FindFloor, 15 s fallback to GetSolidHeight+0.5) and TeleportWorld.Teleport does pass distantTeleport:true with pos = target + forward*1 + up. But the derived altitude table is wrong in two of its three headline scenarios. (1) 'The Long Fall' is refuted by arithmetic: FindFloor casts from target.y+1 down 1000 m (reaches target.y-999); GetSolidHeight(Vector3) casts from target.y+1000 down 2000 m (reaches target.y-1000). Their reach is identical to within 1 m, so any anchor FindFloor misses is also missed by GetSolidHeight, which then returns p.y unchanged; the player is placed at target.y+0.5 and falls the full distance after a 15 s hold. There is no 1000-2000 m soft-landing band. (2) 'The Well' is not 'same-frame' and not 'visually indistinguishable': FindFloor is evaluated on m_teleportTargetPos, which is inside the terrain MeshCollider; a downward ray starting inside a non-convex mesh hits no backface (Unity default), so FindFloor misses and the player sits through the 15 s branch, after which GetSolidHeight(target) (origin target.y+1000) hits the surface above and places them at surface+0.5. Character.UnderWorldCheck runs before UpdateTeleport in the same FixedUpdate (Character.CustomFixedUpdate :1011 vs Player.FixedUpdate :10226) so its snap is overwritten by the pin every frame and does not shorten the hold. Result is correct (surface directly above) but costs a 15 s black screen, the same tell the option attributes to the Long Fall. (3) 'The Drop' overstates lethality: fall damage is Mathf.Clamp01((num-4)/16)*100 (:2966-2968), i.e. a hard cap of 100 damage for any fall >= 20 m, further modified by m_seman.ModifyFallDamage (feather fall). A player with >100 HP survives any drop; landing in water applies no fall damage at all (UpdateSwimming resets m_maxAirAltitude without a Damage call, :1647-1651). Also, anchors above y=3000 flip Character.InInterior (:4538-4541) with environment/map side effects. The seabed and world-edge claims hold. Enforcement 'client-honoured' is accurate: every line here executes on the local player's client only.

### 130. Crypt Ingress — Portals Into Dungeon Interiors

`wildcard:Crypt Ingress — Portals Into Dungeon Interiors` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Dungeon interiors sit at zone-centre XZ with y + 5000, which is the same 64 m sector as the surface, so a portal can drop a player directly into a specific crypt room.


**How it works:** Location.Awake (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133505-133515) instantiates a location's interior at `new Vector3(zoneCenter.x, transform.position.y + 5000f, zoneCenter.z)`. Character.InInterior(Vector3) is literally `position.y > 3000f` (:4538-4541). Zones and sectors are XZ-only — ZoneSystem.GetZone (:115741-115746) and GetSectorIndex (:115748-115753) ignore y entirely. So a dungeon interior occupies the SAME sector as the surface above it, and any ZDO placed at (zoneCentreX, ~5030, zoneCentreZ) syncs, saves and pairs exactly like a surface ZDO with no special handling anywhere.

Finding a specific room: DungeonGenerator.Save (:152970-152999) serialises every placed room into the generator's own ZDO as the byte array ZDOVars.s_roomData (:78573) with the layout `int count; { int roomHash; Vector3 worldPos; Quaternion worldRot; } * count`, read back verbatim by Load (:153002-153033). A server mod can BinaryReader that blob and get real, exact interior room coordinates. Resolving the room hash to a name needs DungeonDB.GetRoom (:152489), which is asset data.

Locating the DungeonGenerator ZDO itself is the hard part: ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash (:75390-75407) refuses ByteArray, so you cannot index on s_roomData. Two workable routes: (a) query Type.Int on ZDOVars.s_location (:78501) to enumerate every LocationProxy ZDO in the world with its location hash and position, then spatially query that zone's sector for a ZDO whose prefab carries a DungeonGenerator; or (b) simply place the anchor at the location's own zone centre + 5000 y and accept landing in whatever room the generator put there.

Critically, the dungeon room ZDOs only exist once that zone has been ghost-generated for some peer (ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation :115162, CreateGhostZones :113934-113938). On a fresh server the ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances entry exists from world creation but the s_roomData blob does not. So the mod must either wait for generation or fall back to the LocationInstance surface position.

Departure is free: the crypt door (class Teleport, :143316-143390) is untouched and still works normally. Note that building a portal inside a dungeon requires the client-honoured GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild key (read at Player piece validation :13353) — but a SERVER-created portal ZDO needs no such permission, because nothing validates placement server-side.


**Player experience:** A dungeon-delve server where clearing a crypt permanently unlocks a shortcut back into its deepest room. The player finishes a Sunken Crypt, and a stone portal appears at the surface entrance tagged 'Crypt VII - Deep'. Walking in gives the normal 8-second portal fade, and they materialise in the same torch-lit chamber they fought the boss in, with the crypt door behind them for the walk out. To a vanilla client this is completely ordinary — the interior geometry loads exactly as it does when you walk in through the front door, because the sector is the same one. The server-authored portal inside the crypt cannot be built by hand without the DungeonBuild key, which means it reads unmistakably as a reward rather than something anyone could place.


**Failure modes:**
- The dungeon interior is a Location prefab instantiated by the client's LocationProxy; if that expansion has not happened when the teleport completes, IsAreaReady (:82076) fails and the player waits out the full 15 s, then lands at GetSolidHeight — which may be the SURFACE terrain 5000 m below, dropping them outside the crypt entirely
- s_roomData only exists after that zone has been ghost-generated for some peer, so on a fresh world the room list is empty and the mod has nothing to aim at
- A portal ZDO physically inside dungeon geometry may intersect a wall; the TeleportWorldTrigger collider still fires but the model clips
- Character.InInterior gates several unrelated client behaviours (crypt door NoBossPortals at :143355, building rules); a player standing at y>3000 is 'in an interior' to all of them
- Interior room positions are stored in the generator ZDO, which is owned by whichever client generated it — reading it is safe, but it can be rewritten under you

- What is the prefab name of the DungeonGenerator component's host object, so it can be found by GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative? IN-GAME: dump prefab names of all ZDOs in a crypt's sector and look for the one carrying s_roomData.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Route (a) (enumerate ZDOVars.s_location Int keys) depends on the LocationProxy ZDO, which is created by ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation during ghost generation (:115162+, :102657) — it does not exist any earlier than s_roomData does. Only m_locationInstances (:113295) is available pre-generation.
- Handle the legacy room format: DungeonGenerator.Load falls back to `rooms` + `room{i}`/`_pos`/`_rot`/`_seed` keys (:153034+) and Save removes them on rewrite (:152987-152998). A world last saved before the byte-array format has no s_roomData until the dungeon is next loaded and saved.
- Departure via the crypt door is gated: Teleport.Interact (:143360-143364) blocks with $msg_blockedbyboss when GlobalKeys.NoBossPortals is set and Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon(pos). Not 'untouched' under that key.
- DungeonDB.GetRoom needs DungeonDB.instance and its hash table (:152489-152496, GenerateHashList :152498); on a dedicated server verify DungeonDB is initialised before relying on room-name resolution — it is asset data, not ZDO data.
- s_roomData write is at :152984, not :152986 (minor).
- The dungeon start room / generator is at the entrance's prefab-local offset (+~5000 y), not at zone centre; m_zoneCenter (:152742-152745) is only the generation Bounds. Dropping a portal at zoneCentre+5000 blindly is likely to land in empty interior air (FindFloor miss → 15 s → GetSolidHeight also misses inside the 500 m-tall EnvZone unless a room is below). Always derive the target from s_roomData positions or from the DungeonGenerator ZDO's own GetPosition() (start room).
- Simpler discovery: DungeonGenerator is its own networked object (ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation :115243-115252) whose ZDO prefab hash is the generator prefab's name; enumerate with ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefab (:77447-77470) instead of the LocationProxy + sector scan. s_roomData is read via zdo.GetByteArray(ZDOVars.s_roomData).
- Add: vanilla already guards the arrival race — DungeonGenerator.LoadRoomPrefabsAsync calls ZoneSystem.SetLoadingInZone (:152786-152787), IsZoneLoaded returns false while rooms load (:114045-114051), so IsAreaReady blocks UpdateTeleport until geometry exists. No timeout: a failed room load hangs the teleport on the black screen.
- GetAllZDOIDsWithHash's default branch (:75403-75406) also calls UnityEngine.Debug.Break() — never pass Type.ByteArray.
- portal_wood.m_allowedInDungeons is asset data; the DungeonBuild claim (:13353) is plausible but unverified from the decompile.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Core geometry holds. Location.Awake (:133505-133515) instantiates m_interiorPrefab at (zoneCenter.x, transform.y+5000, zoneCenter.z) with scale (64,500,64). Character.InInterior(Vector3) is `position.y > 3000f` (:4538-4541). ZoneSystem.GetZone (:115741-115746) and GetSectorIndex (:115748-115753) use only x and z, so an interior ZDO shares the surface sector; ZNetScene.IsAreaReady (:82064-82081) is also zone-XZ only, so a vanilla client's UpdateTeleport will complete at an interior target once the zone's ZDOs are instantiated. DungeonGenerator.Save (:152970-152999) writes `count {roomHash, Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot}` to ZDOVars.s_roomData (:78573, write at :152984) and Load (:153002-153033) reads it back through DungeonDB.instance.GetRoom(hash) (:152489-152496). ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash (:75390-75407) supports only Float/Long/Int/String — ByteArray hits the default branch (LogError + Debug.Break). LocationProxy writes ZDOVars.s_location as an Int (:102657), so route (a) is valid. SpawnLocation (:115162+) instantiates the DungeonGenerator ZNetView and calls Generate(mode) (:115247-115255); CreateGhostZones runs on the server around every peer refpos (:113934-113938), so s_roomData exists only after some peer has been near. Corrections: LocationProxy ZDOs are themselves only created by SpawnLocation, so route (a) has exactly the same generation dependency as s_roomData — only ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances (:113295) exists pre-generation. Older worlds may still carry the legacy `rooms`/`roomN_pos` Int/Vec3 keys (Save cleans them at :152987-152998; Load's else-branch at :153034+ reads them), so a parser must handle both formats. The crypt door's Teleport.Interact is NOT unconditional: it refuses with $msg_blockedbyboss when NoBossPortals is set and the character is inside an active boss dungeon (:143360-143364). The DungeonBuild key check (:13353) is read correctly.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism holds. Location.Awake instantiates the interior EnvZone at (zoneCenter.x, y+5000, zoneCenter.z) (:133505-133515); InInterior is position.y > 3000 (:4538-4541); GetZone/GetSectorIndex ignore y (:115741-115753); ZDOMan.FindObjects is purely sector-keyed (:77374-77387) so interior ZDOs sync like surface ZDOs; GetPortalList has no y filter so an interior portal pairs normally. DungeonGenerator.Save/Load format (int count; {int hash; Vector3 pos; Quaternion rot}) is exact (:152970-153033) and DungeonDB.instance.GetRoom exists in the server assembly (:152489). The DungeonGenerator is instantiated by ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation as its own networked object with its own ZDO (:115243-115252, `component2.Generate(mode)`), and in Ghost mode on the dedicated server (ZoneSystem.Update → CreateGhostZones per peer, :113930-113938) Generate() calls Save() — so s_roomData exists once any peer has ghost-generated the zone, as the option says. Two things the option gets wrong or misses. (a) The generator itself is NOT at zone centre: Generate sets m_zoneCenter = GetZonePos(zone) with y = transform.y - m_originalPosition.y (:152742-152743) only as a bounds box; the generator/start room sits at the entrance's local offset (+5000 y) unless m_useCustomInteriorTransform. Route (b) 'place at zone centre + 5000 and accept whatever room is there' can therefore land in empty air inside the 64x500x64 EnvZone with no room under it — FindFloor then misses and the player is dropped at target after 15 s, falling to whatever the interior has below (possibly nothing until GetSolidHeight fails too). Use roomData positions (or the generator ZDO's own position = start room) instead. (b) A cheaper locator than the LocationProxy spatial query: the generator ZDO's prefab hash is the generator prefab name, obtainable server-side from ZoneSystem.m_locations[i].m_prefab.Asset.GetComponent<Location>().m_generator.name; ZDOMan.GetAllZDOsWithPrefab (:77447-77470) then enumerates them directly. Also, the arrival race is handled by vanilla: DungeonGenerator.LoadRoomPrefabsAsync registers ZoneSystem.SetLoadingInZone (:152786-152787, :115817), which makes IsZoneLoaded false (:114045-114051) and therefore IsAreaReady false, so Player.UpdateTeleport waits for room geometry before FindFloor. Caveat: there is no timeout on that wait. GetAllZDOIDsWithHash's unsupported-type branch also calls UnityEngine.Debug.Break() (:75404) — harmless in a player build but do not call it with ByteArray. Whether portal_wood.m_allowedInDungeons is false (so hand-building is DungeonBuild-gated, :13353) is asset data not visible in the decompile; the server-side placement claim (no validation) is correct because piece placement is a client-authored ZDO. Enforcement: the portal's existence and pairing are server-authored ZDO state, but transit is client-executed; client-honoured is the honest label.

### 131. Ephemeral Event Gates

`wildcard:Ephemeral Event Gates` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portals the server conjures for the duration of an event and destroys afterwards, with no player ever placing a piece.


**How it works:** Creation (the full five-line recipe, because ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO does not do it for you): `int h = <portal prefab hash>; var z = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, h); z.Persistent = true; z.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; z.Distant = false; z.SetPrefab(h); z.SetRotation(rot); z.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, tag);` CreateNewZDO (:76674-76692) pools a ZDO, sets owner to the server session, and calls AddIfPortal(zdo, prefabHash) — which, because the hash is in Game.PortalPrefabHash, files it in m_portalObjects, removes it from the sector array, and sets DirtyPortalObjects (:77732-77752). It does NOT write the prefab onto the ZDO body and does NOT set Persistent; ZNetView.Awake (:82612-82620) is where vanilla does those, and a hand-built ZDO missing SetPrefab has m_prefab = -1 and will spam 'Missing prefab hash' on every client every frame (:82004-82008).

Portal ZDOs are saved by a special path: GetSaveClonePerChunk (:77621-77632) dumps the WHOLE of m_portalObjects into the ChunkPortal file whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set, with no Persistent filter at all — so a mod-created portal survives restart even if you forgot Persistent. Conversely, AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) explicitly excludes portal-hash ZDOs from normal chunks.

Deletion: ZDOMan.DestroyZDO (:76929-76935) is a silent no-op unless zdo.IsOwner(), so always `z.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` first. It queues into m_destroySendList and SendDestroyed broadcasts the routed DestroyZDO RPC to every peer; each client's HandleDestroyedZDO (:76963-77000) removes it from m_portalObjects, sets DirtyPortalObjects, and ZNetScene.OnZDODestroyed (:82186-82194) destroys the GameObject in front of the player. The ZDOID goes into m_deadZDOs (:76997) so it can never be resurrected by a replayed packet.

Lifecycle: trigger on anything the server can see — a boss key appearing (Harmony postfix on ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd, the BossDefeatWatch pattern), a RandEventSystem event starting, a clock, an admin command on the dedicated server's stdin. Pair the gate with Game.instance.ConnectPortals() called directly (:100589) instead of waiting up to 5 s.

To hide a temporary gate from vanilla's pairer entirely, ZDOMan.GetPortals() (:77643) returns the LIVE m_portalObjects dictionary — removing an entry makes Game.ConnectPortals blind to it while the ZDO stays fully alive for clients. That lets a server hold a hand-wired one-way link with no reconciliation race at all.


**Player experience:** Eikthyr dies. Within a second, a stone portal fades into existence in the middle of the sacrificial circle, already glowing 'connected', tagged 'Stag Road - 20m'. Everyone present sees it appear from nothing — no build effects, no materials, no one placed it. It links to a fixed hub the admins maintain. Twenty minutes later it winks out mid-conversation and the ground is empty again. Nobody can deconstruct it for materials while it exists, nobody can retag it into their own network, and it leaves no trace in the world save once the timer runs out.


**Failure modes:**
- Omitting SetPrefab leaves m_prefab at -1 and every client logs 'Missing prefab hash: -1' 30 times per second while standing near it
- Forgetting SetOwner before DestroyZDO makes the delete a completely silent no-op — the portal stays forever
- Game.m_currentlyConnectingPortals (:99903) caches raw ZDO object references across a full 5 s tick; if an ephemeral gate is destroyed inside that window, ZDOPool.Release recycles the object and ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals (:100690-100698) force-writes a connection through a stale reference
- If the gate shares a tag with player portals, Game.ConnectPortals will happily pair a player's portal to it and then strand that player when it vanishes
- Creating a portal ZDO with a hash that is not in Game.PortalPrefabHash skips AddIfPortal entirely, so it lands in m_objectsBySector, is excluded from the chunk save by the portal filter (:77572), and disappears on restart with no error

**Designer citations:** ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76674-76692 ; ZDOMan.AddIfPortal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77732-77752 ; ZNetView.Awake fabrication block — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82612-82620 ; ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk portal branch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77621-77632 ; ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk portal exclusion — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77572 ; ZDOMan.DestroyZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76929-76935 ; ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76963-77000 ; ZNetScene.OnZDODestroyed — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82186-82194 ; ZDOMan.GetPortals returns the live dictionary — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77643-77646 ; Game.ConnectPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100589-100627

- Which prefabs are in Game.m_portalPrefabs (:99828)? Inspector data. IN-GAME: log Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs names and Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash at first Heartbeat on the dedicated server.
- Does removing an entry from ZDOMan.GetPortals() desynchronise HandleDestroyedZDO's later removal attempt? IN-GAME: hide a portal from the dictionary, destroy it, and check for a leaked m_objectsByID entry.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Drop the 'remove from ZDOMan.GetPortals()' hiding trick. Portal ZDOs are not in m_objectsBySector (AddIfPortal → RemoveFromSector :77749), so FindObjects (:77376-77379) is the only route to peers and GetSaveClonePerChunk (:77624) the only route to disk; an unlisted portal is invisible to new peers, receives no revision sync, and is not saved. To keep a hand-wired link from being reconciled, either Harmony-prefix Game.ConnectPortals on the server (this is a server-side mod; Harmony is available) or exploit the reconcile predicate (:100600-100604): a link A→B survives phase 1 whenever B exists, B.tag == A.tag and B has ANY non-None connection — reciprocity is never tested.
- 'Nobody can deconstruct it / nobody can retag it' is not true of a bare server-created portal. Player.RemovePiece → WearNTear.RPC_Remove (:150411-150425) and TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag (:143587-143600) succeed for whichever client ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands ownership to. Those guarantees come only from the Adamant Gate (m_canBeRemoved via LoadFields) plus a tag/connection re-assert loop.
- Calling Game.instance.ConnectPortals() once stages the pair (AddToCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100681, SetConnection immediate for server-owned ZDOs :100636-100648); the ForceSetConnection re-write happens on the NEXT call (ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698). For a gate to a fixed hub, write both ZDO.SetConnection directions yourself instead of relying on the pairer.
- HandleDestroyedZDO starts at :76962 and ZNetView.Awake fabrication at :82613 (minor line drift).
- Do NOT remove the gate from ZDOMan.GetPortals(): m_portalObjects is also the sync index (ZDOMan.FindObjects :77380-77383) and the save index (:77621-77632); a removed portal is never delivered to peers who lack it and is never saved. Hide from the pairer with a Harmony postfix on the public ZDOMan.GetPortalList() (:77648-77656), which allocates a new list per call and is only used by Game.ConnectPortals and ConvertPortals.
- Refute 'nobody can deconstruct it': Player.RemovePiece (:12364-12420) allows any vanilla client to remove a creator-less piece; DropResources yields Max(1, n/3) materials for !IsPlacedByPlayer (:136343-136346). Needs the Piece.m_canBeRemoved LoadFields override to hold.
- Refute 'nobody can retag it': TeleportWorld.Interact/RPC_SetTag (:143470-143480, :143587-143600) is client-side and ward-gated only; an unwarded conjured gate can be retagged (and thereby disconnected) by anyone. Server can only re-assert reactively.
- 'No trace in the save' holds only if the timer completes before a save: the portal chunk ignores Persistent, so a live gate at save time persists across restart. Mark gates with a mod key and sweep on ZDOMan.Load/Game start.
- Game.ConnectPortals is public (:100589), not private as the prior notes implied; SetConnection/ForceSetConnection/RPC_SetConnection are private. A server-owned gate takes the immediate SetConnection path because ZNet.GetPeer(serverSessionId) is null (:100637-100641).
- Player.RemovePiece also emits no message on the m_canBeRemoved refusal, consistent with the Adamant option.

### 132. The Decoy Gate

`wildcard:The Decoy Gate` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A portal that reports itself connected and glows, but silently refuses to teleport forever, built by pointing its connection at a ZDOID that does not exist.


**How it works:** The client evaluates 'connected' and 'usable' with two DIFFERENT functions and only one of them is on the hover path.

TeleportWorld.HaveTarget (:143631-143638) returns `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != ZDOID.None` — a pure field test, no lookup. GetHoverText (:143461) picks between $piece_portal_connected and $piece_portal_unconnected from HaveTarget alone, and UpdatePortal (:143496-143501) fires the m_connected EffectList and drives m_hadTarget from it, which Update (:143511-143515) lerps into the model's _EmissionColor toward m_colorTargetfound.

TeleportWorld.TargetFound (:143640-143656) additionally requires `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connectionZDOID) != null`, and when the ZDO is absent it calls ZDOMan.instance.RequestZDO and returns false. Teleport() gate 1 (:143519-143522) is `if (!TargetFound()) return;` — a bare return with NO player.Message.

So: write `portal.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, new ZDOID(someSessionId, someNeverAllocatedId))`. HaveTarget is true (hover says connected, portal glows blue), TargetFound is permanently false (the ZDO never resolves), and walking through does absolutely nothing with zero feedback. The client's RequestZDO goes to the server's RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692), which calls peer.ForceSendZDO(id); AddForceSendZdos (:77263-77281) then finds GetZDO(id) == null and prunes the entry silently. No log, no packet, no cost.

Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 (:100600-100604) WILL tear this down within 5 s because `zDO == null`. Two ways to keep it: (a) re-assert the fake ZDOID every 2 s with SetOwner + SetConnection + ForceSendZDO, which costs one DataRevision bump per rewrite because ZDOExtraData.SetConnection (:74951-74960) no-ops on an unchanged value and phase 1 always changes it back; or (b) cleanly, remove the decoy from the live ZDOMan.GetPortals() dictionary (:77643) so vanilla's pairer never iterates it at all.

A softer decoy variant: point it at a real Void Anchor that the server deliberately never force-sends and that sits in a sector no peer visits. The link is then legitimate and survives reconciliation (given a matching tag and a self-loop), but every client's TargetFound fails until the server chooses to deliver the anchor — a switchable gate with no visible state change.


**Player experience:** A grand stone portal stands at the top of a ruined tower, humming and glowing exactly like a working one, hover text reading 'Portal, tag: THE DEEP ROAD [connected]'. Players walk in. Nothing. No message, no black screen, no bounce-back — they simply walk out the other side of the frame. They try again. They check their inventory for ore. They ask in chat. The portal is, as far as any vanilla client can tell, perfectly healthy and connected to something. Used deliberately this is the best puzzle primitive in the whole toolkit: the gate is 'sealed' in a way that gives the player no error to Google, and the server can make it real later by simply delivering the anchor — at which point the very same portal, unchanged, suddenly works.


**Failure modes:**
- Game.ConnectPortals nulls a dangling connection every 5 s (:100601, zDO == null branch), so the decoy needs either a re-assert loop or removal from the live portal dictionary
- A re-assert loop that fights vanilla generates a DataRevision bump and a ForceSendZDO per cycle to every peer — budget it like Wonderland's StructureUpkeep 256-broadcast cap
- The complete absence of feedback is genuinely indistinguishable from a mod bug; pair every decoy with a PlayerNotify toast or a DamageText Bonus string, or players will file it as broken
- A fabricated ZDOID could theoretically collide with a real future ZDOID from the same session; mint decoy targets from a real ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO that is then destroyed, so the id lands in m_deadZDOs (:76997) and can never be reused
- ZDOID.UserID values are renumbered on world load, so a hand-built fake id must be re-derived after every restart

**Open questions:**
- How often does a vanilla client actually fire RequestZDO for an unresolvable target — every UpdatePortal tick (0.5 s) or only on transit? UpdatePortal calls TargetFound at :143507, so likely 2/s per nearby player. IN-GAME: count RequestZDO packets server-side with a player idling next to a decoy for 60 s.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- There IS a visible tell: TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal :143505 `m_target_found.SetActive(flag2 && TargetFound())` — the proximity activation effect never turns on for a decoy when a teleportable player is within m_activationRange (5 m). Real portals do. 'Perfectly healthy as far as any vanilla client can tell' is overstated; the hover text and idle glow match, the approach effect does not.
- Remove fix (b). Deleting the decoy from ZDOMan.GetPortals() also deletes it from the only sync path (FindObjects :77376-77379, CreateSyncList :77212-77238) and the save path (:77624). Replace with a server-side Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals that skips mod-flagged ZDOs, or accept the 2 s re-assert cost.
- The 'softer decoy' (undelivered Void Anchor) does not work unmodified: RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692) force-sends any existing ZDO to the requesting client on demand. It needs a Harmony prefix on ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO (or ZDOPeer.ForceSendZDO) to withhold the anchor.
- Not save-stable: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) requires GetZDO(target) != null, so the fake-ZDOID connection is dropped at world save and the decoy reloads as 'unconnected' until the mod re-writes it on startup.
- A vanilla client that receives ownership (ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS) can retag the decoy via RPC_SetTag (:143587-143600), which clears the connection; the mod must re-assert.
- Visible tell: UpdatePortal sets m_target_found active only when `closestPlayer.IsTeleportable && TargetFound()` (:143502-143506); a decoy never shows the in-frame effect when approached — identical to the 'unteleportable items' look, not 'perfectly healthy'.
- 'No packet' is wrong: TargetFound calls ZDOMan.RequestZDO (:143653) on every 0.5 s UpdatePortal with a teleportable player within 5 m and on every trigger enter — one routed RPC each.
- Keep-alive (a) rewrite-every-2s produces a visible flicker every reconcile (HaveTarget false→true fires m_connected.Create at :143498-143501 and toggles hover/emission). Keep-alive (b) removing from m_portalObjects breaks sync and save (FindObjects :77380-77383, GetSaveClonePerChunk :77621-77632). Use a Harmony postfix on ZDOMan.GetPortalList (public, :77648-77656) or on Game.ConnectPortals (public, :100589) to skip/re-assert decoys within the same tick.
- Save boundary: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75475) requires the target ZDO to exist, so a fake-ZDOID connection is dropped at save; re-assert decoys on load.
- Softer variant: the server cannot passively 'never deliver' an existing anchor — RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692) force-sends it on the first client request. Withholding needs a Harmony prefix on ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO filtering that ZDOID.
- Use a fake ZDOID whose UserID is not the server session (or any peer) so m_nextUid growth can never allocate it.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The two-function split is real. GetHoverText (:143453-143464) picks $piece_portal_connected from HaveTarget; UpdatePortal (:143491-143507) fires m_connected on the HaveTarget transition and Update (:143509-143513) lerps emission toward m_colorTargetfound from m_hadTarget. Teleport() gate 1 (:143519-143522) is a bare return. TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143673-143681) has no feedback either. RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692) → ZDOPeer.ForceSendZDO adds to m_forceSend; AddForceSendZdos (:77263-77284) prunes IDs with GetZDO==null silently. So the fake-ZDOID decoy is real. (2) The 'remove from ZDOMan.GetPortals() dictionary' fix is broken: portals live only in m_portalObjects (AddIfPortal RemoveFromSector :77749) and FindObjects (:77376-77379) is the sync path, so an unlisted decoy is never sent to new peers, gets no revision updates and is dropped from the save (:77624). (3) The 'softer' variant ('a real Void Anchor the server deliberately never force-sends') fails in vanilla: the client's TargetFound → RequestZDO → server RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692) → ForceSendZDO → AddForceSendZdos delivers any existing ZDO to the requesting peer regardless of sector (ShouldSend only compares revisions). Withholding the anchor requires a Harmony prefix on ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO / ZDOPeer.ForceSendZDO. (1) There IS a visible tell: UpdatePortal drives m_target_found.SetActive(flag2 && TargetFound()) (:143506) — the in-frame portal effect that vanilla shows when a teleportable player stands within 5 m never appears on a decoy. It looks exactly like the 'carrying ore' state, not like a healthy portal. (2) 'No packet, no cost' is false: every UpdatePortal tick (0.5 s) with a teleportable player within m_activationRange, plus every trigger enter, sends a routed RequestZDO RPC client→server (:143653). Cheap, but not zero. (3) Keep-alive option (a) 'rewrite every 2 s' is a bad design: between the 5 s teardown and the rewrite the client sees HaveTarget flip false→true, which fires m_connected.Create (:143498-143501), swaps hover to $piece_portal_unconnected and starts the emission lerp — a flicker every 5 s. Option (b) 'remove from GetPortals()' breaks sync and save (ZDOMan.FindObjects :77380-77383 and GetSaveClonePerChunk :77621-77632 both read m_portalObjects). The clean primitive is a Harmony postfix on the public ZDOMan.GetPortalList (:77648) filtering decoys, or a postfix on Game.ConnectPortals (public, :100589) that re-asserts in the same frame (ForceSendZDO only queues, so peers see the final state). Enforcement server-enforced is fair: the sealed state is a server-owned connection field the client cannot make usable.
