### 133. The Tag As A Public Broadcast Surface

`wildcard:The Tag As A Public Broadcast Surface` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


ZDOVars.s_tag is an uncapped, unfiltered, server-writable string that a vanilla client renders live through Localization.Localize — the only in-world text channel a server-only portal mod has.


**How it works:** The write side has no limits whatsoever. ZDO.Set(int, string) performs no ownership check and no validation (:73721). The 10-character cap lives only in TeleportWorld.Interact's call to TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, '$piece_portal_tag', 10) (:143482), which sets m_inputField.characterLimit on the CLIENT UI. CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC in the SERVER build is the single statement `return text;` (:94588-94591), and in the CLIENT build (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94901-94947) it early-returns unless ugcType is ServerName or RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() — false on Steam. The censored flag from CensorShittyWords.Filter is computed in GetTagInfo (:143568) and then only surfaced when ZNet.m_onlineBackend == PlayFab (:143462). On a Steam dedicated server the raw string is what every player reads.

The render path is the interesting part. GetHoverText (:143453-143463) builds `Localization.instance.Localize('$piece_portal $piece_portal_tag:"' + text + '" [' + text2 + ']' + newline + text3 + ...)` — the tag is CONCATENATED INTO the string BEFORE Localize runs. Three exploitable consequences:
(1) A tag containing a localization token such as $piece_portal_connected or $KEY_Use is resolved by the client in the player's own language and their own keybinds.
(2) A newline character in the tag produces a genuine multi-line hover panel. The tag is a small text box, not a single line.
(3) Rich text: `text.RemoveRichTextTags()` is applied at :143459, and StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703) is `Regex.Replace(text, '<[/a-zA-Z0-9= "''#;:()$_-]*?>', '')`. The character class EXCLUDES the less-than sign. Regex.Replace makes a single forward pass and does not re-scan its own output. Therefore the input `<<color=red>color=red>` has no match starting at index 0 (the lazy class cannot consume the second less-than), matches `<color=red>` starting at index 1, and the surviving output is exactly `<color=red>` — which TextMeshPro then renders as real markup. Nested-tag smuggling gives coloured, sized and sprite-tagged portal hover text from a pure ZDO write.

Persistence trap: a tag-only write does NOT dirty the portal chunk. DirtyPortalObjects is set by ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection for ConnectionType.Portal (:73661-73676), by AddIfPortal (:77750) and by HandleDestroyedZDO (:76986) — and by nothing else. ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision goes to SetDirtySector (:73839), and SetDirtyChunks marks a normal chunk that portals are explicitly excluded from (:77572). So every server-side tag rewrite MUST be followed by ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702) or it silently vanishes at the next world save.


**Player experience:** Portals stop being labels and become signage. A hub gate reads, on hover, a three-line panel: 'THE CROSSROADS' in gold, then 'Next rotation in 04:12', then 'Currently open to: Ashlands Foothold'. A quest gate's tag counts down live as the server rewrites it. A contested gate turns red when another faction holds it. During a server event every portal in the world briefly reads the same line. And because the tag is also the pairing key for Game.ConnectPortals, the mod has to be careful: the visible text and the routing key are the same field, so a 'display' tag must either be shared byte-for-byte across a whole network or the mod must own pairing outright.


**Failure modes:**
- s_tag is BOTH the display string and Game.ConnectPortals's equality key (:100601, :100669) — any per-portal display text inside one network is torn down every 5 s unless the mod owns pairing
- A tag-only write is lost at the next save unless ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() is called explicitly
- If a player opens the vanilla tag dialog on a server-written long tag, TextInput.Show assigns the existing text after setting characterLimit = 10 (:61515-61522) — a vanilla client may clamp and save back a truncated tag, destroying the display AND the routing key
- RemoveRichTextTags strips plain markup; only the nested-smuggle form survives, and TMP's tolerance for it is unverified
- A very long tag is re-serialized in full on every ZDO send (ZDOMan.SendZDOs :77062 has no delta encoding), so a 500-character tag on 200 portals is real per-peer bandwidth
- Rewriting a distant portal's tag as a message does not reach a player until they are in that portal's sector (CreateSyncList :77212-77227) unless the mod calls ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(peerUid, id)

**Designer citations:** TeleportWorld.GetHoverText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143464 (Localize concatenation at :143463, RemoveRichTextTags at :143459) ; TeleportWorld.GetTagInfo — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143556-143570 ; TeleportWorld.Interact 10-char cap — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143482; TextInput.RequestText/Show — :61509-61522 ; CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC is `return text;` on the server — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:94588-94591; client version assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94901-94947 ; StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags regex — assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703 ; ZDO.Set(int,string) no ownership check — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73721 ; ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702-76705 ; ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision / SetDirtySector — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73832-73840, 76694-76700 ; ZDOVars.s_tag / s_tagauthor — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78617, 78619


**Open questions:**
- Does TextMeshPro actually honour the smuggled <color=...> that survives RemoveRichTextTags, or does the hover label use a non-rich-text component? IN-GAME: set a tag to the doubled form and hover it on a vanilla client.
- Does GuiInputField clamp a programmatically assigned .text to characterLimit? TextInput.Show sets the limit then the text (:61519-61520). IN-GAME: server-write a 40-character tag, open and confirm the vanilla dialog, re-read s_tag.
- Does Localization.Localize resolve tokens embedded mid-string, and does it handle an unknown $token gracefully? Localization lives outside this decompile set. IN-GAME: set a tag to $KEY_Use and hover.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Raw-string rendering depends on the reading CLIENT's platform, not on the server's backend: client CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94901-94947) filters when RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() (:88608-88620: Xbox or HardwareCategory.Console) is true, returning censored text or the $ugc_* placeholder. Crossplay console players will not see rich/long tags as intended.
- AddIfPortal sets DirtyPortalObjects only on first insertion (:77740-77743 early-returns when already listed), so a routine RPC_ZDOData re-application of a tagged portal does NOT dirty the portal chunk either — the SetDirtyPortals() requirement after every server tag write stands and is stricter than stated.
- A vanilla client that holds ownership (ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS) can replace the tag via RPC_SetTag (:143587-143600) with no server-side veto; the display tag needs a re-assert loop and, because the tag is the pairing key, the mod must own pairing (Harmony on Game.ConnectPortals) for any per-portal display text.
- Hover-panel layout/overflow for multi-line or very long tags is UI behaviour not present in the decompile — needs an in-game check before relying on 3-line signage.
- Enforcement is client-honoured, not server-enforced: any vanilla client can overwrite the tag through TeleportWorld.Interact → RPC_SetTag (:143470-143480, :143587-143600) with only a client-side ward check; the server can only reactively re-write. Display fidelity is honoured by the client; the text is not protected.
- Hover text is rendered only while the crosshair is on the portal within interact range; the 'signage' is on-demand, not ambient. No other vanilla surface renders the tag (map pins for portals are not vanilla).
- Every server tag rewrite on a paired portal must update both ends in the same tick; Game.ConnectPortals (:100600-100604) disconnects on any tag mismatch at its next 5 s pass.
- Clear or set ZDOVars.s_tagauthor alongside the tag when rewriting; RPC_SetTag compares both (:143590-143592).
- Localize caches each distinct input (assembly_guiutils.decompiled.cs:863); rapidly changing tags produce unbounded distinct strings — verify cache bound before per-second countdowns on many portals.

### 134. The Adamant Gate — Server-Enforced Indestructible Portals

`wildcard:The Adamant Gate — Server-Enforced Indestructible Portals` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Writing a huge ZDOVars.s_health onto a portal makes it survive any vanilla-client damage, and Repair can never undo it.


**How it works:** WearNTear.ApplyDamage (:150387-150409) reads the CURRENT health straight from the ZDO every hit: `float f = m_nview.GetZDO().GetFloat(ZDOVars.s_health, m_health); if (f <= 0) return false; f -= damage; m_nview.GetZDO().Set(ZDOVars.s_health, f); if (f <= 0) Destroy(hitData);` The prefab field m_health (:149248) is only the DEFAULT when the ZDO key is absent. So a single server-side `portalZdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_health, 1e9f)` means a player must land a billion points of damage to break the portal.

The repair path cannot undo it. WearNTear.Repair (:149522-149539) returns false immediately when `GetFloat(s_health, m_health) >= m_health` — an inflated value always satisfies that, so RPC_Repair (:149541-149548), which would reset s_health to m_health, is never invoked. Cosmetics are also safe: WearNTear.Awake computes `m_healthPercentage = Mathf.Clamp01(num / m_health)` (:149439), which clamps to 1, so the piece renders as pristine rather than glitching.

ZDO.Set performs no ownership check at any type (the okForNotOwner parameter at :73648-73654 is accepted and ignored), so the write lands immediately and propagates by DataRevision. A nearby owning client can clobber it with a higher-revision push (ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77103-77132 replaces the whole blob), so re-assert on a slow tick — the write is idempotent and free when unchanged, because BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue returns false on an equal value and ZDO.Set then skips IncreaseDataRevision.

The complementary half is deconstruction, which ignores health entirely. Player.RemovePiece (:12364-12378) refuses outright when `!piece.m_canBeRemoved`, silently returning false with no message. m_canBeRemoved is a `public bool` on Piece (:136171) — exactly the shape ZNetView.LoadFields can override (see 'Field Injection'). Writing `HasFields`, `HasFieldsPiece` and `Piece.m_canBeRemoved = false` onto the portal ZDO means a vanilla client's hammer refuses to remove it.

Both halves together give a portal that cannot be smashed and cannot be deconstructed by an unmodified client, with no client install. It is still NOT tamper-proof against a modified client — a hostile client can write s_health directly through RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77139, zero validation) or broadcast a forged DestroyZDO (RPC_DestroyZDO :76953, ungated on receive). That is the honest ceiling: this stops griefing, not cheating.


**Player experience:** The public hub portals at spawn are simply unbreakable. A new player swings a hammer at one out of curiosity and the deconstruct prompt does nothing at all — no 'private zone' message, no refusal text, the hammer just declines. A raider who decides to cut the network drops a boulder on the gate and it takes a hit sound and a chip of effect and nothing else. Admins can still remove it with the mod's own command. Critically the portal still looks and behaves completely normally — full health bar, normal wear model, normal glow — so it reads as 'this is a server fixture', not as a bug.


**Failure modes:**
- A modded client can write s_health or forge a DestroyZDO packet; RPC_ZDOData (:77103-77132) and RPC_DestroyZDO (:76953) validate nothing
- LoadFields only runs inside ZNetView.Awake (:82631), so a m_canBeRemoved change reaches a player only after that portal is next created in their scene — they must leave and return to the area
- The field-injection half depends on the portal prefab actually carrying a Piece component; that is asset data
- Terrain destruction, fire spread and a fully destroyed supporting structure can still orphan a portal even if the portal itself is immortal
- A per-hit re-assert loop would fight the owning client's revision; use a slow idempotent re-assert (the write is free when unchanged, BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue at assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:321)
- WearNTear.Destroy (:150427-150477) writes s_health = 0 directly, so an already-destroyed portal cannot be revived by re-inflating health

**Designer citations:** WearNTear.ApplyDamage — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:150387-150409 ; WearNTear.Repair / RPC_Repair — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:149522-149548 ; WearNTear.Awake health read and healthPercentage clamp — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:149428-149439 ; WearNTear.Destroy — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:150427-150477 ; Player.RemovePiece m_canBeRemoved gate — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:12364-12378 ; Piece.m_canBeRemoved — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:136171 ; ZDO.Set ignores okForNotOwner — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73648-73654 ; ZDOVars.s_health — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78443 ; ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData blind apply — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77103-77132 ; ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO ungated — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76953-76999


**Open questions:**
- Does the portal prefab carry WearNTear and Piece at all? IN-GAME: log ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(name).GetComponents<MonoBehaviour>() type names on the dedicated server.
- Does a huge s_health cause any client-side float or UI artifact (health bar, hammer repair highlight)? IN-GAME: set 1e9 and hover with a hammer.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- ZNetView.LoadFields runs only from ZNetView.Awake (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82860, method :82898-82960). Writing HasFields/HasFieldsPiece/Piece.m_canBeRemoved onto a portal already instantiated on a client does nothing until that client re-instantiates it (leaves and re-enters the sector, or relogs). Set the keys at portal creation or accept the delay.
- The health write is subject to a symmetric revision rule, not a one-way clobber: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77103-77116) ignores any incoming blob whose DataRevision is not strictly greater than the local copy, on server and client alike. If the owning client has bumped its copy (any hit) before the server's write arrives, the write is dropped client-side and the client's next push wins on the server. Re-assert by comparing the server-visible s_health to the target and re-writing until it holds; do not assume 'idempotent and free'.
- float ulp at 1e9 is 64: any single hit under 64 damage leaves s_health bit-identical, so ApplyDamage's Set is a no-op and no revision bump occurs on the client — which is actually favourable, but means the server cannot detect hits by watching s_health.
- Structural collapse and rain wear are also absorbed (UpdateWear :149662-149713 routes both through ApplyDamage as 100 / 5 damage), so the portal survives support loss too — a correction in the option's favour.
- RPC_DestroyZDO is at :76952-76960 (minor line drift).
- ZNetView.LoadFields is called once, at the end of ZNetView.Awake (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82860, body :82898-82960). Field overrides written after a client has already instantiated the portal do not apply until that client re-instantiates it (sector unload/reload or relog). Write the keys before first sync for new portals; for existing ones expect a delay.
- The s_health write is subject to the symmetric revision race in ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77107-77117): concurrent server and owner-client writes from the same base revision are mutually discarded. Re-assert on a periodic tick unconditionally; do not rely on 'idempotent when unchanged' since the server copy may have been replaced.
- Damage below ~32 against a 1e9 float is lost to rounding (ulp 64); harmless, but the hit effect still plays via RPC_HealthChanged (:150404-150406).
- Support failure is not a bypass: !HaveSupport sets 100% wear (:149708-149710) which becomes ApplyDamage(m_health) per tick (:149822-149827), still routed through s_health.
- Citation fix: Piece.m_canBeRemoved is at :136171 as stated; WearNTear.m_health at :149248; RPC_ZDOData revision gate is :77107-77117 (option cites 77103-77132 for the whole loop, fine).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Health half verified. WearNTear.ApplyDamage (:150387-150409) reads `GetFloat(s_health, m_health)`, subtracts, writes back, Destroy only when ≤0. It runs on the owning client via Damage → RPC_Damage (:150315-150332, IsOwner-gated). Repair (:149522-149539) returns false when stored health ≥ m_health, so RPC_Repair (:149541-149548) never fires. Awake clamps m_healthPercentage (:149439). m_health is the prefab default (:149248). Support-loss and rain wear also route through ApplyDamage (UpdateWear :149662-149713: rain +5/60 s, no support → 100), so 1e9 absorbs them (float ulp at 1e9 is 64, so hits <64 do not even change the value). ZDO.Set(int,int,okForNotOwner) (:73648-73654) ignores the parameter; there is no owner check on any Set. Deconstruct half: Player.RemovePiece (:12364-12378) returns false with no message when !piece.m_canBeRemoved; Piece.m_canBeRemoved is `public bool` (:136171); client ZNetView.LoadFields (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82898-82960) reads `HasFields`, `HasFields<TypeName>`, `<TypeName>.<field>` straight from ZDO keys with no prefab gating, using GetComponentsInChildren over public instance fields — so `HasFields`, `HasFieldsPiece`, `Piece.m_canBeRemoved=false` is the right key set. Corrections: (1) LoadFields is called only from ZNetView.Awake (:82860), i.e. at instantiation; a client that already has the portal instantiated keeps m_canBeRemoved=true until it leaves the sector and re-instantiates. (2) The revision race is not 'clobber with a higher revision push' but a symmetric rule: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (:77103-77116) on BOTH sides drops an incoming blob unless its DataRevision is strictly greater than the local one. If the owning client bumped its local copy (a hit) between the server's write and its arrival, the client silently ignores the server's value and its next push (higher rev) overwrites the server. A re-assert loop must therefore read back s_health and re-write until the server-visible value sticks; a single slow-tick write that happens to be unchanged is not 'free' — it is the case where the client's copy may still be at the prefab default. (3) The hostile-client ceiling is right: RPC_ZDOData applies any higher-revision blob and RPC_DestroyZDO (:76952-76960) → HandleDestroyedZDO has no sender check. Enforcement client-honoured is correct — both halves rely on the vanilla client reading the values.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Health half verified: WearNTear.ApplyDamage reads GetFloat(s_health, m_health) fresh every hit, subtracts, writes back, and only calls Destroy when <= 0 (:150387-150409); m_health is the prefab default (:149248). All damage sources funnel through ApplyDamage — RPC_Damage (:150334-150359), UpdateWear rain/lava/support (:149705-149710 sets 100% wear when !HaveSupport, applied at :149822-149827 as num/100*m_health per tick) — so even a support failure only removes m_health per tick against 1e9. Repair returns false when GetFloat >= m_health (:149528-149531), so RPC_Repair (:149541-149548) is never reached. WearNTear.Awake clamps m_healthPercentage (:149439) and SetHealthVisual does too (:150222); Hud.m_pieceHealthBar uses GetHealthPercentage (:48135) so the bar reads full. ZDO.Set ignores okForNotOwner (:73648-73654). Deconstruct half verified: Player.RemovePiece returns false silently on !piece.m_canBeRemoved (:12374-12377); Piece.m_canBeRemoved is public bool (:136171); client ZNetView.LoadFields (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82898-82960) needs only ZDO bools 'HasFields', 'HasFieldsPiece' and 'Piece.m_canBeRemoved' — no Inspector opt-in — and is invoked at the end of ZNetView.Awake (:82860). Corrections: (1) LoadFields runs ONLY at instantiation. Writing the keys onto a portal that is already instantiated on a client has no effect until that client re-instantiates it (leaves and re-enters the sector, or relogs). For freshly built player portals the keys must land before the first sync; the mod cannot force re-instantiation without destroying the ZDO. (2) The s_health write can be lost to the vanilla revision race, not just to a 'higher-revision push': RPC_ZDOData drops an incoming packet whenever num4 <= zDO.DataRevision (:77107-77117). If the owning client and the server both increment from the same base in the same sync window, each side discards the other's write and they diverge until the next write; the slow re-assert tick is therefore mandatory, not optional, and the 'free when unchanged' argument only holds when the server's copy still has the value. (3) The float ulp at 1e9 is 64, so damage < 32 rounds to no change at all — cosmetically the 'chip' visual (RPC_HealthChanged → SetHealthVisual) fires but the number never moves. (4) Ceiling stated correctly: a modified client can push s_health via RPC_ZDOData or broadcast DestroyZDO (:76953-76960, no sender check). Enforcement 'client-honoured' is accurate for both halves.

### 135. Field Injection Through ZNetView.LoadFields

`wildcard:Field Injection Through ZNetView.LoadFields` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Vanilla reflects every public field of every component on an instantiated prefab out of the ZDO — which makes per-portal m_allowAllItems, m_exitDistance and m_activationRange genuinely achievable on a 100 percent vanilla client.


**How it works:** ZNetView.LoadFields (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82669-82739, byte-identical in the client at :82898) is called as the last step of ZNetView.Awake (:82631), immediately before AddInstance. It is a reflection override mechanism baked into vanilla for the modding-adjacent 'spawn a variant' use case, and it is entirely ZDO-driven:

1. `if (!zdo.GetBool('HasFields')) return;` — one gate key on the whole object.
2. `gameObject.GetComponentsInChildren(m_tempComponents)` over List<MonoBehaviour> (so self plus active children).
3. Per component, `if (!zdo.GetBool('HasFields' + typeName)) continue;`
4. For each `BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.Public` field, look up the ZDO key `typeName + '.' + fieldName` and, if present, SetValue. Supported types are exactly int, float, bool, Vector3, string, GameObject (resolved by prefab name) and ItemDrop (resolved by prefab name). Color, enum and arrays are NOT supported.

Applied to a portal, the reachable knobs are: TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems (bool, :143429) — a genuine PER-PORTAL ore policy, read by Teleport at :143533 and by UpdatePortal's glow at :143505; TeleportWorld.m_exitDistance (float, :143413) — per-portal arrival offset, used at :143545; TeleportWorld.m_activationRange (float, :143411); TeleportWorld.m_hoverOffset (float, :143431); Piece.m_canBeRemoved (bool, :136171); Piece.m_comfort (int, :136120 region); Piece.m_allowedInDungeons (bool); WearNTear.m_health (float, :149248); WearNTear.m_burnable, m_ashDamageImmune, m_noRoofWear, m_noSupportWear, m_supports, m_triggerPrivateArea (bools, :149201-149258 region).

Server-side write for an ore-permissive gate: `z.Set('HasFields'.GetStableHashCode(), true); z.Set('HasFieldsTeleportWorld'.GetStableHashCode(), true); z.Set('TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems'.GetStableHashCode(), true); ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals();` Booleans are stored as ints by ZDO.GetBool/Set (:73937-73940), which is what GetBool reads back, so this is a plain ZDO int write.

This directly REFUTES the common 'there are no per-portal knobs server-side' conclusion. The correct statement is: the fields are not RPC'd or ZDO-backed by TeleportWorld itself, but ZNetView has a generic override channel underneath them and the server owns the ZDO. It is client-honoured (a modified client can ignore it), on exactly the same footing as vanilla's own boss gating.

The one hard limitation is timing: LoadFields runs only at instantiation. Flipping the field on a portal a player is already standing next to does nothing until that object is destroyed and recreated in their scene — i.e. they walk about 100 m away (ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea, :82298-82320) and come back, or relog. Note also that TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems cannot lift the Inventory.IsTeleportable toolTier >= 1000 gate, which is checked BEFORE allowAllItems (:68862-68872).


**Player experience:** Two portals side by side at the mining outpost, both stone, both tagged. One is labelled 'ORE ROAD - heavy cargo' and the other 'PASSENGER'. A player loaded with iron walks into the ore gate and it works; the same player walking into the passenger gate gets the normal '$msg_noteleport'. Nothing about the ore gate looks unusual — its ready-glow correctly lights up for a player carrying metal, because UpdatePortal reads the same injected field. The catch a server operator has to explain: after an admin flips a gate's policy, players standing beside it will not see the change until they wander away and come back. In practice the mod flips policy on portals nobody is near, or accepts one relog of latency.


**Failure modes:**
- LoadFields fires only in ZNetView.Awake (:82631) — a live change never reaches an already-instantiated portal until the client destroys and recreates it (~100 m away and back, or a relog)
- Client-honoured only: a modified client simply does not apply the override
- Color fields (m_colorUnconnected, m_colorTargetfound) are NOT supported by LoadFields (:82693-82736) — per-portal colour is ruled out through this route
- GlobalKeys.TeleportAll and m_allowAllItems both sit AFTER the m_toolTier >= 1000 rejection in Inventory.IsTeleportable (:68862-68868); some items can never be carried through
- A wrong key spelling silently does nothing — there is no error path in LoadFields
- HasFields keys are plain ZDO ints and count against the per-ZDO per-type item budget; ZPackage.WriteNumItems corrupts above 32767 (:83237-83246) and ZDODataHelper warns above 100 (:74662-74676)
- A stale HasFieldsTeleportWorld key applies to every TeleportWorld component found in children if a modded prefab has more than one

**Designer citations:** ZNetView.LoadFields — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82669-82739; call site ZNetView.Awake :82631 ; TeleportWorld public fields — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143411-143431 ; TeleportWorld.Teleport reads m_allowAllItems — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143533; m_exitDistance at :143545 ; TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal reads m_allowAllItems — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143505 ; Inventory.IsTeleportable toolTier gate before allowAllItems — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:68860-68881 ; Piece.m_canBeRemoved — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:136171 ; WearNTear public fields — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:149201-149258 ; ZDO.GetBool via GetInt — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73937-73940 ; ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82298-82320


**Open questions:**
- THE single highest-value experiment in this whole report: does LoadFields actually apply a server-authored TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems on a live 1.0.7 vanilla client? IN-GAME: write the three ints server-side, have a player carrying iron leave the area and return, then walk through.
- Is TeleportWorld on the portal prefab root or a child, and are all target components active (LoadFields uses the List overload of GetComponentsInChildren, which excludes inactive by default)? IN-GAME: dump the portal prefab hierarchy and component list.
- Does the portal prefab carry Piece and WearNTear, giving the exact type names for the HasFields keys? IN-GAME: log GetComponents<MonoBehaviour>() type names.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Write-path race, not ownership: ZDO.Set has no owner check, but ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData on the RECEIVER drops any update whose DataRevision <= its local copy (:77108-77118). Server and owning client each bump the same counter independently (:73832-73840), so a server write to a client-owned portal can be silently discarded if the client wrote in the same window (rare for portals, but it is why Game.SetConnection routes to the owner :100637-100651). Do SetOwner(session)+Set+ForceSendZDO, or write while owner==0.
- Awake-order caveat for fields read inside a component's Awake: WearNTear.Awake reads m_health at :149428-149440 (GetFloat(s_health, m_health), world-level scaling). That only sees the override if ZNetView.Awake ran first, which depends on prefab component order (unverifiable from decompile). TeleportWorld itself is safe — every listed field is read at runtime, not in Awake.
- 'Runs at instantiation' includes the PLACING client: Player.PlacePiece → ZNetView.Awake else-branch (:82613-82630) → LoadFields with no HasFields yet, so the builder sees defaults until their scene recreates the object.
- Line-number nit: the option's ':82298-82320 ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea' is correct; ':143429/143413' etc. verified exact.
- Another vanilla caller exists: LocationProxy.SpawnLocation calls m_nview.LoadFields() at :102689 after spawning a proxy location — irrelevant to portals but confirms the mechanism is used by shipped content, not a dead path.
- m_exitDistance is read from the portal being ENTERED and applied at the partner's position (Teleport: pos = target.GetPosition() + target.forward * m_exitDistance + up, :143539-143546). It is a per-SOURCE arrival offset at the destination, not a per-destination arrival offset.
- m_activationRange only feeds Player.GetClosestPlayer for the ready-glow in UpdatePortal (:143497-143507). The actual transit trigger is the child Collider handled by TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143664-143681); Colliders are not MonoBehaviours, so GetComponentsInChildren<MonoBehaviour> cannot resize the trigger. Do not describe m_activationRange as changing the transit zone.
- Add the DataRevision race: ZDO.Set on a client-owned portal races the owner's own writes; a same-window collision drops one side's packet (ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData :77108-77117). Write while owner==0, after SetOwner(session), or re-send after the owner's next revision; verify presence before relying on it for the next instantiation.
- Keys persist in the portal save chunk only if ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() is called after the write (plain Set dirties the normal chunk via SetDirtySector :73839 -> :76694, from which portals are excluded at :77572).
- Injected keys outlive the mod: a vanilla server/client keeps applying them. Reverting a policy requires deleting the 'HasFields*' / 'TeleportWorld.*' keys, not just uninstalling.
- Evidence that arbitrary prefabs work without Inspector support: the vanilla client `spawn` command path writes the identical key set and calls LoadFields on any spawned prefab (client :44423-44450).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism verified line-by-line. ZNetView.Awake (server :82560-82632) runs LoadFields() at :82631 AFTER the if/else, i.e. for both network-created (m_initZDO) and locally-created ZDOs, immediately before AddInstance. LoadFields (:82669-82739) is byte-identical to the client copy (:82898-82968, diffed). It gates on zdo.GetBool("HasFields") then per-component "HasFields"+TypeName, then reflects BindingFlags.Instance|Public fields and reads "Type.field" keys for int/float/bool/Vector3/string/GameObject(prefab name)/ItemDrop(prefab name) only. The open question from the prior review ('does it work on prefabs the Inspector did not ship with HasFields') is settled: HasFields is a ZDO int key, not a prefab property, and vanilla's own Terminal `spawn` command (:44423-44450) writes HasFields/HasFields<Type>/Type.field onto an arbitrary freshly-spawned prefab and calls LoadFields — there is no Inspector involvement anywhere. ZDO.GetBool(string) = GetInt(hash)!=0 (:73932-73940) and GetBool(string,out bool) (:73942-73949) exist as claimed; ZDO.Set(string,bool) at :73680. TeleportWorld public fields at :143411 (m_activationRange), :143413 (m_exitDistance), :143429 (m_allowAllItems), :143431 (m_hoverOffset); TeleportWorld.Awake (:143438-143450) caches none of them; UpdatePortal reads m_allowAllItems at :143505 and m_activationRange at :143495; Teleport reads m_allowAllItems :143533 and m_exitDistance :143545. Inventory.IsTeleportable (:68860-68880) tests m_toolTier>=1000 before allowAllItems, as claimed. Save/reload: the keys are ordinary ints, not in ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes (:78689-78693), not in ZDOHelper.s_stripOldData/s_stripOldInts (:75550-75615), and ZDO.Deserialize (:74206-74245) is additive (ZDOExtraData.Add) so the owning client's own writes never remove them. Client re-instantiation after leaving the active area (PointInsideActiveArea :82298-82320, 1.5*64 m Chebyshev) re-runs LoadFields as claimed.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism verified end to end. ZNetView.LoadFields (server :82669-82739) is byte-identical to the client copy (:82898-82968, diffed), is called unconditionally from ZNetView.Awake immediately before AddInstance (:82631 / client :82860), and is gated purely on ZDO int keys read via ZDO.GetBool(string) -> GetStableHashCode -> ZDOExtraData.GetInt (:73932-73950). It is NOT limited to prefabs the Inspector shipped with HasFields: the vanilla client's own `spawn` console path writes exactly these keys ('HasFields', 'HasFields'+component, 'Component.field') onto an arbitrary prefab's ZDO and then calls LoadFields (client :44423-44450), and LocationProxy calls it again after proxy spawn (client :103150). Field type coverage is exactly int/float/bool/Vector3/string/GameObject/ItemDrop as claimed. TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems, m_exitDistance, m_activationRange, m_hoverOffset are public instance fields (:143411-143431) read lazily at UpdatePortal (:143505) and Teleport (:143533, :143545), so Awake ordering is irrelevant for them. Inventory.IsTeleportable tests m_toolTier>=1000 before allowAllItems (:68860-68881) as claimed. Keys are ordinary ints: they replicate (ZDO.Serialize) and save; ZDO.Deserialize merges via ZDOExtraData.Add without clearing (:74232-74238, :74896), so a peer's later sends never strip them. Save persistence requires SetDirtyPortals (only ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection Portal, AddIfPortal, HandleDestroyedZDO and Load set DirtyPortalObjects: :73656-73677, :77751, :76986, :76539). Instantiation-only timing is correct: RemoveObjects destroys the instance when the ZDO leaves the near set (:82196-82225); portals are only ever in the near set because FindDistantObjects reads m_objectsBySector only (:77384-77398), so ~1.5 zones / 112 m radius (PointInsideActiveArea :82298-82320). Enforcement is honestly client-honoured. Two real caveats the option omits: (1) non-owner write revision race — the server's Set bumps DataRevision (:73832-73840); if the owning client also writes in the same send window, each side drops the other's packet (`num4 <= zDO.DataRevision` :77108-77117) and the client never sees the key until the server writes again; claim ownership (SetOwner) or write while owner==0 / a player is not nearby (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76924 re-assigns ownership every 2 s). (2) The mechanism survives mod uninstall — vanilla keeps honouring the keys — so reverting requires actively removing them.

### 136. Portal As Trigger, RPC As Transport

`wildcard:Portal As Trigger, RPC As Transport` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** medium-large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Abandon the connection field entirely: poll character ZDO positions near a portal and force-teleport with RPC_TeleportPlayer — which breaks the one-destination-per-ZDO ceiling and gives true multi-destination hubs.


**How it works:** A ZDO holds at most ONE connection — ZDOExtraData.s_connections is `Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>` and ZDOConnection carries one readonly type and one readonly target (:74794, :75524-75534). Simultaneous multi-destination hubs are therefore structurally impossible through the vanilla mechanism. This option sidesteps it completely.

Leave the portal's Portal connection at ZDOID.None (or pointed anywhere). The portal never teleports anyone — TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 returns silently (:143519). Instead, the server polls: `foreach (peer in ZNet.instance.GetPeers()) { var z = ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID); ... }` at 0.2-0.4 s, comparing z.GetPosition() against every entry of ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals() (:77643, the live zero-alloc dictionary) within about 3-4 m. Position freshness is good: the owning client's ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync writes zdo.SetPosition every physics tick (:87527-87540) and ZDOMan services one peer per Update on a 0.05 s timer (:76843-76861), so character positions are 50-100 ms stale regardless of distance.

On a hit, send `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, 'RPC_TeleportPlayer', pos, rot, true)`. The handler is registered on every vanilla client in Chat.Awake (:41627) and its entire body is `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport);` — no sender check, no admin check, no key check, no item check (:41962-41968). A second, ZDO-scoped path exists: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, 'RPC_TeleportTo', pos, rot, true)`, handled by Character.RPC_TeleportTo (:4126-4132), registered for every Character in Character.Awake (:886) and owner-gated so it cannot be misdirected.

What this buys: the DESTINATION is chosen by the server at the moment of transit, per player, per condition. A hub can route by player identity (character ZDO ZDOVars.s_playerID), by the emote they last performed (ZDOVars.s_emote / s_emoteID), by a map ping they sent (Chat.SendPing broadcasts 'ChatMessage' to peer 0 with the clicked world Vector3), by time of day, by a rotation counter, or round-robin. It also bypasses vanilla's ore check entirely, which is a design decision the operator must make consciously.

Mandatory pre-checks, all readable from the character ZDO: skip if GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead) (Player.UpdateTeleport runs only inside the !IsDead() branch of FixedUpdate at :10213/:10226, so a teleport sent to a dead player latches m_teleporting true and never executes); skip if GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed) (Player.UpdateAttach at :10217 runs BEFORE UpdateTeleport at :10226 and re-snaps to the attach point every tick, and AttachStop early-returns while sleeping at :15892). And rate-limit per player to at least 12 s: Player.TeleportTo refuses while IsTeleporting() or while m_teleportCooldown < 2f (:15309-15316), and m_teleportCooldown is zeroed every tick of a teleport (:15336), so the dead window is the whole 8+ s teleport plus 2 s.


**Player experience:** A single great archway at spawn labelled 'THE WAYGATE'. Walking into it does not take you to a fixed partner. Before stepping through you open your map and middle-click a location you have discovered; that ping goes to the server. You walk into the arch, and after the usual black screen you are standing at the spot you marked. If you did not ping anything, it takes you to the destination you used last. One archway, unlimited destinations, on a completely unmodified client, with the standard portal fade and no visual tell that anything unusual happened. The failure mode players will notice: if you step in twice within about twelve seconds, the second attempt does nothing at all and gives no message.


**Failure modes:**
- Every failure is silent and one-directional: TeleportTo returns false (:15309, :15313), both RPC handlers discard the return (:41966, :4130), and no reply is ever sent — the server's only confirmation is watching the character ZDO position change roughly 2 s later
- The real cooldown is not 2 s after the RPC; m_teleportCooldown is zeroed every tick WHILE teleporting (:15336), so the refusal window spans the entire teleport plus 2 s, at least 10-12 s for distantTeleport
- A dead player latches: the teleport is accepted, m_teleporting goes true, and UpdateTeleport never runs (:10213/:10226). Check ZDOVars.s_dead first
- An attached or sleeping player ping-pongs between the attach point and the target every tick because UpdateAttach runs first (:10217, :15818-15836); check ZDOVars.s_inBed first
- Position polling at 0.2-0.4 s can miss a fast player; a 4 m radius at 5 m/s and 0.5 s sampling is about the floor
- This bypasses NoPortals, NoBossPortals, PrivateArea and the ore check completely — every rule the operator wants must be re-implemented in the mod
- RPC_TeleportPlayer is not a privileged channel: vanilla's own client-side `recall` command sends it peer-to-peer (:44548-44556) and RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID is a self-report (:83487-83495), so shipping this feature obliges the mod to also harden ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC
- With distantTeleport true the player is invulnerable and input-locked for ~8 s (Player.CanMove at :14423-14428, damage suppression at :2425/:2429/:2582) — abusable as a stun if triggered by another player

**Open questions:**
- What poll interval and radius reliably catch a sprinting player through a portal frame without false positives from someone standing nearby? IN-GAME: log character ZDO positions at 0.1 s while a player runs laps through a portal and measure the dwell time inside 4 m.
- What is the real per-peer cadence at which the server receives character position updates on a loaded server? CreateSyncList is per-peer round-robin on a 0.05 s timer (:76843), so it degrades with player count. IN-GAME: log position-change timestamps for one player with 1, 5 and 20 peers online.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Enforcement: client-honoured. RPC_TeleportPlayer is a request the vanilla client obeys; position authority and the teleport state machine live on the client.
- No 'ChatMessage' handler exists on a dedicated server: it is registered in Chat.Awake (:41626), a UI MonoBehaviour that is not instantiated headless. The mod must ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<Vector3,int,UserInfo,string>("ChatMessage", ...) itself (HandleRoutedRPC :83630-83640 dispatches by hash from m_functions). Also RPC_RoutedRPC (:83617-83628) does NOT validate m_senderPeerID against the socket — the 'verified identity' of a ping is the client-supplied field in the routed packet; verify against ZNet.GetPeer(rpc) if identity matters.
- With the hub's Portal connection left at None, Game.ConnectPortals phase 2 (:100608-100622) will pair it with any other unconnected portal carrying the same tag every 5 s; the hub needs a unique tag or the mod must own ConnectPortals. It also renders as 'unconnected' (no glow, HaveTarget false :143630-143637) on every vanilla client — there is a visual tell.
- Position freshness is bounded by the CLIENT→server send cadence (client ZDOMan.Update timer 0.05 s + frame, queue cap 10240 bytes :77008-77016), not only the server→peer scheduler cited at :76843-76861.
- Trigger geometry: the server only has the portal ZDO position (base of the arch) and the character ZDO position; a 3-4 m radius also catches players editing the tag or standing beside it. Needs an entry-edge/dwell rule, not a radius test.
- Player experience: an unlinked portal is visibly unconnected (no glow, '[unconnected]' hover, m_target_found off). Either accept that tell or accept that vanilla's own trigger wins if the portal is linked to anything resolvable.
- Do not point the portal 'anywhere': a resolvable Portal connection lets TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter -> Teleport -> TeleportTo run first on the client and the server's later RPC is refused at IsTeleporting (:15311). The only compatible state is connection == None.
- Replace the '3-4 m sphere' with an edge-triggered, rotation-aware crossing test on consecutive samples plus re-arm-on-exit; a static sphere yanks players who merely stand beside the portal and ping-pongs at any portal-shaped destination (arrival is exitDistance 1 m in front).
- Ping destinations carry the SENDER's current y (Chat.SendPing :42061). Compute y server-side from WorldGenerator (colliders unavailable), else the client sits on the black screen until the 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback (:15364-15371) and may arrive inside terrain/buildings.
- Enforcement wording: the destination is server-chosen, but the teleport act is a client-honoured RPC; a modified client can ignore it (it cannot, however, use this portal to go anywhere else).
- Effort: large, not medium-large — the trigger-geometry/edge logic, y-resolution, and per-player state machine are the bulk of the work; the RPC itself is trivial.

**Verifier reasoning:**

The single-connection ceiling (s_connections :74794, ZDOConnection :75524-75534, GetConnectionZDOID exact-type :75094-75102) is real. So the design works on a vanilla client. But the enforcement label is wrong under the ground rules: the act of teleporting is executed by the client (owner of its character ZDO), the trigger is inferred from a client-authored position, and nothing stops a modded client that owns the portal ZDO (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76924 hands it over within 2 s) from writing its own Portal connection and using vanilla transit. The server chooses a destination and asks; the client honours. That is client-honoured, not server-enforced.
- [vanilla-reality:downgraded] The transport primitive is real: Chat.Awake registers 'RPC_TeleportPlayer' on every vanilla client (:41627) and the handler is unconditionally `Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport)` (:41962-41968); Character.Awake registers the owner-gated 'RPC_TeleportTo' (:886, :4128-4134); ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC routes to a peer id with no permission check (:83554-83596). Player.TeleportTo refuses while IsTeleporting or m_teleportCooldown<2 (:15304-15316) and UpdateTeleport zeroes the cooldown every tick (:15331-15340); single-slot ZDOConnection is confirmed (:74794, :75524-75534). Position freshness claim holds (ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync :87527-87540; ZDOMan send timer :76843-76861). But the claimed player experience is wrong and the trigger design is under-specified. (a) 'No visual tell' is false: with the connection at None, HaveTarget() is false, so the portal's emission stays m_colorUnconnected, m_target_found never activates, and the hover text reads '$piece_portal_unconnected' (client :144193-144205, :144217-144225). (b) 'Or pointed anywhere' is worse: any resolvable target makes vanilla's TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter fire Teleport() on the client instantly, TeleportTo latches m_teleporting, and the server's RPC — which arrives 50-100 ms of ZDO lag plus a 200-400 ms poll later — is refused at IsTeleporting (:15311). Vanilla's destination wins every race. (c) A 3-4 m sphere around the portal ZDO position is not a trigger volume: players standing beside the portal to read/retag it are inside it and get yanked; and any destination that is itself a portal puts the arrival 1 m in front of it, so after the 2 s cooldown the poll fires again — ping-pong unless the mod implements enter-edge/re-arm-on-exit semantics equivalent to OnTriggerEnter. (d) Chat.SendPing sets vector.y = the sender's CURRENT y (:42058-42063), so a pinged destination has the wrong altitude; ZoneSystem height queries are collider-dead on the server, so the mod must use WorldGenerator math; a wrong y is only self-corrected by the client at m_teleportTimer>15 s via GetSolidHeight (:15364-15371) — a 15 s black screen instead of 8. (e) Dead-player latch is harmless (the Player object is destroyed on respawn) but skipping is still right. Enforcement: the route decision is server-owned and the portal itself cannot take a vanilla client anywhere, but delivery is a client-executed RPC the client merely honours.

### 137. Portals As A Data Store

`wildcard:Portals As A Data Store` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portal ZDOs are the only always-resident, always-saved, distance-independent ZDO collection in the game — and they take arbitrary mod-private keys for free.


**How it works:** Portals have four properties no other ZDO family has. (1) They live in their own dictionary ZDOMan.m_portalObjects (:76039) and are removed from the sector array by AddIfPortal (:77750), so they are never unloaded and never released — ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS only reassigns ownership (:76872-76924) and FlushClientObjects is client-only. (2) They are enumerable world-wide for free with ZDOMan.GetPortalList() (:77648) with zero bookkeeping and no prefab-name guess. (3) They save to a dedicated ChunkPortal file (ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal, :113180), written wholesale with NO Persistent filter whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set (:77621-77632). (4) They are loaded straight into m_portalObjects at world load, bypassing FilterZDO entirely (:76474-76483).

A ZDO's extra data is seven independent int-keyed dictionaries — float, Vector3, Quaternion, int, long, string, byte[] (ZDOExtraData s_floats ... s_byteArrays, :74757-74771). Keys are arbitrary ints; vanilla just uses name.GetStableHashCode(). So a mod can hang whatever it likes on a portal: a network id, a rotation index, a cooldown timestamp, an owning faction, a toll price, a puzzle state, an ordered route list serialized into one byte array. It round-trips through both the network (ZDO.Serialize :74112-74174) and the save with no work.

The correct write discipline: ZDO.Set has no ownership check on any overload (:73601-73727), so write freely; but ALWAYS follow with ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702), because only ConnectionType.Portal SetConnection, AddIfPortal and HandleDestroyedZDO set DirtyPortalObjects — a plain field write goes through IncreaseDataRevision to SetDirtySector (:73839), which dirties a normal chunk that portals are explicitly excluded from (:77572). Without SetDirtyPortals the whole portal file is skipped and every portal reverts to its last-dirtied state.

Two hard budgets. ZPackage.WriteNumItems (:83237-83246) encodes a per-ZDO per-type item count in one byte below 128 and two bytes up to 32767 — above that the stream corrupts; ZDODataHelper.WriteToDisk logs a warning above 100 items of a single type (:74662-74676). And ZDOMan.SendZDOs (:77053-77062) re-serializes the ENTIRE ZDO on every send with no delta encoding, under a 10240-byte per-peer queue cap (:77010-77016). So: a handful of scalar keys plus one byte array, never two hundred int keys.

One global landmine: ZDOExtraData.s_sessionOnly is a GLOBAL hash set (:74776) seeded from the 16 entries of ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes (:78689-78693) and from anything ever passed to AddSessionHash. Any key in it is stripped from the save for EVERY ZDO in the world. Never reuse s_support, s_inUse, s_alert, s_velHash and friends for portal metadata.


**Player experience:** Invisible to players — this is infrastructure. What they see downstream is that the network remembers: the hub they set to 'Ashlands' is still pointed at Ashlands after a server restart, a gate they unlocked stays unlocked, a toll they paid stays paid, and the rotation schedule picks up exactly where it left off rather than resetting. Nothing in the world save is a separate mod file that can drift out of sync with the world; the state travels with the portals, which means it also travels with world backups and world copies.


**Failure modes:**
- A field write without ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() is silently lost at the next world save — the single most likely bug in the whole mod
- ZDOIDs are renumbered on every world load (ZDO.Load sets m_uid via ZDOID.SetID), so a portal's identity must be derived from position, tag, or a mod-written key — never from its ZDOID
- Reusing any of the 16 ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes strips that key from the save for every ZDO in the world, not just portals
- More than 100 keys of one type on one ZDO logs a warning; more than 32767 corrupts the wire stream
- Every extra byte is re-sent in full on every ZDO sync to every nearby peer (no delta encoding), so a large byte array on a hub portal is real recurring bandwidth
- A nearby owning client can clobber the whole ZDO with a higher-revision push (RPC_ZDOData :77103-77132) — conflict resolution is whole-ZDO, not per-field

**Open questions:**
- Does a portal ZDO carrying mod-private keys round-trip cleanly through the ChunkPortal save, including a byte array? IN-GAME: write a 512-byte array plus five ints to a portal, force a save, restart, and read them back.
- Does ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash (Type.Int/Long/String, :75390-75407) usefully index mod keys on portals, given portals live outside m_objectsBySector? It scans the field dictionaries directly so it should. IN-GAME: write a marker int to three portals and query it.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- 'Only always-resident, distance-independent ZDO collection' is an overclaim. On a dedicated server EVERY ZDO is resident in m_objectsByID for the whole session (nothing on the server path unloads ZDOs; FlushClientObjects is client-only). What is unique to portals is the cheap enumeration, the exclusion from sector churn, and the no-Persistent-filter save. Network delivery is NOT distance-independent: CreateSyncList → FindSectorObjects → FindObjects (:77212-77240, :77368-77381) only includes m_portalObjects entries whose sector is inside the peer's scanned area; remote portal ZDOs reach a client only via ForceSendZDO (Game.SetConnection :100643) or the client's own RequestZDO (:77684-77692, no prefab check).
- 'Write freely' needs the revision caveat: the receiver drops updates with DataRevision <= its local copy (RPC_ZDOData :77108-77118), and portals near a player are owned by that player within 2 s (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76924). A concurrent client write can silently discard the server's key write. Use the Game.SetConnection pattern (SetOwner(session) then Set then ForceSendZDO :100637-100651) or write when owner==0.
- Key naming: also avoid every hash in ZDOHelper.s_stripOldData/s_stripOldFloats/s_stripOldVecs/s_stripOldQuats/s_stripOldStringData/s_stripOldLongData/s_stripOldUnknownLongData (:75550-75618) — ZDOMan strips those from every ZDO at load (:78213-78223). s_stripOldUnknownLongData is 39 raw uint hashes, so a mod long key has a tiny but nonzero collision risk; prefer int/string/byte[] keys.
- ZDOIDs are reassigned at load (m_nextUid = ZDOID.m_loadID + 1 :76525), so a route list serialized as ZDOIDs into a byte array does not survive a restart; store a stable identity (tag+position or a mod-assigned id key) instead.
- GetSectorIndex is computed from m_position (:73776-73779), so m_portalObjects keys are position-derived — never move a portal ZDO's position after it is filed.
- 'Only always-resident, distance-independent ZDO collection' is overstated for a dedicated server: the server never runs ZNetScene.RemoveObjects, so every persistent ZDO is always resident there; the genuinely unique properties are (a) free enumeration with no prefab scan, (b) the ChunkPortal save path with no Persistent filter and no FilterZDO. Portals are still sector-bucketed and replicated to clients by sector via FindObjects (:77367-77381) — replication is not distance-independent.
- Never store a ZDOID inside a mod key (byte array, long pair, 'ordered route list'): ZDO.Load re-issues every id (`m_uid.SetID(++ZDOID.m_loadID)`, :74549-74552). Only the connection slot (via hash data) and vanilla's s_zdoidUser conversion survive a reload. Reference other portals by tag/position or by a mod-assigned stable id key on the target.
- Non-owner write race: the server's Set bumps DataRevision; if the owning client writes in the same send window, ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData drops whichever packet is not strictly newer (:77108-77117) — the client's copy can miss the key (irrelevant for a server-private store; relevant when a client must see the key, e.g. LoadFields). The server's own copy is what gets saved.
- ZDO.Set still dirties a normal chunk uselessly (SetDirtySector on a Persistent ZDO) — harmless but means each portal write also forces a normal chunk rewrite.
- Portal chunk is written in full whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set (:77621-77632) — a high-frequency counter (per-transit writes) makes every autosave rewrite all portals; batch counters on a slow tick.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Core claims hold. m_portalObjects declared :76039; AddIfPortal (:77732-77752) files by Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash membership, RemoveFromSector's the ZDO and sets DirtyPortalObjects; ZDO.SetSector early-returns for portal prefabs (:73752-73757). ### 138. Non-Portals As Portals — Extending Game.PortalPrefabHash At Runtime

`wildcard:Non-Portals As Portals — Extending Game.PortalPrefabHash At Runtime` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


PortalPrefabHash is a mutable List<int> behind a private setter, so an arbitrary prefab can be enrolled into the portal registry, the portal save chunk and vanilla's own pairing.


**How it works:** Game.PortalPrefabHash is declared `public List<int> PortalPrefabHash { get; private set; }` (:100021) and populated in Game.Awake from the Inspector list m_portalPrefabs (:100027-100032). The SETTER is private but the LIST OBJECT is not — `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Add(someHash)` is a legal, no-reflection mutation of live game state.

Everything portal-specific keys off membership in that list, in four places: ZDOMan.AddIfPortal (:77734) decides whether a new ZDO is filed in m_portalObjects and removed from the sector array; ZDO.SetSector (:73754) early-returns, freezing the sector key; ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) excludes it from normal chunk saves; and GetSaveClonePerChunk (:77621) includes it in ChunkPortal.

Adding a hash makes any FUTURE ZDO of that prefab a portal for all four purposes, and makes it appear in ZDOMan.GetPortalList() and therefore in Game.ConnectPortals's tag-pairing loop (:100592-100622). It does NOT retroactively re-file existing ZDOs — AddIfPortal only runs from CreateNewZDO (:76689) and from the RPC_ZDOData deserialize loop (:77132), so already-loaded instances of that prefab stay in the sector array until they are destroyed and recreated. Conversely, `.Remove(hash)` does not un-register already-tracked ZDOs from m_portalObjects.

The DANGEROUS half is the mirror image: removing a portal hash, or adding a hash for a prefab that already has thousands of instances in the world, changes where those ZDOs are saved. Adding a common prefab hash means every new instance goes into the single global ChunkPortal file, which is written in full whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set — a pathological save-size and save-time regression.

The genuinely useful applications are narrow and deliberate: (a) enrolling a modded portal piece from another server mod so vanilla's own pairing handles it for free; (b) enrolling a rare marker prefab so that mod-created network anchors get the always-resident, always-saved, distance-independent treatment portals get; (c) in reverse, NOT enrolling an anchor so it is invisible to vanilla's pairer while still being a legal teleport destination (see The Void Anchor).

The converse question — can a portal be made into a non-portal — is effectively no: removing the hash after ZDOs exist leaves them stranded in m_portalObjects with a frozen sector key and no path back into the sector array, because ZDO.SetSector for a ZDO whose current prefab is no longer in the list would then try to AddToSector but the ZDO was already RemoveFromSector'd, and nothing re-triggers it.


**Player experience:** Nothing directly visible. What players notice is that a modded portal piece from a different mod suddenly behaves exactly like a vanilla one — it pairs by tag, it survives restarts, it shows up in the server's portal census and its Discord reports — with no per-mod integration code. And, in the other direction, that admin waypoints the server maintains never show up in anyone's portal list and cannot be accidentally paired to by a player who happens to pick the same tag.


**Failure modes:**
- Adding a hash does not retroactively move existing ZDOs into m_portalObjects — only ZDOs created or received afterwards (AddIfPortal call sites :76689 and :77132)
- Removing a hash strands already-tracked ZDOs in m_portalObjects permanently and they are never reachable from the sector array again
- Enrolling a common prefab dumps every new instance into the one global ChunkPortal file, which is rewritten in full on every dirty save — a real save-size and save-time regression
- Portal-hash ZDOs are exempt from ZDO.SetSector (:73752), so an enrolled prefab that MOVES (anything with a Rigidbody) silently stops syncing to clients at its new location
- Load order matters: PortalPrefabHash is filled in Game.Awake (:100027), so the mutation must happen after that and before any relevant ZDO is created or received
- Another mod doing the same thing will collide; the list has no ownership model

- Does Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Add actually take effect for ZDOs received over RPC_ZDOData after the mutation? The AddIfPortal call at :77132 happens per received ZDO, so it should. IN-GAME: enrol a marker prefab, have a client place one, and check GetPortalList().
- What happens on world load if the saved ChunkPortal file contains a prefab hash that is no longer in PortalPrefabHash at boot? LoadChunks puts it straight into m_portalObjects regardless (:76480). IN-GAME: enrol, save, remove the enrolment, restart, and observe.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Enrolling a prefab with existing instances causes SILENT DATA LOSS, not just a size regression. The chunked load path (LoadChunks :76484-76490) sends every non-ChunkPortal ZDO through FilterZDO → InitialAddToSector (:76505-76510) with NO PortalPrefabHash check; only the legacy monolithic ZDOMan.Load (:76576, :76595) files by hash. Those pre-existing instances therefore sit in the sector array, where AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) now EXCLUDES them, while the ChunkPortal writer (:77621-77632) only iterates m_portalObjects. The next dirty save of their chunk writes them nowhere. Enrolling before world load does not help (same chunk path). A mod that enrols a prefab must re-file its existing instances itself (the private AddIfPortal via reflection, or destroy/recreate) before any save.
- ZDO.SetSector for an enrolled prefab returns early (:73752-73757) but the instance stays in m_objectsBySector at its load-time sector — RemoveFromSector is only done by AddIfPortal — so until re-filed it is neither properly a portal nor properly a sector object.
- The vanilla CLIENT's PortalPrefabHash is unchanged. Client-side AddIfPortal/SetSector treat the prefab as a normal piece; this is harmless for data but means client-side ZNetScene distance handling for it is ordinary.
- The reverse (Remove) analysis needs one more consequence: ZDOs already in m_portalObjects are still written to ChunkPortal (no hash check in :77624-77630) and reloaded into m_portalObjects (:76474-76483), so they persist as portals forever; additionally, with the hash gone ZDO.SetSector no longer early-returns and a position change would AddToSector them, double-listing them. 'Effectively no' stands.
- Feasibility for use (a)/(b) is fine; effort should include the re-filing pass and a guard that refuses to enrol a hash that already has instances outside m_portalObjects.
- Enrolling a prefab hash that has existing ZDO instances silently deletes those instances at the next save: they remain in m_objectsBySector but are excluded from normal chunks (:77572) and are not in m_portalObjects (:77624). Only enroll prefabs with zero existing instances, or re-file existing ones via reflection into m_portalObjects before the next save.
- Never Remove a hash while instances exist: HandleDestroyedZDO (:76980-76987) skips the m_portalObjects removal when the hash is absent, then releases the ZDO to the pool — leaving a dangling pooled ZDO in m_portalObjects that GetPortalList/ConnectPortals iterate.
- Enrolled non-portal prefabs are tag-paired by Game.ConnectPortals like any portal; an empty-tag anchor pairs with any empty-tag player portal. Give anchors a reserved tag no player can type (portal tags are capped at 10 chars by TextInput; use a longer/control-character tag).
- Clients never see the enrollment (vanilla PortalPrefabHash); the enrolled prefab works only as a DESTINATION (position/rotation read from its ZDO), never as a source — it has no TeleportWorld/TeleportWorldTrigger.
- Application (a) — enrolling another mod's portal piece — requires that piece to actually carry a TeleportWorld component on the client for transit; enrollment alone only gets it pairing/persistence.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Game.PortalPrefabHash is `public List<int> PortalPrefabHash { get; private set; } = new List<int>()` (:100021), populated in Game.Awake (:100027-100032) from m_portalPrefabs (:99828); Add() on the list is a legal mutation. The list is consulted in exactly six places: ZDO.SetSector (:73754), legacy ZDOMan.Load (:76576, :76595), HandleDestroyedZDO (:76980), AddObjectsPerChunk (:77572) and AddIfPortal (:77734). AddIfPortal is called only from CreateNewZDO (:76689) and RPC_ZDOData (:77132), so enrolment affects only future/network-received ZDOs, as claimed; a client-placed instance of a modded prefab arrives via RPC_ZDOData and is filed. Game.ConnectPortals iterates GetPortalList (:100592) so enrolled prefabs are tag-paired. However the option misjudges the danger of enrolling a prefab that already has instances, and the 'save-size regression' framing understates it.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The mutability claim is literal: `public List<int> PortalPrefabHash { get; private set; } = new List<int>();` (:100021), populated in Game.Awake from m_portalPrefabs (:99828, :100027-100032); the list instance is public and Add/Remove are ordinary calls. All four membership tests are as claimed: AddIfPortal (:77734), ZDO.SetSector early-return (:73752-73757), AddObjectsPerChunk exclusion (:77572), and the save/load portal chunk (:77621-77632, legacy load :76575-76600). AddIfPortal runs from CreateNewZDO (:76685-76691) and the RPC_ZDOData deserialize loop (:77128), so enrollment is prospective only. Game.ConnectPortals iterates GetPortalList (:100589-100627) so enrolled ZDOs are tag-paired by vanilla. But the option under-states the hazards. (1) Enrolling a hash that already has instances is data loss, not just 'they stay in the sector array': at the next save AddObjectsPerChunk skips them (hash now in the list, :77572) and GetSaveClonePerChunk only writes m_portalObjects (:77624) — those ZDOs are written to NO chunk and vanish on the next load. Re-filing them needs reflection into the private m_portalObjects. (2) Removing a hash is worse than 'stranded': HandleDestroyedZDO only removes from m_portalObjects when the hash is present (:76980-76987) and then ZDOPool.Release()s the ZDO — a portal destroyed after its hash was removed leaves a released, recyclable ZDO object inside m_portalObjects, and GetPortalList/ConnectPortals will iterate it. (3) The mod runs only on the server: clients keep the vanilla list, so client-side AddIfPortal/SetSector treat the enrolled prefab as a normal object — harmless, but the enrolled prefab has no TeleportWorld component, so it can only ever be a destination (client Teleport uses ZDOMan.GetZDO(target) position/rotation, :144250-144257, and TargetFound RequestZDOs it, :144386-144395; RPC_RequestZDO honours any id, :77689-77692). (4) Tag pairing applies to enrolled ZDOs: an anchor with an empty tag matches every blank-tag player portal in FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100664-100679); enrolled anchors need a unique, unguessable tag or vanilla will randomly route players into them.
