### 139. The Connection Field Beyond Portals

`wildcard:The Connection Field Beyond Portals` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


An honest map of the other ConnectionType values, what abusing them buys and costs, including the one-connection-per-ZDO ceiling and a latent creature-spawner suppression trick.


**How it works:** ConnectionType is a [Flags] byte enum with None=0, Portal=1, SyncTransform=2, Spawned=3, Target=0x10 (:74747-74754). Note Portal, SyncTransform and Spawned are NOT independent bits — 1, 2 and 3 overlap, so Spawned is bitwise Portal|SyncTransform. Only Target is a real flag. ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID (:75094-75102) requires EXACT type equality, which is what keeps these from cross-matching.

A ZDO holds exactly one connection (s_connections is Dictionary<ZDOID, ZDOConnection>, one readonly type and one readonly target, :74794, :75524-75534). Consequences:
- Writing Portal onto a player's character ZDO destroys their SyncTransform ship-parent link (ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync at :87548 writes it).
- Writing Portal onto a CreatureSpawner's ZDO destroys its Spawned link.
- A portal can never simultaneously be a Portal endpoint and a SyncTransform child, so a portal physically parented to a moving ship is structurally impossible.
- Writing Portal|Target (0x10 | 1 = 0x11) onto a live portal makes GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) return None, so vanilla treats it as unconnected and re-pairs it. The Target bit belongs only to the save-hash representation.

SyncTransform (:87542-87571) is written by the RIDER's client when standing on a Rigidbody with a ZNetView, alongside ZDOVars.s_relPosHash, s_relRotHash and s_attachJointHash. It is a latch, written only when the parent changes (:87546). Reading it server-side is the documented way to know a player is on a ship — though ShipAttachment's ZDOVars.s_user read on the Ship's own ZDO (written by ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl :141332) is stronger because it has no Inspector dependency. There is also a genuine vanilla bug worth not building on: OwnerSync writes relative velocity to ZDOVars.s_velHash while SyncPosition reads s_velRelHash (:87561 vs :87647), so velRel is never written by anything.

Spawned (:5649-5656, :5820) is CreatureSpawner's link to the creature it made. `SpawnedCreatureStillExists(connectionZDOID)` plus `m_respawnTimeMinuts <= 0f` means a spawner whose Spawned connection points at ANY still-resident ZDO never spawns again. Writing `spawnerZdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Spawned, somePermanentPortalZdoId)` therefore permanently silences a fixed creature spawner from the server — an off-label but real world-governance primitive, and a reason a portal mod must be careful never to write a Portal connection onto a non-portal ZDO it did not create.

The save-time collapse is the hard ceiling on all of it: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) gives the source ZDO {type, h} and then OVERWRITES the target's slot with {type|Target, h}. With one slot per ZDO, the disk format can express only a pairwise perfect matching. Rings lose links, one-way links come back bidirectional via ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77879-77885), and self-loops are erased outright (:75472-75475, target != None so the source slot is immediately overwritten).


**Player experience:** Indirectly visible as topology that vanilla could not produce: a one-way drop gate that only works in one direction, a ring of six portals where each leads to the next rather than to a random partner, a fan-in where four remote outposts all exit at one hub. All of it holds at runtime because Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 never checks reciprocity (:100601 tests only that the partner resolves, shares the tag, and is itself non-None). All of it quietly degenerates after a server restart into ordinary random pairs unless the mod re-asserts it on world load — which players experience as 'the network scrambled overnight' if the mod forgets.


**Failure modes:**
- Non-pairwise topologies are runtime-only. Rings above 2, one-way links and self-loops do not survive RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) — they must be re-asserted after every world load
- Writing any connection type onto a ZDO that already has one destroys the old one silently; ZDOExtraData.SetConnection just replaces (:74951-74960)
- ZDO.UpdateConnection (:74962-74976) writes nothing at all when no entry exists — it can never CREATE a link, only overwrite one. TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag uses it (:143595), which is why retagging a never-connected portal is a no-op on the connection field
- Writing Portal|Target onto a live portal makes vanilla read it as unconnected and re-pair it
- Suppressing a CreatureSpawner via a Spawned connection is off-label and will confuse any other world-governance mod inspecting spawner state
- GetAllConnectionZDOIDs(ConnectionType) (:75414-75427) reads s_connectionsHashData — the SAVE-time table — not the live s_connections, so it is empty at steady state. Use the parameterless overload (:75409) or iterate GetPortalList()

**Designer citations:** ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType enum — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74747-74754 ; ZDOExtraData.s_connections and class ZDOConnection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74794, 75524-75534 ; ZDOExtraData.SetConnection / UpdateConnection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74951-74976 ; ZDOExtraData.GetConnectionZDOID exact type match — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75094-75102 ; ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75461-75478 ; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals load-time hash relink makes links reciprocal — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77850-77893 (:77879-77885) ; ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync SyncTransform write — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87542-87571; velHash/velRelHash mismatch :87561 vs :87647 ; CreatureSpawner Spawned connection — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:5649-5656, 5820 ; Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 does not check reciprocity — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100600-100604


**Open questions:**
- Does SpawnedCreatureStillExists actually accept an arbitrary non-creature ZDO as 'still alive'? It takes a ZDOID and the guard at :5651 short-circuits on m_respawnTimeMinuts. IN-GAME: write a Spawned connection to a portal ZDO on a fixed draugr spawner and watch for 30 minutes.
- Does the portal prefab carry a ZSyncTransform at all (which would make SyncTransform parenting of a portal meaningful)? IN-GAME: dump the prefab components.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Do NOT point Spawned at a portal ZDO. At save, RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75470-75476) overwrites the TARGET's single ZDOConnectionHashData slot with {Spawned|Target,h}. Depending on s_connections iteration order this either clobbers the portal's own saved {Portal,h'} pairing (portal comes back unpaired → Game.ConnectPortals re-pairs it randomly) or is itself clobbered (spawner's hash finds no target at load → ConnectSpawners sets it to Spawned→None :77939-77943). Either way the trick corrupts portal pairing. For one-shot spawners (m_respawnTimeMinuts<=0, :5649-5653) a Spawned→ZDOID.None 'done' marker is sufficient and is saved as-is (RegenerateConnectionHashData keeps Spawned regardless of target :75469). For respawning spawners the target must be a persistent non-portal ZDO that has no connection of its own.
- The spawner write must land on the OWNING client's copy: UpdateSpawner is owner-gated (:5633-5637) and CreatureSpawner runs client-side; the same RPC_ZDOData revision race (:77108-77118) applies.
- One-way gate A→B is only runtime-stable if B itself holds a non-None Portal connection (phase-1 predicate :100601 resets A when target.connection==None). A B with connection None gets A reset within 5 s and both re-paired by phase 2. B→B (self-loop) or B→C are the stable sink forms; the self-loop is erased at save (:75472-75475) so it must be re-asserted on load.
- Do not write Portal|Target (0x11) onto a live portal to 'unpair' it: RegenerateConnectionHashData saves it as a real type 0x11 with a fresh hash and its target gets 0x11|0x10=0x11 too, which pollutes the Portal|Target list ZDOMan.ConnectPortals scans at load. Use UpdateConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None) (:73668-73678), which also sets DirtyPortals.
- Ring collapse is worse than 'loses a link': for A→B→C→A the per-ZDO slot overwrite leaves one pair (e.g. B↔C) plus a stranded member, and which pair survives depends on s_connections dictionary order.
- Spawner suppression is not permanent: at save, RegenerateConnectionHashData gives the target ZDO the {Spawned|Target,h} slot (:75473-75476). If the target is a PORTAL, that write collides with the portal's own {Portal,h'} / {Portal|Target,h'} slot in dictionary-iteration order — one of the two links is lost on disk: either the portal comes back unpaired or the spawner comes back unsuppressed (ConnectSpawners :77926-77960 only relinks matching hashes). Point suppression at a dedicated non-portal, otherwise-unconnected persistent ZDO, and re-assert after every world load.
- Ring collapse: for an N-ring the hash-data pass leaves each ZDO with a single slot that later iterations overwrite; a 3-ring A->B->C->A comes back as one bidirectional pair plus one orphan (which vanilla then cannot pair, since the pair re-confirms itself). General statement: after a save/load any topology degrades to a dictionary-order-dependent pairwise matching of at most floor(N/2) pairs — not 'rings lose a link'.
- One-way links are only runtime-stable when the TARGET's own Portal connection is non-None and its tag matches: Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 resets a source whose target has connection None (:100601-100604). A->B with B unconnected is torn down within 5 s.
- Writing Portal|Target (0x11) onto a live portal is self-defeating beyond the 5 s pass: phase 2 sees None and re-pairs it with SetConnection(Portal, ...) which overwrites the slot; it is a way to force a re-pair, not a state.
- Enforcement nuance: the CreatureSpawner reads the server-written connection but the spawn decision runs only on the ZDO owner's client (UpdateSpawner `if (!m_nview.IsOwner()) return;` :5639); the data is server-owned, the effect is client-honoured like all portal routing.
- Game.ConnectPortals start-of-pass ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals force-writes both directions of pairs staged on the previous pass (:100690-100698) — any mod topology written between the staging pass and the next pass is overwritten once.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] ConnectionType enum verified at :74747-74754 (None=0, Portal=1, SyncTransform=2, Spawned=3, Target=0x10; [Flags] but 1/2/3 overlap). s_connections is Dictionary<ZDOID,ZDOConnection> (:74794) with one readonly type/target (:75524-75534); GetConnectionZDOID requires exact type equality (:75094-75102); SetConnection/UpdateConnection replace the single slot (:74951-74976). ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync writes SyncTransform + s_attachJointHash/s_relPosHash/s_relRotHash on parent change only (:87542-87571) and the velRel bug is real: :87561 writes s_velHash, :87647 reads s_velRelHash. ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl writes s_user on the ship ZDO (:141332-141336). CreatureSpawner: Spawned connection set at :5820; UpdateSpawner (:5633-5657) returns if m_respawnTimeMinuts<=0 && any Spawned connection, else if SpawnedCreatureStillExists(target) (:5710-5717). RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) gives the source {type,h} and overwrites the target's slot with {type|Target,h}; ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load pairs Portal with Portal|Target by hash (:77850-77893); Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 (:100594-100606) tests only target-resolves / same tag / target-connection-non-None. The spawner trick and the one-way-gate statements need corrections.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Enum and overlap verified: ConnectionType is [Flags] byte {None=0, Portal=1, SyncTransform=2, Spawned=3, Target=0x10} (:74745-74753); GetConnectionZDOID requires exact type equality (:75094-75102); s_connections is one ZDOConnection per ZDOID with readonly type/target (:74794, :75524-75534); SetConnection overwrites, UpdateConnection only overwrites an existing entry (:74951-74976). ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync writes SyncTransform as a latch on parent change (:87546-87549) and the s_velHash/s_velRelHash write/read mismatch is real (:87561 vs :87647; s_velRelHash is in s_sessionHashes :78692 and nothing writes it). CreatureSpawner: UpdateSpawner returns early when `m_respawnTimeMinuts <= 0 && connection.type == Spawned`, and otherwise when SpawnedCreatureStillExists(connectionZDOID) — which is true for ANY resident ZDO id and also refreshes s_aliveTime (:5648-5660, :5703-5711); Spawn writes the Spawned connection (:5820). Save collapse verified: RegenerateConnectionHashData writes {type,h} for the source then OVERWRITES the target's single slot with {type|Target,h} (:75461-75478); ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load matches Portal sources to Portal|Target targets whose live connection is still None and writes both directions (:77850-77893). Game.ConnectPortals phase 1 tests only target-resolves / same tag / target non-None, never reciprocity (:100596-100606). Corrections: the spawner trick is not 'permanent' and can corrupt a portal's saved pairing; ring collapse is worse than 'lose a link'; one-way links need a non-None target; and the spawner decision is executed on the owning client, i.e. server-owned data but client-honoured behaviour.

### 140. Self-Organising Networks From Player Behaviour

`wildcard:Self-Organising Networks From Player Behaviour` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium-large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Rewire the world's portal topology from what players actually do — transit counts, dwell time, build ownership — using data the server can already see for free.


**How it works:** Every input this needs is already server-readable with no client install.

Usage: PositionWatch-style sampling of character ZDO positions (Wonderland Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:31, IsPortalTransit at :148) already detects a portal transit by checking whether two consecutive position samples both sit within about 40 m of some entry in ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals(), and additionally follows one endpoint's GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) to see whether its partner is near the other endpoint. It was built in Wonderland v0.6.4 precisely because portal transits were tripping a speed check at roughly 110 m/s over a 3 s window. Invert its sense and it is a transit counter.

Ownership: every player-placed piece carries ZDOVars.s_creator (:78393), a PlayerProfile UID written by Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424) from Player.PlacePiece (:12514-12517), plus s_creatorIndex indexing ZNet.World.m_playerHistory (:112396), which the server persists in the .fwl and maintains from socket-verified PlatformUserIDs (ZNet.UpdatePlayerHistory :81436-81461). So 'who built this portal' is durable, offline-readable and account-level.

Dwell and adjacency: ConnectedCharacters.All() gives (peer, character ZDO) pairs; character positions are refreshed every physics tick by the owner's ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync (:87527-87540). Count time spent within a radius of each portal.

The rewiring step is then the standard write triad, applied on a slow tick (30-120 s, not per transit): `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, targetId); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` — literally what Game.SetConnection does at :100643-100645. Because TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads GetConnectionZDOID at the instant of transit (:143539) and never caches, a rewire takes effect on the very next walk-through with no client refresh.

The cleanest way to own the decision without owning the whole algorithm is a Harmony POSTFIX on the private `Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(List<ZDO>, ZDO, string)` (:100664-100679) that overwrites __result — swapping UnityEngine.Random.Range for nearest / most-used / least-used / admin-designated, while leaving vanilla's two-phase commit, ownership handling and logging completely intact. For full control, prefix Game.ConnectPortals (:100589) and return false.

Three structural facts shape what topologies are worth aiming for. Phase 1 never checks reciprocity, so rings and fan-in are stable at runtime. Three or more portals on one tag PERMANENTLY strand exactly one member (the surviving pair keeps re-confirming itself), which is a free 'broken network' detector for an admin report. And which member gets stranded depends on dictionary bucket order and is not stable across restarts, so no admin-facing feature may assume a stable orphan identity.


**Player experience:** The network learns. A player builds a portal at a new outpost and tags it with the same name as their base gate — and instead of the usual coin-flip about which of their three same-named portals it links to, it links to the one they actually use most. Over a week the hub at spawn rotates its outbound link toward whichever frontier the server's population is currently pushing into, and the hover text says so: 'THE CROSSROADS - currently: Mistlands Camp (41 crossings this week)'. A long-abandoned outpost quietly falls out of the rotation. Nobody configured any of it, and nobody installed anything.


**Failure modes:**
- Transit detection is sampled, not eventful — a 3 s sample can miss a transit and a 0.25 s sample costs a per-player allocation and a full portal-dictionary walk each tick
- Three or more same-tag portals permanently strand one member and the victim changes across restarts (dictionary bucket order, ZDOMan.GetPortalList :77648)
- A rewire on a portal an online player currently owns is deferred by Game.SetConnection over RPC_SetConnection (:100649) and the server's local copy still reads the old value that tick — phase 2 then skips it, so a retag near a player takes 2+ ticks
- ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924) hands portal ownership to any peer within roughly 96-112 m every 2 s, so the mod's ownership claim is transient; guard with a ZDO.SetOwner Harmony prefix (the Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine ZdoSetOwnerPatch pattern)
- Never cache ZDO object references across ticks — ZDOPool.Release recycles them and Game's own m_currentlyConnectingPortals violates this; cache ZDOIDs and re-resolve
- A mass rewrite spikes every peer; budget routed broadcasts per sweep (Wonderland StructureUpkeep uses 256)
- Rewiring under a player standing inside a portal's trigger volume does not re-trigger — TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143673) fires on ENTER only; they must step out and back in

**Open questions:**
- Is ZDOVars.s_creator reliably non-zero on a player-placed portal in 1.0.7? Piece.SetCreator only writes when GetCreator()==0 and IsOwner (:136417). IN-GAME: place a portal on a vanilla client and compare s_creator against that character ZDO's s_playerID.
- How expensive is a 0.25 s tick that walks GetPortals() for every connected player on a world with several hundred portals and 20 peers? IN-GAME: Stopwatch the loop at scale.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- 'Three or more portals on one tag permanently strand exactly one member' is wrong for even counts: N same-tag portals pair off in phase 2 until none are unconnected, stranding one only when N is odd (and nobody retags). The stranded member is chosen by Random.Range among the unpaired at pairing time (:100678), not by 'dictionary bucket order'.
- 'Not stable across restarts' is wrong when the world was saved: RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) writes each pair as {Portal,h}/{Portal|Target,h} and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals restores them at load (:77850-77893) before Game.ConnectPortals runs (:76513-76521). The saved pair, and therefore the orphan identity, survives a restart. It is only unstable if the portal file was not dirtied (see SetDirtyPortals) or the pair is manually reset.
- Creator data is client-written, not server-verified: s_creator is the placing client's own PlayerProfile id (GetPlayerID :12516) and s_creatorIndex is an index the client computed against its copy of m_playerHistory, both written owner-gated on that client (:136417-136423). The history list itself is socket-derived and server-persisted; the per-piece link to it is client-honoured.
- A postfix that returns an already-connected portal (e.g. 'most used' that is currently paired) makes ConnectPortals overwrite that portal's connection (:100616-100617) and silently orphan its previous partner into a fan-in; the selector must filter to unconnected candidates unless fan-in is intended.
- Server writes to a portal owned by a nearby client hit the RPC_ZDOData revision gate (:77108-77118); ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924) re-assigns ownership every 2 s, so the triad must run immediately before ForceSendZDO and tolerate an occasional dropped write (the 30-120 s tick will re-assert).
- PositionWatch's 40/60 m two-sample heuristic (PositionWatch.cs:148-200) is a speed-check exemption, not a transit counter: it also fires for a player walking between two portals 40 m apart. A transit counter needs a large positional jump (>>60 m) between consecutive samples plus both endpoints matching a connected pair, and it still counts the 2 s pre-jump window from Player.UpdateTeleport (:15338-15345).
- The player-facing example is self-defeating: the tag IS the pairing key. Writing 'THE CROSSROADS - currently: Mistlands Camp (41 crossings this week)' into s_tag makes phase 1 (`zDO.GetString(s_tag) != @string`, :100601) tear the pair down within 5 s unless the partner carries the identical string. Tag-as-display requires either mirroring the exact string onto the partner or replacing Game.ConnectPortals entirely (prefix returning false) and pairing on a mod-private key.
- Usage/transit counting is reactive detection only: Wonderland's IsPortalTransit (PositionWatch.cs:148-185) classifies a 3 s position jump by 40 m / 60 m proximity to any portal; it cannot distinguish a portal transit from a nearby death/respawn or a server-initiated teleport, and misses back-to-back transits within one sample. No server-visible vanilla event marks a portal use (Game.IncrementPlayerStat(PortalsUsed) is client-local).
- A Harmony postfix on FindRandomUnconnectedPortal only influences portals whose connection is currently None; steering an established pair toward 'most used' requires the mod to first write None on both ends (or let it strand), after which the staged two-tick commit (AddToCurrentlyConnectingPortals -> ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals on the NEXT pass, :100680-100698) delays the new pair by up to 5 s and force-overwrites any mod write made in between.
- Fan-in and one-way shapes are runtime-stable only while every target holds a non-None Portal connection with a matching tag (phase 1 resets a source whose target is None, :100601-100604); they collapse to a pairwise matching at the next save (RegenerateConnectionHashData :75461-75478), so a world-load re-assert pass is mandatory, and it must be keyed on tag/position, not ZDOID (ZDO.Load re-issues ids, :74549-74552).
- 'Takes effect on the very next walk-through' needs a qualifier: the client's TargetFound() requires the new target ZDO to be present locally; if not, it calls RequestZDO and Teleport() returns silently (client :144386-144395, :144229-144232), and the ready-glow drops until the ZDO arrives — one server round-trip, typically well under a second, but a walk-through in that window is a silent no-op.
- s_creator is the per-character PlayerProfile id, not an account id; account-level attribution comes only via s_creatorIndex -> m_playerHistory, which is written by the placing client (SetCreator :136421) and is absent on pieces placed before that field existed or by clients whose history copy was stale at placement.
- ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924) re-assigns portal ownership to a nearby peer every 2 s, so the mod's SetOwner(session) is transient; that is fine for the connection write (Game.SetConnection does the same) but a mod must not assume it retains ownership between ticks.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The rewiring half is solid: Game.ConnectPortals (:100589-100627) is started from Game.Awake only when ZNet.instance.IsServer() (:100071-100075) and runs every 5 s (:100580-100587) with no local-player dependency; FindRandomUnconnectedPortal is `private ZDO FindRandomUnconnectedPortal(List<ZDO>, ZDO, string)` (:100664-100679) and its result feeds AddToCurrentlyConnectingPortals + SetConnection both ways, so a Harmony postfix on __result does swap the selector while keeping the two-tick commit (ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals :100690-100698, IsCurrentlyConnectingPortal :100700-100709). TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143673-143681) is client-only and enter-only. Phase 1 never checks reciprocity (:100601), so fan-in/rings are runtime-stable. Piece.SetCreator writes s_creator/s_creatorIndex (:136415-136424) from Player.PlacePiece (:12516); ZNet.UpdatePlayerHistory (:81436-81461) maintains World.m_playerHistory (:112396) from m_players whose ids come from socket host names (:81273-81276). Wonderland PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit exists at PositionWatch.cs:148 as described. Two factual claims about stranding are wrong and the input-trust framing needs tightening.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Inputs verified. ### 141. Portal-Driven Map Surfaces

`wildcard:Portal-Driven Map Surfaces` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Honest inventory of what a server can put on a vanilla client's map because of a portal — three real channels, none of them portal-specific, and one hard limitation.


**How it works:** Vanilla shows portal tags NOWHERE on the map; TeleportWorld exposes them only through GetHoverText (:143453-143463). So there is no portal pin to influence. What exists are three general server-to-client map channels, all usable in reaction to portal events.

(1) A NAMED, SAVED pin: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, 'RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse', pinName, (int)Minimap.PinType, pos, showMap)`. Game.Start registers this handler on EVERY peer, outside the IsServer block (:100068), and the client body (:100823-100831) calls Minimap.DiscoverLocation, which AddPin(..., save: true) and shows a '$msg_pin_added' toast, optionally centring the map. This is Wonderland's FirstSpawnGrant pattern (Subsystems/WorldGovernor/FirstSpawnGrant.cs:253-263). The hard catch: save:true means the pin lands PERMANENTLY in that player's own profile and there is NO removal RPC. Re-pushing after a rename creates a second pin; HaveSimilarPin only suppresses an identical name+type within 1 m. So this is a one-shot discovery push, not a live-synced pin set.

(2) An ICON-ONLY overlay the server fully owns: ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons (:113581-113593) packs a (Vector3, string) list into a ZPackage and sends the 'LocationIcons' routed RPC; the client's RPC_LocationIcons (:113595-113607) CLEARS and replaces its whole m_locationIcons dictionary, and Minimap.UpdateLocationPins rebuilds pins from it every 5 s. The server therefore controls the entire location-icon pin set on every vanilla client, and can add or remove entries at will. Limits: no label text at all, and only names that resolve to a sprite in the client's compiled Minimap.m_locationIcons render — an invented name is silently dropped. Also note this same channel is the authority for where a vanilla client respawns, via the Game.m_StartLocation ('StartTemple') entry read by Game.FindSpawnPoint.

(3) A TEMPORARY labelled pin plus in-world text plus a chat line, from one RPC: a fabricated 'ChatMessage' (Chat.Awake registration :41626; Chat.RPC_ChatMessage :41970-41973; OnNewChatMessage :41775-41816). Type 2 (Shout) renders a chat line, yellow uppercase floating world text, and an animated map pin labelled '<UserInfo.Name>: <TEXT>' for m_worldTextTTL = 5 s. Type 3 (Ping) gives no chat line and forces the world text to 'PING'. UserInfo.Name is entirely server-chosen, so 'The Waygate' can be the speaker. Less-than and greater-than are replaced with spaces in OnNewChatMessage (:41795-41796), so no markup.

Combined, a portal event can: permanently pin a newly discovered destination (once), keep a live icon-only overlay of every active gate, and flash a 5-second labelled pin plus a floating caption at the moment a hub rotates.


**Player experience:** A player uses a hub gate for the first time this week. As the black screen clears, a toast reads 'Pin added: Ashlands Foothold' and a marker is now permanently on their map at the place they just arrived. Meanwhile a set of small icons has appeared across the map wherever the server currently maintains an open public gate — no names, just markers, updating every five seconds as gates open and close. And at the moment the hub rotates, everyone within range sees 'THE WAYGATE: NOW OPEN TO MISTLANDS CAMP' briefly appear in chat, in the air above the arch, and as a labelled pin on the map for five seconds. None of it required a client install; all of it is vanilla's own discovery and shout machinery.


**Failure modes:**
- RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse pins are save:true and there is NO removal RPC — a demolished portal's pin stays on the player's map forever
- A renamed destination produces a SECOND permanent pin; HaveSimilarPin matches on name AND type AND within 1 m
- LocationIcons pins carry no name and render only for names present in the client's compiled Minimap.m_locationIcons sprite list — invented names are dropped with no error
- LocationIcons is a full replace, not a delta, and it is also what tells a vanilla client where StartTemple is (Game.FindSpawnPoint) — overwriting the set carelessly can move where players respawn
- A fabricated Shout or Ping renders its map pin only if Chat.AddInworldText runs, which is skipped when Minimap.m_mode is None AND the position is beyond m_nomapPingDistance (50 m) — i.e. in nomap worlds or with the HUD hidden
- Minimap.AddPin forces any PinType outside the visible range to Icon3, so exotic types silently collapse
- Map pings are public: Chat.SendPing broadcasts to peer 0 (:42058-42068), so a ping-driven feature is a visible, shared, spammable gesture

**Open questions:**
- Which names exist in the shipped client's Minimap.m_locationIcons sprite list? That bounds the LocationIcons overlay entirely. IN-GAME: on a client, enumerate Minimap.instance.m_locationIcons and log every m_name.
- Does RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse render identically on a PlayFab/Xbox crossplay client? Wonderland ships it but has no dated live-test note. IN-GAME: push a pin to a crossplay client, relog, and confirm persistence.
- Does overwriting the LocationIcons set actually move a vanilla client's respawn point (Game.FindSpawnPoint reads GetLocationIcon(StartTemple))? IN-GAME: omit StartTemple from a push and have a test character die.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Channel (2): ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons is private and builds only from m_locationInstances (server-side GetLocationIcons branch, CLIENT :116093-116103); a mod must craft its own ZPackage and call ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer, 'LocationIcons', pkg) directly. Vanilla re-sends the pure vanilla set on every new peer (ZoneSystem.OnNewPeer, SERVER :113609-113616) and whenever any m_iconPlaced location is placed (SERVER :114998-115001), silently wiping the mod overlay; the mod must include vanilla's entries (public ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcons(dict)) in every push and re-push after those events (Harmony postfix on SendLocationIcons).
- Channel (2) is load-bearing for respawn: the client's Game.FindSpawnPoint resolves m_StartLocation ('StartTemple') via ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(name, out pos), which on a client iterates m_locationIcons (CLIENT :100796-100800, :116062-116088). A mod push that omits the StartTemple entry makes bed-less respawn return false forever; a push that adds a second 'StartTemple' entry can redirect it (dictionary iteration order, first match). Also the dictionary is keyed by exact Vector3, so two overlay icons at the same position collapse to one.
- Channel (2): the set of renderable names is asset data (Minimap.m_locationIcons, CLIENT :56373) not present in the decompile; which names exist must be checked in-game.
- Channel (3): Chat.OnNewChatMessage calls RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync(sender.UserId, CommunicateWithUsingText, ...) for any senderID that is not the local player (SERVER :41780-41786). CheckPermissionAsync returns Error (message dropped) when !user.IsValid, and when PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider != null it calls RelationsProvider.GetUserProfileAsync(user, ...) on the fabricated id (CLIENT :88643-88700). UserInfo deserialises UserId via new PlatformUserID(pkg.ReadString()) (CLIENT :72903-72907). So the server-chosen speaker must carry a syntactically valid platform id string, and the Steam/PlayFab profile-lookup outcome for a fake id is unverifiable here (Splatform assembly not decompiled) — needs an in-game check. The displayed name is also passed through CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC(Name, CharacterName, UserId) (CLIENT :72915-72918).
- Channel (3): the world text and pin are skipped when the receiver is InIntro, and the in-world text is skipped when the large map is open and the receiver is farther than Minimap.m_nomapPingDistance (SERVER :41797, :41808).
- Channel (1): the toast icon and the pin sprite come from Minimap.GetSprite((PinType)pinType); the pin is persisted only when that client next saves its profile.
- Chat-line speaker cannot be server-chosen: Chat.AddString(PlatformUserID,...) SERVER :45950-45955 looks the UserId up in ZNet.m_players (TryGetPlayerByPlatformUserID :81477-81493); unknown id => 'Failed to get player info' LogError and no chat line; known id => attributed to that player's character name. Only AddInworldText/world text and the shout map pin use UserInfo.Name (WorldTextInstance.m_name => m_userInfo.GetDisplayName() :41531).
- Robust send pattern: per-peer InvokeRoutedRPC with UserInfo.UserId = that recipient's own PlatformUserID. CheckPermissionAsync short-circuits to Granted for the local user (CLIENT RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync, 'user == LocalUser.PlatformUserID' branch) so no platform lookup, the chat line is attributed to the recipient's own character, and the world text/pin still reads 'The Waygate: ...'. Any other UserId is subject to RelationsManager (mute list, platform profile lookup) and can be silently dropped.
- All server-fabricated messages share one WorldTextInstance slot keyed by senderID (FindExistingWorldText :41927-41936 uses the routed m_senderPeerID, i.e. the server id) — a second message within 5 s replaces the first instead of stacking.
- RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse has a side effect: if the map is not open the client rotates the player toward the pin for 3.5 s (Player.SetLookDir, SERVER :100826-100829).
- 'Permanent' pin = until the player deletes it manually on the map; there is no server-side removal, but the player can.
- LocationIcons overlay is overwritten by vanilla: ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation calls SendLocationIcons(0L) whenever an m_iconPlaced location is placed (SERVER :114999-115001), wiping the mod's list on every client; the mod must re-send after that (Harmony postfix on SendLocationIcons or periodic rebroadcast). The mod's list must also MERGE vanilla's entries (server GetLocationIcons builds from m_locationInstances m_iconAlways/m_iconPlaced, :116089-116105) — omitting 'StartTemple' makes the client's Game.FindSpawnPoint (CLIENT :100796-100804) fall to Vector3.zero for characters with no bed.
- SendLocationIcons is private; the mod should build the ZPackage (count, then Vector3+string pairs) and call ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer, 'LocationIcons', pkg) directly.
- Citation fixes: Game.Start registration is :100067 not :100068; Minimap.DiscoverLocation CLIENT :58394-58421, HaveSimilarPin :58423-58432, AddPin :58434+ (the listed 58375-58406 / 58363-58374 ranges are off).

### 142. The Tag Is Also The Lock — Puzzle And Progression Gates

`wildcard:The Tag Is Also The Lock — Puzzle And Progression Gates` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium-large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A composite: use the tag, the connection, global keys and the Void Anchor together to build gates that open and close on server-side conditions with no client install.


**How it works:** Four independent levers compose into real puzzle mechanics.

HARD LOCK (server-enforced): null the connection. `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, ZDOID.None); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid);` TeleportWorld.Teleport gate 1 (:143519) is the ONLY genuinely server-enforced gate of the four, because it reads the ZDO connection the server owns. Vanilla's pairer will re-pair it within 5 s if another same-tag unconnected portal exists, so a locked gate must either be alone on its tag or the mod must own pairing.

SOFT LOCK (silent): the Decoy Gate — connection pointed at an unresolvable ZDOID. Hover still reads connected, glow still lights, transit silently does nothing. This is the better puzzle primitive because it gives the player no error to search for.

GLOBAL LOCK (client-honoured, world-wide): `ZoneSystem.instance.SetGlobalKey('noportals')` reaches every connected vanilla client within one network frame — SetGlobalKey (:115943-115946) routes to the server's own handler synchronously, RPC_SetGlobalKey (:116022-116029) adds and then SendGlobalKeys(0L) (:113466-113471) broadcasts the whole key list, and each client's RPC_GlobalKeys clears and rebuilds. TeleportWorld.Teleport reads it live at gate 2 (:143523) and shows '$msg_blocked'. Two operational cautions: this is world-wide, not per-portal; and GlobalKeyAdd mirrors any key below GlobalKeys.NonServerOption (41) into ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys (:113511), permanently baking it into the .fwl — use the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` plus SendGlobalKeys(0L) for a session-only lock.

STATE: per-portal puzzle state lives in mod-private ZDO keys on the portal itself (see Portals As A Data Store), plus per-player once-only flags as world global keys following the Wonderland FirstSpawnGrant convention `<mod>_<feature>_<playerID>` — persisted in the .db, readable synchronously after SetGlobalKey returns.

INPUT: the only reliable vanilla-client-to-server channels are emotes (ZDOVars.s_emote / s_emoteID polled on the character ZDO at 0.25 s, the Wonderland EmoteSignals pattern), map pings (Chat.SendPing broadcasts to peer 0 with a world Vector3), equipped item hashes on the character ZDO (VisEquipment writes s_rightItem etc.), item stands (ZDOVars.s_item is the mounted prefab hash), signs (ZDOVars.s_text, written directly by the client with no RPC), and chest contents (ZDOVars.s_items). Chat text is NOT usable — a solo player's chat produces zero packets.

FEEDBACK: PlayerNotify toasts via the character-ZDO 'Message' RPC, DamageText.TextType.Bonus floating text within 30 m, a granted status effect, a vanilla vfx/sfx through the 'SpawnObject' routed RPC, and the portal's own tag rewritten live.


**Player experience:** A ring of five ancient portals in a stone circle, all tagged with runes, all glowing 'connected', none of them working. Beside each is an item stand. Mount the right offering on the right stand — the server reads ZDOVars.s_item on each stand's ZDO — and when the combination is correct, all five tags change in the same instant from runes to 'THE ROAD OPENS', a vfx flares at each one, everyone present gets a centre-screen toast, and the ring becomes a real fan-in network to a sixth, hidden gate. The puzzle state persists across server restarts because it lives on the portal ZDOs themselves. A player who solves it gets a permanent map pin to the destination. Nobody installed anything; every element is either vanilla's own hover text, vanilla's own effects, or vanilla's own map.


**Failure modes:**
- Nulling a connection is undone by Game.ConnectPortals within 5 s if another same-tag unconnected portal exists (:100607-100621)
- GlobalKeys.NoPortals is world-wide and client-honoured, and RPC_SetGlobalKey has ZERO sender validation (:116022-116029) — any client can lift it unless the mod Harmony-prefixes that RPC
- Setting a portal key at runtime permanently edits the world's .fwl modifier list via GlobalKeyAdd (:113511) unless canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false is passed
- ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys wipes enum ordinals 0..40 on every world load (:115904-115931) and re-adds only what is in the .fwl — mod-owned world-modifier keys must be re-applied in a POSTFIX on it
- Emote polling has a 0.25 s resolution and a first-sighting seed; a player can emote faster than the poll
- Map pings are broadcast to every player, so a ping-based puzzle input is public
- All puzzle logic runs server-side against sampled state; there is no atomic transaction and two players can race a combination

**Open questions:**
- Does a player standing beside a portal see a server-side tag change without leaving the area? UpdatePortal runs on a 0.5 s InvokeRepeating (:143450) but hover text is rebuilt per frame from the ZDO. IN-GAME: stand at a gate, rewrite s_tag, and watch the hover.
- Do item stands reliably write s_item for every mountable item class? IN-GAME: mount a weapon, a trophy and a food item and dump the stand ZDO's ints.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- SOFT LOCK (Decoy Gate) is reverted by vanilla: Game.ConnectPortals first loop calls SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None) when ZDOMan.GetZDO(connection) == null, when the target's s_tag differs, or when the target's own connection is None (SERVER :100594-100606). A dangling ZDOID is therefore cleared within 5 s unless the mod prefixes Game.ConnectPortals (private) to skip locked portals. If instead the target IS a server-held ZDO, the client resolves it via TargetFound -> ZDOMan.RequestZDO -> server RPC_RequestZDO -> peer.ForceSendZDO, which AddForceSendZdos sends irrespective of the peer's area (SERVER :77684-77692, :77263-77285), and the vanilla client then teleports to zdo.GetPosition() (SERVER :143538-143547). There is no configuration in which hover shows 'connected' indefinitely while transit silently does nothing without patching ConnectPortals.
- HARD LOCK re-pairing is faster than stated and symmetrical: nulling portal A leaves its former partner B pointing at A; on the next pass loop 1 nulls B (its target's connection is None, :100600) and loop 2 re-pairs A<->B via FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100608-100620, :100662-100676). The only vanilla-stable states are: unique tag, tag rewritten to a mod-private value, or ConnectPortals suppressed. Ownership is not required for the server's connection write to replicate (ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision has no owner gate on the server build, :73832-73840), but a portal owned by an online peer is normally written via RPC_SetConnection round-trip inside Game.SetConnection (:100637-100650) — the mod should write the ZDO directly and call ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO.
- GLOBAL LOCK persistence: GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys:false) only prevents the .fwl mirror (:113489, :113510-113511). m_globalKeys itself is always cloned into the .db save (ZoneSystem.PrepareSave :113734-113740), so a 'session-only' NoPortals still persists across a restart unless removed (GlobalKeyRemove / RPC_RemoveGlobalKey :113517, :116031-116037) before the save. GlobalKeyAdd and SendGlobalKeys are both private.
- STATE: mod-private keys on a portal ZDO are only written to disk when the portal chunk is dirty; DirtyPortalObjects is double-buffered and reset per save (:76139-76149, :76221-76230), and a plain zdo.Set(...) does not set it. The mod must call the public ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() (:76702-76705) after each puzzle-state write or the state is lost at the next save.
- Per-player once-only flags as global keys are broadcast to every client in the full key list and stamped into every client's PlayerProfile m_knownWorldKeys stats on receipt (:113505-113509) — functional, but noisy and visible to any client that inspects its stats.
- Citation fix: ItemStand s_item mount write is at SERVER :131845 (stableHashCode); :131795 is RPC_DestroyAttachment writing 0.
- Enforcement label applies only to the connection-null hard lock; the global lock and all feedback/input channels are client-honoured.
- Owning pairing is mandatory, not optional: Game.ConnectPortals second loop (:100606-100618) re-pairs any two same-tag unconnected portals every 5 s, and 'alone on its tag' is not a lock (no route existed). Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals (or a filtered ZDOMan.GetPortalList) is required for BOTH hard and soft locks.
- Decoy Gate is wiped by vanilla within 5 s: ConnectPortals first loop (:100598-100603) nulls any connection whose target ZDO resolves to null. Also, while it stands, m_target_found is NOT active (UpdatePortal :143507 gates on TargetFound) — only the emission lerp lights (Update :143512-143516) — and each client with the instance sends a 'RequestZDO' routed RPC every 0.5 s (:143650-143652, :77684-77687).
- Puzzle state on portal ZDOs is lost at the next save unless the mod calls ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() after each write: ZDO.Set -> IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector (:73832-73840, :76694-76699) only dirties normal chunks, which exclude portals (:77572); ChunkPortal is written only when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77632).
- Fan-in network does not survive save/reload: ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75461-75478) stores one ZDOConnectionHashData per ZDO (H's Target entry is overwritten by each spoke, then replaced by H's own Portal entry), and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals on load (:77855-77887) rebuilds pairwise only. After restart the ring is one pair plus unconnected portals which vanilla re-pairs among themselves within 5 s; the mod must rebuild the fan-in at startup from its own persisted state.
- 'SpawnObject' routed RPC is safe only for prefabs without ZNetView: RPC_SpawnObject (:82355-82366) calls Object.Instantiate on every receiving client; a ZNetView prefab would spawn a new ZDO per client (ZNetView.Awake m_initZDO==null path :82615-82626).
- Chat text IS partially usable: with 2+ players Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync sends the shout per recipient uid (CLIENT :42008-42034) and each copy passes through the server's ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC/RouteRPC (CLIENT :83861-83873, :83826-83859) where a Harmony patch can read it; only the solo-with-RelationsProvider case (self-send only, :42007) produces zero packets, and with no RelationsProvider it is sent to Everybody (:42004) and the server handles it.
- Per-player once-only global keys are unknown strings (gk = NonServerOption) so they ARE saved in the .db (:113751-113755 keeps them) and the entire key list is rebroadcast to every client on every change (RPC_SetGlobalKey -> SendGlobalKeys(0L)); each also increments every client's m_knownWorldKeys stats (:113505-113507).
- Per-player route gating is impossible: the connection is one value per portal ZDO read by every client; a route is open for everyone or nobody. The composite is server-enforced ONLY for the hard route lock; NoPortals, the ore check and the offering-detection feedback are client-honoured.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The hard lock is real and route-form: TeleportWorld.Teleport returns before any player check when TargetFound() is false (SERVER :143517-143521), TargetFound is false when the ZDO connection is ZDOID.None (SERVER :143643-143656), and on the server build ZDO.SetConnection -> IncreaseDataRevision has no owner check (SERVER :73656-73665, :73832-73840; contrast InternalSetPosition :73734-73745), so a server write replicates. The global lock path is exactly as cited: SetGlobalKey -> InvokeRoutedRPC(GetServerPeerID()) dispatches synchronously to the local handler when m_server (SERVER :115943-115946, :83559-83593), RPC_SetGlobalKey -> GlobalKeyAdd + SendGlobalKeys(0L) (SERVER :116022-116029, :113466-113471), client RPC_GlobalKeys clears and rebuilds (SERVER :113473-113481), and Teleport reads GlobalKeys.NoPortals live at gate 2 (SERVER :143522-143526); NoPortals sits below NonServerOption in the enum (SERVER :101304, :101313) so GlobalKeyAdd mirrors it into m_startingGlobalKeys when flag is true (SERVER :113483-113511). Input channels check out: Player.StartEmote writes s_emoteID/s_emote/s_emoteOneshot (SERVER :15585-15598), Sign.SetText claims ownership and writes s_text directly (SERVER :141915-141928), ItemStand stores the prefab hash as an int in s_item (SERVER :131845, read :132027), Chat.SendPing broadcasts to 0L (SERVER :42058-42068); shouts on a platform with a RelationsProvider are sent per-target and a solo player's shout is handled locally with no RouteRPC (SERVER :41983-42004, :83583-83593). Feedback: Character 'Message' RPC (SERVER :10072), DamageText.m_maxTextDistance = 30f (SERVER :46338), ZNetScene 'SpawnObject' (SERVER :81954, :82355-82366). But the SOFT LOCK / Decoy Gate as described does not survive vanilla: Game.ConnectPortals nulls any portal whose connection target GetZDO() returns null, or whose target has a different tag or a None connection, on every 5 s pass (SERVER :100594-100606); and if the target does exist server-side, a vanilla client's TargetFound calls RequestZDO, the server's RPC_RequestZDO force-sends it regardless of area (SERVER :77689-77692, :77263-77285), TargetFound becomes true, and Teleport moves the player to that ZDO's position (SERVER :143538-143547). So a decoy is only silent if ConnectPortals is Harmony-suppressed for that portal AND the ZDOID never resolves server-side. The composite's 'server-enforced' label is honest only for the connection-null hard lock; every other lever is client-honoured.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The four levers exist, but two of the four descriptions are wrong about vanilla's reconciliation, and the persistence story is wrong twice. HARD LOCK: TeleportWorld.TargetFound (:143640-143655) does gate on the ZDO connection, so nulling it is a genuine route-form server lock — but Game.ConnectPortals (:100589-100620) re-pairs any two same-tag unconnected portals in its second loop within 5 s, and a portal 'alone on its tag' never had a route to lock, so the mod MUST own pairing (Harmony on Game.ConnectPortals or on ZDOMan.GetPortalList, the only two callers being :77815 load-time and :100592). SOFT LOCK: a decoy ZDOID is wiped by the FIRST loop (:100598-100603, `zDO == null` => SetConnection(None)) within 5 s, so the decoy is also impossible without owning pairing; while it stands, HaveTarget lights the emission (:143512-143516) but m_target_found stays off (:143507 requires TargetFound) and every client that has the portal instantiated fires RequestZDO every 0.5 s (:143650-143652 -> :77684-77692). GLOBAL LOCK: SetGlobalKey -> RPC_SetGlobalKey -> GlobalKeyAdd -> SendGlobalKeys(0L) confirmed (:115943-115946, :116022-116029, :113483-113513, :113466-113471); NoPortals enum ordinal 34 < NonServerOption 43 so it is mirrored into m_startingGlobalKeys with the default flag (:113487, :113511), and ZoneSystem.Save strips keys < NonServerOption from the .db (:113751-113755) so GlobalKeyAdd(key,false)+SendGlobalKeys(0L) is indeed session-only. STATE: mod-private keys on portal ZDOs are NOT saved by default — ZDO.Set->IncreaseDataRevision->SetDirtySector (:73832-73840, :76694-76699) dirties normal chunks which exclude portals (:77572); the ChunkPortal file is written only when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621-77632), so SetDirtyPortals() is mandatory after every write. The fan-in topology in the player experience does not survive a save: RegenerateConnectionHashData keeps one hash slot per ZDO and overwrites H's entry for each incoming link (:75461-75478) and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals on load pairs strictly pairwise (:77855-77887). INPUT list is accurate (StartEmote :15585-15598, Sign.SetText :141916-141928, ItemStand s_item :131795) except the chat claim, which is only true for a solo player when a RelationsProvider exists (CLIENT :42003-42007). FEEDBACK: 'Message' RPC on the character ZDO exists (:10072, :14816); 'SpawnObject' exists (:81954, :82355-82366) but instantiates on every receiving client, so only ZNetView-less vfx/sfx prefabs are safe.

### 143. Sector Zero — Portals Outside The World, And Server-Side Instantiation

`wildcard:Sector Zero — Portals Outside The World, And Server-Side Instantiation` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **needs-ingame-check** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Any ZDO beyond roughly plus or minus 16.4 km clamps into the same sector bucket the dedicated server's own pinned reference position maps to, which makes the server instantiate it.


**How it works:** This is the mechanism nobody documents and it cuts both ways.

ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex (:115760-115773) computes `uint num = (uint)(sectorX + 256)` and clamps ANY sector outside 0..511 to `result.Sector = 0`. Zones are 64 m, so the legal range is roughly x/z in [-16416, +16352]; a normal world is plus or minus 10500, comfortably inside. Sector 0 is therefore shared by zone (-256,-256) and by EVERY out-of-range coordinate.

Game.FixedUpdate in the SERVER build pins `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(new Vector3(1000000f, 0f, 1000000f))` every physics tick (:100458-100466) — a line that exists in no form in the client build. Zone (15625, 15625) maps through SectorToIndex to Sector 0.

Crucially, the server does NOT simply idle there. ZoneSystem.PokeLocalZone (:114021-114037) chooses `SpawnMode.Full` when `ZNet.instance.IsServer() && !IsZoneGenerated(zoneID)`, and SpawnZone (:114071-114107) succeeds and registers the zone in m_zones. So the server's own local zones around (1e6, 0, 1e6) ARE created, and ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded() (:114054-114069) becomes true for them. ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects runs every 1/30 s (:82257-82276) and calls FindSectorObjects for zone (15625,15625) — which, via the clamp, returns m_objectsBySector[0] plus m_portalObjects[SectorIndex 0].

Two real consequences:
(a) A ZDO created at an out-of-range coordinate WILL be instantiated as a real GameObject on the dedicated server. For a portal that means a live TeleportWorld with a ZNetView, a running InvokeRepeating('UpdatePortal', 0.5f, 0.5f), and a TeleportWorldTrigger collider — harmless only because Player.m_localPlayer is null and Player.s_players is empty, so OnTriggerEnter (:143673-143681) can never fire. It is still a per-tick cost and a surprise in any object dump.
(b) The invalid-prefab reaper is SERVER-ONLY: CreateObjectsSorted's `else if (ZNet.instance.IsServer())` branch (:82137-82143) takes ownership and destroys any ZDO whose CreateObject returns null. That branch is the ONLY thing in the game that reaps prefab-less ZDOs — and it only ever sees bucket 0. This is exactly why a Void Anchor placed at normal world coordinates survives indefinitely, and exactly why one placed out of bounds is deleted within a frame.

Practical rules: never create a portal or an anchor beyond about plus or minus 16000 m; if a mod wants a 'nowhere' anchor, put it at a legal but unvisited coordinate (deep ocean, or high above terrain) rather than out of bounds. And if any mod ever moved the server's reference position into the real world, the server would start instantiating real portal GameObjects with real colliders everywhere.


**Player experience:** Nothing intentional — this is a trap to be avoided rather than a feature to sell. The player-visible symptom of getting it wrong is an admin waypoint or an event gate that works for exactly one frame and then vanishes with a 'Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO' line in the server log, or a portal placed 'off the map' that quietly consumes server CPU forever while being reachable by nobody. The one legitimate use is diagnostic: a mod can deliberately park a marker ZDO in bucket 0 to confirm from the log whether the server's active area is loaded on a given build.


**Failure modes:**
- A Void Anchor placed out of bounds is destroyed by the server's own invalid-prefab reaper within a frame (:82137-82143)
- A valid portal prefab placed out of bounds is instantiated server-side as a live MonoBehaviour with a repeating invoke, permanently
- WorldGenerator.GetBiomeHeight returns -400 beyond 10500 m (:151978-151981), so out-of-bounds coordinates have no meaningful terrain at all
- Bucket 0 also holds legitimate zone (-256,-256) content, so anything a mod does there is mixed with real world data
- The whole behaviour hinges on IsActiveAreaLoaded being true for the pinned zone, which depends on HeightmapBuilder succeeding at (1e6, 0, 1e6) — plausible but unverified

**Designer citations:** ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex clamp to Sector 0 — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115755-115774 ; Game.FixedUpdate pins reference position (SERVER build only) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100458-100466 ; ZoneSystem.PokeLocalZone uses SpawnMode.Full on the server — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:114021-114037 ; ZoneSystem.CreateLocalZones / IsActiveAreaLoaded — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113993-114012, 114054-114069 ; ZNetScene.Update / CreateDestroyObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82257-82276 ; ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted server-only invalid-prefab destroy — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82105-82145 (:82137-82143) ; ZDOMan.FindObjects merges m_portalObjects for the clamped sector — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77367-77382 ; TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter requires Player.m_localPlayer — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143673-143681 ; WorldGenerator edge constants — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:151118-151122, 151978-151981

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- The invalid-prefab reaper is not unique to CreateObjectsSorted: ZNetScene.CreateDistantObjects has the same server-only SetOwner + DestroyZDO branch for Distant ZDOs ('Destroyed invalid predab ZDO', SERVER :82156-82181). Both run only over the server's reference-zone neighbourhood, so the conclusion (only bucket 0 is ever reaped) is unchanged.
- Whether the server's active area ever loads (and therefore whether bucket-0 objects are instantiated at all) depends on HeightmapBuilder producing terrain for zones around (15625,15625) — IsTerrainReady queues an HMBuildData and returns false until the builder thread finishes (SERVER :129879-129899). The code has no coordinate guard and WorldGenerator returns a constant ocean-floor height beyond 10500 m, so it should succeed, but this is runtime behaviour that must be confirmed from a server log or object dump before any design relies on 'instantiated on the server'.
- Side effect not mentioned: SpawnZone in SpawnMode.Full calls SetZoneGenerated for the far zones (SERVER :114105), so the server's phantom zones are recorded in m_generatedZones and persisted in the .db.
- A Void Anchor at legal coordinates is never reaped server-side, but a vanilla client inside its area will retry CreateObject every 1/30 s and log 'Missing prefab hash' each time (SERVER :82000-82008, no client-side reaper branch) — a client log-spam cost this option's 'survives indefinitely' framing omits.
- Enforcement label: this is a server-internal lifecycle behaviour, not a rule applied to players; 'server-enforced' is a category error. It is relevant only to mod authors and admins.
- Server-side instantiation is conditional on ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded() (CreateObjectsSorted :82107-82110), i.e. SpawnZone succeeding at zone (15625,15625) via HeightmapBuilder.IsTerrainReady (:114073-114078). The code path has no gate, but whether the heightmap builds at 1e6 needs an in-game log check ('Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO' after parking a hash-less ZDO out of bounds is the probe).
- Client side of the reaper claim: a vanilla client never reaps, but for a ZDO whose prefab hash is non-zero and unknown, CreateObject logs 'Missing prefab hash' (:82004) on every 30 Hz CreateDestroyObjects pass for as long as it is in the active area, because the ZDO never becomes Created (:82115). Only prefab hash 0 is silent (:81999). A Void Anchor at legal coordinates must therefore use hash 0 or a real harmless prefab, not an invented hash.
- SpawnMode.Full at the pinned zone also runs PlaceLocations/PlaceVegetation/PlaceZoneCtrl for zone (15625,15625) (:114093-114095) and adds it to m_generatedZones (SetZoneGenerated :114106, saved by ZoneSystem.Save :113745-113749) — harmless but visible in the .db.
- Precise legal range: sector index x,y in [-256,255] => world x/z in [-16416, 16352) (GetSectorIndex FloorToInt((p+32)/64) :115747-115752). A portal's m_portalObjects key is fixed at AddIfPortal time (CreateNewZDO :76683, RPC_ZDOData) and SetSector is a no-op for portals (:73752-73757), so a portal created in-range and later moved out of range stays in its original bucket, not bucket 0.

Zone(1e6) = floor((1e6+32)/64) = 15625, which SectorToIndex clamps to 0. ### 144. Cross-Server And Multi-World Travel

`wildcard:Cross-Server And Multi-World Travel` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **not-enforceable** · **Effort:** large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


RULED OUT for a zero-client-install mod — no vanilla server-to-client redirect mechanism exists anywhere in the protocol.


**How it works:** I searched the client assembly for every connection-control surface and there is nothing to hook.

ZNet registers exactly three handshake RPCs on a peer: 'Disconnect', 'ServerHandshake' and 'ClientHandshake' (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:79819-79831). ZNet.RPC_Disconnect (:80165-80177) takes no parameters at all — it resolves the peer, sets m_connectionStatus to ErrorDisconnected if the peer was the server, and calls Disconnect. There is no destination, no address, no redirect payload.

The only ways a client ever points itself at a server are ZNet.SetServerHost(string remotePlayerId) / (ulong serverID) / (string host, int port, OnlineBackendType) (:81288-81302) and ZNet.SetServer (:81249). Every call site is in FejdStartup — the main menu — driven by the server list UI (ServerListEntryData, m_startup.SetServerToJoin at :65795, :65812, :66100) or by command-line parsing (:97925). None of them is reachable from any RPC, any ZDO, any global key, or any routed message. A dedicated server cannot make a connected vanilla client change which server it is talking to, full stop.

The character-data half is equally closed. Player.Save (:14091-14170) serialises inventory, recipes, uniques, trophies, foods, skills and customData into a package that PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData (:105706-105711) writes only to that client's own .fch file. ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles (:79653-79670) sounds like it collects profiles and does the exact opposite: it invokes the 'SavePlayerProfile' RPC so each client saves its OWN local file, and returns nothing. No player inventory, skill or recipe state ever crosses the wire in either direction. So even a scheme that somehow moved the client would have nothing to hand the destination server.

What IS possible, and is the honest ceiling: a multi-server OPERATOR-side illusion. Two servers sharing one Discord webhook and one exported state file can present a coherent 'network' — server A's portal tagged 'TO THE NORTHLANDS' is a Decoy Gate that, on transit detection, toasts the player the second server's join address (PlayerNotify, or ZNet.RemotePrint into an admin's console) and optionally kicks them with ZNet.instance.Kick. They then rejoin manually with the same character. That is a social mechanic with a portal-shaped skin, not travel.

A second honest variant: a single server hosting a second WORLD is impossible (ZNet holds one ZNet.World, ZoneSystem holds one m_locationInstances, WorldGenerator is a singleton seeded once in ZNet.ServerLoadWorld at :79273-79285). 'Another world' can only be faked by carving a far region of the same world and gating it, which is a Void Anchor plus a lock, not multi-world.


**Player experience:** The best that can honestly be delivered: a player walks into the gate marked 'TO THE NORTHLANDS', gets a black screen, and arrives standing in front of a rune stone with a centre-screen message reading 'The Northlands lie beyond this world. Rejoin at northlands.example.com:2456 with this character.' Their map may also gain a permanent pin naming it. Then they alt-tab, open the server browser, and connect by hand. Anything smoother requires a client mod.


**Failure modes:**
- There is no redirect RPC — this cannot be made to work without a client install, at any effort level
- Character data never crosses the wire in either direction, so even with a redirect the destination server would receive a fresh character unless both servers share a save directory
- ZNet.Kick / Ban are the only server-initiated disconnects and they carry no destination
- Presenting an address in a toast invites phishing-shaped confusion if any third party can trigger it
- A 'second world' on one server process is structurally impossible: one ZNet.World, one WorldGenerator, one ZoneSystem

**Designer citations:** ZNet peer RPC registrations (Disconnect / ServerHandshake / ClientHandshake only) — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:79819-79831 ; ZNet.RPC_Disconnect takes no destination — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:80165-80177 ; ZNet.SetServerHost overloads, called only from FejdStartup — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:81288-81302, 81249; call sites :65795, :65812, :66100, :97925 ; Player.Save writes to the local profile only — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:14091-14170 ; PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:105706-105711 ; ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles tells clients to save locally and returns nothing — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79653-79675 ; ZNet.ServerLoadWorld single-world init — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79273-79285 ; ZNet.Kick / Ban / RemotePrint — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81658, 81744, 81635


**Open questions:**
- None that would change the verdict. The only thing worth confirming is that no platform-layer assembly (Splatform / PlayFab) exposes a server-initiated join redirect — those assemblies are outside this decompile set. IN-GAME: grep the shipped Splatform and PlayFab DLLs for any join or redirect entry point reachable from a server.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- ZNet registers more than 'exactly three' peer RPCs: PeerInfo, Disconnect, SavePlayerProfile, RPC_RequestValidSimulationDistance, RPC_ValidatedSimulationDistance on every peer, plus Kicked, Error(int) and ClientHandshake on the client and ServerHandshake on the server (CLIENT :79815-79831), and PeerInfo then adds ServerSyncedPlayerData/PlayerList/HistoricalPlayerList/AdminList/RemotePrint (CLIENT :80100-80104). None carries a redirect payload, so the conclusion is unchanged.
- Call-site citations are off: direct ZNet.SetServerHost calls are in FejdStartup.JoinServer at CLIENT :98979, :98984, :99004, :99013, :99019; :97925 is ZNet.SetServer for hosting a local world, and the command-line join path is :97681 (m_joinServer from ServerJoinDataDedicated). :65795/:65812/:66100 are SetServerToJoin calls in the server-list UI, which is consistent with the claim.
- ZNet.RemotePrint reaches ANY connected client's console, not only an admin's: the client registers 'RemotePrint' unconditionally in RPC_PeerInfo (CLIENT :80104) and RPC_RemotePrint prints to Console.instance (CLIENT :80107-80113 region). For the 'rejoin at host:port' message there is also the routed MessageHud 'ShowMessage'(int type, string) RPC registered on every client (CLIENT :55868, :55908-55911), which needs no character ZDO.
- ZNet.OnNewConnection registers eight peer RPCs, not three: PeerInfo, Disconnect, SavePlayerProfile, RPC_RequestValidSimulationDistance, RPC_ValidatedSimulationDistance on all peers; ServerHandshake server-side; Kicked, Error, ClientHandshake client-side (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:79815-79831). Post-handshake registrations (RoutedRPC, ZDOData, PlayerList, RemotePrint, NetTime, CharacterID, ...) likewise carry no host/port. The conclusion is unchanged.
- Citation fix: the actual ZNet.SetServerHost/SetServer call sites are FejdStartup :97925 (command line) and :98974-99019 (JoinServer); :65795/:65812/:66100 are ServerList UI SetServerToJoin calls that feed those, not SetServerHost calls.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The ruling-out stands. ZNet.RPC_Disconnect takes no parameters and only sets ErrorDisconnected and disconnects (CLIENT :80165-80177). ZNet.SetServerHost overloads (CLIENT :81288-81306) and SetServer (CLIENT :81249-81253) are static setters with no RPC, ZDO, or global-key caller; every call site is in FejdStartup (class starts CLIENT :97098): JoinServer at :98979-99019, command-line parsing at :97681/:97746, and the server-list UI via SetServerToJoin at :65680/:65795/:65812/:66100. Nothing registered on a peer carries an address: OnNewConnection registers PeerInfo, Disconnect, SavePlayerProfile, RPC_RequestValidSimulationDistance, RPC_ValidatedSimulationDistance and, on the client side, Kicked, Error(int) and ClientHandshake (CLIENT :79815-79831); RPC_PeerInfo adds ServerSyncedPlayerData, PlayerList, HistoricalPlayerList, AdminList, RemotePrint (CLIENT :80100-80104). None can change the target host. ServerLoadWorld initialises the single ZNet.World (SERVER :79273-79285). Kick/Ban/RemotePrint exist as cited (SERVER :81635, :81658, :81744).
