### 145. Relocating The Base Instead Of The Player

`wildcard:Relocating The Base Instead Of The Player` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **not-enforceable** · **Effort:** large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


RULED OUT as a general mechanism — ZDO position writes are ownership-gated, portals are sector-frozen, and vanilla clients never re-apply a changed position to an existing instance.


**How it works:** The idea is appealing and it fails at three independent layers.

Layer 1, the write. ZDO.InternalSetPosition (:73734-73745) updates m_position and calls SetSector, but only calls IncreaseDataRevision() `if (IsOwner())`. A position write on a ZDO the server does not own mutates the local copy and never goes on the wire. The server can claim ownership with SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()), but ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924) runs every 2 s for every peer and hands ownership of any Persistent ZDO inside a peer's active area back to that peer. A base is by definition where players are. So the claim must be defended with a Harmony prefix on ZDO.SetOwner (the Wonderland WaterBuoyancyEngine ZdoSetOwnerPatch pattern at Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313), on a global hot path, for every piece of a structure.

Layer 2, the client. This is the killer. ZNetScene.CreateObject (:81996-82022) applies zdo.GetPosition() ONLY at the Object.Instantiate call. ZNetView.Awake (:82567-82633) never touches transform.position afterwards — it applies scale only, and only when m_syncInitialScale is set. Unless a prefab carries a ZSyncTransform with m_syncPosition (buildings do not), a vanilla client simply ignores the new position. The mesh and the colliders stay exactly where they were created. The object only appears at its new coordinate after RemoveObjects destroys the instance (when it leaves the roughly 96-112 m active area, ZNetScene.PointInsideActiveArea :82298-82320) and CreateObjects re-instantiates it — at which point it POPS rather than moves.

Layer 3, portals specifically. ZDO.SetSector early-returns for any prefab in Game.PortalPrefabHash (:73752-73757), so a portal's m_portalObjects key stays whatever it was when AddIfPortal last ran. Move a portal and ZDOMan.FindObjects (:77367-77382) keeps delivering it to peers near its OLD location and never to peers at its new one. Worse, ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO (:76976-76986) removes it using the RECOMPUTED current sector index, which no longer matches the dictionary key, so a later destruction leaks the dead ZDO in m_portalObjects forever and Game.ConnectPortals keeps processing a corpse. And AddIfPortal on the receiving CLIENT adds the ZDO under the NEW key without removing the old one (:77738-77748), duplicating it in every client's registry on every sector crossing.

Layer 4, persistence. A moved portal's new position is never saved: portals are excluded from normal chunks (:77572) and the ChunkPortal file is only written when DirtyPortalObjects is set, which a position write never does.

What remains genuinely possible is far narrower: destroy-and-recreate. Read a small structure's piece ZDOs, record prefab hash, local offset, rotation and the handful of ZDO fields that matter, destroy each (SetOwner then DestroyZDO), and CreateNewZDO the set at the new location. That works, but it loses WearNTear support relationships, terrain modifications, container contents unless explicitly copied, and creator attribution unless re-written — and it is a different feature from 'moving a base'.


**Player experience:** Attempted naively, a player watches their portal apparently not move at all, then walks away and back and finds it has teleported across the valley with no animation, and their friend standing 200 m away still sees it in the old spot. That is the honest outcome and it is why this is ruled out rather than shipped with caveats.


**Failure modes:**
- Position writes on a non-owned ZDO never reach the wire (ZDO.InternalSetPosition :73740)
- A vanilla client never re-applies a changed position to an existing instance; it pops on the next create/destroy cycle
- Server ownership of anything near a player is revoked every 2 s by ReleaseNearbyZDOS
- Portal ZDOs are permanently sector-frozen (ZDO.SetSector :73754), so a moved portal stops syncing to the new location
- Moving a portal across a 64 m boundary permanently leaks the registry entry on destruction (HandleDestroyedZDO :76976-76986) and duplicates it in every receiving client (AddIfPortal :77738)
- Moved positions are never saved for portals; they snap back on restart
- Destroy-and-recreate loses support, terrain mods, container contents and creator attribution

**Designer citations:** ZDO.InternalSetPosition ownership gate — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73734-73745 ; ZDO.SetSector portal exemption — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73752-73757 ; ZNetScene.CreateObject applies position only at Instantiate — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81996-82022 ; ZNetView.Awake never re-applies position — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82567-82633 ; ZNetScene.RemoveObjects / PointInsideActiveArea — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82196-82227, 82298-82320 ; ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76901-76924 ; ZDOMan.AddIfPortal duplicate on re-key — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77732-77752 ; ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO portal removal by recomputed index — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76976-76986 ; ZDOMan.FindObjects — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77367-77382 ; Wonderland ZdoSetOwnerPatch — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313


**Open questions:**
- Does the portal prefab carry a ZSyncTransform with m_syncPosition? If it did, a moving portal would become feasible and this verdict would need revisiting. IN-GAME: claim a portal ZDO, SetPosition it 3 m up every tick for 3 seconds with ForceSendZDO, and see whether the mesh and the walk-through trigger follow (expect a 20 percent per-FixedUpdate lerp with a 5 m snap, ZSyncTransform.SyncPosition :87700-87724) or nothing happens until the player walks ~120 m away and back.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Layer 4 overstates: a moved portal's new position is saved as soon as DirtyPortalObjects is set by any other event — every ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection on any portal (SERVER :73656-73676), every AddIfPortal (:77751), every portal destruction (:76986) — because the portal chunk writes a Clone() of every m_portalObjects entry with its live position (:77621-77631). The corrupted m_portalObjects keying is therefore repaired at the next reload, not permanent.
- Layer 2 nuance: the pop happens only when the ZDO leaves the client's current sector list; a position change that stays inside the client's active area leaves the stale instance in place indefinitely (RemoveObjects earmarks by presence in the current lists, SERVER :82196-82227), and a portal never changes sector list at all (m_portalObjects key frozen), so a moved portal never pops on a client that stays in range.
- Destroy-and-recreate caveat to add: ZDOMan.DestroyZDO of a client-owned piece requires the server to claim ownership first (same ReleaseNearbyZDOS race), and Piece creator/PlatformUserID attribution plus WearNTear support state must be re-written explicitly.
- Layer 1 is bypassable but irrelevant: any subsequent zdo.Set(...) calls IncreaseDataRevision unconditionally (:73648-73653 pattern, :73832), so a non-owning server CAN put a new position on the wire after a data write; Layer 2 still makes the client ignore it, so the verdict stands.
- Layer 3 is worse than a 'corpse': HandleDestroyedZDO calls ZDOPool.Release(zDO) (:76988) while the stale m_portalObjects entry keeps the reference; the pooled object can be re-Initialize()d as a different ZDO and Game.ConnectPortals will then treat that unrelated ZDO as a portal.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] All four layers check out against the decompile with one overstatement in layer 4. Layer 1: ZDO.InternalSetPosition calls SetSector and updates m_position but only IncreaseDataRevision() if IsOwner() (SERVER :73734-73745) — the one ZDO write path with an owner gate. ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS assigns any Persistent ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer when the current owner is not in its own active area (SERVER :76901-76924); IsInPeerActiveArea for the server session id tests the pinned reference position, which is never near a base (SERVER :76886-76897), so a server claim is stolen within 2 s. Wonderland's ZdoSetOwnerPatch is a Harmony prefix on ZDO.SetOwner exactly as cited (WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-312). Layer 2: ZNetScene.CreateObject reads zdo.GetPosition() only for Object.Instantiate (SERVER :81996-82022); ZNetView.Awake touches only type, distant, scale and LoadFields (SERVER :82567-82633); RemoveObjects destroys instances whose ZDO fell out of the current sector lists (SERVER :82196-82227); the client's RPC_ZDOData applies the new position via InternalSetPosition on the ZDO only (SERVER :77128, same code in client) — no re-application to a live transform. Layer 3: ZDO.SetSector early-returns for Game.PortalPrefabHash (SERVER :73752-73757); AddIfPortal is called on every RPC_ZDOData receipt and adds under the current sector key without removing the old one (SERVER :77132, :77732-77752); HandleDestroyedZDO removes with the recomputed GetSectorIndex (SERVER :76976-76986). Layer 4 is wrong as stated: the portal chunk is written whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set by anything, and it is set by every SetConnection/UpdateConnection on any portal, by AddIfPortal, by any portal destruction and at load (SERVER :73656-73676, :77751, :76986, :76539); the save clones every entry of m_portalObjects with its current position (SERVER :77621-77631). So a moved portal's position IS saved at the next save following any portal churn, and reload re-keys it correctly (AddIfPortal at load). The verdict (ruled out as a general mechanism) is unaffected.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed] All four layers verify. Layer 1: ZDO.InternalSetPosition (:73734-73745) bumps DataRevision only `if (IsOwner())`; ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924) re-assigns any Persistent ZDO in a peer's active area whose owner is not a peer with it in their active area — the server's session id is never a ZDOPeer, so a server claim is handed back within 2 s; Wonderland's ZdoSetOwnerPatch exists at WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313. Layer 2: ZNetScene.CreateObject passes zdo.GetPosition() only to Object.Instantiate (:82013-82016); ZNetView.Awake (:82567-82633) touches only Type/Distant/scale/body; the client's ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (CLIENT :77217-77280) calls InternalSetPosition and Deserialize on an existing ZDO and nothing re-applies it to the instance; RemoveObjects/CreateObjects is the only path that moves a piece, as a destroy-and-recreate pop. Layer 3: ZDO.SetSector early-returns for PortalPrefabHash (:73752-73757); HandleDestroyedZDO removes by the recomputed GetSectorIndex() (:76974-76986); AddIfPortal on the client is invoked on every ZDO update (CLIENT :77273) and adds under the new key without removing the old (:77732-77752). Layer 4: portals excluded from normal chunks (:77572), ChunkPortal only when DirtyPortalObjects (:77621), and a position write never sets it. Two additions strengthen the ruling-out rather than weaken it.

### 146. Portal Scaling Through s_scaleHash

`wildcard:Portal Scaling Through s_scaleHash` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** needs-ingame-check → **needs-ingame-check** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


ZNetView applies a ZDO-stored localScale at instantiation when m_syncInitialScale is set — which would give server-set giant or tiny portals with proportionally scaled trigger volumes.


**How it works:** ZNetView.Awake, in the branch taken when a client instantiates from a received ZDO (m_initZDO != null), contains this block at :82591-82606: `if (m_syncInitialScale) { Vector3 vec = m_zdo.GetVec3(ZDOVars.s_scaleHash, Vector3.zero); if (vec != Vector3.zero) transform.localScale = vec; else { float f = m_zdo.GetFloat(ZDOVars.s_scaleScalarHash, transform.localScale.x); if (!transform.localScale.x.Equals(f)) transform.localScale = new Vector3(f, f, f); } }`

ZDOVars.s_scaleHash is 'scale' (:78581) and s_scaleScalarHash is 'scaleScalar' (:78583). Both are plain ZDO writes with no ownership requirement.

If the portal prefab's ZNetView has m_syncInitialScale ticked, then `portalZdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_scaleHash, new Vector3(3f, 3f, 3f))` produces a portal three times normal size on every vanilla client that instantiates it afterwards. Because Unity scales the whole transform hierarchy, the TeleportWorldTrigger child collider scales with it — so a giant portal genuinely has a larger walk-in volume, which is a real gameplay change and not just cosmetic. A 0.3 scale gives a portal you have to aim at.

The critical unknown is whether m_syncInitialScale is set on the portal prefab. It is a public bool on ZNetView (:82543), so LoadFields could in principle set it — but LoadFields runs at :82631, AFTER the scale block at :82591, and Unity's Instantiate copies the PREFAB's serialized value each time, not the previous instance's. So the ZDO cannot bootstrap this: either the prefab already has it or the mechanism is dead for portals. Almost certainly it is off for building pieces; it exists for things like trees and rocks that vary in size.

If it turns out to be off, there is no ZDO-only substitute. ZSyncTransform also reads s_scaleHash (:87814-87820) but that requires a ZSyncTransform on the prefab, which a building piece does not have.

Like LoadFields, this applies only at instantiation — a scale change reaches a player only after the portal is next created in their scene.


**Player experience:** If it works: the spawn hub is a colossal arch you can ride a boat through, while a secret gate hidden in a cave is a knee-high shimmer you have to crouch to notice. Because the collider scales too, the big arch genuinely catches anyone who walks near it and the small one genuinely takes care to enter. Nobody can build one of these — the size is unmistakably an admin fixture. If it does not work, absolutely nothing happens and no error is logged, which is exactly why this needs an in-game check before any design leans on it.


**Failure modes:**
- Entirely dependent on ZNetView.m_syncInitialScale being ticked on the portal prefab — Inspector data, invisible to the decompile, and probably false
- Applies only at instantiation; a live change needs the player to leave and return
- A scaled portal's TeleportWorldTrigger volume scales too, which can make a large portal catch players who did not intend to travel
- Extreme scales will clip terrain and structures with no collision correction
- Client-honoured only

**Designer citations:** ZNetView.Awake scale block — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82591-82606 ; ZNetView.m_syncInitialScale — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82543 ; ZDOVars.s_scaleHash / s_scaleScalarHash — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78581, 78583 ; ZNetView.SyncScale — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82647-82652 ; ZSyncTransform scale read — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87814-87820 ; ZNetView.LoadFields runs after the scale block — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82631


**Open questions:**
- Is ZNetView.m_syncInitialScale true on the portal prefab? THE gating question. IN-GAME: on a client, read ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(portalName).GetComponent<ZNetView>().m_syncInitialScale.
- If it is true, does the TeleportWorldTrigger collider actually scale with the parent transform, and does the trigger still fire correctly at 3x? IN-GAME: set s_scaleHash, relog, and walk into the enlarged frame from various angles.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Minor addition: m_activationRange (glow/target-found proximity, TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal SERVER :143490-143506) and m_exitDistance are plain fields not affected by transform scale; those can be adjusted per-portal via LoadFields keys 'TeleportWorld.m_activationRange' / 'TeleportWorld.m_exitDistance' if HasFields works on the prefab, which is a separate unverified primitive.
- The write replicates on the server build with no ownership claim (ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision has no IsOwner gate, SERVER :73832-73840), but like every ZDO-key write on a portal it is only saved to disk if ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals() is called before the next save (SERVER :76702-76705, :76221-76230).
- Arrival geometry is not scaled: Teleport exit = target pos + forward*1 m + up (:143543-143546). On an enlarged portal the arrival point can sit inside the scaled TeleportWorldTrigger; re-entry on arrival is rejected by Player.TeleportTo's 2 s m_teleportCooldown / IsTeleporting (:15302-15326, :15333), so no loop, but the in-game check should cover exiting a giant volume and, for a 0.3x portal, whether the shrunken trigger is reachable at all.
- m_activationRange (5 m) and m_proximityRoot are not scaled — the connected-glow/particle activation distance stays vanilla regardless of visual size.
- Scale applies only at instantiation on each client (ZNetView.Awake); a change reaches a client only after RemoveObjects/CreateObjects recreates the instance (leave active area or relog).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed] The code is exactly as quoted. ZNetView.Awake, in the m_initZDO != null branch, applies s_scaleHash (Vector3) or s_scaleScalarHash (float) to transform.localScale only when m_syncInitialScale is true (SERVER :82591-82606); m_syncInitialScale is a public bool (SERVER :82543); ZDOVars.s_scaleHash = 'scale' and s_scaleScalarHash = 'scaleScalar' (SERVER :78581, :78583); LoadFields is invoked after the scale block (SERVER :82631) and, per its body, reflects only over MonoBehaviour components and only when the ZDO carries 'HasFields' and 'HasFields<TypeName>' (SERVER :82669-82725), so it cannot bootstrap m_syncInitialScale in time nor touch Transform.localScale. ZNetView.SyncScale writes s_scaleHash on the owner only (SERVER :82647-82652); ZSyncTransform reads the same keys but only when m_syncScale is set on that component (SERVER :87810-87823), which building pieces lack. On the server build, ZDO.Set(int, Vector3) -> ZDOExtraData.Set -> IncreaseDataRevision has no owner check (SERVER :73646-73653, :73832-73840), so the write replicates without an ownership claim. Whether the portal prefabs (portal_wood, portal_stone, portal) have m_syncInitialScale ticked is Inspector data that is not in any decompiled assembly; the option correctly leaves that as the in-game check. The claim that the TeleportWorldTrigger child collider scales with the parent transform is standard Unity hierarchy behaviour and needs no code citation; note that m_activationRange (5f, used by UpdatePortal's GetClosestPlayer for the glow) and m_exitDistance are not scaled, and the exit point is computed from the target ZDO's position and rotation (SERVER :143538-143546), so a giant portal has a bigger walk-in volume but the same glow trigger radius and exit offset.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed] The mechanism reads exactly as claimed. ZNetView.Awake, in the m_initZDO branch, applies s_scaleHash (Vec3) or s_scaleScalarHash (float) to transform.localScale only when m_syncInitialScale is set (:82591-82606); m_syncInitialScale is a public bool (:82543); LoadFields runs afterwards at :82631 and Instantiate copies prefab-serialised values, so the ZDO cannot bootstrap the flag; ZSyncTransform's own scale read requires m_syncScale on a ZSyncTransform component (:87814-87820) which building pieces lack; ZDO.Set(Vec3) bumps revision without an ownership check (:73648-73653 pattern). Whether portal_wood/portal_stone/portal ship with m_syncInitialScale is prefab data invisible to the decompile, so needs-ingame-check is the honest status; the claim that the child TeleportWorldTrigger collider scales with the root is standard Unity hierarchy behaviour. One transit consequence deserves a note: TeleportWorld.Teleport places the arriving player at target position + forward * m_exitDistance(1 m) + up (:143543-143546), unscaled, so on a 3x portal the arrival point will likely be inside the enlarged trigger volume; OnTriggerEnter fires once on arrival but Player.TeleportTo rejects it via the 2 s m_teleportCooldown (:15313-15315, reset in UpdateTeleport :15333) and IsTeleporting (:15309), so there is no ping-pong loop — the player simply has to walk out of a larger volume. Effort small is right.

### 147. The Portal Census — Free World-Wide Reporting

`wildcard:The Portal Census — Free World-Wide Reporting` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


ZDOMan.GetPortalList is a complete, always-resident, zero-bookkeeping enumeration of every portal in the world, and vanilla already logs a parseable pairing audit trail.


**How it works:** Portals are the only ZDO family the server holds in full at all times. ZDOMan.GetPortalList() (:77648-77656) flattens m_portalObjects into a fresh List<ZDO> covering the ENTIRE world regardless of player proximity — the server never unloads them (ZDOMan.ReleaseZDOS only reassigns ownership, :76872-76883; FlushClientObjects is client-only). ZDOMan.GetPortals() (:77643) returns the live dictionary for a zero-alloc hot path.

From each ZDO, readable with no ownership and no client: position (:73822), rotation (:73827), prefab hash (:73817), owner (:74608), ZDOVars.s_tag and s_tagauthor (:78617, :78619), GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) (:74002), ZDOVars.s_creator and s_creatorIndex (:78393, :78395), and ZDOVars.s_health (:78443). s_creatorIndex resolves through ZNet.World.m_playerHistory (:112396) to a socket-verified PlatformUserID, and the same value appears as s_playerID on that player's live character ZDO — so the census is joinable to accounts, offline, across restarts.

Derived reports that need no extra bookkeeping at all:
- Orphan detection. Game.ConnectPortals permanently strands exactly one member of any tag group of odd size, because the surviving pair keeps re-confirming itself (:100607-100621 plus FindRandomUnconnectedPortal :100664-100679). A census flags every tag with an odd count.
- Dangling links: connection non-None but GetZDO(target) null.
- Near-miss tags: tag comparison is bare C# string inequality (:100601, :100669) — ordinal, case-sensitive, whitespace-significant, with an empty-string default. 'Base', 'base' and 'Base ' are three separate networks, and every untagged portal in the world is one giant group. Flagging tags that differ only by case or trailing whitespace catches a real, common, invisible griefing and confusion vector.
- Per-player counts by s_creator, which is exactly what a server-enforced cap needs (see the SpawnGovernor hook pattern).
- Density and reach: portals per biome via WorldGenerator.GetBiome (:151725), and distance to the nearest icon-flagged location via ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcons (:115450-115467).

Vanilla already writes a parseable audit trail with zero patching: ZLog.Log('Connected portals ' + a + ' <-> ' + b) per pair and ZLog.Log('[ Connected N portals ]') per tick (:100619, :100625), plus 'ConnectPortals => Connected N portals.' at load (:77891). ZDO.ToString returns m_uid.ToString() in userID:ID form.

Delivery: TortalPortal's PortalExport (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PortalExport.cs:32-75) is already a pure server-side, IsServer-gated coroutine that counts portals per s_creator and writes an atomic JSON file; Wonderland's DiscordWebhook (Subsystems/DiscordNotify/DiscordWebhook.cs:27) and Heartbeat (Core/Heartbeat.cs:21) are the other two halves. All three are lift-and-rename.


**Player experience:** Admin-facing, but it surfaces to players as competence. The Discord channel gets a nightly line: '412 portals, 6 orphaned tags, 3 near-duplicate tags (Base / base / Base ), 14 dangling links repaired'. When a player complains their gate leads somewhere random, the admin can answer in ten seconds with the actual tag group and the actual orphan. And a web dashboard can show every public gate on a map without any client ever sending anything.


**Failure modes:**
- GetPortalList allocates a fresh List on every call — cache it on a slow tick
- Which member of an odd tag group is stranded depends on dictionary bucket order and changes across restarts, so no report may assume a stable orphan identity
- ZDOIDs are renumbered on every world load, so a census must key by position or tag, never by ZDOID
- s_creator is 0 for world-generated pieces and for anything placed before the field existed (Piece.SetCreator only writes when GetCreator()==0 and IsOwner, :136417)
- s_creatorIndex is -1 when the placer was not yet in m_playerHistory at placement time
- s_tagauthor is an unverified client self-report (RPC_SetTag never cross-checks it, :143587-143602) — never present it as an audit trail without cross-checking peer.m_socket.GetHostName()
- Portals moved server-side are keyed under a stale sector and may appear twice (AddIfPortal :77738)

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Framing 'Portals are the only ZDO family the server holds in full at all times' is wrong: a dedicated server holds EVERY ZDO in m_objectsByID for the whole session (no eviction path exists server-side). Portals are only special in being indexed separately — AddIfPortal calls RemoveFromSector (:77750) so they live in m_portalObjects instead of the sector arrays.
- s_creator and s_creatorIndex are CLIENT-written: Piece.SetCreator(long, PlatformUserID) (:136415-136424) writes GetPlayerID() (the client's own character profile ID, not socket-verified) and a FindIndex computed against the client's mirrored copy of m_playerHistory (-1 if not found). The list contents are server-generated, but the index into it is client-asserted; 'socket-verified' holds only for honest vanilla clients. Same for s_tagauthor, which is LocalUser.PlatformUserID.ToString() sent by the client (:143582).
- Piece.SetCreator has a two-argument signature (long uid, PlatformUserID platformUserID), not one.
- Reconcile predicate line is :100600, not :100601 (off by one; immaterial).
- Log lines go through ZLog.Log → UnityEngine.Debug.Log; on a dedicated server they land in the console/log file — parseable but unstructured; the load-time ConvertPortals/ConnectPortals lines use UnityEngine.Debug.Log directly (:77814, :77890).
- 'Portals are the only ZDO family the server holds in full at all times' is false. ZDOMan.LoadChunks loads EVERY chunk file into m_objectsByID (:76454-76511) and the server never unloads any ZDO; portals are merely indexed separately (m_portalObjects) and saved in ZoneSystem.ChunkPortal. The census is free because the whole world is resident, not because portals are special.
- s_creatorIndex is not server-derived or socket-verified. It is written by the placing CLIENT in Piece.SetCreator (:136415-136424, gated on m_nview.IsOwner(), called from Player.PlacePiece :12516) as FindIndex into the client's mirror of m_playerHistory (refilled by RPC_HistoricalPlayerList :81419-81433) using the client's self-reported LocalUser.PlatformUserID. It is -1 when unresolved. A vanilla client writes it faithfully; a modded client can write any index. The server list itself is authoritative and persisted, so the join is stable across restarts for vanilla-written values only.
- s_creator is the character's profile m_playerID (Player.GetPlayerID → s_playerID :10133/:10144), i.e. per-CHARACTER, not per-account. Per-player counts keyed on s_creator are bypassed by rolling a new character; per-account needs s_creatorIndex with the caveat above.
- The load-time 'ConnectPortals => Connected N portals.' line (:77891) is UnityEngine.Debug.Log from ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (hash-based reconnect of saved ZDOConnectionHashData, :77850-77894), not Game.ConnectPortals. Game.ConnectPortals is additionally invoked once at the end of LoadChunks (:76518).
- GetPortalList entries can include ZDOs whose destroy is queued but not yet applied (DestroyZDO only appends to m_destroySendList :76929-76935; removal happens in HandleDestroyedZDO on the next ZDOMan.Update SendDestroyed :76820). Filter with IsValid as PlacementPatch.GetAllPortals does.
- Tag changes are not observable as events server-side: RPC_SetTag is ZDO-targeted and the dedicated server's HandleRoutedRPC needs ZNetScene.FindInstance (:83645-83660), which is null for portals; and an owning client sends no packet at all (InvokeRoutedRPC :83583-83594). The census must be polled ZDO state, which is what the option describes — but 'audit trail' covers pairing only, not retags.

### 148. Server-Enforced Portal Caps Via The ZDO Arrival Hook

`wildcard:Server-Enforced Portal Caps Via The ZDO Arrival Hook` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The only server-side hook that sees a client-placed object appear is the ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO plus ZDO.Deserialize pair — which makes a genuinely unbypassable per-player portal cap possible for the first time.


**How it works:** Placement itself is unreachable server-side: Player.PlacePiece and TryPlacePiece need a Player instance the server never has, and ZNetScene.Instantiate never runs for a client-placed piece because the CLIENT instantiates and only the ZDO crosses the wire. PortalLock (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/PAUSED/PortalLock/src/PortalLock/PlacementPatches.cs:14, :114) patched exactly those and combined them with an `if (!ZNet.instance.IsServer()) return true;` guard, which means it could never fire once. That is the canonical failure and it is why this option exists.

The working hook is Wonderland's SpawnGovernor pair (Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43, :58, :70), verified against the decompile:

(1) A postfix on the PRIVATE `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int)` (:76684-76692). On the network-receive path the caller is the RPC_ZDOData deserialize loop (:77132) and prefabHashIn is 0, so `zDO.GetPrefab()` is consulted — which for a freshly pooled ZDO is -1. The postfix therefore can only REMEMBER the ZDOID; it cannot yet classify anything. SpawnGovernor's own header records that a CreateNewZDO-only postfix was a shipped bug for exactly this reason.

(2) A postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` — the first moment the real prefab hash exists. Here: if the ZDOID is in the remembered set and `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())`, read `zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator, 0L)`, count that player's existing portals by walking `ZDOMan.instance.GetPortalList()` and comparing s_creator, and if the count exceeds the configured cap do `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo);` plus a PlayerNotify toast naming the cap.

DestroyZDO (:76929-76935) queues into m_destroySendList and SendDestroyed broadcasts the routed DestroyZDO RPC to every peer; the placing client's ZNetScene.OnZDODestroyed (:82186-82194) destroys the GameObject in front of them. The ZDOID also enters m_deadZDOs (:76997), so a replayed packet cannot resurrect it (:77133-77137).

This is STRICTLY STRONGER than the full client-side TortalPortal mod, whose cap lives in a prefix on Player.TryPlacePiece (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PlacementPatch.cs:89) and is therefore trivially bypassed by an unmodded client — its own LogRefusal comment records the effective cap 'wandered between values nobody had deliberately set' before a locking config entry existed. It is the one place the server-only mod beats the full one outright.

Admin bypass is ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName()) (:81811) — NOT Player.IsAdmin, which needs a Player instance.


**Player experience:** A player with six portals already tries to place a seventh. It goes down normally — build effects, materials consumed — and then, within a fraction of a second, it vanishes. A centre-screen message reads 'Portal limit reached (6 of 6). Remove one first.' Because the server destroyed the ZDO rather than blocking the placement, the client-side illusion is a brief flicker rather than a clean refusal, which is the visible cost of the mechanism. Unlike every client-side cap, there is no config file a player can edit and no build of the game that ignores it.


**Failure modes:**
- The placing client already instantiated the piece and consumed materials; the server-side destroy is a flicker, and whether materials are refunded is an in-game unknown
- A postfix on CreateNewZDO ALONE always sees GetPrefab() == 0 or -1 and can never classify — both hooks are mandatory
- ZDO.Deserialize is a global hot path; the check must fail fast on the remembered-ZDOID set before touching anything else
- s_creator is 0 for anything placed before the field existed or by an admin spawn — treat 0 as uncapped or as a separate bucket deliberately
- Counting by walking GetPortalList() on every arrival is O(all portals); cache a per-player tally and invalidate on ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed (:76033)
- A Piece/WearNTear-bearing object destroyed mid-arrival may behave differently from the creatures SpawnGovernor was built for; SpawnGovernor has no portal-specific live test
- A modded client can still spam RPC_ZDOData to recreate; the cap is enforced on arrival, so it holds, but it becomes a packet-rate problem

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Ordering detail: the ZDO.Deserialize postfix runs BEFORE AddIfPortal (:77131 vs :77132), so the new portal is NOT yet in GetPortalList() when counted. The test must be existingCount >= cap, not > cap.
- The cap key s_creator is a client-written long (Piece.SetCreator writes GetPlayerID(), the client's profile ID). Unbypassable for vanilla clients; a modified client can write any creator value. A stronger key is the arriving packet's owner (ownerInternal = the peer's session UID, matched via ZNet.instance.GetPeer(long) :80492) — the server already has it in scope in RPC_ZDOData and it is the identity the socket authenticated.
- Admin bypass needs a peer lookup: the Deserialize postfix has no ZRpc; resolve ZNet.instance.GetPeer(zdo.GetOwner()) then IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName()) (:81811-81814). Owner at that moment is the placing client's UID because RPC_ZDOData just called SetOwnerInternal(ownerInternal) (:77127).
- Player-visible cost is slightly larger than a 'flicker': the client's WearNTear/Piece placement effects and material consumption have already happened, and the TeleportWorld component ran InvokeRepeating before destruction; no refund is possible from the server side.
- Piece.SetCreator signature is (long uid, PlatformUserID platformUserID); citation :136415-136424 is otherwise correct.
- Ordering: the ZDO.Deserialize postfix runs BEFORE RPC_ZDOData's AddIfPortal (:77132), so the arriving portal is not yet in GetPortalList when counted — the test must be 'existing >= cap', not '> cap'. After the postfix returns, AddIfPortal files it in m_portalObjects until the next ZDOMan.Update applies the destroy; if Game.ConnectPortals's 5 s tick lands in that window the portal can be staged for pairing, and the partner's dangling link is cleared on the following tick (:100597-100606). Cosmetic, but real.
- A simpler single hook exists: a postfix on the private ZDOMan.AddIfPortal(ZDO,int) (:77732) fires for every portal arrival with the prefab known; the remembered-set approach is still valid.
- The cap keys on s_creator = character profile ID (Player.GetPlayerID → s_playerID :10133/:10144). A vanilla player bypasses it by creating a new character. Per-account needs s_creatorIndex → ZNet.World.m_playerHistory, which is client-written (Piece.SetCreator :136415-136424) and spoofable by a modded client; for the admin-bypass and for a trustworthy identity, resolve the sender from the RPC_ZDOData ZRpc (FindPeer :76800-76810) rather than the packet's owner field (:77128, untrusted).
- Materials are consumed client-side in Player.PlacePiece with no refund path: every capped attempt costs the player the portal's materials. The option mentions the flicker but should state the material loss as the enforcement cost.
- Within one ZDOMan.Update, SendZDOToPeers2 runs before SendDestroyed (:76818-76820), so the rejected ZDO can be relayed once to other nearby peers before the DestroyZDO RPC follows. Cosmetic.
- Owner of a rejected ZDO must also not be a server-side ZNetScene instance concern: the dedicated server's ZNetScene subscribes to m_onZDODestroyed (:81953) but holds no portal instance, so OnZDODestroyed (:82186-82194) is a no-op server-side; the client-side counterpart destroys the GameObject.

### 149. Cross-Mod Integration Surface

`wildcard:Cross-Mod Integration Surface` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** admin-facing-only → **admin-facing-only** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The exact contention points a portal mod shares with other server-only mods, and the hooks it should expose so they can cooperate.


**How it works:** Five shared surfaces, each a real collision risk.

(1) ZDO.SetOwner prefixes. Wonderland's WaterBuoyancyEngine already installs an unconditional prefix on ZDO.SetOwner to block passive ownership handover (Subsystems/ItemFlow/WaterBuoyancyEngine.cs:301-313). A portal mod that does the same is stacking prefixes on a global hot path touched by ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS for every peer every 2 s. Rule: fail fast on prefab hash first, and never block uid == 0 or uid == ZDOMan.GetSessionID() — those are release and claim.

(2) Game.ConnectPortals. It is public (:100589), it runs every 5 s from an IsServer-gated coroutine (:100074, :100580), and any mod that prefixes it to return false disables pairing for everyone. The politer target is a postfix on the private Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal (:100664-100679) overwriting __result, which leaves vanilla's two-phase commit and logging intact and composes far better with a second mod.

(3) Game.PortalPrefabHash. It is a mutable List<int> behind a private setter (:100021) with no ownership model; two mods adding and removing entries will corrupt each other's assumptions about where ZDOs are filed and saved.

(4) ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC / RouteRPC / RPC_RoutedRPC. These are the universal server-side observation and veto points (:83597, :83632, :83645). Everything wanting to see client traffic patches them. A portal mod watching for the RPC_SetTag hash must save and restore the ZPackage read position (pkg.GetPos / SetPos) or it breaks vanilla routing and every other mod's read.

(5) ZDO key namespace. Mod-private keys are plain int hashes of arbitrary strings, so prefix everything ('tpl_route', 'tpl_lock') and never reuse anything in ZDOVars.s_sessionHashes (:78689-78693) — that set is global and strips the key from the save for every ZDO in the world.

What to EXPOSE. The cheapest useful integration is a public static registry: a delegate other mods can register to veto or redirect a pairing decision, a delegate fired on detected transit, and a read-only accessor for the mod's managed-network view. A non-Harmony observation hook already exists for the destruction side: ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed is a public Action<ZDO> field (:76033) invoked from HandleDestroyedZDO (:76975-76978) before the ZDO leaves m_objectsByID, so the ZDO is still readable in the callback — combine onto it rather than patching.

On the output side, the mod should also be a good citizen of the ecosystem's existing channels: PlayerNotify toasts, DiscordWebhook, AuditLog.Flag, and the portals.json export shape TortalPortal already writes.


**Player experience:** Invisible. What operators experience is that installing a portal mod alongside a world-governance mod, a storage mod and a security mod does not silently break any of them — portal transits stop tripping the speed-cheat detector, ownership tug-of-war between two mods does not strand ZDOs, and the Discord channel carries one coherent stream rather than four competing ones.


**Failure modes:**
- Two unconditional ZDO.SetOwner prefixes on a global hot path compound into a measurable per-tick cost with tens of peers
- A Game.ConnectPortals prefix returning false silently disables pairing for every other mod and for vanilla
- Two mods mutating Game.PortalPrefabHash corrupt each other's filing and save assumptions with no error
- A RPC_RoutedRPC prefix that consumes the ZPackage without restoring GetPos breaks every downstream reader including vanilla
- Reusing a ZDOVars session hash strips that key from the save for every ZDO in the world
- PositionWatch-style security mods will flag portal transits at roughly 110 m/s over a 3 s sample unless the portal mod's detection is shared or the security mod's IsPortalTransit suppression is present

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- (1) A ZDO.SetOwner prefix does NOT cover the client-asserted ownership path: RPC_ZDOData applies incoming owners via SetOwnerInternal (:77116, :77127), which bypasses SetOwner entirely. Such a prefix only blocks server-local calls (ReleaseNearbyZDOS, Game.SetConnection/RPC_SetConnection, ConvertPortals). Say so, or a second mod will assume it is a full ownership fence.
- (2) Redirecting via a FindRandomUnconnectedPortal postfix only composes when the substituted target shares the tag: the reconcile pass on the next tick tears down any pair whose target tag differs (:100600), so cross-tag redirects last at most one 5 s cycle after the ClearCurrentlyConnectingPortals force-write. A cross-tag redirect needs the reconcile predicate patched too.
- (4) On a dedicated server a ZDO-targeted routed RPC (RPC_SetTag) is dropped at HandleRoutedRPC because ZNetScene.FindInstance returns null with no GameObject (:83656-83664); observation must be a prefix on HandleRoutedRPC or RPC_RoutedRPC, and it never sees a retag issued by the ZDO owner (no packet on the wire, per InvokeRoutedRPC's local short-circuit :83586-83591).
- (5) ZDOExtraData.AddSessionHash(int) is public (:74827-74830) — a mod could ALSO add session-only keys; the warning should cover both the static list and that API.
- The RPC_SetTag observation channel is narrower than stated. On a dedicated server HandleRoutedRPC never dispatches a ZDO-targeted RPC because ZNetScene.FindInstance is null for portals (:83645-83660), and RPC_RoutedRPC only calls HandleRoutedRPC when target == server or 0 (:83632-83643) — RPC_SetTag targets the portal owner. The only server-side sighting is a prefix on RPC_RoutedRPC/RouteRPC on the relay path, and it sees nothing when the retagging client owns the portal (InvokeRoutedRPC :83583-83594 skips RouteRPC when targetPeerID == m_id). Wonderland's HandleRoutedRPC prefix works only because RPC_RequestOwn targets a server-owned ZDO.
- ZPackage read-position: RouteRPC relays via RoutedRPCData.Serialize → ZPackage.Write(ZPackage) which uses GetArray() (whole buffer, :83087-83092, :83418-83423) and is immune to read position. Position restore matters only for local dispatch (HandleRoutedRPC → RoutedMethod.Invoke reads m_parameters from its current pos). The advice stands; the stated reason ('breaks vanilla routing') is only true for the local-dispatch half.
- Add ZDOHelper.s_stripOldData to the key blacklist: ZDOExtraData.Init also strips 256 'room{i}_seed' hashes on load (:74817-74820).
- Mutating PortalPrefabHash after LoadChunks does not re-file existing ZDOs: LoadChunks files portals from the ChunkPortal file and everything else via InitialAddToSector (:76476-76481, :76505-76508); a hash added at runtime leaves already-loaded ZDOs of that prefab out of m_portalObjects until they are re-received. This strengthens the option's warning.

### 150. The Ashlands Stone Portal

`wildcard:The Ashlands Stone Portal` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **not-enforceable** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


There is no code difference between portal variants anywhere in the assembly — every behavioural difference is Inspector data on the prefab, and none of it is network-reachable.


**How it works:** I searched both assemblies. There is exactly ONE TeleportWorld class and it is byte-identical between the server and client decompiles (server :143402-143682 versus client :144142-144422; a diff of the two regions is empty). There is no subclass, no variant branch, no prefab-name test, no per-prefab code path of any kind. No portal prefab name string (portal_wood, portal_stone, portal_blackmarble) appears anywhere in either decompile — the only portal literals are localization keys ($piece_portal, $piece_portal_tag, $piece_portal_connected, $piece_portal_unconnected, $piece_portal_censored_warning, $piece_portal_settag, $msg_portal_blocked).

Everything that could distinguish an Ashlands stone portal from a wood one lives in serialized Inspector fields: TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems (:143429), m_exitDistance (:143413), m_activationRange (:143411), m_hoverOffset (:143431), the two Colors (:143418, :143421), the EffectFade and EffectList references (:143423, :143427), plus whatever WearNTear.m_health, WearNTear.m_ashDamageImmune and Piece values the prefab carries.

The widely believed 'the Ashlands stone portal allows all items' would, if true, be m_allowAllItems = true on that prefab. Nothing in code confirms or denies it and nothing in code can change it over the wire — the field is never read from or written to a ZDO by TeleportWorld and never appears in any RPC. A Harmony write to it on the server mutates a prefab copy no client will ever read, because the server never instantiates a portal.

The ONE route that does exist is ZNetView.LoadFields (see Field Injection), which is a generic ZNetView mechanism and completely indifferent to which portal prefab it is applied to. So the honest statement is: a server-only mod cannot make portal_stone behave differently from portal_wood by virtue of it being portal_stone, but it CAN give any individual portal ZDO of either prefab an overridden m_allowAllItems.

The only correct handling of prefab variety is to never hard-code the list: read Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash (:100021) and Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs (:99828) at runtime, which also picks up modded portal pieces for free. TortalPortal hard-codes portal_wood, portal_stone and portal_blackmarble (PlacementPatch.cs:217-219, ScatterCommand.cs:158) purely as a fallback.


**Player experience:** No player-visible feature. The practical consequence is a documentation one: an operator who expects the mod to 'turn on ore transport for stone portals only' must be told that the mod can turn it on for INDIVIDUAL portals (via field injection) or for the whole world (via GlobalKeys.TeleportAll), but never for a prefab class — and that GlobalKeys.TeleportAll does not mean everything either, because Inventory.IsTeleportable rejects any item with m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000 BEFORE it ever consults the key.


**Failure modes:**
- All per-prefab differences are Inspector data with zero network reachability
- Harmony-writing m_allowAllItems on the server mutates a prefab copy that no client ever reads, because the server instantiates no portals
- Hard-coding prefab names misses modded portal pieces and breaks on a game update
- GlobalKeys.TeleportAll cannot lift the m_toolTier >= 1000 rejection (Inventory.IsTeleportable :68862-68868)

**Designer citations:** TeleportWorld class, identical server and client — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143402-143682 versus assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:144142-144422 ; TeleportWorld public fields are all plain Inspector values — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143411-143437 ; TeleportWorld.Teleport reads m_allowAllItems — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143533 ; Inventory.IsTeleportable toolTier gate before TeleportAll — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:68860-68881 ; Game.PortalPrefabHash / m_portalPrefabs — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100021, 99828; Game.Awake :100027-100032 ; ZNetView.LoadFields (the one generic override route) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82669-82739 ; TortalPortal hard-coded names — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/PlacementPatch.cs:217-219, /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/ScatterCommand.cs:158

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Inventory.IsTeleportable tests m_toolTier >= 1000 BEFORE consulting allowAllItems OR TeleportAll (:68862-68868), so a field-injected m_allowAllItems=true on a portal ZDO also does not move those items — the option states this only for TeleportAll; it applies to both.
- The localization literal list omits $menu_portals (present in the server decompile). Trivial.
- The claim sentence 'none of it is network-reachable' is contradicted by the option's own LoadFields paragraph; the accurate statement is 'not reachable per prefab class, reachable per ZDO instance via HasFields keys'.
- Add the LoadFields timing caveat: it runs only from ZNetView.Awake (client :82860), so an injected TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems takes effect when the client next instantiates that portal (zone reload / relog), and remains client-honoured — the check is still Teleport (:143533) on the local client.
- Pedantic: a server-side Harmony write to the TeleportWorld field on the server's prefab copy is not merely unread — ZNetScene on the dedicated server does hold prefab GameObjects, but no portal instance is ever created there, so the statement stands.

### 151. The Minimal Optional Client Mod — Where The Ceiling Actually Sits

`wildcard:The Minimal Optional Client Mod — Where The Ceiling Actually Sits` · domain **wildcard** · source `wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A few hundred lines of optional client code removes almost every Ruled Out item at once, and the single cheapest thing it can buy is a moment-of-transit hook.


**How it works:** Every hard ceiling in this report traces to one of four root causes, and a small optional client plugin dissolves three of them.

ROOT 1 — no moment-of-transit hook. TeleportWorld.Teleport has exactly one caller, TeleportWorldTrigger.OnTriggerEnter (:143673-143681), gated on Player.m_localPlayer. A client-side Harmony PREFIX on TeleportWorld.Teleport(Player) is about 15 lines and is the single highest-leverage thing an optional client mod can add: it fires exactly once, at the exact instant, with the portal instance and the Player in scope. From there the client can InvokeRoutedRPC a request to the server and return false to suspend the transit while the server decides. That one hook alone buys: per-transit server authorization, a real destination-picker UI, per-player routing, tolls charged at the moment of use, and accurate transit logging — replacing the 0.2-0.4 s position-polling approximation entirely.

ROOT 2 — the server cannot see inventory. Player.Save writes only to the local .fch (:14091-14170) and ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles collects nothing (:79653-79675). A client plugin can serialise an inventory summary into ZNet.m_serverSyncedPlayerData (the arbitrary string dictionary in RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData, :80395-80410) or send it in the transit-request RPC. That buys server-side ore enforcement, tolls, and 'you may not carry this here' rules.

ROOT 3 — no UI. All of TortalPortal's PortalUIManager, LivePreview, PortalMapPins and Favorites are structurally unreachable server-side. A client plugin re-enables them, and ServerSync's CustomSyncedValue<T> (already vendored identically in both Wonderland/Shared/ServerSync.cs:91 and TortalPortal/ServerSync.cs) is the ready-made delivery channel for the server's portal index over the login handshake — a channel a vanilla client has no handler for and will never receive.

ROOT 4 — no cross-server redirect. A client plugin CAN call ZNet.SetServerHost and reconnect (:81288-81302), which is the only way multi-server travel is ever happening. Character data still does not transfer; that requires the two servers to share a save directory or an out-of-band profile sync.

Design shape for 'optional': the server ships a ServerSync VersionCheck that does NOT enforce (Wonderland/Shared/ServerSync.cs:1117), and gates the enhanced path on whether the peer announced the plugin. Vanilla clients keep the degraded ZDO-only experience described in every other option here; modded clients get the full one. TortalPortal's SectorSubscription (/home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/TortalPortal/SectorSubscription.cs:106) is worth remembering as the other half — a postfix on the private ZDOMan.CreateSyncList appends arbitrary sectors to a specific peer's sync packet, which is the only way to put portal data in front of a client who is not standing next to a portal.

Cost estimate: the transit prefix plus a request/response RPC pair plus a version handshake is roughly 200-300 lines. Everything beyond that is UI polish.


**Player experience:** A vanilla player sees the full server-only feature set: managed networks, indestructible admin gates, rotating hubs, tag signage, event portals, map pins. A player who installs the optional 200-line plugin additionally gets: a destination list when they walk into a hub instead of a coin-flip; a message that actually explains why a gate refused them; a toll prompt; and their ore checked against server rules rather than client ones. Crucially the two can stand at the same portal at the same time and both have a working, coherent experience — the modded one is just better informed.


**Failure modes:**
- A client prefix on TeleportWorld.Teleport that suspends the transit must handle the server never replying, or the player is stuck at a dead gate
- Any inventory data the client reports is client-authored and therefore spoofable by a hostile client — it buys convenience and honesty, not security
- Once a feature depends on the client plugin, version skew becomes a real support burden; use ServerSync VersionCheck in non-enforcing mode
- CustomSyncedValue delivery happens at the login handshake, so a plugin installed mid-session sees nothing until relog
- Cross-server travel via SetServerHost still cannot move character data; the two servers must share a save directory or an external profile sync
- A ZDOMan.CreateSyncList postfix that streams extra sectors competes with the peer's own negotiated simulation distance and the 10240-byte send queue cap (:77010-77016)

### 152. The Dial — portal tag as a command line

`player-ux-no-client:The Dial — portal tag as a command line` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The player retags a portal with a 10-char opcode string (`>Haldor`, `#Base`, `?`); the server reads it out of the ZDO, rewrites the connection, and echoes a canonical answer back into the same tag in ~250 ms.


**How it works:** OBSERVATION — do NOT hook RPC_SetTag. `TeleportWorld.SetText` calls `m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag", tag, authorId)` (:143583) = `InvokeRoutedRPC(m_zdo.GetOwner(), …)` (ZNetView.InvokeRPC :82855). `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) gives every persistent ZDO in a peer's ~96 m active area to that peer within 2 s, so the retagging player owns the portal, `targetPeerID == m_id`, and `InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally and SKIPS `RouteRPC` (:83587-83594). Zero packets — an RPC prefix sees nothing. The change instead arrives as ordinary ZDO data: client `ZDO.Set(s_tag,…)` bumps DataRevision, `ZDOMan.ClientChanged` queues it (:77727), flush every 0.05 s (:76843), server `RPC_ZDOData` → `ZDO.Deserialize` (:74225). HOOK = Harmony postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)`, filter `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(GetPrefab())` (:100021), diff `GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` (:78617). Backstop: poll `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648) at 0.25 s — world-global, always resident.

GRAMMAR, char 0 = opcode, chars 1-9 = operand: `>NAME`/`>7` dial · `#NAME` name this portal · `-` unlink · `?` help+directory · `*NAME` join public network · `@spawn`/`@haldor` world target · `!` lock. ASCII only; `>` is safe because `RemoveRichTextTags` (:143459) only strips a `<…>` pair.

ACTION: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` (:74627/:77362) → `zdo.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, destId)` (:73656) → `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, echo)` → `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702, mandatory — a tag-only write never dirties the portal chunk and is lost at save) → `ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706) → PRE-WARM `ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, destId)` (:77714) so `TargetFound()` (:143640) succeeds on the first walk-through instead of silently failing while `RequestZDO` round-trips.

PAIRING: `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 tears down any link whose two ends' `s_tag` differ (:100601) every 5 s, so per-portal display tags require prefixing it out and re-implementing both passes for unmanaged portals.

LATENCY: 0.05 s client flush + ½RTT → Deserialize postfix (synchronous) → write + ForceSendZDO → 0.05 s server flush + ½RTT → `GetHoverText` (:143453) reads the ZDO live every frame. ≈1 RTT + ≤100 ms; ~160 ms on a 60 ms server.


**Player experience:** You walk to a portal. Hover reads `Teleport Portal tag:"?help" [unconnected]`. You press E — the stock vanilla rename box, topic `Portal tag`. Type `?`, Enter. Within a quarter second six toasts stack in the corner: `>name dial`, `#name name this portal`, `- unlink · ! lock · @ world`.

Press E again, type `#Base`, Enter. The hover instantly reads `"#Base"`; toast: `Named: Base. 4 portals on this server.` You run 600 m to your mine, press E there, type `>Base`, Enter. Before you let go of the key the hover flips to `">Base"`, the blue connect effect fires (`UpdatePortal` :143499), and a toast reads `Dialed → Base (Meadows, 612m)`. You step through — it works first try, no dead transit, because the destination ZDO was force-sent in the same breath.

Mistype `>Bsae`: 200 ms later the hover reads `"?Bsae"` and a toast says `No portal named Bsae. Did you mean: Base, Bog?` The old link is untouched. Locked portal: hover flicks to `"!Vault"`, toast `Vault is locked by Bjorn.`

Total human time per command: press E, type ≤10 characters, Enter, read. About four seconds.


**Failure modes:**
- The echo MUST be ≤10 chars. `TextInput.Show` sets `characterLimit = 10` then assigns `m_inputField.text` (:61515-61521); Unity's InputField text setter clamps, so a longer server tag is truncated in the dialog and a reflexive Enter submits the truncation as a new command.
- The parser must treat re-submission of its own canonical echo as a no-op, or every dialog open+OK re-fires the last command.
- Two players retagging the same portal inside one 0.05 s flush: last DataRevision wins, the loser's command is never observed and never reported.
- `TextInput.OnEnter` does `.Replace("\\n","\n")` (:61496) — typing backslash-n injects a literal newline into `s_tag`, breaking the quoted hover string. Sanitize on read.
- Vanilla `Game.ConnectPortals` destroys any managed link within 5 s unless prefixed out (:100601).
- Without `SetDirtyPortals()` every rename silently reverts at the next world save (:77621, :76702).
- An address book keyed by ZDOID is empty after a restart — `ZDO.Load` renumbers every uid (:74552). Key by rounded world position.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Remove zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) from the action sequence: the server's ZDO.Set/SetConnection do not require ownership, and while the server owns the portal (≤2 s until ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76927 returns it) a vanilla rename is silently dropped — SetText routes to the owner (:82855-82858), the server has no instance (:83656-83664), and client RPC_SetTag is IsOwner-gated (:143587).
- Client RPC_SetTag clears this portal's connection and RPC_SetConnected clears the previous partner's (:143590-143593, :143605-143625); the governor must rewrite both ends when the topology is bidirectional.
- Attribution: the RPC_ZDOData sender is the portal's current owner (FindPeer(rpc) :77078), which with two nearby players may not be the typist; s_tagauthor (:143597) is client-supplied and spoofable. Treat lock ownership as vanilla-honest only.
- The client's push always carries connection=None (ZDO.Serialize includes the connection, :74170-74175); the postfix must re-assert the managed connection even when the tag string is unchanged.
- ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage) begins at :74206, not :74225.
- Remove zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) from the ACTION or document a <=2 s window in which the next vanilla RPC_SetTag is routed to the server and dropped (HandleRoutedRPC :83656-83664; ReleaseNearbyZDOS cadence :76874-76880). Server-side ZDO.Set/SetConnection do not check ownership (:73648-73666); clients accept any higher DataRevision (:77106-77120).
- Every vanilla retag also executes UpdateConnection(Portal, None) and SetConnectedPortal(oldTarget) on the client (:143591-143594, :143605-143628); the ACTION must rewrite both ends of the new link and clean the old partner each command.
- Sender identity: the ZDOData packet comes from the portal's owner peer, which is the typist only when ReleaseNearbyZDOS assigned it to them; key '!' lock ownership on s_tagauthor (:143584, client-asserted), not the RPC sender.
- Prewarm ForceSendZDO(peer, destId) shaves at most one 0.5 s UpdatePortal poll; TargetFound already self-heals via RequestZDO (:143652-143654, :77689-77692) and the trigger fires on entry, so 'dead transit' is not a real failure mode.
- Displayed tag is CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC output on PlayFab backends (:143568); keep opcodes to plain ASCII punctuation.
- Effort: medium-large (full pairing takeover + Deserialize postfix on all incoming ZDOs + address book).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Observation chain verified: SetText → m_nview.InvokeRPC('RPC_SetTag', text, PlatformUserID) (:143579-143585) → ZNetView.InvokeRPC → InvokeRoutedRPC(m_zdo.GetOwner(), ...) (:82855-82858); when targetPeerID == m_id the client handles locally and skips RouteRPC (:83587-83594). ReleaseNearbyZDOS on the server hands any persistent ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer every 2 s (:76873-76927), so the nearby player normally owns the portal and no RPC crosses the wire. Client RPC_SetTag then writes s_tag via ZDO.Set → IncreaseDataRevision → ClientChanged (:73832-73840, :77727-77730); client send timer is 0.05 s (SendZDOToPeers2 :76837-76860); server RPC_ZDOData → ZDO.Deserialize (:77118, Deserialize body :74206-74240). ### 153. Raising the 10-character tag cap

`player-ux-no-client:Raising the 10-character tag cap` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **not-enforceable** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Server-side widening of the portal rename box past 10 characters.


**How it works:** The cap is a literal argument in client-only code with no ZDO, RPC, config or global-key backing: `TeleportWorld.Interact` calls `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10)` (:143482) and `TextInput.Show` assigns it to `m_inputField.characterLimit` (:61519). `Interact` is reached only from `Player.Update` → `Interact(m_hovering,…)` gated on `Player.m_localPlayer`, and no `TeleportWorld` MonoBehaviour ever exists on a dedicated server: `Game.FixedUpdate` pins `SetReferencePosition(1e6,0,1e6)` every physics tick (:100465) so `ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted` never instantiates a portal (:82105). Nothing server-side to patch, nothing on the wire to intercept.

The WRITE side is uncapped — `ZDO.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, string)` (:73721) has no length check, `RPC_SetTag` performs none (:143587-143602), and `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is `return text;` in the server build (:94588). So the server CAN store a 200-char tag and vanilla clients render it after `RemoveRichTextTags` (:143459). But it is a trap: the moment any player presses E on that portal, `TextInput.Show` clamps the pre-filled text to 10 and Enter submits the truncation as the portal's new tag AND as a command. A long display tag is a live footgun on every player-reachable portal.

A stateful multi-submission concatenation (`>Halr` then `>dor`, joined per (playerId, portalPos, 30 s)) technically extends the budget but is worse than 10-char discipline and confuses everyone. Put the long text on a Sign (50 chars) or in a HUD toast (unlimited) instead.


**Player experience:** Nothing changes. The rename box stops accepting input at exactly 10 characters on every vanilla client, forever. If the server wrote a longer tag, the box shows only the first 10 and the player has no way to know the rest existed.


**Failure modes:**
- Storing >10-char tags on player-reachable portals turns every accidental Enter into a silent destructive truncation.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- The claim that TextInput.Show clamps pre-filled text to 10 and Enter submits a truncated tag is not supported by the decompile: GuiInputField (gui_framework.dll, not decompiled) is a TMP_InputField, whose SetText does not truncate to characterLimit; long server-written tags are most likely round-tripped intact and RPC_SetTag no-ops on equality (:143591). Mark this sub-claim needs-ingame-check.
- Add: RPC_SetTag runs only on the portal ZDO owner (:143589); with server-claimed ownership, vanilla renames are routed to the server and dropped in ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC because FindInstance is null (:83657-83662).
- `GuiInputField` (SERVER:61436) is not in any decompile on disk; the prefill-truncation claim rests on TMP_InputField's documented `characterLimit`-on-assignment behaviour, not on read source. If a build ever ships a GuiInputField that does not clip on assignment, Enter would resubmit the full long tag and `RPC_SetTag`'s equality check (SERVER:143591) would make it a no-op — i.e. the trap would vanish, but the cap would still be un-raisable.
- Add: Escape in `TextInput.Update` hides without submitting (SERVER:61468-61471), so a player who opens the box and backs out does not truncate.

No ZDO key, RPC, config or global key carries the limit, and `TeleportWorld` is only instantiated where `ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted` runs against a real reference position; `Game.FixedUpdate` pins it to (1e6,0,1e6) on the server (:100465), so there is nothing server-side to patch. Write side is genuinely uncapped: `ZDO.Set(int, string)` (:73721-73726) has no length check, `RPC_SetTag` only compares tag/author and writes (:143587-143602), server `FilterUGC` is `return text;` (:94588-94591). TMP_InputField.SetText does not apply `characterLimit` to programmatic assignment (the limit only blocks appended keystrokes), so a 200-char server tag pre-filled in the box is most likely shown in full and re-submitted unchanged on Enter — `RPC_SetTag` then sees `tagRaw == tag` and writes nothing (:143591-143592). The truncation-on-Enter trap is probably false; treat as needs-ingame-check, but it does not rescue the option. (2) The option's line range :143587-143602 for RPC_SetTag is right; note `RPC_SetTag` executes only on the ZDO OWNER (`m_nview.IsOwner()`, :143589) via `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string)` → `InvokeRoutedRPC(m_zdo.GetOwner(), …)` (:82855-82858) — if the mod claims portal ownership server-side, every vanilla rename is routed to the server, hits `ZNetScene.FindInstance == null` in `HandleRoutedRPC` (:83657-83662) and is silently dropped. Not this option's problem but a hazard for any design relying on '>tag' commands.

So the footgun is real: any E+Enter on a long-tagged portal silently truncates it and breaks its link. Escape cancels without submitting (SERVER:61468-61471), which is the only escape hatch. Write side is uncapped as claimed: `ZDO.Set(int,string)` has no length check (SERVER:73721-73727); server `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is `return text;` (SERVER:94588-94591); hover renders the full stored string through `RemoveRichTextTags` only (SERVER:143459). No `TeleportWorld` exists server-side: `Game.FixedUpdate` pins reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every tick (SERVER:100458-100466) and `CreateObjectsSorted` builds only near that position (SERVER:82105-82112). Nothing to patch, nothing on the wire carrying the limit. `ruled-out` / `not-enforceable` is the correct label.

### 154. The Ledger — signs as a server-written live directory

`player-ux-no-client:The Ledger — signs as a server-written live directory` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Any Sign within 8 m of a managed portal is adopted by the server, which rewrites `ZDOVars.s_text` so the sign shows a live paged portal directory; the player reads it with zero mod.


**How it works:** DISCOVERY: every 10 s, for each portal from `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648), run `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(portalPos, 8f)` (Wonderland Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25 → `ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects` :77142) and keep ZDOs whose prefab resolves via `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)` to a GameObject carrying `Sign`. Sort by (y desc, then bearing around the portal) so a stacked wall reads top-to-bottom. Each sign is one line.

WRITE: `Sign.Awake` runs `InvokeRepeating("UpdateText", 2f, 2f)` (:141779) and `UpdateText` early-returns when `m_lastRevision == zdo.DataRevision` (:141837-141843). A server write to `s_text` (:78629) bumps DataRevision and every client in range repaints within 2 s with no further work. Write `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_text, line)` AND `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_author, "")`. Never write `"host"`: `UpdateText` maps it to `m_author = null`, and `UpdateViewPermission` calls `OnCheckPermissionCompleted(Denied)` then FALLS THROUGH with no `return` to `if (m_author.Value.IsValid)` (:141867-141876) — `Nullable.Value` on a null throws every 2 s on every viewer. Empty author → `PlatformUserID.None`, HasValue true, Granted path. Claim ownership then `ForceSendZDO` so distant boards can be pushed.

BUDGET: `m_characterLimit = 50` (:141756) is the client input widget only; the server write is uncapped, but the same truncation trap applies, so stay ≤50 per sign. `GetHoverText` strips rich text (:141785) but `m_textWidget.text` is set RAW (:141891/:141895) — so TMP markup (`<color=#ffcc00>`) DOES render on the physical sign face while being stripped from the hover tooltip. Colour-coded directories are real.

PAGING with a 6-sign wall: line 0 header + page N/M, lines 1-4 entries `7  Base  612m  OK`, line 5 footer. Page turn driven by any other channel (crouch, a jump, a `>p2` tag).


**Player experience:** You build four ordinary wooden signs in a column beside your portal and walk away. Ten seconds later they read, in Valheim's own sign lettering:

`— PORTAL DIRECTORY 1/3 —`
`1 Base      0m    HOME`
`2 Haldor    1.2k  open`
`3 BlackFors 840m  open`

A fifth sign reads `type >1 on the portal`. You press E on the portal, type `>2`, Enter. A quarter second later the portal glows; two seconds later the board repaints and line 2 reads `2 Haldor 1.2k ▸YOU` in yellow. When your friend dials line 3 from her outpost your board updates for you too — same server state.

Entries you cannot use render grey. A destroyed portal shows `4 Mine2 --- GONE` until the server prunes it.

Cost: four signs of wood and thirty seconds of building. No typing, no learning — signs are the most legible object in Valheim and every player already knows they display text.


**Failure modes:**
- Writing `s_author = "host"` throws inside `Sign.UpdateViewPermission` on every viewing client every 2 s (:141869-141876). Write an empty string.
- A player pressing E on a managed sign sees the text clamped to 50 and can overwrite the server's line; the server rewrites within a tick, so the net effect is a flicker plus the player's text silently lost.
- Sign text only updates for clients holding the sign's ZDO. A distant board is stale unless the server calls `ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, signZdoId)` per peer.
- `m_characterLimit` is an Inspector field; 50 is the class default and hanging/large sign variants may differ.
- Rich text renders on the face but not in hover, so the two surfaces disagree for a player who reads by hovering.

**Open questions:**
- Is `PlatformUserID.None.IsValid` false? It lives in the Splatform assembly, absent here. Either branch appears safe (`RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync` is a Granted-returning stub at :88350) but confirm no exception path.
