- Does `RelationsManager.UpdateAuthorIfHost(resolvedAuthor, ref resolvedAuthor)` (:141848, runs when the viewer owns the sign) rewrite an empty author to `"host"` and walk into the NRE? IN-GAME: stand at a server-written sign for 60 s.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Exception on author "host" is InvalidOperationException from Nullable<PlatformUserID>.Value (:141872), swallowed by Unity's InvokeRepeating; effect is 2 s log spam and the runic hidden text, not a crash.
- Ownership claim is unnecessary: ZDO.Set (:73721) and ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(long, ZDOID) (:77714) have no owner check; server→peer sync is sector+revision only (:77212-77238, :76003-76013). Remove 'claim ownership'.
- Add revision-collision caveat: a client write issued before the server's reply arrives produces equal DataRevisions and both sides drop each other's packet (:77105-77110); rely on the periodic rewrite to reconverge.
- Rich-text rendering on the sign face depends on the prefab's TMP richText flag (not in the decompile); vanilla sign colour tags are common knowledge, but mark needs-ingame-check for markup beyond <color>.
- Enforcement: server-written but overwritable by any player who can Interact (client-side ward check only, :141917); re-assert on timer.
- Enforcement: not `server-enforced`. It is a server-AUTHORED, client-RENDERED display; any vanilla client can overwrite or destroy the sign between passes (`Sign.SetText` SERVER:141915-141929; `RPC_DestroyZDO` has no sender check). Label as client-honoured output.
- `RPC_ZDOData` discards client updates whose DataRevision <= the server copy's (SERVER:77104-77114). Server rewrites bump the revision; a player editing an adopted sign in the delivery window loses the edit silently. Only rewrite when the text actually changes.
- Drop `ClaimOwnership`: `ForceSendZDO` requires no ownership (SERVER:77706) and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` reassigns server-owned persistent ZDOs near a player every 2 s (SERVER:76874-76925).
- Non-ASCII glyphs (▸ — ·) and space-aligned columns are unverified against the sign font atlas — needs-ingame-check for the rendered layout, not for the mechanism.
- `s_text` is saved to disk: directory text persists across restart and after mod removal as stale plain text.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism verified. `Sign.Awake` → `InvokeRepeating("UpdateText", 2f, 2f)` (:141779); `UpdateText` gates on `m_lastRevision == zdo.DataRevision` (:141837-141842), reads `s_text` (:141844), and ends in `OnCheckPermissionCompleted` which assigns `m_textWidget.text = m_currentText` raw (:141895). Server `ZDO.Set(int,string)` bumps DataRevision with no owner check (:73721-73726, :73832-73840); server→client sync is sector-based and ownership-agnostic — `CreateSyncList` on the server collects `FindSectorObjects` results filtered only by `peer.ShouldSend` (revision compare, :76003-76013; :77212-77238); the client's `RPC_ZDOData` applies any packet with `num4 > zDO.DataRevision` regardless of who owns it (:77105-77127). `ForceSendZDO(long peerID, ZDOID)` is public (:77714). The 'host' hazard is real and present in the client build too: `resolvedAuthor == "host"` → `m_author = null` (:141857-141859), `UpdateViewPermission` calls Denied then falls through to `m_author.Value.IsValid` (:141867-141876; client :142607-142613). Rich text: `GetHoverText` strips tags (:141785), widget receives raw string (:141895) — vanilla players already use colour tags on signs, so rendering is a safe assumption though the TMP `richText` flag is prefab data not in the decompile. Corrections: (1) the thrown exception is `InvalidOperationException` (Nullable.Value), not an NRE, and it is caught by Unity's InvokeRepeating dispatcher — log spam plus the runic Denied text, not a client crash. Vanilla itself writes "host" when `!IsSignedIn` (:141922) and only the OWNER remaps it via `UpdateAuthorIfHost` (:141848, :88385) — so avoid "host" as stated. (2) 'Claim ownership then ForceSendZDO' — ownership is unnecessary for the write or the push; `ZDO.Set` and `ForceSendZDO` have no owner requirement, and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` would hand it back anyway. Drop the claim. (3) Revision race: after a server write the server copy is at rev N+1; if the owning client writes the sign again before the push lands, its rev also becomes N+1 and BOTH directions are discarded by the `<=` guard (:77108, server side symmetric) — the sign silently diverges until the next write. Harmless for an output-only board but must be re-asserted on a timer (the 10 s rewrite already does this). (4) 8 m adoption will overwrite any pre-existing player sign (chest labels) near a portal — needs an opt-in marker or ignore-signs-with-existing-non-directory-text rule. (5) Enforcement label: the server authors the text but any player outside a ward can retype it (`Sign.SetText` checks only client-side `PrivateArea.CheckAccess`, :141917); it is server-written output, not protected state.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism verified. `Sign.Awake` runs `UpdateText()` then `InvokeRepeating("UpdateText", 2f, 2f)` (SERVER:141772-141780); `UpdateText` early-returns on `m_lastRevision == DataRevision` (SERVER:141837-141842) and otherwise reads `s_text`/`s_authorDisplayName`/`s_author` (SERVER:141844-141847). Server-side `ZDO.Set` has no ownership check and bumps `DataRevision` (SERVER:73648-73654, 73832-73840); the server's sync list is sector-based per peer and `ShouldSend` compares `DataRevision` (SERVER:77212-77238, 76003-76013), so any viewer in range receives the new text and repaints within 2 s. Client `RPC_ZDOData` applies incoming data whenever `num4 > zDO.DataRevision` regardless of ownership (same code, SERVER:77104-77128). The `"host"` trap is real and identical in the client build: `resolvedAuthor == "host"` → `m_author = null` (SERVER:141855-141858) → `UpdateViewPermission` calls Denied then falls through to `m_author.Value.IsValid` (CLIENT:142604-142616) → `InvalidOperationException` every 2 s. Empty author → `PlatformUserID.None` → `IsValid` false → Granted (SERVER:141851-141853, 141871-141879). Raw `m_textWidget.text = m_currentText` (SERVER:141895) and hover via `RemoveRichTextTags` (SERVER:141785) both confirmed. `m_characterLimit = 50` is only the `Interact` widget cap (SERVER:141756, 141831). Attacks that land: (1) The enforcement label is a category error — this is an OUTPUT surface; nothing is enforced, and any vanilla client can overwrite the text (`Sign.SetText` is a plain owned write, SERVER:141915-141929) or delete the sign (`RPC_DestroyZDO`, no sender check) until the next 10 s pass. (2) DataRevision race: `RPC_ZDOData` DROPS any client ZDO update whose revision is not strictly greater than the server's copy (SERVER:77104-77114). Every server rewrite bumps the server revision; a player who presses E on an adopted sign between the server's write and its delivery (~50 ms + ½ RTT) has their edit silently discarded. Small but real, and it means the mod must never rewrite unchanged text (harmless: `ZDOExtraData.Set` returns false on equal value so no bump). (3) `ClaimOwnership` + `ForceSendZDO` is unnecessary — `ForceSendZDO` needs no ownership (SERVER:77706-77712) and `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` hands ownership to any nearby peer every 2 s anyway (SERVER:76874-76879, 76901-76925). (4) Glyphs: `▸`, `—`, `·` are not guaranteed to exist in the sign's TMP font atlas; missing glyphs render as boxes/blank. Columns aligned with spaces will not line up in a proportional font. Needs an in-game check. (5) Save/restart: `s_text` is persistent (not a session hash), so directory text survives restarts and mod removal as frozen text — cosmetic, but the option should say so. (6) The paging channel and toast are prereqs (Ledger alone has no input).

### 155. Signs as INPUT — the 50-character command line

`player-ux-no-client:Signs as INPUT — the 50-character command line` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Instead of the 10-char portal box, the player writes a full sentence on an ordinary sign beside the portal; the server reads `s_text` and treats it as the routing order.


**How it works:** The biggest usable-bandwidth win available to a zero-client mod, and absent from the research digest. `Sign.SetText` runs entirely on the writing client: `m_nview.ClaimOwnership(); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_text, text); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_author, …)` (:141915-141929) — no RPC, a pure ZDO write. It reaches the server as `RPC_ZDOData` → `ZDO.Deserialize` (:77124-77132) within one 0.05 s client flush plus ½ RTT. The input widget is `TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_sign_input", m_characterLimit)` with `m_characterLimit = 50` (:141831, :141756) — five times the portal tag's budget, on a UI the player already knows, with the text left permanently visible in the world rather than hidden behind a hover.

HOOK: the same `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` postfix; filter to prefabs whose GameObject carries a `Sign` (resolve once at world-ready via `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash).GetComponent<Sign>()`, cache the hash set). On a text change, find the nearest managed portal with `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(signPos, 8f)` filtered by `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` (:100021). The control sign is by convention the lowest-y adopted sign, or any whose text starts with a verb.

GRAMMAR AT 50 CHARS is a real command line: `dial Haldor` · `dial Base and lock` · `route Mine2 -> Base one-way` · `name this portal Northgate` · `allow Bjorn, Astrid` · `list plains`. One-way links, aliases, permission lists, multi-token commands and human-readable errors all become expressible.

PAIR WITH THE LEDGER: one column of server-owned output signs plus one designated input sign at the bottom that the player types into and the server replaces with the reply. That is a terminal — prompt line and scrollback — built from vanilla wood.

OWNERSHIP: `SetText` calls `ClaimOwnership()` so the writer owns the sign afterwards; the server's reply still lands because `ZDO.Set` has no ownership check (`okForNotOwner` is a dead parameter, :73648) and the server's DataRevision is higher.


**Player experience:** You place one sign under your portal, press E — the ordinary sign box, 50 characters, the one you've used to label chests a hundred times — and type `dial Haldor and lock`, Enter.

The sign shows your text for about a second, then repaints to `→ HALDOR  1.2km  LOCKED to you` in yellow, and a toast reads `Portal locked. Only you and Bjorn may re-dial.` The portal beside it lights up; its hover tag reads `">Haldor"`.

You type `list plains` on the same sign. It repaints to `plains: Fuling1 2.1k · Tarpit 3.4k · Bog 4k` — three destinations, full names, distances, readable from five metres without hovering anything.

Mistype `dial Halodr`: the sign repaints to `? no portal "Halodr" — try Haldor, Home` and stays that way until you fix it. The portal keeps its old link throughout.

Genuinely close to a real console. The only jank is that you are typing into a wooden plank.


**Failure modes:**
- The server's reply overwrites the player's typed text; if a reply exceeds 50 chars, a later E+Enter submits the clamp as a command. Keep replies ≤50 and make the parser idempotent on its own replies.
- Two signs near one portal are ambiguous without an explicit convention plus a toast saying which sign was used.
- A sign inside a ward the player cannot access silently refuses `SetText` client-side (`PrivateArea.CheckAccess`, :141917) with no message — the box just does nothing on Enter, and the server sees no ZDO change and cannot distinguish that from the player not typing.
- Sign text is public: anyone can read another player's routing commands and, unless gated on `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) or ward permission, retype the sign and re-dial someone else's portal.
- The visible reply lags the toast by up to 2 s (`UpdateText` cadence), which reads as the sign thinking — arguably good feedback.

**Open questions:**
- Do all sign prefabs share `m_characterLimit = 50` or do some override it? IN-GAME: press E on each variant and count accepted characters.
- Does `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` inside `Sign.SetText` swallow the write with genuinely no player-visible message? Reading :141917 there is no `Message` call. IN-GAME: build a sign in someone else's ward and try to write.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Game.PortalPrefabHash is `List<int>` (:100021-100032); use Contains(zdo.GetPrefab()), not equality.
- Revision collision: a second player write within the server-reply RTT is silently dropped on both sides (RPC_ZDOData `num4 <= DataRevision` guard, :77105-77110); re-assert the reply on a timer.
- ZDO.Deserialize postfix fires for every client ZDO update including character ZDOs at 20 Hz; gate on cached Sign prefab-hash set before touching ZDOExtraData.
- The okForNotOwner dead parameter exists only on Set(int,int,bool) (:73648); Set(int,string) (:73721) has no owner parameter at all — same conclusion, cite correctly.
- Hook `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc,ZPackage)` (SERVER:77076), not `ZDO.Deserialize`: Deserialize has no sender parameter and no old-text view. Identity from the `ZRpc` peer (private `ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` SERVER:80504) or `zdo.GetOwner()` after `ClaimOwnership`.
- Commands are silently dropped if the client's ZDO copy is stale: `RPC_ZDOData` requires `dataRevision > server DataRevision` (SERVER:77104-77114). Never rewrite the input sign on a timer; only in direct reply.
- Server reply must set `s_author` to `""`, never leave `"host"` (SERVER:141925 → NRE at 141867-141876 on every viewer).
- `LOCKED` / `allow Bjorn` semantics are reactive-detection-only: an owning client retags with zero packets (SERVER:83587-83594); the server can only revert after the fact.
- Route writes must be reconciled with `Game.ConnectPortals`' tag-equality predicate (SERVER:100596-100605) or they are undone within 5 s — dependency on the address-book prereq, not free.
- Effort: small-medium is optimistic once identity resolution, change detection, replay-guard after world load, and the 5 s reconcile interplay are included; medium.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Verified end to end. `Sign.Interact` → `TextInput.instance.RequestText(this, "$piece_sign_input", m_characterLimit)` with `m_characterLimit = 50` (:141831, :141756). `Sign.SetText` is a pure owner-side ZDO write: client-side `PrivateArea.CheckAccess`, `ClaimOwnership()`, `Set(s_text)`, `Set(s_author)`, optional `Set(s_authorDisplayName)` (:141915-141929) — no RPC. `ZDO.Set(int,string)` → `IncreaseDataRevision` → `ClientChanged(m_uid)` on non-servers (:73832-73840); the client flush timer is 0.05 s (`SendZDOToPeers2`, :76837-76862) and the server's `RPC_ZDOData` calls `zDO.Deserialize(pkg2)` (:77128) — `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` is public at :74206, so a Harmony postfix is available. `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash` exists but is a `List<int>` property (:100021), not a single hash — filter with `.Contains`. `ZDO.Set(int,int,bool okForNotOwner)` ignores the flag (:73648-73654); the string overload has no such parameter at all (:73721). Server reply lands because the server's rev is client-rev+1 and the client applies any higher rev (:77105-77127). Corrections/caveats: (1) same revision-collision hazard as the Ledger — if the player re-submits within the RTT of the server's reply, both packets are dropped and the sign diverges; the command parser should also key on the s_author/text pair and re-assert. (2) `ZDO.Deserialize` on the server is called for EVERY ZDO update from every client (character ZDOs every 50 ms); a postfix must early-exit on prefab hash before any string read. World load uses a different path, so the hook does not fire during load. (3) The reply overwrites the prompt, so the next E pre-fills the server's reply text; whether TMP's focus-select-all makes this painless is a UI detail not in the decompile. (4) `Sign.SetText` writes `s_author` as the writer's PlatformUserID (or "host" when not signed in, :141922) — the server can use `s_author` to attribute the command to a platform identity, and should map "host" per `UpdateAuthorIfHost` semantics rather than trusting it.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism holds. `Sign.SetText` is `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` → `ClaimOwnership` → `zdo.Set(s_text)` → `zdo.Set(s_author, PlatformUserID or "host")` → optional `s_authorDisplayName` → `UpdateText()` (SERVER:141915-141929); no RPC. The owning client queues it via `IncreaseDataRevision` → `ClientChanged` (SERVER:73832-73840) and the client `ZDOMan.Update` flushes every 0.05 s (SERVER:76843-76860); server `RPC_ZDOData` applies it via `ZDO.Deserialize` (SERVER:77104-77132), which merges keys with `ZDOExtraData.Add` (SERVER:74206-74241). `Sign.Interact` calls `RequestText(this, "$piece_sign_input", m_characterLimit)` with the default 50 (SERVER:141831, 141756). `Game.PortalPrefabHash` is a `List<int>` populated in `Game.Awake` (SERVER:100021, 100027-100032). `ZDO.Set` ignores ownership (SERVER:73648) so the server reply lands. Refutations/corrections: (1) `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` has NO sender context — a postfix there cannot tell who wrote the sign. Hook `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` instead (SERVER:77076) and resolve the peer from `rpc` (`ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` is private, SERVER:80504); or trust `zdo.GetOwner()` (set to the writer by `ClaimOwnership`) / `s_author` (client-supplied, vanilla-honest, spoofable). A Deserialize postfix also cannot see the OLD text — keep a per-sign text cache to detect changes. (2) Silent-drop hazard: `RPC_ZDOData` skips any update with `dataRevision <= server DataRevision` (SERVER:77104-77114). The server reply bumps the revision; if the player submits before the reply has been delivered (~50-150 ms) the command is discarded with no error. Typing takes seconds so this is rare, but the mod must not rewrite the input sign on a timer. (3) The `"host"` author: a non-signed-in writer stores `"host"` (SERVER:141925), which is the NRE path in every viewer's `UpdateViewPermission` (SERVER:141867-141876) until the owner's `UpdateAuthorIfHost` (CLIENT:88762-88780) rewrites it — the server reply should always overwrite `s_author` with `""`. (4) Enforcement: the ROUTE write is server-side and honest; but the playerExperience's `LOCKED to you — only you and Bjorn may re-dial` is not enforceable at the act: `RPC_SetTag` runs on the owning client and when the sender owns the portal no packet is routed (`InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally when `targetPeerID == m_id`, SERVER:83587-83594). A lock can only be REVERTED reactively when the server sees the tag change in `RPC_ZDOData`. (5) The written route must survive `Game.ConnectPortals`, whose predicate tears down any connection whose target tag differs (SERVER:100596-100605) — the address-book prereq must equalize tags or the link dies within 5 s. (6) The `s_text` write persists to disk, so a stale command survives restart — replay-guard by (zdoid, text) after load.

### 156. Map ping as a freehand destination picker

`player-ux-no-client:Map ping as a freehand destination picker` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The player middle-clicks the map; the server receives the exact world coordinate and routes their portal there — the only vanilla input that carries an arbitrary Vector3.


**How it works:** `Chat.SendPing(Vector3)` is `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, "ChatMessage", vector, 3, UserInfo.GetLocalUser(), "")`, with `vector.y` forced to the player's own y and x/z from the map click (:42058-42071). `targetPeerID == 0` makes `InvokeRoutedRPC` run `HandleRoutedRPC` locally AND `RouteRPC` (:83587-83594), so the packet ALWAYS reaches the dedicated server regardless of player count — unlike chat text, which is addressed per-listed-player and produces zero packets for a solo player. Three vanilla gestures fire it: `Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick`, `Minimap.OnMapDblClick` with the Ping pin selected, and gamepad JoyButtonX on the large map. Mouse and controller both covered, no keybind config.

HOOK: prefer a Harmony prefix on the private `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC(RoutedRPCData)` (:83646) over `ZRoutedRpc.Register`, because `Register` uses `Dictionary.Add` (:83672) and throws if a `Chat` MonoBehaviour already claimed the name headless. Match `data.m_methodHash == "ChatMessage".GetStableHashCode()`, snapshot `data.m_parameters.GetPos()`, deserialize `Vector3,int,UserInfo,string`, restore the position, return true. Filter `type == 3`.

BINDING: the ping carries no portal reference. Bind it to the player's LAST TOUCHED PORTAL — `Dictionary<long playerId,(ZDOID portal,float time)>` refreshed whenever that player's character ZDO (`ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` :81024) is within 6 m of a portal from `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` (:77643), 5-minute TTL. On a ping, resolve the nearest managed portal within 64 m of the ping x/z and route the remembered portal to it. If nothing is in range, either reject with a toast or fabricate an anchor: `ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, portalPrefabHash)` + `SetPrefab` + `Persistent = true` + `SetRotation` (:76674, :73808, :73323, :73781), height from `WorldGenerator.GetHeight(x,z)` (:151944) + 1 m, validated against `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap` (:115637) and sea level 30.

DEBOUNCE: pings are public and cheap. Rate-limit to one acted-on ping per player per 3 s and require the ARM step so casual pings during a hunt do not re-route a base portal.


**Player experience:** You stand at your portal, press M, scroll to the Black Forest, put the cursor on your friend's outpost and middle-click. The normal vanilla ping marker appears — everyone online sees and hears it.

You close the map. Within about 200 ms a toast reads `Dialed → Northgate (Black Forest, 1,140m)`. The portal you were standing at is already glowing, and the destination ZDO has been pushed to you so the first step through works.

Middle-click empty ocean: `Nothing within 64m of that ping.` Middle-click 30 m from an unmanaged portal: `Nearest is "Bog" (unmanaged). Name it with #Bog first.`

Because it is public, a group sees where you just sent yourself — either party coordination or a privacy leak. The mod should never echo the destination NAME to anyone but you.

Cost: open map, one click. The fastest input in the inventory and the only one where the player expresses an arbitrary PLACE rather than picking from a list.


**Failure modes:**
- Pings broadcast to every connected player — the gesture is inherently public and spammable.
- `data.m_senderPeerID` is deserialized straight off the wire and never cross-checked against the ZRpc connection (`RoutedRPCData.Deserialize` :83487-83495, `RPC_RoutedRPC` :83632). A modified client can ping 'as' someone else.
- `SendPing` overwrites y with the PLAYER's y, not terrain height (:42063-42064). Re-derive height with `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` — never `ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight`, a collider raycast that silently returns `p.y` server-side because no terrain collider exists near real coordinates (:115502, :100465).
- Ping precision is bounded by map zoom; at full zoom-out a click spans tens of metres. Snap to the nearest managed portal rather than using the raw coordinate.
- If a `Chat` MonoBehaviour exists headless, `ZRoutedRpc.Register("ChatMessage",…)` throws ArgumentException at Awake and takes the plugin down.
- A prefix that reads `data.m_parameters` without restoring `GetPos()` corrupts vanilla's own dispatch of the same packet.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Sender identity is NOT verified at HandleRoutedRPC: m_senderPeerID comes from the client's packet (:83487-83495, :83651). Hook RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage) (:83632) and map the ZRpc to a peer via ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc) (private, :80504) for a socket-verified identity.
- CreateNewZDO(Vector3,int) registers the ZDO as a portal via AddIfPortal but does not set m_prefab (:76684-76690); SetPrefab must still be called (:73808). The result is a real, visible, reconciled portal piece, not an invisible anchor.
- Ping Vector3.y is the sender's own y (:42063); derive target height from WorldGenerator.GetHeight only.
- Dictionary.Add collision on Register is irrelevant server-side (no Chat MonoBehaviour); keep the prefix approach for the identity fix, not for this reason.
- Identity: `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` is packet-supplied (SERVER:83487-83495), not verified. Prefix `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc,ZPackage)` (SERVER:83632) and map `rpc` → peer via the private `ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` (SERVER:80504). `HandleRoutedRPC` also fires for the server's own local invocations.
- Route survives only if both portals carry equal `s_tag` — `ConnectPortals` clears mismatched links every 5 s (SERVER:100596-100605). Hard dependency on the address-book prereq.
- Fabricated anchors are physical portals: `CreateNewZDO` registers in `m_portalObjects` (SERVER:76684-76692) but leaves `m_prefab`=0 and `Persistent`=false unless set; vanilla `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` pairs untagged portals with each other (SERVER:100664-100680), so an untagged anchor is immediately eligible for vanilla pairing.
- Vanilla already fetches the target ZDO via `TargetFound → RequestZDO` (CLIENT:144380-144396); no server push needed for the first step.
- Feasibility: feasible-with-caveats — the anchor branch and the reconcile interplay are the risk, not the ping channel.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism verified. `Chat.SendPing` sets `vector.y = localPlayer.transform.position.y` and calls `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, "ChatMessage", vector, 3, UserInfo.GetLocalUser(), "")` (:42058-42071); 3 == `Talker.Type.Ping`. `InvokeRoutedRPC` handles locally when `targetPeerID == 0` and always calls `RouteRPC` when `targetPeerID != m_id` (:83577-83595); client-side `RouteRPC` sends to every peer, i.e. the server (:83621-83627). Server `RPC_RoutedRPC` → `HandleRoutedRPC` (target 0) and relays to all other ready peers except the sender (:83632-83644, :83603-83619). `HandleRoutedRPC` with `m_targetZDO.IsNone()` looks up `m_functions` and silently drops on miss (:83646-83654); `Register` uses `Dictionary.Add` (:83667-83679). Shout chat, by contrast, is addressed per player through `CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync` (self + each listed player, :41983-42040), so a solo shout never leaves the client when a RelationsProvider exists — the contrast claim holds (it goes to 0L only when `RelationsProvider == null`, :41999-42002). Ping call sites confirmed: `Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick` (:58516-58524), `OnMapDblClick` with `m_selectedType == PinType.Ping` (:58478-58489), large-map `JoyButtonX` (:56999-57002). Anchor-creation cites are correct: `CreateNewZDO(Vector3,int)` (:76674-76682) already calls `AddIfPortal` with the passed hash (:76686-76688) but does NOT call `SetPrefab` — that must follow (:73808-73815); `Persistent` is a public settable flag (:73323-73338); `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` (:151944); `IsLavaPreHeightmap` (:115637-115645); `GetAllCharacterZDOS` (:81024-81044); `ZNetPeer.m_characterID` (:78794). CORRECTIONS: (1) 'sender's verified identity' is wrong at the HandleRoutedRPC layer: `m_senderPeerID` is read verbatim from the packet (`RoutedRPCData.Deserialize`, :83487-83495) and passed to handlers unchanged (:83651); a modded client can forge it. Prefix `RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` instead and resolve identity from the socket via the private `ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)` (:80504). (2) A fabricated 'anchor' created with a portal prefab hash is a full vanilla portal: clients in range instantiate the piece, it enters `m_portalObjects` and `Game.ConnectPortals` reconciliation, and it is visible/interactable. It is not a hidden anchor. (3) Ping y is the SENDER's altitude, not terrain at the target; never use it. (4) The server-side `Register` collision concern is moot on a dedicated server (no Chat/Hud instance), but the HandleRoutedRPC/RPC_RoutedRPC prefix is still the right choice for the identity reason above.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Channel verified end to end. `Chat.SendPing` → `InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, "ChatMessage", vector, 3, UserInfo.GetLocalUser(), "")` with `vector.y` = local player y (CLIENT:42058-42071). Call sites: `Minimap.OnMapMiddleClick` (CLIENT:58581-58585), `OnMapDblClick` with Ping pin (CLIENT:58546-58549), gamepad `JoyButtonX` on large map (CLIENT:57060-57063). `InvokeRoutedRPC` with `targetPeerID == 0` handles locally AND `RouteRPC`s (SERVER:83587-83594) so the server always receives it. Server `RPC_RoutedRPC` handles target-0 locally (no `Chat` handler → `m_functions.TryGetValue` miss → silently dropped) then relays to all other ready peers (SERVER:83632-83644, 83646-83665). `Register` uses `Dictionary.Add` (SERVER:83668-83670) so a duplicate name throws — prefix advice is sound. `UserInfo` is `ISerializableParameter` with `Name` + `UserId` (SERVER:72774-72800). Client `TeleportWorld.TargetFound` calls `ZDOMan.RequestZDO` itself when the target ZDO is missing (CLIENT:144380-144396), so no push is needed. Corrections: (1) 'sender's verified identity' is FALSE at the `HandleRoutedRPC` level: `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID` is read straight from the packet (SERVER:83487-83495) and never overwritten by `RPC_RoutedRPC`. Vanilla clients are honest, but the honest hook is a prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (SERVER:83632) resolving the peer from `rpc` (`ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc)`, private, SERVER:80504) — also the only place the mod can distinguish the server's own local `HandleRoutedRPC` calls from network ones. (2) The route write is undone by `Game.ConnectPortals` within 5 s unless the two portals' `s_tag` values are equal (SERVER:100596-100605) — the option leans entirely on the address-book prereq for that. (3) The 'fabricated anchor' is a REAL portal ZDO: `CreateNewZDO(pos, hash)` registers it in `m_portalObjects` via `AddIfPortal` (SERVER:76684-76692) but does not set `m_prefab` or `Persistent` (caller must `SetPrefab`+`Persistent=true`); every vanilla client in range instantiates a visible `portal_wood` at that spot; it participates in `FindRandomUnconnectedPortal` (SERVER:100664-100680) — note vanilla does NOT skip empty tags, so an untagged anchor pairs with any other untagged portal. (4) Height from `WorldGenerator.GetHeight` ignores player terraforming and buildings; the spawned portal can clip into a base. (5) Server-only `nomap`/NoMap worlds have no map to ping. Enforcement claim is honest for the route write itself.

### 157. Animator SetTrigger as a real-time gesture channel (jump, dodge, forsaken power)

`player-ux-no-client:Animator SetTrigger as a real-time gesture channel (jump, dodge, forsaken power)` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Every jump, dodge-roll and forsaken-power activation is broadcast as a routed RPC that passes through the dedicated server carrying the player's character ZDOID — a zero-latency, zero-polling gesture input absent from the research digest.


**How it works:** NEW FINDING, verified. `ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger(string name)` is `m_nview.InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, "SetTrigger", name)` (:87260-87263). `ZNetView.Everybody` is 0, and `ZNetView.InvokeRPC(long,…)` becomes `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, m_zdo.m_uid, "SetTrigger", name)` (:82850). `targetPeerID == 0` → the client handles locally AND calls `RouteRPC`, sending it to the server; the server's `RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632) sees `m_targetPeerID == 0`, calls `HandleRoutedRPC` (dropped — `ZNetScene.FindInstance` is null server-side, :83659) and relays to every other peer. A Harmony PREFIX on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage)` therefore sees every animation trigger from every player, one hop, no polling.

Payload: `(ZDOID m_targetZDO = the character's ZDO, string name)`. Map ZDOID → player via `ZNet.instance.GetPeers()` → `peer.m_characterID`, then `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetLong(ZDOVars.s_playerID)` (:78539) for stable identity and `GetPosition()` for where.

VERIFIED VOCABULARY: `"jump"` (`Character.ForceJump` :3483, every spacebar press) · `"dodge"` (Player roll :15196) · `"gpower"` (forsaken power :15717, cooldown-limited, unmistakable as a commit) · `"eat"` (:7705/:7766) · `"interact"` (:7659) · `"equip_hip"` (:8749/:8777) · `"attach"`/`"detach"`/`"attack_abort"`/`"stagger"`.

GRAMMAR: per-playerId ring of (trigger, time, position). JUMP×3 within 4 s while within 6 m of a portal and having moved <2 m between jumps = advance; JUMP×2 = back; `gpower` = commit. Combine with the crouch bit for a 2×N modal menu.

WHY IT BEATS EMOTES: `Player.StartEmote` requires `CanMove() && !InAttack() && !IsDrawingBow() && !IsAttached() && !IsAttachedToShip()` (:15585-15590) and is observed only by POLLING `s_emoteID` (:78419). `SetTrigger` is pushed, arrives in one hop, needs no emote wheel, and works while moving.


**Player experience:** You stand in front of your portal, tag `"Base"`. You jump — nothing. You jump twice more inside four seconds and a toast appears: `Base → next: Haldor (2/5)`. Three more jumps: `Base → next: Mine2 (3/5)`. You crouch to confirm and a toast reads `Locked in: Mine2`; the tag flips to `>Mine2` and the portal glows.

About eight seconds of hopping in place, which looks exactly like a player being impatient. No UI opened, no typing, works with a full load of ore, works on a controller.

The forsaken-power variant is one gesture: stand at the portal, hit your power key, toast reads `Committed → Mine2`. Unmistakable, un-accidental, naturally rate-limited — but it burns your Eikthyr/Elder power, which most players will resent.

Honest assessment: jumping-as-a-menu is the most embarrassing-looking mechanic in this document. It works, it is fast, it needs nothing — and a new player watching a veteran hop three times and vanish will have no idea what happened. Power-user shortcut layered over a legible primary input, never the primary.


**Failure modes:**
- Every jump on the server becomes a mod event; a player bunny-hopping near a portal trips the window constantly. Require proximity <6 m AND near-stationarity between jumps AND an armed state.
- Triggers fire on the OWNING client only; a dead, teleporting or attached player produces none (`Player.CanMove()` is false while `m_teleporting`, :14423).
- `"jump"` also fires from knockback and the grappling hook via `ForceJump`, so it is not purely voluntary.
- The prefix must not consume the ZPackage read position — deserialize a copy (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())`) or vanilla's relay of the same packet reads garbage.
- `m_senderPeerID` is spoofable; resolve identity from `m_targetZDO` (the real character ZDOID) instead.
- This prefix runs on EVERY routed RPC on a busy server. Compare the int method hash first and return immediately.

**Designer citations:** ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87260-87263 ; ZSyncAnimation.Awake registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87157 ; ZNetView.InvokeRPC(long,…) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82850-82853 ; ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83632-83644 ; Character.ForceJump ("jump") — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:3473-3490 ; Player dodge ("dodge") — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15196 ; Player guardian power ("gpower") — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15717 ; Player.StartEmote preconditions — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15585-15599 ; ZNetPeer.m_characterID — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78794


**Open questions:**
- Does the dedicated server ever hold a ZNetView for a character ZDO such that `HandleRoutedRPC` dispatches rather than dropping? It should not (`Game.FixedUpdate` pin :100465). IN-GAME: log `ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances()` (:82334) on a live server.
- How many `SetTrigger` packets per second does a busy 10-player server carry? Determines whether the hot-path hash compare is acceptable. IN-GAME: count for 60 s.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Jump and dodge are blocked when encumbered (Character.Jump :3406-3410; Player.UpdateDodge :15186) — 'works with a full load of ore' holds only below the weight limit.
- ForceJump clears the crouch toggle (SetCrouch(false), :3487); any crouch+jump grammar must latch the armed state on the crouch edge server-side.
- "gpower" requires m_guardianSE != null and cooldown == 0 (:15702-15716); unavailable to players without a forsaken power.
- Sender/target identity in the routed packet is client-supplied (:83487-83495); verify by hooking RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage) and matching ZNet.GetPeer(ZRpc).m_characterID to data.m_targetZDO.
- ZSyncAnimation.Awake registration line is :87157-87158 (Register<string>("SetTrigger")); fine as cited.
- Crouch cannot be held across jumps: `ForceJump` → `SetCrouch(false)` (SERVER:3486) → `UpdateCrouch` writes `crouching=0` (SERVER:15669-15672). The '2×N modal menu with the crouch bit' must be redesigned as a latched arm state; drop the concurrent-modifier framing.
- Hook `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc,ZPackage)` (SERVER:83632), not `HandleRoutedRPC`, and take identity from the `ZRpc` peer; verify `m_targetZDO == peer.m_characterID` — both `m_senderPeerID` and `m_targetZDO` are packet fields (SERVER:83487-83495).
- Filter on character ZDOIDs before deserializing: all creature ZSyncAnimation triggers from all clients traverse the same RPC (SERVER:87157 registers `SetTrigger` on every ZSyncAnimation).
- `"jump"` also fires on out-of-stamina and swimming jumps (SERVER:3412-3457); the '<2 m between jumps' rule must allow the forward impulse of `m_jumpForceForward` (SERVER:3450).

### 158. Posture bits — crouch and block as a silent modifier key

`player-ux-no-client:Posture bits — crouch and block as a silent modifier key` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Crouching and raising a shield are each mirrored into the character ZDO as a live boolean the server can poll — a hands-free arming gate that costs one keypress.


**How it works:** NEW FINDING, verified. `Player.UpdateCrouch` calls `m_zanim.SetBool(s_crouching, …)` where `s_crouching = ZSyncAnimation.GetHash("crouching")` (:9984, :15667, :15671). `ZSyncAnimation.SetBool(int hash, bool)` does, when `m_nview.IsOwner()`, `zdo.AddSessionHash(438569 + hash); zdo.Set(438569 + hash, value ? 1 : 0)` (:87270-87281); the salt is the literal `c_ZDOSalt = 438569` (:87144). Server read:

  int key = 438569 + UnityEngine.Animator.StringToHash("crouching");
  bool crouching = characterZdo.GetInt(key) != 0;

`Animator.StringToHash` is a pure static in UnityEngine.AnimationModule, callable headless. The key is registered as a SESSION hash so `ZDOExtraData.GetSaveData` strips it from disk (:75507), but session hashes are NOT filtered from `ZDO.Serialize` — the value is live on the wire every tick.

Second bit, already a named constant: `ZDOVars.s_isBlockingHash` = `"IsBlocking"` (:78463), written on the character ZDO at :8690/:8708. Third, analogue: `ZDOVars.s_stealth` (:78613) written at :16372.

USE: poll `ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` (:81024) at 0.2 s. Crouch alone as the ARMING gate for the ping and jump channels solves their biggest problem — accidental activation — at essentially zero cost. Crouch is a TOGGLE in Valheim (`m_crouchToggled`, `SetCrouch` :15675) so the armed state can be held indefinitely with no input strain; block is momentary (held mouse button) so it suits a transient 'show me detail' mode.

IMPORTANT: `UpdateCrouch` calls `SetCrouch(false)` when `IsBlocking()` (:15662), so the crouch+block combination is UNREACHABLE. Three modes exist, not four.


**Player experience:** You walk to your portal. Nothing happens — you are standing normally and the server is ignoring you. You press crouch (default Ctrl) and a toast appears instantly: `Portal armed — jump to cycle, crouch again to commit.` Your character is visibly crouching, which IS the feedback: anyone watching can see you are 'in the menu'.

You jump. `1/5 Base`. Jump. `2/5 Haldor`. You raise your shield and the toast expands to `2/5 Haldor · 1,140m · Black Forest · open`. You lower it, press crouch again, and the toast reads `Dialed → Haldor.` The portal glows.

Six seconds, no menu, no typing, one hand.

The honest problems: crouching is something players do constantly for sneaking, so ARMED fires whenever anyone sneaks past a portal — it needs a proximity gate and a 15 s auto-disarm. And crouch-as-a-modifier is invisible to a new player; nothing in the game hints that crouching near a portal means anything. This is a shortcut for people who already know.


**Failure modes:**
- Crouch is a common movement action; without tight proximity gating and auto-disarm, arming fires constantly.
- `IsBlocking()` forces crouch off (:15662) — crouch+block is unreachable, so only three of four states exist.
- `UpdateCrouch` also clears crouch on `!HaveStamina() || IsSwimming() || InBed() || InPlaceMode() || m_run || IsFlying()` (:15662), so the armed state silently drops when the player sprints or runs out of stamina.
- The write depends on `ZSyncAnimation.SetBool` running, which it does whenever the owner's `UpdateCrouch` runs — but never hard-code the resulting integer key; `Animator.StringToHash` is Unity-internal and only stable within one build.
- Session hashes are stripped from the save, so the armed state does not survive a relog — correct behaviour, but no persistent flag is possible here.

### 159. Emote signalling near a portal

`player-ux-no-client:Emote signalling near a portal` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The player uses a vanilla emote while standing at a portal; the server polls the character ZDO's emote counter and treats each of 24 emotes as a command token.


**How it works:** `Player.StartEmote(string emote, bool oneshot)` writes three fields on the player's own character ZDO: `ZDOVars.s_emoteID` incremented (:78419), `ZDOVars.s_emote` = the lowercased enum name (:78417), `ZDOVars.s_emoteOneshot` (:78421) — see :15585-15599. `StopEmote` bumps the counter with an empty name (:15601-15609). No RPC; the change reaches the server as ZDO data within one 0.05 s client flush.

SERVER LOOP: reuse Wonderland's `EmoteSignals` verbatim (Core/Data/EmoteSignals.cs:38/:46/:125) — every 0.25 s, for each `ConnectedCharacters.All()` entry read `s_emoteID`; if it differs from cache, read `s_emote` and dispatch. Seed the counter on first sighting so a pre-existing emote does not fire a phantom command. Ignore empty names.

VOCABULARY: 24 usable emotes (`enum Emotes` :6216-6246). A sane portal mapping: Point → next destination · ThumbsUp → confirm · NoNoNo → cancel · Wave → list destinations as toasts · Challenge → lock/unlock · Shrug → status. Bind to the nearest managed portal within 6 m via `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` (:77643) and the character ZDO position.

WHY SECOND-CHOICE: `StartEmote` refuses when `!CanMove() || InAttack() || IsDrawingBow() || IsAttached() || IsAttachedToShip()` (:15587) — no emoting while seated, on a boat, mid-swing or mid-teleport. The emote wheel is a real UI the player must open; typing `/point` is faster but requires knowing the names, and an unknown name is silently swallowed by the client's own `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:41947-41955). The 0.25 s poll adds a perceptible beat, and 24 tokens is far more than anyone will memorise — realistically 4-6 are usable.

It is nevertheless completely reliable, independent of player count, and the one channel Wonderland has already shipped and live-tested in production (`CacheClaimControl.cs`, `SupplySwitch.cs`).


**Player experience:** You stand at your portal, hold the emote key, and pick Wave. Your character waves. About a third of a second later five toasts stack up:

`1 Base      612m`
`2 Haldor  1,140m`
`3 Mine2     840m`
`4 Bog      3,010m`
`Point to cycle · ThumbsUp to confirm`

You emote Point: `▸ 1 Base (612m)`. Point again: `▸ 2 Haldor (1,140m)`. On the one you want you emote ThumbsUp: `Dialed → Haldor.` The portal glows, the tag flips to `>Haldor`.

Twelve to fifteen seconds, because opening the wheel and picking takes two to three seconds each time and every emote plays a full animation. Visibly slower than typing into the portal.

The upside: entirely mouse-driven, works on a controller, and your character is visibly doing something — a bystander sees you pointing at a portal and can guess what is happening, which is more than the jump or crouch channels offer.


**Failure modes:**
- `StartEmote` returns false and writes nothing while attached, on a ship, attacking, drawing a bow, or unable to move (:15587). The player gets no feedback that the command was swallowed.
- 0.25 s polling collapses two emotes in one tick into one observed event. Read the `s_emoteID` DELTA — a jump of 2 means a step was missed, and the mod should say so rather than silently mis-advance.
- Emotes are social: waving hello beside a portal fires a directory dump. Proximity gating plus an armed state is mandatory.
- `Sit`, `Rest`, `Relax`, `Vibe` are non-oneshot (`[Emote(OneShot=false)]`, :6219) and latch; the following `StopEmote` bumps the counter with an empty string that must be ignored.
- 24 tokens is beyond memorisation; only 4-6 are practical.
- Two players emoting at the same portal inside one tick are indistinguishable in ordering.

### 160. Equipped item as a destination selector

`player-ux-no-client:Equipped item as a destination selector` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Hold a specific item while touching the portal; its prefab hash is already in your character ZDO, so the server reads which one and dials the matching destination.


**How it works:** `VisEquipment` mirrors every VISIBLE equipped item into the character's own ZDO as a prefab stable hash: `s_rightItem` (+variant/quality), `s_leftItem`, `s_helmetItem`, `s_chestItem`, `s_legItem`, `s_shoulderItem`, `s_utilityItem`, `s_trinketItem`, `s_leftBackItem`, `s_rightBackItem` — written at :20569-20708 by the owning client. Server reads `characterZdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_rightItem)` and resolves via `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)?.name` (:82045).

SCHEME: a binding table `itemPrefabHash → destination` (server config or per-player). Torch = home, Cultivator = farm, a boss trophy = that boss's altar (resolvable server-side from `ZoneSystem.m_locationInstances` :113295 via `FindClosestLocation` :115707). Poll `ZNet.instance.GetAllCharacterZDOS()` (:81024) at 0.25 s; when an ARMED player within 6 m of a managed portal changes `s_rightItem`, dial.

WHY IT IS INTERESTING: it is the only channel that is simultaneously zero extra actions (players swap items constantly), physically legible (everyone can SEE what you hold), and thematically native (hold the key to the door). A row of stone portals where you show a Fine Wood for the Meadows and a Black Metal for the Plains reads as a game mechanic rather than a mod UI. The back slots (`s_leftBackItem`/`s_rightBackItem`) are also visible, doubling the vocabulary without the player holding anything awkward.

CRITICAL LIMIT: this reads EQUIPPED items only. A living player's inventory is never mirrored into any ZDO — `ZDOVars.s_items` (:78475) is written by exactly one live path, `Container.Save` (:122293-122300), and an exhaustive scan of Character/Humanoid/Player ZDO writes yields only vitals, identity, pose and equipment visuals. So 'carry a key item' cannot be a requirement, only 'hold' one, and nothing can be charged.


**Player experience:** You are at your base portal holding a Bronze Axe and you want the mine. You open your inventory, right-click your Antler Pickaxe to equip it, close the inventory, and step toward the portal.

As the pickaxe goes into your hand a toast reads `Pickaxe → Mine2 (840m). Step through.` The tag flips to `>Mine2` and the portal glows. You walk through.

At the mine you swap back to the axe and the return portal reads `Axe → Base`. You never opened a menu, never typed, and the thing in your hand is the thing that tells you where you are going. A friend watching sees you draw a pickaxe and walk into a portal, and understands the rule the first time they see it.

The failure is equally concrete: you arrive at the portal holding a Draugr Fang because you were fighting on the way, and the portal silently re-dials itself. Hence the arming gate — crouch, swap, un-crouch — or bind only to items nobody carries by accident.

Jank rating: low-to-medium. It feels like a game mechanic rather than a workaround, which is rare in this list.


**Failure modes:**
- Equipping happens constantly in normal play; without an arming gate a player re-dials portals by fighting near them.
- Only VISIBLE slots are in the ZDO — backpack contents are invisible, so no 'must be carrying X' requirement and no fee.
- `VisEquipment`'s read-back branches on `m_isPlayer` (:20857-20885), an Inspector bool; some slots may not be written for a Player specifically.
- The binding table has to be taught — nothing in the game indicates a Cultivator means anything to a portal.
- Two portals within 6 m are ambiguous; bind to the nearest and name it in the toast.
- Requires `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash)` to be non-null on a dedicated server.

### 161. Item stand token board

`player-ux-no-client:Item stand token board` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A row of vanilla item stands beside a portal; mounting an item on a stand selects that stand's destination, read from `ZDOVars.s_item` on the stand's own ZDO.


**How it works:** `ItemStand.UpdateAttach` (on the stand's owning client) does `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_item, m_queuedItem.m_dropPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode())` plus `ItemDrop.SaveToZDO(itemData, zdo)` and `m_nview.InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, "SetVisualItem", …)` (:131834-131854). Detach writes `Set(ZDOVars.s_item, 0)` (:131824). `HaveAttachment()` is `GetInt(s_item) != 0` (:132018).

SERVER: discover stands like signs — `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(portalPos, 8f)` filtered to prefabs carrying `ItemStand`. Order deterministically by bearing around the portal then y. Poll `GetInt(ZDOVars.s_item)` (:78465) at 0.5 s, or better catch it in the `ZDO.Deserialize` postfix. Stand index N occupied → destination N.

TWO ENCODINGS: (a) POSITIONAL — the stand index is the address, item identity irrelevant; simple, teachable, and a sign under each stand becomes its label. (b) SEMANTIC — the item's prefab hash is the address; one stand, N destinations.

PUSH NOTIFICATION FOR FREE: `"SetVisualItem"` is `InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, …)` (:131849), targetPeerID 0, so it also passes through the server as a relayed routed RPC carrying `(itemHash, variant, quality, orientation)` and the stand's ZDOID — catchable with the same `RPC_RoutedRPC` prefix as the animation triggers, matching `"SetVisualItem".GetStableHashCode()`. No polling needed.

HARD LIMIT — NO STACK COUNT. The 'stack count = index' idea does not work here: `UpdateAttach` sets `itemData.m_stack = 1` unconditionally (:131843) and mounts exactly one item. Stack encoding requires a Container.

SERVER WRITE-BACK: the mod can clear a stand (`SetOwner(GetSessionID())`, `Set(s_item,0)`, `Set(s_type,0)`, `ForceSendZDO`) — but the item is then GONE, because spawning the drop needs a live GameObject (`DropItem` at :131820). Never auto-clear a player's item; that is item destruction.


**Player experience:** Beside your hub you have five item stands in a row, each with a sign under it: `1 Base`, `2 Haldor`, `3 Mine2`, `4 Bog`, `5 Swamp`. You are holding a Torch.

You walk to stand 3, press E, and the torch mounts with the usual vanilla animation. Within half a second a toast reads `Dialed → Mine2 (840m)` and the portal lights up. You step through.

The torch is still sitting on stand 3 across the map — so your base portal is still pointed at Mine2, which is what you want. The board is a physical, persistent, at-a-glance record of where every portal in your hub currently points. Anyone walking into your base reads the routing state off the wall without hovering anything or knowing any commands.

To re-route you take the torch off stand 3 (`Mine2 released`) and put it on stand 2 (`Dialed → Haldor`).

The most physically satisfying scheme in this list and arguably better than a UI — it is a patch panel. Its costs are build effort (five stands plus five signs is a real project) and that it scales only as far as you are willing to build.


**Failure modes:**
- An item on a stand is a persistent world object anyone can take; removing your torch silently un-dials your portal.
- `m_stack = 1` is forced (:131843) — no stack-count encoding.
- The server cannot return a mounted item; clearing `s_item` destroys it.
- Stand ordering must derive from world position (bearing around the portal), never ZDOID — `ZDO.Load` renumbers uids (:74552).
- Stands inside a ward the player cannot access refuse the interaction client-side with no server-visible signal.
- Two occupied stands need an explicit precedence rule (last-changed wins, via the Deserialize hook ordering).

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Vocabulary for the SEMANTIC encoding is far smaller than 'the item's prefab hash': ItemStand.CanAttach (:131963-131981) requires GetAttachPrefab(item.m_dropPrefab) != null (the item prefab must carry an 'attach' child) AND the type to be in m_supportedTypes / m_supportedItems. Raw materials (Coal, Wood, ore, Amber…) cannot be mounted; only weapons, tools, shields, torches, trophies and a few misc items can. The Torch example works; a 'Coal token' does not.
- The SetVisualItem RPC is also fired on DETACH (DropItem :131825, RPC_DestroyAttachment) with all-zero args, so the RPC catcher receives clear events too — treat hash==0 as release, do not dispatch it as a selection.
- Server write-back caveat should be stated in ownership terms: after a mod SetOwner(sessionID) on a stand, RPC_RequestOwn from a player is dropped on the server (no ZNetView) until ReleaseNearbyZDOS returns ownership within ≤2 s; a player pressing E in that window gets nothing and must retry.
- Server write-back makes the stand dead for up to 2 s: ItemStand.UseItem (:131757-131775) sends RPC_RequestOwn to m_zdo.GetOwner() (ZNetView.InvokeRPC(string) :82856-82858); if the mod has set owner = server session ID, the RPC lands on the server where HandleRoutedRPC finds no instance (:83646-83661) and is dropped, and UpdateAttach spins on IsOwner() (:131836) until ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925, 2 s cadence :76870-76885) reassigns the stand to the nearby peer. Same handback applies to any 'proactive' server claim — the server cannot hold a stand near a player.
- Client visual refresh after a server-side s_item write is slow: the client's ItemStand only re-reads the ZDO in InvokeRepeating("UpdateVisual", 1f, 4f) (:131573), so a server-cleared stand keeps showing the item for up to 4 s unless the mod also sends the SetVisualItem routed RPC itself (ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(0, standZdoId, "SetVisualItem", 0,0,0,0)). Since the option already says never auto-clear, this is informational.
- SetVisualItem carries (hash, variant, quality, orientation) but NOT the stand index — the prefix must map RoutedRPCData.m_targetZDO back to the board slot; and the RPC is only fired by the attaching client, so a stand loaded from disk already populated produces no RPC — the 0.5 s poll (or a ZDO.Deserialize postfix) is still required for startup/relog state, the RPC is only an accelerator.
- ZDOVars.s_item = "item" is at :78465 as cited; s_items = "items" (:78475) is the Container key — do not conflate; a stand ZDO also carries ItemDrop.SaveToZDO fields (durability, quality, variant, crafterID...) written at :131844.

### 162. Chest tokens — item type as destination, stack count as index

`player-ux-no-client:Chest tokens — item type as destination, stack count as index` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Drop a specific item into a chest beside the portal; the server parses the chest's serialized inventory blob and reads item type AND stack size as a two-field command — the only channel that can also charge a fee.


**How it works:** A Container's whole inventory is one serialized byte blob on its ZDO: `Container.Save` does `m_inventory.Save(pkg); zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_items, pkg.GetArray())` on every `OnContainerChanged` (:122286-122300); `ZDOVars.s_items` = `"items"` (:78475). Decode server-side with Wonderland's `ZdoInventoryIO.Load` (Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs), which builds a scratch `Inventory` over the blob — already shipped and tested.

Unlike an ItemStand, a Container DOES carry stack counts, so 'item type = destination, stack count = index' is available here and nowhere else: one Coal = network 'Mine', three Coal = slot 3 within it.

TIMING AND THE IN-USE GATE: `Container` runs `InvokeRepeating("CheckForChanges", 0f, 1f)` (:121922) and `Load()` early-returns while `m_inUse` (:122305). `UpdateUseVisual` writes `ZDOVars.s_inUse` (`"InUse"`, :78673) into the ZDO when the client owns it (:121990-122001), so the server can SEE that the chest is open and must not write `s_items` during that window (Wonderland's `ZdoInventoryIO.IsBusy`). The player's deposit reaches the server as soon as their `Save()` fires and the ZDO flushes (≤0.05 s + ½ RTT), but the server's REPLY does not repaint on their screen until they close the chest.

TOLL VARIANT: because the server can also WRITE `s_items`, this is the only channel that can charge for a teleport — consume 1 Coal per long-range dial via `ZdoInventoryIO.MoveMatchingItem`. Nothing else in the zero-client toolkit can take an item from a player.

WRITE PROCEDURE: `if (zdo.GetInt(ZDOVars.s_inUse) == 1) defer;` then `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, mutate the scratch inventory, `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_items, newBlob)`, `ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)`.


**Player experience:** There is a chest under your portal with a sign on it reading `DROP A TOKEN`. You open it — ordinary vanilla chest UI — drag two Coal in, and close it.

About a second later a toast reads `Coal x2 → Haldor (1,140m). Fee paid.` The portal glows. You look back at the chest: empty, the coal spent on the trip.

Drop in something unrecognised and the toast reads `Flint is not a token. Valid: Coal, Amber, Ruby.` and the flint is still there when you reopen. Drop Coal x7 with only five destinations: `Only 5 destinations. Coal x1-x5.` and the coal stays.

The unavoidable weirdness: if you keep the chest OPEN, nothing visibly changes inside it no matter what the server does, because vanilla refuses to reload a container's contents while its UI is up. You must close it to see the result. The toast fires immediately, so you are told what happened — you just cannot watch it happen.

Cost: open inventory, open chest, drag, close. Six or seven seconds, and it costs an item. High jank as routine navigation; excellent as an economy layer under a different primary input.


**Failure modes:**
- `Container.Load` refuses while `m_inUse` (:122305), so the server's reply is invisible until the player closes the chest.
- Writing `s_items` while the player has the chest open races their client's own Save and can destroy items. Always check `ZDOVars.s_inUse` first.
- Chests are public containers; anyone can drop a token into someone else's control chest unless the mod gates on ward permission or `s_creator`.
- The 1 s `CheckForChanges` cadence plus the flush means the observed deposit can lag a deposit-then-immediately-withdraw by enough to misread the state.
- Charging a fee is a destructive operation on player property — it must be opt-in, clearly signed, and never silent.

**Designer citations:** Container.Save / Load — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:122293-122322 ; Container.OnContainerChanged — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:122286-122292 ; Container InvokeRepeating("CheckForChanges", 0f, 1f) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:121922 ; Container.UpdateUseVisual (s_inUse write) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:121990-122001 ; ZDOVars.s_items / s_inUse — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78475, :78673 ; Wonderland ZdoInventoryIO — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs


**Open questions:**
- Does a fresh chest write `s_items` promptly, or only after the owning client's first `OnContainerChanged` tick? Matters for a newly-built control chest. IN-GAME: build a chest, drop one item, and time how long until the server reads a non-null blob.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Act on CLOSE, not on deposit: Save() fires on every inventory change while the chest is open, so a read-on-change design sees intermediate states (drag 1 Coal → 'Base', drag second → 'Haldor'). Trigger only on the s_inUse 1→0 transition (or require IsBusy()==false at read time as ZdoInventoryIO.Load already enforces) — the howItWorks text implies acting as soon as Save() fires.
- Ownership window: after the mod's SetOwner(sessionID) write, a player's RPC_RequestOpen targets the server, which has no Container GameObject and drops it (ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC → FindInstance null). ReleaseNearbyZDOS returns ownership within ≤2 s; a player who presses E in that window gets no OpenResponse and must retry. Same behaviour Wonderland already tolerates; document it.
- Race at open: s_inUse=1 is written only after RPC_OpenResponse → InventoryGui.Show → SetInUse(true) (client :122850-122866), so there is an RTT-sized window where the server sees s_inUse==0 but the chest is about to be owned+opened. A server write landing there is overwritten by the opener's next Save(). Mitigate by re-checking s_inUse and DataRevision immediately before commit and never writing to a chest whose owner changed in the last tick.
- The prescribed SetOwner(sessionID) makes the chest unopenable for up to 2 s: Container.Interact (:122042-122068) sends RPC_RequestOpen to m_zdo.GetOwner() (:82856-82858); on the server there is no Container instance so HandleRoutedRPC drops it (:83646-83661) and the player gets no RPC_OpenResponse at all (not even '$msg_inuse'). Ownership returns only via ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76925, 2 s timer :76870-76885). Wonderland's ZdoInventoryIO.Save (Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs:52-58) claims only at commit for this reason; the design must say 'E does nothing for ~2 s after a fee is charged'.
- Revision race can void the fee: RPC_ZDOData rejects a packet whose DataRevision is <= the local one (:77108-77118). If the client bumps its revision (any Save) between the server's read and the client receiving the server's write, both copies sit at the same revision with different contents and neither side ever reconciles. The s_inUse gate closes most of it, but a re-open in the ~RTT window after the server's write opens the UI on the stale local m_inventory; because the incoming packet has already flipped the owner to the server, OnContainerChanged skips Save (IsOwner() false :122288) and the player can take the 'spent' coal into their own (client-authoritative) inventory. Mitigation: debit only after s_inUse == 0 has been observed on two consecutive polls AND the depositor's character ZDO is > ~3 m from the chest.
- byte[] ZDO writes ALWAYS increment DataRevision: BinarySearchDictionary.SetValue compares with Equals (utils_SERVER:321-333), which is reference equality for arrays, so even an identical blob is a 'change'. Harmless for the toll, but a server loop that re-Saves an unchanged inventory every tick would flood every nearby peer with the full blob — write only on actual mutation.
- Inventory.Load on the server resolves items through ObjectDB.instance.GetItemPrefab; that works on a dedicated server (Wonderland ships it) but any modded/unknown prefab in the blob is dropped by Inventory.Load and would be silently destroyed on the server's Save — token chests should be rejected/ignored if any item fails to resolve rather than re-saved.
- 'Stack all' cannot deposit by accident from a distance: Container.StackAll (:122174-122215) and InventoryGui.OnStackAll (:50610-50615) act only on the currently OPEN container; there is no 'stack to nearby chests' in 1.0.7. Accidental deposits require opening the token chest.
- The toast while the chest is open is achievable (Player "Message" RPC :10072/:14820 renders through MessageHud independent of InventoryGui), but the DEBIT must wait for s_inUse == 0, so 'Fee paid' should be shown only when the debit actually committed, i.e. after close.

### 163. Debiting a living player's own inventory

`player-ux-no-client:Debiting a living player's own inventory` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **not-enforceable** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Taking an item directly from the player (rather than from a chest), or checking what they are carrying — the obvious design that is structurally impossible.


**How it works:** `ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles()` does NOT collect anything — it invokes a `"SavePlayerProfile"` RPC on each peer whose handler calls `Game.instance.SavePlayerProfile` on that client, writing that client's own local `.fch` file; nothing returns to the server (:79653-79675). `Player.Save(ZPackage)` serialises inventory, known recipes, skills and uniques into `PlayerProfile.m_playerData`, stored only on that client's disk (:14091-14170, :105706-105711). An exhaustive read of every `Set(ZDOVars.s_*)` call inside Character (:178-6796), Humanoid (:6796-9414) and Player (:9414-16500) finds only vitals, identity, pose, emote and equipment-visual fields — never items.

The single exception is a DEAD player: `Player.CreateTombStone` moves the whole inventory into a tombstone Container whose ZDO carries `s_items` plus `s_owner`/`s_ownerName`/`s_timeOfDeath`/`s_spawnPoint` (:12702-12714, :19845-19853, :19732-19740). So the server can read and debit a corpse, and nothing else.

CONSEQUENCE FOR PORTAL UX: the server can never reproduce vanilla's ore/metal restriction for a server-issued teleport, because `Inventory.IsTeleportable` (:68860-68880) runs entirely client-side against data the server does not hold. Any forced-teleport feature silently allows ore through. Design around it — advertise it honestly, or never use forced teleport as the primary movement and let the vanilla portal (which DOES check) do the work.


**Player experience:** Not applicable — nothing can be built, so the player experiences nothing. Any documentation promising 'the server checks what you are carrying' or 'the portal charges you a coin' without a chest is a promise that cannot be kept.


**Failure modes:**
- Any design stating 'the server checks the player is carrying X' or 'the server takes X from the player' is impossible without a client mod.
- A server-issued teleport always bypasses the ore/metal restriction, which will be perceived as a cheat vector if not stated plainly.

**Designer citations:** ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles / RPC_SavePlayerProfile — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79653-79675 ; Player.Save — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:14091-14170 ; PlayerProfile.SavePlayerData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:105706-105711 ; Container.Save (only live s_items writer) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:122293-122300 ; Player.CreateTombStone / TombStone.Setup / TombStone.Awake — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:12702-12714, :19845-19853, :19732-19740 ; Inventory.IsTeleportable — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:68860-68880

### 164. Positional input — plates, walk-sequences, approach vector

`player-ux-no-client:Positional input — plates, walk-sequences, approach vector` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The server polls every connected character's ZDO position and treats named spots, dwell times, ordered sequences and the compass bearing of approach as commands.


**How it works:** POSITION IS THE CHEAPEST AND FRESHEST SIGNAL THE SERVER HAS. `ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync` writes `zDO.SetPosition(GetPosition())` every FixedUpdate on the owning client (:87527-87534), and client→server ZDO delivery is distance-independent (`ZDOMan.ClientChanged` :77727 → `CreateSyncList`'s non-server branch drains `m_clientChangeQueue` wholesale :77241-77258, flushed every 0.05 s :76843). So `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(peer.m_characterID).GetPosition()` is fresh to ~50-100 ms regardless of how far the player is from the server's pinned reference position (1e6,0,1e6, :100465).

PRIMITIVES:
(1) PLATE — a mod-side `(worldPos, radius, action)`. A player whose horizontal distance drops below radius and stays for a dwell time (default 1.5 s) triggers. Accumulate `dwell[playerId] += dt` while inside, reset on exit. Ignore y so a raised platform still counts.
(2) SEQUENCE — an ordered list of plates entered within a window. `A→B→A` inside 20 s is deliberate and essentially unspoofable. Bounded per-player ring of (plateId, time).
(3) APPROACH VECTOR — the bearing from which the player entered the portal's 6 m radius, quantised to 8 sectors. Walk in from the north for destination 1, from the east for 3. Zero construction, zero UI, the most invisible input available.
(4) LOOK DIRECTION — `CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation` writes `ZDOVars.s_lookTarget = eyePos + lookDir * 100f` into the character ZDO, at most every 0.2 s and only on change (:5041-5081). Disambiguates which of several adjacent portals/signs/stands the player means.

MARKING: the plates are ordinary player-built decoration (a stone tile, a rug, a torch ring); the mod needs only a coordinate list.

SAMPLING: 0.1-0.2 s is comfortable — a player at ~5 m/s covers 0.5-1 m per sample, so a 3 m plate is never missed. Far tighter than Wonderland's `PositionWatch` 3 s security sampling (Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:31), costing one `GetAllCharacterZDOS()` allocation plus N distance checks per tick.


**Player experience:** In front of your portal you have laid three stone tiles in a row, each with a torch, and a sign above reading `STAND TO CHOOSE`. The tiles are pure decoration you built with the hammer.

You walk onto the left tile and stop. About a second and a half later a toast reads `▸ Base (612m). Walk into the portal.` and the tag flips to `>Base`. You step off; nothing changes — the dial is set.

You walk onto the middle tile, wait, `▸ Haldor (1,140m)`. You step into the portal and you are in Haldor's meadow.

The approach-vector variant is quieter still: there are no tiles. You walk into the portal from the north and come out at your mine; from the east and you come out at the swamp. After the third time you stop thinking about it. A guest walks straight in from whichever side, gets destination 1, and is confused about nothing because they never knew there was a choice.

Cost: walking. Literally zero extra actions — that is its whole appeal. The problem is that it is undiscoverable and accident-prone; you will re-dial your hub by pathing across a tile on the way to a workbench.


**Failure modes:**
- Players path across their own base constantly; without an armed state and generous dwell times this fires by accident all day.
- Undiscoverable — nothing in the game hints that a floor tile means anything. Requires player-built visible marking plus a sign written by the server.
- Approach-vector input is invisible even after you know about it: a guest cannot tell there was a choice, and a player who circles a portal while fighting gets a random destination.
- Position is owner-authoritative; a player being knocked back or teleported crosses plates involuntarily.
- Dwell timers must be reset on death/respawn (`ZDOVars.s_dead`, :78403) and on large position jumps (dungeon transits cross y=3000, `Character.InInterior` :4538) or the tracker desyncs.

**Designer citations:** ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87527-87540 ; ZDOMan.ClientChanged / CreateSyncList non-server branch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77727-77730, :77241-77258 ; ZDOMan.Update 0.05 s send cadence — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76843-76852 ; CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation (s_lookTarget) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:5041-5081 ; Game.FixedUpdate reference-position pin — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100465 ; Character.InInterior — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:4538-4541 ; Wonderland PositionWatch — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/Security/PositionWatch.cs:31


**Open questions:**
- Does the Player prefab have `CharacterAnimEvent.m_headRotation` enabled and `m_head` assigned? Both are Inspector fields gating the `s_lookTarget` write (:5043). IN-GAME: poll `s_lookTarget` for 10 s while a player spins in place; a changing non-zero Vector3 confirms the channel.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Freshness is bounded by socket back-pressure, not just the 0.05 s timer: ZDOMan.SendZDOs skips the tick when the peer socket's send queue exceeds 10240 bytes or has <2048 bytes free (SendZDOs head), so under congestion position updates batch and the ~50-100 ms figure degrades. Dwell timers (1.5 s) absorb this; the approach-vector variant, which relies on the first sample inside the 6 m ring, should use two consecutive samples or a minimum inbound displacement to avoid mis-quantised bearings when a burst arrives.
- s_lookTarget is written only when the value CHANGES at a 0.2 s check (:5065-5071); a perfectly still player emits nothing, so the mod must keep the last value rather than expect a heartbeat, and the initial value for a freshly connected character may be Vector3.zero until the first head move.
- Approach vector has a hard timing budget: from the 6 m ring to the trigger collider at sprint (~7 m/s) is ≈0.6 s. The dial must traverse server poll (0.1-0.2 s) + ZDO.SetConnection (:73656-73666, bumps revision + SetDirtyPortals) + 0.05 s flush + RTT, AND the client must already hold the destination ZDO: client TeleportWorld.TargetFound (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:144383-144399) returns false and calls ZDOMan.RequestZDO when it does not, and Teleport() then returns SILENTLY (:144259-144262) — no message. Because TeleportWorldTrigger fires only on OnTriggerEnter (:144413-144421), the player must step out and back in. Fix: detect at 10-12 m and pre-push every managed destination ZDO to the peer via ZDOMan.ForceSendZDO(peerID, id) (:77714) when the player enters the outer ring.
- The 'portal glows' feedback in the player experience lags: client UpdatePortal polls HaveTarget/TargetFound every 0.5 s (:144231-144248) and the emission colour lerps over ~1 s (:144251-144255), so a plate dial is visible on the portal 0.5-1.5 s after the toast, not with it.
- Look-direction as a disambiguator is 0.2 s stale and quantised by the 'only on change' guard (:5066-5071); it is fine for 'which of three stands' but not for sub-second gestures.
- Dwell plates are exposed to Character.InInterior (:4538-4541): a player inside a crypt has y > 3000, so a horizontal-only distance check would match plates whose x/z lie under the dungeon; include a |Δy| < ~10 m guard rather than ignoring y outright.
- The prereq 'Arming gesture' (crouch) is a real server-readable bit — Player.UpdateCrouch -> m_zanim.SetBool(s_crouching) (:15667-15671) stores int at key 438569 + Animator.StringToHash("crouching") (ZSyncAnimation.SetBool :87271-87281, session-hash, never saved) — but Player.StartEmote force-uncrouches (:15591), so an emote confirm cancels the arm; and IsCrouching on the server cannot use GetCurrentAnimHash (no Animator), only that ZDO int.
