### 165. Build-shape input — placing a piece as a latching switch

`player-ux-no-client:Build-shape input — placing a piece as a latching switch` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Placing (or removing) a specific build piece in a specific socket near a portal is detected the moment the ZDO arrives and acts as a permanent, visible switch.


**How it works:** THE HOOK IS THE NON-OBVIOUS PART. A dedicated server never sees `Player.PlacePiece` (no Player instance) and never runs `ZNetScene.Instantiate` for a client-placed piece (the client instantiates locally and only the ZDO arrives). The PAUSED PortalLock project patched exactly those and could never fire once (`PAUSED/PortalLock/src/PortalLock/PlacementPatches.cs:14, :114`).

The correct hook is Wonderland's SpawnGovernor pair (`Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43, :58`): a postfix on the private `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int)` (:76684) that only REMEMBERS the ZDOID — on the network-receive path `prefabHash` is 0 and `GetPrefab()` returns 0, so nothing can be decided — plus a postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` (:74225), the first moment the prefab hash is known. There, read `GetPrefab()`, `GetPosition()` and `GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator)` (:78393 — the placer's stable PlayerProfile UID, written by `Piece.SetCreator` :136415-136424, the same value as that player's `ZDOVars.s_playerID`).

SWITCH DESIGN: per portal, a set of SOCKETS `(relativeOffset, acceptedPrefabSet, action)`. A Wood Beam in socket 1 → dial destination 1. A blue-burning torch in the lock socket → lock the portal. Because the ZDO persists, the switch is latching, survives restarts, and a visitor reads the routing state off the architecture.

DESTRUCTION is the other half: subscribe to the public `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` `Action<ZDO>` field (:76033), invoked from `HandleDestroyedZDO` (:76975) BEFORE the ZDO leaves `m_objectsByID`, so it is still readable inside the callback. No Harmony needed.

SAME HOOK = THE SERVER-ENFORCED PORTAL CAP: on a new portal-prefab ZDO, read `s_creator`, count that player's portals in `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648), and if over the limit `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo);` (:76929 — owner-gated on send, so the SetOwner is mandatory) plus a toast. Strictly stronger than TortalPortal's client-side `Player.TryPlacePiece` cap, which any client can ignore.


**Player experience:** Your portal sits in a stone frame. On the left there are three empty 1×1 sockets where a wood beam obviously goes — you built the frame that way because the server-written sign beside it reads `PLUG A BEAM: 1 Base · 2 Haldor · 3 Mine`.

You take out your hammer, select Wood Beam, and place one in socket 2. It snaps in with the normal building sound. Within about a quarter second a toast reads `Haldor plugged. Portal → Haldor (1,140m).` The portal glows. The beam stays there forever.

A week later you come back and need to remember nothing: there is a beam in socket 2, so the portal goes to Haldor. Anyone standing in your base can read it. To change it you remove the beam (`Haldor unplugged`) and place one in socket 3.

Cost: equip hammer, select piece, place — about five seconds and one piece of wood. Slower than typing but permanent, visible, and it turns routing state into architecture, which is a genuinely Valheim-native idea.

Jank rating: medium. The mechanism is elegant; discoverability depends entirely on the server writing a sign that explains the sockets and on the sockets being visually obvious, which is on the player's building skill.


**Failure modes:**
- A `CreateNewZDO`-only postfix always sees `GetPrefab() == 0` on the network path and can never act — SpawnGovernor's header records this as a shipped bug in its own first version.
- Patching `Player.PlacePiece` / `Player.TryPlacePiece` / `ZNetScene.Instantiate` produces code that can never execute on a dedicated server (PortalLock's precedent).
- Socket matching must tolerate snap-grid offsets and rotation; a hard equality on position will miss almost every placement. Use a radius of ~0.75 m around the expected offset, in the portal's local frame.
- `Piece.SetCreator` only writes when `m_nview.IsOwner() && GetCreator() == 0` (:136417), so world-gen structures and some pieces have `s_creator == 0`. Do not treat a missing creator as 'unowned' without checking.
- Destroying a client-created ZDO inside the Deserialize postfix may leave an orphaned local instance on the placing client until the zone reloads; the build materials may or may not be refunded.
- Players rebuild and remodel constantly — a socket that overlaps a common building position will fire spuriously.

**Open questions:**

SpawnGovernor does this for creatures and is shipped, but a Piece/WearNTear-bearing object may differ. IN-GAME: set a cap of 1, place a second portal on a vanilla client, and observe whether the ghost disappears cleanly and whether materials are refunded.
- Is `ZDOVars.s_creator` reliably non-zero on a player-placed portal in 1.0.7? TortalPortal's export treats 0 as 'admin-spawned or older'. IN-GAME: place a portal and confirm `s_creator` equals that player's `s_playerID`.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage) begins at assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74206, not :74225 (the cited range is mid-body).
- The Deserialize postfix fires on EVERY ZDO update, not only creation; the pending-ZDOID set from the CreateNewZDO postfix (SpawnGovernor.cs:34-66) is mandatory to distinguish new arrivals, and must only record when prefabHash==0 (network path). World-load never passes through CreateNewZDO/Deserialize (ZDOMan.Load uses ZDOPool.Create() at :76478/:76488 and ZDO.Load), so loaded sockets must be indexed separately at startup by scanning m_objectsByID/GetPortalList.
- Inside the Deserialize postfix the new portal is NOT yet in GetPortalList() — AddIfPortal runs after Deserialize (:77132) — so the count is of pre-existing portals only (correct for a cap, but do not expect the new one to be present).
- Destroying a client-placed piece from the server gives no resource refund on the client (it is a DestroyZDO, not a WearNTear.Remove); the toast should say so.
- The capped portal's materials are already gone: the client runs ConsumeResources right after TryPlacePiece succeeds (client Player.Update :10803-10809), before the ZDO ever reaches the server. A server-side destroy therefore eats the piece cost unless the mod spawns refund ItemDrop ZDOs itself. State this in howItWorks.
- The Deserialize hook fires only on the network-receive path. ZDOs loaded from disk at boot go through ZDOMan.Load, never CreateNewZDO(ZDOID,Vector3,int) with hash 0, so socket state does NOT come back from the hook after a restart; the mod must rebuild it with a spatial scan of m_objectsByID / sector lists at load. 'Survives restarts' is true of the ZDO, not of the derived switch state.
- Per-creator portal count via GetPortalList() (:77648) relies on s_creator on every existing portal; portals placed by a build-plan/copy tool or pre-existing world portals may carry creator 0 and are uncountable — treat 0 as 'unowned' explicitly.
- m_onZDODestroyed also fires for the server's own DestroyZDO calls (RPC to 0L is handled locally in InvokeRoutedRPC :83587-83590), so the destroy callback must ignore ZDOs the mod itself is destroying to avoid re-entrancy/double toasts.
- The 'quarter second' toast latency is plausible but unmeasured: it is client SendZDOs cadence + server Update + routed 'Message' RPC; mark as needs in-game timing.

### 166. Chat commands (`/portal home`)

`player-ux-no-client:Chat commands (`/portal home`)` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** not-enforceable → **not-enforceable** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Typing a command in chat — the obvious design, dead on a dedicated server for three independent reasons.


**How it works:** (1) SLASH COMMANDS NEVER LEAVE THE CLIENT. `Chat.InputText` does `text = ((text[0] != '/') ? ("say " + text) : text.Substring(1)); TryRunCommand(text, this);` (:41947-41955). `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:45734-45758) looks the name up in the CLIENT's own compiled dictionary; `/portal` is not in it and the call uses silentFail, so the client does nothing and prints nothing. There is no network path for an unrecognised slash command.

(2) PLAIN CHAT IS INVISIBLE TO A SOLO PLAYER. Plain text becomes `say <text>` → `Chat.SendText`. Shout goes through `CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync` (:41996-42042), which — when a RelationsProvider exists, i.e. on Steam — sends one RPC to `ZNet.instance.LocalPlayerCharacterID.UserID` (the sender's OWN peer id) plus one per OTHER listed player's `m_characterID.UserID`. `InvokeRoutedRPC` calls `RouteRPC` only `if (targetPeerID != m_id)` (:83591). For a lone player every target IS their own id, so ZERO packets go on the wire. Normal/Whisper take `Talker.Say` → `m_nview.InvokeRPC(user, "Say", …)` (:18942-18950), same addressing, same result.

(3) WITH 2+ PLAYERS IT IS RELAY-ONLY. The packets pass through the server's `RPC_RoutedRPC` → `RouteRPC` (:83632-83643) but are never addressed to the server, so no registered handler fires. A prefix CAN sniff them — but a channel that works only when a second player is online is not a channel.

THE ADMIN EXCEPTION: `ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879-81889) is gated on `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())` and runs the string through the SERVER's `Console.instance.TryRunCommand`; replies return via `ZNet.RemotePrint` → the client's console (:81635-81656). A mod-registered server-side `Terminal.ConsoleCommand` with `onlyServer: true, remoteCommand: true` gives ADMINS a genuine text console — invisible to ordinary players and landing in a window most people never open.


**Player experience:** The player types `/portal home` and presses Enter. Absolutely nothing happens — no error, no message, no log line on their machine or the server's. The chat box closes. They try `/tp home`, `!home`, `portal home`. The last one appears in chat as a shout nobody but they can see if they are alone. They conclude the mod is broken and file a bug.


**Failure modes:**
- Silent failure is the worst possible outcome for a discovery path — the player tries the obvious thing and gets zero signal.
- Any documentation saying 'type /portal …' generates support tickets forever.
- Sniffing shouts via a RouteRPC prefix works only with 2+ players online: untestable solo and unreliable in production.

If yes, `SendText` shout collapses to a `targetPeerID 0` broadcast (:42002-42005) and shout-as-command becomes fully viable even solo — a total reversal of this ruling and by far the highest-value single test in this document, because it would give the mod a free-text command channel and make most of the janky schemes unnecessary. IN-GAME: prefix `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` on the server, have a SOLO player type a plain sentence and a `/s` shout, and see whether `"ChatMessage"` arrives.

Needs a one-line in-game test (register 'ChatMessage' on ZRoutedRpc server-side, shout while alone).

The Steam platform implementation (Splatform.Steam) is NOT in the decompile set on disk (libs-Tools/1.0/client contains only Splatform.dll core with the IRelationsProvider interface), so 'i.e. on Steam' is unverified. Plain text → 'say' → Chat.SendText (:41975-41994): Shout uses CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync (:41996-42042) which, when a RelationsProvider exists, targets the sender's own LocalPlayerCharacterID.UserID first and then each other player's m_characterID.UserID; Normal/Whisper go through Talker.Say → m_nview.InvokeRPC(user, 'Say') (:18942-18950) with the same addressing. ### 167. Ward toggle as a switch (and ward data as the permission source)

`player-ux-no-client:Ward toggle as a switch (and ward data as the permission source)` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Using a guard stone's Enable/Permit buttons as a portal command — dead as an RPC intercept, fine as a ZDO poll, and far more valuable as the source of portal permissions.


**How it works:** RPC PATH (ruled out): `PrivateArea` registers `"ToggleEnabled"` and `"TogglePermitted"` on its own ZNetView in `Awake` (:137200-137201); `Interact` sends them with `m_nview.InvokeRPC(...)` (:137370-137392), targeting the ward ZDO's OWNER — normally the interacting player, so the RPC is handled locally and never hits the wire (:83587-83594). Even when it crosses, the server's `HandleRoutedRPC` needs `ZNetScene.instance.FindInstance(zdo)` non-null (:83659) and it never is (`Game.FixedUpdate` pin :100465). A patch on `RPC_ToggleEnabled`/`RPC_TogglePermitted` compiles and never fires. Worse, both handlers IGNORE the routed `uid` and act on the payload `playerID` (:137399-137421), so sender hardening buys nothing.

ZDO PATH (works): every field is plain ZDO data. `ZDOVars.s_enabled` (:78423) — the on/off state. `ZDOVars.s_permitted` (:78529) — the permitted COUNT; entries are raw runtime-concatenated string keys `"pu_id" + i` (long) and `"pu_name" + i` (string), with id==0 skipped on read (`SetPermittedPlayers` :137338-137347, `GetPermittedPlayers` :137349-137363). These have NO ZDOVars constant — hash the concatenated string. `ZDOVars.s_creator` (:78393) and `s_creatorName` (:78397) give the builder.

SO: poll `s_enabled` at 0.5 s and treat a double-toggle within 5 s as a command — or, far more usefully, build the SERVER-SIDE WARD MODEL portal permissions actually need: 'may this player re-dial this portal?' answered from `s_creator` plus the pu_id list, entirely from ZDO reads with no `PrivateArea` instance.

NEVER call `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` (:137547-137593): it iterates the static `m_allAreas` list populated only in `Awake` (:137197), which is permanently EMPTY on a dedicated server, so it returns true for every point — a silent allow-all that looks like a working permission check.

RADIUS is the missing piece: `PrivateArea.m_radius` is a compiled Inspector field with a class default of 10f (:137132) and no ZDO backing.


**Player experience:** You press E on your guard stone to switch it off, then E again to switch it back on within a couple of seconds. A toast reads `Portal network unlocked for 60s.` You walk to any portal inside the ward and re-dial freely. After a minute it relocks: `Relocked.`

More useful and entirely invisible: you add your friend Bjorn to the ward's permitted list the normal vanilla way (he presses E while the stone is off). From then on, when Bjorn types `>Vault` on your portal it just works, and when a stranger types it they get `Vault is warded. Ask Bjorn or Astrid.` The server derived all of that from the ward's own list without anyone configuring anything mod-specific.

That second use — ward-derived permissions — is far more valuable than ward-as-a-button. The toggle gesture is clumsy, since it disables your base's protection to press a button, and should never be a routine input.


**Failure modes:**
- `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` returns TRUE for everything server-side because `m_allAreas` is always empty (:137173, :137197, :137547) — a silent allow-all masquerading as a permission check.
- `m_radius` is Inspector data (class default 10f, :137132); hardcoding 10 will mis-cover every real ward.
- Toggling a ward off to issue a command disables base protection for the duration — a bad trade.
- Any client can add itself to an un-enabled ward's permitted list, because `RPC_TogglePermitted` gates only on `m_nview.IsOwner() && !IsEnabled()` and trusts the payload playerID (:137399-137412). Ward-derived permissions inherit that vanilla weakness.
- `pu_id<i>`/`pu_name<i>` have no ZDOVars constant; writing `s_permitted` without the matching indexed keys produces phantom entries.

**Designer citations:** PrivateArea.Awake RPC registrations — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:137200-137201 ; PrivateArea.Interact — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:137370-137392 ; PrivateArea.RPC_ToggleEnabled / RPC_TogglePermitted — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:137399-137421 ; PrivateArea.SetPermittedPlayers / GetPermittedPlayers — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:137338-137363 ; PrivateArea.CheckAccess / m_allAreas — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:137547-137593, :137173, :137197 ; PrivateArea.m_radius — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:137132 ; ZDOVars.s_enabled / s_permitted / s_creator / s_creatorName — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78423, :78529, :78393, :78397 ; ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC FindInstance gate — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83646-83665


**Open questions:**
- What is the guard_stone prefab's actual `m_radius`? IN-GAME: place one and binary-search the distance at which another player's build is refused; or dump the prefab.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- PrivateArea.Interact has an additional early-out 'if (m_ownerFaction != 0) return false' (:137375-137378) before the creator check — irrelevant for player-built wards but present.
- Ward pu_id values are the same s_playerID namespace as Piece s_creator, so the permission model needs no name matching; pu_name is display-only.
- The toggle RPC targets the ward ZDO's OWNER, which after ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76927) can be any nearby peer, not necessarily the interacting player; and if the server session momentarily owns the ward ZDO the toggle is silently dropped by the FindInstance gate (:83659). The ZDO-poll design is unaffected but the write may originate from a different client than the presser.
- m_radius: the class default 10f (:137132) is NOT the guard_stone prefab value (Inspector-serialized, 32 m in vanilla). The server cannot read the prefab; the mod must hardcode 32 m for guard_stone and treat it as an in-game-verified constant, not derive it from the decompile.
- The 'double-toggle within 5 s' input is creator-only (Interact requires m_piece.IsCreator() to send ToggleEnabled, :137380) and each toggle also fires FlashShield to everyone; document that only the ward's creator can use the gesture.
- Enforcement should read: server-enforced for the permission decision (route form), client-honoured for the toggle detection (the server merely observes a ZDO field the owning client writes).

### 168. Feedback: the tag echo (primary confirmation surface)

`player-ux-no-client:Feedback: the tag echo (primary confirmation surface)` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The server rewrites the portal's own `s_tag` and the vanilla client redraws the hover text from the live ZDO every frame — the fastest, most in-context confirmation available.


**How it works:** `TeleportWorld.GetHoverText` (:143453-143464) calls `GetTagInfo()`, which reads `zdo.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)` FRESH on every call — no cache, no timer, no DataRevision gate. The hover UI calls it each frame the player looks at the portal, so the instant a server-written ZDO update lands the text under the crosshair changes. Sub-frame repaint, no polling on either side.

The write: `zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, reply)` + `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702, mandatory or the change is lost at save) + `ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706). No ownership claim is strictly required — no ZDO setter checks ownership (`okForNotOwner` is a dead parameter, :73648) and `IncreaseDataRevision` fires regardless — but claiming (`SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`, :74627/:77362) guarantees the server wins a revision race with the nearby owning client. `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) hands ownership back within 2 s, which is fine and keeps vanilla retagging working.

HARD CONSTRAINTS ON THE ECHO:
• ≤10 characters, always (the `TextInput.Show` clamp, :61515-61521).
• No rich text — `GetHoverText` runs `RemoveRichTextTags()` (:143459), regex `<[\/a-zA-Z0-9= "\"''#;:()$_-]*?>` (assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703). Colour is impossible here; it IS possible on a Sign face.
• ASCII only pending a glyph test.
• Both ends of a vanilla-paired link must carry BYTE-IDENTICAL tags or `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 tears the pair down within 5 s (:100601).
• Censoring is not a concern: `CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC` is `return text;` server-side (:94588-94591) and the censored flag is surfaced only on PlayFab (:143462).

ECHO ALPHABET (char 0 = state glyph): `>NAME` dialed · `#NAME` this portal's own name · `?NAME` unknown/ambiguous · `!NAME` denied/locked · `-` unlinked · `.NAME` pending.


**Player experience:** You are hovering the portal; the text under your crosshair reads `Teleport  Portal tag:"#Base" [Connected]`. You press E, type `>Haldor`, hit Enter. The dialog closes, you are looking at the portal again — and the text now reads `Teleport  Portal tag:">Haldor" [Connected]`. It changed while you were watching it, with no perceptible gap.

A bad name reads `"?Haldr"` instead, and the `?` tells you at a glance something is wrong before you read the toast in the corner. A portal locked against you reads `"!Vault"`.

This is the single best feedback surface available: instant, exactly where the player is already looking, and persistent — you can walk away, come back tomorrow, hover the portal, and it still tells you where it points. A toast cannot do that.


**Failure modes:**
- An echo longer than 10 characters is truncated in the rename dialog and the truncation is submitted as a command on the player's next Enter.
- Rich text is stripped, so the echo cannot use colour to distinguish states — the leading glyph is the only channel.
- Distinct per-portal echoes are incompatible with vanilla pairing (`Game.ConnectPortals` tag-equality teardown, :100601) without prefixing it out.
- Without `SetDirtyPortals()` the echo is lost at the next world save.
- A player who opens the dialog and presses OK re-submits the echo as a command unless the parser is idempotent on its own canonical strings.

**Designer citations:** TeleportWorld.GetHoverText / GetTagInfo — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143470, :143556-143570 ; ZDO.Set (no ownership check) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:73648-73654, :73721 ; ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals / ForceSendZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76702, :77706 ; ZDO.SetOwner / ZDOMan.GetSessionID — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:74627, :77362 ; ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76901-76927 ; StringExtensionMethods.RemoveRichTextTags — assembly_utils_SERVER.decompiled.cs:6700-6703 ; Game.ConnectPortals tag teardown — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100601 ; CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC (server stub) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:94588-94591


**Open questions:**
- Does a client already standing at a portal pick up the tag change without a zone reload? `GetHoverText` reads live so it should be immediate, but confirm the ZDO update actually reaches a client that currently OWNS the portal. IN-GAME: stand at a gate, server-write a new tag, and watch the hover.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- '≤10 characters, always' is a dialog constraint, not a display one: GetHoverText renders a tag of any length; 10 is the characterLimit passed by TeleportWorld.Interact → TextInput.RequestText(this, "$piece_portal_tag", 10) (:143482) and applied to m_inputField.characterLimit in Show (:61515-61521). The real hazard is that opening the dialog on a longer echo pre-fills a truncated string the player may re-submit; keep echoes ≤10 for that reason and verify GuiInputField's truncation on set in-game.
- Ownership does not make the server 'win a revision race'. Client RPC_ZDOData applies incoming data purely on DataRevision (skips when incoming ≤ local, :77107-77116 server mirror), and ZDOPeer.ShouldSend (:76003-76013) is also revision-only. Claiming ownership stops the client's RPC_SetTag handler from writing (it is IsOwner-gated, :143587-143589) but a concurrent local Set on the client still bumps its revision and can beat the server's. Use ForceSendZDO plus a re-check on the next poll rather than relying on ownership.
- Vanilla ConnectPortals phase 2 (:100608-100620) pairs ANY two unconnected portals with equal tags — two portals echoing '>Haldor' would be vanilla-paired to each other. The 'Pairing takeover' prereq is therefore hard, not optional.
- Client-side GetTagInfo runs CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC which is a no-op only when !RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() (client FilterUGC body); Steam PC is unfiltered, console/PlayFab clients may censor server-written echoes.
- Line reference: ZDO.Deserialize-independent; TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag body starts :143587 as the brief says.
- Censoring: the server stub (:94588-94591) is irrelevant — hover text is rendered on the CLIENT, whose CensorShittyWords.FilterUGC is real (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:94901-94940). It passes text through when !RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering() (Steam PC), but on console/crossplay clients a server-authored tag with an empty or stale s_tagauthor can resolve to BlockedByPrivilege and render as the '$ugc_text' placeholder. State 'Steam PC unaffected; console clients need an in-game check'.
- 'Claiming ownership guarantees the server wins the race' is wrong on both counts. (a) Race: if server and owning client each Set from revision N, both produce N+1 and each side's RPC_ZDOData discards the other's packet (`num4 <= DataRevision` → continue, :77109-77118) — split-brain, not a server win; ForceSendZDO does not bypass ShouldSend. (b) Side effect: while the server holds ownership, a vanilla retag is routed to owner=server and dropped by the FindInstance gate (:83659), so vanilla retagging is dead for up to the 2 s ReleaseZDOS cadence (:76870-76884). Recommend no ownership claim for pure tag echoes; rely on the fact the client only writes s_tag inside RPC_SetTag.
- The `-` unlinked glyph must coincide with an actual ZDOID.None connection, otherwise the vanilla suffix reads '[Connected]' (HaveTarget = connection != None, :143632-143638) beside an 'unlinked' tag.
- The echo alphabet (`>NAME` on the dialing portal, `#NAME` on the target) is by construction incompatible with vanilla pairing (tags must be byte-identical, :100601-100606); it works ONLY with the 'Pairing takeover' prereq that suppresses Game.ConnectPortals, and that takeover must also re-apply the connection after every client RPC_SetTag, which clears it (UpdateConnection(Portal, None) :143594-143596). Make the dependency explicit rather than listing it as a soft prereq.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] TeleportWorld.GetHoverText (:143453-143464) calls GetTagInfo() (:143556-143570) which does zDO.GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag) with no cache; the client Hud.UpdateCrosshair calls hoverable.GetHoverText() every frame (client decompile, UpdateCrosshair body). ZDO.Set(int,int,bool okForNotOwner) never reads okForNotOwner (:73648-73654) and Set(int,string) (:73721-73727) has no owner check; IncreaseDataRevision always fires. SetDirtyPortals (:76702-76705) is genuinely required: portal ZDOs are saved in the separate ChunkPortal file only when DirtyPortalObjects is set (GetSaveClonePerChunk :77621-77635), and a plain Set only dirties the sector chunk via SetDirtySector. - [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism verified. ### 169. Feedback: MessageHud toasts (the detail channel)

`player-ux-no-client:Feedback: MessageHud toasts (the detail channel)` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Server-pushed top-left or centre-screen HUD messages, addressed to one player, localized client-side, with no length limit and no truncation trap.


**How it works:** TWO INDEPENDENT PATHS, both proven in Wonderland.

(A) PER-CHARACTER, safer. `Player.Start` registers the routed RPC `"Message"(int type, string msg, int amount)` on the player's own ZNetView and ONLY when `m_nview.IsOwner()` (:10072); `Player.RPC_Message` re-checks IsOwner before calling `MessageHud.ShowMessage` (:14820-14825). Server: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "Message", (int)MessageHud.MessageType.TopLeft, text, 0)`. Because it is registered only on the owning client it can never be delivered to the wrong player. Wonderland ships this as `PlayerNotify.Toast` (Core/Data/PlayerNotify.cs:15).

(B) GLOBAL. `MessageHud.Start` registers `"ShowMessage"(int type, string text)` on `ZRoutedRpc` (:55799-55809) and `RPC_ShowMessage` calls `ShowMessage` unconditionally (:55848-55851). Server: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "ShowMessage", (int)type, text)`, or `0L` to broadcast. No ZDOID needed, so it works in the window before `peer.m_characterID` is populated.

`MessageHud.MessageType` is `TopLeft = 1, Center = 2` (:55705-55709). TopLeft stacks and persists briefly; Center is the big single-line banner vanilla uses for `$msg_blocked`. Text is run through `Localization.Localize` on the RECEIVING client, so sending `"$piece_portal"` renders in that player's own language — a free i18n path for any string with a vanilla token.

NO LENGTH LIMIT and no truncation trap, because this is one-way output that never becomes input. Use it for everything the 10 characters cannot hold: distances, biome names, error explanations, directory listings, permission reasons. Sending 5 toasts in one frame produces 5 stacked TopLeft lines — that is how a directory is delivered. Keep it to ~6 lines before they scroll off.


**Player experience:** You type `>Haldor` on the portal. As the hover flips to `">Haldor"`, a line appears in the top-left: `Dialed → Haldor · 1,140m · Black Forest`. It fades after a few seconds.

You type `?`. Six lines stack up:

`— PORTALS —`
`1 Base      612m   yours`
`2 Haldor  1,140m   public`
`3 Mine2     840m   yours`
`4 Vault   2,300m   LOCKED`
`type >1 .. >4 or >name`

You try a locked one and get a Center banner across the middle of your screen, the same one vanilla uses when a portal is blocked: `Vault is locked by Bjorn.`

This is the workhorse. It carries everything the tag cannot, needs no construction, no proximity and no learning, and it looks identical to vanilla's own messages — a player will not perceive it as 'a mod talking to me'.


**Failure modes:**
- More than ~6 stacked TopLeft lines scroll off before they can be read.
- Center messages are intrusive; overusing them for routine confirmations trains players to ignore the banner that also carries vanilla's real warnings.
- Path (A) requires `peer.m_characterID` to be populated — it is `ZDOID.None` between connect and `Game.SpawnPlayer` and again between death and respawn (:100270, :100413). Guard with `!peer.m_characterID.IsNone()` and fall back to path (B).
- Path (B) depends on a `MessageHud` existing on the RECEIVING client (it always does) but the registration is global, so another mod registering `"ShowMessage"` server-side would collide.
- Toasts are transient — a player who alt-tabs misses the only record of what happened. Pair with the persistent tag echo.

IN-GAME: dump `m_functions` keys at server start.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- TopLeft does NOT stack. MessageHud queues TopLeft messages and shows one per second in a single text field (:55864-55869, :55910-55953); five toasts in one frame = five sequential 1-second replacements. Identical text repeated within 4 s is merged with an ' xN' suffix (:55916-55925).

- ShowMessage is suppressed entirely while Hud.IsUserHidden() unless showDespiteHiddenHUD, which the RPC path never sets (:55855-55858, :14824).
- Every TopLeft/Center message is also appended to MessageHud.m_messageLog (:56056-56062), bounded by m_maxLogMessages.
- Rewrite the multi-line claim: TopLeft is a one-slot queue drained at 1 message/second with a 4 s fade (MessageHud.UpdateMessage :55910-55950). N messages sent in one frame display sequentially over N seconds, one at a time. There is no stacking.
- Possible workaround for a directory: send ONE TopLeft/Center message containing embedded '\n' — m_messageText is a TMP_Text and will render multiple lines unless the prefab clips/overflows; this is unverified and needs an in-game check (layout, wrapping, vertical growth).
- All toasts are also appended to the Logs list capped at m_maxLogMessages and readable in Inventory → Texts → Logs (:61904-61908); that is the only place a full listing persists client-side, and it is the honest 'directory' surface.
- Enforcement label: nothing is enforced; the client renders (and drops when HUD is hidden). Mark client-honoured.
- Path A vs B: RPC_ShowMessage ignores the sender entirely, so any client can spam any other client's HUD via 'ShowMessage' — irrelevant to the mod but worth noting when choosing path A for per-player addressing.

- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Both paths verified. Player.Start registers 'Message'(int,string,int) on the player's ZNetView only inside if (m_nview.IsOwner()) (:10070-10072); RPC_Message re-checks IsOwner before MessageHud.instance.ShowMessage (:14820-14825); Wonderland PlayerNotify.Toast (PlayerNotify.cs:15-29) sends InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, zdo.m_uid, 'Message', type, text, 0) exactly as claimed. MessageHud.Start registers 'ShowMessage'(int,string) on ZRoutedRpc (:55808) and RPC_ShowMessage calls ShowMessage unconditionally (:55848-55851). MessageType is TopLeft=1, Center=2 (:55705-55709). ShowMessage runs Localization.instance.Localize(text) on the receiver (:55859). However the stacking claim is false: TopLeft messages are Enqueued into m_msgQeue (:55864-55869) and UpdateMessage dequeues ONE per second (m_msgQueueTimer >= 1f, :55910-55919) into the single m_messageText, with an identical consecutive text within 4 s collapsed into an 'xN' counter (:55916-55925). ### 170. Feedback: server-pushed map pin

`player-ux-no-client:Feedback: server-pushed map pin` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


`RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` puts a named, permanently-saved pin on a vanilla client's map plus an iconed HUD toast — with no way ever to remove it again.


**How it works:** `Game.Start` registers `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"(string pinName, int pinType, Vector3 pos, bool showMap)` on EVERY peer, outside any IsServer branch (:100068). The handler calls `Minimap.instance.DiscoverLocation(pos, (PinType)pinType, pinName, showMap)` and, if map mode is None, also `Player.m_localPlayer.SetLookDir(pos - playerPos, 3.5f)` — physically turning the player's head toward the target (:100823-100830).

`Minimap.DiscoverLocation` (:58334-58361): if `HaveSimilarPin(pos, type, name, save:true)` it bails (showing `$msg_pin_exist` only when showMap); otherwise `AddPin(pos, type, name, save: true, isChecked: false, 0L)`. In BOTH branches it calls `Player.m_localPlayer.Message(MessageType.TopLeft, "$msg_pin_added: " + name, 0, sprite)` — so every pin push also yields an iconed HUD toast for free.

`HaveSimilarPin` matches name AND type AND save AND `Utils.DistanceXZ < 1f` (:58363-58373), so re-pushing the identical pin with showMap:false is idempotent and silent. `AddPin` clamps an out-of-range PinType to `Icon3` and force-enables that icon's filter if the player had turned it off (:58375-58405) — the server's pins cannot be filtered away.

`Minimap.PinType` verified: Icon0=0, Icon1, Icon2, Icon3, Death=4, Bed=5, Icon4=6, Shout=7, None=8, Boss=9, Player=10, RandomEvent=11, Ping=12, EventArea=13, Hildir1-3, Memorial=17 (:56079-56099).

THE FATAL CAVEAT: `save: true` is hard-coded. The pin goes permanently into that player's own PlayerProfile map data on their disk. There is NO removal RPC anywhere in the assembly. A demolished or renamed portal leaves its pin stuck on every player's map forever, and a re-push under a new name creates a SECOND pin. This is a one-shot discovery gift, NOT a live-synced set — TortalPortal's client-side PortalMapPins rebuilds every 2 s precisely because it can add AND remove.

SANE USE: push exactly once per (player, portal) when that player first NAMES a portal, storing the pairs in mod state so a restart does not re-push.

SECOND, NON-SAVING CHANNEL: `ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons` / the `"LocationIcons"` routed RPC (:113581-113607) replaces the client's whole `m_locationIcons` dictionary, which `Minimap.UpdateLocationPins` rebuilds from every 5 s as `save:false` pins — fully server-controlled and removable, but ICON-ONLY with no name, and rendering only for names present in the client's compiled sprite list.


**Player experience:** You name your first portal: press E, type `#Base`, Enter. The hover flips to `"#Base"` and simultaneously a toast with a small map-pin icon appears: `Pin added: Base`. You open your map and there it is, a named marker at your base, exactly like one you placed yourself — because it IS a pin you now own, saved into your character file, surviving logout.

Each new portal you name drops another pin. After a week your map has every portal labelled and you never placed a pin by hand.

The ugly part arrives when you tear down the mine portal. The `Mine2` pin stays on your map forever. You can delete it manually the vanilla way but the server cannot do it for you and will never try. Rename `Mine2` to `DeepMine` and you now have two pins a metre apart.

So the mod must be conservative: one pin per portal per player, pushed once at naming time, with a toast reading `Pin added: Base (delete it yourself if you move it)`. Anything more aggressive turns the player's map into litter.


**Failure modes:**
- `save: true` is hard-coded and there is no removal RPC — every pushed pin is permanent on that player's disk.
- Renaming a portal and re-pushing creates a duplicate pin one metre from the old one, because `HaveSimilarPin` matches on name.
- `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` calls `Minimap.instance.DiscoverLocation` unguarded (:100825); harmless on a client but it means the RPC must never be sent to the server's own peer id.
- `AddPin` force-enables the icon filter (:58400-58403), overriding a player's deliberate choice to hide that pin category.
- Repeated pushes with showMap:true spam `$msg_pin_exist` and re-centre the player's map, which is intensely annoying. Always send showMap:false for routine pushes.

**Designer citations:** Game.Start registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100068 ; Game.RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100823-100830 ; Minimap.DiscoverLocation — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:58334-58361 ; Minimap.HaveSimilarPin — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:58363-58373 ; Minimap.AddPin — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:58375-58406 ; Minimap.PinType enum — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:56079-56099 ; ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons / RPC_LocationIcons — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113581-113607 ; Wonderland FirstSpawnGrant.GrantBoat — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/FirstSpawnGrant.cs:253-263


**Open questions:**
- Does `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` render identically on a PlayFab/Xbox crossplay client? Wonderland ships it behind StarterBoatMapPin but carries no dated live-test note for it. IN-GAME: push a pin, confirm it appears, log out and back in to confirm save:true persisted, then re-send the identical payload and confirm HaveSimilarPin suppresses the duplicate.
- Which names does the client's compiled `Minimap.m_locationIcons` sprite list contain? That bounds what the non-saving LocationIcons overlay can render. IN-GAME: enumerate it on a client.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- The LocationIcons secondary channel is overwritten by vanilla: the server re-sends the real location list on every new peer (ZoneSystem.OnNewPeer :113615) and broadcasts SendLocationIcons(0L) whenever a location with m_iconPlaced is spawned (:114998-115001). A mod using this channel must postfix SendLocationIcons (private) or re-send after those events.

- Add: PinType.Icon4 (=6) is the vanilla portal icon, so a pushed portal pin can use the same glyph players place by hand — cite :56085.
- Add: the SetLookDir head-yank (:100826-100829) happens on EVERY push while the map is closed, including idempotent re-pushes that show no toast; a passive re-sync at login would still turn the player's head. Reinforces 'push once'.
- Add for the LocationIcons channel: replacing the dictionary drops vanilla's real location icons (Haldor, Hildir, bosses, start temple) unless the mod re-includes them from ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcons (:113627-113640); portal markers must borrow an existing sprite name from Minimap.m_locationIcons and render double-size with no name (:58690-58696). SendLocationIcons is private; the mod invokes the routed RPC directly.

**Verifier reasoning:**

Minimap.DiscoverLocation (:58334-58361): HaveSimilarPin(pos,type,name,save:true) → bail (Center '$msg_pin_exist' only if showMap); else AddPin(pos,type,name,save:true,isChecked:false,0L) and a TopLeft '$msg_pin_added: name' with the type sprite in both showMap branches. Minimap.DiscoverLocation (:58334-58361): HaveSimilarPin(save:true) bail (Center '$msg_pin_exist' only if showMap), else AddPin(save:true) and a TopLeft '$msg_pin_added: name' toast with the pin sprite in both showMap branches. ### 171. Feedback: the server as a speaking voice (fabricated ChatMessage)

`player-ux-no-client:Feedback: the server as a speaking voice (fabricated ChatMessage)` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


One forged `"ChatMessage"` RPC yields a chat line, floating world text and a labelled animated map pin from an arbitrary named speaker.


**How it works:** `Chat.Awake` registers `"ChatMessage"(Vector3 pos, int type, UserInfo user, string text)` on `ZRoutedRpc` (:41626); `Chat.RPC_ChatMessage` hands it to `OnNewChatMessage` (:41970-41973). The server forges one: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "ChatMessage", worldPos, (int)Talker.Type.Shout, userInfo, text)` with `userInfo.Name` set to anything — `"Portal Network"`, `"The Gate"`.

WHAT ONE PACKET PRODUCES (`OnNewChatMessage` :41775-41816): `type != Ping` → `AddString(sender.UserId, text, type)`, a real persistent scrollable chat line; `AddInworldText(go, senderID, pos, type, sender, text)`, floating text at `pos` with TTL `m_worldTextTTL` = 5 s, Shout uppercased and yellow; and `Minimap.UpdateShoutPins`/`UpdatePingPins` render a large animated map pin labelled `"<Name>: <TEXT>"` for Shout or `"<Name>: PING"` for Ping (:57591-57650).

GATE: `AddInworldText` is skipped only when `Minimap.instance.m_mode == MapMode.None` AND the position is farther than `m_nomapPingDistance` (50 m) (:41808). Normal play has the small minimap up, so it always runs.

PERMISSIONS: `OnNewChatMessage` routes through `RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync` unless the sender id equals the local character — and that is a one-line stub returning Granted synchronously in 1.0.7 (:88350-88353). No mute filter to defeat, no async delay.

SANITISATION: `text.Replace('<',' ').Replace('>',' ')` (:41795-41796). No rich text — and note this mangles a `>` sigil, so strip sigils before speaking a tag string.

PING TYPE (3) is the interesting one for portals: NO chat line, world text forced to the literal `"PING"`, and a labelled map pin at the given position. So the server can drop a transient, self-expiring beacon at a portal's DESTINATION — a 'this is where you are about to go' preview that costs nothing and leaves nothing behind, unlike the permanently-saved `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` pin.


**Player experience:** You dial your portal to Haldor. Along with the tag flip and the toast, a line appears in your chat log:

`Portal Network: → HALDOR, 1,140M NNE, BLACK FOREST`

and for five seconds a yellow shout-text hangs above the portal frame saying the same thing, and a labelled marker pulses on your minimap at Haldor's position so you can see where you are about to end up. Because it went into the chat log you can scroll back ten minutes later and find out where you sent yourself.

The beacon variant: you type `>Haldor` and a Ping-type message drops a pulsing marker at the destination with no chat spam at all. You check your map, see where it is, and decide whether to step through.

The risk is tone. A server that 'speaks' in the chat log reads as a bot, and if it speaks too often players tune it out. Reserve it for consequential events: a dial confirmed, a lock changed, a portal destroyed.


**Failure modes:**
- `<` and `>` are replaced with spaces (:41795-41796), mangling any echoed sigil and ruling out rich text.
- Shout-type messages clutter the chat log; over-use trains players to ignore the channel.
- The forged speaker name is arbitrary, which is also an impersonation vector if the mod ever lets player-supplied text set it.
- Ping type suppresses the chat line entirely and forces the world text to `"PING"` — you cannot say anything with it, only point.
- `AddInworldText` is skipped in nomap worlds beyond 50 m (:41808), so the world-text half silently vanishes on those servers.

**Designer citations:** Chat.Awake "ChatMessage" registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41626 ; Chat.RPC_ChatMessage — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41970-41973 ; Chat.OnNewChatMessage — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41775-41816 ; Chat.m_worldTextTTL — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41594 ; Minimap.UpdateShoutPins / UpdatePingPins — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:57591-57650 ; RelationsManager.CheckPermissionAsync (stub) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:88350-88353 ; Chat.SendPing (the Ping type reference) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:42058-42071

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- REFUTED: 'Portal Network: ...' chat-log line. Terminal.AddString(PlatformUserID,...) (:45933-45959) ignores UserInfo.Name, looks the sender up in ZNet.m_players via TryGetPlayerByPlatformUserID (:81477-81493) and returns without adding a line when not found. A headless server is never in that list (UpdatePlayerList :81248). Chat line only achievable by sending a real listed player's PlatformUserID, and it is then attributed to that player's name.
- The arbitrary speaker name is real only for the floating world text and the map pin (WorldTextInstance.m_name :41531 -> FilterUGC identity :94588-94591; pins :57604, :57633).

A second message replaces the first; a Shout and a Ping cannot coexist; 'one label per portal' is impossible via ChatMessage (use RPC_DamageText for that).
- Ping/Shout world text is never distance-culled: off-screen texts are clamped to the screen edge (:41843-41858). A beacon at a distant destination is also a 5 s HUD-edge label.

- Chat-log line requires UserId to match an entry in the client's ZNet.m_players (Terminal.AddString(PlatformUserID) :45950-45954, ZNet.TryGetPlayerByPlatformUserID client :81668); otherwise the message is dropped with a LogError and no line appears.
- The chat-log speaker name is playerInfo.m_name from the player list, never UserInfo.Name — 'Portal Network' cannot be the chat-log speaker; only floating text and the map pin honour the forged Name (WorldTextInstance.m_name :41531).
- All server messages share one world-text/pin slot because FindExistingWorldText keys on senderID = server's ZRoutedRpc.m_id (:41919-41928, :83581); successive messages overwrite each other rather than stacking.
- Ping beacon label is '<Name>: PING' with the text field ignored (:41898-41901, :57603) — encode the destination in Name.
- PlatformUserID(string) parsing is in the Splatform assembly (not decompiled); use a real online player's m_userInfo.m_id.ToString() rather than an invented id string.
- Enforcement is client-honoured (server sends, vanilla client renders); the RPC has no sender validation so any client can forge it equally.

### 172. Feedback: floating world text over a portal (RPC_DamageText)

`player-ux-no-client:Feedback: floating world text over a portal (RPC_DamageText)` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Arbitrary text hovering in 3D above any object within 30 m of the viewer, addressed to one player — the only surface that says WHICH portal changed.


**How it works:** `DamageText.Awake` registers the routed RPC `"RPC_DamageText"(ZPackage)` (:46352-46356). Payload is `{int TextType, Vector3 pos, string text, bool mySelf}`; `RPC_DamageText` localizes the string and hands it to `AddInworldText` (:46494-46510). Server side:

  var p = new ZPackage();
  p.Write((int)DamageText.TextType.Bonus);
  p.Write(portalPos + Vector3.up * 2.2f);
  p.Write("→ HALDOR");
  p.Write(false);
  ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_DamageText", p);

`TextType` is `Normal, Resistant, Weak, Immune, Heal, TooHard, Blocked, Bonus` (:46309-46319). `Bonus` is the attention-grabber — orange, 1.5× font, ~3 s. AVOID `TooHard` and `Blocked`: those branches overwrite or prefix the string with `$msg_toohard` / `$msg_blocked:`, mangling whatever you sent. `Heal` is green and reads as positive confirmation; `Immune`/`Weak` have distinct colours usable as a status palette.

CULLING: `m_maxTextDistance = 30f` (:46338) plus `Hud.IsUserHidden()`. Beyond 30 m nothing renders — strictly a 'label the thing in front of you' channel.

WHY USE IT over a toast: it is anchored in 3D to a specific object. With three portals side by side, a toast saying `Dialed → Haldor` does not tell you WHICH portal changed; a Bonus text over the middle one does. On entering a hub, push one DamageText per portal in range naming its current destination and the whole hub is annotated in-world for three seconds without hovering anything.

Strictly per-peer — send only to the player who acted, so a hub does not spam text for everyone standing there.


**Player experience:** You walk into your portal hall — six portals in a row in a stone building. You crouch (the arming gesture). For three seconds a line of orange text pops above each frame:

`→ BASE`   `→ HALDOR`   `→ MINE2`   `→ BOG`   `— UNLINKED —`   `LOCKED: VAULT`

Then it fades. You know instantly which door goes where without hovering six objects one at a time. You walk into the third one.

When you dial a portal, a green `→ HALDOR` floats up out of its frame — the same visual language as a heal number, which every player already reads as 'good thing happened here'.

The best surface in this list for disambiguating which object a command applied to, and it costs one small RPC.


**Failure modes:**
- 30 m culling (`m_maxTextDistance`, :46338) means nothing renders for a distant portal — useless for remote feedback.
- `TextType.TooHard` overwrites the string with `$msg_toohard` and `Blocked` prefixes `$msg_blocked:` — both mangle the payload.
- Text is localized on the client, so a raw string containing a `$` prefix that happens to match a token is substituted unexpectedly.
- Broadcasting instead of per-peer spams everyone standing at a hub.
- The payload is hand-packed into a ZPackage; a field-order mistake produces garbage with no error.

**Designer citations:** DamageText.Awake registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46352-46356 ; DamageText.ShowText / RPC_DamageText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46486-46510 ; DamageText.AddInworldText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46395-46445 ; DamageText.TextType enum — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46309-46319 ; DamageText.m_maxTextDistance — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:46338


**Open questions:**
- Does `Bonus` text render legibly against a lit portal at 2.2 m above the frame, or does it clip into the portal's own emissive glow? Purely visual. IN-GAME: push one and look.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Distance cull is camera-to-point (:46503), not player-to-point; third-person camera offset matters at the 30 m edge.
- Font size is 8 px beyond 10 m from the camera (m_smallFontDistance :46421-46428) and 16 px (x1.5 for Bonus) inside it — annotate hubs from close range or the labels are barely legible.
- Position is randomly jittered by up to 0.5 m per call (:46402); anchor slightly higher than intended.
- Text passes Localization.Localize (:46405) and keeps TMP rich text — '$' tokens will expand; Chat's '<' '>' mangling does not apply here.
- Enforcement: client-honoured (client-rendered), not server-enforced.
- Only TextType.Bonus lasts 3 s; all other types last m_textDuration = 1.5 s (:46333, :46437-46440).
- Heal prefixes '+' to the string (:46432-46434) — a Heal-typed '→ HALDOR' renders as '+→ HALDOR'.
- Font size is 8 pt beyond m_smallFontDistance = 10 m from the camera (12 pt for Bonus), 16/24 pt inside it (:46335-46336, :46420-46427); far hub portals get small labels.
- Position is jittered by Random.insideUnitSphere * 0.5f (:46402) and the 30 m cull is measured from the camera, not the player (:46504).
- Enforcement is client-honoured, not server-enforced; the RPC has no sender validation.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited member exists with the claimed signature and behaviour. DamageText.Awake registers 'RPC_DamageText'(ZPackage) on ZRoutedRpc (:46352-46356). ShowText writes {int type, Vector3 pos, string text, bool player} (:46486-46494). RPC_DamageText (:46495-46510) requires a main camera and !Hud.IsUserHidden(), culls at m_maxTextDistance = 30f (:46338) measured from the CAMERA not the player, and calls AddInworldText. AddInworldText (:46395-46445): Localization.Localize(text), colour table matches the option (Bonus = (1,0.63,0.24)), TooHard replaces the string with $msg_toohard, Blocked prefixes '$msg_blocked: ', Heal prefixes '+', Bonus multiplies font size by 1.5 and sets duration 3 s. Each call creates a NEW WorldTextInstance (no per-sender slot as in Chat), so pushing one label per portal works. Unlisted details: position is jittered by Random.insideUnitSphere*0.5 (:46402); font drops to m_smallFontSize=8 when the camera is farther than m_smallFontDistance=10 m (:46421-46428), so labels across a large hub are tiny; the string passes through Localization.Localize so '$' tokens expand and TMP rich text is NOT stripped (unlike Chat). The mySelf flag only matters for types <= Immune and when sender == ZNet.GetUID(); pass false. Server needs no DamageText.instance: targeted InvokeRoutedRPC never runs locally (:83566-83573). Enforcement relabelled: client-rendered feedback.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Mechanism verified end to end. DamageText.Awake registers `RPC_DamageText`(ZPackage) on ZRoutedRpc (:46352-46356); RPC_DamageText (:46494-46510) requires a main camera and !Hud.IsUserHidden(), reads {int type, Vector3 pos, string text, bool mySelf}, culls at `Vector3.Distance(camera.position, pos) > m_maxTextDistance (30f, :46338)` — distance is measured from the CAMERA, not the player — and calls AddInworldText (:46395-46445). AddInworldText: Localizes the string, jitters position by `Random.insideUnitSphere * 0.5f` (:46402), colours per TextType (Bonus = (1,0.63,0.24), Heal = (0.5,1,0.5,0.7)), and chooses font size by distance: `m_smallFontSize (8) if distance > m_smallFontDistance (10f) else m_largeFontSize (16)` (:46420-46427). Bonus multiplies by 1.5 and sets duration 3 s (:46437-46440); every other type uses m_textDuration = 1.5 s (:46333), not 3 s. Heal prefixes '+' (:46432-46434) so a Heal-typed '→ HALDOR' renders as '+→ HALDOR'; TooHard replaces the text entirely and Blocked prefixes '$msg_blocked: ' (:46429-46436) — the option's warning is right. Text rises 1 m/s and fades with alpha = 1 - (t/duration)^3 (:46370-46380). The `mySelf` red override only applies when `flag && sender == ZNet.GetUID()` (:46506) and type <= Immune — send false. Practical consequences for the 'annotate a six-portal hub' use: beyond 10 m from the camera the text is 8 pt (12 pt for Bonus), so labels on far portals in a large hall are small; the 0.5 m random jitter means side-by-side portals' labels can drift toward each other. Per-peer targeting via InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, ...) is real (:83577-83596, RouteRPC delivers only to the target peer :83598-83608). Enforcement: the client renders whatever it receives; nothing is enforced, and the RPC has no sender check (vanilla's own ShowText broadcasts to 0L :46486-46493), so it is client-honoured.

### 173. Feedback: status effect as a persistent state indicator

`player-ux-no-client:Feedback: status effect as a persistent state indicator` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The server grants a vanilla status effect so the player carries a buff icon representing portal state — the only indicator that survives walking away from the portal.


**How it works:** `SEMan` registers `"RPC_AddStatusEffect"(int nameHash, bool resetTime, int itemLevel, float skillLevel, int variant)` on the character's own ZNetView (SEMan shares `Character.m_nview`) (:28724-28729). Server: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "RPC_AddStatusEffect", nameHash, true, 0, 0f, -1)`. `Internal_AddStatusEffect` (:28831-28850) resolves the hash purely against the RECEIVING client's own `ObjectDB.m_StatusEffects`, so only effects every vanilla client already ships can be granted. Wonderland ships this as `StatusEffectRpc.Grant` (Core/Data/StatusEffectRpc.cs:27) with a `StatusEffectRegistry` keyed on `effect.name` (not `m_name`).

WHAT IT BUYS: a persistent, always-visible UI element where the player is already trained to look — the buff bar — with an icon and a countdown, that survives walking away. Nothing else in the zero-client toolkit gives persistent per-player UI state.

THE HARD LIMIT: there is NO RemoveStatusEffect RPC anywhere in the assembly. A granted effect can only be allowed to expire. So the vocabulary is restricted to short, self-expiring effects, and 'armed' must be a re-pinged short buff rather than a toggle. `BuffRosterEngine` is the reference re-ping loop: `RepingInterval = clamp(ttl*0.4, 0.2, ttl-0.2)`, decremented by real frame dt (Wonderland Subsystems/StatusEffects/BuffRosterEngine.cs:121).

The semantics are borrowed, not authored: granting `Rested` to mean 'armed' is a lie the game acts on (it actually gives regen). Pick effects whose mechanical side-effect is harmless or thematically apt — an asset question, not a code one.


**Player experience:** You crouch near a portal. A new icon appears in your buff bar with a short timer. You now know, without looking at the portal or reading anything, that the server is listening — and the timer tells you how long before it stops.

You pick a destination and stand up; the icon fades. You walk through the portal. On arrival a different icon appears for ten seconds — the server's way of saying 'this trip was logged'.

Honestly the weakest feedback channel here. The icon has a vanilla meaning players already know, and using `Rested` to mean 'portal armed' confuses people who then wonder why they are getting regen. Its one real strength is persistence — the only indicator that stays on screen after you stop looking at the portal — so it is worth exactly one slot, for the armed state, and nothing else.


**Failure modes:**
- No RemoveStatusEffect RPC exists — an effect can only expire, so every state must be modelled as a re-pinged short buff.
- Effect semantics are borrowed: any effect chosen carries its real gameplay side-effect (regen, resistance, movement) which the player will notice and misattribute.
- Only effects present in the client's `ObjectDB.m_StatusEffects` can be granted; no novel icon or name is possible.
- `ObjectDB.instance` is frequently still null at the ZNetScene.Awake 'world ready' hook (live-confirmed in Wonderland 2026-09-11) — any registry build must retry per tick until it resolves.
- A re-ping loop that stalls leaves the icon showing a stale state for up to the effect's full TTL.

**Designer citations:** SEMan ctor "RPC_AddStatusEffect" registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:28724-28729 ; SEMan.AddStatusEffect non-owner branch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:28815-28821 ; SEMan.RPC_AddStatusEffect / Internal_AddStatusEffect — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:28823-28850 ; Wonderland StatusEffectRpc.Grant — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/StatusEffectRpc.cs:27 ; Wonderland BuffRosterEngine re-ping — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/StatusEffects/BuffRosterEngine.cs:121


**Open questions:**
- Is there a vanilla status effect with a near-zero mechanical side-effect and a neutral icon, suitable as a pure indicator? This is asset data. IN-GAME: enumerate `ObjectDB.instance.m_StatusEffects` and inspect each one's tooltip and modifiers.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Restrict to effects with m_ttl > 0: StatusEffect.IsDone() only expires when m_ttl > 0 (see IsDone), so a ttl-0 effect granted via RPC can never be removed by the server — a permanent, irreversible footgun. BuffRosterEngine's 120 s re-ping for ttl<=0 effects (:112) is not a mitigation for this.
- SEMan.AddStatusEffect(StatusEffect,...) runs statusEffect.CanAdd(m_character) (:28866) — virtual, subclass overrides may reject silently; the server gets no result back.
- Only effects with a non-null m_icon render in the buff bar; verify the asset, not just the name.
- Enforcement: client-honoured (owner-side IsOwner/CanAdd gate, client-rendered), not server-enforced.
- Effect duration is the asset's m_ttl; the server cannot set or shorten it. The buff-bar countdown reflects m_ttl, not the mod's arming window, unless the two are deliberately matched.
- The icon does not fade when the player stands up; it persists until m_ttl elapses after the last re-ping (no removal RPC exists — verified by grep of all Register calls).
- resetTime:true on an already-active vanilla effect (e.g. Rested) resets its timer and extends the real buff (Internal_AddStatusEffect :28833-28840).
- Every fresh grant fires the effect's m_startMessage and start effects (StatusEffect.Setup :31079-31086).
- Only effects with m_ttl > 0 self-expire (IsDone :31173-31179); an m_ttl == 0 effect granted by mistake is permanent until relog.
- Enforcement is client-honoured, not server-enforced.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] SEMan ctor registers 'RPC_AddStatusEffect'<int,bool,int,float,int> on the character's ZNetView (:28724-28729). AddStatusEffect non-owner branch invokes it (:28815-28821); RPC_AddStatusEffect is gated on m_nview.IsOwner() (:28823-28829) which is true on the player's own client; Internal_AddStatusEffect resolves via ObjectDB.instance.GetStatusEffect(nameHash) on the receiver (:28831-28850) and either ResetTime()s an existing instance or adds a Clone after CanAdd (:28852-28880). Delivery: routed RPC with targetZDO = character ZDOID reaches ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC on the client (:83646-83664 -> :82838-82848), no ownership filter at the dispatcher. The 'no remove RPC' claim is confirmed: grep finds only 'RPC_AddStatusEffect' as a status-effect RPC; RemoveStatusEffect (:28882+) is a local call with no network path. Wonderland StatusEffectRpc.Grant (:27) and BuffRosterEngine RepingInterval (:112-114) match. Corrections: StatusEffect.IsDone() returns true only when m_ttl > 0 && m_time > m_ttl — an effect with m_ttl == 0 granted this way is PERMANENT on that character with no removal path at all (until the client-side code that owns it removes it), so the vocabulary must be restricted to finite-ttl effects; CanAdd is virtual and some subclasses reject; an effect with no m_icon shows nothing in the buff bar. Enforcement relabelled: the owner client decides (IsOwner, CanAdd) and renders.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Wire path verified: SEMan ctor registers `RPC_AddStatusEffect`(int,bool,int,float,int) on the Character's ZNetView (:28724-28729); RPC_AddStatusEffect gates on m_nview.IsOwner() (:28823-28829) which is true for the recipient's own Player; Internal_AddStatusEffect resolves via ObjectDB.instance.GetStatusEffect(nameHash) on the receiving client (:28831-28850) and, if already present with resetTime, calls ResetTime() (m_time = 0, :31182-31185). AddStatusEffect(StatusEffect,...) clones, calls CanAdd (virtual, default true :31074-31077) and Setup (:31079-31086), which fires m_startMessage via Character.Message and TriggerStartEffects. A grep of every Register call finds no removal RPC — only `RPC_AddStatusEffect` (:28728) and Character's `RPC_UpdateEffects` (:139442, unrelated) — so the 'no RemoveStatusEffect RPC' claim is confirmed. IsDone = `m_ttl > 0 && m_time > m_ttl` (:31173-31179). Wonderland's StatusEffectRpc.Grant (Core/Data/StatusEffectRpc.cs:27-42) and BuffRosterEngine's RepingInterval formula (Subsystems/StatusEffects/BuffRosterEngine.cs:111-114) exist as cited. Corrections to the player experience: (1) duration is owned by the asset's m_ttl, not the server — the icon countdown shows the effect's own TTL, so 'the timer tells you how long before it stops [listening]' is only true if the mod's arming window is set equal to the chosen effect's m_ttl; (2) 'You pick a destination and stand up; the icon fades' is false — the server cannot remove it, so it persists for the full m_ttl after the last re-ping; (3) resetTime:true on an effect the player ALREADY has (e.g. Rested from a bed) resets its timer to zero each ping and thereby EXTENDS the real buff (:28833-28840), a mechanical side-effect beyond the icon; (4) every first grant fires the effect's m_startMessage and start effects (:31081-31085), so each arming pings a vanilla message like the effect's own toast; (5) the mod must ship a vetted list of vanilla effects with short m_ttl > 0, an icon, and harmless m_attributes/SE_Stats — effects with m_ttl == 0 never expire client-side (IsDone :31174) and would become permanent until relog. The RPC routes to a ZDO (HandleRoutedRPC → ZNetScene.FindInstance → ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC :83645-83664), which always succeeds for the player's own character. Enforcement: client-honoured (the client applies the effect from its own ObjectDB; nothing is enforced; any client can send the same RPC to any character ZDO — no sender check).
