### 174. Feedback: forced teleport as the delivery mechanism

`player-ux-no-client:Feedback: forced teleport as the delivery mechanism` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Skip the portal entirely — the server moves the player with a routed RPC, visually indistinguishable from a portal transit, but bypassing every vanilla rule.


**How it works:** TWO INDEPENDENT PATHS against a 100% vanilla client.
(A) `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_TeleportPlayer", pos, rot, true)` — `Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer` is `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport);` with no sender, admin, key or item check (:41962-41968), registered in `Chat.Awake` on every client (:41627). The server needs no `Chat.instance`: `Chat.TeleportPlayer` is a one-line wrapper (:41957-41960) and `InvokeRoutedRPC` with `targetPeerID != m_id` never touches a local handler.
(B) `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, peer.m_characterID, "RPC_TeleportTo", pos, rot, true)` — `Character.RPC_TeleportTo` is registered on every Character in `Character.Awake` (:886) and gates on `m_nview.IsOwner()` (:4126-4132), so it can only move that character on its own owner.

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE A PORTAL: `Hud.UpdateBlackScreen` picks the teleport swirl purely from `ShowTeleportAnimation()` = `m_teleporting && m_distantTeleport` (:47872, :15386), and `TeleportWorld.Teleport` passes `distantTeleport: true` (:143546). A forced teleport with `true` is byte-for-byte the same experience — same black screen, same swirl, same ~8 s duration. Nothing to add, nothing missing.

ALWAYS PASS TRUE. With `false`, if `ZoneSystem.FindFloor` misses at the destination the client rubber-bands the player back to the origin and shows `$msg_portal_blocked` (:15369-15374) — a lie that will be reported as a mod bug. With `true` it cannot fail: the 15 s fallback force-lands on `GetSolidHeight + 0.5` (:15360-15366).

MANDATORY SERVER PRE-CHECKS, all off the character ZDO: `GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)` (:78403) — `UpdateTeleport` runs only inside the `!IsDead()` branch of `Player.FixedUpdate` (:10213, :10226), so a teleport to a dead player latches `m_teleporting` and never executes. `GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed)` (:78457) — `UpdateAttach` (:10217) runs BEFORE `UpdateTeleport` (:10226) and re-snaps to the attach point every tick, and `AttachStop` early-returns while `m_sleeping` (:15892), so a sleeping player is stuck outright. And your own cooldown table: `Player.TeleportTo` returns false with NO message if `IsTeleporting()` or `m_teleportCooldown < 2f` (:15309-15316), and the cooldown is zeroed every tick while teleporting (:15331-15336), so the real dead window is the whole ~8 s trip plus 2 s. `m_teleporting` is a private compiled bool never written to any ZDO (:9901) — the server can NEVER see it. Space forced teleports ≥12 s.


**Player experience:** You crouch at the portal, pick Haldor, and instead of walking through the frame the screen goes black with the same swirling teleport animation you have seen a thousand times. Eight seconds later you are standing outside Haldor's tent. If you did not know a mod was involved you would assume you had walked into a portal.

The difference you might notice: you did it carrying a full stack of iron and nothing stopped you.

Try again immediately and nothing at all happens — no message, no error, no swirl. That is vanilla's 2-second cooldown silently eating the request, and the server has no way to know. A good mod tracks its own send times and says `Wait 9s` instead of leaving you confused.

Best used NOT as the primary movement — walking into a portal is more satisfying and free — but as the escape hatch: 'send me home', the admin rescue, the 'you fell out of the world' recovery.


**Failure modes:**
- Bypasses `NoPortals`, `NoBossPortals`, ward checks and `Inventory.IsTeleportable` entirely; every rule must be re-implemented, and the ore check CANNOT be because the server never holds the player's inventory.
- Silent failure in both directions: `TeleportTo` returns false, both handlers discard it (:41966, :4130), and no reply is ever sent. The only after-the-fact signal is the character ZDO position changing ~2 s later.
- The cooldown window is the whole teleport plus 2 s (≥10 s), not 2 s after the RPC — anything retrying faster burns every retry.
- A dead player latches `m_teleporting` true and never advances; check `ZDOVars.s_dead` first.
- An attached player ping-pongs between attach point and target every tick; a sleeping one is stuck outright. Check `ZDOVars.s_inBed`.
- `distantTeleport: false` rubber-bands the player back with a misleading `$msg_portal_blocked`.

**Designer citations:** Chat.TeleportPlayer / RPC_TeleportPlayer — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41957-41968, registration :41627 ; Character.Awake "RPC_TeleportTo" registration / RPC_TeleportTo — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:886, :4126-4132 ; Player.TeleportTo — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15302-15327 ; Player.UpdateTeleport — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15329-15378 ; Player.FixedUpdate (UpdateAttach before UpdateTeleport, !IsDead gate) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:10213-10226 ; Player.ShowTeleportAnimation / Hud.UpdateBlackScreen — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15386-15393, :47855-47880 ; TeleportWorld.Teleport distantTeleport:true — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143546 ; ZDOVars.s_dead / s_inBed — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78403, :78457 ; Player.AttachStop (m_sleeping early-return) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15890-15918


**Open questions:**
- Does a vanilla client complete a forced distantTeleport into a never-visited, ungenerated zone within the 15 s fallback on low-end hardware? The gates are clear in code but terrain-generation latency is empirical. IN-GAME: force-teleport a test player 8 km into unexplored Ashlands and time the black screen; confirm no fall damage and no '$msg_portal_blocked'.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- s_inBed only covers beds (AttachStart sets it to isBed, :15799). UpdateAttach (:15818-15836) re-snaps for every attach kind. Pre-check the animator ints ZSyncAnimation writes: zdo.GetInt(438569 + Animator.StringToHash(<attach anim>)) (:87278-87279) for attach_chair, attach_bed, attach_sitship/attach_lox and the other attach_* names used by Chair/Sadle/Ship components.
- The trip is >= 8 s AND ZNetScene.IsAreaReady(target) (:15351; IsAreaReady = zone loaded + every valid sector ZDO instantiated), capped by the 15 s fallback — not a fixed ~8 s.
- Enforcement: client-honoured. Player.TeleportTo's IsTeleporting/m_teleportCooldown rejections (:15309-15316) are local and invisible to the server.
- Forced teleport does not increment PlayerStatType.PortalsUsed (only TeleportWorld.Teleport does, :143547) — cosmetic.
- A sleeping player is deferred, not stuck: Game.SleepStop → SetSleeping(false) + AttachStop (:100761-100767) lets the latched teleport complete on waking.
- s_inBed only covers beds (AttachStart sets s_inBed = isBed :15799); chair/throne attachment also blocks the teleport via UpdateAttach re-snapping (:15820-15837) and prevents IsAreaReady from ever passing. Read the ZSyncAnimation bool keys (438569 + Animator.StringToHash('attach_chair'/'attach_bed'/...) — ZSyncAnimation.SetBool :87271-87281) to detect all attach states.
- Distant teleport duration is >= 8 s AND gated on ZNetScene.IsAreaReady(target) (:15348, :82064-82080); it can exceed 8 s and can hang indefinitely if the target area never becomes ready.
- The player transform is moved at t = 2 s (:15342-15347), not at the end of the swirl; a server-side position watcher must whitelist the jump.
- Minimum safe spacing is 8 s + 2 s cooldown = 10 s; 12 s is a margin, not a derived constant.
- Enforcement is client-honoured: the client decides whether to execute (cooldown, IsTeleporting, dead, attached) and can silently drop the request; the RPC also has no sender check so any client can teleport any other player.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Both paths verified. (A) Chat.Awake registers 'RPC_TeleportPlayer'<Vector3,Quaternion,bool> (:41627); RPC_TeleportPlayer is exactly 'if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport)' (:41962-41968); Chat.TeleportPlayer wrapper (:41957-41960); targeted InvokeRoutedRPC never runs locally (:83566-83573). (B) Character.Awake registers 'RPC_TeleportTo' (:886); RPC_TeleportTo gates on m_nview.IsOwner() (:4126-4132). Player.TeleportTo (:15302-15327): returns false silently on IsTeleporting() or m_teleportCooldown < 2f; sets m_teleporting/m_distantTeleport. UpdateTeleport (:15329-15378): zeroes cooldown while teleporting, moves the transform at >2 s, requires (timer > 8 || !distant) AND ZNetScene.IsAreaReady(target); FindFloor success ends it; else at >15 s distant lands at GetSolidHeight+0.5, non-distant rubber-bands with $msg_portal_blocked. Hud.UpdateBlackScreen picks the teleport progress panel from ShowTeleportAnimation() = m_teleporting && m_distantTeleport (:47852-47875, :15386-15393). TeleportWorld.Teleport passes distantTeleport: true (:143546). FixedUpdate ordering UpdateAttach (:10217) before UpdateTeleport (:10226) inside !IsDead() (:10213) confirmed. m_teleporting is a private bool (:9901). ZDOVars.s_dead :78403, s_inBed :78457 confirmed; s_dead is written by Player.OnDeath (:12734). Corrections: the s_inBed pre-check is insufficient — Player.UpdateAttach (:15818-15836) re-snaps for ANY attach (chair, bench, ship attach point, sadle), and AttachStart only sets s_inBed when isBed (:15799). Non-bed attaches are not sleeping so AttachStop is not blocked, but until the player stands up the forced teleport is overwritten every FixedUpdate. The attach state IS visible to the server: AttachStart calls m_zanim.SetBool(attachAnimation, true) and ZSyncAnimation.SetBool writes the animator bool to the ZDO as an int at key 438569 + Animator.StringToHash(name) (:87278-87279, session hash), so the server should pre-check GetInt(438569 + Animator.StringToHash('attach_chair'/'attach_bed'/'attach_sitship'/etc.)) != 0. Also the 8 s is a minimum: UpdateTeleport also waits on IsAreaReady (:15351, :zone loaded + all sector ZDOs instantiated), so a target in an unloaded/heavy zone runs longer, up to the 15 s fallback. Dead-latch note: Player.OnDeath sets s_dead and the object is replaced on respawn, so the latch only wastes the send. Enforcement: the client's Player.TeleportTo makes the cooldown/IsTeleporting decision and the server cannot observe it — client-honoured.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Both paths verified. (A) Chat.Awake registers RPC_TeleportPlayer (:41627); the handler is `if (Player.m_localPlayer != null) Player.m_localPlayer.TeleportTo(pos, rot, distantTeleport)` with no sender/admin check (:41962-41968); Chat.TeleportPlayer wrapper at :41957-41960. (B) Character.Awake registers RPC_TeleportTo (:886); handler gates on m_nview.IsOwner() (:4126-4132). Player.TeleportTo (:15302-15327): returns false silently if IsTeleporting() or m_teleportCooldown < 2f; sets m_teleporting/m_distantTeleport. UpdateTeleport (:15329-15378): cooldown zeroed each tick while teleporting; at timer > 2 s the transform is MOVED to the target (:15342-15347); then `if ((!(timer > 8f) && distant) || !ZNetScene.IsAreaReady(target)) return;` — so a distant teleport lasts at least 8 s AND until the target area is ready (IsAreaReady :82064 requires the zone loaded and every valid ZDO in it instantiated); then FindFloor, else at timer > 15 s the distant branch lands on GetSolidHeight + 0.5 with no message, while the non-distant branch rubber-bands and shows $msg_portal_blocked (:15355-15375). Vanilla TeleportWorld.Teleport passes distantTeleport: true (:143546); Hud.UpdateBlackScreen shows the teleport swirl from ShowTeleportAnimation() = m_teleporting && m_distantTeleport (:47855-47875, :15386-15393) — so the visual claim holds. Corrections: (1) Sleeping is NOT 'stuck outright' — it is deferred: UpdateAttach (:15820-15837) re-snaps the transform every FixedUpdate while m_attached, and AttachStop early-returns while m_sleeping (:15890-15894), but Game.SleepStop calls SetSleeping(false) then AttachStop (:100761-100767), after which the still-latched m_teleporting completes normally (the swirl replaces the sleep screen; UpdateBlackScreen prefers IsSleeping first :47869). (2) The `s_inBed` pre-check is insufficient: AttachStart writes `s_inBed = isBed` (:15799), which is false for chairs/thrones/benches, yet m_attached is true and UpdateAttach snaps the player back every tick, and because the player is snapped back to the chair the client never loads the target zone, so IsAreaReady never passes and the teleport hangs until the player presses a movement key (AttachStop via input :16020-16027). The server CAN see attach state: ZSyncAnimation.SetBool writes the animator bool into the ZDO at int key `438569 + Animator hash` (:87271-87281) and AttachStart calls m_zanim.SetBool(attachAnimation, true) (:15798) with names like 'attach_chair' (:17904, :119499, :120770) and 'attach_bed' (:119721) — check those keys, not only s_inBed. (3) The transform jumps to the target at 2 s, six seconds before the swirl ends; a server-side position-anomaly watcher (Wonderland PositionWatch) sees the jump at t+2 s and must be told to expect it. (4) The dead gate is confirmed: UpdateTeleport only runs inside the !IsDead() branch (:10213-10226) and s_dead is written by Player at :12734/:12866. (5) `IsAreaReady` failing forever (target outside the world, or a zone the client cannot instantiate) leaves the player black-screened indefinitely — the same failure mode as vanilla, so validate the destination. (6) Security: RPC_TeleportPlayer and RPC_TeleportTo have no sender check — any connected client can forcibly teleport any other player; the mod does not create this hole but should not present the channel as server-controlled. Enforcement: the CLIENT executes the move and can silently drop it (cooldown, already teleporting, dead, attached); nothing is enforced server-side, so client-honoured. Minimum spacing 8 s + 2 s = 10 s; the option's ≥12 s is a sensible margin only while IsAreaReady passes promptly.

### 175. Feedback: global keys as a world-wide state signal (and their silence)

`player-ux-no-client:Feedback: global keys as a world-wide state signal (and their silence)` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Server-set global keys that a vanilla client honours exactly as it honours vanilla's own boss gating — the only truly global lever, and it comes with no UI at all.


**How it works:** `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string)` is a one-liner over `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name)` (:115943-115946); on the server the target resolves to itself, `RPC_SetGlobalKey` runs synchronously (:116022-116029) and calls `SendGlobalKeys(0L)`, broadcasting the WHOLE key set (:113466-113471). Each client's `RPC_GlobalKeys` clears and rebuilds its local set (:113473-113481). One routed-RPC hop, no timer — connected players update essentially instantly, no relog.

KEYS: `NoPortals` (32), `NoBossPortals` (33), `DungeonBuild` (34), `TeleportAll` (35) — all below `NonServerOption` (41), so `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors them into `ZNet.World.m_startingGlobalKeys`, persists them in the .fwl and shows them in the browser modifiers badge (:113483-113513). For a SESSION-ONLY key, call the publicized `GlobalKeyAdd(key, canSaveToServerOptionKeys: false)` + `SendGlobalKeys(0L)` instead of `SetGlobalKey`.

READS: `TeleportWorld.Teleport` checks `NoPortals` → `$msg_blocked` and `NoBossPortals && (GetBossEvent() != null || activeBosses > 0)` → `$msg_blockedbyboss`, both LIVE at the instant of transit (:143523, :143528). `Inventory.IsTeleportable` honours `TeleportAll` (:68869) — but only AFTER rejecting any item with `m_shared.m_toolTier >= 1000` (:68862-68868), so it is not 'allow everything'.

THE UX PROBLEM, and it is severe: A VANILLA CLIENT GIVES NO WARNING. `GetHoverText` reports only connected/unconnected from `HaveTarget()` (:143453-143463) and `UpdatePortal` lights `m_target_found` purely from `IsTeleportable && TargetFound()` (:143491-143508). Neither consults either key. With `noportals` set, every portal still LOOKS connected and still glows; the player discovers the block only by walking in and getting a centre-screen `$msg_blocked`. Any affordance beyond that must come from the mod: a tag rewrite to `!CLOSED`, a sign banner, a toast on approach, or actually nulling the ZDO connections so portals visibly read `[Unconnected]`.

SECURITY: `RPC_SetGlobalKey` and `RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` have ZERO sender validation (:116022-116037). Any connected vanilla client can set or clear `noportals`/`teleportall` at will. A lockdown on these keys is one packet from being lifted unless the mod Harmony-prefixes both RPCs to drop non-server senders.


**Player experience:** A boss fight starts somewhere on the server. Every portal everywhere stops working, including yours 4 km away with no boss in sight. Your portal still glows blue and still says `[Connected]`. You walk into it and a red banner flashes: `Portals are blocked by a boss.` You walk in again to check. Same banner. No way to tell how long or why.

That is vanilla. With the mod layered on, the moment the key flips your portal's tag is rewritten to `!BOSS` and a toast reads `Portals closed: Bonemass is awake (4,100m SW). Reopens when the fight ends.` The glow is unchanged — the server cannot touch that — but you know exactly what happened.

The clearest case in this document of the mod's real job being to ADD THE MISSING FEEDBACK to a vanilla mechanism that is otherwise silently confusing.


**Failure modes:**
- Zero client-side affordance: portals still glow and read [Connected] while blocked (:143453-143508). The mod must supply every signal itself.
- `RPC_SetGlobalKey`/`RPC_RemoveGlobalKey` accept any sender (:116022-116037) — any client can lift a lockdown.
- `SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.NoPortals)` stringifies to PascalCase `"NoPortals"` while the store holds lowercase, so `RPC_SetGlobalKey`'s dedupe guard never trips and every call re-broadcasts the whole key list. Pass lowercase literals or pre-check with `GetGlobalKey`.
- Setting a portal key at runtime permanently edits the world: `GlobalKeyAdd` mirrors ordinals <41 into `m_startingGlobalKeys` (:113511) which is written to the .fwl at the next autosave. Removing the mod later leaves `noportals` baked in.
- `ZoneSystem.SetStartingGlobalKeys` wipes ordinals 0..40 on every world load (:115906-115910); mod-owned keys must be reapplied in a POSTFIX on it.
- `NoBossPortals` is a world-wide blackout the moment ANY boss anywhere is alerted, and `activeBosses` is maintained by whichever client has the boss loaded — a crash mid-fight can leave it stuck above zero and portals permanently blocked.
- `TeleportAll` does not lift the `m_toolTier >= 1000` gate (:68862-68868).

### 176. Feedback: server-driven VFX/SFX at the portal

`player-ux-no-client:Feedback: server-driven VFX/SFX at the portal` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The server broadcasts `"SpawnObject"` with a vanilla effect prefab hash and a vanilla client plays it locally — the only non-textual acknowledgement available.


**How it works:** `ZNetScene.Awake` registers the routed RPC `"SpawnObject"(Vector3 pos, Quaternion rot, int prefabHash)` (:81954); `RPC_SpawnObject` does a bare `UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(GetPrefab(prefabHash), pos, rot)` and logs `"Missing prefab <hash>"` on an unknown hash (:82355-82366). Server: `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "SpawnObject", pos, rot, "vfx_name".GetStableHashCode())`. Wonderland ships this working in `VacuumEngine.PlayVacuumEffect` (Subsystems/ItemFlow/VacuumEngine.cs:162, RPC at :199) with `vfx_fermenter_add` / `sfx_fermenter_add`, sent per-peer to everyone within 80 m.

NEVER use a ZNetView-bearing prefab — each recipient would independently Instantiate and create a duplicate ZDO. Effect prefabs (`vfx_*`, `sfx_*`) are non-networked and safe. A server-side `Object.Instantiate` of an effect reaches nobody, so the RPC is the only path.

USE: a flare when a hub rotates, a puff when a portal locks, a sound cue confirming a gesture. This matters most for gesture inputs (jump, crouch, emote) where a corner toast is easy to miss while you are watching your own character.

IMPORTANT NON-CAPABILITY: the portal's own visual state is untouchable. `TeleportWorld.m_connected` (EffectList) and `m_target_found` (EffectFade) are driven by `UpdatePortal` on a 0.5 s `InvokeRepeating` reading `HaveTarget()` and `Player.GetClosestPlayer(...).IsTeleportable(...)` (:143491-143508), and `Update` lerps `m_colorAlpha` into the model's `_EmissionColor` (:143511-143515) — all plain Inspector references with zero networking. The server cannot make a portal glow or change colour directly.

BUT THERE IS AN INDIRECT PATH WORTH USING: `UpdatePortal` fires `m_connected.Create(...)` when `HaveTarget()` newly flips true (:143497-143500). So nulling and re-establishing a portal's ZDO connection makes every nearby client replay the portal's own 'connected' effect, in the portal's own visual language, within 0.5 s.


**Player experience:** You jump three times in front of your portal. Rather than squinting at a corner toast, you hear a soft chime and see a small puff of particles at the portal's base each time your selection advances. When you commit, a bigger flare goes off and the portal's own blue connection effect fires — the same one you see when a portal first links up — because the server briefly cleared and reset the connection.

It reads as the portal responding to you, in the portal's own visual language, with no HUD involved. The closest this toolkit ever gets to feeling like a designed feature rather than a bolted-on mod.


**Failure modes:**
- Using a ZNetView-bearing prefab creates one duplicate ZDO per recipient — permanent world pollution.
- An unknown hash silently logs `"Missing prefab"` on the client and plays nothing; the server gets no error.
- Effect prefab names are Unity asset data; a name that exists on the client may not resolve on the server for hashing purposes (hashing is name-based so it does not matter, but choosing a name requires a client-side dump).
- The indirect 'replay the connect effect' trick costs a real connection round-trip — nulling a connection makes the portal briefly unusable and, if `Game.ConnectPortals` has not been prefixed out, invites vanilla to re-pair it randomly.
- Per-peer distance gating is the mod's job; broadcasting plays the effect for players nowhere near the portal.

**Designer citations:** ZNetScene.Awake "SpawnObject" registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81954 ; ZNetScene.RPC_SpawnObject — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82355-82366 ; ZNetScene.GetPrefab(int) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:82045-82052 ; TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal (m_connected fires on HaveTarget flip) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143491-143509 ; TeleportWorld.Update (_EmissionColor lerp) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143511-143515 ; Wonderland VacuumEngine.PlayVacuumEffect — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/ItemFlow/VacuumEngine.cs:162, :199

IN-GAME: send a portal-flavoured vanilla effect hash at a portal position and confirm it plays; also confirm whether the prefab must exist in the SERVER's `ZNetScene.m_prefabs` for the hash to be meaningful, or only the client's.
- Which `vfx_`/`sfx_` names resolve through `GetPrefab`? IN-GAME: dump `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefabNames()` (:82345) and grep for portal-adjacent effects.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- The connection-flap trick requires the client to observe the None state: the null must survive at least one ZDO sync to that peer and one 0.5 s UpdatePortal tick before re-establishing; a same-tick null+restore on the server produces no effect on the client.
- Side effects of the flap window: Teleport() early-returns on !TargetFound() (:143520-143523) so a player mid-walk-through is refused, hover text reads unconnected, and the emission colour lerps toward m_colorUnconnected at 1/s (:143513-143514) — visible if the window exceeds a few hundred ms.
- The flap races Game.ConnectPortals' 5 s reconciler (two-tick staged commit); either re-establish inside one reconciler period or let the reconciler do it and accept up to ~10 s latency.
- Enforcement: client-honoured (client-rendered), not server-enforced.
- The m_connected replay via null/re-set requires the None state to be visible for >= one 0.5 s UpdatePortal poll plus sync latency, during which Update dims the emission toward m_colorUnconnected (:143511-143515) and the portal is unusable; it is a flicker, not a free flare.
- The connection write must be made by the ZDO owner (vanilla routes clears through RPC_SetConnected when owner != 0, :143604-143629); with a player standing at the portal ReleaseNearbyZDOS will have handed ownership to that client, so a server-side direct write is not guaranteed to stick.
- Game.ConnectPortals (5 s) may re-pair the temporarily-None portal to a different same-tag portal before the mod restores it.
- SpawnObject has no receiver-side distance cull (:82355-82366); range gating is the sender's job.
- Enforcement is client-honoured, not server-enforced; no sender validation on SpawnObject.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] ZNetScene.Awake registers 'SpawnObject'<Vector3,Quaternion,int> (:81954) after adding m_nonNetViewPrefabs to m_namedPrefabs by name hash (:81950), so vfx_*/sfx_* effect prefabs are resolvable. RPC_SpawnObject (:82355-82366) is a bare GetPrefab(hash) + Object.Instantiate, logging 'Missing prefab' on miss; no distance or sender check. Targeted InvokeRoutedRPC never runs the server's own handler (:83566-83573). Wonderland VacuumEngine.PlayVacuumEffect matches (per-peer, 80 m, vfx_fermenter_add/sfx_fermenter_add; file :162-205). Non-capability claims verified: TeleportWorld.m_connected (EffectList), m_target_found (EffectFade), m_model, m_colorUnconnected/m_colorTargetfound are plain Inspector fields (:143408-143422); UpdatePortal (:143491-143509) fires m_connected.Create only on the HaveTarget() false->true edge tracked by the client-local m_hadTarget, and Update lerps m_colorAlpha toward m_hadTarget at 1/s into _EmissionColor (:143511-143515). The indirect 'null then re-establish' trick therefore works in principle, but with unlisted costs: the client's m_hadTarget must actually observe the None state, so the null window must span at least one ZDO sync to that client plus one 0.5 s UpdatePortal tick; during the window HaveTarget is false so hover reads $piece_portal_unconnected, TeleportWorld.Teleport early-returns on !TargetFound() (:143520-143523), and the emission dims toward m_colorUnconnected at 1/s; and Game.ConnectPortals reconciles unconnected portals every 5 s with a two-tick staged commit, so the mod must either re-establish before the reconciler's next pass or accept the reconciler re-pairing it (which does fire the same effect). Enforcement: client-rendered feedback.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Verified. ZNetScene.Awake adds every m_nonNetViewPrefabs entry to m_namedPrefabs (:81948-81951) and registers `SpawnObject`(Vector3, Quaternion, int) (:81954); RPC_SpawnObject does GetPrefab(hash) and a bare Object.Instantiate(prefab, pos, rot), logging 'Missing prefab' otherwise (:82355-82366); GetPrefab(int) is a m_namedPrefabs lookup (:82045-82052). Since m_namedPrefabs also contains every ZNetView prefab, the warning about duplicate ZDOs is correct — instantiating a networked prefab on each recipient would run ZNetView.Awake and create a ZDO per client. Wonderland's VacuumEngine.PlayVacuumEffect uses exactly this per-peer within 80 m of peer.GetRefPos() (VacuumEngine.cs:162-205). The portal-visuals non-capability is confirmed: UpdatePortal (:143491-143509) drives m_connected.Create on the HaveTarget() false→true edge and m_target_found from IsTeleportable && TargetFound(); Update lerps m_colorAlpha toward m_hadTarget at 1/s and writes _EmissionColor (:143511-143515); HaveTarget() is simply `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal) != ZDOID.None` on the client's ZDO copy (:143631-143638). The indirect 'null then re-set' replay therefore works in principle but with caveats the option omits: (1) the client must observe the None state on at least one 0.5 s UpdatePortal poll, so the server must hold the connection at None for > 0.5 s plus ZDO sync latency; during that window m_colorAlpha starts lerping toward m_colorUnconnected (visible dimming flicker) and the portal is genuinely unusable; (2) the write must be applied on the ZDO's owner — vanilla itself routes clears through RPC_SetConnected when the ZDO has a non-zero owner (:143604-143629), and per the HANDOFF ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands portal ownership to a nearby peer every 2 s, which is precisely the case here (a player standing at the portal); a non-owner write on the server does not reliably reach or survive the owner's copy; (3) Game.ConnectPortals runs every 5 s and treats a None connection as a candidate for re-pairing to any other same-tag portal, so the mod's re-set must beat that pass or own the tag topology; (4) RPC_SpawnObject has no distance cull on the receiving side — the recipient instantiates the effect wherever it is; SFX prefabs are 3D audio so distance attenuates naturally, but the sender must do the range gating (as VacuumEngine does). Enforcement: purely client-honoured — the client instantiates whatever it is told and there is no sender check on SpawnObject (any client can spawn effects on any other).

### 177. RECOMMENDED — "The Dial": tag CLI + sign terminal + map ping + gesture arming

`player-ux-no-client:RECOMMENDED — "The Dial": tag CLI + sign terminal + map ping + gesture arming` · domain **ux** · source `player-ux-no-client`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


One coherent scheme: the portal's own rename box is the command line, a wall of signs is the screen, the map ping is the pointer, crouch arms and jumps navigate — with tag echo, HUD toasts and in-world text as three feedback layers.


**How it works:** L0 — PAIRING TAKEOVER. Harmony prefix `Game.ConnectPortals` (:100589) returning false; re-implement its two passes over `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648) for UNMANAGED portals only, faithfully including the `m_currentlyConnectingPortals` guard (:100609) and the phase-0 force-commit (:100690). This removes the 5 s tag-equality teardown (:100601) that otherwise makes per-portal display tags impossible.

L1 — STATE. Address book `{name → (worldPos rounded to 0.5 m, ownerPlayerId, locked, wardPos)}` persisted to a per-world mod file (write-temp then File.Replace). NEVER key by ZDOID — `ZDO.Load` renumbers every uid (:74552), the exact bug TortalPortal's Favorites.cs hit and fixed by switching to rounded position. Re-resolve positions to live ZDOs from `GetPortalList()` each tick.

L2 — INPUT, four channels into one dispatcher.
(a) TAG CLI (primary). Postfix `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` (:74225), filter `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(GetPrefab())` (:100021), diff `GetString(ZDOVars.s_tag)`. Grammar ≤10 chars: `#NAME` name · `>NAME`/`>N` dial · `-` unlink · `!` lock · `?` help+directory · `@spawn`/`@haldor` world target.
(b) SIGN TERMINAL (rich). Same postfix on Sign prefabs, 50-char budget (:141756), full-word commands. The control sign is the lowest-y adopted sign within 8 m.
(c) MAP PING (freehand). Prefix `ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC` (:83646) on `"ChatMessage".GetStableHashCode()`, `type == 3`; snapshot/restore `m_parameters.GetPos()`. Route the player's last-touched portal to the nearest managed portal within 64 m of the ping x/z. Acts only while ARMED.
(d) GESTURE (hands-free). Prefix `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` (:83632) on `"SetTrigger"` for `"jump"` (:3483)/`"dodge"` (:15196); crouch bit from `characterZdo.GetInt(438569 + Animator.StringToHash("crouching"))` (:87144, :87270, :9984) at 0.2 s. Crouch within 6 m of a managed portal = ARM (15 s auto-disarm); jump = advance; un-crouch on a shown candidate = commit.

L3 — ACTION, one atomic routine: `SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())` (:74627/:77362) → `SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, destId)` (:73656) → `Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, echo)` (≤10 ASCII chars, no `<`) → `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702) → `ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid)` (:77706) → PRE-WARM `ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, destId)` (:77714) so `TargetFound()` (:143640) succeeds on the first walk-through. Budget bulk operations at ≤256 broadcasts per sweep (Wonderland StructureUpkeep's lesson).

L4 — OUTPUT, three layers per action: TAG ECHO (instant, in-context, persistent — `GetHoverText` reads the ZDO fresh each frame, :143453); TOAST via `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, characterZdoId, "Message", 1, text, 0)` (:10072, :14820) for the detail 10 chars cannot hold; WORLD TEXT via `"RPC_DamageText"` `TextType.Bonus` at `portalPos + up*2.2` (:46352, :46494) to say WHICH portal. Plus, once per (player, portal) at naming time only, `"RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse"` (:100068) for a saved map pin — never repeated, because no removal RPC exists.

PERMISSIONS from ward ZDO data: `s_creator` (:78393) + `s_permitted`/`pu_id<i>` (:78529, :137349). Never call `PrivateArea.CheckAccess` — `m_allAreas` is empty server-side and it is a silent allow-all (:137547).

DISCOVERABILITY, the honest weak point, attacked four ways: every unnamed portal gets its tag seeded to `?help`; `?` dumps the grammar as six toasts; the first sign built within 8 m of a managed portal is rewritten once into a help card; a one-line login toast `Portals: press E on any portal and type ? for help.` Four independent chances to stumble in, all inside the game.


**Player experience:** FIRST CONTACT. You log in. One line top-left: `Portals: press E on any portal and type ? for help.` You forget about it.

Later you build a portal. Hovering it, the tag reads `"?help"` — the server seeded it. You press E out of curiosity (the box is already familiar), clear it, type `?`, Enter. Six lines stack up:
`— PORTALS — you have 0 named` / `#name  name this portal` / `>name  dial to a portal` / `?  this help` / `- unlink   ! lock` / `or write a sign under it`

NAMING. You type `#Base`. The hover flips to `"#Base"` before you finish reading it. Toast: `Named: Base. Pin added to your map.` You open the map; a labelled pin sits at your base.

DIALLING. You run to your mine, build a portal, press E, type `>Base`, Enter. ~200 ms later the hover reads `">Base"`, the portal fires its blue connect effect, a toast reads `Dialed → Base · 840m · Meadows`, and an orange `→ BASE` floats over the frame for three seconds. You step through and it works first try — the destination ZDO was pre-sent.

GROWING INTO IT. Later, eleven portals. You build a column of four signs beside your hub and walk away; ten seconds later they show a live directory, page 1 of 3, updating whenever anyone changes anything. You write `dial Haldor and lock` on the bottom sign; it repaints to `→ HALDOR 1.2km LOCKED to you` and the portal follows.

SOMEWHERE NEW. You crouch at the portal (toast: `Armed`), press M, middle-click a spot in the Plains, close the map. Toast: `Dialed → Tarpit (3,410m).` You un-crouch. The arming step is what stops your hub re-routing itself every time someone pings during a raid.

HANDS FULL. Carrying a full load, you crouch at the hub and jump-jump-jump through the list watching the toast tick `1/6 Base`, `2/6 Haldor`, `3/6 Mine2`, then un-crouch on the one you want. Six seconds, no menu, no typing.

WHEN IT GOES WRONG. Typo: hover flips to `"?Halod"`, toast `No portal "Halod". Did you mean Haldor?`, nothing broke. Locked: hover reads `"!Vault"`, Center banner `Vault is locked by Bjorn.` Boss up: hover reads `"!BOSS"`, toast `Portals closed: Bonemass is awake. Reopens after the fight.` — feedback vanilla never gives you.

HONEST JANK RATING vs. a real client UI. The tag CLI is 3/10 — it reuses the exact vanilla interaction (press E on a portal, type a name) and only changes what the name MEANS, so it barely registers as a workaround. The sign terminal is 4/10 and genuinely charming. The ping is 2/10 and the fastest thing here. Crouch-and-jump is 7/10 and deliberately optional, for people who already know. TortalPortal's real client UI — a scrollable destination window with live 3D previews and favourites — is strictly better as an interface; what The Dial buys instead is that every player on the server gets it immediately with nothing to install, and the server is genuinely the authority rather than politely asking clients to behave.


**Failure modes:**
- Echo strings >10 chars are truncated in the rename dialog and can be re-submitted as garbage commands; the parser must also be idempotent on its own canonical echoes.
- Taking over `Game.ConnectPortals` means the mod now owns correctness for UNMANAGED portals too — a bug there breaks vanilla portal behaviour server-wide.
- Four input channels feeding one dispatcher creates ordering ambiguity: a player who pings while crouched and jumping produces three commands in ~200 ms. Serialize per-player with a 500 ms debounce and act on the last one.
- The armed state is the load-bearing safety mechanism; if the 15 s auto-disarm or the 6 m proximity gate is wrong, hubs re-route themselves during normal play and the mod will be perceived as haunted.
- Ownership churn: `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:76901) returns portal ownership to nearby players every 2 s, so every write must be self-contained (claim, write, ForceSendZDO) and never assume a held claim.
- Without `SetDirtyPortals()` on every tag write, the entire naming layer silently evaporates at the next world save (:77621, :76702).
- Map pins are permanent and unremovable — a single over-eager push loop litters every player's map forever.
- Discoverability remains the genuine risk: all four bootstrap paths are passive, and a player who ignores the login toast and never presses E on a portal out of curiosity never finds the system.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- GESTURE PROTOCOL IS SELF-CONTRADICTORY: Character.ForceJump calls SetCrouch(crouch:false) right after SetTrigger("jump") (:3483-3487) and Player.UpdateCrouch then writes crouching=0 into the ZDO (:15669-15673 client). 'Crouch = arm, jump = advance, un-crouch = commit' therefore commits on the FIRST jump. Redesign: e.g. arm with a crouch toggle, advance with dodge (dodge does not touch crouch, :15188-15200), commit with a second crouch toggle or the emote channel (Wonderland EmoteSignals pattern, s_emote/s_emoteID).
- RETAG WINDOW LOSS: after L3 does SetOwner(server), the nearby player's client is no longer owner, so a tag edit in that window goes ZNetView.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag") -> InvokeRoutedRPC(owner=serverID, zdoid, ...) (:82855-82858) -> server HandleRoutedRPC -> ZNetScene.FindInstance(zdo)==null -> silently dropped (:83646-83663). ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands ownership back within ~2 s (:76901-76927; IsInPeerActiveArea(pos, sessionID) is false because the reference position is pinned at 1e6, :100465), but the dispatcher must ALSO handle routed "RPC_SetTag" targeted at the server in its HandleRoutedRPC prefix, or edits are lost.
- EVERY vanilla tag edit clears BOTH ends: RPC_SetTag does zDO.UpdateConnection(Portal, None) and SetConnectedPortal(oldPartner) which either claims the partner (owner==0) and clears its connection or routes RPC_SetConnected to its owner (:143587-143620). On a fan-in/hub topology a player typing a command at a spoke breaks the hub's own outbound route until the mod reasserts. Treat every observed tag edit as 'reassert both ends'.
- L1 STATE is incomplete: the address book stores name->position/owner/lock but no per-portal dialed destination. On restart ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75462-75477) collapses each ZDO to ONE ZDOConnectionHashData slot and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77850-77893, called from LoadChunks :76515) restores only pairwise bidirectional matchings; one-way dials and fan-in are lost unless the mod persists the intended destination per portal (by rounded position) and reasserts after load.
- Idempotent-command dead zone: RPC_SetTag is a no-op when tagRaw==tag && authorId==authorId (:143590-143592). If the echo the mod writes equals the command text (e.g. writing ">Base" for command ">Base", or leaving "?" as "?"), retyping the same command produces no ZDO change and the server never sees it. Always rewrite the tag to something different from any valid command.
- RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse has a side effect not mentioned: the client calls Player.m_localPlayer.SetLookDir(pos - playerPos, 3.5f) when the map is closed (:100826-100829), snapping the camera toward the pin, and showMap=true opens the map (client Minimap.DiscoverLocation :58394-58420). Pass showMap=false and expect the camera turn.
- Sign author: the mod-written sign must set s_author to "" (PlatformUserID.None -> IsValid false -> Granted, :141874-141880), not "host" — the decompiled UpdateViewPermission routes a null m_author to Denied (:141867-141872) and the text renders as runes.
- Line cites: ZNetPeer.m_uid is :78784 not :78786; ZDOExtraData.GetData signature is :75109 not :75108; c_ZDOSalt is :87146. TextInput limit for the portal tag box is 10 chars (:143482) — confirmed. Tag comparison in FindRandomUnconnectedPortal/phase 1 is ordinal string != (:100601, :100668).
- OWNERSHIP RACE (real UX bug): after every L3 SetOwner(server) write, until ReleaseNearbyZDOS returns ownership (<=2 s), a vanilla client's next rename goes TeleportWorld.SetText -> m_nview.InvokeRPC("RPC_SetTag") -> routed to m_zdo.GetOwner() = server -> server HandleRoutedRPC -> ZNetScene.FindInstance == null -> silently dropped (:143581-143585, :83652-83660). The player's command vanishes with no feedback. Mitigation: do NOT claim ownership for writes -- ZDO.Set/SetConnection have no owner check and ZDOPeer.ShouldSend compares only revisions, so the server propagates writes on client-owned ZDOs regardless; ownership claiming is only needed if you copy Game.SetConnection verbatim.
- REVISION-COLLISION on freshly built portals: seeding `?help` in the Deserialize postfix of a brand-new ZDO races Piece.SetCreator/WearNTear init writes on the builder's client. Both sides bump DataRevision from the same base; RPC_ZDOData rejects any packet with `num4 <= DataRevision` (:77108-77118) on BOTH ends, so the client keeps creator-without-tag and the server keeps tag-without-creator until the next server-side bump. Delay seeding >=2 s after first sight or re-bump after verifying peer.m_zdos[id].m_dataRevision.
- GRAMMAR GAP: a portal carries ONE 10-char tag, so a portal cannot simultaneously display its name (`#Base`) and its dial (`>Haldor`); the hub in the described 11-portal flow loses its visible name the moment it dials. Names are effectively <=9 chars because TextInput is capped at 10 (:143473).
- SAVE BOUNDARY: fan-in topology (many `>Base` portals pointing at one `#Base`) collapses at save -- ZDOExtraData.RegenerateConnectionHashData (:75459-75477) gives each ZDO a single hash slot, later iterations overwrite earlier ones, so on load ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (:77863) restores at most one pair per target. The option's address book stores names only; dial state must be re-derived on world-ready from the persisted `>NAME` tags (which DO survive, provided SetDirtyPortals ran before the save). State this explicitly.
- RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse side effect: the client also runs Player.m_localPlayer.SetLookDir(pos - playerPos, 3.5f) when the map is closed (:100826-100829); at naming time the player is standing on the pin so the look vector is near-zero -- harmless but should be known.
- Every map-ping dial is also a normal ping broadcast to all other players (RouteRPC to every ready peer :83600-83607); arming limits accidental dials but not the ping spam.
- Citation nits: ZDO.Deserialize begins at :74206 (:74225 is a line inside it); ZSyncAnimation.SetBool body is :87270-87281 but :87270 itself is blank; DamageText.RPC_DamageText starts :46495.

(:42065) and the server's RPC_RoutedRPC calls HandleRoutedRPC for targetPeerID==0 (:83636-83639) before forwarding, so a HandleRoutedRPC prefix sees it. The jump/dodge gesture is ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger -> m_nview.InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, ...) (:87260-87263) -> InvokeRoutedRPC(0, zdoid, ...) which both handles locally AND RouteRPC()s to the server because targetPeerID != m_id (:83583-83590) — it does reach the server as a RoutedRPC packet; the crouch bit is ZSyncAnimation.SetBool -> zdo.Set(438569+hash) on the owner (:87270-87281), session-only (not saved) but networked (:74827). Tag writes really do need SetDirtyPortals: ZDO.Set -> IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector -> SetDirtyChunks(sector) (:73832-73840, :76694-76699) but portals live in m_portalObjects, not the sector chunks, and only DirtyPortalObjects triggers the portal chunk save (:77621-77631); AddIfPortal early-returns for already-registered portals without dirtying (:77732-77751). However several design details are wrong or unmentioned and one input channel is self-contradictory (see corrections). Enforcement stays server-enforced for what it actually governs — routes — with the explicit caveat that every per-player transit check (ore, NoPortals, boss) runs only in TeleportWorld.Teleport on the local client (:143517-143548) and the mod can only open/close routes.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanisms hold up against the decompile. (L0) Game.ConnectPortals is public (:100589), its phase-1 predicate is `zDO == null || tag != mine || partner.connection == None` with no reciprocity test (:100601), and it is also invoked from ZDOMan.LoadChunks (:76522) so a prefix blocks both call sites. (L2a) Client tag edits reach the server only through ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData -> zDO.Deserialize(pkg2) (:77131, method at :74206) -- the only Deserialize call site -- so a postfix sees every incoming tag. Note vanilla TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag on the owning client clears its own connection first (UpdateConnection(Portal, None) :143594) and, because it reads the connection AFTER clearing it, never clears the partner; every command therefore arrives as {new tag, connection None} and the mod must re-link -- which also means the 'blue connect effect' fires on EVERY command, not just dials (m_hadTarget false->true in UpdatePortal :143491-143499). (L2c) Chat.SendPing is InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, "ChatMessage", pos, 3, UserInfo, "") (:42065); on the server ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC calls HandleRoutedRPC for target 0 (:83636) and, since the Chat MonoBehaviour is never instantiated headless, m_functions has no handler and the packet is dropped silently -- a prefix on HandleRoutedRPC (:83646) does see it. (L2d) Character.ForceJump -> m_zanim.SetTrigger("jump") (:3483), Player.UpdateDodge -> SetTrigger("dodge") (:15196), ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger = m_nview.InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody, ...) (:87260-87263) so the server relays it; crouch is ZSyncAnimation.SetBool -> zdo.Set(438569+hash, int) on the owner (:87270-87281) which replicates via normal ZDO sync and is readable server-side by GetInt(438569+Animator.StringToHash("crouching")). (L4) Player registers "Message" only on its owner client (:10072) -> works for a peer-targeted, ZDO-targeted routed RPC; DamageText.Awake registers RPC_DamageText on clients (:46352-46356), m_maxTextDistance = 30f (:46338), TextType.Bonus exists; RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse (:100823) calls Minimap.DiscoverLocation which dedups via HaveSimilarPin and, with showMap=false, adds silently -- but it ALSO calls Player.SetLookDir toward the pin for 3.5 s (:100826-100829), a side effect not mentioned. Tag/hover: GetHoverText -> GetTagInfo reads the ZDO every call (:143453, :143561-143574). SetDirtyPortals is genuinely required: ZDO.Set(string) only calls IncreaseDataRevision -> SetDirtySector (:73721-73727, :73832-73839) which dirties a zone chunk the portal is NOT stored in (portals live only in m_portalObjects, saved in ChunkPortal only when DirtyPortalObjects :77621-77631); ZDO.SetConnection does call SetDirtyPortals itself (:73656-73665). Ownership: ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76927) includes portals via FindObjects (:77376) and hands a server-owned portal to any nearby peer within 2 s because the server ref-pos (1e6,0,1e6 :100465) is never in the peer's active area. Server-enforced is honest at the route level (which portal connects to which, locks, boss lockdown all live in the server-owned connection field); per-player transit remains client-side, which the option does not claim otherwise. Effort 'large' is if anything optimistic.

### 178. Phantom Destination Portal (foundation)

`targeted-portals:Phantom Destination Portal (foundation)` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A persistent portal-prefab ZDO minted server-side at any computed coordinate with no GameObject; the vanilla client instantiates it as a real portal when near, and every other targeted option builds on it.


**How it works:** Creation (all public API, no reflection): `int hash = Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash[i]` (list built in Game.Awake from m_portalPrefabs; resolve the wood-portal entry at runtime via `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(hash).name`, never hard-code). `ZDO z = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, hash)` — this pools a ZDO, sets owner to the server session, runs `AddIfPortal(z, hash)` which files it in `m_portalObjects` and flags `DirtyPortalObjects`, and indexes it in m_objectsByID. CreateNewZDO does NOT set prefab, Persistent, Type, Distant or rotation, so replicate ZNetView.Awake's five lines in this exact order: `z.Persistent = true; z.Type = ZDO.ObjectType.Default; z.Distant = false; z.SetPrefab(hash); z.SetRotation(rot);` (Persistent before SetPrefab so the IncreaseDataRevision→SetDirtySector call marks chunks). Then `z.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, tag); z.Set(ZDOVars.s_tagauthor, "server"); z.Set("TPL_phantom", 1); z.Set("TPL_kind", kind)` for later cleanup/identification (mod-private int/string keys round-trip through save and network). Pairing: `src.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); src.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, z.m_uid); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(src.m_uid); z.SetConnection(ConnectionType.Portal, src.m_uid); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(z.m_uid);` — reciprocal AND same literal s_tag on both ends is mandatory, because Game.ConnectPortals (5 s coroutine) tears down any link whose partner's tag differs or whose partner's connection is None, and because the phantom is in GetPortalList() it is iterated and would otherwise be randomly re-paired with any player portal sharing the tag. Optionally write LoadFields overrides the client honours at instantiation: `z.Set("HasFields", true); z.Set("HasFieldsPiece", true); z.Set("Piece.m_canBeRemoved", false); z.Set("HasFieldsTeleportWorld", true); z.Set("TeleportWorld.m_exitDistance", 1.5f)` (keys are `<TypeName>.<PublicField>` strings). Maintenance tick (1–5 s): for each managed (source, phantom) pair re-resolve by ZDOID via ZDOMan.GetZDO (never cache ZDO refs — vanilla's own m_currentlyConnectingPortals bug shows pooled reuse), re-assert tag+connection (idempotent: unchanged values do not bump DataRevision), and if the source is gone (`GetZDO==null`) destroy the phantom with `z.SetOwner(GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(z)` (DestroyZDO is owner-gated on send). Save footprint: phantoms live in the dedicated ChunkPortal file with all other portals and are written whenever DirtyPortalObjects is set; connections persist as hash pairs and are re-linked reciprocally by ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load. Uninstall residue: the phantoms remain as ordinary vanilla portals (visible, hammer-removable unless m_canBeRemoved was overridden, and vanilla keeps pairing them by tag); a `tpl_purge` server console command should enumerate GetPortalList() and destroy every ZDO carrying TPL_phantom before removing the mod.


**Player experience:** The source portal's hover text reads `Portal tag:"<tag>" [connected]` — the tag is the only label the server controls, so the mod writes a descriptive tag such as `>Eikthyr` (no client-side 10-char cap applies to server writes; rich text is stripped). The portal glows connected. Walking in gives the standard 8-second portal swirl and the player arrives at phantom.pos + forward*m_exitDistance + 1 m up, facing the phantom's rotation. Looking back they see a real, ordinary-looking portal standing there with the same tag; it hums, glows, and can be walked back through (returns to the source). Nothing appears on the map unless the mod separately pushes a pin. The first walk-through after a fresh pairing can silently do nothing if the client has not yet received the phantom ZDO (TargetFound() fires RequestZDO and returns) — the second attempt works; the mod avoids this by ForceSendZDO to every peer at creation.


**Failure modes:**
- Third player portal with the same tag: vanilla's random pairer can orphan one member; use a reserved tag namespace (e.g. prefix with a non-typeable glyph) or postfix Game.FindRandomUnconnectedPortal to exclude TPL_phantom ZDOs.
- Player hammer-removes the phantom: WearNTear.Destroy drops full recoverable materials — an infinite-materials exploit if the mod recreates it; mitigate with LoadFields Piece.m_canBeRemoved=false (client-honoured) plus a recreate cooldown keyed off ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed.
- Player damages the phantom to 0 health: same drop; mitigate with LoadFields WearNTear.m_health=1e9 and z.Set(ZDOVars.s_health,1e9f).
- Ownership steal: ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands the phantom to any peer within ~96 m every 2 s; the connection value already sent survives, but any later server write must re-claim (Wonderland ZdoSetOwnerPatch pattern if a hard hold is needed).
- Never call z.SetPosition on a phantom after creation: ZDO.SetSector early-returns for portal prefabs, leaving m_portalObjects keyed by the old sector (delivery breaks, HandleDestroyedZDO leaks the entry). Destroy and recreate instead.
- Retag race: if a client owns the source and retags it, RPC_SetTag clears the connection and the tag mismatch tears the pair down within 5 s; the maintenance tick must detect the tag change and either re-write the mod tag or accept the player's choice and drop the phantom.

- Does a vanilla client apply LoadFields overrides Piece.m_canBeRemoved / WearNTear.m_health on a server-authored ZDO exactly as expected (single highest-value experiment)?

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Exit offset uses the ENTERED portal's m_exitDistance (TeleportWorld.Teleport :143545; field :143413). Writing TeleportWorld.m_exitDistance on the phantom changes only the return hop from the phantom; arrival placement at the phantom is set by the SOURCE portal's field (also overridable via LoadFields on the source ZDO).
- The Persistent-before-SetPrefab rationale is wrong: ZDO.IncreaseDataRevision→ZDOMan.SetDirtySector (:73832-73839, :76694-76700) marks zone chunks, which portals are excluded from (AddObjectsPerChunk :77572); the ChunkPortal file is driven solely by DirtyPortalObjects, already set by AddIfPortal (:77750) and ZDO.SetConnection (:73661-73664). Order is harmless, not required.
- Piece.m_canBeRemoved=false stops only Player.RemovePiece (client :12377). The instantiated phantom carries WearNTear; damage destruction by the owning client sends DestroyZDO → RPC_DestroyZDO with no sender/ward check (:76950-76960). The maintenance tick must detect a missing phantom and re-mint.
- Ownership is handed to any nearby peer every 2 s (ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901-76924). Re-assert writes that change nothing produce no DataRevision bump and are not resent; after a concurrent equal-revision collision the client copy stays stale. Include a nonce key write when repairing tag/connection.
- Uninstall residue is understated: phantoms persist in ChunkPortal and vanilla's pass 2 will pair them by tag with player portals after the mod is removed; the purge command is mandatory, not optional.
- Ground-support hazard: vanilla WearNTear on the instantiated portal (m_noSupportWear default true, client :149945) deals 100 damage per UpdateWear when UpdateSupport finds no terrain/static collider in its bounds (client :150445-150451, :150748-150800); a floating or buried phantom is destroyed by the first visiting client that owns it. Mint at Heightmap ground height, or write `HasFieldsWearNTear=true` + `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false` through LoadFields.
- Maintenance tick: compare before writing and only SetOwner(session) when a write is needed; unconditional SetOwner every 1-5 s bumps OwnerRevision (:74627-74634) and fights ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76924, 2 s) for as long as a player stands near the phantom.
- `TeleportWorld.m_exitDistance` override affects exits FROM the phantom only; arrival offset at the phantom is `phantom.pos + phantom.forward * SOURCE.m_exitDistance + up` (:143542-143545).
- Do not write s_tagauthor = "server": GetTagInfo constructs `new PlatformUserID(authorString)` for any non-empty value on every hover (:143557-143565); PlatformUserID is outside this decompile set and its handling of a malformed id is unverified. Leave it empty (PlatformUserID.None path) or use a real platform id.
- Citation fix: client LoadFields is called from ZNetView.Awake at assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82860 (not :82631); LoadFields body :82898-82970 is correct.
- The 'silent first walk-through' concern is largely mitigated by vanilla itself: UpdatePortal (0.5 s) calls TargetFound → RequestZDO whenever a teleportable player is within m_activationRange (:143488-143504, :143640-143655), so the request is normally in flight before the trigger is reached; ForceSendZDO at creation is still worthwhile for peers already standing at the source.
- Destroyability: m_canBeRemoved=false blocks only the hammer path (Player.RemovePiece client :12377); weapon damage still runs WearNTear.Destroy → ZNetScene.Destroy → DestroyZDO, and RPC_DestroyZDO has no sender or ward check (:76953-76960), so phantoms are not indestructible.

### 179. Invisible Anchor ZDO (non-portal destination)

`targeted-portals:Invisible Anchor ZDO (non-portal destination)` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Point a portal at a Persistent ZDO carrying prefab hash 0 or a mod-private hash: no mesh, no collider, invisible to vanilla's pairer, cheap to move — at the cost of a one-way arrival and possible client log spam.


**How it works:** TeleportWorld.Teleport does a bare `ZDOMan.instance.GetZDO(connectionId)` and reads only GetPosition()/GetRotation() — it never checks the target's prefab. So any ZDO the client holds is a valid destination. Create: `ZDO a = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, 0)` (hash 0 → AddIfPortal is skipped, the ZDO is filed in m_objectsBySector by ZDO.Initialize→AddToSector), then `a.Persistent = true; a.SetPrefab(0 or "TPL_Anchor".GetStableHashCode()); a.SetRotation(rot); a.Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, sameTagAsSource); a.Set("TPL_anchor",1)`. Link: source→anchor via SetOwner/SetConnection/ForceSendZDO, and anchor→source reciprocally. Vanilla's runtime reconciler only iterates GetPortalList(), so the anchor is never a candidate for random pairing; but it still validates the SOURCE's link (`partner != null`, `partner.tag == tag`, `partner.connection != None`), which the reciprocal write satisfies. Client side: ZNetScene.CreateObject returns null for prefab 0 silently, and for an unknown hash logs `Missing prefab hash` — and crucially only `ZNet.instance.IsServer()` destroys 'invalid prefab' ZDOs in CreateObjectsSorted, which a vanilla client is not, so the anchor survives. Because `Created` never becomes true, the client re-attempts CreateObject every CreateDestroyObjects pass (1/30 s) while the anchor is in its near set: prefer prefab 0 (silent) over a custom hash (per-tick warning spam). Delivery: the anchor sits in the normal sector map, so ZDOMan sends it to peers whose active area covers it; a distant traveller gets it via TeleportWorld.TargetFound→RequestZDO→ForceSendZDO(peer,id). Save: Persistent non-portal ZDOs go into the normal zone chunk (AddObjectsPerChunk excludes only portal prefabs); FilterZDO on load puts unknown-prefab ZDOs into warningZDOs and 'Will load anyway'; RegenerateConnectionHashData persists the pair because both endpoints resolve, and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals relinks both ways at load (it enumerates hash data, not m_portalObjects). Moving an anchor IS safe (unlike a phantom portal): `a.SetOwner(GetSessionID()); a.SetPosition(newPos)` goes through the full SetSector re-filing path and bumps DataRevision because the server owns it. Cleanup: SetOwner(session)+DestroyZDO. Uninstall residue: an unknown-prefab or prefab-0 Persistent ZDO per anchor, loaded 'anyway' with a startup warning each boot, invisible in play; the source portal keeps a dangling one-way link that vanilla clears (GetZDO of the anchor still succeeds, so actually the link survives until the anchor is deleted) — ship a purge command.


**Player experience:** The source hover reads `Portal tag:"<tag>" [connected]` and glows; walk-through gives the normal 8 s swirl; the player arrives at anchor.pos + forward*1 m + 1 m up on open ground with NOTHING there — no portal to walk back through. Return is only possible via another portal, an emote command (Wonderland EmoteSignals) that asks the server to RPC_TeleportPlayer them back, or on foot. No map marker unless pushed separately. If the mod used a custom prefab hash, the player's own log file (not the screen) fills with `Missing prefab hash` lines while they stand near the arrival spot.


**Failure modes:**
- Custom prefab hash: every nearby vanilla client spams `Missing prefab hash: …` at up to 30 Hz into its log while the anchor is in range — use prefab 0, which returns null silently in CreateObject.
- One-way by construction: nothing to walk back into; must be paired with a return mechanism or documented as one-way.
- A future Valheim patch that makes clients destroy invalid-prefab ZDOs (currently gated on IsServer()) would delete anchors on first approach.
- If the source portal is retagged by a player, the tag mismatch nulls the source's link within 5 s and vanilla re-pairs the source with a random same-tag player portal; the anchor keeps its stale reciprocal link (harmless, but the maintenance tick should reap it).
- Anchor near an existing structure: the mod cannot raycast, so it may place the arrival point inside a building; validate against nearby piece ZDOs with ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear.

**Open questions:**
- Does a 1.0.7 vanilla client tolerate a prefab-0 ZDO in its near set indefinitely with no side effects (IsZoneReadyForType with Type=Default, no exceptions)? IN-GAME: create one, stand on it for 10 minutes, watch the client log.
- Does TeleportWorld.TargetFound's RequestZDO round-trip deliver a non-portal ZDO to a client that has never had that zone loaded, and does the subsequent Teleport succeed on the second walk-through?
- Is a Persistent prefab-0 ZDO actually written into the zone chunk and reloaded (ZDO.Save/Load path with m_prefab==0)?

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Uninstall residue: with the mod gone, the source→anchor link SURVIVES vanilla's reconciler as long as the anchor ZDO exists (pass 1 predicate :100600-100604 is satisfied: target non-null, same tag, connection non-None); it is only cleared after the anchor is purged. Rewrite the contradictory sentence.
- Arrival position is anchor.pos + anchorForward * SOURCE.m_exitDistance + up (TeleportWorld.Teleport :143545 uses the entered portal's field), not a fixed 1 m unless the source is a stock portal.
- FilterZDO warns about unknown prefabs only when the chunk's saved world version differs from the running version (:76346-76360 `if (newVersion)`); on same-version loads the anchor loads silently — the 'startup warning each boot' claim is conditional.
- Any vanilla client can delete the anchor via RPC_DestroyZDO (no sender check :76950-76960); the re-assert tick should re-mint a missing anchor from the position-keyed registry.
- After SetPosition on an anchor, call ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(anchor.m_uid): SetSector → ZDOSectorInvalidated (:73764-73767, :75988-75996) removes the anchor from every out-of-area peer's m_zdos and tells the client to InvalidateSector (client :77230-77233); the client keeps the stale position and TargetFound/Teleport still succeed on it, so an un-resent move sends travellers to the old coordinate.
- Keep anchors inside the sector grid (|x|,|z| < 256×64−32 ≈ 16352 m): beyond that SectorToIndex clamps to sector 0 (:115760-115774), the only bucket the dedicated server's CreateDestroyObjects scans (:82268-82276, ref pos :100465), and CreateObjectsSorted's IsServer branch destroys uncreatable ZDOs there (:82141-82147).
- Uninstall residue, stated cleanly: the anchor loads with a warning (:76346-76375) and the source portal remains linked to it indefinitely because pass 1 only checks null/tag/None (:100600-100604); vanilla never clears it. A purge command is mandatory, not optional.
- Prefab-0 anchors are re-attempted by the vanilla client's CreateObjectsSorted every 1/30 s while in its near set (client :82334-82372, :82489-82493) — silent, but avoid minting hundreds within one active area.
- The 'anchor.tag' must be kept equal to the source's s_tag at all times (pass 1 :100601); a player retag of the source (RPC_SetTag :143587-143602) nulls the source's connection and pass 2 will then pair the source with any same-tag player portal — the maintenance tick must re-assert both the tag on the anchor and the source→anchor link.

### 180. Admin Coordinates

`targeted-portals:Admin Coordinates` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


An operator names an X/Z (and optional Y/rotation) in the config or server console; the mod validates it against procedural terrain and drops a phantom there.


**How it works:** Input: a hot-reloaded config entry (Wonderland PollConfigFile pattern) or a Terminal.ConsoleCommand registered `onlyServer:true` (usable from the dedicated server stdin and by admins via ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand, which gates on the adminlist). Validation must be pure math because every ZoneSystem raycast helper (GetGroundHeight, GetSolidHeight, FindFloor, IsBlocked, GetGroundData) silently returns its fallback on a dedicated server (Game.FixedUpdate pins the reference position at 1e6 so no terrain collider exists near real coordinates). Use: `float h = WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(x, z)`; reject if `x*x+z*z > 110250000` (beyond waterEdge, height is −400); reject if `h < 30` unless the operator flagged 'allow water'; reject if `ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap(new Vector3(x,h,z))`; reject if `WorldGenerator.instance.GetNormal(new Vector2(x,z), 1f).y < 0.7` (steep); reject if y > 3000 (interior space). Optional structure check: `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(pos, 3f)` and reject if any ZDO whose prefab has a Piece component is within 1.5 m (approximate — no colliders). For a fast pre-filter use `ZNet.World.m_biomeData.PointHeights[WorldSpaceToMapSpace(x), WorldSpaceToMapSpace(z)]` (12 m grid, O(1)). Then create the phantom (Option 1) at (x, h + 0.2, z) with rotation from the config yaw, tag = the operator's label, and pair it to the operator-named source (identified by position or existing tag, since ZDOIDs change per load). Arrival correctness on the client: Player.UpdateTeleport calls ZoneSystem.FindFloor(target) (raycast down 1000 m from target+1 m) which hits the terrain the client generated locally; if the pre-flattening WorldGenerator height is a metre off, the 8 s/IsAreaReady gate plus the 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback still lands the player on the actual surface. Tick cost: creation is one-shot; validation is ~10 noise evaluations; the maintenance re-assert loop is shared with all managed pairs.


**Player experience:** The admin runs `tpl_target "Ashlands Camp" 1234 -5678 yaw=90 source="hub3"`; within one tick the hub portal's hover text changes to `Portal tag:"Ashlands Camp" [connected]` for anyone standing there (UpdatePortal re-reads HaveTarget every 0.5 s; hover text re-reads the tag every frame). A player walks in, gets the 8 s swirl, and steps out of a real portal at the coordinate facing the configured yaw. The destination portal shows the same tag. If the coordinate was underwater/lava/off-map the command prints the rejection reason to the admin's console via ZNet.RemotePrint and nothing changes.


**Failure modes:**
- WorldGenerator is blind to player terraforming and location flattening: an arrival point may be up to a few metres off or inside a raised earth wall; the client fallback still lands on solid ground but possibly on top of it.
- Coordinates inside a player base can drop travellers inside walls; only approximate piece-ZDO proximity checks are possible.
- Console commands from a vanilla player's own console never reach the server unless the player is an admin and the command is RemoteCommand-flagged.

**Open questions:**
- How far off is WorldGenerator.GetHeight from the real placed surface at typical location sites (needs a sampled comparison against a client-side raycast)?

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Dedicated server has no stdin command reader in vanilla: Console.Update polls ZInput only (SERVER :42883-42900); no Console.In/ReadLine in the assembly. 'usable from the dedicated server stdin' requires a mod-added stdin thread.
- 'usable by admins via ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand' is false for a mod-specific command: vanilla client Terminal.TryRunCommand rejects unknown command names before the RemoteCommand branch (:45734-45758). Only vanilla commands flagged remoteCommand:true are forwarded; a mod would have to intercept one of those (e.g. `setkey <payload>`, :43529-43534) on the server, or use chat.
- ZNet.RemotePrint feedback only exists for the RPC path (needs the ZRpc); config-file input can only report via log.
- Terminal.ConsoleCommand ctor signature confirmed: (command, description, action, isCheat, isNetwork, onlyServer, isSecret, allowInDevBuild, hideBehindDevCommands, optionsFetcher, alwaysRefreshTabOptions, remoteCommand, onlyAdmin) at :43094; Terminal.commands is protected static (:43241) so a server-side mod can register into it, but registration on the server does not make the client aware of it.
- PointHeights pre-filter: array is indexed [mapX, mapY] where mapX derives from world x and mapY from world z (GenerateBiomePoints :92440-92450); values are GetBiomeHeight (pre-flattening), -1000 outside waterEdge.
- Remove 'usable from the dedicated server stdin' — the vanilla dedicated server has no stdin command reader; the mod must add its own thread (grep: no ReadLine/Console.In in assembly_valheim_SERVER).
- Remove 'by admins via ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand' for a mod-registered command: the vanilla client's Terminal.TryRunCommand (SERVER:45734-45760, same on client) only forwards commands it has itself registered with RemoteCommand=true; an unknown name prints 'not a recognized command' locally and nothing is sent.
- Replace the input channel with: (a) map ping (Chat.SendPing CLIENT:42058-42066 → routed RPC 'ChatMessage' type 3 to peer 0, no permission check) for X/Z, with adminlist check server-side; and/or (b) a Harmony prefix on ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand/InternalCommand (SERVER:81879-81894) intercepting a vanilla remoteCommand-flagged command carrying free text, e.g. `setkey tpl:...` (SERVER:43546) — adminlist gate at 81881 is vanilla.
- Chat keywords are unreliable: chat text is sent per-OTHER-player (CLIENT:41996-42040); a lone admin emits nothing.
- Phantom y must sit within ~0.15 m of the client's real terrain or the owning vanilla client's WearNTear destroys it ~30 s after instantiation (CLIENT:150361-150389 bounds margin, 150781-150838 terrain support, 150445-150450 + 150561-150567 damage). Set `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false` through LoadFields keys (HasFields, HasFieldsWearNTear, 'WearNTear.m_noSupportWear') on every phantom; Piece.m_canBeRemoved does not help (Piece.CanBeRemoved CLIENT:137050-137062 ignores it).
- Effort: medium (input channel + validation + LoadFields keys), not small-medium.
- GetHoverText format is `$piece_portal $piece_portal_tag:"<tag>" [$piece_portal_connected]` (SERVER:143453-143463); `[connected]` reflects HaveTarget (connection ID != None) while the glow needs TargetFound, which triggers ZDOMan.RequestZDO → server ForceSendZDO with no distance filter (SERVER:143643-143657, 77689-77692, 77263-77285).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] The validation math and arrival path hold up against the decompile: WorldGenerator.GetHeight -> GetBiomeHeight edge guard returns -2*GetHeightMultiplier() = -400 beyond 10500 m (SERVER :151978-151981, :152396); GetNormal is pure height sampling (:151925-151932); IsLavaPreHeightmap is pure WorldGenerator mask math (:115637-115646); FindFloor/GetGroundHeight are Physics.Raycast (:115604-115612, :115502-115510) and Game.FixedUpdate pins the server reference position at 1e6 (:100458-100466). Client arrival: TeleportWorld.Teleport passes distantTeleport:true (:143546) so Player.UpdateTeleport applies the 8 s/IsAreaReady gate and the 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback (:15349-15378; GetSolidHeight raycasts from p.y+1000 and returns p.y on miss). The phantom position/rotation come from the destination ZDO on the client (:143541-143545), so the route is server-authoritative. The INPUT CHANNEL claims are wrong, though. (1) The vanilla dedicated server reads no stdin at all: Console.Update only polls ZInput (:42883-42900) and there is no Console.In/ReadLine anywhere in the server assembly - a 'server console' command needs the mod's own stdin thread or the config file. (2) Admins on vanilla clients cannot reach a mod-registered command through RPC_RemoteCommand: Terminal.TryRunCommand looks the command name up in the client's static `commands` table first (:45734-45737) and prints 'not a recognized command' for unknown names (:45757); the RemoteCommand forwarding branch (:45743-45745) is only reached for commands the vanilla client already has. The adminlist gate itself is real (:81879-81889). So enforcement of the DESTINATION is server-side; the operator input surface is config/own-stdin only unless the mod hijacks a vanilla remoteCommand-flagged command (setkey/removekey/listkeys/players/genloc/sleep/setworldmodifier, e.g. :43529-43546) or chat.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] The core mechanism (pure WorldGenerator validation + phantom at the coordinate) holds: WorldGenerator.GetHeight/GetNormal/waterEdge guard and ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap are pure math (SERVER:151944-151949, 151978-151981, 151122, 151925-151932, 115637-115645); Game.FixedUpdate pins the ref pos at 1e6 (SERVER:100458-100466) and ghost zones destroy their root immediately after PlaceLocations/PlaceVegetation (ZoneSystem.SpawnZone SERVER:114085-114104), so GetGroundHeight/FindFloor raycasts (SERVER:115502-115511, 115604-115613) are dead at real coordinates. The client arrival path is as described (Player.UpdateTeleport CLIENT:15331-15380: 8 s distant gate, FindFloor from target+1 m, 15 s GetSolidHeight fallback). BOTH claimed input channels are wrong for a vanilla client, though. (1) No stdin reader exists in the dedicated server assembly (no Console.ReadLine/Console.In anywhere in assembly_valheim_SERVER); the mod would have to run its own stdin thread. (2) RPC_RemoteCommand is only reached from a client whose own Terminal already has the command registered with RemoteCommand=true: Terminal.TryRunCommand (SERVER:45734-45760, identical on the client) does commands.TryGetValue(name) first and prints 'not a recognized command' for anything a mod registered server-side only; the forward `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text)` is in the else-branch of that lookup. A vanilla admin therefore cannot type `tpl_target ...` anywhere that reaches the server. Chat is also not a reliable channel: Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync sends one routed RPC per OTHER player (CLIENT:41996-42040), so a lone admin generates no packet. Real vanilla-client admin channels are: the map ping (Chat.SendPing CLIENT:42058-42066, routed to peer 0 = server, carries a free world X/Z), and hijacking a vanilla remoteCommand:true command that accepts free text such as `setkey <arg>` (SERVER:43546, onlyServer+remoteCommand, isCheat:false) by Harmony-prefixing ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand/InternalCommand (SERVER:81879-81894, adminlist-gated at 81881) — the vanilla client forwards it unmodified because IsValid fails on OnlyServer (SERVER:43203-43218). ZNet.RemotePrint (SERVER:81635-81647) works for feedback given the admin's ZRpc from ZNet.GetPeer(uid).m_rpc. A second systemic problem shared by every option in this batch: y = WorldGenerator height + 0.2 is the PRE-modifier height; the client's actual terrain includes TerrainComp/location edits. The vanilla client's WearNTear support check overlaps the piece colliders expanded by only 0.15 m per side (SetupColliders CLIENT:150361-150389); if no terrain-layer collider is inside that box (CLIENT:150781-150784, 150830-150838) m_support drops to 0, and with m_noSupportWear (public, CLIENT:149945) the owner applies 100 % damage after the 30 s ShouldUpdate grace (CLIENT:150392-150399, 150445-150450, 150561-150567). Piece.CanBeRemoved() does not consult m_canBeRemoved (CLIENT:137050-137062) so that override does not save it. Mitigation is real and vanilla-honoured: write HasFields/HasFieldsWearNTear/`WearNTear.m_noSupportWear`=false via ZNetView.LoadFields (CLIENT:82898-82960), or accept the GlobalKeys.NoBuildingFall side effect. Effort is medium, not small-medium, once the input channel is built.
