### 181. World Spawn / Start Temple

`targeted-portals:World Spawn / Start Temple` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portal to the exact spot vanilla respawns new characters, read from the server's own LocationIcons source.


**How it works:** `ZoneSystem.instance.GetLocationIcon(Game.instance.m_StartLocation, out Vector3 pos)` — the server branch scans m_locationInstances for the first entry whose ZoneLocation is icon-flagged and whose `m_prefab.Name == "StartTemple"`; this is the very value the server ships to clients in the LocationIcons RPC and the one Game.FindSpawnPoint uses for a fresh spawn (`pos + Vector3.up * 2f`). m_locationInstances is populated by ZNet.ServerLoadWorld→GenerateLocationsIfNeeded before any peer connects, so this works at OnWorldReady with zero players. Place the phantom (Option 1) ~6–8 m from the temple centre on the side away from the stones: sample four candidate offsets, keep the one with the lowest `|WorldGenerator.GetHeight − pos.y|` and best GetNormal.y, orient the phantom's forward toward the temple. Because the start temple has m_clearArea the placed terrain may differ from the stored pre-flattening height by a metre or two — set phantom y = max(stored, GetHeight) + 0.2 and rely on the client's FindFloor/15 s fallback. Persistence: the temple never moves, so this is a create-once pair; the maintenance tick only re-asserts. Multiple hubs can each get their own phantom near the temple (spread them around the ring so exit points do not overlap). Tick cost: one dictionary scan at creation, nothing afterwards.


**Player experience:** Hover: `Portal tag:"Spawn" [connected]`. Walk in → 8 s swirl → step out of a real portal a few metres from the Sacrificial Stones, facing them, with the temple's own map icon already on their map (vanilla LocationIcons). Walking back into that portal returns to the source hub.


**Failure modes:**
- Two mods or a heavily modified world could register additional StartTemple instances; GetLocationIcon returns the first dictionary match, not the closest — acceptable since vanilla uses the same call.
- If the temple's location flags (m_iconAlways) were altered by a location mod, GetLocationIcon returns false; fall back to FindClosestLocation("StartTemple", Vector3.zero).

### 182. Boss Altars (per boss / nearest / next-undefeated)

`targeted-portals:Boss Altars (per boss / nearest / next-undefeated)` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portal to any boss altar, the nearest altar of a given boss, or the altar of the next boss not yet marked defeated in the server's global keys.


**How it works:** Discovery: altars are world-gen Locations, present in `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locationInstances` from world load regardless of whether any player has visited. Per boss: `ZoneSystem.instance.FindLocations(altarName, ref list)` for all instances, or `FindClosestLocation(altarName, refPoint, out inst)` for nearest to the source portal (both are O(all location instances) linear scans — cache a name→List index at OnWorldReady). Altar location prefab names are Unity asset data, not in the decompile: build the map at boot by dumping `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locations` and matching `m_iconAlways==true && m_quantity small` plus name heuristics, then confirm in-game (open question). Next-undefeated: `ZoneSystem.instance.GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.defeated_eikthyr)` … `defeated_goblinking` (enum ordinals 42–46; later bosses use string keys, enumerate GetGlobalKeys()) in canonical order; pick the first false and resolve that altar. Position: `inst.m_position` already carries a WorldGenerator ground height (sea level 30); place the phantom (Option 1) at `inst.m_position + dir * (inst.m_location.m_exteriorRadius + 4)` where dir is the flattest of 8 compass samples by GetNormal.y and not lava (IsLavaPreHeightmap — Fader's altar is in Ashlands), forward facing the altar. Do NOT try to reach the OfferingBowl object: OfferingBowl is a MonoBehaviour with no ZDO of its own (GetComponentInParent<ZNetView> in Start) and its parent piece ZDO only exists after a peer's ghost-generation of that zone; the LocationInstance is always available. 'Next-undefeated' re-evaluates on a slow tick (30 s) or from a postfix on ZoneSystem.GlobalKeyAdd (BossDefeatWatch pattern, pre-seeding at boot to avoid the SetStartingGlobalKeys replay) and re-targets the phantom by destroy-and-recreate (never SetPosition on a portal prefab). NoBossPortals interaction: when the key is set and a boss is alerted (activeBosses > 0), the client refuses transit with `$msg_blockedbyboss` — the mod cannot override that per-portal.


**Player experience:** Hover: `Portal tag:">Bonemass" [connected]` (or `>Next Boss` for the auto mode). 8 s swirl, arrive on flat ground ~4 m outside the altar's footprint facing the altar; the altar's vanilla map icon is already visible. For 'next boss', after Bonemass is killed anywhere on the server, within ~30 s the hub portal's tag flips to `>Moder` and the old phantom vanishes from the Bonemass swamp (it simply ceases to exist on the next zone load for anyone there). If a boss is currently alerted and NoBossPortals is on, walking in shows the vanilla `Portals are blocked by a boss` message.


**Failure modes:**
- Altar location prefab names unknown until an in-game dump; a wrong name yields FindLocations empty and the option silently disables.
- m_position is the pre-placement height; altars with m_clearArea may sit a metre lower/higher — client fallback handles it but the phantom mesh can float/sink visually.
- Boss fights: a phantom 4 m outside the altar is inside the arena; consider 15–20 m offsets so it is not destroyed by the boss (WearNTear damage → Destroy → resources drop).
- Deep North / Ashlands: IsLavaPreHeightmap only means lava inside Ashlands; sample multiple offsets.

The existence of the Vegvisir path is the reason altars are not iconAlways, so the proposed boot heuristic 'm_iconAlways==true && m_quantity small' would select the StartTemple, not altars. Corrections: (1) the GlobalKeys enum order is eikthyr, dragon, goblinking, gdking, bonemass (SERVER:101314-101318) — NOT progression order; the mod must hard-code eikthyr→gdking→bonemass→dragon→goblinking→queen→fader, and queen/fader are string keys set from Character.m_defeatSetGlobalKey (SERVER:275, 3153-3155) not present in the enum. (3) GlobalKeyAdd is private (SERVER:113483) — patchable, but must be a Harmony patch on a private member; SetStartingGlobalKeys (SERVER:115904) replays existing keys at load as the catalog says. (4) Re-targeting by destroy-and-recreate requires the mod to own the ZDO first (ZDOMan.DestroyZDO only queues if IsOwner, SERVER:76927-76933) and to rewrite BOTH tags and BOTH connections before the next 5 s Game.ConnectPortals pass, which otherwise nulls the hub (target==null predicate, SERVER:100600-100606) and may randomly re-pair it with any other portal carrying the same tag (FindRandomUnconnectedPortal SERVER:100663-100677). (5) Same WearNTear floating-collapse caveat as the other options: altar surroundings are often uneven and m_position is the pre-placement height (SERVER:114735), so use LoadFields WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false. Enforcement is server-enforced for the route only; the boss/ore/NoPortals transit gates remain client-executed.

### 183. Traders (Haldor, Hildir, Bog Witch)

`targeted-portals:Traders (Haldor, Hildir, Bog Witch)` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portal to any trader camp, resolved from the location registry; traders are placed-on-discovery icons so gating on m_placed is the difference between 'exists' and 'has been generated'.


**How it works:** Trader camps are Locations (prefab names live in asset data — dump `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locations` at boot and pick entries whose `m_iconPlaced==true` and `m_unique==true`, which in vanilla is the trader set; confirm names in-game). `FindLocations(name, ref list)` gives every instance with `m_position` and `m_placed`. Vanilla shows the trader map icon only once `m_placed` is true (GetLocationIcons: `m_iconAlways || (m_iconPlaced && m_placed)`), i.e. once some peer's reference position has ghost-generated the zone. The mod can choose either: (a) 'discovered only' — offer the trader as a destination only when `m_placed`, matching vanilla's reveal rules; or (b) 'always' — target the instance position regardless, which lets a hub portal lead players to an undiscovered trader (a design choice, not a technical limit). Place the phantom (Option 1) at `m_position + dir * (m_exteriorRadius + 3)` on the flattest compass sample, forward toward the camp. Trader camps are unique and static, so this is create-once; the phantom should carry `Piece.m_canBeRemoved=false` via LoadFields because trader camps are heavily visited. A 'nearest trader' mode picks min Vector3.Distance over all three (or N) instances relative to the source portal. Optionally push a saved map pin to travellers on first use with `InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse", "Haldor", (int)Minimap.PinType.Icon3, pos, false)` — redundant once m_placed because vanilla's own icon appears, but useful for mode (b).


**Player experience:** Hover: `Portal tag:">Haldor" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, arrive a few metres outside the camp facing it. If mode (a) and the trader has never been generated, the hub's tag reads `>Haldor (unfound)` and the portal is deliberately left unconnected (hover shows `[unconnected]`, no glow) until someone discovers the camp on foot, at which point the maintenance tick creates the phantom and the tag flips within one tick.


**Failure modes:**
- Trader location names unverified until an in-game dump.
- Camp ZDOs (the trader NPC itself) do not exist until the zone is ghost-generated; arriving via portal in mode (b) triggers generation on the arriving client's own CreateGhostZones — expect a longer black screen on first arrival.
- m_exteriorRadius is Inspector data per location; if 0 the offset math needs a default (12 m).

- Unique locations have multiple candidate instances until one is placed (GenerateLocationsTimeSliced :114662-114669); RemoveUnplacedLocations (:114994-114996, :115005-115020) deletes the others after placement. ### 184. Dungeon / Crypt Entrances (interior ruled out)

`targeted-portals:Dungeon / Crypt Entrances (interior ruled out)` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portal to the surface entrance of a crypt/dungeon location; targeting the interior itself is possible geometrically but pairs a portal with a space the client only builds on demand, and crypt doors are invisible to the server.


**How it works:** Entrances are Locations (Crypt2/3/4, SunkenCrypt4, MountainCave02, GoblinCamp is not a dungeon, etc. — names from a boot dump of m_locations filtered on `m_hasInterior`-bearing prefabs, an Inspector flag readable only after the prefab loads; the mod can instead filter by name pattern confirmed in-game). Nearest-of-type: `FindClosestLocation(name, sourcePos, out inst)`; place the phantom (Option 1) `m_exteriorRadius + 3` m from `inst.m_position`. Many crypt entrances are on slopes (Black Forest burial chambers are half-buried, sunken crypts sit in swamp water at y≈30): validate with GetNormal.y and reject h<31 for swamp crypts or accept and set y=30.5. Interior: `Location.Awake` instantiates the interior at `(zoneCenter.x, surfaceY + 5000, zoneCenter.z)` and `Character.InInterior` is `y > 3000`, so the interior origin is derivable server-side and a phantom COULD be placed at (zoneCenter.x, surfaceY+5000+k, zoneCenter.z). RULED OUT in practice: the interior geometry is generated client-side from DungeonGenerator room data (`ZDOVars.s_roomData` byte blob on the DungeonGenerator ZDO, readable but unsearchable via GetAllZDOIDsWithHash), the safe floor of any room is unknown without colliders, the client's FindFloor over a 5000 m-high interior raycasts 1000 m down and would hit interior geometry only if the arrival point is above a room floor — otherwise the 15 s fallback uses GetSolidHeight from y+1000 (hits the dungeon roof mesh or nothing → keeps y). And building portals inside interiors is normally blocked (m_allowedInDungeons) unless GlobalKeys.DungeonBuild is set — a phantom bypasses that, which is a gameplay-policy concern. The crypt doors themselves (`class Teleport`) have no ZDO, no RPC, and a compiled `m_targetPoint` reference: a server-only mod cannot re-route, pair, or even enumerate them.


**Player experience:** Hover: `Portal tag:">Crypt" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, arrive outside the burial chamber entrance facing its door; the player walks through the vanilla crypt door (which ignores NoPortals and the ore check). Return by walking out and into the phantom. No map pin unless pushed.


**Failure modes:**
- Entrance locations are numerous (dozens per type); 'nearest' relative to the source is the only sane picker.
- Sunken crypts: arrival on swamp water at y≈30; phantom exit +1 m puts the player in knee-deep water — acceptable but wet.
- Interior targeting: unknown floor height, possible arrival inside a wall, and DungeonBuild policy bypass — do not ship.

**Open questions:**

- Does a phantom placed at a derived interior coordinate ever land a player on a room floor (interior test with a client, purely for the record)?

### 185. Biome Targets (nearest edge, centroid, nearest N, random-in-biome)

`targeted-portals:Biome Targets (nearest edge, centroid, nearest N, random-in-biome)` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portal into a biome using the server's precomputed 12 m biome/height grid and flood-filled biome sectors — no player, no ZDO scan.


**How it works:** `AltBiomeWorldData d = ZNet.World.m_biomeData` (populated in ZNet.ServerLoadWorld via VerifyBiomeData, disk-cached as biomedatacache.bin). Grid: 2048×2048 cells, 12 m each; `PointBiomes[x,y]`, `PointHeights[x,y]`, `PointSectors[x,y]`; convert with `WorldSpaceToMapSpace(float)` and `MapSpaceToWorldSpace(Vector2i)` (= (map−1024)*12+6). Nearest edge of biome B from the source: spiral outward in map space from the source cell until `PointBiomes==B && PointHeights>=31`; cost is O(cells searched), cache per (source, biome). Centroid: `d.Biomes[B].Sectors` gives every contiguous region as a BiomeSector with world-space `Center`, `Min`, `Max`, `HeightMin/Max/Avg`, `EdgeCount` (size proxy) and `DistanceFromCenter`; pick the largest by EdgeCount or nearest by `Vector2.Distance(Center, sourceXZ)`. Never use `BiomeSector.MinZone/MaxZone` (both computed from Min with z=0 — garbage). `Center` is a perimeter centroid and can fall outside a crescent-shaped region, so re-validate `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(x,z)==B` and walk toward the region's Min/Max interior if not. Nearest N: sort Sectors by distance, take N, emit N phantoms with tags `>Plains 1..N`. Random: `d.GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel(B)` (UnityEngine.Random; seed if reproducibility matters). Final point: `h = WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(x,z)` (exact, not the 12 m sample), reject lava (IsLavaPreHeightmap) and slopes (GetNormal.y<0.7), then Option 1 phantom at (x, h+0.2, z). Ashlands: `WorldGenerator.IsAshlands` and ashlandsMinDistance=12000 mark the boundary; Deep North via IsDeepnorth. Tick cost: all queries are array reads; centroid enumeration is O(sectors per biome), done once.


**Player experience:** Hover: `Portal tag:">Plains (nearest)" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, arrive on open ground just inside the biome edge, a real portal behind them for the return trip. For 'nearest N' the hub shows several portals side by side tagged `>Plains 1`, `>Plains 2`, each leading to a different region. Random mode re-rolls on a configurable timer; players see the tag change to `>Mistlands (random)` and the destination silently differ next transit.


**Failure modes:**
- Perimeter-centroid bug: without re-validation a 'Meadows centroid' can be in the Ocean.
- A biome edge cell adjacent to Ocean may be a beach at y≈31 — fine — or a cliff; the slope test rejects but the spiral must continue rather than stop.
- Random mode + phantom re-target requires destroy-and-recreate (portal prefab cannot be moved); do it only when nobody is within 100 m of the old phantom to avoid a visible pop (check ConnectedCharacters positions).

**Designer citations:** AltBiomeWorldData class assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:92332; c_pixelSize/c_halfWidth :92342-92346 ; AltBiomeWorldData.MapSpaceToWorldSpace/WorldSpaceToMapSpace assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:92414/:92424 ; AltBiomeWorldData.GenerateSectors assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:92476-92616 (MinZone/MaxZone bug :92577-92578; perimeter centroid :92531-92535) ; BiomeSector assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:93884-93925 ; AltBiomeWorldData.GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:92683 ; ZNet.ServerLoadWorld VerifyBiomeData assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79273-79285 ; WorldGenerator.GetBiome assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:151725; IsAshlands :151697; IsDeepnorth :151719 ; ZoneSystem.IsLavaPreHeightmap assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115637


**Open questions:**
- Memory footprint of BiomeTypeInfo.AllPoints lists on a dedicated server (log counts per biome at boot).

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- PointBiomes[x,y] is Heightmap.BiomeIndex (:92360); compare against `B.ToBiomeIndex()` (:129559) or convert with `.ToBiome()`.
- AshLands, DeepNorth, Ocean are single global sectors created up-front (:92481-92486) and filled in the first pass (:92487-92500); Biomes[AshLands].Sectors has one entry whose Center is the perimeter centroid of the whole ring - do not use centroid/nearest-N modes for those three biomes; use the spiral edge search or GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel.
- BiomeSector.HeightMin/HeightMax are computed only over edge cells (:92520-92556) and HeightAvg = (HeightMin+HeightMax)/2 (:92578) - they are not interior statistics.
- GetRandomPointByBiomeAboveSeaLevel falls back to any point (including underwater) when AllPointsAboveSeaLevel is empty (:92690-92693); always re-check GetHeight >= 30.
- IsAshlands boundary is DUtils.Length(x, y-4000) > 12000 + noise (:151697-151700), i.e. the Ashlands circle is centred at z=+4000; a plain 'distance from origin' test is wrong.
- Sector flood fill uses 4-neighbour adjacency on BiomeIndex equality (:92460-92470) - biome mask combinations (RandomBiomeFromBiomes) are only handled by the random helpers, not by Sectors.
- BiomeSector.Min is always (-12282,-12282) world: the field defaults to zero (SERVER:93906) and GenerateSectors only lowers it (92539-92550); do not use Min (or MinZone/MaxZone/ZoneCount). Max, Center, EdgeCount, HeightMin/Max are valid.
- AshLands, DeepNorth, Ocean each have exactly one pre-seeded sector (SERVER:92481-92503); centroid/nearest-N modes degenerate for them — use nearest-edge spiral or GetRandomPointByBiomesAboveSeaLevel.
- PointBiomes holds Heightmap.BiomeIndex (SERVER:92357); convert with ToBiomeIndex()/ToBiome() before comparing.
- Filter sectors by EdgeCount (single-cell sectors exist) and treat HeightAvg as (min+max)/2 of perimeter cells only (SERVER:92579).
- Apply the LoadFields `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false` override on phantoms; biome-edge terrain is steep and the owning vanilla client collapses a phantom floating >0.15 m (CLIENT:150361-150389, 150445-150450, 150781-150838).
- Random re-roll = destroy (needs ownership, ZDOMan.DestroyZDO SERVER:76927-76933) + recreate + rewrite hub connection before the next 5 s Game.ConnectPortals pass (SERVER:100592-100626).

The 'walk toward Min/Max interior' fallback must use Max/Center or a re-flood of PointSectors. (2) AshLands, DeepNorth and Ocean are pre-seeded as ONE sector each and skipped by the flood fill (92481-92503), so 'nearest N' and 'centroid' modes are meaningless for Ashlands/Deep North (single sector whose perimeter centroid lies in the ocean ring); use the spiral/nearest-edge or random-point modes there. (3) PointBiomes is Heightmap.BiomeIndex[,], not Biome (92357) — compare with B.ToBiomeIndex(). (4) Sectors include one-cell slivers; filter by EdgeCount before ranking. (5) HeightAvg is (HeightMin+HeightMax)/2 over edge cells (92579), not a real average. Arrival-side: same floating-collapse caveat — biome edges are often steep and WorldGenerator height ignores player terrain edits; apply the LoadFields WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false override (CLIENT:150361-150389, 150781-150838, 150445-150450). Random-mode re-roll must destroy-and-recreate with ownership claim and rewrite the hub connection inside the 5 s reconcile window (Game.ConnectPortals SERVER:100592-100626).

### 186. Named World-Gen Locations (generic) and LocationProxy ZDOs

`targeted-portals:Named World-Gen Locations (generic) and LocationProxy ZDOs` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Any location type by name — runestone camps, villages, tar pits, shipwrecks — from the registry; plus the ZDO-level LocationProxy index for 'only locations that physically exist'.


**How it works:** Registry route: `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locations` (List<ZoneLocation>) is the vocabulary (m_prefabName, m_biome, m_quantity, m_iconAlways/m_iconPlaced, m_exteriorRadius) and `GetLocationList()` / `FindLocations(name)` / `FindClosestLocation(name, point)` give instances. This is exactly what vanilla's `find` console command does. Build a name→List<LocationInstance> index once at OnWorldReady (thousands of entries; O(n) per query otherwise). Place the phantom (Option 1) outside m_exteriorRadius on the flattest sample. Materialised-only route: `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(ZDOExtraData.Type.Int, ZDOVars.s_location)` enumerates every LocationProxy ZDO in the world (one per placed location, written by LocationProxy.SetLocation with the location hash as an Int) — an unindexed full scan of every ZDO's int fields, so run it once and cache; each proxy ZDO's GetPosition() is the actual placed origin and its s_location int identifies the type. Use this when the design wants 'only places someone has already discovered/generated'. Config exposes a list of (label, locationName, mode=nearest|random|index) per hub; the maintenance tick creates missing phantoms and reaps ones whose config entry was removed. Locations never move, so no moving-target logic is needed; 'random' mode re-rolls on a timer with destroy-and-recreate.


**Player experience:** Hover: `Portal tag:">Tar Pit" [connected]`. Standard swirl, arrival outside the location's footprint facing it. For icon-flagged locations the vanilla map icon is already present; for others the mod can push a saved pin via RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse with the location's display name.


**Failure modes:**
- `SoftReference<GameObject>.Name` (used by FindClosestLocation) is in an assembly not in the decompile set; if it forces an asset load, index by ZoneLocation.m_prefabName (plain string) instead.
- GetAllZDOIDsWithHash default branch calls Debug.Break() for unsupported types — only pass Int here.
- Locations flagged m_snapToWater sit at y=30 regardless of m_position.y.

**Designer citations:** ZoneSystem.m_locations assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113248; SetupLocations :113619-113672 ; ZoneSystem.GetLocationList assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115999 ; Terminal 'find' helper assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:45602-45631 ; ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75390-75407 ; ZDOVars.s_location assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78501; LocationProxy.SetLocation :102653-102659 ; ZoneSystem.PlaceLocations m_snapToWater assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:114963-114968


**Open questions:**

- Is SoftReference.Name a cheap string property?

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- The 'find' Terminal helper (SERVER:45602-45631) is a static local function that also calls UnityEngine.Object.FindObjectsOfType and GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative; it is not a server-side template. Drop the 'exactly what vanilla's find does' framing - only the m_locationInstances loop is relevant.
- Registry position vs. placed position differ: PlaceLocations snaps p via GetGroundData (collider raycast) and forces p.y=30 for m_snapToWater (SERVER:114961-114968) before creating the proxy ZDO, while LocationInstance.m_position.y is WorldGenerator height (SERVER:114737). Compute phantom y from WorldGenerator, never from the registry y, and treat the proxy ZDO position as the true origin when available.
- m_placed is only ever set on the server's own copy (SERVER:114985-114991) because only the server spawns in Full/Ghost mode (SERVER:114028, 114086) - it is authoritative on the dedicated server, which strengthens the 'materialised-only' route; the Int scan is not needed just to learn 'placed', only to get the snapped origin.
- Hash->ZoneLocation mapping: ZoneSystem.m_locationsByHash (SERVER:113250) is private; either publicize it or rebuild the map from m_locations using m_prefab.Name.GetStableHashCode() (as SetLocation does at SERVER:102655).
- Enforcement is server-enforced only in the 'route' sense; the ore/NoPortals/boss checks in TeleportWorld.Teleport (SERVER:143520-143533) run on the client.
- Replace the GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Int, s_location) full scan with LocationInstance.m_placed (S:113001-113008, persisted via ZoneSystem.Load S:113813-113817) and ZoneSystem.m_locationIDCache (S:113297); the ZDO scan adds nothing and is O(all ZDO int fields).
- Random-mode re-roll MUST destroy-and-recreate the phantom rather than SetPosition it: portal ZDOs never re-bucket (ZDO.SetSector returns early for PortalPrefabHash; portals live in m_portalObjects keyed by creation sector, S:77738-77752, and are excluded from m_objectsBySector so Wonderland's sector sweepers never see them).
- RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse side effect: Player.SetLookDir toward the pin for 3.5 s when the map is closed (S:100825-100830); pin is saved and cannot be removed remotely.
- For m_snapToWater locations (shipwrecks) the phantom must be placed on land found by WorldGenerator height >= 30 or the traveller exits into water; FindFloor (C:116244) hits seabed terrain so the teleport still completes, they just swim.
- Location terrain is levelled inside the location radius by TerrainModifiers that pure WorldGenerator math does not see; keep the phantom outside m_exteriorRadius as written.

The actual transit remains client-executed (TeleportWorld.Teleport SERVER:143516-143548).

### 187. Player's Bed

`targeted-portals:Player's Bed` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portal to a bed a player has claimed, found by scanning bed ZDOs for ZDOVars.s_owner == the player's stable profile ID.


**How it works:** Identity: the player's stable ID is `characterZdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_playerID)` (ConnectedCharacters.PlayerId); never peer.m_uid (session) and never peer.m_playerID (always 0 — the PlayerID RPC is never invoked by a vanilla client). Bed ownership: Bed.RPC_SetOwner writes `s_owner` (long = profile UID) and `s_ownerName` into the bed's own ZDO, persistent and offline-readable. Discovery: bed prefab names are asset data; enumerate `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs` at OnWorldReady and keep hashes of prefabs with a Bed component (Wonderland ContainerRegistry pattern), then run ZdoSpatialQuery.PrefabSetSweeper over those hashes with a sector budget to build a map playerId→List<(ZDOID, pos)>; incrementally maintain it with the SpawnGovernor CreateNewZDO+Deserialize postfix pair (new bed ZDOs) and ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed (removed beds); watch s_owner on a slow tick because claiming happens later than placement. Ambiguity: vanilla lets a player own unlimited beds and never clears s_owner — 'the player's bed' must be chosen by rule: (a) the bed nearest the player's last known position, (b) the most recently claimed (mod records the tick it first saw s_owner set), (c) the one the player was last seen sleeping in — infer from `characterZdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_inBed)` and match the character position to the nearest bed ZDO within 2 m (Game.EverybodyIsTryingToSleep reads the same field server-side). Placement: the bed's spawn offset (Bed.m_spawnPoint child Transform) is not in the ZDO; place the phantom (Option 1) 3–4 m from the bed ZDO position along the flattest compass sample with a piece-proximity check (FindNear 2 m) to avoid dropping the phantom inside the player's own walls — imperfect without colliders. Because a bed is inside a base, the arrival exit may hit a wall; the client's FindFloor still lands them on the floor piece (piece layer is in m_solidRayMask). Per-player hub: a single 'Home' hub portal cannot be per-player (one connection per ZDO); implement as one phantom per player, re-targeted when the requesting player emotes (EmoteSignals) — or use the two-hop relay (Option 20).


**Player experience:** The player stands at the 'Home' hub, performs the configured emote (e.g. /wave); within 0.25 s the server writes the hub's tag to `>Home: Rohan` and links it to a phantom beside Rohan's bed; a toast says `Home portal set to your bed`. They walk in, 8 s swirl, step out next to their bed inside their base. The phantom stays there (they can return through it). Another player emoting at the hub re-targets it for themselves; hover text changes for everyone nearby.


**Failure modes:**
- Beds inside cramped houses: arrival point may be inside a wall or on a roof; the mod can only approximate structure clearance from piece ZDO positions.
- A player with no claimed bed: fall back to StartTemple with a toast.
- Shared hub re-targeting is a race between players; a per-player phantom per hub or the relay option removes it.
- Bed destroyed: bed ZDO vanishes → phantom orphaned; maintenance tick reaps it and toasts the owner.

**Designer citations:** Bed.RPC_SetOwner assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:119813-119819; Bed.GetOwner :119822-119829 ; Bed.Interact never clears ownership assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:119670-119725 ; Bed.GetSpawnPoint child Transform assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:119796-119799 ; Player.SetPlayerID / ZDOVars.s_playerID assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:10129-10136; :78539 ; ZNet.RPC_PlayerID never invoked (client grep) assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:80108 ; Game.EverybodyIsTryingToSleep s_inBed assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100735-100748 ; Player.AttachStart/AttachStop s_inBed assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15799, :15917 ; ZdoSpatialQuery.PrefabSetSweeper Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:135-153 ; SpawnGovernor CreateNewZDO+Deserialize postfixes Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43-70 ; ZoneSystem.m_solidRayMask includes piece layer assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:113424


**Open questions:**
- Do all bed prefabs carry both Piece (s_creator) and Bed (s_owner) on the same ZDO?
- Is s_inBed set for chairs/ship seats too (AttachStart isBed param) — if so the sleep-inference must also require night-time or a Bed prefab within 2 m.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Ownership churn on the phantom: ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands every PERSISTENT ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer whenever the current owner is not in its own active area, and the server's session is never 'in area' because its ref pos is (1e6,0,1e6) (IsInPeerActiveArea SERVER:77268-77280; ReleaseNearbyZDOS SERVER:77282-77306). A phantom parked beside a bed inside a base will therefore be client-owned whenever anyone is home. ZDO.Set(...) still propagates (IncreaseDataRevision unconditional, SERVER:73600-73607) but ZDO.SetPosition only bumps DataRevision when IsOwner (SERVER:73734-73745) - so any re-positioning must SetOwner(session) first, or use a non-persistent phantom (RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS keeps m_sessionID-owned ZDOs: IsPeerConnected SERVER:77423-77435).
- 'the player's bed' identity gating is NOT enforced: the server sets the route, but any vanilla client near the hub can walk through after the retarget (TeleportWorld.Teleport SERVER:143516-143548 has no identity check). State this explicitly in the option.
- Bed index keyed by ZDOID must be rebuilt on every boot (ZDOIDs are session-scoped; prior-session note) - the PrefabSetSweeper pass is the boot path, the SpawnGovernor postfix pair only covers incremental arrivals.
- The client-side FindFloor claim is right about the mask but note FindFloor raycasts 1000 m down (SERVER:  ZoneSystem.FindFloor), so it returns true even when the frozen target is above a roof; arrival inside a multi-storey base can land on the roof/upper floor, not necessarily beside the bed.
- Sleeping requires the bed to be the CURRENT custom spawn point (Bed.Interact: IsMine() && IsCurrent() before AttachStart, S:119691-119714; IsCurrent S:119790-119793). s_inBed + nearest bed ZDO therefore identifies the active spawn bed exactly — make rule (c) the primary rule, (a)/(b) fallbacks only.
- Return trip is single-slot: once any other player emotes at the hub, the previous phantom is disconnected by Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 (S:100597-100604) and cannot be re-paired. Say so in playerExperience; reap stale phantoms.
- FindFloor (C:116244) does not relocate the player; UpdateTeleport pins them at phantom pos + forward*1 + up*1 (C:15347-15370). Wall-adjacent placement leaves them inside geometry. Piece layer being in the mask only affects when the swirl ends.
- Phantom is a genuine portal_wood ZDO: retaggable via RPC_SetTag on the owner client (S:143583-143600) and deletable via the ungated DestroyZDO path (S:76953-76960). The mod must re-assert.
- Server writes to hub/phantom must SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()) first and ForceSendZDO; ReleaseNearbyZDOS (S:76901-76926) returns ownership to a nearby peer within 2 s; tag-only writes need ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals (S:76702) or are lost at save.
- Wonderland PrefabSetSweeper walks m_objectsBySector only (ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:153-176) — fine for beds, but it will never enumerate portal ZDOs (AddIfPortal removes them from the sector map, S:77738-77752).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Bed.RPC_SetOwner writes s_owner (long) and s_ownerName into the bed ZDO on the ZDO owner (SERVER:119813-119819), triggered from Bed.Interact's owner==0 branch (SERVER:119683-119692); no code path in Bed ever clears s_owner. Bed.GetOwner reads s_owner (SERVER:119822-119829). Player.SetPlayerID writes s_playerID/s_playerName once (SERVER:10129-10136; s_playerID SERVER:78539). The client only REGISTERS the 'PlayerID' RPC (CLIENT:80108) and never invokes it - peer.m_playerID stays 0, so the character-ZDO route for identity is correct. s_inBed is written by Player.AttachStart(isBed) (SERVER:15799) and cleared in AttachStop (SERVER:15917); Game.EverybodyIsTryingToSleep reads it server-side from GetAllCharacterZDOS (SERVER:100735-100748). Bed.GetSpawnPoint is a child Transform (SERVER:119796-119799), not in the ZDO. m_solidRayMask includes 'piece' (SERVER:113424). Wonderland helpers cited exist (ZdoSpatialQuery.PrefabSetSweeper:135-153, SpawnGovernor postfixes:43-70, EmoteSignals reads s_emote/s_emoteID which Player.StartEmote writes at SERVER:15592-15595). ZNetScene.m_prefabs is public (SERVER:81921). Route selection is server-owned; the rest of the mechanism holds.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Identity and ownership chain verified: Bed.Interact claims via SetOwner(profile.GetPlayerID(), name) -> RPC_SetOwner writes s_owner/s_ownerName on the owner client (S:119680-119690, S:119813-119819); Player.SetPlayerID writes s_playerID/s_playerName on the character ZDO (S:10129-10135); the client registers 'PlayerID' (C:80108) but never invokes it, so peer.m_playerID is 0 — s_playerID is the correct key and it equals the bed's s_owner. s_inBed is written by AttachStart/AttachStop (S:15799, S:15917) and read server-side by EverybodyIsTryingToSleep (S:100744). Bed.Interact never clears s_owner. GetSpawnPoint is a child Transform (S:119796-119799), not in the ZDO. Route mechanics hold (mutual tag + connection between hub and a server-created portal ZDO is a fixed point of Game.ConnectPortals S:100589-100626). Corrections: (a) the disambiguation rule is stronger than stated — Bed.Interact only allows AttachStart when IsMine() AND IsCurrent() (S:119691-119714; IsCurrent compares GetSpawnPoint to the profile's custom spawn point within 1 m, S:119790-119793), so s_inBed + nearest bed identifies the player's ACTIVE spawn bed, not merely a candidate; prefer rule (c). (b) 'The phantom stays there (they can return through it)' is only true until another player re-targets the hub: when the hub's tag/connection moves to phantom B, phantom A's target now has a different tag so ConnectPortals pass 1 nulls A's connection (S:100597-100604) and pass 2 finds no same-tag partner — A becomes a dead portal at Rohan's base until reaped. (c) FindFloor does not 'land' anyone: Player.UpdateTeleport pins transform.position = m_teleportTargetPos (phantom pos + forward*1 + up*1) and FindFloor only decides when teleporting ends (C:15331-15370, mask C:114064 includes 'piece'); the traveller drops by physics from 1 m up, so a phantom whose forward faces a wall <1 m away leaves them inside geometry. (d) A server-written phantom is a real portal_wood piece: the owner can retag it (RPC_SetTag) or WearNTear-destroy it, and ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO has no ownership check. (e) The server's ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands the hub and phantom (persistent) to nearby peers every 2 s (S:76901-76926); writes must SetOwner(session) first so the DataRevision bump propagates (ZDO.InternalSetPosition/Set only bump when IsOwner for position, C:73849-73858), and tag writes need SetDirtyPortals (S:76702) because ZDO.Set only dirties chunks (S:73832-73840, S:76707).

### 188. Player's Custom Spawn Point (direct read ruled out; inference feasible)

`targeted-portals:Player's Custom Spawn Point (direct read ruled out; inference feasible)` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** reactive-detection-only → **reactive-detection-only** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The active spawn point lives only in the client's .fch profile and is never networked; the server can infer it from peer.m_refPos while the player is dead and from sleep events.


**How it works:** RULED OUT as a direct read: `PlayerProfile.WorldPlayerData.m_spawnPoint/m_haveCustomSpawnPoint` are written by Bed.Interact's non-claim branch via `Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().SetCustomSpawnPoint(...)` with no RPC and no ZDO write, and ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles only tells clients to save their own files. No packet ever carries it. INFERENCE 1 (respawn leak): Game.UpdateRespawn on the client calls `ZNet.instance.SetReferencePosition(customSpawnPoint)` (or the logout point on login, or the StartTemple icon) while the character is dead; the client's periodic ServerSyncedPlayerData (every 2 s) then delivers that reference position into `peer.m_refPos`. Server logic: on `characterZdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_dead)==true` (or peer.m_characterID.IsNone() after RPC_CharacterID(None) in _RequestRespawn), sample peer.m_refPos over the next few seconds; the stable value before the new character ZDO appears is the spawn point. Persist it in a mod file keyed by playerID. INFERENCE 2 (sleep): `s_inBed==true` on the character ZDO plus nearest bed ZDO within 2 m → that bed is at least a candidate; vanilla only lets you sleep in a bed you own, and most players sleep in their spawn bed. INFERENCE 3 (login leak): on first RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData after PeerInfo, m_refPos equals the logout point (Game.UpdateRespawn uses HaveLogoutPoint first), a good proxy for 'home'. Combine: spawn-point candidate = INFERENCE 1 if ever observed, else INFERENCE 2, else INFERENCE 3, else bed rule from Option 10. Then Option 1 phantom near that point, or Option 20 relay. The mod cannot SET a player's spawn point either (Bed.Interact is local).


**Player experience:** Identical to Option 10 from the player's side (`>Home` hub, emote to claim, arrive beside their bed). Difference: the destination matches where they actually respawn, but only after the mod has observed at least one death/respawn or login of that player on this server; before that, a toast explains `No home known yet — using your nearest bed`.


**Failure modes:**
- Never-died, never-relogged players have no INFERENCE 1 sample; fall back to bed/login heuristics.
- peer.m_refPos is also written during ordinary play (position lagging ≤2 s); the sampling window must be strictly gated on s_dead / characterID None.
- A player who changes spawn bed after the last observation is targeted at the stale point until they die or relog.
- Cross-world profiles: WorldPlayerData is per world UID, so a stale spawn point from another world is never leaked — only this world's.

**Designer citations:** PlayerProfile.WorldPlayerData / SetCustomSpawnPoint assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:105526-105545; :106224-106238 ; Bed.Interact non-claim branch (local only) assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:119719-119725 ; ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79653-79670 ; Game.FindSpawnPoint SetReferencePosition(logout/custom/StartTemple) assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100313-100375 ; ZNet.RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData writes peer.m_refPos assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:80395-80410; 2 s cadence :80337-80345 ; Player.IsDead → ZDOVars.s_dead assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15244; OnDeath :12734 ; Game._RequestRespawn SetCharacterID(None) assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100403-100417


**Open questions:**
- Exact timing: how many ServerSyncedPlayerData packets arrive between death and the new character ZDO (determines how reliable the refPos sample is).
- Is m_refPos updated during the loading screen at all, or only after the new Player is spawned?

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Trigger on peer.m_characterID.IsNone(), NOT on s_dead: Player.OnDeath sets s_dead then calls Game.RequestRespawn(10f, afterDeath:true) (SERVER:12847); for those 10 s the local Player still exists and Player.Update keeps ref pos at the corpse (SERVER:11070-11074). Only after _RequestRespawn destroys the player and sends CharacterID(None) does FindSpawnPoint (called from UpdateRespawn while m_requestRespawn, CLIENT:100937-100941) drive the ref pos. The window is at least m_respawnLoadDuration = 8 s (SERVER:100295), i.e. >=3 periodic sends.
- If the player has no custom spawn point (or its bed is gone: ClearCustomSpawnPoint at SERVER:100357 then falls through next tick), the leaked ref pos is the StartTemple icon + 2 up (SERVER:100365-100369). The mod must compare the sample against ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(StartTemple) and discard it, or it will record the spawn temple as 'home'.
- The leaked value is the bed's m_spawnPoint.position captured at claim time (SERVER:119689/119724, GetSpawnPoint SERVER:119796-119799), not the bed ZDO position; FindBedNearby tolerates 5 m (SERVER:100350). Match beds within ~5 m, not 2 m.
- peer.m_refPos is never blanked by the privacy flag (SERVER:80399-80400 unconditional); only the player-list position is (UpdatePlayerList). The option's login inference therefore works for privacy-off players too.
- The SetReferencePosition calls live in Game.FindSpawnPoint (SERVER:100313-100375), not in UpdateRespawn itself; UpdateRespawn only calls it (CLIENT:100939).
- Sleep observation (s_inBed on the character ZDO while within ~1 m of a bed ZDO) proves the bed is the CURRENT custom spawn point, because Bed.Interact requires IsMine() && IsCurrent() before AttachStart (S:119691-119714, IsCurrent S:119790-119793). Promote INFERENCE 2 above INFERENCE 3.
- Respawn leak has a second, exact channel: the new character ZDO's initial position after a death equals bed.GetSpawnPoint() (Game.FindSpawnPoint C:100784-100791 -> UpdateRespawn/SpawnPlayer C:100937-100947) or StartTemple pos + 2 m if no custom point.
- INFERENCE 3 is wrong as 'home': on login the logout point branch is taken first (C:100746-100774) and the custom-spawn branch never runs; peer.m_refPos on login is the quit position, which is at best 'last seen', not home.
- Window sizing: m_respawnLoadDuration = 8 s (C:100295) and periodic send cadence 2 s (C:80532) → ≥3 refPos samples of the spawn point per death; s_dead is visible on the old character ZDO for ~10 s before it is destroyed (C:12849, C:100831-100845).
- Observed spawn points can go stale: FindSpawnPoint calls ClearCustomSpawnPoint when no Bed is within 5 m (C:100793-100801); a destroyed bed silently reverts the player to StartTemple with no signal to the server other than the next respawn refPos.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Direct read correctly ruled out: PlayerProfile.WorldPlayerData.m_spawnPoint/m_haveCustomSpawnPoint (SERVER:105526-105545) are set by SetCustomSpawnPoint (SERVER:106224-106238) from Bed.Interact (SERVER:119689, 119724) with no RPC/ZDO write; ZNet.SaveOtherPlayerProfiles just invokes 'SavePlayerProfile' on peers (SERVER:79653-79670). The respawn leak is real: Game.FindSpawnPoint calls ZNet.SetReferencePosition(logoutPoint | customSpawnPoint | StartTemple pos) (SERVER:100317, 100346, 100367) and the client's SendServerSyncPlayerData writes m_referencePosition unconditionally every 2 s (CLIENT SendPeriodicData/SendServerSyncPlayerData; server RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData writes peer.m_refPos SERVER:80395-80410, cadence SERVER:80337-80345). RPC_CharacterID sets peer.m_characterID (server) after _RequestRespawn sends ZDOID.None (SERVER:100403-100417). Inference is reactive by nature - enforcement label is right.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Direct-read ruling confirmed: Bed.Interact's non-claim branch calls Game.instance.GetPlayerProfile().SetCustomSpawnPoint(GetSpawnPoint()) with no RPC/ZDO write (S:119719-119731); nothing networks WorldPlayerData. Respawn leak confirmed and STRONGER than described: client Game.FindSpawnPoint (C:100741-100813) calls ZNet.SetReferencePosition(customSpawnPoint) every frame while m_requestRespawn, waits m_respawnWait > m_respawnLoadDuration (8 s, C:100295) plus IsAreaReady, and the client's SendPeriodicData pushes m_referencePosition to the server every 2 s regardless of the privacy flag (C:80529-80568; server RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData writes peer.m_refPos S:80395-80404) — so at least 3-4 samples equal the custom spawn point exactly. Then SpawnPlayer places the new character at bed.GetSpawnPoint() (C:100786-100791), so the first position of the new character ZDO after a death is itself the spawn point. Death timeline: Player.OnDeath sets s_dead (C:12736) and RequestRespawn(10f, afterDeath:true) (C:12849); _RequestRespawn destroys the character and sends CharacterID(None) (C:100831-100845, C:81080). Sleep inference is also stronger: Bed.Interact only allows sleeping when IsCurrent() (S:119691-119714), so s_inBed ⇒ that bed IS the active spawn point at that moment. Correction to INFERENCE 3: on login (m_respawnAfterDeath false) FindSpawnPoint uses the LOGOUT point, which is wherever the player quit — not a 'home' proxy — and the logout branch runs before the custom-spawn branch, so login never leaks the spawn point. Also: if no bed exists within 5 m of the custom point at respawn, ClearCustomSpawnPoint runs and the player falls back to StartTemple (C:100793-100801), so an observed refPos may be a spawn point the client has since cleared. Enforcement 'reactive-detection-only' is honest.

### 189. Player's Death Spot / Tombstone

`targeted-portals:Player's Death Spot / Tombstone` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portal to a player's most recent tombstone, read straight off the TombStone container ZDO (owner, time of death, death position, and even the items).


**How it works:** Player.CreateTombStone (client) instantiates the tombstone prefab and TombStone.Setup writes `ZDOVars.s_ownerName` (string) and `ZDOVars.s_owner` (long = profile UID); TombStone.Awake on the owner writes `s_timeOfDeath` (ZNet time ticks) and `s_spawnPoint` (the death position) once. The tombstone is a real persistent ZDO in the sector map. Detection: the SpawnGovernor CreateNewZDO(prefab 0)+ZDO.Deserialize postfix pair sees every client-created ZDO the instant it arrives; filter on the tombstone prefab hash (asset name unknown in the decompile — discover at boot by scanning ZNetScene.m_prefabs for a TombStone component, or match the first ZDO carrying both s_ownerName and s_timeOfDeath) and index playerId→(ZDOID, pos, ticks). Alternatively bootstrap with `ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Long, ZDOVars.s_timeOfDeath)` once at boot (s_timeOfDeath is written only by TombStone). Filter by prefab because `s_owner` is also used by Bed (profile UID) and GrapplingPoint (a ZDOID.ID). Target: the newest tombstone for the requesting player (max s_timeOfDeath); place the phantom (Option 1) 3 m from `zdo.GetPosition()` on the flattest sample (deaths are often on slopes, in water, or in lava — validate with GetHeight/IsLavaPreHeightmap and if the death spot is underwater, walk toward the nearest cell with PointHeights≥31). Lifecycle: the tombstone despawns when emptied (TombStone.UpdateDespawn) and the ZDO is destroyed → ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed fires → reap the phantom and clear the hub link, toast the player `Your grave has been recovered`. Optional flourish: read the tombstone's `s_items` blob via ZdoInventoryIO.Load to toast `12 items waiting`, and push a saved map pin via RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse (PinType.Death) — vanilla already adds a death pin client-side, so only useful as a named marker.


**Player experience:** Player dies in the Plains, respawns at their bed, walks to the `>Grave` hub portal and performs the claim emote; toast `Grave portal set: 2 min ago, 14 items`; hover reads `Portal tag:">Grave: Rohan" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, arrive 3 m from their skull marker with a portal behind them for the return trip. Once they loot the grave it despawns; the phantom is removed on the next tick (visibly vanishing if they are still standing there) and the hub tag reverts to `>Grave (none)` / unconnected.


**Failure modes:**
- Death in deep water/lava: the phantom must be displaced to the nearest land; the arrival is then a swim/run away.
- Death near a boss/mob camp: arrival drops the player straight back into danger — a 'safe radius' from the death spot (10–20 m) is advisable.
- The tombstone's s_items blob only lands once the owning client's Container ticks after MoveInventoryToGrave; item count may read 0 for a second.
- Tombstone prefab name unverified (assumed Player_tombstone).

**Designer citations:** Player.CreateTombStone assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:12702-12714 ; TombStone.Setup assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:19845-19853 ; TombStone.Awake s_timeOfDeath/s_spawnPoint assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:19732-19740 ; TombStone.UpdateDespawn assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:19875-19890 ; ZDOVars.s_owner overload (GrapplingPoint) assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:127909 ; ZDOExtraData.GetAllZDOIDsWithHash assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:75390-75407 ; ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76033; invoked :76975 ; ZdoInventoryIO.Load Wonderland/Core/Data/ZdoInventoryIO.cs ; Game.RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100823-100831


**Open questions:**
- Tombstone prefab name/hash (kill a test character and log the new ZDO's prefab).
- Does s_spawnPoint on the tombstone differ from GetPosition() once the ragdoll body settles (m_body velocity in Setup)?

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- 's_timeOfDeath is written only by TombStone' is FALSE: Corpse.Awake (class SERVER:5444, write SERVER:5460-5463) writes the same key for creature corpses. The Long-scan bootstrap must additionally require s_owner != 0 / s_ownerName present (Corpse writes neither) or filter by prefab hash.
- Do not use s_spawnPoint as a discriminator or as the death position: it is also written by BaseAI (SERVER:25933-25936), Fish (SERVER:126104-126107), RandomFlyingBird (SERVER:137940-137943) and the legacy ZDO loader (SERVER:74399). Use zdo.GetPosition() - the tombstone has a Rigidbody + Floating (SERVER:19730-19733) and can drift/float to the surface.
- A tombstone only exists when the inventory was non-empty and DeathKeepInventory is unset (SERVER:12694-12695); the '(none)' state is the common case for empty-handed deaths.
- Despawn runs only on the ZDO-owning CLIENT (SERVER:19883 `if (m_nview.IsOwner())`); the server never runs UpdateDespawn. An emptied grave whose area nobody is loading stays as a ZDO until a client instantiates it - the phantom reap will lag until then.
- Index keyed by ZDOID must be rebuilt each boot (ZDOIDs are session-scoped); the boot scan is mandatory, not optional.
- s_timeOfDeath is ALSO written by Corpse.Awake (S:5460-5462) — bootstrap scans on (Type.Long, s_timeOfDeath) must additionally require s_ownerName (string) or match the tombstone prefab hash discovered from ZNetScene.m_prefabs.
- No tombstone is created when the inventory is empty or GlobalKeys.DeathKeepInventory is set (Player.CreateTombStone C:12696); the feature has nothing to target for such deaths — toast accordingly.
- Return-trip portal beside the grave is single-slot: re-targeting the hub for another player disconnects it (Game.ConnectPortals S:100597-100604).
- Tombstone ZDO position moves (Floater/Rigidbody, TombStone.PositionCheck/UpdateFloater S:19882-19886); keep using zdo.GetPosition() and re-place the phantom if it drifts >N m.
- Server-created phantom writes need SetOwner(session) + ForceSendZDO and SetDirtyPortals for tag writes (S:76702); ReleaseNearbyZDOS (S:76901-76926) reassigns persistent ZDOs near players every 2 s.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [decompile:confirmed-with-correction] Player.CreateTombStone instantiates m_tombstone and calls TombStone.Setup(name, playerID) (SERVER:12692-12714); Setup writes s_ownerName + s_owner (SERVER:19845-19853); TombStone.Awake on the owner writes s_timeOfDeath (ZNet time ticks) and s_spawnPoint once (SERVER:19728-19741); UpdateDespawn destroys via m_nview.Destroy when empty (SERVER:19875-19890). ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed (SERVER:76033) is invoked in RPC_DestroyZDO (SERVER:76975-76978). GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Long, ...) exists (SERVER:75390-75407). s_owner is also written by Bed (SERVER:119817) and GrapplingPoint with a ZDOID.ID (SERVER:127909, class at 127731). RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse (SERVER:100823-100831) pushes a pin. Route selection is server-owned; mechanism holds with corrections.
- [vanilla-reality:confirmed-with-correction] Chain verified: client Player.CreateTombStone instantiates m_tombstone at GetCenterPoint() and calls TombStone.Setup(name, profile.GetPlayerID()) (C:12694-12716); Setup writes s_ownerName and s_owner (S:19845-19853); TombStone.Awake on the owner writes s_timeOfDeath and s_spawnPoint once (S:19735-19738); UpdateDespawn destroys via m_nview.Destroy() on the owner when the container is empty and not in use (S:19875-19890) → RPC_DestroyZDO → HandleDestroyedZDO fires m_onZDODestroyed on the server (S:76953-76977). GrapplingPoint overloads s_owner with a ZDOID.ID (S:127909) — prefab filtering is required as stated. GetAllZDOIDsWithHash(Type.Long, hash) exists (S:75390-75407). Refuted sub-claim: 's_timeOfDeath is written only by TombStone' — Corpse.Awake writes the same key (S:5444-5463), so a boot scan on s_timeOfDeath also returns every Corpse container ZDO; additionally require s_ownerName or the tombstone prefab hash. Also unstated: no tombstone exists at all when the inventory was empty or GlobalKeys.DeathKeepInventory is set (C:12696), and tombstones have a Floater/Rigidbody so the live ZDO position (not s_spawnPoint) is the right coordinate — the option already uses GetPosition(). Same single-slot return caveat as the bed option: the phantom's return link dies the moment another player re-targets the hub (ConnectPortals pass 1, S:100597-100604). Mechanism is server-authored route; verdict holds with corrections.

### 190. Player's Ship (moving vehicle)

`targeted-portals:Player's Ship (moving vehicle)` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium-large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portal toward a ship a player is steering or riding; the destination can be the Ship ZDO itself (live position) but vanilla's 8-second frozen-snapshot teleport guarantees the traveller lands in the water behind a moving boat.


**How it works:** Which ship: (a) confirmed signal — `shipZdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_user)` equals the helmsman's stable playerID (written by ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl on the ship's own ZDO, zeroed on release) — Wonderland ShipAttachment.IsSteeringShip already implements a 40 m scan; (b) passenger signal — `characterZdo.GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.SyncTransform)` gives the Rigidbody+ZNetView parent the rider stands on, written by ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync only if the Player prefab's `m_characterParentSync` Inspector bool is on (unverified); prefab-check the target for a Ship component before trusting it, cross-check `shipPos + shipRot*GetVec3(s_relPosHash) ≈ playerPos` to reject stale latches. Destination choice 1 — point the source portal DIRECTLY at the Ship ZDO: `src.SetConnection(Portal, shipZdo.m_uid)`; TeleportWorld.Teleport reads the ship ZDO's live position/rotation at the instant of transit with no prefab check. But Game.ConnectPortals nulls it within 5 s unless the ship ZDO carries the same s_tag AND a reciprocal Portal connection — writing `shipZdo.Set(s_tag, tag)` and `shipZdo.SetConnection(Portal, src.m_uid)` is safe (ships never hold a SyncTransform parent of their own, and a ZDO has exactly one connection slot), but it means the ship's ZDO now carries a Portal link that must be scrubbed when the feature ends. Also the client fetches the ship ZDO once (TargetFound→RequestZDO) and never re-requests, so the server must `ForceSendZDO(peer, shipUid)` on a tick for peers standing at the source to keep the position fresh. Destination choice 2 — a moving Invisible Anchor (Option 2) re-positioned every tick to `shipPos + shipRot*(-forward*6)` (behind the stern) with `a.SetOwner(session); a.SetPosition(...)`: no writes on the ship, but the same ForceSendZDO requirement. Arrival physics: Player.UpdateTeleport snapshots m_teleportTargetPos once, pins the player there from t>2 s, and for distantTeleport waits until t>8 s AND IsAreaReady; FindFloor's mask omits the vehicle layer so the deck never counts as floor — the traveller lands at sea level behind wherever the ship was 8 s ago. Recommended product: 'portal to the ship' only for anchored/moored ships (velocity ≈0 from position deltas), arriving in the water 5 m astern; for moving ships use the Two-hop Relay (Option 20) which re-teleports to the live position.


**Player experience:** At the `>Ship` hub the player emotes; toast `Linked to Rohan's longship (moored)`; hover `Portal tag:">Ship: Rohan" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, splash into the water a few metres behind the boat, swim to the ladder. If the ship was sailing, they surface 50–100 m behind it in open sea with no portal to return through. If the helmsman lets go of the tiller (s_user→0) the mod keeps the last ship for a grace period then unlinks with a toast.


**Failure modes:**
- 8 s frozen snapshot: landing on a moving deck is impossible in vanilla; open-sea arrival with no return portal.
- m_characterParentSync unverified → passenger detection may not exist; helmsman-only (s_user) is the safe subset.
- Writing tag/connection onto a Ship ZDO is invasive; if the mod is removed the ship keeps a Portal connection (vanilla ignores it because the ship is not in the portal list, but the source portal stays linked until reconciled).
- Continuous ForceSendZDO of a ship ZDO to every peer near the source costs ~100 bytes/peer/cycle.
- Ship destroyed/despawned: GetZDO null → reconcile clears the link within 5 s.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Server writes on the client-owned ship ZDO propagate because ZDO.Set/SetConnection bump DataRevision unconditionally (SERVER:73600-73607, 73656-73665), and the owner's subsequent higher-revision update is accepted by RPC_ZDOData whose Deserialize is ADDITIVE (ZDOExtraData.Add; the connection is only replaced if the packet carries one, SERVER ZDO.Deserialize) - so tag+connection survive on the server copy. But the OWNER client never receives them (ShouldSend false after its own update, SERVER:76003-76013) and exactly one owner position update is dropped by the `num4 <= DataRevision` check in RPC_ZDOData. Harmless, but 'safe' needs this reasoning, not 'ships have no connection'.
- Save boundary: a ship<->hub Portal link is serialised by RegenerateConnectionHashData as a (Portal,hash)/(Portal|Target,hash) pair on BOTH ZDOs regardless of prefab (SERVER:75461-75478) and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals re-links them at load and SetOwner(session) on both (SERVER:77850-77889). The ship keeps the s_tag string and Portal connection across restarts unless the mod scrubs at boot as well as at feature end.
- s_user goes stale: only the ship-owner client clears it via RPC_ReleaseControl (SERVER:141344-141350); a helmsman who disconnects mid-sail leaves s_user set forever. Cross-check the playerID against ConnectedCharacters before trusting it (the option's grace period should be a hard timeout).
- Direct ship link arrival point is shipPos + shipRot*forward*1 + up (SERVER:143541-143546) - 1 m ahead of the ship pivot, i.e. inside the hull; FindFloor raycasts 1000 m down through 'terrain' (seabed) so it returns true over open water and ends the teleport at that frozen point. Use the anchor variant only.
- Anchor ownership: a PERSISTENT server-owned anchor is handed to the nearest peer every 2 s by ReleaseNearbyZDOS (Persistent-only loop, SERVER:77282-77306; the server session is never 'in area', IsInPeerActiveArea SERVER:77268-77280), after which SetPosition no longer bumps DataRevision (SERVER:73734-73745) and updates stop. Either make the anchor non-persistent (RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS keeps m_sessionID-owned ZDOs: IsPeerConnected SERVER:77423-77435) or accept per-tick SetOwner (OwnerRevision churn).
- TargetFound re-issues RequestZDO every 0.5 s (UpdatePortal InvokeRepeating) until the ZDO exists locally, then never again - 'single RequestZDO' is right in effect but the per-tick ForceSendZDO(peer, uid) is only useful if the ship's DataRevision keeps rising (it does while moving; a moored ship with no changes will not resend, which is fine).
- Player.TeleportTo refuses when m_teleportCooldown < 2 s (SERVER:15310-15313) - relevant to any relay chaining.
- Moving anchor ownership: ZDO.InternalSetPosition only bumps DataRevision when IsOwner() (S:73734-73744), and ReleaseNearbyZDOS reassigns every PERSISTENT ZDO in a peer's active area to that peer every 2 s (S:76901-76926). Create the anchor NON-persistent (server-owned non-persistent ZDOs survive RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS because IsPeerConnected(sessionID) is true, S:77406-77419) or re-SetOwner(session) each tick (extra OwnerRevision churn).
- Arrival geometry: the traveller is pinned at targetPos + targetForward*1 + up*1 (S:143542-143545, C:15347-15352); FindFloor (C:116244) only decides when the swirl ends and succeeds on seabed terrain. Direct ship link ⇒ arrival ~1 m ahead of the ship ORIGIN (inside/over the hull for a moored ship), not astern; astern requires choice 2's offset anchor.
- Direct link persists across save/reload: RegenerateConnectionHashData (S:75461-75477) and ZDOMan.ConnectPortals at load (S:77850-77889) rebuild any mutual Portal pair with no prefab filter — scrub s_tag and the ship's Portal connection on feature end or the ship remains a portal endpoint after restart.
- RPC_SetTag on the source by any nearby player triggers SetConnectedPortal → RPC_SetConnected on the ship owner, clearing the ship's Portal connection (S:143583-143622); the mod must re-assert.
- TargetFound/RequestZDO only runs while a teleportable player is within m_activationRange (5 m) of the source (C:144231-144247); a sprinter can trigger before the ship ZDO arrives → Teleport() silently does nothing (S:143539-143548, zDO == null branch).
- m_characterParentSync on the Player prefab remains unverified (Inspector bool, S:87361); passenger detection via SyncTransform connection must be treated as probable, not proven.

### 191. Nearest Player (player-to-player portal)

`targeted-portals:Nearest Player (player-to-player portal)` · domain **targeted** · source `targeted-portals`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Portal to the nearest online player, or a named player, using the live character ZDO position; the character ZDO can be the destination directly but is non-persistent and must never receive a Portal connection.


**How it works:** Positions: ConnectedCharacters.All() → `zdo.GetPosition()` refreshed every physics tick by the owner's ZSyncTransform (distance-independent client→server delivery), far fresher than peer.m_refPos (2 s, and blank in GetPlayerList for privacy-off players). Nearest: min distance from the source portal over all connected characters excluding the traveller. Destination mechanism A — direct: `src.SetConnection(Portal, characterZdo.m_uid)`; TeleportWorld.Teleport would read the character's live position. But Game.ConnectPortals will null it within 5 s (the character ZDO has no matching tag and no Portal connection back) and you MUST NOT write a Portal connection onto a player ZDO (it would overwrite their SyncTransform parent slot). So A requires a prefix on Game.ConnectPortals (or a 1 s re-assert that always loses the race half the time) — a Harmony prefix that skips reconcile for TPL-managed sources is clean (SubsystemRegistry.SafePatch). Character ZDOs are also destroyed on disconnect (RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS) and s_dead players sit at their corpse. Mechanism B — an Invisible Anchor (Option 2) re-positioned to `targetPos + 2 m` behind the target each 0.5–1 s with SetOwner+SetPosition, plus `ForceSendZDO(peer, anchorUid)` to peers near the source so their copy is fresh. Arrival lands where the target was ~8 s earlier (frozen snapshot); fine for a standing player, off by up to 60 m for a runner. Safety: skip targets with `s_dead`, `s_inBed`, InInterior (y>3000 — the anchor would need to be at interior coordinates, which works geometrically but the client must have that interior loaded, i.e. be there already), or in water (GetHeight<30 at their XZ). Tag: `>Nearest: <s_playerName>`. Selection input: emote at the hub cycles through candidates (toast the name each press) — EmoteSignals.


**Player experience:** At the `>Player` hub the traveller presses the cycle emote; toasts show `Target: Erik (412 m)`, `Target: Anna (2.1 km)`; hover updates to `Portal tag:">Erik" [connected]`. 8 s swirl, arrive ~2 m behind where Erik stood 8 s ago. No portal at the far end (anchor is invisible); return via another portal or the relay. If Erik logs out mid-transit the anchor is reaped and the traveller still arrives at the last position.


**Failure modes:**
- Direct-link variant fights vanilla's reconciler; without a ConnectPortals prefix it is unreliable.
- Never write Portal connections onto character ZDOs (single connection slot; destroys ship/mount parenting).
- Target in a dungeon interior: anchor at y>3000 — the traveller's client only completes if it has that interior instanced (it will not), leading to the 15 s fallback and a drop at GetSolidHeight (surface) — block interior targets.
- Griefing vector: portal-stalking a player; gate with a consent emote on the target side or restrict to group/ward-permitted players (ward permitted lists are ZDO-readable).

**Open questions:**
- Does the vanilla client accept a destination ZDO that moves between TargetFound() and Teleport() without issue (it reads once at transit — expected fine)?

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Mechanism A does NOT give 'live position': the traveller's client only holds the target character ZDO if it is in its sector sync range or force-sent. After TargetFound's RequestZDO (one ForceSendZDO, SERVER:77689-77692, consumed at SERVER:77048) the copy is frozen. ForceSendZDO(peer, uid) per tick (SERVER:77714) is required for A exactly as for B; ShouldSend passes because the target's DataRevision rises every tick it moves (SERVER:76003-76013).
- Server-side src.SetConnection on a client-owned hub works without Game.SetConnection's owner routing because ZDO.SetConnection bumps DataRevision unconditionally (SERVER:73656-73665) and portals never self-update; but note every such write calls SetDirtyPortals and marks the ZDO for the next save, and the reconcile prefix must also cover the load-time ZDOMan.ConnectPortals (SERVER:77850-77889), which would otherwise pair the hub with whatever (Portal|Target,hash) entry was saved.
- Anchor (mechanism B) ownership churn: a PERSISTENT server-owned anchor 2 m behind a player is inside that player's active area and ReleaseNearbyZDOS transfers it to them every 2 s (Persistent-only loop SERVER:77282-77306; server session never in-area via IsInPeerActiveArea SERVER:77268-77280); after that ZDO.SetPosition no longer bumps DataRevision (SERVER:73734-73745) and the client copies stop updating. Make the anchor NON-persistent (kept alive because IsPeerConnected(m_sessionID) is true, SERVER:77423-77435) rather than re-SetOwner every tick.
- Interior caveat is overstated: ZoneSystem.GetZone uses x/z only (SERVER:115740-115745) and ZNetScene.IsAreaReady only requires the target's zone loaded and its sector ZDOs instantiated (SERVER:82064-82081); after the 2 s snap the traveller's own Player.Update sets the ref pos to the target (SERVER:11070-11074) so that zone (including interior ZDOs at y~5000 in the same sector) loads. Whether the dungeon interior spawns correctly for a player who arrives by teleport without entering through the Teleport door has not been checked in game - mark that sub-case needs-ingame-check rather than 'must already be there'.
- When the target disconnects, the hub's dangling connection is nulled by the reconcile `zDO == null` branch within <=5 s (SERVER:100598-100601) if the prefix does not intercept it; the traveller who is mid-transit still lands at the frozen snapshot (client already holds m_teleportTargetPos, SERVER:15324).
- Identity/ore/boss gating remains client-side (TeleportWorld.Teleport SERVER:143516-143533); 'server-enforced' applies only to which route is open.
- Mechanism A (direct character-ZDO link) needs the same per-tick ForceSendZDO(peer, characterUid) to peers near the source as mechanism B; RequestZDO yields a single send (force-send entries removed after send, S:77048) and nothing else pushes a far-away character ZDO to that client.
- Anchor must be created NON-persistent: ReleaseNearbyZDOS reassigns persistent ZDOs in the target player's active area to that player within 2 s (S:76901-76926) and ZDO.InternalSetPosition only bumps DataRevision when IsOwner() (S:73734-73744). Server-owned non-persistent ZDOs are not orphan-collected (IsPeerConnected(sessionID) true, C:77562-77565).
- Anchor needs s_tag == source tag AND a Portal connection back to the source or Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 nulls the source within 5 s (S:100597-100604); tag-only is not enough.
- s_dead window is ~10 s: Player.OnDeath sets s_dead (C:12736) and RequestRespawn(10f) destroys the character (C:12849, C:100831-100845); afterwards the peer has no character ZDO until respawn (peer.m_characterID = None via C:81080).
- Harmony prefix on Game.ConnectPortals must skip only pass 1 for TPL-managed sources; pass 2 already ignores them because their connection is non-None (S:100609-100611).
- 'Off by up to 60 m for a runner' is a lower bound: the 8 s gate is a minimum and IsAreaReady (C:82293-82310) can extend it while the destination zone streams in.

Direct-link analysis holds: Game.ConnectPortals pass 1 nulls the source because the character ZDO has neither the tag nor a Portal connection back (S:100597-100604); a single connection slot per ZDO (S:74797) means writing Portal onto a player ZDO would clobber the SyncTransform parent ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync maintains (S:87542-87562); Game.ConnectPortals is public (S:100589) so a Harmony prefix is possible. Non-persistent character ZDOs are destroyed on disconnect (RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS S:77406-77419). TeleportWorld.Teleport reads the target ZDO's live position with no prefab check (S:143539-143548); the traveller's client obtains the target via TargetFound→RequestZDO (S:143640-143658) → server per-peer force-send (S:77689-77692, S:77714-77724). (2) Anchor persistence/ownership: an anchor 2 m behind the target sits in the target's active area; if persistent, ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands it to the target within 2 s (S:76901-76926) and server SetPosition then stops bumping DataRevision (S:73734-73744) — create it non-persistent (safe under RemoveOrphanNonPersistentZDOS because IsPeerConnected(sessionID) is true, S:77406-77419, C:77562-77565). (3) The anchor must itself carry the source's s_tag and a Portal connection back or ConnectPortals nulls the route every 5 s (S:100597-100604). (4) s_dead players do not 'sit at their corpse' for long: OnDeath sets s_dead then RequestRespawn(10f) destroys the character ZDO (C:12736, C:12849, C:100831-100845). (5) Save boundary for mechanism A is benign: the source gets a Portal hash whose Portal|Target lands on a non-persistent ZDO, so the link is simply absent after reload (S:75461-75477) and must be re-asserted.
