### 242. Non-Portals As Portals — The Mandatory Migration Pass

`gapfill:wildcard:Non-Portals As Portals — The Mandatory Migration Pass` · domain **wildcard** · source `gapfill:wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


Enrolling a prefab into Game.PortalPrefabHash at runtime silently orphans every pre-existing instance from the next save and freezes mobile ones; the option is only safe with a migration pass, an immobile-prefab restriction and an uninstall reversal.


**How it works:** Save partitioning is a two-set split with no overlap: `AddObjectsPerChunk` clones only ZDOs that are `Persistent && !PortalPrefabHash.Contains(prefab)` out of `m_objectsBySector` (:77566-77576), while the ChunkPortal file clones only `m_portalObjects` and only when `DirtyPortalObjects` (:77619-77627). An instance of the enrolled prefab that was already in `m_objectsBySector` when the hash was added is now excluded from the normal chunk (hash matches) and absent from the portal file (never went through AddIfPortal) — it is dropped from the next save of its chunk and gone after restart. Migration pass (run once, immediately after adding the hash, before any save): walk `GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative(prefabName, list, ref index)` to completion (dedupe sector 0), and for each ZDO call `RemoveFromSector(zdo, zdo.GetSectorIndex())` (public :76745) then the private `AddIfPortal(zdo, hash)` (:77732-77752, publicizer) — which files it into m_portalObjects and sets DirtyPortalObjects — then `SetDirtyPortals()`. Also postpone the world save (or force one) so both files are consistent. Immobility: `ZDO.SetSector` early-returns for any enrolled hash (:73752-73755), so an enrolled ship or cart stays keyed under its original sector forever and stops being delivered to clients at its new position — restrict enrolment to static prefabs. Uninstall reversal: on a later boot without the mod, `LoadChunks` inserts every ChunkPortal ZDO straight into `m_portalObjects` regardless of prefab (:76474-76482), so the enrolled objects stay in the portal registry, get paired by tag by `Game.ConnectPortals` (empty tag = the global untagged group), and — because `HandleDestroyedZDO` only removes from m_portalObjects when the prefab IS in PortalPrefabHash (:76979-76986) — leak there when destroyed. Reversal pass (run while the mod is still installed, before removal): for each enrolled-prefab ZDO in `GetPortals()`, remove it from the live dictionary, `AddToSector(zdo, zdo.GetSectorIndex())` (public :76723), clear its Portal connection, `SetDirtyPortals()`, and remove the hash from PortalPrefabHash; then save.


**Player experience:** Nothing visible when done right. Done wrong, every runestone/altar/marker of the enrolled prefab that existed before the mod was installed disappears from the world at the next restart, with no log line, and the admin blames world corruption.


**Failure modes:**
- Skipping the migration: silent loss of every pre-existing instance at the next save.
- Enrolling a mobile prefab: instances stop re-sectoring and vanish for clients that move away from the original sector.
- Uninstall without reversal: enrolled objects persist only via ChunkPortal, are paired by tag with real untagged portals, and leak in m_portalObjects on destruction.
- GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative returns portals (and now the enrolled prefab) only on its terminal call, and re-scans sector 0 — a partial walk migrates nothing.
- A save that runs between adding the hash and finishing the migration commits the loss; suspend `Game.m_saveInterval` or trigger the migration synchronously at OnWorldReady before any autosave.

**Designer citations:** ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk filter assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77566-77576 ; ZDOMan.GetSaveClonePerChunk portal branch :77619-77627 ; ZDOMan.AddIfPortal :77732-77752 ; ZDOMan.RemoveFromSector :76745 / AddToSector :76723 ; ZDOMan.LoadChunks portal branch :76474-76482 ; ZDOMan.HandleDestroyedZDO portal branch :76976-76986 ; ZDO.SetSector portal early-return :73752-73755 ; Game.PortalPrefabHash :100021


**Open questions:**
- Does a chunk save between hash-add and migration ever happen in practice at OnWorldReady (autosave default 1800 s, but ZNet.Shutdown saves)? IN-GAME CHECK: add hash, kill server without migration, restart, count instances.
- Does `Game.ConnectPortals` pairing an enrolled non-portal ZDO with a real untagged portal produce a usable teleport on a vanilla client (yes at the transit site; visual state untested)?

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- The 'server-enforced' label is honest only in the sense that ZDOMan's save-partitioning logic is 100% server-side authority with zero player input — there is no player-facing permission gate here at all; this option is really about save-file data-integrity risk for the mod's OWN prefab-enrollment choice, not an enforcement mechanism directed at players. Worth noting for precision, not a reason to downgrade.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Directly verified every cited ZDOMan member. AddObjectsPerChunk filters `item3.Persistent && !PortalPrefabHash.Contains(item3.GetPrefab())` for normal chunks — confirmed exact. AddIfPortal confirmed: early-returns if the prefab hash isn't in PortalPrefabHash, else files into m_portalObjects and sets DirtyPortalObjects=true. LoadChunks' ChunkPortal branch confirmed to insert every ZDO from that file straight into m_portalObjects with zero prefab-hash filtering — confirming the 'uninstall leaves them in the portal registry forever' claim. ZDO.SetSector confirmed to early-return unconditionally for any prefab in PortalPrefabHash (immobility claim confirmed). RPC_ZDOData confirmed to call AddIfPortal(zDO, zDO.GetPrefab()) on every incoming ZDO update, meaning even a peer-synced (non-locally-created) ZDO gets correctly filed if its prefab is enrolled — a detail supporting rather than undermining the option.

### 243. The Adamant Gate, Rewritten — Indestructible Only As A Composite

`gapfill:wildcard:The Adamant Gate, Rewritten — Indestructible Only As A Composite` · domain **wildcard** · source `gapfill:wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A huge s_health defeats damage and Repair only; hammer removal, support wear, forged DestroyZDO and ZDOData overwrite all bypass it — the portal is indestructible only when five levers are present together.


**How it works:** What s_health buys: `WearNTear.RPC_Damage` runs on the owning client, applies resistances and subtracts from the stored `s_health` via `ApplyDamage` (:150332-150409); `Repair` refuses when stored health ≥ prefab m_health (:149522-149531). What it does not buy: (a) Hammer removal — `Player.RemovePiece` → `WearNTear.Remove` → "RPC_Remove" to the ZDO owner → `Destroy` (:150411-150466), health never consulted; (b) Support loss — wear applies `m_health` per update forever (:149705-149712, :149822-149828), draining even 1e9 given time; (c) A forged `DestroyZDO` routed RPC (`ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO` → `HandleDestroyedZDO`, :76953-76999, no sender/ownership check) deletes the ZDO outright; (d) `RPC_ZDOData` applies any higher-revision blob wholesale (:77076-77139), so a client can set s_health to 1. Composite: (1) s_health = k·m_health as the damage buffer, re-asserted on the watchdog tick and protected by an `RPC_ZDOData` postfix that restores it if a peer lowered it; (2) LoadFields `Piece.m_canBeRemoved = false` so the vanilla hammer refuses at :12375 before any RPC is sent, plus `WearNTear.m_noSupportWear = false` / `m_noRoofWear = false` so support and rain wear are never evaluated (:149686, :149705); (3) Ownership pin — SetOwner-block prefix keeps the server as owner so any RPC_Remove/RPC_Damage that a modified client sends anyway is routed to a machine with no instance and dies in `ZNetScene.FindInstance` (HandleRoutedRPC :83646-83663); note RPC_SetTag then also dies, so pinned gates are retag-frozen — acceptable for admin gates; (4) Destroy veto — prefix on `ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO` that drops ZDOIDs belonging to protected portals, or a `ZDOMan.m_onZDODestroyed` observer that immediately re-fabricates the gate (new ZDOID, `m_deadZDOs` forbids reusing the old id, :76043/:77133); (5) `Piece.CanBeRemoved()` is separate and irrelevant for portals (:136310-136326). Vanilla-respecting side: (1) and (2) are honoured by unmodified clients; (3) and (4) are server-enforced against modified ones. Only with all present does 'indestructible' hold; state that in the option's headline.


**Player experience:** A raider's axe bounces off the admin gate showing damage numbers that never dent it; their hammer's remove prompt simply does nothing; a modded client's forged destroy packet is dropped and the gate stays. A vanilla builder trying to retag a pinned gate gets no response — the tag dialog closes and nothing changes.


**Failure modes:**
- Ownership pin freezes vanilla retagging (RPC_SetTag routes to the owner, which has no instance) — acceptable only for admin-managed gates.
- LoadFields overrides apply at instantiation; a client that already has the instance can still hammer-remove until it re-creates it (RPC_Remove then reaches the pinned server and dies anyway, so the pin covers the gap).
- A Destroy veto prefix must resolve targets by ZDOID from a ZPackage it then re-positions; a mistake corrupts vanilla's destroy handling for every object in the packet.
- Re-fabrication after a successful destroy changes the ZDOID; every portal pointing at the old gate is unlinked until the mod re-pairs them.
- s_health re-assert needs a real value change or ForceSendZDO to reach peers whose cached revision is current (AddForceSendZdos is gated on ShouldSend, :77268-77273).
- The support/roof overrides are client-honoured; a modified client still applies wear — but its ApplyDamage writes are then reverted by the watchdog.

- How quickly does a k·m_health buffer drain under support loss on a live client (UpdateWear cadence)?

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- Top-level enforcement label should be corrected from 'server-enforced' to 'client-honoured' as the primary characterization, since against the project's actual all-vanilla-client population, indestructibility is fully achieved by the two client-honoured LoadFields levers (Piece.m_canBeRemoved=false, WearNTear.m_noSupportWear/m_noRoofWear=false) alone — see also the Phantom Survival correction above, where m_canBeRemoved=false already independently zeroes all non-forced wear damage, further reducing what lever (2) needs to do. Levers (3)/(4) (RPC_DestroyZDO veto, RPC_ZDOData watchdog) are real and correctly described but defend only against a hypothetical modified client, which is explicitly outside this project's stated scope.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] Directly verified WearNTear.ApplyDamage (health<=0 immunity, `@float -= damage` then Destroy on reaching 0), Repair-equivalent health-ceiling behavior, and RPC_ZDOData's revision-gated wholesale-apply (`if (num4<=zDO.DataRevision) continue; ... zDO.Deserialize(pkg2)`) confirming that ANY higher-revision blob — including a forged lower s_health — is applied with no ownership/sender check beyond 'is this peer known' (FindPeer). This matches the option's core 'four levers, none alone sufficient' thesis precisely. However, the project's own stated environment is 100% vanilla clients, not modified/cheating clients — levers (3) RPC_DestroyZDO-veto and (4) RPC_ZDOData-watchdog exist specifically to defend against a MODIFIED client forging packets, which is outside the stated threat model (no player here can run modified code). Against the actual vanilla-only population this audit is scoped to, levers (1) Piece.m_canBeRemoved=false and (2) WearNTear field overrides (both client-honoured, both already verified real via LoadFields) are sufficient on their own for true indestructibility — (3)/(4) are precautionary hardening against a threat that, per the project's own ground rules, doesn't exist in-scope. The headline 'server-enforced' therefore overstates what's actually load-bearing day-to-day; the option's own body is honest about this split, but the top-level label should read 'client-honoured (with optional server-enforced hardening against non-vanilla clients, out of primary scope)'.

### 244. Sector Zero, Named — The Headless Zone-Spawn Predicate And Its Reaper

`gapfill:wildcard:Sector Zero, Named — The Headless Zone-Spawn Predicate And Its Reaper` · domain **wildcard** · source `gapfill:wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** needs-ingame-check → **needs-ingame-check** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed


Any ZDO beyond ±16.4 km, and every ZDO in zone (-256,-256), lands in sector 0 — the bucket the server's pinned reference position queries; whether the server instantiates them hinges on one predicate, ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded() at zone (15625,15625), and if it is true the server-only reaper destroys any prefab-less ZDO it finds there.


**How it works:** `ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex` maps any zone with (x+256) ≥ 512 or (y+256) ≥ 512 to `Sector = 0` (:115760-115773); zone (-256,-256) legitimately maps to 0 as well; `ZDO.SetSector` routes OutsideZones ZDOs to `ZoneSystem.SectorZero` (:73757-73758). The server's `Game.FixedUpdate` pins the reference position at (1e6,0,1e6) → zone (15625,15625); `ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects` queries `FindSectorObjects` around that zone, and because every neighbouring sector clamps to index 0, `FindObjects` (which dedupes by SectorIndex) visits `m_objectsBySector[0]` + `m_portalObjects[0]` once. `CreateObjectsSorted` (:82105-82143) returns immediately unless `IsActiveAreaLoaded()` (:114054-114069) — true only when every zone within NearSimulationDistance of (15625,15625) is in `m_zones`. Those zones are created by `ZoneSystem.Update` → `CreateLocalZones(GetReferencePosition())` (:113930) → `PokeLocalZone` → `SpawnZone(zone, Full)` (:114071-114092), which needs `HeightmapBuilder.IsTerrainReady` at zonePos (1e6, …) — WorldGenerator returns the edge height (−400) there, so the build should succeed, but nothing in the decompile proves the builder completes at that coordinate. If it does, the server instantiates sector-0 ZDOs: `IsZoneReadyForType` does not require m_zones membership (:115797-115810), `CreateObject` runs, and the server-only branch destroys any ZDO whose prefab cannot be instantiated — `item.SetOwner(session); DestroyZDO(item)` with the log line 'Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO' (:82137-82143). Consequences: (a) a Void Anchor (prefab 0) whose coordinate is typo'd beyond ±16.4 km, or placed in zone (-256,-256), is reaped within a frame; (b) a real portal placed there is instantiated on the server — a live TeleportWorld with Awake/UpdatePortal and RPC_SetTag registered, the one place a server-side portal component exists; (c) `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` uses zone distance, not sector index (:76887-76899), so the server never auto-owns those objects — the reaper's explicit SetOwner is what makes DestroyZDO work. Decisive test: log `ZoneSystem.instance.IsActiveAreaLoaded()` and `m_zones.ContainsKey(new Vector2s(15625,15625))` 60 s after world load, and `ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances()`.


**Player experience:** None directly. If the predicate is true, an admin who fat-fingers a Void Anchor coordinate to 20000 sees the server log 'Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO' and the connected portal goes dark; if false, the anchor silently works but the ZDO is filed in a bucket nothing but the server ever queries.


**Failure modes:**
- Predicate unknown: HeightmapBuilder at (1e6,0,1e6) may never report ready, leaving IsActiveAreaLoaded false forever and the server inert on the scene side.
- If true, every prefab-0 Void Anchor or unknown-hash ZDO in sector 0 is reaped server-side.
- Zone (-256,-256) at world coordinates (−16384, −16384) is beyond the 10.5 km world edge — harmless in practice, but any ZDO there shares the bucket.
- Server-instantiated GameObjects in that bucket run full component logic headless (UpdatePortal, WearNTear owner checks) with no Player present — untested code paths.

**Designer citations:** ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115760-115773 ; ZDO.SetSector OutsideZones :73752-73768 ; ZoneSystem.Update CreateLocalZones :113925-113940 ; ZoneSystem.CreateLocalZones/PokeLocalZone :113945-113990 ; ZoneSystem.SpawnZone :114071-114092 ; ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded :114054-114069 ; ZoneSystem.IsZoneReadyForType :115797-115810 ; ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted reaper :82105-82143 ; ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS zone-distance test :76887-76899 ; Game.FixedUpdate reference pin :100458-100466


**Open questions:**
- Is IsActiveAreaLoaded() true on a headless 1.0.7 server (does HeightmapBuilder build zones at 1e6)? IN-GAME CHECK as described.
- If true, does a real portal ZDO placed in sector 0 get instantiated server-side with a working TeleportWorld (RPC_SetTag then handled by the server)? IN-GAME CHECK: place one at x=20000 and retag from a client.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Directly verified SectorToIndex: `num=(uint)(sectorX+256); if (num>=512 || num2>=512) Sector=0; else Sector=num2*512+num;` — confirms both the ±16.4km-out-of-range wraparound-to-0 claim AND that zone (-256,-256) legitimately computes Sector=0 via the else branch (num=0,num2=0). IsActiveAreaLoaded confirmed to check `!m_zones.ContainsKey(...)` for every zone within simulation distance of GetZone(reference position) — matches. Most importantly, CreateObjectsSorted's reaper logic was found at the EXACT cited line (82105 in this copy) and matches the option's description almost verbatim: `if (!IsActiveAreaLoaded()) return;` then for each candidate ZDO, `if (CreateObject(item)!=null) {...} else if (IsServer()) { item.SetOwner(GetSessionID()); ZLog.Log("Destroyed invalid prefab ZDO:"+uid); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(item); }` — this is a precise, high-confidence match. The option's own feasibility label (needs-ingame-check) is appropriately conservative given IsActiveAreaLoaded()'s truth at the pinned reference position still depends on HeightmapBuilder.IsTerrainReady succeeding at (1e6,0,1e6), which this pass did not independently test.

### 245. Admin Command Channel — RPC_RemoteCommand Is Alive

`gapfill:wildcard:Admin Command Channel — RPC_RemoteCommand Is Alive` · domain **wildcard** · source `gapfill:wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed


A vanilla admin client's console forwards any RemoteCommand-flagged vanilla command it cannot run locally to the server, which runs it through the headless Console after an adminlist check — a prefix on Terminal.TryRunCommand keyed on a mod prefix makes this a real text command channel.


**How it works:** The client's `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (client :45734-45758) looks the first token up in its own `commands` dictionary; if the command exists but `IsValid` fails (e.g. onlyServer commands like `setkey`, `removekey`, `listkeys`, :43509-43533) and the command is `RemoteCommand`, it calls `ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text)` (client :45741-45744). On the server `ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879-81888) rejects non-admins via `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())` — the socket-verified identity — and otherwise `InternalCommand` logs and runs `Console.instance.TryRunCommand(command)` (:81891-81895); `Console` is instantiated headless in `Game.Awake` (:100038-100041). The mod adds a Harmony prefix on the server's `Terminal.TryRunCommand(string text, bool, bool)`: if `text` starts with `removekey tpl ` (or any RemoteCommand-flagged vanilla verb followed by a mod sentinel), parse the remainder as the mod's command, execute, reply with `ZNet.instance.RemotePrint(rpc, ...)` — the ZRpc is available by prefixing `ZNet.InternalCommand(ZRpc rpc, string command)` instead, which is the cleaner hook — and return false so vanilla never sees a malformed key. Replies land in the admin's console (`RPC_RemotePrint`). This is an admin-only channel by construction (non-admins get 'You are not admin'); ordinary players still have only emotes/pings. Use for portal admin verbs: list, lock, unlock, retag, pair, place phantom, report.


**Player experience:** An admin presses F5 on an unmodified client and types `removekey tpl lock Hub-North`. The console prints 'tpl: Hub-North locked (3 links cleared)' a moment later. A non-admin typing the same sees 'You are not admin'. Nobody else sees anything.


**Failure modes:**
- Only vanilla commands flagged RemoteCommand and failing IsValid on the client are forwarded; the sentinel must ride one of them (`removekey`, `setkey`, `listkeys` are the natural carriers).
- If the prefix misses, vanilla `removekey tpl` runs on the server and harmlessly tries to remove a non-existent key — but `setkey` as a carrier would ADD a junk world key; prefer `removekey`.
- The client's own console echo shows the raw command line; cosmetic.
- ListContainsId semantics changed in 1.0.12 to accept either id form (per MIGRATE-1.0.md) — more permissive, not less.

**Designer citations:** Terminal.TryRunCommand assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:45734-45758 (server copy assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:45734-45758) ; ZNet.RPC_RemoteCommand assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81879-81888 ; ZNet.InternalCommand :81891-81895 ; Game.Awake Console instantiation :100038-100041 ; Terminal setkey/removekey/listkeys registrations :43509-43533, :43606


**Open questions:**
- Confirm end-to-end on a live server: admin client `removekey tpl ping` → server log 'Remote admin … executed command' → RemotePrint reply visible in the client console.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Directly verified the entire chain. Terminal.TryRunCommand: `if (value.IsValid(...)) RunAction(...); else if (value.RemoteCommand && ZNet.instance && !ZNet.instance.IsServer()) ZNet.instance.RemoteCommand(text);` confirmed exact. ZNet.RemoteCommand: `if (IsServer()) InternalCommand(null,command); else GetServerRPC()?.Invoke("RPC_RemoteCommand", command);` confirmed. Server's RPC_RemoteCommand confirmed to gate on `ListContainsId(m_adminList, rpc.GetSocket().GetHostName())` — a socket-verified identity check, unspoofable by a plain vanilla client — before calling InternalCommand→`Console.instance.TryRunCommand(command)`. Confirmed 'setkey'/'removekey' are registered with `onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true` (both explicitly checked in source), validating the mechanism generically. Confirmed Console (subclass of Terminal, not overriding TryRunCommand) is instantiated server-side in Game.Awake (`if (!Console.instance) Instantiate(m_consolePrefab);`) — necessary for Console.instance.TryRunCommand to have anything to call, and independently corroborated by its use inside the already-verified RPC_RemoteCommand→InternalCommand path. This is a genuinely server-enforced, authenticated admin channel; the Harmony-prefix-on-Terminal.TryRunCommand design is sound because Console doesn't override that method.

**Verifier evidence:** assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:45734-45745 Terminal.TryRunCommand RemoteCommand branch confirmed exact ; assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:81869-81895 ZNet.RemoteCommand/RPC_RemoteCommand/InternalCommand confirmed exact, including adminlist socket-hostname check ; assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:43509,43535-43552 setkey/removekey registered onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true confirmed ; assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100038-100041 Console instantiated in Game.Awake confirmed ; assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:42856-42879 class Console : Terminal, does not override TryRunCommand, confirming a Harmony prefix on Terminal.TryRunCommand reaches the server-side Console instance

### 246. Boss Blackout, Corrected — The Half That Is World-Wide And The Half That Is On-Screen

`gapfill:wildcard:Boss Blackout, Corrected — The Half That Is World-Wide And The Half That Is On-Screen` · domain **wildcard** · source `gapfill:wildcard`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed


NoBossPortals blocks constructed portals when EITHER the traveller's own HUD shows an active boss (per-client) OR the server-broadcast activeBosses key is > 0 (world-wide); only the second half is a server-observable or server-drivable blackout.


**How it works:** `TeleportWorld.Teleport` gate 3 (:143528) is `NoBossPortals && (RandEventSystem.instance.GetBossEvent() != null || (GetGlobalKey(activeBosses, out v) && v > 0))`. `GetBossEvent()` (:106939-106949) returns `EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss().m_bossEvent` — the boss health bar currently displayed on THAT client (within EnemyHud's boss show distance and alerted) — so this half is local to each traveller's screen and cannot be read or set by the server. The `activeBosses` half is a float global key the owning client of a boss increments in `BaseAI.SetAlerted` (once per boss via the s_bossCount ZDO bool) and decrements on death (`Character.OnDeath` :3153-3165), broadcast by the server's key store to everyone — world-wide, server-readable, and server-writable (`ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, n)`). Practical consequences for a portal mod: (1) an 'auto-lockdown during boss fights' feature that sets NoBossPortals gets a world-wide blackout only while some client has raised activeBosses; a player fighting a boss whose HUD shows it is additionally blocked locally even when the key is 0 (e.g. the increment was lost). (2) The server can manufacture a blackout by writing `activeBosses 1` and lift it with `activeBosses 0`, independent of any real boss — and should watch for the leak case where a crash leaves the counter stuck. (3) Dungeon doors use a different, positional, EnemyHud-dependent test (`Teleport.Interact` :143355 → `Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon` :133631-133645) and are unaffected by the key value alone. (4) Any server-side 'blanket drop of remote SetGlobalKey' hardening must whitelist `activeBosses` and `defeated_*`, or client-driven boss progression breaks (:3153-3165).


**Player experience:** With NoBossPortals set, a player 200 m from an aggroed Bonemass (no health bar on screen) is blocked only if some client's increment reached the server; a player inside the fight with the bar on screen is blocked regardless. When the server writes activeBosses 1 for a scheduled 'blackout hour', every portal in the world answers 'blocked by boss' with no boss anywhere.


**Failure modes:**
- The HUD half is invisible to the server: it cannot log or override a local boss-bar block.
- activeBosses is client-maintained; crashes leave it non-zero and portals blocked world-wide until the server zeroes it.
- A blanket server-side veto of remote SetGlobalKey (a plausible hardening for NoPortals/TeleportAll) silently breaks `defeated_*` and `activeBosses` updates from clients.

**Designer citations:** TeleportWorld.Teleport boss gate assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143528 ; RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent :106939-106949 ; BaseAI.SetAlerted activeBosses increment :27256-27262 ; Character.OnDeath decrement :3153-3165 ; Teleport.Interact dungeon gate :143355 ; Location.IsInsideActiveBossDungeon :133631-133645


**Open questions:**
- EnemyHud boss show distance and the exact conditions under which a boss bar appears for a non-participant (Inspector m_maxShowDistanceBoss) — decides how often the HUD half fires for bystanders.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Directly verified TeleportWorld.Teleport's boss gate at the literally cited line: `if (GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && (RandEventSystem.instance.GetBossEvent()!=null || (GetGlobalKey(activeBosses, out float value) && value>0f)))` — exact match to the option's split-predicate claim. GetBossEvent confirmed to be purely `EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss()`-based, i.e. per-client/local-HUD-only, with no server involvement whatsoever — confirming the 'first half is local and unreadable/unsettable by the server' claim. BaseAI.SetAlerted confirmed to increment/decrement the world-wide `activeBosses` global key exactly once per boss (gated by ZDOVars.s_bossCount), and Character.OnDeath confirmed to decrement it back down — confirming the 'second half is world-wide, server-readable and server-writable' claim and the practical consequence that a server can fabricate or clear a blackout by writing the key directly.

**Verifier evidence:** assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143528 TeleportWorld.Teleport boss gate confirmed exact ; assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:106939-106949 GetBossEvent confirmed EnemyHud-based, purely client-local ; assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:27253-27260 BaseAI.SetAlerted activeBosses increment/decrement confirmed ; assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:3163-3165 Character.OnDeath decrement confirmed

### 247. Raid Beacon

`gapfill:lockdown:Raid Beacon` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


Start a vanilla random event at a locked gate from the server: its own centre-screen message, forced music/weather, animated map pin, and client-run spawners become the lockdown's announcement and hazard.


**How it works:** `RandEventSystem.SetRandomEventByName(string name, Vector3 pos)` is public (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:107067-107071) and calls private `SetRandomEvent(ev, pos)` (:107083-107109), which clones the RandomEvent, sets `m_pos`, and — because `ZNet.instance.IsServer()` — calls `SendCurrentRandomEvent()` (:106952-106962), a `ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, "SetEvent", name, time, pos)` broadcast. `RandEventSystem.instance` is live headless: `ZNet.SaveWorld` calls `RandEventSystem.instance.PrepareSave()/Save()` (:80534, :80626) and world load calls `Load` (:80765). The server re-broadcasts the current event every 2 s from `UpdateRandomEvent` (:106879-106884), so late joiners get it. Client `RPC_SetEvent` (:106965-106978) sets the same event locally. On each client, `FixedUpdate` (:106812-106821) makes it the *active* event only while `IsInsideRandomEventArea` — `Utils.DistanceXZ(pos, m_pos) < m_eventRange` and `y <= 3000` (:106829-106836). Activation shows `m_startMessage` via `MessageHud.ShowMessage(Center)` (:107539-107550); `EnvMan` takes `GetEnvOverride()` (:107308-107315, client consumer assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:96284) and `MusicMan` takes `GetMusicOverride()` (:107317-107324, client :103759). The client's `Minimap.UpdateEventPin` (client :57464-57503) draws an `EventArea` pin of `m_eventRange*2*0.9` plus an animated `RandomEvent` pin labelled `Localize(m_startMessage)` for **every** client regardless of distance, and removes both when the event clears. Spawners: `SpawnSystem.UpdateSpawning` on the zone-owning client calls `RandEventSystem.GetCurrentSpawners()` (:110812) — non-null only when the local player is inside the area and `m_time > m_spawnerDelay` (:107299-107306) — and spawns around players in the zone via `FindBaseSpawnPoint` (:110879), marking each creature `s_eventCreature=true` (:110960-110963). Duration: `RandomEvent.Update` (:107521-107537) only advances `m_time` when `playerInArea` (server computes `IsAnyPlayerInEventArea` from `GetAllCharacterZDOS`, :107111-107121), and ends when `m_time > m_duration` (`m_duration<=0` = never). Mod loop: on lockdown of a managed gate, `SetRandomEventByName(cfgEvent, gatePos + up)`; each tick if `GetCurrentRandomEvent()?.m_name != cfgEvent` re-set it; on lift call `ResetRandomEvent()` (:107073-107076). Event names are Inspector data — enumerate `RandEventSystem.instance.m_events` (public, :106747) at OnWorldReady and expose a config dropdown.


**Player experience:** The instant the beacon starts, every online player sees a pulsing red event marker with the event's own name (e.g. the localized $enemy_army_* text) on their map at the gate. A player who walks within m_eventRange (default 96 m, Inspector per event) gets the vanilla centre-screen raid message, the raid music and forced weather; the zone's spawner then spawns the event's creatures around them (not at the gate), exactly like a vanilla raid. Stepping outside the range ends the music/weather. When the lockdown lifts the pin vanishes, the message clears, and remaining event creatures walk off and despawn (BaseAI :27885-27892).


**Failure modes:**
- There is ONE random-event slot (`m_randomEvent`); a beacon evicts any organic raid in progress and vanilla's own `UpdateRandomEvent` timer (:106844-106852) or a standalone event (:106858-106878) can evict the beacon — the re-assert tick (or a `StartRandomEvent` prefix, see Event Slot Governor) is mandatory.
- Creatures spawn around PLAYERS inside the area, not at the gate; a beacon at an empty gate spawns nothing and its timer does not advance (`m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea`), so it persists until someone visits — intended, but the Discord/heartbeat must not report it as 'active'.
- `m_duration` ticks only while someone is inside; a config 'beacon lasts 60 s' is 60 s of player presence, not wall-clock.
- Events carrying `m_requiredGlobalKeys` are irrelevant here (SetRandomEventByName bypasses HaveGlobalKeys), but `GetEvent` (:107051-107065) refuses `m_enabled==false` events silently.
- `RandomEvent.Update` dereferences `GameCamera.instance.AddShake` when `m_cameraShakeCurve.length > 0` (:107532-107535) — on the server this is headless; vanilla raids survive it in production, implying either empty curves or a live camera object, but a modded event with a shake curve could NRE the server FixedUpdate.
- Event pin label and message are the event's own strings; you cannot say 'PORTAL LOCKED' — pair with PlayerNotify/ShowMessage for the actual reason.
- Interiors are excluded (y>3000 check) so a beacon on a dungeon-side portal never activates for the player inside.
- The event is saved with the world (`Save` :107400-107408); a crash mid-lockdown reloads with the beacon armed — the mod's reconciler must clear stale beacons at OnWorldReady.

**Designer citations:** RandEventSystem.SetRandomEventByName — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:107067-107071 ; RandEventSystem.SetRandomEvent — :107083-107109 ; RandEventSystem.SendCurrentRandomEvent / RPC_SetEvent / Start registration — :106952-106978, :106781 ; RandEventSystem.IsInsideRandomEventArea — :106829-106836 ; RandEventSystem.UpdateRandomEvent (2 s resend, organic eviction) — :106838-106885 ; RandEventSystem.IsAnyPlayerInEventArea — :107111-107121 ; RandomEvent fields (m_eventRange=96, m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea, m_startMessage, m_forceMusic, m_forceEnvironment, m_spawn) — :107435-107498 ; RandomEvent.Update / OnActivate — :107521-107550 ; RandEventSystem.GetCurrentSpawners / GetEnvOverride / GetMusicOverride — :107299-107324 ; SpawnSystem.UpdateSpawning event spawner use — :110795-110816; FindBaseSpawnPoint at :110879; SetEventCreature at :110960-110963 ; Client Minimap.UpdateEventPin — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57464-57503 ; BaseAI event-creature despawn — :27885-27892 ; ZNet save/load of the event — :80534, :80626, :80765


**Open questions:**
- Exact vanilla event names, m_eventRange, m_duration and m_pauseIfNoPlayerInArea per event — Inspector data; IN-GAME: log `RandEventSystem.instance.m_events` fields at OnWorldReady.
- Whether any vanilla event has a non-empty m_cameraShakeCurve and whether GameCamera.instance is null headless — IN-GAME: start each event via the API on a dedicated server and watch for NRE in FixedUpdate.
- Whether the client shows the pin for an event whose position is inside an unexplored map region (AddPin does not check exploration; unverified visually).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Every cited member verified exact: SetRandomEventByName/GetEvent/SetRandomEvent (:107067-107109), SendCurrentRandomEvent as InvokeRoutedRPC(0L,"SetEvent",...) (:106952-106962), RPC_SetEvent (:106964-106977), IsAnyPlayerInEventArea/IsInsideRandomEventArea, GetBossEvent/GetForcedEvent unrelated to this event (confirmed separately). Enforcement label is honest: the server only owns the shared m_randomEvent broadcast (a route/world-state write), while message/music/spawns are correctly described as client-honoured per-player reactions to that shared state. ### 248. Event Slot Governor

`gapfill:lockdown:Event Slot Governor` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


Own vanilla's single random-event slot: veto organic raids near managed hubs or during a beacon, and keep a beacon from being evicted, with a prefix on the public StartRandomEvent.


**How it works:** Organic raids start only server-side in `RandEventSystem.UpdateRandomEvent` (:106838-106852) via `StartRandomEvent()` (public, :107030-107049) and via the standalone-interval branch (:106858-106878) which calls the private `SetRandomEvent(ev, pos)` directly. A Harmony prefix on `StartRandomEvent` returning false suppresses the periodic pick; a prefix on `SetRandomEvent(RandomEvent ev, Vector3 pos)` (AccessTools by name) can (a) return false when `ev != null` and a beacon is armed, or (b) return false when `pos` is within `HubRadius` of any managed hub in `ZDOMan.GetPortalList()` (:77648), which also covers the admin `randomevent`/`event` console commands (:43942-43971) and the admin routed RPC `RPC_ConsoleStartRandomEvent` (:106992-107003). The prefix must let the mod's own calls through (a static re-entrancy flag set around the mod's `SetRandomEventByName`). Because `SendCurrentRandomEvent` already re-broadcasts every 2 s, no extra sync is needed. Persist nothing: the vanilla slot is saved with the world (:107383-107408).


**Player experience:** Players at a managed hub never get an organic raid rolled onto them (the roll still fires elsewhere for other players). During a beacon, the beacon stays up until the mod lifts it; nobody notices the governor exists.


**Failure modes:**
- Blocking `StartRandomEvent` outright halves the raid rate globally if the prefix is too broad — scope it to positions near hubs or to beacon-active windows only.
- The standalone-interval branch bypasses StartRandomEvent; if only StartRandomEvent is patched, standalone events (e.g. bat swarms) still evict a beacon.
- `GetPossibleRandomEvents` picks a random player position (:107123-107140) — vetoing by position means the roll is consumed for that interval (no re-roll), a mild rate reduction.
- Admin console `event`/`randomevent` are dead on a dedicated console anyway (`Player.m_localPlayer` deref at :43958), but the routed admin RPC is live and the governor must decide whether admins override.

**Designer citations:** RandEventSystem.StartRandomEvent — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:107030-107049 ; RandEventSystem.UpdateRandomEvent — :106838-106885 ; RandEventSystem.SetRandomEvent (private) — :107083-107109 ; RandEventSystem.RPC_ConsoleStartRandomEvent (admin-gated by IsAdmin(hostName)) — :106992-107003 ; Terminal 'event'/'randomevent'/'stopevent' commands — :43942-43971 ; ZDOMan.GetPortalList — :77648


**Open questions:**
- Whether the standalone-interval events are enabled on vanilla worlds (m_standaloneInterval is Inspector data) — IN-GAME: dump m_events.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] StartRandomEvent (:107030-107049, server-gated by IsServer() at top), UpdateRandomEvent's periodic call, private SetRandomEvent (:107083-107109), and RPC_ConsoleStartRandomEvent (:106992-107003, calls StartRandomEvent() directly, admin-checked) all confirmed exact. The gated resource (m_randomEvent/m_forcedEvent) is a pure server-owned field with no per-player semantics -- this is a legitimate 'should this ROUTE (event slot) be occupied' server-enforced veto, not a mislabeled per-player check. Passes the route-vs-player test cleanly.

### 249. NoBossPortals Gate Model Correction

`gapfill:lockdown:NoBossPortals Gate Model Correction` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed


Correct the catalog: the boss gate is 'activeBosses key > 0 (world-wide) OR a boss on THIS traveller's HUD (within 100 m and alerted)', not 'RandEventSystem boss event world-wide'.


**How it works:** `TeleportWorld.Teleport` gate 3 (:143528) is `GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && (RandEventSystem.instance.GetBossEvent() != null || (GetGlobalKey(activeBosses, out v) && v > 0f))`. `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent()` (:106939-106949) is `EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss()?.m_bossEvent` when non-empty — `GetActiveBoss` (:46873-46884) returns the first boss in the LOCAL HUD's `m_huds`, which `TestShow` (:46706-46728) fills only for bosses within `m_maxShowDistanceBoss` (100 f, :46661) of the local player that are alerted or `m_dontHideBossHud`+visible. It has no relation to `m_randomEvent`/`SetEvent`; the server's copy of `RandEventSystem` never sets a boss event (`GetForcedEvent` :106921-106929 is the same HUD lookup). So per traveller: blocked iff (world-wide) the `activeBosses` float key (ordinal 47, written by `BaseAI.SetAlerted` :27256-27262 and decremented in `Character.OnDeath` :3161-3165, both on the boss-owning client) is > 0, OR (local) a boss is on that player's screen. Consequences for Boss Auto-Lockdown: (1) the server-observable half is only the key — read `GetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, out v)`; (2) the watchdog that zeroes a leaked counter must NOT zero while any boss-prefab ZDO with `s_alert` true exists (`ZDOVars.s_alert` is session-only but live) — scan `ZDOMan` for boss prefabs (`Character.m_boss` on the prefab via `ZNetScene.GetPrefab`) and `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_alert)`; (3) a server can *raise* the world-wide half deliberately with `SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys.activeBosses, 1f)` to blackout every portal for every player without any boss existing — a cheaper Tier-A lockdown than NoPortals with a distinct message ($msg_blockedbyboss), but it collides with vanilla's own accounting (a later boss death decrements to 0 and lifts it early; an alert increments to 2). The blast-radius model for the catalog: key half = whole world, HUD half = ~100 m around each alerted boss, per player.


**Player experience:** With NoBossPortals set: a player 200 m from an alerted boss whose fight has not yet bumped activeBosses passes; a player 50 m from an alerted boss is blocked with $msg_blockedbyboss even if the counter is 0; once the counter is >0 everyone everywhere is blocked. Dungeon doors use a different, narrower test (Teleport.Interact :143355, EnemyHud + same-zone) and are never blocked inbound.


**Failure modes:**
- Treating `GetBossEvent` as server-visible produces a wrong radius model; the server can never observe the HUD half.
- Zeroing activeBosses while a fight is live re-enables portals mid-fight and desyncs vanilla's per-boss `s_bossCount` guard (:27256) — the next death decrements to -1→clamped 0 (:3164), but the next alert of a different boss goes to 1 again; net effect is a fight-long window of open portals.
- Forcing activeBosses=1 as a lockdown is undone by any boss death anywhere (Mathf.Max(0, v-1)).

**Designer citations:** TeleportWorld.Teleport gate — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143523-143531 ; RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent — :106939-106949 ; RandEventSystem.GetForcedEvent — :106921-106929 ; EnemyHud.TestShow / GetActiveBoss / m_maxShowDistanceBoss — :46706-46728, :46873-46884, :46661 ; BaseAI.SetAlerted activeBosses increment + s_bossCount — :27256-27262 ; Character.OnDeath activeBosses decrement — :3161-3165 ; Teleport.Interact dungeon boss gate — :143355


**Open questions:**
- Which boss prefabs have non-empty m_bossEvent and m_dontHideBossHud — Inspector; IN-GAME: iterate ZNetScene prefabs with Character.m_boss and log m_bossEvent.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Verified byte-for-byte: TeleportWorld.Teleport gate at line 143528 is exactly `GetGlobalKey(NoBossPortals) && (GetBossEvent()!=null || (GetGlobalKey(activeBosses,out v) && v>0f))`; GetBossEvent/GetForcedEvent both resolve via EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss() with no relation to RandEventSystem's m_randomEvent/SetEvent; EnemyHud.TestShow boss branch is exactly `(isVisible && m_dontHideBossHud) || BaseAI.IsAlerted()` gated by m_maxShowDistanceBoss=100f; dungeon Teleport.Interact boss check at :143355 confirmed separate and narrower. This correction is fully accurate and should replace the prior catalog's model.

**Verifier evidence:** TeleportWorld.Teleport gate :143523-143531 (exact match confirmed by direct read) ; RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent/GetForcedEvent :106921-106949 ; EnemyHud.TestShow/GetActiveBoss/m_maxShowDistanceBoss :46706-46728,46873-46884,46661 ; Teleport.Interact dungeon gate :143355

### 250. Teleport-Area Placement Gate Audit

`gapfill:lockdown:Teleport-Area Placement Gate Audit` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** needs-ingame-check → **needs-ingame-check** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed


Discover which pieces carry Piece.m_onlyInTeleportArea and which prefabs carry an EffectArea with the Teleport bit, because vanilla has a placement gate that mentions teleporting by name and nobody knows what uses it.


**How it works:** `EffectArea.Type` is a byte flags enum {Heat=1, Fire=2, PlayerBase=4, Burning=8, Teleport=0x10, NoMonsters=0x20, WarmCozyArea=0x40, PrivateProperty=0x80} (:124062-124073). `Player.UpdatePlacementGhost` sets `PlacementStatus.NoTeleportArea` when `component.m_onlyInTeleportArea && !EffectArea.IsPointInsideArea(point, EffectArea.Type.Teleport)` (:13349-13352), and `TryPlacePiece` refuses it with `$msg_noteleportarea` (:12461-12462). `IsPointInsideArea` is a `Physics.OverlapSphereNonAlloc` on the client's `character_trigger` layer (:124252-124268) — live colliders only, so the server can neither evaluate nor spoof the check; it can only cause a client to instantiate a prefab that carries such an EffectArea. Both `Piece.m_onlyInTeleportArea` (:136153) and `EffectArea.m_type` (:124082) are Inspector fields; no prefab name appears in either decompile. The audit is a one-shot server-side pass at OnWorldReady over `ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs`/`GetPrefabNames()` (:82345): for each prefab log `GetComponent<Piece>()?.m_onlyInTeleportArea` and every `GetComponentsInChildren<EffectArea>(true)` whose `m_type & Type.Teleport != 0`, plus the PlayerBase/NoMonsters/WarmCozyArea sets, and the same for every `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locations[i].m_prefab` (load via `m_prefab.Load()`/`Asset`, release after) since locations are not in ZNetScene. Output feeds the placement-policy engine (a gated piece cannot be placed outside such areas by a vanilla client anyway) and the Fabricated Location Pad option (which location, if any, ships the Teleport area).


**Player experience:** None directly — a log/report. If a portal variant is gated, players see $msg_noteleportarea when trying to place it outside the area; the report tells the operator which variant and where such areas exist.


**Failure modes:**
- The dedicated server's ZNetScene prefab table is assumed populated with components (Wonderland's ContainerRegistry relies on it) — if a prefab's EffectArea sits on an inactive child, `GetComponentsInChildren(true)` is required.
- Location prefabs are SoftReferences; loading all of them at once may spike memory — time-slice and Release.

- Which prefab(s) set m_onlyInTeleportArea (candidates: a portal variant added with 1.0) and which location/prefab carries EffectArea.Type.Teleport — IN-GAME dump as described.
- Whether the Ashlands portal_stone or any Deep North portal is the gated piece — same dump.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] EffectArea.Type flags enum (Heat=1,Fire=2,PlayerBase=4,Burning=8,Teleport=0x10,NoMonsters=0x20,WarmCozyArea=0x40,PrivateProperty=0x80) confirmed exact at :124062-124073; IsPointInsideArea confirmed as live-collider Physics.OverlapSphereNonAlloc (client-only, unspoofable server-side, as claimed); Piece.m_onlyInTeleportArea (:136153) and its placement-ghost gate (:13349) confirmed exact. Correctly labeled needs-ingame-check since no prefab name carrying these flags appears anywhere in either decompile -- this really is undiscoverable without a runtime log pass.

### 251. Fabricated Location Pad

`gapfill:lockdown:Fabricated Location Pad` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


Mint a LocationProxy ZDO server-side so every vanilla client materialises a location's non-networked parts (EffectAreas: NoMonsters, PlayerBase, WarmCozyArea, Teleport) around a hub — a spawn-free, base-flagged, comfort-bearing, and possibly build-unlocking pad with no client mod.


**How it works:** A vanilla client that receives a ZDO whose prefab is `ZoneSystem.m_locationProxyPrefab` (:113216) instantiates it; `LocationProxy.Awake` (:102631-102635) calls `SpawnLocation()` (:102663-102696), which reads `ZDOVars.s_location` (int hash of the location prefab name) and `ZDOVars.s_seed`, waits on `ShouldDelayProxyLocationSpawning` (:115139-115148, just async asset loading — no key gate), then `ZoneSystem.SpawnProxyLocation(hash, seed, pos, rot)` → `SpawnLocation(..., SpawnMode.Client, ...)` (:115150-115160). In Client mode (:115294-115341) every ZNetView-bearing child is disabled and `Utils.Instantiate(location.m_prefab, pos, rot)` creates ONLY the static parts — meshes, colliders, EnvZones and `EffectArea` components (which register themselves in `EffectArea.Awake`, :124113-124143). Recipe on the server: `int proxyHash = ZoneSystem.instance.m_locationProxyPrefab.name.GetStableHashCode(); var z = ZDOMan.instance.CreateNewZDO(pos, proxyHash); z.SetPrefab(proxyHash); z.Persistent = true; z.SetRotation(rot); z.Set(ZDOVars.s_location, locName.GetStableHashCode()); z.Set(ZDOVars.s_seed, seed); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(z.m_uid);` (mirrors `CreateLocationProxy`/`SetLocation`, :115347-115356, :102653-102661). Effects the client then honours: `NoMonsters` makes `BaseAI` flee targets inside and keep out of the +15 m halo (:27924-27940 via :124228-124250); `PlayerBase` counts in `Player.m_baseValue` (20 m radius, :11395) and blocks `SpawnSystem`/`CreatureSpawner` spawns unless `m_insidePlayerBase` (:111010, :5661); `WarmCozyArea` feeds the resting check (:11633); `Teleport` satisfies the `m_onlyInTeleportArea` gate (:13349). Deleting the pad = `SetOwner(session)+DestroyZDO`.


**Player experience:** Walking into the hub the player sees whatever static geometry the chosen location has (this is the catch — you get the location's meshes, not an invisible field), monsters refuse to path in and flee, ambient spawns stop, resting comfort applies near it, and if the location carries a Teleport area the otherwise-gated portal variant becomes placeable there.


**Failure modes:**
- You cannot fabricate a bare EffectArea — only whole vanilla locations; the pad looks like that location (a runestone camp, an altar…). Picking a visually small location with the right areas is the whole design problem and is Inspector data.
- The zone's own generated location (if any) still spawns; two locations can overlap.
- `PlayerBase` areas raise `baseValue` toward the raid threshold (`CheckBase` ≥3, :107212-107223) — the pad can make hubs raid-eligible; combine with Event Slot Governor.
- The proxy ZDO is a normal sector ZDO (not a portal), so it is delivered only to peers whose active area covers it — correct behaviour; ForceSendZDO is only for the first push.
- If the location has a DungeonGenerator/interior it is skipped in Client mode (ZNetView children disabled) — safe but confusing.
- Persistence: `CreateNewZDO` does not set Persistent or prefab (:76684-76692) — both lines are mandatory or the pad vanishes on restart.

**Designer citations:** LocationProxy.Awake/SetLocation/SpawnLocation — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:102621-102696 ; ZoneSystem.m_locationProxyPrefab — :113216 ; ZoneSystem.SpawnProxyLocation — :115150-115160 ; ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation Client-mode branch — :115294-115341 ; ZoneSystem.CreateLocationProxy — :115347-115356 ; ZoneSystem.ShouldDelayProxyLocationSpawning / PokeCanSpawnLocation — :115139-115148 ; EffectArea.Awake registration — :124113-124143; consumers :27924-27940, :11395, :11633, :111010, :5661, :13349 ; ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO — :76674-76692


**Open questions:**
- Name of m_locationProxyPrefab and its ZNetView m_persistent flag — IN-GAME: log `ZoneSystem.instance.m_locationProxyPrefab.name` and its ZNetView.
- Which vanilla locations carry which EffectArea types — audit option.
- Whether a vanilla client cleanly destroys the spawned static location when the proxy ZDO is destroyed (LocationProxy.OnDestroy only unsets loading; the instance is parented to the proxy transform so Unity destroys it with it — expected yes).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] LocationProxy.Awake->SpawnLocation() confirmed reading ZDOVars.s_location/s_seed ints and calling ZoneSystem.SpawnProxyLocation->SpawnLocation(...,SpawnMode.Client,...); Client-mode branch confirmed disabling ZNetView children then Utils.Instantiate(location.m_prefab,...) -- static parts only, exactly as claimed. ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(Vector3,int) confirmed public, and confirmed it does NOT auto-set Persistent or call SetPrefab (both are caller responsibilities per the prior review note) -- the option's own recipe already correctly includes z.SetPrefab(proxyHash) and z.Persistent=true, so it has already absorbed that caveat correctly rather than missing it.

### 252. Placement Policy Engine

`gapfill:lockdown:Placement Policy Engine` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium-large · **Verdict:** confirmed


Generalise the per-player cap into a rule chain evaluated at the ZDO-arrival hook: spacing, biome bans, spawn exclusion, ward-permission, interior ban, and ward-proximity — all pure ZDO/geometry reads, rejection by SetOwner+DestroyZDO.


**How it works:** Hook pair from Wonderland SpawnGovernor (SpawnGovernor.cs:43, :58): postfix on private `ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO(ZDOID, Vector3, int)` (:76684-76692) remembering ZDOIDs created with `prefabHashIn == 0` (the `RPC_ZDOData` path at :77123 passes only uid+position), and postfix on `ZDO.Deserialize(ZPackage)` — the first moment `GetPrefab()` is real. `RPC_ZDOData` calls `AddIfPortal` AFTER Deserialize (:77132), so at evaluation the new portal is NOT yet in `GetPortalList()` — the spacing rule compares against the existing list without self-collision. Filter: `Game.instance.PortalPrefabHash.Contains(zdo.GetPrefab())` (:100021). Rules, all server-side: (1) spacing — min XZ distance to any `GetPortalList()` entry (:77648; use `GetPortals()` :77643 keyed by `ZoneSystem.GetSectorIndex` :115748 and its 8 neighbours for O(1)); (2) biome ban — `WorldGenerator.instance.GetBiome(pos)` (:151725); (3) spawn exclusion — `ZoneSystem.instance.GetLocationIcon(Game.instance.m_StartLocation, out spawn)` (:115422) distance; (4) interior ban — `Character.InInterior(pos)` (:4538, y>3000); (5) ward permission — Shadow Ward Index: for each guard-stone ZDO within radius, permitted iff `zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator)==placerId || pu_id{i}==placerId` (PrivateArea.GetPermittedPlayers shape :137349-137363) and `s_enabled` (:137423); (6) ward proximity — no portal within N m of a ward the placer is not permitted on; (7) cap — count `s_creator == placer` in the list. Placer identity: `zdo.GetLong(ZDOVars.s_creator)` (written client-side in `Piece.SetCreator` :136415-136424 from `Player.PlacePiece` :12517). Reject: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)` (:76929 owner-gated) → `SendDestroyed` broadcast → the placing client's `HandleDestroyedZDO` destroys its instance. Toast the reason via `PlayerNotify.Toast` on the peer whose character ZDO has `s_playerID == s_creator`. Rules live in the hot-reloaded .cfg; each rule is independently enabled and logged via AuditLog.


**Player experience:** The player places the portal normally (ghost turns green, materials are consumed by the client), the portal appears for a fraction of a second, then vanishes; a top-left toast says why ('Portals must be 200 m apart', 'No portals in the Ashlands', 'Not permitted on this ward'). With the refund option, the materials drop at their feet.


**Failure modes:**
- `s_creator` is client-authored and is 0 for pieces the client did not attribute (`Piece.SetCreator` only writes when IsOwner && creator==0) — treat 0 as 'unattributed' and apply only the non-owner rules.
- Ward radius is Inspector data (`PrivateArea.m_radius` default 10 f at :137132); the ward rules are wrong until it is read in-game.
- `s_creator` can be spoofed by a modified client to another player's id — the cap and ward rules are then attributable to the wrong player; cross-check against the sending peer's character ZDO `s_playerID` (`FindPeer(rpc)` gives the ZDOPeer; map to ZNetPeer by `m_rpc`).
- Destroying a WearNTear/Piece-bearing ZDO in the Deserialize postfix is proven for creatures only (SpawnGovernor); the placing client's `Player.PlacePiece` also ran `WearNTear.OnPlaced` and effects — IN-GAME check for orphaned local instance.
- Client `ConsumeResources` runs after `TryPlacePiece` returns (:10801-10807) — the materials are gone before the server rejects; refund option required for acceptable UX.
- A rejected portal is still in `m_deadZDOs` (:76997) — never reuse its ZDOID.

**Designer citations:** ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData order (CreateNewZDO→Deserialize→AddIfPortal) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77121-77132 ; ZDOMan.CreateNewZDO private overload — :76684-76692 ; ZDOMan.DestroyZDO — :76929-76935 ; Game.PortalPrefabHash — :100021 ; ZDOMan.GetPortalList / GetPortals — :77648, :77643 ; ZoneSystem.GetSectorIndex — :115748 ; WorldGenerator.GetBiome — :151725 ; ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon — :115422 ; Character.InInterior — :4538-4541 ; Piece.SetCreator / Player.PlacePiece — :136415-136424, :12517 ; PrivateArea.GetPermittedPlayers / IsEnabled / m_radius — :137349-137363, :137423, :137132 ; Player.UpdatePlacement ConsumeResources after TryPlacePiece — :10801-10807 ; Wonderland SpawnGovernor hook pair — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Subsystems/WorldGovernor/SpawnGovernor.cs:43-70


**Open questions:**
- Client-side cleanliness of destroy-on-arrival for a Piece (orphaned instance? effects?) — IN-GAME with cap=1.
- PrivateArea.m_radius on guard_stone — IN-GAME.
- Whether s_creator is reliably non-zero for player-placed portals in 1.0.7 — IN-GAME.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Confirmed the exact ordering claim that is the option's core premise: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData creates a fresh ZDO via CreateNewZDO(zDOID,vector) with prefabHashIn defaulted to 0 (so the private CreateNewZDO's AddIfPortal(zdo,0) call is a no-op), THEN calls zDO.Deserialize(pkg2), THEN calls AddIfPortal(zdo,zdo.GetPrefab()) at line 77132 with the real hash -- meaning a postfix on ZDO.Deserialize genuinely sees the new portal's real prefab before it is added to GetPortalList(), exactly as claimed. ZDOMan.DestroyZDO (public, :76929), Game.PortalPrefabHash, GetPortalList/GetPortals, ZoneSystem.GetSectorIndex, WorldGenerator.GetBiome, ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon, Character.InInterior(Vector3) static overload, Piece.Requirement/SetCreator all confirmed exact. ### 253. Ground-Drop Refund

`gapfill:lockdown:Ground-Drop Refund` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


When the policy engine destroys a freshly placed portal, drop its full build cost on the ground at the site so a server-side rejection never costs materials.


**How it works:** The server cannot touch the placer's inventory (never networked), but it can create item ZDOs. Read the cost from the prefab, not ObjectDB: `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(zdo.GetPrefab()).GetComponent<Piece>().m_resources` — `Piece.Requirement[]` of `m_resItem` (ItemDrop) and `m_amount` (:136071-136085; `GetAmount(1)` returns `m_amount`, :136087-136096). Skip the refund when the client paid nothing: piece ZDO `s_cheated` is set true by `Player.PlacePiece` when `NoCostCheat()` or cheated items (:12492, :12561), and `ConsumeResources` is skipped when `GetGlobalKey(piece.FreeBuildKey())` (NoBuildCost, :10805-10807, :136619-136626). For each requirement: `var data = req.m_resItem.m_itemData.Clone(); data.m_dropPrefab = req.m_resItem.gameObject;` (mandatory — ItemDrop.Awake never runs for a prefab, FirstSpawnGrant.cs:218 pattern) then `ItemDrop.DropItem(data, req.m_amount, pos + Vector3.up * 0.5f + jitter, Quaternion.identity)` (:70674-70691), which Instantiates the drop prefab server-side; its `ZNetView.Awake` mints a persistent server-owned ZDO and `component.Save()` writes `s_itemData`; the server's `ZNetScene.RemoveObjects` reaps the GameObject next frame while the ZDO stays and syncs to the placer. Split stacks above `m_shared.m_maxStackSize`. Budget: one refund per rejection, at most N per second globally.


**Player experience:** The portal blinks out, a toast explains why, and a pile of fine wood, greydwarf eyes and surtling cores appears at the placement point for the player to pick up (auto-pickup grabs them if in range).


**Failure modes:**
- Duplication exploit if the destroy fails or the client never actually consumed (NoBuildCost set, s_cheated): the guards above must be applied, and the refund must be issued only after `DestroyZDO` was accepted (zdo.IsOwner() true).
- Position: dropping at the portal origin may be inside its own collider volume on the client — jitter 0.5–1 m and lift; items on water float away (Wonderland WaterBuoyancy already handles).
- Items dropped in a non-loaded zone (placer disconnected between placement and evaluation — microseconds, essentially impossible) persist as normal item ZDOs.
- `m_extraAmountOnlyOneIngredient`/`m_amountPerLevel` are item-crafting fields; pieces use m_amount only.
- A modified client can re-send the same piece ZDO repeatedly to farm refunds — rate-limit refunds per s_creator and per peer.

### 254. Portal Sanctuary

`gapfill:lockdown:Portal Sanctuary` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


Destroy hostile creature ZDOs the moment they arrive within N m of any portal (or managed hubs only), making arrival points safe without wards, using the same arrival hook as the placement engine.


**How it works:** Creature spawns are client-side (SpawnSystem.UpdateSpawning gated on `Player.m_localPlayer`, :110795-110800) but every new ZDO arrives server-side through `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` → `CreateNewZDO(uid,pos)` → `Deserialize` (:77121-77131). At the Deserialize postfix (SpawnGovernor.cs:58): resolve `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(zdo.GetPrefab())`, require a `Character` component with `m_faction` not in {Players, PlayerSpawned, TrainingDummy, AnimalsVeg(optional), Dverger(optional)} (`Character.Faction` enum :180-195; `m_faction` :255 is Inspector but readable on the server's prefab table), skip `zdo.GetBool(ZDOVars.s_tamed)` (written by `Character.RPC_SetTamed` :4490-4496; present in the first packet because `Character.Awake` reads it from the ZDO on the spawning client), skip bosses (`Character.m_boss`). Distance: `ZoneSystem.GetSectorIndex(pos)` (:115748) and its 8 neighbours into `ZDOMan.GetPortals()` (:77643, keys are creation-time sectors — portals never move, so exact) then XZ distance ≤ SanctuaryRadius (default 24 m) — or against a managed-hub list only. Reject: `zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); ZDOMan.instance.DestroyZDO(zdo)`. Event creatures (`s_eventCreature`, :110960-110963) are included by default so a beacon's spawns cannot land inside the sanctuary. Budget: the check is O(9 sectors) per creature arrival; cap destroys per second (e.g. 32) and log via AuditLog. Optional: also sweep pre-existing hostile ZDOs near a hub once at OnWorldReady using `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear` (ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25).


**Player experience:** A greydwarf that spawns 15 m from the hub portal blinks out the instant it appears (the spawning client sees it for one sync tick, ~50–100 ms). Creatures that WALK into the radius are untouched — this is spawn suppression, not a shield; pair with a Fabricated Location Pad's NoMonsters area for pathing avoidance.


**Failure modes:**
- Only new ZDOs are caught; creatures wandering in, or already-loaded ones, are not — advertise as 'no spawns', not 'safe zone'.
- CreatureSpawner (dungeon/camp spawners) and RandomFlyingBird/Fish also arrive this way — the faction filter must whitelist ambient fauna or fish near a dock hub disappear.
- Player-summoned skeletons are Faction.PlayerSpawned (Inspector) — verify per prefab; a wrongly-factioned modded summon would be deleted.
- Tames arriving as NEW ZDOs (an offspring born near the portal, `Procreation` spawns with SetTamed) carry s_tamed in the first packet — expected, but IN-GAME verify.
- A creature whose spawning client sets fields over two packets (rare) could be evaluated before s_tamed lands — mitigate by re-checking at destroy time.
- `ZDOMan.m_deadZDOs` holds destroyed ids for the session; harmless.

**Open questions:**
- Faction values of summoned/allied prefabs and of ambient fauna — IN-GAME dump of Character.m_faction per prefab.
- Whether Procreation offspring carry s_tamed in their first ZDO packet — IN-GAME.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Character.Faction enum confirmed exact (Players, AnimalsVeg, ..., PlayerSpawned, TrainingDummy, DeepNorth all present as named). RPC_SetTamed/s_tamed write and Awake-time read confirmed. SpawnSystem.Spawn's SetEventCreature(despawn:true) for eventSpawner creatures, MonsterAI.SetEventCreature/IsEventCreature via ZDOVars.s_eventCreature, and BaseAI's despawn condition `IsEventCreature() && !RandEventSystem.HaveActiveEvent() && no target && !IsAlerted()` all confirmed exact, matching the 'aggro'd troll stays' caveat in playerExperience. ### 255. Authenticated Global-Key Relay Filter

`gapfill:lockdown:Authenticated Global-Key Relay Filter` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


Replace the blanket 'drop client SetGlobalKey/RemoveGlobalKey' with a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC that authenticates by socket and drops only world-modifier keys (ordinal < NonServerOption) and mod-reserved prefixes, passing boss/progression keys through.


**How it works:** Why the existing option is wrong: (1) vanilla clients legitimately send these RPCs — `Character.OnDeath` calls `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(m_defeatSetGlobalKey)` and decrements `activeBosses` (:3153-3165), `BaseAI.SetAlerted` increments it (:27256-27262); `ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string)` is `InvokeRoutedRPC("SetGlobalKey", name)` (:115943-115946) to `GetServerPeerID()` (:83564-83574). (2) `RPC_SetGlobalKey(long sender, string)` (:116022-116029) receives `RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID`, deserialised straight off the wire (:83487-83495) — spoofable to the server's id. The only place the authentic connection is in scope is `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg)` (:83632-83643), which both handles locally (target==m_id) and relays. Prefix: `int pos = pkg.GetPos(); var d = new ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData(); d.Deserialize(pkg); pkg.SetPos(pos);` (`RoutedRPCData` is public, :83463). If `d.m_methodHash` is `"SetGlobalKey".GetStableHashCode()` or `"RemoveGlobalKey"`: `string key = d.m_parameters.ReadString()` (params package is positioned at 0 after Deserialize); classify with `ZoneSystem.GetKeyValue(key, out val, out gk)` (public static, :113560-113581) — DROP (return false) iff `gk < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption` (ordinals 0-40, all world modifiers incl. NoPortals=32, NoBossPortals=33, DungeonBuild=34, TeleportAll=35) or the lowercased name starts with a mod-reserved prefix (`tpl_`); PASS everything else (defeated_*, activeBosses=47, killed_*, StoneCircle, AshlandsOcean, custom mod keys). Resolve the real peer by `ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)` (`m_rpc` public, :78780) and allow admins (`ZNet.instance.IsAdmin(peer.m_socket.GetHostName())`, :81811) if configured; log drops through AuditLog with the socket host name. Returning false from the prefix skips both `HandleRoutedRPC` and `RouteRPC`. The server's own writes never pass through RPC_RoutedRPC (self-dispatch in InvokeRoutedRPC :83588), so no re-entrancy flag is needed.


**Player experience:** Nothing visible. Boss kills still set defeated_* and raise/lower activeBosses; a hacked client sending `removekey noportals` gets silently ignored and logged.


**Failure modes:**
- `setkey`/`removekey` from an admin's F5 console travel as `RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879-81889), not as SetGlobalKey, so admin-in-game toggles are unaffected by this filter — but a non-admin cannot use them anyway.
- World-modifier keys legitimately arrive from clients only through ServerOptionsGUI on a listen host (never on a dedicated server) — so dropping ordinal<41 is safe on dedicated only; guard with `ZNet.instance.IsDedicated()`.
- A vanilla client running Character.OnDeath for a boss whose m_defeatSetGlobalKey is a value-carrying key is still passed (ordinal ≥42).
- Peeking the package: the prefix must restore `pkg` position exactly, or the real handler reads garbage; deserialise a copy if in doubt (`new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray())` then SetPos).

**Designer citations:** ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83632-83643 ; ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData (public) Deserialize — :83463, :83487-83495 ; ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC / RouteRPC — :83645-83663, :83597-83630 ; ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC self-dispatch — :83577-83595; GetServerPeerID — :83564-83574 ; ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(string) — :115943-115946; RPC_SetGlobalKey/RPC_RemoveGlobalKey — :116022-116037 ; ZoneSystem.GetKeyValue — :113560-113581; GlobalKeys enum — :101270-101325 ; Character.OnDeath key writes — :3153-3165; BaseAI.SetAlerted — :27256-27262 ; ZNetPeer.m_rpc — :78780; ZNet.IsAdmin — :81811


**Open questions:**
- Whether any vanilla client path ever sends a world-modifier (ordinal<41) key to a dedicated server legitimately — none found in the decompile; IN-GAME: log all dropped keys for a week before enforcing.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] The strongest-verified option in the batch. Confirmed exact: ZNetPeer.m_rpc is public; ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData is a public class with Serialize/Deserialize exactly as described, params package (m_parameters) is a fresh ZPackage from ReadPackage() positioned at 0; ZPackage.GetPos/SetPos exist; RPC_RoutedRPC's local-handle-vs-relay logic confirmed exact (target==m_id or 0 handles locally, m_server relays); ZoneSystem.GetKeyValue confirmed exact, returning GlobalKeys.NonServerOption on parse failure (so unrecognized/mod-custom keys correctly fall outside the ordinal-based block, matching the design); GlobalKeys enum ordinals hand-counted and confirmed exact -- NonServerOption=41, so 'ordinals 0-40' for the world-modifier block (incl. NoPortals=32, NoBossPortals=33, DungeonBuild=34, TeleportAll=35) is precisely correct, and activeBosses=47 (used elsewhere in the catalog) also checks out. This is a legitimate route-form filter (should this GLOBAL KEY WRITE be applied) with no per-player ambiguity -- passes the enforceability test cleanly and is technically sound as described (Harmony can patch this private method).

### 256. Managed-Portal Relay Shield

`gapfill:lockdown:Managed-Portal Relay Shield` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


Rewrite or drop relayed packets that would delete or rewire a managed portal — DestroyZDO batches, Game.RPC_SetConnection, TeleportWorld's RPC_SetConnected — at the same RPC_RoutedRPC choke point, without breaking legitimate destructions in the same batch.


**How it works:** Three vanilla RPCs can alter a managed portal from any client: (a) `DestroyZDO` — global routed, `RPC_DestroyZDO` (:76953-76961) reads a count and N ZDOIDs and `HandleDestroyedZDO`s each with no sender/ownership check, then the server relays the same packet to everyone (RouteRPC :83597-83618, target 0); (b) `RPC_SetConnection(ZDOID portal, ZDOID target)` — global routed, handled server-side (:100653-100662) with no checks, also relayed; (c) `RPC_SetConnected(ZDOID portalID)` — a ZNetView RPC TeleportWorld sends to the partner's owner (:143604-143629) which the server only relays. Prefix on `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ref ZPackage pkg)` (Harmony allows `ref` on original args): deserialise a copy; for `DestroyZDO`, read the ZDOID list from `m_parameters`, remove any id in the managed set (position-keyed vault → live ZDOID), and if anything was removed rebuild `m_parameters` (`Write(count)`, remaining ids) and re-serialise the whole RoutedRPCData into a fresh ZPackage assigned to `pkg` so vanilla handles/relays the filtered batch — never drop the whole packet (it batches unrelated deletions). For `RPC_SetConnection` and `RPC_SetConnected` whose target/portal ZDOID is managed: return false unless the real peer (`GetPeers().First(p=>p.m_rpc==rpc)`) is an admin. Vanilla's own server-originated `RPC_SetConnection` (Game.SetConnection :100637-100651) never traverses RPC_RoutedRPC. Also optionally drop `RequestStartEvent`/`RequestStopEvent` (PersistentEventSystem, registered :105284-105287, handled server-side with no sender check :105341-105381) from non-admins. Note the shield covers only the RPC layer; a hostile client can still rewrite the portal via `RPC_ZDOData` (:77076-77139) — that is the Invariant Assertion Harness's job (detect-and-revert from the vault).


**Player experience:** Nothing visible for honest players. A player who legitimately demolishes their own managed portal with a hammer sees it refuse to disappear (the WearNTear destroy path ends in DestroyZDO from the owning client, which is now filtered) — so managed portals must be visibly marked as admin-owned, or the filter must allow the creator.


**Failure modes:**
- Filtering DestroyZDO blocks LEGITIMATE demolition of managed portals by their creator; decide policy (allow s_creator / allow admins).
- `ZNetView.Destroy` on the owning client destroys the local GameObject before sending DestroyZDO; a filtered destroy leaves that client with no instance until the zone reloads — the server should `ForceSendZDO(peer, id)` the surviving portal back.
- Re-serialising the package must reproduce RoutedRPCData.Serialize exactly (:83478-83485); a malformed rewrite kills the handler for every peer.
- RPC_ZDOData-level rewrites are not covered; the shield is one layer of a two-layer defence.

**Designer citations:** ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO / HandleDestroyedZDO — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:76953-76999 ; Game.RPC_SetConnection — :100653-100662; Game.SetConnection — :100637-100651 ; TeleportWorld.SetConnectedPortal / RPC_SetConnected — :143604-143629 ; ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC / RouteRPC / RoutedRPCData.Serialize — :83632-83643, :83597-83630, :83478-83485 ; PersistentEventSystem RPC registrations / RPC_RequestStartEvent — :105284-105287, :105341-105381 ; ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData (uncovered path) — :77076-77139


**Open questions:**
- Whether Harmony's `ref ZPackage pkg` substitution in a prefix on this method is honoured under HarmonyX 2.9 (it is per API, but verify with a log).
- Client behaviour when its own DestroyZDO for a piece is not echoed back (instance already gone locally) — IN-GAME.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] All three exploit paths confirmed exact and, notably, WORSE than the option even states in one respect I independently verified: Game.RPC_SetConnection (registered globally via ZRoutedRpc.Register<ZDOID,ZDOID> at :100067, handler at :100653) performs ZERO ownership/legitimacy check -- any client can broadcast InvokeRoutedRPC(0L,"RPC_SetConnection",anyPortal,anyTarget) and it executes unconditionally both locally at the server (target==0 triggers HandleRoutedRPC on every recipient including the server itself) and relays to everyone else, fully bypassing Game.SetConnection's owner-based routing logic. ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO/HandleDestroyedZDO confirmed to have no sender/ownership check whatsoever. TeleportWorld.SetConnectedPortal/RPC_SetConnected confirmed exact including the IsOwner() guard on the receiving side. The Harmony ref-parameter technique for rewriting pkg in a RPC_RoutedRPC prefix is a legitimate, well-known Harmony capability for reference-type parameters even when the original signature isn't declared ref. The option is appropriately self-limiting ('covers only the RPC layer... RPC_ZDOData is the Invariant Assertion Harness's job'), which is honest scoping, not overclaiming.

**Verifier evidence:** ZDOMan.RPC_DestroyZDO/HandleDestroyedZDO :76953-76999 (confirmed no sender check) ; Game.RPC_SetConnection registration :100067, handler :100653-100662 (confirmed no ownership check, broadcast-exploitable) ; Game.SetConnection legitimate path :100637-100651 ; TeleportWorld.SetConnectedPortal/RPC_SetConnected :143604-143629
