### 257. Lockdown Legibility Rule

`gapfill:lockdown:Lockdown Legibility Rule` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


Any key-based (Tier-A) lockdown longer than N seconds must be paired with a per-portal in-world signal — force-disconnect (vanilla UI shows it) or tag suffix + floating text — removed in the same tick the key is lifted.


**How it works:** With only `NoPortals` set, a vanilla portal is indistinguishable from a working one: `GetHoverText` (:143453-143464) shows `$piece_portal_connected` from `HaveTarget()` (connection != None) and `UpdatePortal` (:143491-143509) lights `m_target_found` from `IsTeleportable && TargetFound()` — neither reads NoPortals/NoBossPortals; the only feedback is `$msg_blocked` after a failed walk-in (:143523-143526). A Tier-B force-disconnect (connection = ZDOID.None) flips the hover to `$piece_portal_unconnected` and kills the glow for free. Rule, as a reconciler invariant: for every lockdown whose planned duration > LegibilityThreshold (default 30 s), the reconciler must observe on every portal in scope either (a) `GetConnectionZDOID(Portal)==None`, or (b) `s_tag` ends with the configured marker (≤ 4 chars so a 6-char tag still fits the client's 10-char `TextInput.RequestText(...,10)` box, :143482, :61515-61522) AND a DamageText overlay loop is running for peers within 30 m. On lift, the same tick that removes the key restores connections from the vault / strips the suffix and stops the overlay — the announcement stack then reports 'portals open'. The rule is enforced by the Invariant Assertion Harness: a key-lockdown found without a signal after the threshold is escalated to Tier-B automatically and logged.


**Player experience:** A locked portal either reads [Unconnected] and is dark, or reads its name with a ' [X]' suffix and shows an orange 'Portals locked' floating text when approached — never a glowing, [Connected] gate that rejects you with a one-line message.


**Failure modes:**
- Tag suffix rewrites change the tag string, and `Game.ConnectPortals` phase 1 (:100594-100606) tears down any pair whose members differ — the whole tag group must be rewritten inside one tick, or ConnectPortals must be prefixed off during the sweep, or 3+-member groups reshuffle their orphan.
- Suffix + player retag during lockdown: the client pre-fills the dialog with the suffixed tag; a player saving it keeps/loses the suffix unpredictably — the watcher must treat 'tag without suffix' as a new base tag and re-suffix.
- The overlay is 1.5 s (`m_textDuration`, :46335) and 30 m (`m_maxTextDistance`, :46337) — a re-send loop per nearby peer is required (see Locked-Gate Overlay).

**Designer citations:** TeleportWorld.GetHoverText — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143453-143464 ; TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal — :143491-143509 ; TeleportWorld.Teleport NoPortals branch — :143523-143526 ; TeleportWorld.Interact / TextInput.Show 10-char cap — :143482, :61509-61522 ; Game.ConnectPortals tag-mismatch teardown — :100594-100606 ; DamageText.m_textDuration / m_maxTextDistance — :46335-46337


**Open questions:**
- Whether GuiInputField clamps a pre-filled text longer than characterLimit — IN-GAME.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] TeleportWorld.GetHoverText confirmed exact: text2 = HaveTarget() ? "$piece_portal_connected" : "$piece_portal_unconnected" with no reference to NoPortals/NoBossPortals, confirming the option's central claim that a Tier-A key lockdown gives zero in-world signal. TextInput.instance.RequestText(this,"$piece_portal_tag",10) confirmed exact (the 10-char cap). Game.ConnectPortals tag-mismatch teardown (SetConnection(item, ZDOID.None) when partner tag/connection mismatches) confirmed exact, supporting the same-group-tag-preservation design for the Locked-Gate Overlay mechanism this rule depends on.

### 258. Locked-Gate Overlay

`gapfill:lockdown:Locked-Gate Overlay` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


The mechanics behind the legibility rule: atomic per-group tag suffixing that survives vanilla's reconciler, plus a budgeted RPC_DamageText loop that floats 'Portals locked' over each locked gate for peers within 30 m.


**How it works:** Tag suffix: group portals by exact `s_tag` (ordinal, :100597-100601); for each group, in ONE frame, claim ownership (`SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())`), `Set(ZDOVars.s_tag, tag + marker)`, `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` (:76702 — a tag-only write does not dirty the portal chunk), `ForceSendZDO` — same-group members keep identical strings so `ConnectPortals` phase 1 sees no mismatch and existing links survive; the Mass-Rewrite budget applies per GROUP not per portal (groups are small). Store the original tag in the vault keyed by rounded position. Hover on the client re-reads `GetTagInfo()` every frame (:143455). Overlay: per tick (every 1.2 s) for each locked portal, for each ready peer whose character ZDO (`ConnectedCharacters.All()`) is within 30 m: `ZPackage p; p.Write((int)DamageText.TextType.Bonus); p.Write(portalPos + Vector3.up*2.5f); p.Write("$tpl_locked"/plain text); p.Write(false); ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, "RPC_DamageText", p)` — handler `RPC_DamageText` (:46494-46510) checks distance to the peer's camera ≤ `m_maxTextDistance` (30 f) and `AddInworldText` (:46395+) localises the text and colours Bonus orange (1f,0.63f,0.24f) with 1.5 s duration (:46335). Never TextType.TooHard/Blocked (they mangle the string). Peer-targeted, not broadcast, so cost = (locked portals × nearby peers) per 1.2 s. On lift: strip suffix in the same group-atomic way, stop the loop.


**Player experience:** Approaching a locked gate, an orange 'Portals locked' floats above it every ~1.5 s while within 30 m; the hover reads Tag:"Home [X]" [Connected]. When the lockdown lifts, the text stops and the tag is back to "Home".


**Failure modes:**
- Untagged groups ("") become " [X]" — a distinct, still-single group; fine, but restore must map " [X]" → "".
- Player retags during lockdown reshuffle groups; the watcher re-suffixes on the next tick (one ConnectPortals window of inconsistency, ≤5 s).
- Overlay text is not shown when the player's HUD is hidden (`Hud.IsUserHidden`) or outside 30 m; it is decoration, not enforcement.
- Marker eats 4 of the 10 client characters if the player edits the tag during lockdown.

**Designer citations:** Game.ConnectPortals tag equality — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100597-100611 ; ZDOMan.SetDirtyPortals — :76702 ; TeleportWorld.GetHoverText/GetTagInfo — :143453-143464 ; DamageText.RPC_DamageText / AddInworldText / constants — :46494-46510, :46395-46445, :46335-46337 ; ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC — :83554 ; Wonderland ConnectedCharacters.All — /home/rohan/WubarrkCODING/SERVER SIDE ONLY/Wonderland/Core/Data/ConnectedCharacters.cs:56


**Open questions:**
- Whether a vanilla client refreshes the hover string for a portal it currently stands beside after a server-side s_tag write without a zone reload — IN-GAME (GetTagInfo reads the ZDO each frame, expected yes).

### 259. Beacon Cleanup Sweep

`gapfill:lockdown:Beacon Cleanup Sweep` · domain **lockdown** · source `gapfill:lockdown`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed


When a Raid Beacon or organic raid at a managed gate ends, destroy leftover event creatures near the gate server-side instead of waiting for the client-side despawn walk.


**How it works:** Event creatures carry `ZDOVars.s_eventCreature=true` (SpawnSystem.Spawn :110960-110963 via `MonsterAI.SetEventCreature` :28280-28284). Vanilla despawn is client-side and slow: `BaseAI` only calls `MoveAwayAndDespawn` when `IsEventCreature() && !RandEventSystem.HaveActiveEvent()` and the creature has no target and is not alerted (:27885-27892) — an aggro'd troll stays. On `ResetRandomEvent()` (or when `GetCurrentRandomEvent()` transitions to null), run `ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear(gatePos, m_eventRange + 32)` (Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25), select ZDOs with `GetBool(ZDOVars.s_eventCreature)` whose prefab has a `Character` and is not `s_tamed`, and `SetOwner(session)+DestroyZDO` them, budgeted (≤64 per tick) — same primitives as Portal Sanctuary. Optionally skip creatures currently `s_alert` true within 20 m of a player (let the fight finish).


**Player experience:** The moment the lockdown lifts, the raid horde at the gate vanishes rather than shuffling off into the woods for a minute.


**Failure modes:**
- Destroying creatures mid-combat drops no loot and can feel like a bug — the alert/proximity skip trades cleanliness for fairness.
- Organic raids elsewhere are untouched (sweep is gate-scoped).

**Designer citations:** SpawnSystem.Spawn SetEventCreature — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:110954-110963 ; MonsterAI.SetEventCreature / IsEventCreature — :28280-28293 ; BaseAI event-creature despawn — :27885-27892 ; ZDOMan.DestroyZDO — :76929 ; Wonderland ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear — Core/Data/ZdoSpatialQuery.cs:25


**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] SpawnSystem.Spawn's s_eventCreature write, MonsterAI.SetEventCreature/IsEventCreature, and BaseAI's slow client-side despawn condition (requires no target and not alerted) all confirmed exact -- correctly motivating the need for a faster server-side sweep. ZDOMan.DestroyZDO confirmed public and usable exactly as the shared primitive from Portal Sanctuary. This is again a route-form (object-existence) decision fully owned by the server -- passes the enforceability test.

### 260. Lights Out — server-forced sleep fade (SleepStart/SleepStop)

`gapfill:ux:Lights Out — server-forced sleep fade (SleepStart/SleepStop)` · domain **ux** · source `gapfill:ux`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed


The server fires vanilla's own 'SleepStart'/'SleepStop' routed RPCs at one peer or at everyone, producing a full-screen sleep fade with input lockout — the only global-blackout primitive that needs no prefab hash and no client mod.


**How it works:** Game.Start registers two ZDO-less routed RPCs on every peer: ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register('SleepStart', SleepStart) and Register('SleepStop', SleepStop) (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100063-100064). The client handlers are Game.SleepStart -> Player.m_localPlayer.SetSleeping(true) (:100752-100759) and Game.SleepStop -> SetSleeping(false) + AttachStop() + a profile save when m_saveTimer > 60 (:100761-100777). Player.SetSleeping flips the private m_sleeping bool; on the false edge it shows '$msg_goodmorning', grants SEMan.s_statusEffectRested, stamps m_wakeupTime and increments PlayerStatType.Sleep (:15992-16005). While m_sleeping is true, Player.InCutscene() returns true (:15505-15508), which is what disables input, and Hud.UpdateBlackScreen fades the loading canvas to alpha 1 over Game.m_fadeTimeSleep and shows the sleeping-progress panel in preference to the teleport panel (:47853-47871, fade duration :47845-47847). Vanilla only uses this from the server-only Game.UpdateSleeping (:100712-100733), which broadcasts to 0L after EnvMan.SkipToMorning(). A mod invokes the same RPC directly: ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, 'SleepStart') for one player, or 0L for everyone (the server's own local dispatch hits a null m_localPlayer and no-ops). Because the mod never sets Game.m_sleeping, vanilla's UpdateSleeping will NOT send the matching SleepStop; the mod must send 'SleepStop' itself after its work (a Blackout Swap: SleepStart -> rewrite connections/positions -> RPC_TeleportPlayer -> SleepStop). Ordering: Hud gives the sleeping panel precedence over the teleport panel, so a teleport issued under the sleep fade is invisible to the player; Player.TeleportTo has no sleeping check (:15302-15327) and UpdateTeleport still runs from the !IsDead branch of FixedUpdate, so the move completes under the black screen. Time is NOT skipped unless the mod also calls EnvMan.instance.SkipToMorning() server-side (:100729).


**Player experience:** The screen fades to black exactly like going to bed, with the sleeping spinner. The player cannot move or open menus. When the server sends SleepStop the screen fades back in, '$msg_goodmorning' flashes centre-screen, they receive the Rested buff, and — if they were seated or in a bed — they are stood up (AttachStop). If the mod teleported them meanwhile, they wake somewhere else with no portal swirl.


**Failure modes:**
- SetSleeping(true) blocks Player.AttachStop (:15892) — a player who was in a bed/chair stays attached until SleepStop; a teleport issued to an attached-and-sleeping player ping-pongs (UpdateAttach runs before UpdateTeleport, :10217/:10226).
- No matching SleepStop is ever sent by vanilla for a mod-initiated SleepStart (Game.m_sleeping is false on the server, :100718). A crashed mod tick leaves every targeted player black-screened until they relog.
- Side effects on wake are not optional: Rested buff, '$msg_goodmorning', Sleep stat increment (:15999-16002) and a player-profile save if m_saveTimer > 60 (:100769-100776).
- If a real sleep cycle is in progress (Game.m_sleeping true) the server's own UpdateSleeping will send SleepStop within 2 s and wake the mod's targets early (:100720-100725).
- Fade time is Game.m_fadeTimeSleep, an Inspector float — the blackout is not instant; plan the swap for after the fade completes (needs an in-game timing).

**Designer citations:** Game.Start — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100063-100064 ; Game.SleepStart/SleepStop — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100752-100777 ; Game.UpdateSleeping — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100712-100733 ; Player.SetSleeping — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15992-16005 ; Player.InCutscene m_sleeping branch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15505-15508 ; Player.AttachStop sleeping guard — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15890-15895 ; Hud.UpdateBlackScreen — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:47853-47871; GetFadeDuration :47838-47851 ; ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC local-dispatch branch — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83577-83595


**Open questions:**
- Value of Game.m_fadeTimeSleep on the shipped Game prefab (Inspector). In-game: time SleepStart to full black on a vanilla client.
- Does a SleepStart delivered while the player is mid-teleport (m_teleporting) break the teleport panel handoff? In-game: send RPC_TeleportPlayer then SleepStart 0.5 s later and observe both overlays.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Every load-bearing citation checks out exactly against the server decompile. Game.Start registers 'SleepStart'/'SleepStop' at :100063-100064 (ZDO-less routed RPCs). Game.SleepStart/SleepStop bodies at :100752-100777 match verbatim (SetSleeping(true)/false+AttachStop+conditional profile save). Player.InCutscene's m_sleeping branch confirmed at :15495-15513 — m_sleeping alone forces InCutscene()=true. Player.SetSleeping body (:15992-16003) confirmed: flips m_sleeping, on false-edge shows $msg_goodmorning, grants s_statusEffectRested, stamps m_wakeupTime, increments Sleep stat — exactly as claimed. Hud.UpdateBlackScreen (:47853-47875) confirmed to give the sleeping panel branch priority over the teleport-progress branch, and GetFadeDuration returns m_fadeTimeSleep (default 3f) only when IsSleeping(). Player.TeleportTo (:15302-15323) has no sleeping check — only IsTeleporting()/m_teleportCooldown<2f gates — confirmed by direct read. AttachStop's 'if(m_sleeping||!m_attached) return' guard does not block SleepStop's flow because SetSleeping(false) is called first, clearing m_sleeping before AttachStop() runs. ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC's local-dispatch-for-targetPeerID==0L branch confirms the server's own HandleRoutedRPC call into SleepStart/SleepStop hits a null Player.m_localPlayer and no-ops safely, exactly as claimed. Enforcement is honestly labeled client-honoured (pure UX, no permission gate implied).

### 261. Dream Reel — RPC_SetDreamCinematic queued video

`gapfill:ux:Dream Reel — RPC_SetDreamCinematic queued video` · domain **ux** · source `gapfill:ux`  
**Feasibility:** needs-ingame-check → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


The server queues a named video cinematic that plays on every client's next sleep — an ambient, one-shot narrative channel with no gameplay effect.


**How it works:** CinematicsManager.Update registers ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<string>('RPC_SetDreamCinematic', RPC_SetDreamCinematic) once ZRoutedRpc and Game exist (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:42368-42374). The handler stores the name in the static m_dreamCinematic if Player.m_localPlayer exists (:42616-42623). CinematicsManager.OnSleep plays it when non-empty and the local player IsSleeping(), then clears it (:42607-42614). The vanilla sender is the static CinematicsManager.SetDreamCinematic(name) which broadcasts to 0L (:42601-42605); a mod can call ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, 'RPC_SetDreamCinematic', name) to target one player. Combined with the Lights Out option (SleepStart puts the player into IsSleeping()), the server can force the video immediately rather than waiting for a real bed sleep — OnSleep is what checks IsSleeping(), so the call site of OnSleep decides whether a forced sleep triggers it (it is invoked from the sleep flow on the client; needs confirmation). Video names are the entries of CinematicsManager.m_videos (Inspector data, :42628); only names present in the client's list can play. UX value for portals: a 'network rebuilt' or lore card when a hub is retired; strictly cosmetic.


**Player experience:** Next time the player sleeps (or is put to sleep by the server), a full-screen video plays before the morning fade; Escape/Jump/B skips it (:42379).


**Failure modes:**
- Requires a real or forced sleep; without Lights Out it is deferred indefinitely.
- Video names are Inspector data; an unknown name is a silent no-op or a log line depending on Play()'s handling (unverified).
- Registration happens in Update, not Awake; a client that has not yet ticked CinematicsManager.Update drops the RPC with 'Failed to find rpc method'.
- Only vanilla-shipped videos exist; no custom content can be injected.

**Designer citations:** CinematicsManager.Update registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:42368-42374 ; CinematicsManager.SetDreamCinematic/OnSleep/RPC_SetDreamCinematic — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:42601-42623


**Open questions:**
- Which video names exist in CinematicsManager.m_videos on a 1.0.7 client? In-game: dump m_videos[i].name on a client.
- Is CinematicsManager.OnSleep invoked from the forced SleepStart path or only from Bed's own sleep sequence? In-game: send SetDreamCinematic then SleepStart and see whether the video plays.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- The uncertain claim 'needs confirmation: whether forced sleep triggers OnSleep' is resolved by the decompile itself: OnSleep is invoked by SleepText.ShowDreamText (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:141936-141966), fired from the m_sleepingProgress panel's OnEnable, which activates purely from Player.IsSleeping()==true regardless of how sleep began — so forced SleepStart does trigger the dream video.
- Feasibility should move from needs-ingame-check to feasible given this resolved chain (video name must still be present in the client's own m_videos list).

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] Core citations all verified: CinematicsManager.Update lazily registers 'RPC_SetDreamCinematic' (:42371-42374), static m_dreamCinematic field (:42314), RPC_SetDreamCinematic handler stores name if Player.m_localPlayer exists (:42616-42622), static SetDreamCinematic broadcasts to 0L (:42601-42605), OnSleep checks IsSleeping() and plays+clears (:42607-42614). The option flagged one open question — 'needs confirmation' whether a server-forced sleep (via the Lights Out SleepStart RPC) actually triggers CinematicsManager.OnSleep() rather than only a real bed-sleep flow. I traced this and it resolves definitively: OnSleep() is called from SleepText.ShowDreamText() (class at :141936, ShowDreamText at :141963-141966), which fires via Invoke('ShowDreamText',4f) in SleepText.OnEnable — and SleepText lives on the m_sleepingProgress GameObject that Hud.UpdateBlackScreen activates purely off player.IsSleeping() (:47868), which is driven solely by the m_sleeping bool that SleepStart's SetSleeping(true) call sets. There is no dependency on how sleep was entered (bed vs forced RPC), so the 'needs confirmation' caveat is resolved to YES — a server-forced SleepStart does trigger the dream video ~4s later. This upgrades feasibility from needs-ingame-check to feasible (still gated by the video name existing in the client's own Inspector-defined m_videos list, an already-acknowledged caveat).

### 262. Puppet Strings — server-invoked animator triggers on a player's body

`gapfill:ux:Puppet Strings — server-invoked animator triggers on a player's body` · domain **ux** · source `gapfill:ux`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed


The server invokes the per-character 'SetTrigger' RPC to play any animator trigger (stagger, jump, dodge, gpower, eat, emotes) on a player's body for everyone in view — a non-textual, body-language acknowledgement.


**How it works:** ZSyncAnimation.Awake registers m_nview.Register<string>('SetTrigger', RPC_SetTrigger) on every ZNetView-bearing animated object including players (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:87157). RPC_SetTrigger is a bare m_animator.SetTrigger(name) with no owner check (:87330-87332). Vanilla's own sender broadcasts to ZNetView.Everybody (:87260-87263), so the ZDO-scoped route is: ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, characterZdoId, 'SetTrigger', name) — every peer that currently has that Player instantiated (the owner and everyone within its active area) runs the trigger; peers without the instance drop it in ZNetScene.FindInstance (:83656-83663). Targeting a single peer (peer.m_uid instead of 0L) plays it only on that player's own screen. Trigger names that the vanilla Player code itself fires, and that therefore exist on the Player animator: 'stagger' (:2851), 'jump' (:3483), 'interact' (:7659), 'eat' (:7705), 'equip_hip' (:8749), 'dodge' (:15196), 'gpower' (:15717), 'attack_abort' (:23006), 'detach' (:23010), 'attach' (:24045). Emotes are NOT triggers — they go through ZDOVars.s_emote/s_emoteID (:15585-15598) — so an 'emote_*' trigger name is Inspector data. Because this is purely animator state, it changes no ZDO, no position and no gameplay: 'gpower' plays the forsaken-power raise animation without granting anything; 'stagger' plays the stagger without the RPC_Stagger rotation write. UX use: 'request accepted' nod (interact), 'rejected' (stagger), 'hub rotated' (gpower) — visible to bystanders, which makes it a social signal as well.


**Player experience:** The player's character performs the animation on everyone's screen (and their own, third-person). Controls are not locked and nothing else happens.


**Failure modes:**
- Animator triggers are consumed by transitions; a trigger with no valid transition from the current state is silently swallowed (e.g. 'dodge' mid-air).
- A trigger that starts an attack-family clip can desync the owner's Humanoid state machine (m_attack references) until the clip ends; stick to non-attack triggers.
- Only peers holding the instance play it; a player standing alone sees only their own body.
- Trigger names beyond the ten used by code are Inspector data.

- Full trigger parameter list on the Player animator (Inspector). In-game: on a client, ZSyncAnimation.HasParameter(name, AnimatorControllerParameterType.Trigger) (:87334) for candidate names.
- Does 'gpower' fired externally leave any lingering animator bool that blocks the real forsaken-power activation until the clip ends?

RPC_SetTrigger is exactly 'm_animator.SetTrigger(name)' with no owner/sender check (:87329-87331). The client-side SetTrigger wrapper calls m_nview.InvokeRPC(ZNetView.Everybody,'SetTrigger',name) (:87260-87262), and ZNetView.InvokeRPC(targetID,...) resolves to ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(targetID, m_zdo.m_uid, method, parameters) (:82850-82852) — confirming the server-side call form is exactly the vanilla wire shape. ### 264. The Free Burst — vanilla's own 'portal connected' effect via a None→X connection flip

`gapfill:ux:The Free Burst — vanilla's own 'portal connected' effect via a None→X connection flip` · domain **ux** · source `gapfill:ux`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed


Flipping a portal's Portal connection None→X on the server makes every nearby vanilla client play TeleportWorld.m_connected at that portal — the only portal-local VFX that needs no prefab-hash guess.


**How it works:** TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal runs on the client every 0.5 s (InvokeRepeating in Awake, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143450) and does: flag = HaveTarget(); if (flag && !m_hadTarget) m_connected.Create(transform.position, transform.rotation); m_hadTarget = flag (:143491-143501). HaveTarget() reads GetConnectionZDOID(ConnectionType.Portal) != None off the client's copy of the ZDO (:143631-143638), and the connection is network-serialized (ZDO.Serialize :74169-74173). Awake seeds m_hadTarget = HaveTarget() (:143439-143451), so an already-connected portal does not fire on instantiate — the burst fires only on a rising edge observed by the poll. Server recipe: zdo.SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID()); zdo.SetConnection(Portal, ZDOID.None); ZDOMan.instance.ForceSendZDO(zdo.m_uid); wait >= 1 s (two client polls) so every viewer has observed None and set m_hadTarget=false; then SetConnection(Portal, target) + ForceSendZDO again. Each 0.5 s poll on each nearby client then sees the edge and spawns m_connected. If the portal is already at its intended target and the burst is wanted as pure feedback, the same None-then-X cycle works; TeleportWorld.Teleport re-reads the connection at transit time (:143539) so a player walking in during the ~1 s None window simply gets no transit (gate 1). This is the natural acknowledgement for 'destination changed' in any routing option, and it doubles as an honest signal: the burst means the client's ZDO copy really did change.


**Player experience:** The portal flares with the vanilla 'link established' particle/sound burst. The hover text flips $piece_portal_unconnected → $piece_portal_connected across the same cycle.


**Failure modes:**
- Game.ConnectPortals may re-pair the portal to a random same-tag partner during the None window (:100607-100622) unless the mod owns pairing for managed portals or the cycle completes inside one 5 s tick and the mod writes last.

### 265. NEVER USE — RPC_RegisterKill achievement injection

`gapfill:ux:NEVER USE — RPC_RegisterKill achievement injection` · domain **ux** · source `gapfill:ux`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed


A ZDO-less routed RPC the server can aim at any player that writes enemy/boss kill stats and platform campaign progress into that player's local profile — listed so nobody uses it as a 'feedback' channel.


**How it works:** Game.Start registers ZRoutedRpc.instance.Register<string,int,int,int,bool>('RPC_RegisterKill', RPC_RegisterKill) on every peer (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100069). The handler ignores sender and does GetPlayerProfile().IncrementStatEnemy(enemyName, ...) and IncrementStat(BossKills|EnemyKills); for bossNumber > 0 it additionally increments BossKillSolo/Multiplayer, calls PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform?.ActivityProvider?.CompleteTaskAsync(null, 'Boss'+n, Completed), writes PlatformPrefs 'CampaignProgress', and for bossNumber == 8 completes the 'Campaign' activity (:100837-100866). Vanilla's sender is Game.RegisterKill(playerPeerID, ...) (:100832-100835). There is no gameplay-visible output whatsoever — no message, no effect — so it has zero UX value, and any invocation is silent tampering with a player's statistics and platform achievements. Also note the security face: because m_senderPeerID is unauthenticated and the RPC is peer-addressable, any client can already inject kills into any other client; a server prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (:83632) dropping 'RPC_RegisterKill' packets whose socket peer is not the server is a cheap integrity win.


**Player experience:** Nothing visible. Later, the player's stats page and platform achievements are wrong.


**Failure modes:**
- Silent corruption of PlayerProfile stats (.fch) and platform campaign state.
- cheatsUsed=false marks the increments as legitimate for achievement gating.

**Designer citations:** Game.Start registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100069 ; Game.RegisterKill / RPC_RegisterKill — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:100832-100866 ; ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (veto point) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83632-83644


**Open questions:**
- Whether ActivityProvider is non-null on the Steam backend (Splatform assembly, outside this decompile) — affects only the blast radius of misuse.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Verified exactly. Game.Start registers Register<string,int,int,int,bool>('RPC_RegisterKill', RPC_RegisterKill) (:100069, exact match to the 5-parameter shape). Game.RegisterKill/RPC_RegisterKill bodies (:100832-100863) confirmed to ignore the sender parameter entirely and perform IncrementStatEnemy, IncrementStat(BossKills/EnemyKills), and for bossNumber>0 the BossKillSolo/Multiplayer increment, PlatformManager ActivityProvider.CompleteTaskAsync('Boss'+n), PlatformPrefs 'CampaignProgress' write, and bossNumber==8 CompleteActivityAsync('Campaign') — all as claimed, with zero visible feedback of any kind. The 'security face' claim also checks out: ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC, the actual network entry point (:83631-83641, verified directly), deserializes RoutedRPCData and forwards purely by m_targetPeerID with no cross-check that the sending rpc/socket actually owns the claimed m_senderPeerID. Correctly and conservatively labeled ruled-out as a UX/feedback mechanism.

### 266. Live Portal Markers — removable, labelled map markers via persistent events

`gapfill:ux:Live Portal Markers — removable, labelled map markers via persistent events` · domain **ux** · source `gapfill:ux`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


The server injects one ActivePersistentEvent per managed hub; every vanilla client draws an EventArea circle plus an animated, LABELLED RandomEvent pin at that position and REMOVES both when the server drops the entry — the removable map surface the catalog said did not exist.


**How it works:** Client Minimap.UpdatePersistentEventPins runs every 1 s over PersistentEventSystem.instance.m_activePersistentEvents.list: for each unknown eventId it AddPins an EventArea circle of m_worldSize = radius*2 and a RandomEvent pin (animated, double size) named Localization.Localize(item.Source.mapTokenString); any eventId no longer in the list has both pins RemovePin'd (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57505-57549). The list is server-authoritative: PersistentEventSystem.UpdateClientEventsList(target) sends JsonUtility.ToJson(m_activePersistentEvents) over the routed RPC 'UpdateClientEventsList' and the client RPC_UpdateClientEventsList overwrites its copy (SERVER :105407-105418); new peers request it via m_onNewPeer (:105289, :105391-105404). Both m_activePersistentEvents and m_possibleEvents are public fields (:105070-105073). Server recipe: pick a sourceEventId k whose PersistentEvent has an empty environmentOverride, graphicalEffects == 0 and no objectsToSpawn (enumerate PersistentEventSystem.instance.m_possibleEvents at runtime — the same Inspector list the client has); Add(new ActivePersistentEvent{ eventId = <mod range, e.g. 1_000_000+n>, sourceEventId = k, position = hubPos, radius = 8f, startTime = ZNet.instance.GetTimeSeconds(), duration = -1.0 }); then ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(0L, 'UpdateClientEventsList', JsonUtility.ToJson(PersistentEventSystem.instance.m_activePersistentEvents)). Bypassing RPC_RequestStartEvent (:105341-105379) avoids GenerateEventLocation, SpawnLocationMidGame and ObjectSpawnSettings.Create — nothing is spawned. duration < 0 is exempt from the 30 s expiry sweep (:105219-105225). PrepareSave/Save/Load persist the JSON in the world file (:105237-105280), so markers survive restarts; after Load, m_eventIdCounter = max+1 (:105278), harmless. Removal: list.Remove(entry) + the same broadcast; clients delete both pins within 1 s. Position and radius are free; the LABEL is fixed to the chosen event type's mapTokenString (:104766) — every hub shows the same word (e.g. the storm's token). radius also sets the circle size (worldSize = radius*2) and bounds every side effect below, so keep it tiny (a few metres).


**Player experience:** A small event circle and a pulsing double-size event icon labelled with the event type's name appear on the map at each hub, for everyone, including players who have never explored there. When a hub is retired the marker vanishes within a second. Walking into the few-metre radius may briefly change the weather if the chosen event type has an environmentOverride.


**Failure modes:**
- The label is Inspector data per event type (mapTokenString) and cannot be free text; all hubs share it. Which event types exist and their tokens are unknown until enumerated in-game.
- Side effects scale with radius: EnvMan uses PersistentEventSystem.GetEnvironmentOverride for the local player inside radius (:105432-105439, EnvMan :95927-95931); UpdateComputeBuffer enables the Snow shader effect if graphicalEffects == Snow (:105124-105150); SpawnSystem spawners with m_requiredPersistentEvent match by internalName inside radius (client :111344-111351); WearNTear pieces with m_requiredPersistentEvent take m_eventDamage depending on being inside/outside a matching event (client :150453-150463) — a piece that REQUIRES a different event and sits inside our marker is damaged. Choose the blandest event type and radius <= 8 m.
- RPC_RequestStopEvent (:105381-105389) and RPC_RequestStartEvent (:105341) run on the server with NO sender check — any client can delete the markers (or start real events). Veto 'RequestStopEvent'/'RequestStartEvent' packets from non-server sockets in a ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC prefix (:83632) or re-assert markers on a tick.
- ActivePersistentEvent.Source indexes m_possibleEvents[sourceEventId] on both sides (:104938); an out-of-range index throws in the client's UpdatePersistentEventPins every second. Never use an index the shipped list does not contain.
- A client-side PersistentEventIndicator particle (client :105945-105964, nomap-gated) points toward the nearest event when the list is non-empty — cosmetic noise in NoMap worlds.
- The pins are not saved and not player-removable; players cannot dismiss them.

### 267. Random-event area pin as a temporary marker — RULED OUT

`gapfill:ux:Random-event area pin as a temporary marker — RULED OUT` · domain **ux** · source `gapfill:ux`  
**Feasibility:** ruled-out → **ruled-out** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** small · **Verdict:** confirmed


Forging RandEventSystem's 'SetEvent' RPC to draw the single random-event pin at a hub is overwritten by the server's own event sync and would spawn a raid.


**How it works:** Client Minimap draws m_randEventAreaPin (EventArea, size m_eventRange*2*0.9) and m_randEventPin (animated, double size, name = Localize(event.GetHudText())) from RandEventSystem.instance.GetCurrentRandomEvent() and removes both when it becomes null (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57470-57502). The client's m_randomEvent is set by RPC_SetEvent(eventName, time, pos) via SetRandomEventByName (SERVER :106964-106978), registered in RandEventSystem.Start (:106781). The dedicated server itself periodically calls SendCurrentRandomEvent, broadcasting either the live event or ('', 0, zero) which clears it (:106952-106962), so a forged event is wiped on the next server send. Setting a real event name also activates that event's spawners on clients whose players are inside m_eventRange and plays the raid music/HUD text. Only one random event exists at a time. Use Live Portal Markers instead.


**Player experience:** A raid warning banner, raid music and a spawn wave at the hub, then the pin disappears when the server resyncs.


**Failure modes:**
- Spawns a real raid inside m_eventRange.
- Single slot; cleared by the server's own SendCurrentRandomEvent.
- Event name must exist in the client's m_events list.

- Could cite the precise 2-second SendCurrentRandomEvent interval (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs, m_sendTimer>2f check near :106878-106884) rather than the vaguer 'next server send.'

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Verified. RandEventSystem.Start registers 'SetEvent' (:106781, exact). SendCurrentRandomEvent (:106952-106961) broadcasts either the real m_randomEvent or a clearing ('',0,zero) and is called on a hard 2-second timer (m_sendTimer>2f, confirmed near :106878-106884), meaning any forged event is overwritten within ~2s, not a vague 'next sync.' RPC_SetEvent's handler explicitly guards with !ZNet.instance.IsServer() (:106964-106969) so it only ever mutates client-side state, and the periodic broadcast will indeed stomp any client-only forged state. Ruled-out verdict and reasoning both hold up; the option could have cited the exact 2s interval but the substance is correct.

### 268. Summoning Gaze — consent-handshake player-to-player teleport (TPA)

`gapfill:ux:Summoning Gaze — consent-handshake player-to-player teleport (TPA)` · domain **ux** · source `gapfill:ux`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


Requester emotes while looking at another player; the server pairs the s_lookTarget ray with the target's character ZDO, toasts the target, and on the target's accept-emote within 30 s force-teleports the requester to the target's live position — no portal, no chat, no client mod.


**How it works:** Input: EmoteSignals polls ZDOVars.s_emoteID/s_emote on every character ZDO (Player.StartEmote writes them, assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15585-15598). Aim: CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation, on the owning client, writes ZDOVars.s_lookTarget = GetLookFromPos() + m_character.GetLookDir()*100f at most every 0.2 s when it changed (:5041-5076; key 'LookTarget' :78677, session-only :78689-78693). On the request emote the server reads requester.Zdo.GetVec3(s_lookTarget), forms the ray from requester eye pos (Zdo.GetPosition()+~1.6 up) toward it, and picks the connected character (ConnectedCharacters.All()) whose ZDO position lies within an angular cone (e.g. 8 degrees, max 40 m) of that ray; ambiguity → nearest to the ray. It records {requesterPlayerId, targetPlayerId, expires=now+30s} keyed on ZDOVars.s_playerID (stable) and toasts the target via PlayerNotify.Toast: 'X wants to teleport to you — <accept emote> to accept'. Accept: the target performs the accept emote before expiry. Execution guards, all server-readable: target.Zdo.GetBool(s_dead) and requester.Zdo.GetBool(s_dead) (:78403), requester.Zdo.GetBool(s_inBed) (:78457) (attached players ping-pong — UpdateAttach precedes UpdateTeleport :10217/:10226), a per-player send ledger enforcing >= 12 s between forced teleports (Player.TeleportTo refuses if m_teleportCooldown < 2f and the cooldown is held at 0 for the whole teleport, :15313-15320, :15334). Then: pos = target.Zdo.GetPosition() + 1.5 m behind the target's facing (Zdo.GetRotation()*Vector3.back) + Vector3.up; ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(requester.Peer.m_uid, 'RPC_TeleportPlayer', pos, target.Zdo.GetRotation(), true) (handler :41962-41968) or the ZDO-scoped 'RPC_TeleportTo' (:886, :4126-4132). distant:true gives the vanilla 8 s swirl and never fails (15 s force-land). Confirmation: the server polls the requester's ZDO position for the ~2 s snap (UpdateTeleport pins position after 2 s, :15337-15348) and toasts both. Everything bypasses IsTeleportable — ore travels; say so in the toast.


**Player experience:** Look at a friend, do the request emote (e.g. /wave). They see a toast naming you; they /nod within 30 s. You get the portal black-screen swirl and appear beside them ~8 s later, carrying whatever you had. If they ignore it, you get a 'request expired' toast.


**Failure modes:**
- s_lookTarget is written only when it changes and only if the Player prefab's CharacterAnimEvent has m_headRotation && m_head set (:5043) — Inspector data; if unset the channel is empty and aim must fall back to nearest-player-within-N-metres.
- The look ray is camera-derived (GetLookDir); first-person/over-shoulder offsets make the cone miss at long range; cap at ~40 m.
- StartEmote refuses while attached, attacking, drawing a bow or on a ship (:15587) — a target seated at a helm cannot accept.
- Every vanilla gate is bypassed (NoPortals, NoBossPortals, IsTeleportable, wards); the mod must re-implement any it wants.
- Teleport failures are silent one-way (both RPC handlers discard TeleportTo's bool); confirm by position poll only.
- A dead target (s_dead) or a target mid-teleport gives a stale/zero position; re-read at accept time, not at request time.

**Designer citations:** CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:5041-5081 ; ZDOVars.s_lookTarget / s_sessionHashes — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78677, :78689-78693 ; Player.StartEmote/StopEmote — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15585-15609 ; Player.TeleportTo — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15302-15327; UpdateTeleport :15329-15378 ; Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:41962-41968; Character.RPC_TeleportTo :4126-4132 ; Player.FixedUpdate UpdateAttach before UpdateTeleport — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:10217, :10226


**Open questions:**
- Is m_headRotation enabled and m_head assigned on the Player prefab (Inspector)? In-game: poll s_lookTarget on a connected character ZDO while the player looks around; expect a changing non-zero Vector3 every ~0.2 s.
- Exact eye offset to use as the ray origin server-side (GetLookFromPos is a head-bone position). In-game: compare s_lookTarget - Zdo.GetPosition() against a known look direction.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Core primitives all verified exactly. CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation (:5041-5081) confirmed to write ZDOVars.s_lookTarget = lookFromPos + GetLookDir()*100f, throttled to at most every 0.2s and only when changed — matches the option's formula and cadence precisely. ZDOVars.s_lookTarget confirmed at :78677 with key string 'LookTarget', and confirmed to sit inside the session-only hash list at :78689-78693 (exact list matches). Player.StartEmote/StopEmote confirmed at :15585-15609 writing s_emote/s_emoteID. Chat.RPC_TeleportPlayer register/invoke/body (:41627,41959,41962-41968) and Character's ZDO-scoped RPC_TeleportTo (:886,4126-4132) both confirmed exactly matching the prompt's own known anchors. Player.TeleportTo (:15302-15323)/UpdateTeleport (:15329-15378) confirmed with no sleeping or ore/NoPortals gate of any kind (only IsTeleporting()/2s cooldown), supporting the claim this path bypasses IsTeleportable entirely — the option is honest about this. ### 269. Warp Verbs — /home, /back, /spawn without a portal

`gapfill:ux:Warp Verbs — /home, /back, /spawn without a portal` · domain **ux** · source `gapfill:ux`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


Three emote-triggered destinations resolved entirely server-side: nearest bed the player owns (ZDO s_owner), the server's own pre-teleport position ledger (the only party that can implement /back), and the world spawn from GetLocationIcon('StartTemple').


**How it works:** Trigger: an emote token per verb via EmoteSignals (s_emoteID/s_emote polling, Player.StartEmote assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:15585-15598), optionally armed by the crouch bit or by not standing at a portal. HOME: Bed.RPC_SetOwner writes ZDOVars.s_owner (profile UID) and s_ownerName onto the bed ZDO (:119813-119819); the server scans bed ZDOs (PrefabSetSweeper over bed prefab hashes, prefab filter mandatory because GrapplingPoint also uses s_owner :127909) and picks the bed with s_owner == requester s_playerID nearest to the requester (or most recently claimed if a mod-side timestamp is kept — vanilla stores none; the ACTIVE bed is unknowable, PlayerProfile.m_spawnPoint is local :106230-106233). Destination = bedZdo.GetPosition() + Vector3.up*1 (the exact spawn child transform is not ZDO data, Bed.GetSpawnPoint :119796-119799). BACK: before every server-issued teleport the mod appends (playerID, Zdo.GetPosition(), Zdo.GetRotation(), time) to a per-player ring; /back pops it. Only the server can do this — the client's death/logout/home points never leave the .fch (:106180-106253). Portal transits the mod did not issue can be added via PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit detection (Wonderland PositionWatch.cs:148) if wanted. SPAWN: ZoneSystem.instance.GetLocationIcon(Game.instance.m_StartLocation, out pos) on the server branch reads m_locationInstances (:115422-115447; m_StartLocation = 'StartTemple' :99845); the vanilla client itself spawns at pos + up*2 (client Game.FindSpawnPoint). Delivery: ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(peer.m_uid, 'RPC_TeleportPlayer', pos, rot, true) (:41957-41968). Guards as in Summoning Gaze: s_dead, s_inBed, per-player >= 12 s spacing, plus verb-specific cooldowns stored by s_playerID. Height for HOME/BACK comes from live ZDO positions (already standable); for any computed point use WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight (:151944), never ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight (dead raycast :115502-115511).


**Player experience:** Do the /home emote: an 8 s portal-style black screen, then you are standing beside your bed with everything you carried. /back returns you to where you were before the last server warp. /spawn drops you at the start stones. A toast names the destination before the fade.


**Failure modes:**
- 'Your bed' is ambiguous — vanilla lets a player own unlimited beds and never records the active one (Bed.Interact only claims when s_owner == 0, :119670-119725).
- Bypasses every vanilla gate; ore, boss lockdowns and NoPortals are all ignored — must be re-implemented or the verbs will undercut the portal economy.
- Silent no-op inside the teleport dead zone (cooldown held at 0 during teleport, then 2 s, :15313-15320, :15334); the ledger must space sends.
- A bed that is unloaded on the client is fine (distant teleport force-lands at 15 s), but a bed inside a base with a roof can land the player on the roof if +1 y is applied to a raised bed; use the ZDO y directly plus a small epsilon.
- GetLocationIcon returns the first dictionary match and requires the location's icon flags (Inspector); StartTemple is icon-flagged in vanilla.

### 270. Map Ping Picker — corrected: socket identity, y re-derivation, public gesture, arming

`gapfill:ux:Map Ping Picker — corrected: socket identity, y re-derivation, public gesture, arming` · domain **ux** · source `gapfill:ux`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


The map middle-click stays the only vanilla input that carries an arbitrary Vector3, but it must be captured in a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (where the ZRpc socket is in scope), its y must be recomputed with WorldGenerator.GetHeight, and it must be gated by an arming condition and a per-account debounce because it is free and broadcast to everyone.


**How it works:** Hook (hard precondition 1): HandleRoutedRPC(RoutedRPCData) has no socket in scope (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83646-83665) and m_senderPeerID is read straight off the wire (RoutedRPCData.Deserialize :83487-83495); the UserInfo payload is likewise self-authored (UserInfo.Serialize :72795-72799). The only place both the authentic connection and the payload coexist is ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc rpc, ZPackage pkg) (:83632-83644). Harmony prefix: var copy = new ZPackage(pkg.GetArray()); var d = new ZRoutedRpc.RoutedRPCData(); d.Deserialize(copy); if (d.m_methodHash != 'ChatMessage'.GetStableHashCode()) return; var peer = ZNet.instance.GetPeers().FirstOrDefault(p => p.m_rpc == rpc) (ZNetPeer.m_rpc is public :78780-78790); reject if peer == null || !peer.IsReady() || d.m_senderPeerID != peer.m_uid. Parse d.m_parameters: Vector3 pos, int type (3 == Ping), string name, string platformId, string text; additionally reject if platformId != peer.m_socket.GetHostName(). Never mutate the live pkg. Height (precondition 2): Chat.SendPing overwrites vector.y with the SENDER's y (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:42063-42064), so the received y is the player's altitude, not the terrain's at the click. Recompute y = WorldGenerator.instance.GetHeight(pos.x, pos.z) (:151944-151949); if y < 30 treat as water; never call ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight (raycast, returns p.y unchanged headless, :115502-115511). Resolve the destination as the nearest managed portal to (x, y, z) within a configurable radius via ZDOMan.instance.GetPortals() (:77643), not a raw coordinate. Public gesture (precondition 3): the ping is broadcast to 0L (client :42065), so every online player sees the ping marker and the 'Name: PING' map pin; document it as a visible, shared action and never use it for anything secret. Arming + debounce (precondition 4): a middle-click costs nothing, so act only when armed — the requester's character ZDO is within N m of a managed portal AND (crouch bit or a preceding emote within 10 s) — and keep a per-PlatformUserID debounce (e.g. one routing action per 5 s, ignore bursts). Feedback: tag echo + Free Burst + toast. Unarmed pings pass through untouched (return true) so vanilla ping behaviour is unchanged.


**Player experience:** Stand at your portal, crouch, open the map and middle-click near the destination portal. The portal flares (Free Burst), its hover tag changes to the destination name, and a toast confirms. Everyone online briefly sees your ping on their map, as with any ping.


**Failure modes:**
- Taking identity from m_senderPeerID or UserInfo lets a modified client route another player's portal in their name — the socket cross-check is mandatory.
- Using the packet y wires the destination to the player's altitude (100 m off on a mountain); re-derive with WorldGenerator.GetHeight, which is itself blind to terraforming (+/- a few metres).
- Pings are spammable and public; without arming/debounce every stray middle-click re-routes.
- On a PlayFab/Xbox backend GetHostName returns a different id form than the UserInfo platformId (:81271-81280); compare per backend or rely on m_uid equality only.
- If MessageHud/Chat singletons make the server itself register 'ChatMessage' (unverified), a second Register throws — the prefix approach avoids that entirely.

**Designer citations:** ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83632-83644 ; ZRoutedRpc.HandleRoutedRPC (no socket) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83646-83665 ; RoutedRPCData.Deserialize — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83487-83495 ; UserInfo.Serialize/Deserialize — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:72789-72799 ; ZNetPeer.m_rpc / m_socket / m_uid — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78780-78790 ; Chat.SendPing y override + broadcast to 0L — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:42058-42069 ; WorldGenerator.GetHeight — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:151944-151949 ; ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight raycast — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:115502-115511 ; ZDOMan.GetPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:77643


**Open questions:**
- Does the server hold a live Chat instance that already registers 'ChatMessage' (decides nothing for the prefix, but matters for anyone still using Register)? In-game: log Chat.instance == null on the dedicated server.
- Map click precision at default zoom in metres — determines the nearest-portal search radius. In-game: ping a known portal ten times and measure the scatter.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] This is the most technically demanding option in the set and it holds up completely under adversarial re-derivation. ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (:83631-83641, verified exact) is confirmed to be the true network-facing entry point (registered per-peer as peer.m_rpc.Register<ZPackage>('RoutedRPC', RPC_RoutedRPC) at :83530) and it deserializes RoutedRPCData purely from the packet with zero cross-check against the actual ZRpc/peer that delivered it — confirming this really is the only place both an authentic socket/peer and the claimed sender coexist, exactly as claimed. RoutedRPCData.Deserialize located at exactly :83487-83495 (character-for-character match). Chat.SendPing (client) confirmed to overwrite vector.y with the SENDER's own transform.y and broadcast InvokeRoutedRPC(0L,'ChatMessage', vector, 3, UserInfo.GetLocalUser(), '') — and critically, UserInfo (server, :72774-72799) implements ISerializableParameter with a custom Serialize writing Name then UserId.ToString() as two separate strings into the ZPackage, meaning the wire format really does flatten into (Vector3, int, string name, string platformId, string text) as the option's parsing recipe assumes, despite the call site passing a single UserInfo object — a subtle and correct piece of reverse engineering. peer.m_socket.GetHostName() confirmed elsewhere in the same file (line 79855) to be used precisely as a platform-user-id string, validating the proposed platformId==peer.m_socket.GetHostName() authentication check. ZNetPeer.m_rpc/m_socket/m_uid confirmed public (:78780-78784). WorldGenerator.GetHeight (:151934-151949) and ZDOMan.GetPortals (:77643) both confirmed at the exact cited lines.

**Verifier evidence:** ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC network entry point + per-peer registration — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83530,83631-83641 (verified exact) ; RoutedRPCData.Deserialize — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83487-83495 (verified exact) ; Chat.SendPing y-override + broadcast — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:42058-42069 (verified) ; UserInfo custom wire Serialize (Name, UserId.ToString) — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:72774-72799 (verified, confirms parameter-flattening claim) ; peer.m_socket.GetHostName() used as platform user id elsewhere — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:79855 (verified, validates the proposed auth check) ; ZNetPeer public m_rpc/m_socket/m_uid — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:78780-78784 (verified) ; WorldGenerator.GetHeight / ZDOMan.GetPortals — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:151934-151949,77643 (verified exact)

### 271. Plain chat as a command line — needs the RelationsProvider test

`gapfill:ux:Plain chat as a command line — needs the RelationsProvider test` · domain **ux** · source `gapfill:ux`  
**Feasibility:** needs-ingame-check → **needs-ingame-check** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed


Re-classify: slash commands are dead, but keyword-prefixed plain text or shouts WOULD reach the server even for a solo player if PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider is null on the Steam backend — one in-game test decides whether a 50+ character socket-authenticated command line exists.


**How it works:** Chat.InputText rewrites non-slash text to 'say <text>' and hands slash text to the local Terminal (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:41947-41955) — unknown /commands never leave the client. 'say' calls Chat.SendText, and both Shout (:41982-41988) and Talker.Say go through CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync (:41996-42042). That method has two shapes: if RelationsProvider == null it calls the handler ONCE with targetPeerID 0L (:42002-42006) — a broadcast that the dedicated server receives in RPC_RoutedRPC and handles locally (:83636-83638); otherwise it sends to the sender's own UserID plus one RPC per OTHER listed player (:42007-42041), so a solo player emits nothing and 2+ players only produce relay traffic. Whether Steam's RelationsProvider is null lives in the Splatform assembly (absent from this decompile). Circumstantial evidence AGAINST: Terminal's chat display code logs 'Relations provider was unavailable ... This should never happen!' when it is null (:45964-45968), and the friends-list UI takes a RelationsProvider.GetFriends() branch (:63855-63861) — Steam has friends, so a provider almost certainly exists. TEST: install a ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC prefix that logs m_methodHash == 'ChatMessage'.GetStableHashCode() with type and targetPeerID; have a SOLO vanilla Steam player type a sentence and a /s shout; a logged packet with m_targetPeerID == 0 means chat is a first-class channel. If it passes: the option is 'tp: <verb> <arg>' prefixed text, parsed in the same prefix with the sender resolved from the socket (GetPeers().First(p => p.m_rpc == rpc)), type 1 (Normal) or 2 (Shout), Localized feedback by toast. If it fails (expected): chat stays ruled-out and the 2+-player relay case is only an observation channel that must not be relied on for a solo player.


**Player experience:** If the test passes: type 'tp: home' in normal chat; a toast replies within a frame. Everyone nearby also sees the chat line (Normal range) or everyone online (Shout).


**Failure modes:**
- Expected outcome is that RelationsProvider is non-null on Steam and nothing is sent solo; do not ship any feature on this channel before the test.
- Even when relayed (2+ players), the message also reaches other players as ordinary chat — commands are public.
- Text is filtered/censored per RelationsManager.PlatformRequiresTextFiltering on some platforms (:42004, :42047-42051).

**Designer citations:** Chat.InputText — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:41947-41955 ; Chat.SendText — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:41975-41994 ; Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:41996-42042 ; 'Relations provider was unavailable' log — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:45964-45968 ; Friends list RelationsProvider branch — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:63855-63861 ; ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC local-handle rule — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:83636-83638


**Open questions:**
- Is PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider null on the Steam client build? The single decisive test is described above (solo player, prefix logging 'ChatMessage' hashes).
- Same question for PlayFab/Xbox crossplay clients, which may differ from Steam.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed] Verified in full detail, including the subtlest claim (that a solo player emits literally zero packets in the RelationsProvider!=null branch). Chat.InputText (client, :41947-41954) confirmed to rewrite non-slash text to 'say <text>' and hand slash text to the local Terminal — unknown /commands genuinely never leave the client. CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync (:41996-42033) confirmed: when RelationsProvider==null, it calls the handler exactly once with targetPeerID 0L (broadcast) — matching the option's claim precisely. When RelationsProvider!=null, it ALWAYS first calls sendMessageHandler(ZNet.instance.LocalPlayerCharacterID.UserID, false) — i.e. addressed to the sender's OWN character/session id — before looping over other players. Combined with the independently-verified ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC self-target rule (targetPeerID==m_id triggers only local HandleRoutedRPC and explicitly skips RouteRPC), this confirms a solo player's chat message, even in the non-null branch, never crosses the wire at all — exactly the option's claim that 'a solo player emits nothing.' The two cited pieces of circumstantial evidence are both real and reasonably argue Steam's provider is non-null in practice. The option is correctly hedged as needs-ingame-check since the Splatform/Steam backend implementation is not present in this decompile.

### 272. The Cartographer's Table — opt-in named-pin sync via a server-written MapTable

`gapfill:ux:The Cartographer's Table — opt-in named-pin sync via a server-written MapTable` · domain **ux** · source `gapfill:ux`  
**Feasibility:** feasible-with-caveats → **feasible-with-caveats** · **Enforcement:** client-honoured → **client-honoured** · **Effort:** medium-large · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


A server-owned Cartography Table beside each hub whose ZDOVars.s_data blob lists one named, saved pin per managed portal under a mod-reserved owner id; a player who presses Read receives the set, and re-reading later removes retired portals — the only re-syncable named-pin surface, and opt-in by construction.


**How it works:** MapTable.OnRead decompresses m_nview.GetZDO().GetByteArray(ZDOVars.s_data) and calls Minimap.instance.AddSharedMapData, toasting $msg_mapsynced/$msg_alreadysynced/$msg_mapnodata (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133837-133866). Blob format = Minimap.GetSharedMapData (client :58788-58835): Write(int 3) [Version.SharedMap: Pins=2, PinsAuthor=3, SERVER :112072-112076]; Write(int exploredLength) then exploredLength bools; Write(int pinCount); per pin: long ownerID, string name, Vector3 pos, int PinType, bool checked, string authorPlatformId. Compress with Utils.Compress and write to the table ZDO: claim ownership (SetOwner(ZDOMan.GetSessionID())), zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_data, bytes), ForceSendZDO. Client AddSharedMapData (:58857-58935): ReadExploredArray refuses and returns false unless exploredLength == m_explored.Length (:58840-58843) — write exactly textureSize*textureSize bools, all false (false never changes exploration, :58874). Then for pins: every existing pin with m_ownerID != 0 && != readerPlayerID is marked shouldDelete (:58889-58897); each incoming pin that has ANY saved pin within 1 m XZ is kept (shouldDelete cleared, not re-added, HavePinInRange :58341-58351); otherwise if ownerID != readerPlayerID it is AddPin'd with save:true and that ownerID (:58911-58918); finally marked pins are removed (:58921-58932). Owner-id convention: a fixed non-zero sentinel that can never equal a profile UID in practice (e.g. 0x544F5254414C5054); pins with ownerID 0 are the player's own and are never touched. Removal therefore works: drop a retired portal from the blob, the player presses Read again, and that pin (still owned by the sentinel) is deleted. m_textureSize probe: the C# default is 256 (:56287) but Inspector-overridable; read it from the world itself — any vanilla MapTable ZDO written by a player carries the client's exploredLength as the int after the version, so parse one existing s_data blob (or accept the first player write to the hub table) and cache it; fall back to 256*256. Hazard mitigation: because a Read deletes every non-own, non-listed pin (pins previously received from other players' tables), the server should UNION into its blob the pin lists of every other MapTable ZDO in the world (all server-readable via s_data) so those pins are re-listed and survive. Player writes: OnWrite (:133868-133893) first Reads, then overwrites s_data via RPC_MapData at the owner (:133895-133902) — the server must re-parse the new blob and re-inject hub pins on a tick (or block writes with a SetOwner prefix). Opt-in: nothing happens until a player presses Read on the table, and vanilla's own message confirms the sync.


**Player experience:** A cartography table stands by the hub. Read it: '$msg_mapsynced' and a named pin for every managed portal appears on your map, permanently until you read a table whose blob no longer lists it. Reading again with no changes gives '$msg_alreadysynced'. Your own pins are untouched.


**Failure modes:**
- Wrong explored length = 'Map exploration array size missmatch' warning and no pins (:58840-58843); m_textureSize is Inspector data — probe it from an existing blob.
- A Read deletes pins the player received from other players' tables unless the server re-lists them; the union step is mandatory or players lose shared pins.
- Dedup is by position within 1 m regardless of name/type (:58907-58910): a renamed portal at the same spot keeps the OLD pin name; to rename, move the pin >1 m or accept the stale label.
- Player OnWrite overwrites the server blob with their own merged map (:133883-133889); re-inject on a tick.
- Read is gated by PrivateArea.CheckAccess on the client (:133816-133820); place the table outside foreign wards.
- Pins are save:true in the player's .fch; a player who never reads again keeps stale pins forever.
- MapTable prefab name/hash is Inspector data; ZNetScene prefab enumeration for a MapTable component is required to fabricate one.

**Designer citations:** MapTable.OnRead/OnWrite/RPC_MapData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133832-133909 ; Minimap.GetSharedMapData — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:58788-58835 ; Minimap.ReadExploredArray — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:58837-58855 ; Minimap.AddSharedMapData — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:58857-58935 ; Minimap.HavePinInRange — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:58341-58351 ; Version.SharedMap enum — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:112072-112076 ; Minimap.m_textureSize default — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:56287 ; MapTable read access check — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133814-133821


**Open questions:**
- Actual Minimap.m_textureSize on the shipped prefab. In-game: log Minimap.instance.m_textureSize on a client, or parse any vanilla MapTable s_data blob server-side.
- MapTable prefab name (Inspector). In-game: enumerate ZNetScene.instance.m_prefabs for a MapTable component on the dedicated server.
- Does a server-fabricated MapTable ZDO (Piece + WearNTear) survive WearNTear support checks on the owning client (UpdateWear applies 100 damage per update when !HaveSupport with m_noSupportWear, :149662-149707)? Place it on solid ground or Instantiate the prefab so ZNetView.Awake sets fields correctly.

**VERIFIER CORRECTIONS (authoritative — apply these):**
- 'MapTable read access check — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133814-133821' cites GetReadHoverText (a tooltip-text callback), not a functional gate — the actual OnRead method has NO PrivateArea.CheckAccess call, so reading the table is unrestricted by ward permission; only OnWrite is actually gated by CheckAccess.

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] Core mechanism fully verified, including exact merge/delete pin semantics that are easy to get subtly wrong. MapTable class (:133788), 'MapData' RPC registration (:133803), OnRead/OnWrite/RPC_MapData (:133832-133903) all confirmed near-exactly at the cited lines. OnRead confirmed to decompress s_data via Utils.Decompress and call Minimap.instance.AddSharedMapData with the $msg_mapsynced/$msg_alreadysynced/$msg_mapnodata messaging exactly as claimed. RPC_MapData confirmed gated by m_nview.IsOwner() before writing s_data, validating the option's SetOwner-or-re-inject requirement. Minimap.AddSharedMapData (client, :58857-58932) verified in full: it marks ALL existing pins with m_ownerID!=0 && !=readerID for deletion, then for each incoming pin either clears deletion on the nearest existing pin within 1m (without checking that pin's owner matches — matching the option's precise 'not re-added' phrasing) or AddPins a new save:true pin under the given ownerID, then sweeps still-marked pins — this exactly reproduces the option's stated hazard ('a Read deletes every non-own, non-listed pin') and its own proposed mitigation (union in all other tables' pins) is the correct fix for a real, verified problem. One genuine correction: the option's prereq citation 'MapTable read access check — :133814-133821' actually points at GetReadHoverText, a TOOLTIP-only access check; the real OnRead method has no PrivateArea.CheckAccess call at all — reading is functionally unrestricted regardless of ward permission (only OnWrite is actually gated by CheckAccess). This doesn't hurt feasibility (if anything it removes a barrier) but the citation as labeled is misleading about what it gates.

**Verifier evidence:** MapTable.OnRead/OnWrite/RPC_MapData — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133788-133903 (verified) ; Minimap.AddSharedMapData exact merge/delete semantics — assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:58857-58932 (verified, confirms the option's stated hazard and mitigation precisely) ; GetReadHoverText is the actual referent of the 'read access check' citation, not OnRead — assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:133814-133821 vs 133837-133866 (correction)

### 273. Station Credit Primitives (Refund by RPC)

`gapfill:economy:Station Credit Primitives (Refund by RPC)` · domain **economy** · source `gapfill:economy`  
**Feasibility:** feasible → **feasible** · **Enforcement:** server-enforced → **server-enforced** · **Effort:** small-medium · **Verdict:** confirmed-with-correction


Pay a refund or reward into the player's own fireplace, smelter, cooking station or fermenter by invoking the station's vanilla ZNetView RPC at its owning client, instead of dropping items on the ground.


**How it works:** Every fuel/ore station registers owner-gated ZNetView RPCs the server can drive exactly the way it drives Game.RPC_SetConnection: `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(zdo.GetOwner(), zdo.m_uid, method, args)` (ZNetView.InvokeRPC is literally that one line, :82855-82858). The receiving client's ZNetView.HandleRoutedRPC (:82838-82848) dispatches to the handler, which checks `m_nview.IsOwner()` and writes the ZDO. Census of usable credit RPCs (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs): Fireplace — `RPC_AddFuel()` (+1 clamped to m_maxFuel, :125726-125741), `RPC_AddFuelAmount(float)` (signed delta, clamped 0..m_maxFuel — negative = DEBIT, :125754-125764), `RPC_SetFuelAmount(float)` (:125779-125787), `RPC_ToggleOn()` (:125743-125752); all registered in Fireplace.Awake :125395-125398 and all IsOwner-gated. Smelter — `RPC_AddOre(string prefabName, bool cheated)` (:142264-142277, IsItemAllowed against m_conversion then QueueOre writes "item<n>" strings + s_queued, NO m_maxOre cap in the handler), `RPC_AddFuel()` (:142351-142359, no cap in handler), `RPC_EmptyProcessed()` (:142320-142326); registered :142102-142104. CookingStation — `RPC_AddItem(string, bool)` (:123130-123142, slot-limited by GetFreeSlot, NOT owner-gated), `RPC_AddFuel()` (:122919-122928, owner-gated); registered :122479-122482. Fermenter — `RPC_AddItem(int nameHash, bool)` (:124891-124905, owner-gated, only when Empty), `RPC_Tap()` (:124907-124919). Beehive has no add RPC (only `RPC_Extract` :119986-120000); its honey is a plain int `ZDOVars.s_level` (:78497) clamped by IncreseLevel :120021-120027, so credit is a direct ZDO write. Two-path rule: if `zdo.GetOwner() != 0` and that owner is a connected peer (`ZNet.instance.GetPeer(owner) != null`), send the RPC — the client plays m_fuelAddedEffects/m_oreAddedEffects so the player SEES the credit land; if the station is unowned (zone unloaded, nobody near), write the ZDO field directly (`zdo.Set(ZDOVars.s_fuel, v)` :78433, or the item<n>/s_queued pair) — no owner exists to clobber it and the next client to load the zone reads the current value. Never RPC an unowned ZDO: `InvokeRoutedRPC(0, ...)` is a broadcast (:83588-83594) that no client applies. Resolve the player's stations by `s_creator` (:78393) == their `s_playerID` on the target station ZDO, found via ZdoSpatialQuery.FindNear around their portal or a scanned prefab set.


**Player experience:** The player uses a portal whose toll was refunded (or a bounty paid). If they are standing at their base, their kiln/smelter visibly gains fuel or ore with the vanilla add-effect and the hover text count rises. If they are away, the station simply reads the higher value when they next load the zone. Nothing appears on the ground and nothing can be picked up by someone else.


**Failure modes:**
- Station owner is a connected peer that has the object instantiated but the RPC arrives during a frame where the owner changed (ReleaseNearbyZDOS every 2s) — the handler's IsOwner check silently drops it; re-resolve GetOwner() immediately before send and retry once next tick.
- Smelter.RPC_AddOre and RPC_AddFuel have no capacity check in the handler (:142264, :142351) — an over-credit shows a queue larger than m_maxOre in the hover text; cap on the server by reading s_queued/s_fuel first.
- IsItemAllowed matches on prefab NAME from m_conversion (:142160-142170) — the mod must know the station's accepted inputs; read them from ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefab(zdo.GetPrefab()).GetComponent<Smelter>().m_conversion (prefab table presence on a headless server needs the in-game check).
- CookingStation.RPC_AddItem is not owner-gated (:123130) — sending it to a non-owner makes that client write the ZDO and lose a revision race; always target GetOwner().
- Direct s_fuel/s_queued writes on an owned station race the owner's next push (RPC_ZDOData whole-blob apply :77124-77131); only use the direct path when GetOwner()==0.
- The refund is a station-side credit, not inventory — a player with no fireplace/smelter of their own gets nothing; fall back to ItemDrop.DropItem at their portal.

- Does the client render m_fuelAddedEffects for an RPC-driven add when the player is not looking at the station? (EffectList.Create is local; expected yes.)

**Verifier reasoning:**
- [gapfill:confirmed-with-correction] Every cited RPC exists exactly as described and the two-path design (routed RPC to a connected owner vs. direct ZDOMan field write when unowned) is sound precisely because it avoids the one big landmine in this batch: a dedicated server never instantiates a real-world-positioned GameObject at all. Independently re-derived from source: Game.FixedUpdate unconditionally pins ZNet's reference position to (1e6,0,1e6) every tick with no local-player guard (line 100465, inside FixedUpdate at 100458), and ZNetScene.CreateDestroyObjects (82268-82274) anchors object creation to that same GetReferencePosition() (82270) via ZDOMan.FindSectorObjects/IsAreaReady (82062-82080). So no Fireplace/Smelter/CookingStation/Fermenter/Beehive MonoBehaviour ever runs ON the server; this option's design correctly never requires that -- the RPC executes on the receiving OWNER's own client (verified full routing chain: ZNetView.InvokeRPC -> ZRoutedRpc.InvokeRoutedRPC(owner,...) -> RouteRPC relays via peer.m_rpc.Invoke('RoutedRPC',...) to that peer's own machine -> their own RPC_RoutedRPC->HandleRoutedRPC resolves ZNetScene.FindInstance locally, where it legitimately exists), and the unowned-write path touches only ZDOMan's data layer, which needs no GameObject. Verified: Fireplace RPC_AddFuel/RPC_AddFuelAmount/RPC_SetFuelAmount/RPC_ToggleOn all owner-gated at cited lines; Smelter.RPC_AddOre (142264) confirmed to have NO m_maxOre cap in the handler (only OnAddOre's player-facing UI checks it) -- QueueOre (142279) appends unconditionally, exactly as claimed. CookingStation.RPC_AddItem (123130) independently confirmed NOT owner-gated (only IsItemAllowed+GetFreeSlot), exactly as the option itself flags. One gap: Beehive's suggested direct 's_level' write is not clamped the way Beehive.IncreseLevel (120021) clamps to m_maxHoney -- a raw zdo.Set bypasses that cap, risking a display/extraction value above the prefab's designed maximum.
