(6) WearNTear.UpdateWear applies 100 damage per update when !HaveSupport() with m_noSupportWear default true (:149205, :149705-149711): a floating fabricated phantom is demolished by the owning client; place at terrain height. (7) RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() is EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss().m_bossEvent (:106939-106949) — per-client HUD state; only the activeBosses key half of the TeleportWorld boss gate is world-wide. (8) ZNetScene.IsAreaReady ignores ZDOs whose prefab is invalid (IsPrefabZDOValid false for hash 0, :82077), so a Void Anchor does not stall a traveller's arrival, whereas a LocationProxy in async-load state marks the zone loading (client :103137-103141) and correctly delays arrival until the location exists. (9) The server-only invalid-prefab reaper (:82137-82143) only runs for ZDOs in the server's pinned active area, so anchors elsewhere are safe from it. (10) SectorSubscription-style CreateSyncList postfix can be driven by server policy alone (append the destination sector for any peer near a managed portal) — the 'needs a client request' framing was wrong; combined with pre-generation it lets a vanilla client pre-load the destination zone's ZDOs before transit. Still Inspector-bound and needing one in-game pass each: m_locationProxyPrefab ZNetView flags, which location children are ZNetView vs static, whether SpawnSystem lives on m_zoneCtrlPrefab, the tombstone prefab name, and whether LoadFields overrides of Location.m_noBuild take effect on a stock client.

### gapfill:access
Three findings reshape the access domain. (1) Enforcement is not only 'one ZDO, every peer reconverges': the server chooses what each peer is SENT (ZDOMan.CreateSyncList :77212-77241 + AddForceSendZdos :77263-77286 are the only delivery paths, RouteRPC :83597-83629 forwards RPCs only), so per-peer withholding is a genuine server-enforced per-player gate; it must be paired with a revision-aware ownership pin because ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) hands ownership to peers holding no copy and RPC_ZDOData applies foreign owners through SetOwnerInternal (:77114, :77128), bypassing any ZDO.SetOwner prefix. (2) TeleportWorld's own RPC_SetTag/RPC_SetConnected (:143587-143629) are usable in the server→owner direction as cooperative write primitives, which removes the DataRevision race for every revert on a client-owned portal; the returning ZDOData never dirties the portal chunk (AddIfPortal :77738-77742), so SetDirtyPortals (:76702) is mandatory after any tag-only change, client- or server-originated. (3) Vanilla-honoured global-key gating is weaker than the briefs stated: the GetBossEvent() half of gate 3 is a per-client EnemyHud read (:106939-106950), so only activeBosses is world-wide. Shaky-claim verdicts in this domain: PersistentEventSystem's four registrations at :105284-105287 are NOT RandEventSystem's (whose only routed RPC is SetEvent) and RequestStart/StopEvent run on the server unauthenticated with unchecked indices (:105347, :105386); Ship Forward/Backward/Stop/Rudder handlers have no owner or sender gate (:140538-140580); the SectorSubscription CreateSyncList postfix needs no client request and is the mechanism for destination pre-delivery; AddForceSendZdos is gated on peer.ShouldSend (:77273) so 'ForceSendZDO pushes regardless' is false once a peer's cache is current; the admin RPC_RemoteCommand channel is real for names the client already knows (Terminal.TryRunCommand :45737-45746, RPC_RemoteCommand :81879-81889) and dead for new names. Everything per-player that acts on the traveller rather than their property remains reactive (Arrival Bouncer) except withholding, which is preventive because the vanilla client cannot obtain a ZDO from anywhere but the server.

### gapfill:routing
DELIVERY, NOT ROUTING, IS THE BOTTLENECK. Every routing option in the catalog writes a ZDOID into a portal and assumes the traveller can use it. The decompile says otherwise: a peer only ever receives ZDOs inside FindSectorObjects around its own m_refPos (ZDOMan.CreateSyncList :77212-77240), portals are NEVER in the distant ring (FindDistantObjects reads only m_objectsBySector :77384-77404), the server's own portal-pairing writes go to peers only via the one-shot ForceSendZDO in Game.SetConnection, and a vanilla client's only self-help is the RequestZDO fired from TeleportWorld.TargetFound (:143651-143654) — which UpdatePortal polls only while a *teleportable* player is inside m_activationRange (5 m) because of the `flag2 && TargetFound()` short-circuit at :143507. So the 'silent dead first walk-through' is real but NARROWER than the digest says: it bites when a player crosses the trigger within roughly one 0.5 s poll + RTT + one 0.05 s send cycle of (a) entering the 5 m ring or (b) the server re-pointing the portal. A walking player usually wins the race; a sprinting player, a player already standing in the ring when the server re-points, or a player carrying ore (flag2 false, so TargetFound is never polled and the glow stays off) does not. The five gap options below turn that race into a guaranteed-delivered state. Corrections to the digest confirmed this pass: (1) ForceSendZDO is distance-independent but revision-gated — AddForceSendZdos drops any id for which peer.ShouldSend is false (:77273) and ShouldSend is purely a revision compare (:76003-76014); a 'touch to resync' needs a real DataRevision bump. (2) TeleportWorld.Teleport uses the SOURCE portal's compiled m_exitDistance (this.m_exitDistance :143545), not the destination's. (3) RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent is EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss().m_bossEvent (:106939-106949) — per-client HUD state; only the activeBosses global key half of the NoBossPortals gate is world-wide. (4) ZNetView.Awake corrects Type/Distant only when the client owns the ZDO (:82583-82590) and never touches Persistent on the existing-ZDO path; a server-set Type on a real portal is reverted the moment ReleaseNearbyZDOS hands it to a nearby player, but sticks on a prefab-less anchor no ZNetView ever adopts. (5) ZDO.m_prefab defaults to -1 (:73317) but ZDO.Initialize sets Valid=true which writes 0 (:73468-73478, :73503), so a CreateNewZDO'd anchor with no SetPrefab serializes prefab 0; the client's CreateObject returns null silently for 0 (:81999-82002) and IsPrefabZDOValid excludes it from the IsAreaReady wait (:81986-81994, :82076) — the Void Anchor claim holds. (6) The CLIENT never evicts a received ZDO: the only removal path is HandleDestroyedZDO; ZNetScene.RemoveObjects destroys instances, and DestroyZDO only for non-persistent owned ZDOs (:82196-82227). A destination pushed once is held for the whole session, so a join-time push permanently satisfies TargetFound for static portals. (7) A vanilla client generates zones at its destination one per 0.1 s tick (CreateLocalZones returns after the first PokeLocalZone that spawns :113993-114012; ZoneSystem.Update 0.1 s :113925) in SpawnMode.Client (:114028, never generates vegetation/location ZDOs — it depends on the server having ghost-generated the zone), and CreateObjectsSorted refuses to instantiate anything until IsActiveAreaLoaded() (:82107) — so even a perfectly pre-streamed distant:false teleport has a client-local floor of ~2 s timer + ~1.5-3 s zone spawning; still well under vanilla's 8 s. (8) The server has a per-peer ledger of exactly which ZDOs each peer holds and at which revision: ZDOPeer.m_zdos (:75981), readable through the private ZDOMan.m_peers list (:76041) with the publicizer — the missing 'readiness' primitive for every JIT option. (9) The server's own send loop services ONE peer per Update frame and then waits 0.05 s (:76843-76861); with N peers a full cycle is 0.05 s + N frames, and each SendZDOs call is capped at 10240 bytes minus the socket's pending queue and abandons the cycle if fewer than 2048 bytes are free (:77010-77019). (10) Chat-free RTT is available: Game registers RPC_Ping/RPC_Pong on EVERY peer (:100065-100066), the client's RPC_Ping echoes the float back to the sender (:100877-100880), and a Harmony prefix on the private Game.RPC_Pong(long sender, float time) (:100882) yields per-peer RTT = Time.time - time; ZRpc's own 1 s ping (:83862-83879) is liveness-only. ZSteamSocket.GetConnectionQuality (:86627-86648) exposes Steam's m_nPing but calls the CLIENT-side SteamNetworkingSockets API (:86641) while every other server-build call uses SteamGameServerNetworkingSockets (:86595) — expect 0 on a dedicated server; needs an in-game check. Flagged-claim positions: EnvMan/GetDayFraction headless, ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync, PrivateArea.m_radius and portal-prefab WearNTear support settings remain Inspector/in-game unknowns and are out of scope for these five gaps; the WearNTear caveat (unsupported phantom portals demolished by m_noSupportWear on the owning client :149662-149711) is real for Phantom Anchor Fabrication and is why every option below prefers prefab-0 'void anchors' or existing portals as pushed destinations.

## Completeness critics (ran after first-round verification; their gaps produced the gap-fill round)


### Critic: mechanism-coverage


The twelve briefs were organised around the portal component, the ZDO connection slot, global keys and the RPC relay — i.e. around the OBJECT a player walks into — and treated the world around it as static, read-only data (WorldGenerator math, m_locationInstances, biome grids). That framing systematically missed the server-authoritative subsystems that CONSTRUCT places: ZoneSystem's ghost generation and `m_generatedZones` (clients never generate anything; the server decides what exists in every zone), the location pipeline (`RegisterLocation`/`SpawnLocationMidGame`/`SpawnLocation(Full)`/`LocationProxy` — one ZDO conjures an entire vanilla structure plus a client-honoured no-build ring), `TerrainComp` (`s_TCData`, the only server-writable geometry in the game), and `PersistentEventSystem` (a persisted, radius-bearing, JSON-broadcast world-state channel with removable labelled map pins, localized weather and event-gated spawns/wear). Because of that blind spot the catalog repeatedly 'rules out' or caveats things vanilla already provides: removable map markers, server-controlled weather, arrival-site preparation, and the admin text channel (the piggyback on remote-flagged console commands). A second systematic error: RPC analysis was done in one direction only. The briefs correctly proved that client→server ZDO-targeted RPCs never dispatch on a dedicated server, then never asked what the SERVER can send to a client that DOES hold the instance — so TeleportWorld's own `RPC_SetTag`/`RPC_SetConnected`, ship steering, `FlashShield`, `SetTrigger`, `SleepStart`, station `AddFuel`-style RPCs and the whole 'owner-executed delegation' pattern that `Game.RPC_SetConnection` already models were left out, and the access domain was built on 'overwrite and fight' instead of 'instruct the owner'. Third, the routed-RPC census was copied between briefs without being opened: four PersistentEventSystem handlers are mislabelled and never read, two of them sender-ungated server-executing spawners. Fourth, persistence was examined only for MOD writes; the interaction of vanilla client edits with `DirtyPortalObjects`, and of phantom objects with WearNTear support and vegetation generation, was never traced, so several 'feasible' options have silent world-state failure modes. Finally, several catalog entries contradict the domain notes written for them (the ops admin-channel entry is ruled-out while its own notes say the RPC works; the boss-gate blackout radius is described as world-wide while the code is per-client HUD), which suggests options were finalised before the notes were reconciled against the decompile.


**Gaps identified:**
- **[wildcard]** PersistentEventSystem (Bog Witch / 1.0) was never opened. It is a server-authoritative, world-persisted (.db, JSON+Brotli — PersistentEventSystem.PrepareSave/Save/Load :105237-105250), radius-bearing world-state channel: `m_activePersistentEvents.list` holds {sourceEventId, eventId, position, radius, startTime, duration} (ActivePersistentEvent :104922-104939); the server broadcasts it as JSON via `UpdateClientEventsList(0L)` (:105407-105410) and re-sends it to every joining peer (m_onNewPeer hook :105288-105289). A vanilla client reacts in four ways: (1) Minimap draws an EventArea circle of `radius*2` PLUS an animated, double-size RandomEvent pin labelled with the localized `Source.mapTokenString`, and REMOVES both when the entry disappears (client Minimap.UpdatePersistentEventPins assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57505-57545); (2) EnvMan applies `Source.GetEnvironmentOverride(pos)` — localized WEATHER — to any player inside the radius (client EnvMan :96299-96303); (3) SpawnSystem gates spawners on `m_requiredPersistentEvent` (client :111346-111352); (4) WearNTear damages pieces inside/outside the event (`m_requiredPersistentEvent`/`m_takeDamageIfInsideEvent`, WearNTear.UpdateWear :149710-149718). `TriggerEvent(name)` (:105292-105303) → `RPC_RequestStartEvent` on the server spawns `locationToSpawn` via ZoneSystem.SpawnLocationMidGame and `objectsToSpawn` via server-side Object.Instantiate using WorldGenerator math (:105341-105379, ObjectSpawnSettings.Create :104990+). Option spec: inject an ActivePersistentEvent at every managed portal/hub (or at a lockdown/raid site) to get a REMOVABLE labelled map marker with a radius ring, a localized weather signature, and event-gated spawns/piece wear — none of which any brief lists. Constraints: `sourceEventId` must index the Inspector list `m_possibleEvents` (label text and env override are per-event-type asset data — dump names at boot), `Source` property throws on a bad index, `Update` (:105213-105235) auto-expires entries by `ZNet.GetTimeSeconds()`, and `UpdateClientEventsList` is private (publicizer). — This is the only server-controlled map marker that can be REMOVED, the only server-controlled localized weather lever, and a server-side location/object spawner — the routing brief called weather 'heavy caveats', the UX brief says pushed pins can never be removed, and the privatearea brief's routed-RPC census mislabels the four PersistentEventSystem registrations at :105284-105287 as 'the RandEventSystem event RPCs' and never analyses them.
- **[targeted]** Server-authored vanilla STRUCTURES via the location pipeline — three distinct primitives, none examined. (a) Fabricate a `LocationProxy` ZDO (prefab `ZoneSystem.m_locationProxyPrefab` :113216; ZDO ints `ZDOVars.s_location` = location name stable hash :78501 and `s_seed` :78587): every vanilla client's LocationProxy.Awake → ZoneSystem.SpawnProxyLocation → SpawnLocation(SpawnMode.Client) instantiates the ENTIRE location prefab with its ZNetView children disabled — visual geometry, colliders, EnvZone/EffectArea volumes, Location component — at that position (client assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:103082-103153, :115790-115800, Client branch :115934-115985), then calls `m_nview.LoadFields()` on the proxy (:103148), so ZDO keys like `Location.m_noBuild` / `Location.m_noBuildRadiusOverride` override the spawned instance. `Location.m_noBuild` (default true, :133462) makes `Location.IsInsideNoBuildLocation` (:133619-133628) refuse piece placement (Player :12379, :13484) AND hoe/cultivator/pickaxe TerrainOps (Attack :24126-24138) — a client-honoured no-build/no-terraform ring around a managed portal with one ZDO and zero pieces. (b) `ZoneSystem.SpawnLocationMidGame(name, pos, out spawnedPos)` (public, server-only, :115079-115102) registers a LocationInstance so the location is placed with full ZDOs, terrain clearing (`m_clearArea`) and vegetation exclusion when the zone is ghost-generated — but it calls `GetGroundHeight` (a dead raycast on the server) so `pos.y` is unchanged, and for an already-generated zone it registers something that is NEVER placed (SpawnZone only runs PlaceLocations when `!IsZoneGenerated`, :114084-114091; CanSpawnLocationMidGame :114936-114944). (c) `ZoneSystem.SpawnLocation(location, seed, pos, rot, SpawnMode.Full, list)` (private, :115802) — what `TestSpawnLocation` (public, :115034-115076) wraps — instantiates the location on the server with all ZNetView children as real persistent ZDOs, runs DungeonGenerator.Generate (rooms included), and creates the proxy with spawnNow=true; the wrapper is booby-trapped (unguarded `MessageHud.instance.ShowMessage` :115066, `m_didZoneTest = disableSave` :115067 which disables world saving, and `s_cheated` stamping :115075) so call the private method directly. Option spec: 'terminal architecture' — drop a stone circle/ruin/altar shell at every managed hub, a crypt entrance shell at a dungeon gate, a no-build ring around a public portal, an entire vanilla fort as an event hub. — Every 'phantom portal' and 'Customs House' option leaves the player standing on bare terrain with a lone portal frame; the world-gen subsystem the server already drives for every peer can build the place around it, and nobody looked at LocationProxy, SpawnProxyLocation, SpawnLocationMidGame or the Full-mode SpawnLocation path.
- **[wildcard]** Server-authored terraforming via `TerrainComp` was never examined. Each zone's terrain modifications live in one `_TerrainCompiler`-family ZDO (`Heightmap.m_terrainCompilerPrefab` :128241, created at the heightmap/zone centre by Heightmap.GetAndCreateTerrainCompiler :129532-129537) under the byte[] key `ZDOVars.s_TCData` :78353. The format is a Utils.Compress'd ZPackage — version, m_operations, m_lastOpPoint, m_lastOpRadius, then (width+1)^2 entries of {modified:bool, levelDelta:float, smoothDelta:float} and the same count of {modifiedPaint:bool, r,g,b,a} (TerrainComp.Save :143793-143835, Load :143863-143934) — fully writable server-side with no colliders. Clients re-apply whenever the ZDO's DataRevision changes (CheckLoad :143837-143861 → m_hmap.Poke) and `TerrainComp.FindTerrainCompiler(pos)` locates the compiler by an XZ bounds test (:143936-143948), so a server-written or server-fabricated compiler ZDO (CreateNewZDO at the zone centre + SetPrefab + Persistent) flattens a landing pad, raises a platform out of water, digs a moat, or paints a paved circle marking a managed portal. Constraints: exactly one compiler per zone or FindTerrainCompiler returns the first match; array length must equal the heightmap's (m_width+1)^2 or Load logs 'height array missmatch' and aborts; ownership must be claimed before writing (owner clobber); no `SetDirtyPortals` needed (normal chunk save). Option spec: 'Landing Pad Engine' — auto-flatten a 6 m disc under every server-placed phantom and under every player-built managed hub; combine with the Destination Safety Validator so Skyfall/Seabed exits become real ground. — Arrival safety is currently handled by rejecting coordinates; the server can instead MAKE the coordinate safe. TerrainComp is the only server-writable geometry in the game and appears in no brief.
- **[targeted]** Zone-generation control is entirely unexamined and directly determines what a traveller finds at a phantom destination. Facts: clients NEVER generate zones — `PokeLocalZone` picks `SpawnMode.Client` for any non-server (:114021-114036), so every zone's vegetation, locations and `_ZoneCtrl` are created ONLY by the server's `CreateGhostZones(peer.GetRefPos())` (:113930-113938, :113971) when a peer's reference position approaches; `m_generatedZones` (private HashSet<Vector2s>, :113276, persisted by ZoneSystem.Save) is the sole record; `SpawnZone` skips PlaceLocations/PlaceVegetation/PlaceZoneCtrl for a generated zone (:114084-114091). Consequences no option handles: (1) a phantom portal placed in an ungenerated zone will later have trees/rocks/boulders generated THROUGH it, because PlaceVegetation only honours location clear-areas, not existing ZDOs; (2) the mod can pre-generate the destination ring itself (`SpawnZone(zone, SpawnMode.Ghost, out _)` per zone, publicized) at route-write time instead of at arrival, so the traveller's 8-15 s `IsAreaReady` wait is not also paying for generation; (3) 'barren pad' trick — adding a zone to `m_generatedZones` WITHOUT generating it yields terrain with no vegetation, no location and no `_ZoneCtrl` (`PlaceZoneCtrl` :114109-114126; `m_zoneCtrlPrefab` :113214 is where the per-zone SpawnSystem lives — verify in-game), i.e. a creature-spawn-free clearing for a hub; the inverse (removing a zone) re-runs generation on top of whatever exists. Option spec: 'Destination Zone Governor' — pre-ghost-generate, optionally mark-barren, and record generation state per managed destination. — The targeted brief notes 'objects materialise per zone the first time a peer's reference position brings that zone within range' but no option acts on it; vegetation-through-portal and un-generated arrival zones are guaranteed failure modes for every phantom-destination option.
- **[routing]** Server-initiated destination pre-streaming. The codebase brief dismisses TortalPortal's `ZDOMan.CreateSyncList` postfix (SectorSubscription.cs:106) as 'useless to a zero-client Lite because vanilla clients never send the request RPC' — but the server needs no request: a postfix on the private `ZDOMan.CreateSyncList(ZDOPeer, List<ZDO>)` (:77212-77246) can append `FindSectorObjects(destinationZone, …)` results for any peer the mod chooses (e.g. one standing within 15 m of a managed portal whose destination the mod just wrote), so the traveller already HOLDS the destination portal and its surroundings before stepping in — eliminating the silent first-transit failure (`TargetFound` → `RequestZDO` :143646-143654) and shortening `IsAreaReady`. Two related unexamined knobs: `ZDO.Type = ObjectType.Prioritized` sorts a ZDO ahead of everything else in `ServerSendCompare` (:77288-77309) — set it on phantom portals/anchors; and `ZDO.Distant` does NOTHING for portals because `FindDistantObjects` reads only `m_objectsBySector` (:77383-77401) while portals live in `m_portalObjects` — but a non-portal anchor with Distant=true is delivered from the far ring (only when the near list is <10 items, :77229-77237). Note ZNetView.Awake overwrites Type/Distant only when the client owns the ZDO (:82580-82587) and never touches Persistent. Option spec: 'Pre-Stream Engine' with a per-peer byte budget (the 10240-byte queue cap :77010-77016) and `RPC_Ping`/`RPC_Pong` (:100065-100066, :100869-100876) to measure each peer's RTT for the JIT-routing lead-time budget. — Every routing option's worst UX defect (dead first walk-through) has a server-only fix that was explicitly, wrongly written off; and the sync-ordering knobs (Type/Distant) that decide how fast a fabricated destination reaches a client were never read.
- **[access]** The server→owning-client direction of TeleportWorld's OWN RPCs was never considered. `TeleportWorld.RPC_SetTag(long sender, string tag, string authorId)` (:143587-143602) and `RPC_SetConnected(long sender, ZDOID portalID)` (:143622-143629) are registered on every client-side portal instance (:143448-143449) and gate only on `m_nview.IsOwner()`. The server can therefore send `ZRoutedRpc.instance.InvokeRoutedRPC(ownerPeer, portalZdoId, "RPC_SetTag", newTag, "")` to make the OWNING CLIENT execute vanilla's own rename path (clear own connection, notify the partner via SetConnectedPortal :143604-143620, write s_tag/s_tagauthor) and push the result back as ZDOData — exactly the race-free delegation `Game.SetConnection` already uses for connections via `RPC_SetConnection` (:100646-100649). This is the correct write primitive for Tag Watchdog / Reserved Namespace / Anti-Grief reverts on a portal a player currently owns (every portal a player is standing next to, per ReleaseNearbyZDOS :76901), instead of blind ZDO writes that lose the DataRevision race (RPC_ZDOData :77107-77132). Caveats: authorId is written verbatim (send the verified PlatformUserID or empty); the client's RPC_SetTag uses `UpdateConnection` so an unconnected portal's connection is untouched; and the server-side copy is not dirtied by the returning ZDOData (see the DirtyPortalObjects gap). — Every access-control option treats client-owned portals as adversarial state to be overwritten and re-fought every tick; vanilla already provides a cooperative, owner-executed rename instruction that the briefs only ever analysed as a client→server packet that never arrives.
- **[ops]** A working admin text-command channel from a 100%-vanilla client exists and the catalog rules it out. `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (:45734-45758) forwards ANY command whose `RemoteCommand` flag is set to the server via `ZNet.RemoteCommand` whenever `IsValid` fails on the client (:45741-45744) — and `IsValid` fails for every `onlyServer:true` command on a client (:43203-43217), cheat-flagged or not. The server's `RPC_RemoteCommand` (:81879-81889) checks `m_adminList` against the socket host name and runs `Console.instance.TryRunCommand(command)` (:81891-81895); `Console.instance` exists headless because Game.Awake instantiates it (:100038-100041). Thirteen vanilla commands carry `remoteCommand:true` (:43359-44599); the non-cheat ones an admin can type are `removekey`, `resetworldkeys`, `setworldpreset`, `setworldmodifier`, `genloc`, `restartparty`. A server-side Harmony prefix on `Terminal.TryRunCommand` (or on the `removekey` handler :43535-43546, whose only side effect for an unknown key is a no-op RemoveGlobalKey) can intercept `removekey tpl <verb> <args…>` from an admin's F5 console, execute mod logic, and answer with `ZNet.RemotePrint(rpc, text)` (:81635-81648) into that admin's console. Constraints: `ZNet.RemoteCommand` called ON the server passes a null rpc into InternalCommand which dereferences `rpc.GetSocket()` (:81893) — never call it server-side; `Terminal.commands` is registered by indexer so name collisions clobber silently (:43096/:43114); replies land in the F5 console only. — The ops catalog entry 'Admin command channel: server-registered ConsoleCommand + RPC_RemoteCommand' is marked ruled-out while the ops domain notes say the channel works — the missing piece was that the client must already know the command, which piggybacking a remote-flagged vanilla command solves outright.
- **[ops]** Client-originated portal edits never set `DirtyPortalObjects`. `ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData` (:77076-77139) applies an incoming portal ZDO via `Deserialize` (raw `ZDOExtraData.SetConnection`, raw string add — no dirty flag) and then `AddIfPortal` (:77732-77752), which early-returns at :77739-77742 for a portal already in its bucket WITHOUT reaching `DirtyPortalObjects = true` (:77751). The only things that dirty the portal chunk are ZDO.SetConnection/UpdateConnection of type Portal (:73661-73675), AddIfPortal for a NEW portal, HandleDestroyedZDO (:76986), world load (:76539) and the public SetDirtyPortals (:76702). So a vanilla client's rename reaches the server's RAM but is persisted only because Game.ConnectPortals' own SetConnection writes happen to dirty the chunk within 5 s — a rename of an UNCONNECTED portal (no reconciler write follows) is silently lost at the next save unless some other portal event dirties the world-wide chunk first. Option spec: the Tag Watchdog / AuditEngine must call `ZDOMan.instance.SetDirtyPortals()` on every OBSERVED client change (not just mod writes), and the HealthScan should report 'renamed-but-not-dirty' portals; also note that `ZDO.Deserialize` (:74205-74240) never clears keys, so a key can never be removed from a peer once delivered — reverts must overwrite with a sentinel, not delete. — Three briefs warn that MOD tag writes need SetDirtyPortals; none noticed that VANILLA client writes have the same hole, which will surface as 'my portal rename vanished after restart' bug reports blamed on the mod.
- **[wildcard]** Structural integrity will demolish floating phantom portals. `WearNTear.UpdateWear` (:149662-149707) runs on the OWNING CLIENT and, with `m_noSupportWear` (default true, :149205), calls `UpdateSupport()` and applies 100 damage per update when `!HaveSupport()` (:149700-149707; HaveSupport = m_support >= GetMinSupport :150148-150151); support comes from collider contacts with terrain or other supporting pieces (UpdateSupport :149959-150130). A phantom portal fabricated in mid-air, on a slope above the terrain mesh, or over water is therefore destroyed by the first client to own it — within seconds — and the ZDO is gone from `m_portalObjects`. Every 'Skyfall', 'Seabed', 'Void Anchor next to a phantom', and 'Ephemeral Event Gate' option is affected. Server-side mitigations, none listed: place phantoms at `WorldGenerator.GetHeight(x,z)` exactly (client terrain collider then supports them); or override via LoadFields (`WearNTear.m_noSupportWear=false`, `m_noRoofWear=false`, and `m_health` so rain/support wear cannot kill it); also `WearNTear.m_requiredPersistentEvent`/`m_takeDamageIfInsideEvent` (:149710-149718) means a phantom inside an active persistent event of the wrong type takes event damage. OutsideActiveArea pieces are exempt (:149671-149679) so the failure only appears when a player is near — i.e. exactly when it matters. — The zdo brief states a fabricated portal 'needs no health/creator/support fields to instantiate correctly' — true for instantiation, wrong for survival; no option models the support pass at all.
- **[ux]** Unlisted server→client output RPCs and their UX value. (1) `SleepStart`/`SleepStop` (Game.Start :100063-100064; handlers :100752-100769) → `Player.SetSleeping(true/false)` (:15992-16005): a server-forced full-screen sleep fade on ALL clients, with a '$msg_goodmorning' message and a Rested buff on wake — a global blackout primitive for the Blackout Swap Protocol (caveat: SetSleeping(true) also blocks AttachStop). (2) `RPC_SetDreamCinematic(string)` (CinematicsManager :42373, :42616-42623) queues a video cinematic to play on every client's next sleep. (3) `ZSyncAnimation` `SetTrigger` invoked BY the server at the character owner plays any animator trigger on that player's body for everyone (the UX brief covers only the client→server direction, :87260). (4) `PrivateArea` `FlashShield` (:137202) is a no-arg ZDO RPC the server can fire at any ward's owner to pulse its dome. (5) `TeleportWorld.UpdatePortal` fires the `m_connected` EffectList on the rising edge of `HaveTarget()` (:143495-143503) — flipping a connection None→X on the server plays vanilla's own 'portal connected' burst on every nearby client for free. (6) `RPC_RegisterKill` (:100069, :100837-100862) writes kill/boss stats and platform achievements into the target player's local profile — an accidental achievement-injection primitive that must be listed as 'never use'. Option spec: fold into the feedback stack with the honest tier (all client-honoured). — The UX brief enumerated eight output channels and missed six vanilla RPCs, two of which (SleepStart, the m_connected effect) are the only global-blackout and portal-local VFX signals that need no prefab-hash guessing.
- **[lockdown]** `RandEventSystem` writes were never examined — only reads. `RandEventSystem.instance.SetRandomEventByName(name, pos)` (public, :107067-107071) is server-authoritative and broadcast by `SendCurrentRandomEvent` via the `SetEvent` routed RPC (:106952-106978); clients then show `m_startMessage`, force `m_forceMusic`/`m_forceEnvironment` inside `m_eventRange` (RandomEvent fields :107435-107494), draw an EventArea pin of `m_eventRange*2` (client Minimap :57474-57500) and run the event's spawners. The server can therefore START a raid at a portal (a hazard/announcement at a locked gate), and, combined with `NoBossPortals`, MUST correct the catalog's boss-gate model: `TeleportWorld.Teleport`'s check at :143528 calls `RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent()`, which is `EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss().m_bossEvent` (:106939-106949) — a per-CLIENT HUD lookup (boss within EnemyHud range and shown), NOT the world random event; only the `activeBosses` float key is world-wide. Option spec: 'Raid Beacon' (server-started event at a managed gate during lockdown, with the event's own pin/music/message as the announcement) and a corrected Boss Auto-Lockdown that stops describing GetBossEvent as global. — The lockdown and routing options treat raids purely as inputs and the globalkeys brief mis-describes the NoBossPortals gate as 'RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() != null OR activeBosses>0 → world-wide', which will produce a wrong blackout-radius model.
- **[access]** Three unauthenticated non-portal RPCs a client can use to attack any portal policy, absent from Ungated RPC Hardening: (1) `PersistentEventSystem.RPC_RequestStartEvent(sender, int)` and `RPC_RequestStopEvent` (:105341-105389) execute on the server with no sender check — any client can make the server spawn event locations (`SpawnLocationMidGame`) and objects (`Object.Instantiate` server-side) anywhere within the event's placement rules, or kill live events; (2) `RPC_UpdateClientEventsList(sender, json)` (:105412-105418) is applied by any NON-server recipient, so a client can broadcast a forged event list to every other client (fake map pins, fake weather) via the server relay; (3) `Ship.RPC_Forward/Backward/Stop/Rudder` (:140482-140485, bodies :140538-140575) set state on whatever machine receives them with no owner or sender check, so any client can steer any ship whose owner is another player. Add all three to the `ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC` prefix's veto table alongside SetGlobalKey/RPC_SetConnection/DestroyZDO/RequestZDO. — The access domain's hardening list was built from the privatearea brief's routed-RPC census, which never opened the PersistentEventSystem handlers and did not consider ZDO RPCs that lack an IsOwner gate on the receiving side.
- **[lockdown]** `EffectArea.Type.Teleport` and `Piece.m_onlyInTeleportArea` — a vanilla portal-placement gate nobody identified. `EffectArea.Type` is a byte flags enum {Heat, Fire, PlayerBase, Burning, Teleport=0x10, NoMonsters, WarmCozyArea, PrivateProperty} (:124062-124073); `Player.UpdatePlacementGhost` refuses any piece with `m_onlyInTeleportArea` (:136153) unless `EffectArea.IsPointInsideArea(point, Type.Teleport)` (:13349-13352, status NoTeleportArea → '$msg_noteleportarea' :12461-12462). Which piece(s) set `m_onlyInTeleportArea` and which prefab carries an `EffectArea` of type Teleport are Inspector data (candidates: the Ashlands/Deep North portal variants, or a location-only 'portal pad'); if a portal variant is gated this way, then (a) the per-player cap / placement options must account for a vanilla placement restriction they do not know about, and (b) a server-fabricated LocationProxy for the location that carries the Teleport EffectArea (see the structures gap) would let vanilla clients build that portal variant anywhere — a client-honoured 'unlock placement here' lever. Also relevant: fabricated locations carrying `NoMonsters`/`PlayerBase`/`WarmCozyArea` EffectAreas give spawn-free, base-flagged, comfort-bearing pads around a hub. In-game check: dump every prefab in `ZNetScene.m_prefabs` with a Piece whose `m_onlyInTeleportArea` is true and every EffectArea whose `m_type` has the Teleport bit. — The wildcard 'Ashlands Stone Portal' option asserts 'no code difference between portal variants … none of it network-reachable' without having found the one placement-gating mechanism in the assembly that mentions teleporting by name.
- **[wildcard]** Server-driven vehicles as a transport primitive, and the real limits of moving a ship with riders. `ShipControlls`/`Ship` are steered by ZDO-targeted RPCs the server can send to the ship's OWNER: `Forward`/`Backward`/`Stop`/`Rudder(float)` (:140482-140485) — an autopilot ferry that moves a whole crew without any teleport, cooldown or black screen, and is a genuine 'portal alternative' for the ship-as-destination case every brief declared physically impossible. Separately, a server that pins ownership of a ship (WaterBuoyancyEngine SetOwner-block pattern) and writes its ZDO position makes non-owning clients lerp 20 %/tick or hard-snap when >5 m (ZSyncTransform.SyncPosition :87700-87724), and a rider standing on a ship their client does not own is re-glued to `m_lastAttachBody.TransformPoint(m_lastAttachPos)` ONLY while the correction is <4 m (Character.UpdateMotion :2118-2135; >4 m clears the attach and drops them in the water). So incremental server-driven ship motion (<4 m per physics tick) carries passengers; a long jump does not. Option spec: 'Ferry Route' (server steers an unattended vanilla ship between docks by RPC; timetable + `s_user` helmsman check) and a corrected 'Player's Ship' option that names the 4 m attach limit. — Both ship-related options stop at 'you land in the water behind the boat'; the steering RPC surface and the attach-correction limit that decide whether a server can MOVE a boat with people on it were never read.
- **[ux]** Removable server-controlled map surfaces exist and the catalog says they do not. Beyond `RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse` (permanent) and `LocationIcons` (unlabelled), a vanilla client renders and later REMOVES: (1) per-persistent-event pins — an EventArea circle sized `radius*2` plus an animated double-size RandomEvent pin labelled with the localized `mapTokenString` (client Minimap.UpdatePersistentEventPins assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:57505-57545, removal :57530-57544); (2) the random-event area pin `m_randEventAreaPin` sized `m_eventRange*2*0.9` (:57474-57500), removed when the event ends. Both are driven by server-authoritative state (PersistentEventSystem JSON broadcast :105407; RandEventSystem `SetEvent` :106952). Labels are per-event-type Inspector tokens, not free text; position and radius are free. Option spec: 'Live Portal Markers' — one persistent-event entry per managed hub (label = the event type's token), removed when the hub is retired; document the fixed-label limitation and the weather side effect. — The UX brief's map-pin option and the wildcard 'Portal-Driven Map Surfaces' option both state there is no way to remove a server-pushed marker, which is false and shapes the whole 'pins are one-shot' design stance.
- **[economy]** Economy-side vanilla RPCs the server can send to a station's OWNER to credit or debit world objects were not enumerated: `Fireplace` `AddFuel` (used by the Charge Cells option only as a read), `Smelter` `AddOre`, `CookingStation`/`Fermenter`/`Beehive` add-item RPCs, and `Door` state (`ZDOVars.s_state` 0/1/-1, Door :123781-123949) as a three-state physical switch. Each is a ZNetView RPC with an `IsOwner` gate on the receiving client, so the server can drive it exactly the way it drives `RPC_SetConnection`. Option spec: 'Refund and Credit Primitives' — pay a toll refund by `AddFuel`/`AddOre` at the player's own station rather than by dropping items on the ground (ItemDrop.DropItem is the only credit path the economy brief names), and 'Door Lever' as a fourth cheap input channel next to item stands and signs. — The economy domain's credit path is limited to ground drops and chest blobs; the owner-executed station RPCs are cheaper, tamper-safe (owner gate) and were never listed.

**Unverified/shaky claims flagged:**
- globalkeys brief / Boss Auto-Lockdown option: 'NoBossPortals is a WORLD-WIDE blackout … RandEventSystem.GetBossEvent() != null OR activeBosses > 0'. Verified against assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:106939-106949: GetBossEvent() returns EnemyHud.instance.GetActiveBoss().m_bossEvent — a per-client HUD lookup — so only the activeBosses key is world-wide; the GetBossEvent half is local to each traveller's screen.
- privatearea brief routed-RPC census: the four registrations at :105284-105287 are described as 'the RandEventSystem event RPCs'. They are PersistentEventSystem's s_updateClientEventsList / s_requestActiveEventsList / s_requestStartEvent / s_requestStopEvent; RandEventSystem's only routed RPC is 'SetEvent' at :106781. The census also omits that RPC_RequestStartEvent/StopEvent run on the server with no sender check.
- ops catalog option 'Admin command channel: server-registered ConsoleCommand + RPC_RemoteCommand' is marked ruled-out, but Terminal.TryRunCommand (:45741-45744) forwards any RemoteCommand-flagged command from a vanilla client when IsValid fails, RPC_RemoteCommand (:81879-81889) is admin-gated and runs Console.instance.TryRunCommand, and Console is instantiated headless (Game.Awake :100038-100041). A server-side prefix on TryRunCommand keyed on 'removekey tpl …' makes it a working channel.
- zdo-connection brief: 'A server-fabricated portal ZDO needs no health/creator/support fields to instantiate correctly'. Instantiation yes; survival no — WearNTear.UpdateWear (:149662-149707) with m_noSupportWear (default true :149205) applies 100 damage per update when !HaveSupport() on the owning client, so unsupported phantoms are demolished. Needs an in-game check of the portal prefab's WearNTear settings.
- codebase brief: 'SectorSubscription's CreateSyncList postfix is useless to a ZERO-CLIENT Lite (vanilla clients never send the request RPC)'. The postfix can be driven purely by server-side policy (append the destination sector for any peer near a managed portal); no client request is required.
- zdo-connection / ops briefs: 'a tag-only write is silently lost unless the mod calls SetDirtyPortals' — correct, but the same is true of CLIENT-originated tag edits: RPC_ZDOData (:77076-77139) → AddIfPortal early-returns for an existing portal (:77739-77742) without dirtying; vanilla is rescued only when Game.ConnectPortals happens to write a connection afterwards.
- targeted brief: LocationInstance.m_position.y 'already carries a procedurally-valid ground height'. True for world-gen-placed instances; ZoneSystem.SpawnLocationMidGame (:115079-115102) sets pos.y = GetGroundHeight(pos), a raycast that is dead on the server, so mid-game-registered instances keep the caller's y until placement re-resolves it in the ghost zone (and in an already-generated zone they are never placed at all: SpawnZone :114084-114091).
- routing brief 'World-State Conditional Routing (… Weather)' and the wildcard notes treat weather as a read-only, heavily caveated input. PersistentEventSystem.PersistentEvent.environmentOverride + GetEnvironmentOverride (client EnvMan :96299-96303) gives the server a localized weather override inside any radius it chooses, subject to the event type's Inspector data.
- ux brief and wildcard 'Portal-Driven Map Surfaces': 'no way ever to remove a pushed map pin'. Persistent-event pins (client Minimap :57505-57545) and the random-event area pin (:57474-57500) are server-driven and removed when the server drops the event.
- wildcard 'The Ashlands Stone Portal': 'every behavioural difference is Inspector data … none of it is network-reachable'. Unverified against Piece.m_onlyInTeleportArea (:136153) / EffectArea.Type.Teleport (:124068) placement gating at :13349-13352; which prefabs use it is unknown and may be a portal variant.
- access brief claim (c) 'ZDO.Deserialize does not wipe fields absent from an incoming packet' — CONFIRMED this pass (ZDO.Deserialize :74205-74240 calls only ZDOExtraData.Add via ZDODataHelper.ReadData :74718-74730; no Release/Reset); corollary that mod keys can never be deleted from a peer stands.
- prior-review item 'ZNetView.Awake corrects Type/Distant when owner' — confirmed (:82580-82587); Persistent is never corrected from an existing ZDO (only set on the create path :82615), so a server-set Persistent=true on a fabricated ZDO survives client ownership.
- zdo-connection brief: 'Portals sync to nearby clients normally … subject to ReleaseNearbyZDOS' — correct, but the digest's implicit assumption that ZDO.Distant could widen delivery is wrong for portals: FindDistantObjects (:77383-77401) reads only m_objectsBySector, never m_portalObjects.

### Critic: option-space


The catalog is wide but built on one unexamined axiom: 'a ZDO is one object and every peer reconverges on it, therefore nothing is per-player'. That axiom is true of DATA and false of DELIVERY. ZDOMan.CreateSyncList, AddForceSendZdos and RPC_RequestZDO are the only three routes a ZDO takes to a client, all three are server-side and patchable, and a client cannot obtain a ZDO any other way. Per-peer withholding turns the 'Per-Player Transit Gate — RULED OUT', 'Per-Peer Divergent ZDO Routing — RULED OUT' and the economy domain's 'four independent reasons' into a fourth enforcement tier that the taxonomy does not have: server-enforced-by-omission. Every access, economy and lockdown option should be re-scored against it.

Second, the catalog is far more redundant than 197 suggests. Rotating hub appears as Carousel, Rotating Hub, Event Topologies and One-Way Ring Rotation; pairing takeover appears as Displaced Routing, Pairing Authority Takeover, Managed Network Governor and The Routing Kernel; the portal cap appears in wildcard, economy and access; map pins appear in at least four places. A designer choosing between them has no dependency graph and no de-duplicated list of primitives. Collapse to ~25 primitives (connection write, tag write, anchor fabrication, arrival hook, sync-list filter, force-send, global key, routed RPCs to client, ZDO polling of character/stand/sign/chest, ghost-zone spawn, LocationIcons) and express every option as a composition.

Third, the option space is player-centric to the exclusion of everything else that moves through a portal: not one option concerns tames, carts, or creatures at the destination, which is the largest single user-visible hole relative to the mods people actually install.

Fourth, the silent-first-transit failure is named as a gotcha in ten places and solved as a feature in none; the join event is never used as a lifecycle hook; and 'destination exists' is treated as luck (has a player been there) rather than something the server can manufacture with a ghost SpawnZone. These three are the same structural blind spot: the catalog reasons about what the server can WRITE and almost never about what the server can PRE-DELIVER.

Fifth, the ops and wildcard domains carry internal contradictions the catalog never reconciles (Console.instance non-null vs the admin-command option ruled out; ForceSendZDO 'regardless' vs the ShouldSend gate; Sector Zero asserted vs never traced). A verification column per option — 'read in decompile / inferred / needs in-game' — should be mandatory before any of this becomes a spec."


**Gaps identified:**
- **[access]** Per-peer ZDO withholding (sync-list filtering) as a server-ENFORCED per-player portal gate. Mechanism: the ONLY ways a portal ZDO reaches a client are ZDOMan.CreateSyncList (private, :77212-77241 — FindSectorObjects near peer.m_refPos then peer.ShouldSend) plus the force-send queue drained by AddForceSendZdos (:77263-77287, also gated on peer.ShouldSend) and RPC_RequestZDO (:77689-77692, GetPeer(sender)?.ForceSendZDO). A Harmony postfix on CreateSyncList(ZDOPeer peer, List<ZDO> toSync) that removes portal ZDOs (and their partner/anchor ZDOs) the peer's socket-verified account is not permitted to hold, plus a veto of RequestZDO for those ids in the ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC prefix, means the non-member client never receives the ZDO: no mesh, no TeleportWorldTrigger, and — if the withheld ZDO is the DESTINATION — TeleportWorld.TargetFound (:143646-143654) is false forever so gate 1 of Teleport (:143519) refuses silently while the source still hovers '[Connected]'. A modified client cannot obtain the ZDO from any other source (clients never relay ZDOs to each other; RouteRPC on the server forwards RPCs only, :83597-83629). Revocation mid-session: invoke the routed 'DestroyZDO' RPC (registered on every client at :76155) TARGETED at that one peer with a ZPackage of the ids — the client's RPC_DestroyZDO/HandleDestroyedZDO removes it locally; the m_deadZDOs resurrection block is IsServer()-only (:76994-76998) so re-grant later works, but the server's ZDOPeer.m_zdos cache must be cleared for that id or ShouldSend stays false. Verified caveat: ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901-76926) assigns ownership to any nearby peer WITHOUT checking peer.m_zdos, so a withheld portal near a non-member becomes 'owned' by a client that has no copy — Game.RPC_SetConnection on that client no-ops on GetZDO==null (:100653-100662) and RPC_SetTag from a member is dropped — so withheld portals must be ownership-pinned to the server (SetOwner prefix + SetOwnerInternal guard). This single mechanism falsifies 'Per-Player Transit Gate — RULED OUT', 'Per-Peer Divergent ZDO Routing — RULED OUT' (withholding is not divergence: nothing reconverges) and the economy domain's 'should THIS PLAYER pass — impossible for four reasons'. In-game check: withhold one portal from peer B, confirm B sees nothing at the site, confirm B's partner-side portal hovers connected but never teleports, confirm A still transits normally. — The catalog's entire enforcement taxonomy rests on 'one ZDO object, every peer reconverges' — but the server decides what each peer is SENT, and the vanilla client has no other source. Every private-network, faction, admin-only-infrastructure and per-player-lock feature is currently marked reactive or impossible when a genuinely enforced form exists.
- **[wildcard]** Tame and cart follow-through (moving non-portal persistent ZDOs across a transit). Vanilla tames and carts cannot use portals; this is the most-requested portal feature after ore (TamesPatch in TortalPortal, 'Teleport Wolves', 'CartPortal'). Server-only version: on a detected transit (PositionWatch.IsPortalTransit) enumerate creature ZDOs within N m of the SOURCE whose ZDOVars.s_tamed is true and whose s_follow string (:78429, written by Tameable.RPC_Command :19444/:19457) equals the traveller's s_playerName, plus Vagon ZDOs within reach (Vagon has a Container field, :147342+21, so cargo rides along in s_items). For each: wait until no peer's active area covers it (ReleaseNearbyZDOS will release owner to 0 within 2 s once the traveller has left), then SetOwner(GetSessionID()), SetPosition(destination + offset), ForceSendZDO. Unlike portals, ZDO.SetSector for a non-portal prefab DOES re-file the ZDO (:73752-73768: RemoveFromSector/AddToSector + ZDOSectorInvalidated, which per-peer drops it from m_zdos when outside their area, :75989-75996) so sector sync delivers it at the new location, and the arriving client's Tameable.UpdateSavedFollowTarget (:19478-19497) re-attaches the follow by name via Player.GetAllPlayers on that client. Caveats: only when the source zone is unloaded by everyone (a second player standing at the source keeps ownership and the client's ZSyncTransform overwrites the position — 5 m snap :87715); creatures with ZSyncTransform pop rather than walk; the traveller must be the only same-named player. Must specify: radius, max followers, unsummon/boss exclusions, what happens to a cart mid-pull (s_attachJointHash bool :147661). — Not one of 197 options touches creatures or vehicles as things that travel, despite it being a top-3 request for every portal mod and despite the mechanism (non-portal ZDO relocation) being cleanly distinct from the ruled-out 'move the portal' case.
- **[targeted]** Destination pre-generation via ghost-zone spawning at the TARGET. ZoneSystem.CreateGhostZones is private (:113971-113992) and only ever runs at peer.GetRefPos() (:113937), which is why the targeted domain concedes 'an unvisited corner has a LocationInstance but no altar/trader ZDO'. The server can call the publicized ZoneSystem.SpawnZone(zone, SpawnMode.Ghost, out _) (:114071) for the destination zone and its neighbours itself, materialising LocationProxy, OfferingBowl-parent, Trader and DungeonGenerator ZDOs (with s_roomData) before any player arrives — turning 'boss altar', 'trader', 'crypt room' targets from 'sometimes' into 'always', and letting the Destination Safety Validator check real placed objects instead of pre-flattening heights. Also fixes m_iconPlaced traders never appearing on LocationIcons. Caveats: SpawnZone instantiates and destroys real GameObjects on the server main thread (:114085-114102) — budget one zone per tick; requires ZoneSystem.IsZoneGenerated check first; interacts with the sector-0 clamp for out-of-range coordinates. — Every 'portal to X location' option is currently gated on a player having wandered near X first; this is the one call that removes the dependency and nobody proposed it.
- **[routing]** Delivery-guarantee engine: join-time portal broadcast + destination pre-streaming. Verified: a joining peer receives only ZDOs near its refPos (CreateSyncList :77212-77241) — there is NO vanilla 'send all portals on join' path (ZDOMan.AddPeer :76767-76773 only registers ZDOData). So every far portal ZDO is absent until RequestZDO, which is exactly the silent first-transit failure the digest names ten times as a gotcha and solves nowhere. Option: (a) on PeerJoinLeaveHook join, ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, id) for every id in GetPortalList() plus every managed anchor — ShouldSend is true for never-seen ZDOs so it always lands, cost is O(portals) small packets once; (b) on every route write, ForceSendZDO(peer, destId) to every peer within activation range of the source; (c) a CreateSyncList postfix that appends the destination zone's ZDOs (FindSectorObjects at the target) for any peer standing within 12 m of a managed portal — the SectorSubscription mechanism from TortalPortal/SectorSubscription.cs:106 but server-initiated, so a vanilla client already holds the arrival area and Player.UpdateTeleport's IsAreaReady gate (:15349) clears at the 8 s floor instead of stalling toward the 15 s fallback. Caveat: AddForceSendZdos is ShouldSend-gated (:77273) — force-send is distance-independent but NOT revision-independent. — The catalog treats the missing-destination-ZDO failure as an unavoidable tax on every dynamic feature; it is a fixable delivery problem with three cheap, verifiable mechanisms.
- **[access]** Untagged-portal auto-pair suppression. ZDO.GetString(s_tag) defaults to '' (:75079-75082) so every freshly placed, never-named portal in the world is one tag group and Game.ConnectPortals phase 2 (:100607-100622) links it to a RANDOM untagged portal anywhere — a stranger's base, an admin hub — within 5 s of placement. Popular request ('new portals should not connect until named'). Server-enforced fix at the arrival hook (CreateNewZDO+Deserialize postfix, SpawnGovernor.cs:43/:58): if s_tag == '' write a unique invisible tag ('<' + rounded position hash + '>', stripped from hover by RemoveRichTextTags assembly_utils_SERVER:6700 but distinct for pairing) plus SetDirtyPortals(); the Tag Watchdog reverts to '' → unique on any later clear. Must also handle the load-time case (portals loaded with '' from ChunkPortal, :76474-76482) before the synchronous Game.ConnectPortals at :76523. Caveat: the player's rename box pre-fills with the raw tag (:143551, :61519) so the suffix must be ≤10 chars or the client truncates it on save. — Anti-Grief Tag Integrity covers squatting and near-duplicates but not the '' group, which is the single most common accidental cross-base link on any real server.
- **[economy]** Presence-conditioned routes: routes that are wired only while the builder (s_creator :78393 == s_playerID :78539 of a ready peer) or a member of the route's network is ONLINE, or only while nobody from the network is online (the inverse: offline-raid protection — no one can portal INTO a base whose owners are all logged out). Pure 'should this ROUTE be open' predicate over ZNet.GetPeers()/ConnectedCharacters.All(), so server-enforced at the connection layer; combine with the Customs House decoy so the gate still glows. Variant: owner-nearby (builder within N m of either end) for 'escort-only' gates. Needs the join/leave hooks (PeerJoinLeaveHook.cs:26/:48) as edge triggers and a reconcile tick as the truth. — Debtor's Lien proved that per-player rules become enforceable when re-expressed over property; presence is the most obvious such predicate for PvP servers and it is absent.
- **[lockdown]** Placement policy engine at the ZDO arrival hook, with ground-drop refund. The catalog only uses the CreateNewZDO+Deserialize pair (SpawnGovernor.cs:43/:58, verified :76684/:76929) for a numeric per-player cap. Popular server rules it can equally enforce, all as pure geometry/ZDO reads at Deserialize time: minimum spacing between portals (GetPortalList distance), biome bans (WorldGenerator.GetBiome :151725 — e.g. no Ashlands portals), no portals within N m of world spawn (GetLocationIcon('StartTemple')), no portals outside a ward the placer is permitted on (Shadow Ward Index), no portals in interiors (y > 3000), no portals within N m of another player's wards. Rejection = SetOwner(session)+DestroyZDO. Refund: the server cannot touch the placer's inventory, but ItemDrop.DropItem(itemData, amount, pos, rot) with m_dropPrefab set by hand (FirstSpawnGrant.cs:218 pattern) drops the recipe cost on the ground at the site — reading the recipe from ObjectDB.instance.GetRecipe on the server (retry until ObjectDB resolves). Toast the reason via PlayerNotify. — Placement rules are the second most common admin request after caps and the hook already exists; nobody generalised the cap into a policy engine or addressed the material-loss complaint a destroy-on-arrival produces.
- **[ux]** Consent-handshake player-to-player teleport (TPA/summon) and emote warp verbs with no portal involved. Popular mods: 'TPA', '/home', '/back', '/spawn'. Server-only shape: requester performs emote X while their s_lookTarget (:78677, written every 0.2 s by CharacterAnimEvent.UpdateHeadRotation :5041-5081) points within a cone at another connected character — the server records a pending request keyed on both s_playerIDs and toasts the target; the target performs emote Y within 30 s to accept; the server sends RPC_TeleportPlayer/RPC_TeleportTo (distant:true) to the requester at the target's live ZDO position. Verbs: 'home' = nearest bed with s_owner == playerID; 'back' = the server's own pre-teleport position ledger (the only party that can implement /back, since the client never networks its own history); 'spawn' = GetLocationIcon('StartTemple'). All must respect the 2 s cooldown (:15309-15316), s_dead (:78403), s_inBed (:78457), and bypass every vanilla gate (so ore travels — say so). No 'accept' is possible via chat; emote-only. — The catalog uses RPC_TeleportPlayer only as a portal delivery mechanism; the portal-less warp/summon family that every server-admin mod ships is entirely missing, and the consent handshake is a novel use of s_lookTarget.
- **[wildcard]** Per-peer LocationIcons payload: per-player respawn override and per-player landmark reveal. ZoneSystem.SendLocationIcons(long peer) is per-peer (:113581-113593) and the client's RPC_LocationIcons REPLACES its whole m_locationIcons dictionary (:113595-113607). Client Game.FindSpawnPoint falls through to GetLocationIcon(m_StartLocation) whenever there is no logout point and no custom spawn point (verified in the client decompile: logout → bed → StartTemple → zero) — so sending peer B a payload whose 'StartTemple' entry is the faction hall makes B's NEW characters and bed-less deaths respawn there, on a vanilla client, with no other peer affected. Same payload controls which boss-altar/trader icons B's map shows (hide undiscovered altars, reveal a faction's private hub as a 'Vendor' icon). Requirements: prefix SendLocationIcons to substitute the per-peer dictionary (the PlaceLocations re-broadcast at :115000-115003 and OnNewPeer :113609 would otherwise reset it), keep names inside the client's Minimap.m_locationIcons sprite list, and note that a custom bed spawn always wins. — 'World Spawn / Start Temple' mentions in passing that the server can relocate the world spawn; nobody noticed the channel is per-peer, which makes it the one place a vanilla client's RESPAWN is per-player server-controlled.
- **[routing]** Fast-transit mode (skip the 8 s hold). Portals always pass distantTeleport:true (:143546) and the traveller is pinned for ≥8 s (:15349). A two-hop relay whose second hop sends RPC_TeleportTo with distantTeleport:false completes at t≈2 s once IsAreaReady (:15337-15352), reproducing the 'Fast Portals / Portal Stations' feel — but only if the destination area is already held by the client (delivery-guarantee engine) and FindFloor succeeds, otherwise UpdateTeleport reverts the player to m_teleportFromPos with '$msg_portal_blocked' (:15369-15374). Spec must define: pre-stream trigger radius, fallback to distant:true when the destination zone was never generated (SpawnZone ghost first), and the fact that no swirl animation plays (Hud keys the swirl on m_distantTeleport, :47872). — Instant portals are a headline feature of several popular mods; the catalog only warns against distant:false rather than designing the conditions under which it is safe.
- **[wildcard]** Arrival-triggered world events. RandEventSystem.SetRandomEventByName(name, pos) is public and the event system is server-driven (IsServer gates at :105343-105414, :106791-106805). On a detected transit (or on a route being opened) the server can start a raid at the arrival point ('ambush gate'), or at the SOURCE when a lockdown is violated. Combine with the Raid-Time Geofenced Restriction so the gate that summoned the raid also closes. Caveat: reactive (~2 s late), and the event radius/duration are Inspector data on the RandomEvent asset; must not fire inside boss-alerted areas because of the activeBosses leak (:27256-27261). — The catalog reads event state as an input to routing but never treats routing as a trigger for events, which is the mechanism behind every 'cursed portal' / 'dungeon-of-the-day with a welcoming party' design.
- **[economy]** Post-transit status effects (portal sickness / arrival buff). 'Portal Sickness' is a widely-used mod. Server-only: on PositionWatch transit detection, StatusEffectRpc.Grant (Wonderland StatusEffectRpc.cs:27, SEMan.RPC_AddStatusEffect :28823) a vanilla effect on the traveller's character ZDO — Wet/Cold/Burning as a penalty, Rested as a reward — with a per-player cooldown so re-ping loops (BuffRosterEngine pattern) make it last N minutes. Honest classification: reactive, ~2 s after the move, cannot be removed early (no RemoveStatusEffect RPC exists anywhere), and only vanilla effect assets. Also the only server-side way to express 'portal cooldown per player' visibly, since the route-level cooldown option closes the gate for everyone. — The economy domain has route cooldowns and the ux domain has status effects as feedback, but nobody composed them into the per-player consequence that players actually recognise from existing mods.
- **[access]** Ownership transfer and orphan adoption by rewriting s_creator/s_creatorIndex. Piece.Awake reads s_creator/s_creatorIndex from the ZDO on every client (:136246-136250) and Piece.SetCreator only writes when GetCreator()==0 (:136417), so a server write of s_creator (no setter checks ownership, :73648) permanently reassigns 'built by' as every vanilla client sees it — the basis for 'transfer this gate to player X', 'adopt admin-spawned portals (creator 0) to a maintenance account', and 'reassign a departed player's portals to a guild'. Cross-check against ZNet.World.m_playerHistory (:112396) so s_creatorIndex stays consistent. Needs SetDirtyPortals(). Caveat: this also flips ward IsCreator semantics on wards themselves if applied to guard stones — scope to portal prefabs. — Every access option treats s_creator as read-only evidence; it is also the writable lever for the ownership-management features (transfer, adopt, reclaim) that admins ask for constantly.
- **[lockdown]** Portal sanctuary — spawn suppression around portals. SpawnGovernor already destroys creature ZDOs on arrival (SpawnGovernor.cs:43-70); a portal-specific rule 'no hostile creature ZDO may appear within N m of any portal in GetPortalList()' (or of managed hubs only) makes arrival points safe without wards. Server-enforced at the ZDO layer (creature ZDOs are client-spawned and arrive via ZDOData). Must exclude tames (s_tamed) and player-summoned creatures, and budget per tick. — Safe arrival is a standard 'portal hub' feature and the hook is already shipped in the sibling mod; nothing in lockdown/safety addresses creatures at the destination.
- **[routing]** Character-ZDO-bit predicates for approach-triggered routing: s_pvp (:78551), s_crowned (:78399), s_inBed, s_dead, equipped-item hashes, s_stealth. Example: an arena gate whose destination is parked unless every player within the arming radius has s_pvp true — the only way to keep non-PvP players out of a PvP zone on a vanilla client. Example: a 'no armour' challenge gate that parks when the approaching player's s_chestItem != 0. All are JIT variants (write before the trigger, ~2 s lead) and inherit JIT's two-player contention problem; spec them as predicates on the existing JIT option rather than as new gates. — The JIT option only uses position; the character ZDO carries a dozen server-readable bits that turn 'who is approaching' into 'what state are they in', which is what PvP/challenge servers actually want to gate on.
- **[targeted]** Auto corpse-run gate. On tombstone creation (TombStone ZDO with s_owner/s_timeOfDeath/s_spawnPoint, :19732-19740, :19845-19853) fabricate an ephemeral phantom portal at the player's bed (s_owner match) or the hub, pointed at a Void Anchor 2 m from the tombstone, tagged with an invisible per-player suffix so only that pairing exists, and destroy both when the tombstone despawns (TombStone.UpdateDespawn :19875-19890) or after a TTL. Composes Ephemeral Event Gates + Tombstone target + Anchor, but the lifecycle (death → gate → pickup → cleanup) is not specified anywhere. — Corpse-recovery is one of the most-installed QoL portal features and the pieces exist in three different domains without a composed spec.
- **[ops]** On-join briefing and login-time state push. PeerJoinLeaveHook (Wonderland) fires on RPC_PeerInfo; nothing in the catalog uses the join event as a lifecycle hook for portals. Spec: at join (after the character ZDO appears and s_playerID is non-zero), toast the player's own portal count and orphaned tags, re-push idempotent map pins for their own portals (HaveSimilarPin dedups, client :58363-58374), force-send all managed anchors (gap above), and — for admins by socket host name — a health summary. Also the correct place to seed per-player state (last-seen for lease/GC engines keyed on PlatformUserID, since m_playerHistory carries no timestamp). — Several ops/economy options quietly need a 'last seen' ledger and a per-player state seed, and the catalog never names the event that provides it.

**Unverified/shaky claims flagged:**
- 'Sector Zero — Portals Outside The World' (wildcard): that a ZDO beyond ±16.4 km lands in the same bucket as the server's pinned reference position AND gets instantiated server-side. ZDO.SetSector does route OutsideZones ZDOs to ZoneSystem.SectorZero (:73758), but whether ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted on the server actually passes IsActiveAreaLoaded at (1e6,0,1e6) and instantiates sector-0 ZDOs was not read; treat as needs-ingame-check, not feasible.
- 'The Void Anchor' claim that prefab hash 0 makes ZNetScene.CreateObject return null silently (:81996-82002) while an unknown non-zero hash logs every frame, and that ZDO's default m_prefab is -1 not 0 — not independently verified this pass; every anchor option depends on it.
- ZNetView.LoadFields on vanilla-shipped portal prefabs: whether the client's LoadFields gate is zdo.GetBool('HasFields') alone or also requires prefab-side state, whether the HasFields* keys survive the owning client's own ZDO pushes (Deserialize is additive, so probably yes) and a save/load round-trip, and whether TeleportWorld is reached by GetComponentsInChildren. 'The Ore Gate' and 'Field Injection' are unproven until one in-game test.
- Ops 'Admin command channel: server-registered ConsoleCommand + RPC_RemoteCommand' is marked ruled-out while the ops domain notes assert Console.instance IS non-null on a dedicated server (Game.Awake :100038-100041) and RPC_RemoteCommand is a working admin-gated channel. The catalog contradicts itself; one of the two is wrong and the in-game check (send a registered onlyServer/remoteCommand command from an admin client's F5 console) has not been run.
- Whether an HttpListener (ops HTTP endpoint) works under the dedicated server's Mono runtime and BepInEx sandbox; never checked.
- Whether Chat.instance / MessageHud.instance / Minimap.instance exist on the dedicated server. Evidence is contradictory (Game.UpdateSaving guards MessageHud at :100474; ZNet.LowDiskLeftInformer dereferences it unguarded under IsDedicated at :80258). This decides whether a server-side ZRoutedRpc.Register('ChatMessage') throws and whether WorldSaveFinished ever fires.
- The rich-text regex doubling bypass ('<<color=red>color=red>' survives RemoveRichTextTags) — regex reasoning is plausible but TMP rendering of the survivor on a vanilla client is untested.
- That destroying a client-placed portal ZDO inside the ZDO.Deserialize postfix leaves the placing client in a clean state (no orphaned local instance, materials consumed) — SpawnGovernor proves it for creatures only.
- ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync on the Player prefab (Inspector) — every 'portal to a player's ship' and 'rider parent' claim rests on it; the confirmed fallback is only ZDOVars.s_user for the helmsman.
- PrivateArea.m_radius on the guard_stone prefab — the Shadow Ward Index is wrong at every ward until the Inspector value is read.
- The catalog repeatedly states ForceSendZDO 'pushes regardless of distance'; verified this pass that AddForceSendZdos is still gated on peer.ShouldSend (:77273), so a force-send to a peer whose cached DataRevision is current sends nothing. Any 'touch to resync' design needs a real revision bump.
- That 3+ same-tag portals strand exactly one member PERMANENTLY across ticks (pairing-algorithm digest). Plausible from the two-tick commit but the interaction with phase-1 teardown of a pair whose partner later gets ownership-deferred was not traced.
- EnvMan.instance and GetDayFraction() being live headless — the entire scheduled-routing family assumes it and nothing verifies it.
- Whether a vanilla client that has already received a ZDO discards it cleanly on a peer-targeted 'DestroyZDO' routed RPC and accepts re-delivery later (client-side HandleDestroyedZDO path) — required for the revocation half of per-peer withholding.

### Critic: honesty


The catalog's biggest honesty problem is not any single option but the enforcement vocabulary. 'server-enforced' is applied to options whose route gate is server-owned but whose triggering condition is client-authored ZDO data (Prepaid Toll Escrow, Token Turnstile, Charge Cells, Key-Item Requirement), while the Ore Gate — which has exactly the same trust model — is labelled client-honoured. The digest's own test ('should this ROUTE be open' vs 'should this PLAYER pass') is necessary but not sufficient; a second axis is missing: 'is the INPUT the decision reads server-authored or client-authored, and is there a validator?'. Every option needs an explicit dependency line ('server-enforced given: Ungated RPC Hardening + Inline ZDOData validator') instead of a bare tier word. Second, the option one-liners carry no citations at all — every `file:line` lives in domain notes and the digest — so an option cannot be audited in isolation, and the prior-session review notes show that when the digest is wrong (m_exitDistance source-vs-destination, RPC_SetTag interception as 'the only hook', nomap 'correctly branching', RPC_RemoteCommand 'working channel') the error propagates into three or four options unnoticed. Each option should restate its two or three load-bearing citations inline. Third, the ruled-out entries are written as absolutes where degraded forms exist (per-player transit → reactive ejection; chat → pending a single RelationsProvider test; admin console channel → setkey piggyback), which is the opposite failure from over-claiming and equally costly. Fourth, the research briefs collectively raise ~40 'IN-GAME CHECK' items and the catalog operationalises none of them: there is no probe engine, and needs-ingame-check options do not name the predicate that decides them (Sector Zero, HTTP endpoint, Scaling). Fifth, cross-cutting engineering requirements that every dynamic option depends on — DestinationPrewarm (ForceSendZDO on re-point), SetDirtyPortals after every non-connection write, ZDOID-vs-position keying, the OwnerRevision race — appear as footnotes repeated in six domain notes rather than as owned components with a defined trigger set; a designer reading one option will miss them. Sixth, the ops block is visibly un-researched relative to the others (its domain notes contradict its own ruled-out entry on RPC_RemoteCommand, and it asserts a runtime facility the decompile cannot see). Finally, 197 options is inflation: at least a third are recombinations of five primitives (SetConnection ownership-claim write, phantom/anchor ZDO, global key write, RPC_TeleportPlayer, ZDO field poll) and would be better expressed as one primitive spec plus a table of compositions, which would also make the tier and dependency labels consistent by construction."


**Gaps identified:**
- **[wildcard]** Field Injection / Ore Gate / Phantom Destination Portal all say per-portal m_exitDistance is overridable 'on the destination phantom'. The decompile says the opposite: TeleportWorld.Teleport computes `pos = targetPos + rot*forward * m_exitDistance + up` with `this.m_exitDistance` — the SOURCE portal's field (assembly_valheim_SERVER.decompiled.cs:143539-143546). A LoadFields override written on the destination ZDO does nothing to the exit throw; it must be written on the portal the player walks INTO. Same for m_allowAllItems (:143533, source). Also m_activationRange only feeds Player.GetClosestPlayer for the glow (:143495) — it does not enlarge the transit collider. Rewrite the three options with a per-field table: field → which portal it lives on (source vs destination) → what it actually changes → applies-at-instantiation caveat. Note in the option's favour that vanilla's own `spawn` console command writes exactly these HasFields keys (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:44423-44430), so the path is a supported vanilla data contract, not an accident. — Three options (wildcard Field Injection, economy Ore Gate, targeted Phantom Destination Portal) and the targeted domain notes propagate a factual inversion from the research digest; a designer following them would write the override onto the wrong ZDO and conclude the mechanism is broken.
- **[access]** Ownership Pin is described as 'permanently hold managed portals' ownership' via the WaterBuoyancyEngine ZDO.SetOwner prefix. That prefix is insufficient: ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData applies an incoming owner with ZDO.SetOwnerInternal (:77114, :77128), never SetOwner, and the :77112-77117 branch applies an owner change whenever the incoming OwnerRevision is higher even when DataRevision is not. A vanilla client's ZNetView.ClaimOwnership (:82769 → SetOwner → IncreaseOwnerRevision) therefore steals the pin back on the next ZDOData packet. Spec a real pin: (1) SetOwner prefix for ReleaseNearbyZDOS (:76901); (2) a postfix on ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData or ZDO.Deserialize that re-claims with SetOwner(GetSessionID()) whenever a pinned portal arrives with a foreign owner, bumping OwnerRevision above the client's; (3) an analysis of the ping-pong (each side bumps OwnerRevision by 1; an honest client claims rarely, a hostile one can force a loop — cap and escalate to kick); (4) the unpin path, because a pinned gate cannot be hammer-removed by anyone (WearNTear.Remove :150411 routes RPC_Remove to the owner, the server, which has no instance). — The option is marked client-honoured/feasible-with-caveats but its core mechanism is broken as written; every option that relies on 'the server holds ownership' (Tag-Scramble Lockdown, Managed Network Governor, Adamant Gate, NetworkReassertEngine) inherits the hole.
- **[targeted]** Two-Hop Relay (phantom landing pad + RPC_TeleportPlayer) omits the cooldown arithmetic that dominates its UX. Player.TeleportTo sets m_teleportCooldown = 0 on acceptance (:15320) and UpdateTeleport keeps it at 0 for the whole teleport (:15334), only accruing once m_teleporting is false. A distantTeleport does not end before t>8s (:15349). So the server sees the character ZDO land in the lobby at t≈2s, but any second hop sent before ≈t=10s is silently dropped (IsTeleporting :15309, then cooldown<2f :15313), with no signal for when the first hop finished. Spec the relay with: a fixed ≥10 s hold after the lobby position appears, a 'standing in the lobby for ~2 s' UX moment, total black-screen budget (~8+2+8 s), distantTeleport:false for the second hop (completes on IsAreaReady, ~2 s, but rubber-bands with $msg_portal_blocked if FindFloor misses — :15369-15374), and a dead-player / in-bed pre-check (s_dead, s_inBed). — The option is sold as the answer to per-player destinations and rule enforcement, but as written every second hop would silently fail; the honest cost is a ~20 s transit that must be designed around, not discovered in testing.
- **[ops]** Ops rules out the admin command channel entirely ('a vanilla client never forwards a mod command'), and the ops domain notes simultaneously call RPC_RemoteCommand 'a genuine, working channel'. Both are half right. A vanilla Terminal.TryRunCommand only forwards commands present in its own dictionary (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:45737-45744), so `tplite.*` never leaves the client — but `setkey`, `removekey`, `listkeys`, `resetworldkeys` are registered isCheat:false, onlyServer:true, remoteCommand:true (:43509-43533, :43605), so a vanilla ADMIN typing `setkey tplite:dump 3` in F5 sends RPC_RemoteCommand (admin-gated on the socket host name, :81879-81887) and the server runs Console.instance.TryRunCommand (:81893). Spec a piggyback channel: a server-side Harmony prefix on Terminal.TryRunCommand (or on the setkey action) that intercepts a reserved `setkey tplite:...` namespace before vanilla's SetKeyAndValueIsCheat check (:43513), executes the mod command, replies via ZNet.RemotePrint(rpc, ...) (:81635) into the admin's console, and never lets the fake key reach GlobalKeyAdd. Document that the server-side ZNet.RemoteCommand(cmd) path NREs on rpc==null (:81873→:81893) so the stdin console must not use it. — The catalog and its own domain notes contradict each other, and a real, zero-client admin channel from the vanilla F5 console is currently listed as impossible.
- **[lockdown]** Global-Key RPC Hardening and Ungated RPC Hardening say 'drop any SetGlobalKey/RemoveGlobalKey packet that did not originate from the server'. Two errors. (1) Vanilla clients legitimately originate these RPCs: Character.OnDeath calls ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(m_defeatSetGlobalKey) and decrements activeBosses on the killing client (:3153-3165), BaseAI.SetAlerted increments activeBosses (:27258), and every killed_*/StoneCircle/AshlandsOcean key comes the same way. A blanket drop breaks boss progression and the activeBosses accounting the lockdown's own watchdog depends on. (2) The `long sender` argument of ZoneSystem.RPC_SetGlobalKey (:116022) is RoutedRPCData.m_senderPeerID, deserialized off the wire (:83489) — a client can set it to the server's id, so a prefix on RPC_SetGlobalKey cannot tell local from remote.
