Spec the hardening as: a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC (the only place the authentic ZRpc is in scope, :83632) matching m_methodHash against SetGlobalKey/RemoveGlobalKey, parsing the key name, and dropping only keys with GetKeyValue ordinal < GlobalKeys.NonServerOption (world modifiers) plus the mod's reserved prefixes, while passing every ≥41 key through untouched. Add TeleportWorld's client→client 'RPC_SetConnected' (:143622) and 'DestroyZDO' to the relay-drop list for managed portals. — As written, the flagship 'tamper-proof lockdown' either breaks vanilla boss progression or is trivially bypassed by sender spoofing; the fix changes the hook location and adds an allow-list, which is a different option spec.
- **[wildcard]** Non-Portals As Portals (extending Game.PortalPrefabHash at runtime) omits a data-loss hazard. ZDOMan.AddObjectsPerChunk clones into normal chunk files only ZDOs with `Persistent && !PortalPrefabHash.Contains(prefab)` (:77572), while the ChunkPortal file only clones m_portalObjects (:77621-77627). Any ZDO of the enrolled prefab that already existed in m_objectsBySector when the hash was added is in neither set — it is silently absent from the next save of its chunk and gone after restart. Additionally ZDO.SetSector early-returns for the enrolled prefab (:73752), so a mobile enrolled object (ship, cart) stops re-sectoring and its delivery to clients freezes. Spec the option with a mandatory migration pass (walk GetAllZDOsWithPrefabIterative for the prefab, RemoveFromSector + AddIfPortal each, SetDirtyPortals), a restriction to immobile prefabs, and an uninstall reversal (the vanilla server will load them from ChunkPortal into m_portalObjects regardless of prefab, then pair them by tag). — The option is marked feasible-with-caveats but the caveat that matters — every pre-existing instance of the enrolled prefab is lost on the next save — is absent; shipping it as written destroys world data.
- **[access]** The catalog rules out per-player transit gating absolutely (access 'Per-Player Transit Gate — RULED OUT', economy 'RULED OUT — Point-of-Transit Enforcement'). Prevention is indeed impossible, but reactive ejection is not: the server sees the traveller's character ZDO land at t≈2 s (:15343), the player is frozen and invulnerable until t>8 s (:15349, damage suppressed :2425), and at ≈t=10 s RPC_TeleportPlayer / RPC_TeleportTo can send a non-permitted arrival straight back to their origin (or to a holding cell). The player sees the destination for ~2 s and cannot act during the frozen window (Player.CanMove false :14425). Spec a 'Bouncer' option: arrival detection via the PositionWatch straddle heuristic plus the destination portal's connection, an ACL lookup keyed on s_playerID, the ≥10 s hold, distantTeleport:true for the return (never fails), a per-player 'ejected' toast, and the honest tier: reactive-detection-only, undoes but never prevents, defeated only by the same RPC-spoofing a hardened relay already blocks. — A whole class of degraded-but-real per-player enforcement is missing because the ruled-out entries were written as absolutes; the economy and access domains both lose their only per-player consequence that acts on the person rather than their property.
- **[economy]** Every escrow/turnstile/charge-cell option (Prepaid Toll Escrow, Token Turnstile, Charge Cells, Key-Item Requirement) is marked 'feasible/server-enforced' while the Ore Gate is marked client-honoured — but both read client-authored ZDO data. The route gate is server-owned, but the CONDITION (s_items on a chest, s_item on a stand, s_fuel on a fireplace) is written by the owning client and ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData applies it wholesale with no validation (:77107-77131). A modified client forges a full chest and the toll is free; no ZDOData validator option exists anywhere in the catalog. Spec (a) a tier correction: 'server-enforced against unmodified clients; condition inputs forgeable without (b)'; and (b) an 'Inline ZDOData validator' option: a Harmony postfix on ZDO.Deserialize (or prefix on RPC_ZDOData that re-parses a copy of the package, saving/restoring pkg position) that, for bound escrow containers and managed portals, compares the arriving fields against the last server-approved state and reverts inside the same frame — collapsing the Tag Watchdog's one-tick window to zero and giving the economy its only real anti-forgery line. — The enforcement tier is applied inconsistently across options that share the same trust model, and the one mechanism that would make the economy's inputs trustworthy is not in the catalog.
- **[ux]** Map Ping → Destination and the UX ping picker cite a HandleRoutedRPC prefix as the 'collision-free' hook and take the sender from the packet. HandleRoutedRPC(RoutedRPCData) (:83645) has no socket in scope; both m_senderPeerID (:83489) and the UserInfo payload are client self-reports. The hook must be a prefix on ZRoutedRpc.RPC_RoutedRPC(ZRpc, ZPackage) (:83632) with the peer resolved via ZNet.instance.GetPeers().First(p => p.m_rpc == rpc). Also missing: Chat.SendPing overwrites vector.y with the PLAYER's y (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:42063), so the destination height must be re-derived with WorldGenerator.GetHeight (:151944) — never ZoneSystem.GetGroundHeight, which is a dead raycast headless; pings are broadcast to every peer (the 'send me here' gesture is public); and a middle-click costs nothing, so the option needs a per-account debounce and an arming gate (crouch bit or proximity) before it re-routes anything. Spec the option with those four requirements as hard preconditions. — The most-recommended input channel in the catalog is specified against the wrong hook for identity and omits the y-override, so a naive implementation attributes pings to spoofed players and wires portals to a height 100 m off the ground.
- **[ux]** 'Chat commands (/portal home)' is marked ruled-out/not-enforceable, but the UX domain's own notes identify the one branch that would make it a first-class channel: Chat.CheckPermissionsAndSendChatMessageRPCsAsync collapses to a single targetPeerID 0 broadcast when PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider == null (:42002-42005). That type lives in the Splatform assembly, outside this decompile set. Slash commands remain dead (Chat.InputText :41947-41955), but plain text and shouts would reach the server even solo if RelationsProvider is null on Steam. Re-classify as needs-ingame-check with the exact test (RPC_RoutedRPC prefix logging 'ChatMessage' hashes while a SOLO vanilla player types a sentence and a /s shout), and pre-write the resulting option: keyword-prefixed plain chat as a 50+ character command line with the authentic sender from the socket. — A research-raised open question with the highest payoff of any single test was silently converted into a ruled-out entry; if the test passes, most of the emote/item-stand/crouch schemes become unnecessary.
- **[ops]** No option exists for a boot-time capability probe, yet roughly a dozen options are gated on Unity Inspector data the decompile cannot answer. Spec a first-class 'CapabilityProbe' engine that runs once at OnWorldReady and logs: Game.instance.m_portalPrefabs names + PortalPrefabHash; for each portal prefab, GetComponents<MonoBehaviour>() type names (the LoadFields HasFields<TypeName> keys), ZNetView m_persistent/m_distant/m_type/m_syncInitialScale, presence of ZSyncTransform, TeleportWorld.m_allowAllItems/m_exitDistance/m_activationRange; PrivateArea.m_radius on guard_stone; Player prefab ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync and CharacterAnimEvent.m_headRotation; null-ness of Chat.instance, MessageHud.instance, Minimap.instance, DamageText.instance, Console.instance; the key set of ZRoutedRpc.m_functions (decides Register-vs-Harmony for ChatMessage); ZNetScene.instance.NrOfInstances(); ZNet.GetReferencePosition(); ZoneSystem.IsActiveAreaLoaded() and m_zones.Count (Sector Zero); EnvMan.instance and GetDayFraction() advancing; and ZNetScene.GetPrefab('portal_wood')?.GetComponent<TeleportWorld>(). Each subsequent engine reads the probe result and self-disables with a logged reason when its precondition is absent. — Every research brief ends with 4-8 'IN-GAME CHECK' items and the catalog carries none of them as a deliverable; without a probe the mod either hard-codes guesses or ships engines that silently no-op, which is exactly the failure mode Wonderland's history records.
- **[wildcard]** The Adamant Gate overstates 'indestructible'. Writing a huge ZDOVars.s_health only defeats damage: WearNTear.RPC_Damage compares totalDamage against the stored health (:150350) and Repair correctly refuses when health >= m_health (:149528). But hammer removal (Player.RemovePiece → WearNTear.Remove → RPC_Remove to the ZDO owner, :150411-150425) ignores health entirely; support loss applies 100 wear per update forever (:149705-149711) and will eventually drain even 1e9; a forged DestroyZDO (:76953, ungated) deletes it outright; and any client can overwrite s_health via ZDOData. Rewrite the option as a composite: s_health for damage immunity + Ownership Pin (so RPC_Remove routes to a machine with no instance) + Destroy Veto + a support-independent re-assert of s_health on the watchdog tick, and state that it is only 'indestructible' once all four are present. — The option is marked feasible-with-caveats/client-honoured with a headline claim that a single ZDO write makes a portal indestructible; three vanilla paths delete it regardless of health.
- **[wildcard]** No option turns the LocationIcons channel into what it actually controls: the vanilla client's DEFAULT RESPAWN POINT. Game.FindSpawnPoint (client :100796-100800) falls back to ZoneSystem.GetLocationIcon(Game.m_StartLocation = 'StartTemple') when the profile has no logout/custom point, and that dictionary is filled only by the server's LocationIcons RPC (:113581-113607, replaced wholesale per receive). A server that sends a StartTemple entry at a different coordinate relocates where new/bedless characters spawn, with zero client mod. Spec it: an OnNewPeer/SendLocationIcons prefix that rewrites the StartTemple position to a mod-chosen hub, the honest scope (only players without a bed/logout point; the real temple still exists), the Minimap side effect (the temple icon moves on every client's map), and the uninstall restore. — The 'Portal-Driven Map Surfaces' and 'World Spawn' options treat LocationIcons as a read-only pin overlay and miss that it is the authority for a gameplay-relevant coordinate the server can steer.
- **[routing]** The first-transit warm-up is mentioned in five domain notes but exists as no option or engine. TeleportWorld.TargetFound returns false with NO message when the client does not hold the destination ZDO, firing a one-shot RequestZDO (:143646-143654); ZDOMan.RPC_RequestZDO answers with a single ForceSendZDO (:77689-77692) consumed on first send (:77048). Every server-side re-point to a far or freshly-fabricated destination therefore produces exactly one silent dead walk-through per player unless the mod pre-pushes. Spec 'DestinationPrewarm': on every managed connection write, ForceSendZDO(peer.m_uid, destId) to every peer within N m of the source portal; on every peer join, push the destinations of all managed portals within their active area; a re-push after any destination ZDO DataRevision bump (moving anchors); and the budget interaction with the 10240-byte send-queue cap (:77010-77016). — This is the single most common way a server-only routing mod will be reported as 'broken', and it is currently a footnote rather than a required component with a defined trigger set.
- **[wildcard]** Sector Zero is listed needs-ingame-check but its option does not state the decisive predicate or its side effects. Verified: SectorToIndex clamps any |x+256|>=512 or |y+256|>=512 to sector 0 (:115760-115773); FindObjects dedupes by SectorIndex so all neighbours of the server's pinned zone collapse to one visit of m_objectsBySector[0] + m_portalObjects[0] (:77366-77380); IsZoneReadyForType does NOT require m_zones membership (:115797-115810); the only real gate is IsActiveAreaLoaded() (:114054), i.e. whether PokeLocalZone(SpawnMode.Full) succeeds at zone (15625,15625). If it does, the server instantiates every ZDO beyond ±16.4 km AND every ZDO in the legitimate zone (-256,-256), and its server-only reaper (:82137-82143) destroys any prefab-less one it sees there. Spec the option around that predicate, list the reaper as a hazard for any Void Anchor with a typo'd coordinate, and note that ReleaseNearbyZDOS uses zone distance not sector index (:76887-76899) so the server will not auto-own those objects. — The option is marked suspicious by the prior reviewer; the sector math checks out but the actual instantiation hinges on one headless zone-spawn predicate nobody has named, and the side effect on Void Anchors is unstated.
- **[ux]** The MapTable shared-map blob is described in the UX domain notes as a server-craftable opt-in 'sync the portal network to my map' button but never became an option. MapTable.OnRead feeds ZDOVars.s_data straight into Minimap.AddSharedMapData (:133831-133865, client :58797-58875), which adds named saved pins on demand — the only vanilla channel that can deliver a SET of named pins to a player who chooses to receive them. Its two hazards are precise: it deletes every non-own-owner pin not re-listed in the blob (:58824-58875), and the explored array must be exactly Minimap.m_textureSize^2 bools (default 256, Inspector-overridable). Spec it: a server-written MapTable ZDO near each hub, the blob format from Minimap.GetSharedMapData (:58728-58775), a pin owner id convention that keeps player pins safe, the m_textureSize probe, and the reason it is opt-in (the player must press Read). — RPC_DiscoverLocationResponse pins are permanent and unremovable; the MapTable path is the only re-syncable named-pin surface and it was dropped between research and catalog.
- **[lockdown]** Session-Only Key Writes, Save-Boundary Transparency and Boss Auto-Lockdown never reconcile with each other about what a vanilla client is TOLD. NoPortals produces $msg_blocked only on walk-in; GetHoverText (:143453-143463) and UpdatePortal (:143491-143509) never consult the keys, so a blocked portal reads [Connected] and glows. The catalog's 'Graceful Lockdown and Announcement' covers announcements but no option specifies the per-portal in-world signal that a Tier-B (force-disconnect) lockdown gives for free and a Tier-A (key) lockdown does not: with the connection nulled the hover flips to $piece_portal_unconnected and the glow dies. Spec a 'Lockdown Legibility' rule: any key-based lockdown longer than N seconds must be paired with either a force-disconnect (so vanilla's own UI shows it) or a server-written tag suffix ≤10 chars (e.g. ' [X]') plus a DamageText overlay, and must be removed in the same tick the key is lifted. — Two of the lockdown options rely on the client-honoured key path whose only feedback is a centre-screen message after a failed walk-in; without a legibility rule operators will ship lockdowns that look like bugs.
- **[ops]** Output surface: in-process HTTP endpoint asserts HttpListener works under the game's Mono runtime without any evidence; nothing in the decompile can confirm it (it is a System.dll facility, not game code), and Unity's bundled Mono HttpListener has known prefix-binding and HTTPS limitations. Spec the option as needs-ingame-check with the exact probe (bind http://127.0.0.1:port/ in a BepInEx Awake on the dedicated server, GET from curl, confirm a 200 and that ZLog shows no ThreadAbort on shutdown), a fallback (the atomic JSON file export polled by an external script), and the threading contract already stated in the ops notes (main-thread snapshot → immutable DTO → listener thread). — Ops was generated without a research brief and this is the one option whose feasibility rests on a runtime the decompile cannot see; it is marked feasible-with-caveats rather than needs-ingame-check.

- ZNetView.LoadFields exists on the client (assembly_valheim.decompiled.cs:82898-82970), runs from ZNetView.Awake (:82860), and vanilla's own `spawn` command writes the HasFields keys (:44423-44430) — VERIFIED mechanism; whether TeleportWorld sits under GetComponentsInChildren of the portal prefab and the exact TypeName strings remain Inspector data (unverified).
- ZSyncAnimation.SetTrigger broadcasts to ZNetView.Everybody (:87260) and SetBool/SetFloat/SetInt write 438569+hash session keys on the owner's ZDO (:87270-87326) — VERIFIED; whether the Player prefab's crouch parameter name is 'crouching' is Inspector data (unverified).
- ZDOMan.RPC_ZDOData applies ownership via SetOwnerInternal (:77114, :77128) bypassing ZDO.SetOwner — VERIFIED.
- Vanilla client Terminal.TryRunCommand forwards RemoteCommand only for commands in its own dictionary (client :45737-45744); setkey/removekey/listkeys are isCheat:false onlyServer:true remoteCommand:true (:43509-43533, :43605) — VERIFIED.
- Character.OnDeath sets m_defeatSetGlobalKey and decrements activeBosses from the client (:3153-3165) — VERIFIED; blanket remote SetGlobalKey drop breaks progression.
- AddObjectsPerChunk excludes PortalPrefabHash prefabs from normal chunks (:77572) and the ChunkPortal file only takes m_portalObjects (:77621-77627) — VERIFIED.
- Player.TeleportTo zeroes m_teleportCooldown on accept (:15320) and UpdateTeleport holds it at 0 for the whole teleport (:15334) — VERIFIED; second hop dead zone ≥10 s.
- ZoneSystem.SectorToIndex clamp (:115760-115773), FindObjects SectorIndex dedupe (:77366-77380), server-only invalid-prefab reaper (:82137-82143), IsZoneReadyForType not requiring m_zones (:115797) — VERIFIED; whether IsActiveAreaLoaded() is true at (1e6,0,1e6) on a headless server is UNVERIFIED.
- ZNetScene.CreateObject returns null silently on prefab==0 (:81996-82000) and IsPrefabZDOValid returns false for 0 (:81986-81992); FilterZDO only warns for unknown prefabs (:76346-76360) — VERIFIED; whether a vanilla client keeps a prefab-0 ZDO indefinitely without evicting it is UNVERIFIED.
- WearNTear.Repair refuses when stored health >= m_health (:149528) and support loss applies 100 wear per update (:149705-149711) — VERIFIED.
- ZNet.WorldSaveStarted fires before ZDOMan.PrepareSave inside SaveWorld (:80524-80532); WorldSaveFinished is reached only via PrintWorldSaveMessage which dereferences MessageHud.instance unguarded (:80574-80578) — VERIFIED.
- EnvMan.instance is dereferenced unguarded by the server-only Game.UpdateSleeping (:100720-100727) — VERIFIED it exists headless; whether GetDayFraction/weather advance correctly headless is UNVERIFIED.
- RandEventSystem event radius test `DistanceXZ(position, re.m_pos) < re.m_eventRange` (:106835) and server-gated update (:106793-107105) — VERIFIED.
- Chat.SendPing overwrites vector.y with the player's own y and broadcasts to peer 0 (client :42058-42068) — VERIFIED.
- Minimap.DiscoverLocation always toasts and AddPins with save:true and ownerID 0 (client :58394-58420) — VERIFIED; behaviour on PlayFab/Xbox clients UNVERIFIED.
- Sign.UpdateText sets m_author=null for author 'host' and UpdateViewPermission then dereferences m_author.Value (client Sign.UpdateText/UpdateViewPermission) — VERIFIED.
- ZoneSystem.SetGlobalKey(GlobalKeys) stringifies PascalCase and RPC_SetGlobalKey's dedupe is case-sensitive (:115938-115946, :116022-116029) — VERIFIED.
- HttpListener availability and stability under the dedicated server's Unity Mono runtime — UNVERIFIABLE from the decompile.
- PlatformManager.DistributionPlatform.RelationsProvider null on the Steam backend (would make chat a server input) — UNVERIFIABLE from this decompile set (Splatform assembly absent).
- Chat.instance / MessageHud.instance / Console.instance / Minimap.instance null-ness on a 1.0.7 dedicated server — contradictory evidence in the decompile (Game.Awake instantiates only Console/ServerOptionsGUI at :100038-100045; ZNet.LowDiskLeftInformer and PrintWorldSaveMessage dereference MessageHud.instance unguarded) — UNVERIFIED.
- Contents of Game.m_portalPrefabs, portal prefab ZNetView flags (m_persistent/m_distant/m_type/m_syncInitialScale), presence of ZSyncTransform on portal prefabs, PrivateArea.m_radius on guard_stone, ZSyncTransform.m_characterParentSync on the Player prefab, portal_stone's baked m_allowAllItems — all Inspector data, UNVERIFIED.
